body.translated_text: Composed by <s>Āryabhaṭa</s>

body.text: Āryabhaṭīyam
body.translated_text: <s>Āryabhaṭīya</s>

body.text: Bhāskara-viracita-bhāṣyopetam
body.translated_text: Accompanied by the commentary composed by <s>Bhāskara</s>

body.text: Gītikāpādaḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Gītikāpāda</s> (Chapter on the Gītikā Verses)

body.text: maṅgalācaraṇam
body.translated_text: Invocatory Verse

body.text:
yasmāt aśeṣajagatām prabhavam sthitim ca
saṃhāram api upadiśanti samagradhīkāḥ |
bhṛgvaṅgiraḥprabhṛtayaḥ viditāntarāyāḥ
tasmai namaḥ kamalajāya caturmukhāya |
body.translated_text: Since those of complete understanding — <s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Aṅgiras</s>, and others — who know the obstacles, teach the origin, sustenance, and also the dissolution of all worlds without remainder, salutation to that four-faced one born from the lotus [i.e., <s>Brahmā</s>].

body.text: atha aśeṣajagadanugrahāya ācāryāryabhaṭamukhāravindavinissṛta-daśagītikā-sūtravyākhyānam ārabhyate | tasya eva aśeṣavighnanirākaraṇāya sarvavidyāprabhavasya bhagavataḥ kamalayoneḥ praṇāmaprakrāntaśāstravastuparigrahāya āryām ādau prayuktavān ã
body.translated_text: Now, for the benefit of all the worlds without exception, the explanation of the ten <s>Gītikā</s> verses and the <s>sūtras</s> (aphorisms) that have issued from the lotus-mouth of the teacher <s>Āryabhaṭa</s> is commenced. For the removal of all obstacles of that very [work], and for the purpose of commencing the subject-matter of the treatise through an act of obeisance to the blessed lotus-born one [<s>Brahmā</s>], who is the source of all knowledge, he employed an <s>āryā</s> verse at the beginning:

children.text: praṇipatya ekam anekam kam satyām devatām param brahma |
children.translated_text: Having bowed to the one [who is] one, many, <s>Ka</s> (i.e., <s>Prajāpati</s>), the true deity, the supreme <s>Brahman</s>,

children.text: āryabhaṭaḥ trīṇi gadati gaṇitam kālakriyām golam || 1 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Āryabhaṭa</s> sets forth three [subjects]: mathematics (<s>gaṇita</s>), reckoning of time (<s>kālakriyā</s>), and the sphere (<s>gola</s>). // 1 //

body.text: asyāḥ padavibhāgaḥ: ã praṇipatya, ekam, anekam, kam, satyām, devatām, param, brahma, āryabhaṭaḥ, trīṇi, gadati, gaṇitam, kālakriyām, golam |
body.translated_text: The word-by-word analysis of this [verse] is: <s>praṇipatya</s> (having bowed), <s>ekam</s> (one), <s>anekam</s> (many), <s>kam</s> (<s>Ka</s>), <s>satyām</s> (true), <s>devatām</s> (deity), <s>param</s> (supreme), <s>brahma</s> (<s>Brahman</s>), <s>āryabhaṭaḥ</s> (<s>Āryabhaṭa</s>), <s>trīṇi</s> (three), <s>gadati</s> (sets forth), <s>gaṇitam</s> (mathematics), <s>kālakriyām</s> (reckoning of time), <s>golam</s> (the sphere).

body.text:
atra praṇipatya iti "pra"-śabdaḥ prakarṣavācī, prakarṣeṇa nipatya praṇipatya, praṇāmam kṛtvā iti arthaḥ | ktvāpratyayena pūrvakālakriyā abhidhīyate, yathā snātvā bhuṅkte iti | snānakriyā anantaram bhojanakriyā | evam atra api praṇipatanānantaram gaṇitam, kālakriyām, golam ca gadati | ekam, abhedarūpeṇa vyavasthitam, nirvikāram | anekam, na ekam anekam, bhedarūpeṇa vyavasthitam | kam, kaḥ iti prajāpateḥ ākhyānam | kam praṇipatya evaṃguṇaviśiṣṭam
|
body.translated_text: Here, regarding <s>praṇipatya</s> (having bowed down): the prefix 'pra' expresses excellence; having fallen down with excellence — [that is] having bowed, having performed obeisance — this is the meaning. By the <s>ktvā</s> suffix, a prior action is expressed, as in 'having bathed, he eats.' The bathing-action [precedes], thereafter the eating-action. Similarly here too, after the act of bowing down, he sets forth mathematics, reckoning of time, and the sphere. <s>Ekam</s> (one) — established in the form of non-difference, without modification. <s>Anekam</s> — 'not one' [is] 'many,' established in the form of difference. <s>Kam</s> — 'Ka' is a name of <s>Prajāpati</s>. Having bowed to <s>Ka</s> who is distinguished by such qualities,

body.text:
atha yadi asau prajāpatiḥ ekaḥ katham asau anekaḥ? yadi asau anekaḥ katham ekaḥ? ekānekayoḥ parasparaviruddhayoḥ yugapat ekatra avasthānam na sambhavati, yathā atyantaviruddhayoḥ cchāyā ātapayoḥ uṣṇaśītayoḥ vā iti | atra ucyate ã yathā vṛkṣaḥ ekavasturūpeṇa [tiṣṭhati], asau eva yadā mūla-skandha-śākhā-prarohādiprapañcena vikalpyate tadā anekaḥ | evam asau api paramātmā nirvikāraḥ nirañjanaḥ ekaḥ eva, asau eva [yadā] anekaprāṇiśarīre vyavasthitaḥ
vikalpyate [tadā] anekaḥ | āha ca ã
body.translated_text: Now, if he is one <s>Prajāpati</s>, how is he many? If he is many, how is he one? The simultaneous existence in one [entity] of the mutually contradictory [properties of] oneness and manyness is not possible — just as [the co-existence] of the extremely contradictory shadow and sunlight, or of heat and cold. To this it is replied: Just as a tree [exists] in the form of a single entity, [but] that very [tree], when differentiated into the multiplicity of root, trunk, branches, shoots, and so on, is many — so too, that <s>Paramātmā</s> (Supreme Self), without modification, untainted, is one alone; that very [Self], when established in the bodies of many living beings, is differentiated [and thus becomes] many. And it is said:

children.text: ekaḥ eva hi bhūtātmā bhūte bhūte vyavasthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: The one Self of beings alone, established in each and every being,

children.text: ekadhā bahudhā ca eva dṛśyate jalacandravat ||
children.translated_text: is seen as one and as many, like the moon [reflected] in water.

body.text: amṛtabindūpaniṣat, śloí 12
body.translated_text: <s>Amṛtabindūpaniṣad</s>, verse 12

body.text: iti | athavā asau ekaḥ eva āsīt, tataḥ svayam ardhena puruṣaḥ abhavat ardhena nārī iti | tataḥ sarvān prāṇinaḥ asṛjat iti | athavā asau bhagavān prajāpatiḥ viśvarūpaḥ | tasmāt tasya viśvarūpatvāt ekānekatvam ekasmin yugapat sambhavati iti ayam adoṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: Or, he was one alone; then, with one half he became male and with the other half female; then he created all living beings. Or, that blessed <s>Prajāpati</s> is of universal form (<s>viśvarūpa</s>). Therefore, because of his universal form, the [simultaneous] oneness and manyness in a single [entity] is possible — and this is without fault.

body.text: satyām devatām | devaḥ eva devatā, satyā ca devatā ca | sa eva kaḥ satyatvena devatātvena ca viśiṣyate | kam satyām devatām praṇipatya | na kevalam satyatvena devatātvena ca viśeṣitaḥ | kena ca tarhi iti āha ã param brahma | param ca tat brahma param brahma | param śrūyate pulastya-pulaha-kratvādikam | evam asau bhagavān kaḥ, satyā devatā, param brahma ca | kam, satyām devatām, param brahma ca praṇipatya |
body.translated_text: 'The true deity' — <s>deva</s> (god) itself is <s>devatā</s> (deity); true and a deity. He, <s>Ka</s>, is distinguished by truthfulness and divinity. Having bowed to <s>Ka</s>, the true deity. Not only is he distinguished by truthfulness and divinity — by what else then? He says: 'The supreme <s>Brahman</s>.' Supreme and that is <s>Brahman</s> — [hence] the supreme <s>Brahman</s>. 'Supreme' refers to [those such as] <s>Pulastya</s>, <s>Pulaha</s>, <s>Kratu</s>, and others. Thus, that blessed one is <s>Ka</s>, the true deity, and the supreme <s>Brahman</s>. Having bowed to <s>Ka</s>, the true deity, and the supreme <s>Brahman</s>.

body.text:
atha katham kaḥ śabdaḥ pulliṅgaḥ, satyā devatā strīliṅgaḥ, param brahma napuṃsakaliṅgaḥ? taiḥ bhinnaliṅgaiḥ ekam vastu abhidhīyate | nanu ca atra sarvaiḥ eva śabdaiḥ ekaliṅgaiḥ bhavitavyam? na iti āha | ete śabdāḥ āviṣṭaliṅgāḥ | taiḥ āviṣṭaliṅgaiḥ śabdaiḥ ekam eva vastu abhibhīyate | yathā ã "kāraṇam iyam brāhmaṇī, bhūtam iyam brāhmaṇī, āvapanam iyam uṣṭrikā" iti [aṣṭādhyāyī aí 4, pādaḥ 1, sūtram 3, pātañjalamahābhāṣyam, ākṣepavārtikaḥ
5117]
body.translated_text: Now, how is it that the word '<s>Ka</s>' is masculine, 'true deity' (<s>satyā devatā</s>) is feminine, and 'supreme <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>param brahma</s>) is neuter? By these words of different genders, a single entity is designated. Should not all the words here be of a single gender? No — he says: These words have fixed genders. By these words with fixed genders, a single entity alone is designated. Just as: '<s>kāraṇam</s> (neuter) this <s>brāhmaṇī</s> (feminine), <s>bhūtam</s> (neuter) this <s>brāhmaṇī</s> (feminine), <s>āvapanam</s> (neuter) this <s>uṣṭrikā</s> (feminine).' [<s>Aṣṭādhyāyī</s> 4.1.3, <s>Patañjala Mahābhāṣya</s>, objection-<s>vārtika</s> 5117]

body.text:
athavā brahmaṇoḥ dvayoḥ apy ācāryeṇa praṇipātaḥ kṛtaḥ, śabdabrahmaṇaḥ parabrahmaṇaḥ ca | tayoḥ upavarṇanā iyam kriyate ã praṇipatya iti | nigadavyākhyānam evam ã ekam, parijñānataḥ tu tattvasya abhedarūpatvāt, yasmāt sarveṣu eva jñeyeṣu parijñānamātrasāmānyam ekam; anekam ṛgyajuḥsāmātharvetihāsapurāṇaśikṣākalpavyākaraṇaniruktachandovicitijyotiṣam iti ādiśabdarūpeṇa vyavasthitatvāt anekam | kaḥ iti śabdabrahmaṇaḥ ākhyānam | kam ekam anekam
praṇipatya | satyām devatām iti etat dvayoḥ brahmaṇoḥ śeṣaḥ, satyā devatā śabdabrahma | uktam ca ã
body.translated_text: Alternatively, the teacher performed obeisance to two <s>Brahmans</s> — to <s>Śabdabrahman</s> (the Brahman that is Word) and to <s>Parabrahman</s> (the Supreme Brahman). The description of those two is now given: 'Having bowed' — the word-by-word explanation is thus: <s>ekam</s> (one) — because, from the standpoint of complete knowledge, reality is of the nature of non-difference, since the generality of complete knowledge alone is one in all objects of knowledge; <s>anekam</s> (many) — because it is established in the form of many words such as <s>Ṛgveda</s>, <s>Yajurveda</s>, <s>Sāmaveda</s>, <s>Atharvaveda</s>, <s>Itihāsa</s>, <s>Purāṇa</s>, <s>Śikṣā</s>, <s>Kalpa</s>, <s>Vyākaraṇa</s>, <s>Nirukta</s>, <s>Chandoviciti</s>, and <s>Jyotiṣa</s>. '<s>Ka</s>' is the designation of <s>Śabdabrahman</s>. Having bowed to <s>Ka</s>, the one [and] many. 'The true deity' — this is a shared qualifier of both <s>Brahmans</s>; the true deity is <s>Śabdabrahman</s>. And it is said:

children.text: jñānāntarabhāvi yat ca hi phalam jñātvā kriyā ataḥ ca yat
children.translated_text: The result that follows from knowledge, and the action that follows from knowledge —
the certainty in the stability of knowledge is that it is the unfailing cause of everything.
And the knowable is immeasurable; scriptural and other <s>śāstras</s> (sciences), whose scope is limited, on the other hand —

children.text: divyam cakṣuḥ atīndriye api viṣaye vyāhanyate na kvacit ||
children.translated_text: [but] the divine eye is never obstructed even in the domain of the supersensuous.

body.text: param brahma | "param"-śabdaḥ prakarṣavācī | prakṛṣṭam brahma param brahma, yat sarvaiḥ api muktivādibhiḥ prārthyate, mokṣadaḥ paramātmā iti arthaḥ | evam ca dvayoḥ brahmaṇoḥ praṇāmaḥ kṛtaḥ | anyatra api "brahma"-śabdena śabdabrahma-parabrahmaṇoḥ eva grahaṇam | tad yathā ã
body.translated_text: 'The supreme <s>Brahman</s>' — the word 'supreme' (<s>param</s>) expresses excellence. The excellent <s>Brahman</s> is the supreme <s>Brahman</s> — that which is sought by all who advocate liberation, the <s>Paramātmā</s> (Supreme Self) who grants liberation — this is the meaning. And thus, obeisance has been made to the two <s>Brahmans</s>. Elsewhere too, by the word '<s>Brahman</s>,' only <s>Śabdabrahman</s> and <s>Parabrahman</s> are denoted. For instance:

children.text: dve brahmaṇī veditavye śabdabrahma param ca yat |
children.translated_text: Two <s>Brahmans</s> are to be known — <s>Śabdabrahman</s> (Word-<s>Brahman</s>) and the supreme [<s>Brahman</s>].
One who is accomplished in <s>Śabdabrahman</s> attains the supreme <s>Brahman</s>.

body.text: amṛtabindūpaniṣad, śloí 7; vāyupurāṇam, amśaḥ 6, aí 5, śloí 64
body.translated_text: <s>Amṛtabindūpaniṣad</s>, verse 7; <s>Vāyupurāṇa</s>, part 6, chapter 5, verse 64

body.text: iti |

athavā, praṇipatya kam hiraṇyagarbham, ekānekasvarūpam, sarvaprāṇinām mahat nāma | tatra viśeṣaḥ ekam, tasya tasya yataḥ adhiṣṭhātṛdevatā hiraṇyagarbhaḥ ekaḥ eva | yadā kāraṇānām adhiṣṭhātṛdevatāviśeṣabhedena vivakṣyate tadā anekam | tat yathā ã trayodaśa kāraṇāni, tvacaḥ vāyuḥ, cakṣuṣaḥ sūryaḥ, śrotrasyāḥ ākāśaḥ, rasanasyāḥ āpaḥ, ghrāṇasya pṛthivī, evam pañcānām buddhīndriyāṇām adhiṣṭhātryaḥ devatāḥ, vācaḥ agniḥ, pāṇeḥ indraḥ, pādasya
viṣṇuḥ, pāyunaḥ mitraḥ, upasthasya prajāpatiḥ, evam karmendriyādhiṣṭhātryaḥ devatāḥ, manasaḥ candraḥ, buddheḥ savitā, ahaṅkārasya rudraḥ iti | satyām devatām antaryāminaḥ īśvarasya bhagavataḥ paramātmanaḥ kāraṇaśaktyā adhiṣṭhitāḥ sarve eva padārthāḥ svārthe pravartante | ataḥ tām paramātmanaḥ kāraṇaśaktim satyām devatām | ataḥ eva strīliṅgena nirdeśaḥ kṛtaḥ | param brahma yat tat adhikārī brahma paramātmā tam | evam brahmatrayam praṇipatya
| yadi evam, cakāraḥ tarhi kartavyam | na kartavyam | antareṇa api cakāram ca arthaḥ gamyate eva | tat yathā ã
body.translated_text: Alternatively: having bowed to <s>Ka</s>, <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, whose nature is one-and-many, the great name of all living beings. Therein, the specification: 'one' — because the presiding deity of each [sense], <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, is one alone. When he is spoken of in terms of the specific divisions of presiding deities of the [various] causes, then he is 'many.' That is as follows: Thirteen causes — of the skin, <s>Vāyu</s> (Wind); of the eye, <s>Sūrya</s> (Sun); of the ear, <s>Ākāśa</s> (Space); of the tongue, <s>Āpas</s> (Water); of the nose, <s>Pṛthivī</s> (Earth) — thus the presiding deities of the five cognitive sense-organs; of speech, <s>Agni</s> (Fire); of the hand, <s>Indra</s>; of the foot, <s>Viṣṇu</s>; of the anus, <s>Mitra</s>; of the generative organ, <s>Prajāpati</s> — thus the presiding deities of the organs of action; of the mind, <s>Candra</s> (Moon); of the intellect, <s>Savitṛ</s> (Sun); of the ego, <s>Rudra</s>. 'The true deity' — all entities, presided over by the causal power of the inner controller (<s>antaryāmin</s>), the Lord, the blessed <s>Paramātmā</s>, function in their respective purposes. Therefore, that causal power of the <s>Paramātmā</s> is 'the true deity.' For this very reason, it is referred to in the feminine gender. 'The supreme <s>Brahman</s>' — that which is the presiding <s>Brahman</s>, the <s>Paramātmā</s>. Thus, having bowed to the triad of <s>Brahmans</s>. If so, then the conjunction '<s>ca</s>' (and) should have been used. It need not be used. Even without the conjunction '<s>ca</s>,' the meaning of 'and' is understood. For instance:

body.text: bāle vṛddhe kṣate kṣīṇe kṣīram yuktyā prayojayet |
body.translated_text: For a child, an elderly person, one who is wounded, and one who is emaciated, one should administer milk in the proper manner.

body.text: iti | bāle ca vṛddhe ca kṣate ca kṣīṇe ca iti gamyate | evam atra api ca arthaḥ, kam ca satyām devatām ca param brahma ca iti |
body.translated_text: This is understood as: for a child, and for an elderly person, and for one who is wounded, and for one who is emaciated. Similarly here too, the meaning of 'and' [is understood]: to <s>Ka</s>, and to the true deity, and to the supreme <s>Brahman</s>.

body.text:
āryabhaṭaḥ ācāryasya samākhyānaḥ | trīṇi gadati | trīṇi vastūni gadati iti | nanu atra evam yuktam vaktum ã "āryabhaṭaḥ aham trīṇi gadāmi" iti, anyathā anyasya kasyacit etat vākyam ābhāti | yathā kiṃcit kaścit pṛcchati ã "rājakule kena kim uktam iti āha ã evam ukte rājani evam devadatto bravīti | yajñadattaḥ api evam eva nigadati" iti | tasmāt tatra api āryabhaṭaḥ trīṇi gadati iti, na tat ācāryasya vacanam iti | atra ucyate | ayam ācāryaḥ mahānubhāvaḥ svayam
eva bruvan paratvam āpādya kathayati, yathā āha kauṭilyaḥ ã
body.translated_text: '<s>Āryabhaṭa</s>' is the proper name of the teacher. 'Sets forth three' — he sets forth three subjects. Now, it would be appropriate here to say: 'I, <s>Āryabhaṭa</s>, set forth three [subjects]' — otherwise this appears to be the statement of some other person. Just as when someone asks something in the royal court: 'Who said what?' — one replies: 'When the king said thus, <s>Devadatta</s> speaks thus. <s>Yajñadatta</s> too declares exactly thus.' Therefore, there too, '<s>Āryabhaṭa</s> sets forth three' is not the teacher's own statement. To this it is replied: This teacher, being a person of great eminence, speaks of himself by adopting the third person, just as <s>Kauṭilya</s> says:

children.translated_text: Easy to grasp, to be known through its principles, with its meanings and words well-determined,
this <s>śāstra</s> (science) was composed by <s>Kauṭilya</s>, discarding prolixity of composition.

body.text: arthaśāstram, 1.1.19
body.translated_text: <s>Arthaśāstra</s>, 1.1.19

body.text: iti | athavā yaḥ tejasvī puruṣaḥ samareṣu nikṛṣṭāsitejovitānacchuritabāhuḥ śatrusaṅghātam prakāśam praviśya praharan evam āha ã "ayam asau uditaḥ aditikulaprasūtaḥ samareṣu anivāritavīryaḥ yajñadattaḥ praharati | yadi kasyacit śaktiḥ pratipraharatu" iti | evam asau api ācāryaḥ gaṇitakālakriyāgolātiśayajñānodadhipāragaḥ vitsabhām avagāhya "āryabhaṭaḥ trīṇi gadati gaṇitam kālakriyām golam" iti uktavān |
body.translated_text: Or, just as a valiant warrior in battles — his arms flashing with the splendor of drawn swords — entering openly into the mass of enemies and striking, declares thus: 'This is that <s>Yajñadatta</s>, risen, born of the lineage of <s>Aditi</s>, of unobstructed valor in battles — he strikes! If anyone has the power, let him strike back!' — so too, this teacher, having crossed over the ocean of supreme knowledge of mathematics, reckoning of time, and the sphere, entering the assembly of the learned, declared: '<s>Āryabhaṭa</s> sets forth three [subjects] — mathematics, reckoning of time, and the sphere.'

body.text:
gaṇitam kālakriyām golam | gaṇitam, kṣetracchāyāśreḍhīsamakaraṇakuṭṭākārādikam | kālaḥ, prāṇavināḍīnāḍyahorātrapakṣamāsasaṃvatsarayugādikam | tatparijñānārtham kriyā kālakriyā | anye punaḥ kriyā avyatiriktam kālam etena abhyupagacchanti | teṣām ayam vigrahaḥ ã kālaḥ ca asau kriyā ca kālakriyā | evam etau dvau pakṣau ã kecit kālam kriyāvyatiriktam manyante, anye kriyā eva kālaḥ iti | ubhayathāḥ asmākam adoṣaḥ iti, yena asmadīye siddhānte
sūryodayāt prabhṛti yāvat aparaḥ sūryodayaḥ tāvat ahorātram, yaḥ ca sūryācandramasoḥ paraḥ viprakarṣaḥ saḥ ardhamāsaḥ, yaḥ ca tayoḥ paraḥ sannikarṣaḥ sa māsaḥ; evam dvādaśamāsāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ iti ayam kālaḥ, kriyāvyatiriktaḥ vā astu kriyā vā iti | golam, grahabhramaṇadharitrīsaṃsthānadarśanopāyam | gadati iti kartṛvācakaḥ śabdaḥ, vākyatvāt | gaṇitakālakriyāgolānām dvitīyaikavacane nirdeśaḥ gaṇitam kālakriyām golam iti gaṇitaśabdaḥ napuṃsakaliṅgam, kālakriyā
strīliṅgam, golaḥ pulliṅgam | eteṣām sāmānyopakrameṇa napuṃsakaliṅgena eva ācāryeṇa abhidhānam [kṛtam] "trīṇi gadati" iti |
body.translated_text: 'Mathematics, reckoning of time, the sphere.' Mathematics (<s>gaṇita</s>) — [including] area calculations, shadow [problems], series, equations, <s>kuṭṭākāra</s> (pulverizer method), and the like. Time (<s>kāla</s>) — <s>prāṇa</s> (breaths), <s>vināḍī</s> (sub-divisions), <s>nāḍī</s> (time-divisions), day-and-night, fortnight, month, year, <s>yuga</s> (age), and the like. The operation [of determining] that is 'reckoning of time' (<s>kālakriyā</s>). Others, however, consider time as not different from action; for them, the compound analysis is: time itself being action, [it is] <s>kālakriyā</s>. Thus, there are these two positions: some consider time as different from action, others [hold that] action alone is time. In either case, there is no fault for us, since in our <s>siddhānta</s> (established system), from one sunrise until the next sunrise is a day-and-night; the maximum distance between the sun and the moon is a half-month; and their maximum proximity is a month; thus, twelve months is a year — this is time, whether it be different from action or identical with it. The sphere (<s>gola</s>) — the means for observing the configuration of the earth and the revolution of the planets. '<s>Gadati</s>' (sets forth) is a word denoting an agent, because of its sentence-nature. The references to mathematics, reckoning of time, and the sphere are in the accusative singular: <s>gaṇitam</s> (neuter), <s>kālakriyām</s> (feminine), <s>golam</s> (masculine). These [subjects], through a generic approach, were designated by the teacher in the neuter gender alone as 'three' (<s>trīṇi gadati</s>).

body.text:
atra ayam gaṇitaśabdaḥ aśeṣagaṇitābhidhāyī, tasmāt aśeṣagaṇitābhidhāyitvāt yathā kṣetragaṇitam bravīti, evam grahagaṇitam api; grahagaṇitasya ca kṣetrādyavyatiriktatvāt kālakriyāgolayoḥ ca gaṇitāvyatiriktatvāt gaṇitam nigadati iti etāvat eva siddhe kālakriyāgolagrahaṇam kurvan ācāryaḥ jñāpayati ã kṣetracchāyāśreḍhīsamakaraṇakuṭṭākārādikam sāmānyagaṇitam kiṃcit vakṣye, viśeṣagaṇite punaḥ kālakriyayā golena tātparyam iti | anyathā
aśeṣagaṇitābhidhāyigaṇitaśabdena eva siddhatvāt kālakriyāgolayoḥ pṛthaggrahaṇam anāvaśyakam syāt | tathā ca, ācāryeṇa gaṇitapāde gaṇitavastu diṅmātram eva abhihitam, kālakriyāgolayoḥ kālakriyāgola [vastu] viśeṣeṇa | avaśyam ayam arthaḥ abhyupagantavyaḥ ã kiṃcit gaṇitam iti / anyathā hi mahat gaṇitavastu, aṣṭau vyavahārāḥ miśraka-śreḍhī-kṣetra-khāta-citi-krākacika-rāśi-cchāyābhidhāyinaḥ | miśrakaḥ iti sakalagaṇitavastusaṃmiśrakaḥ saṃsparśakaḥ iti arthaḥ
| śreḍhī iti ādyuttarapracitaḥ iti arthaḥ | kṣetram iti anekāśrikṣetraphalāni ānayati iti arthaḥ | khātaḥ iti khanyapramāṇam nirdiśati iti arthaḥ | citiḥ iti iṣṭakāpramāṇena uparinicitavastupramāṇam āvedayati iti arthaḥ | krākacikam iti, krakacaḥ nama dārucchedakam, tasmin krakace bhavaḥ krākacikaḥ, tadvastupramāṇam avagamayati iti arthaḥ | rāśiḥ iti dhānyādirūpavastunicitam tadvastupramāṇam janayati iti arthaḥ | chāyā iti śaṅkvādicchāyāpramāṇena kālam kathayati
iti arthaḥ | iti vyavahāragaṇitasya aṣṭābhidhāyinaḥ catvāri bījāni prathamadvitīyatṛtīyacaturthāni yāvat tāvat vargāvargaghanāghanaviṣamāṇi | etat ekaikasya granthalakṣaṇalakṣyam maskari-pūraṇa-mudgala-prabhṛtibhiḥ ācāryaiḥ nibaddham kṛtam, sa katham anena ācāryeṇa alpena granthena śakyate vaktum | tat suṣṭhu uktam asmābhiḥ kiṃcit gaṇitam viśeṣataḥ kālagolau iti | evam iyam āryā vyākhyātā || 1||
body.translated_text: Here, the word '<s>gaṇita</s>' (mathematics/computation) denotes the entirety of mathematics. Therefore, since it denotes the entirety of mathematics, just as it speaks of area-computation (<s>kṣetragaṇita</s>), so too [it speaks of] planetary computation (<s>grahagaṇita</s>). And since planetary computation is not separate from area-computation and the like, and since time-reckoning (<s>kālakriyā</s>) and the sphere (<s>gola</s>) are not separate from computation, in separately mentioning <s>kālakriyā</s> and <s>gola</s> when this much is already established [by the word '<s>gaṇita</s>' alone], the master (<s>ācārya</s>) indicates: 'I shall state some general mathematics — area, shadow, series, equalization, <s>kuṭṭākāra</s> (pulverizer), and so forth — but in specialized mathematics, the emphasis is on time-reckoning and the sphere.' Otherwise, since [everything] is already established by the word '<s>gaṇita</s>' which denotes the entirety of mathematics, the separate mention of <s>kālakriyā</s> and <s>gola</s> would be unnecessary. And accordingly, in the mathematics chapter (<s>gaṇitapāda</s>), the master has stated mathematical content in outline only, while in <s>kālakriyā</s> and <s>gola</s>, [he has stated] the content of time-reckoning and the sphere in detail. This meaning must necessarily be accepted: 'some mathematics.' For otherwise, the body of mathematical knowledge is vast — the eight operations (<s>vyavahāras</s>), designated as <s>miśraka</s> (mixture), <s>śreḍhī</s> (series), <s>kṣetra</s> (area), <s>khāta</s> (excavation), <s>citi</s> (pile), <s>krākacika</s> (saw-cut), <s>rāśi</s> (heap), and <s>chāyā</s> (shadow). <s>Miśraka</s> means: mixed with all mathematical subjects, i.e., 'combination' — this is the meaning. <s>Śreḍhī</s> means: accumulated with a first [term] and a common difference — this is the meaning. <s>Kṣetra</s> means: it derives the areas of polygonal figures — this is the meaning. <s>Khāta</s> means: it indicates the measure of what is to be excavated — this is the meaning. <s>Citi</s> means: it reports the measure of a substance piled up above with bricks of a given measure — this is the meaning. <s>Krākacika</s> — <s>krakaca</s> means a wood-cutting [saw]; what pertains to that saw is <s>krākacika</s>; it makes known the measure of that substance — this is the meaning. <s>Rāśi</s> means: a pile of substance in the form of grain and the like; it yields the measure of that substance — this is the meaning. <s>Chāyā</s> means: it tells the time by the measure of the shadow of a gnomon (<s>śaṅku</s>) and the like — this is the meaning. Thus, of the applied mathematics (<s>vyavahāragaṇita</s>) comprising these eight [topics], the four seeds (<s>bījas</s>) — first, second, third, and fourth — are the [operations involving] squares, non-squares, cubes, non-cubes, and unknowns. This [body of knowledge], each topic having the characteristics of a full treatise, has been composed by teachers such as <s>Maskari</s>, <s>Pūraṇa</s>, <s>Mudgala</s>, and others — how then can it be stated by this master in a brief text? Therefore, it is well said by us: 'some mathematics, with emphasis on time and sphere.' Thus this <s>āryā</s> verse has been explained. (1)

body.text: saṃkhyāvinyāse paribhāṣā
body.translated_text: Definition regarding the arrangement of numerals

body.text: yugabhagaṇādisaṅkhyāsaṃkṣepam vivakṣuḥ ācāryaḥ [pari]bhāṣāsūtrapradarśanāya gītikāsūtram āha ã
body.translated_text: The master (<s>ācārya</s>), wishing to concisely [express] the numbers of revolutions in a <s>yuga</s> (cosmic age) and the like, states the <s>gītikā</s>-sūtra for the purpose of presenting the definitional rule (<s>paribhāṣā</s>):

children.text: vargākṣarāṇi varge avarge avargākṣarāṇi kāt ṅmau yaḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>varga</s>-letters (consonants of the classified groups) [are placed] in the <s>varga</s> (odd) [places], and the <s>avarga</s>-letters (unclassified consonants) in the <s>avarga</s> (even) [places], starting from <s>ka</s>; <s>ṅa</s> and <s>ma</s> [together equal] <s>ya</s>;

children.text: khadvinavake svarāḥ nava varge avarge navānti avarge vā || 2 ||
children.translated_text: the nine vowels [are placed] in two nines of places starting from the void (<s>kha</s>); [they apply to] nine [places] in the <s>varga</s> [position] and nine ending in the <s>avarga</s> [position], or [nine ending] in the <s>avarga</s> [position]. (2)

body.text: asya gītisūtrasya padāni ã vargākṣarāṇi, varge, avarge, avargākṣarāṇi, kāt, ṅmau, yaḥ, khadvinavake, svarāḥ, nava, varge, avarge, nava, atyantavarge, vā |
body.translated_text: The words of this <s>gītikā</s>-sūtra are: <s>vargākṣarāṇi</s> (classified-group letters), <s>varge</s> (in the odd place), <s>avarge</s> (in the even place), <s>avargākṣarāṇi</s> (unclassified letters), <s>kāt</s> (starting from <s>ka</s>), <s>ṅmau</s> (<s>ṅa</s> and <s>ma</s>), <s>yaḥ</s> (<s>ya</s>), <s>khadvinavake</s> (in two nines of places), <s>svarāḥ</s> (vowels), <s>nava</s> (nine), <s>varge</s> (in the odd place), <s>avarge</s> (in the even place), <s>nava</s> (nine), <s>atyantavarge</s> (ending in the odd place), <s>vā</s> (or).

body.text:
vargākṣarāṇi, vargākṣarāṇi kakārādīni makāraparyantāni | "te vargāḥ pañca pañca" iti [kātantram, 1.1.10 ] | vargākṣaroccāraṇakrameṇa yā saṅkhyā abhidhīyate sā saṅkhyā vargaśabdena ucyate, abhedopacārāt | ataḥ vargākṣarasaṅkhyā iti arthaḥ | sā varge, varge iti gaṇitaśāstre viṣamasthānasyāḥ ākhyā, tasmin viṣamasthāne vargākṣarasaṅkhyā upacīyate | avarge, na vargaḥ avargaḥ samasthānaḥ, tasmin avargasaṃjñite samasthāne | avargākṣarāṇi, tāni yakārādīni
hakāraparyavasānāni | kutaḥ etat? "nañ iva yuktam anyasadṛśādhikaraṇe tathā hy arthagatiḥ" [aṣṭādhyāyī, 3.1.12, pātañjalabhāṣyam] iti | vargākṣarāṇi kakārādīni |
body.translated_text: <s>Vargākṣarāṇi</s> (classified-group letters) — the classified-group letters are those from <s>ka</s> to <s>ma</s>. [As stated:] 'Those five groups of five' [<s>Kātantra</s> 1.1.10]. The number that is denoted by the sequential order of uttering the classified-group letters is called by the word '<s>varga</s>' (square), by the figure of speech of non-differentiation. Hence the meaning is: the number of the classified-group letter. That [number is placed] 'in the <s>varga</s> [place]' — in mathematical science, the designation of the odd place is '<s>varga</s>'; in that odd place the classified-group letter number is accumulated. '<s>Avarge</s>' (in the even place) — what is not <s>varga</s> is <s>avarga</s>, i.e., the even place; in that place designated <s>avarga</s>, i.e., the even place. <s>Avargākṣarāṇi</s> (unclassified letters) — those are from <s>ya</s> to <s>ha</s>. Whence is this [known]? [From the principle:] 'Like [the prefix] <s>nañ</s>, [the negative is] appropriate when [the referent] is similar in substrate to what is [positively] denoted — for thus the meaning is understood' [<s>Aṣṭādhyāyī</s> 3.1.12, <s>Pātañjala Bhāṣya</s>]. The classified-group letters are those from <s>ka</s> and following.

body.text:
yādīnām [tu] yathā abrāhmaṇam ānaya iti ukte brāhmaṇākṛtitulyam eva kṣatriyam ānayati nāntyajādi, evam atra api kevalam vyañjanānām eva grahaṇam | teṣām yakārādīnām avargākṣarāṇām yā saṅkhyā sā avargasthāne upacīyate | sā [vargākṣarāṇām saṅkhyā] vargasthāne upacīyamānā avargasthānam api yadā prāpnoti, tadā prāpnuvānā yā teṣām svavargākṣarāṇām upacitiḥ sā vargasthānaḥ eva, tasyāḥ antyopacititvāt | vargākṣarasaṅkhyāyāḥ vargasthāne
upacīyamānāt avakāśaḥ na asti cet saṅkhyāyāḥ sargaḥ na vidyate iti vargāvargayoḥ sthānayoḥ sthāpyate | athavā, yā daśādikā saṅkhyā sā dvisthānāvagāhinī, tasyāḥ dvisthānāvagāhanaśīlatvāt dvayoḥ api sthānayoḥ sthāpyate | anyathā daśādisaṅkhyāyāḥ abhāvaḥ eva syāt | tad ekādinavāntasaṅkhyayā eva vyavahāraḥ syāt |
body.translated_text: As for [the letters] from <s>ya</s> onward — just as when one says 'bring a non-Brahmin,' one brings a <s>kṣatriya</s> who is similar in form to a Brahmin, not an outcaste and such, similarly here too, only consonants [are taken]. Of those unclassified letters from <s>ya</s> onward, their number is accumulated in the <s>avarga</s> (even) place. When that [number of classified-group letters], being accumulated in the <s>varga</s> (odd) place, also reaches the <s>avarga</s> (even) place, then whatever accumulation of their own classified-group letters [extends into the even place], that [accumulation] belongs to the <s>varga</s> (odd) place only, because it is the final accumulation [of that number]. If there is no room for the number being accumulated in the <s>varga</s> place of the classified-group letter number, and [if the next position] does not exist for that number, then it is placed in both positions — the <s>varga</s> and the <s>avarga</s>. Alternatively, a number of ten and above occupies two places; because of its nature of occupying two places, it is placed in both places. Otherwise, numbers of ten and above would simply not exist — and computation would proceed only with numbers from one to nine.

body.text:
athavā "ṅmau" iti atra makāragrahaṇam kurvan ācāryaḥ jñāpayati ã yā daśottaravargākṣarasaṅkhyā sā varge vā avarge ca bhavati | anyathā "go yaḥ" iti evam brūyāt | evam avargākṣarasaṅkhyā api vargashāne yojyā | vargākṣarāṇām saṅkhyā vargasthāne kakārād upacīyate | etat uktam bhavati ã yāni vargākṣarāṇi śrūyate tāni kakārāt prabhṛti paṭhitāni bhavanti iti | anyathā hi "svam rūpam śabdasya aśabdasaṃjñā" [aṣṭādhyāyī, 1.2.68] iti | yat yat akṣaram
uccāritam tat tasya eva rūpasya pratipādakam syāt, na kādisaṅkhyāyāḥ | ataḥ uktam "kāt" iti |
body.translated_text: Alternatively, by making the inclusion of <s>ma</s> in '<s>ṅmau</s>,' the master indicates that the classified-group letter number of ten and above can occur either in the <s>varga</s> or in the <s>avarga</s> [place]. Otherwise, he would have said '<s>go yaḥ</s>' [instead]. Similarly, the unclassified-letter number too should be applied in the <s>varga</s> place. The number of the classified-group letters is accumulated in the <s>varga</s> place starting from <s>ka</s>. This is what is being said: whatever classified-group letters are heard, they are read starting from <s>ka</s>. For otherwise, [by the rule] 'the own form of a word is its designation when it is not a technical term' [<s>Aṣṭādhyāyī</s> 1.2.68], whatever letter is uttered would be indicative of its own form only, not of the number [in the system] starting from <s>ka</s>. Therefore it is said '<s>kāt</s>' (starting from <s>ka</s>).

body.text:
ṅmau, ṅaḥ ca maḥ ca ṅmau | anackau eva ṅakāramakārau, tayoḥ dvi[vaca]nanirdeśaḥ ṅmau | ṅakāramakārayoḥ yā saṅkhyā sā ekatra saṃvṛttā yakārasaṅkhyā bhavati | ṅakāraḥ pañca, makāraḥ pañcaviṃśatiḥ, ete saṅkhye ekatra triṃśat, tena triṃśatsaṃkhyo yakāraḥ | rephādīnām avargākṣaratvāt yakārasaṅkhyā eva kevalam prāpnoti, anirdeśāt anyatsaṅkhyāyāḥ | na rephādīnām yakārasaṅkhyā | kutaḥ? yadi rephādīnām api yakārasaṅkhyā eva syāt tadā yakāram
eva sarvatra brūyāt, na rephādīni | "navarāṣahaḥ gatvāṃśakān prathamapātāḥ" iti atra [rā]ṣaheṣu ekam eva avargākṣaram brūyāt | tasmāt na rephādīnām yakārasaṅkhyā | kā tarhi? kecit āhuḥ ã ekaikavṛddhyā rephādīnām saṅkhyā, yakāratriṃśat, rakāraḥ ekatriṃśat, lakāraḥ dvātriṃśat iti ādi | etat na | kutaḥ? ekatriṃśadādisaṅkhyāyāḥ anyena eva prakāreṇa siddhatvāt | yakāraḥ triṃśat, sa eva yadā yakāraḥ kakārasaṃyuktaḥ tadā hi ekatriṃśat, khakārādibhiḥ dvātriṃśat,
trayaḥ triṃśat ādiḥ iti saṅkhyā |
body.translated_text: <s>Ṅmau</s> — <s>ṅa</s> and <s>ma</s> [together are called] <s>ṅmau</s>. The letters <s>ṅa</s> and <s>ma</s>, being without a vowel, are stated in the dual; [that is] <s>ṅmau</s>. The number of <s>ṅa</s> and <s>ma</s>, when combined into one, becomes the number of <s>ya</s>. <s>Ṅa</s> is five, <s>ma</s> is twenty-five; these numbers combined into one make thirty — hence <s>ya</s> has the number thirty. Since <s>ra</s> and the following are unclassified letters, only the number of <s>ya</s> would be obtainable [for them], since no other number is specified. But <s>ra</s> and the following do not have the number of <s>ya</s>. Why? If <s>ra</s> and the following also had the number of <s>ya</s>, then one would always say <s>ya</s> everywhere, not <s>ra</s> and the others. In [the expression] '<s>navarāṣahaḥ gatvāṃśakān prathamapātāḥ</s>,' one would use only one unclassified letter among <s>ra</s>, <s>ṣa</s>, and <s>ha</s>. Therefore, <s>ra</s> and the following do not have the number of <s>ya</s>. What then? Some say: by increments of one, <s>ra</s> and the following have [their] numbers — <s>ya</s> is thirty, <s>ra</s> is thirty-one, <s>la</s> is thirty-two, and so forth. This is not [correct]. Why? Because numbers like thirty-one and above are already obtainable by another method. <s>Ya</s> is thirty; when that <s>ya</s> is conjoined with <s>ka</s>, it becomes thirty-one; with <s>kha</s> and following, thirty-two, thirty-three, and so on — [these] numbers [are obtained].

body.text:
anye āhuḥ ã rephādayaḥ daśottaravṛddhyā vardhante iti, rephaḥ catvāriṃśat, lakāraḥ pañcāśat | evam avargākṣarābhāvāt na śakyate pratipattum | yathā kāt iti ācāryeṇa abhihitatvāt ekādyekottaritā saṅkhyā vargākṣarāṇām pratipadyate, evam avargākṣarāṇām api yāt iti yadā ucyate tadā daśottaritā saṅkhyā pratipattum śakyate | anyathā "yāt" iti api ucyamāne katham daśottaritā saṅkhyā, nanu ca ekottaritā syāt | na iti āha ã yasmāt kāt iti [vargākṣarāṇi]
vargasthāne upacīyante tasmāt teṣām ekottaritā saṅkhyā, yāni punar avargākṣarāṇi yādīni ekottaropacayāni avargasthāne tasmāt daśottaritā eva vṛddhiḥ bhavati, avargasthānasya daśakasaṅkhyādhāratvāt | evam tarhi yādgrahaṇam kartavyam | na kartavyam | katham? akriyamāṇe ayam arthaḥ avagamyate | akṛtam eva yadi kṛtam eva, kim iti na paṭhyate? paṭhyate eva "ṅmau yaḥ" | atra ayam yakāraḥ anackaḥ ṅmau yaḥ, aparaḥ yakāraḥ api anackaḥ evam pañcamīvibhaktyantaḥ
ṅmau yaḥ | atra ekaḥ yakāraḥ luptanirdiṣṭaḥ pratipattavyaḥ | yathā "kṅiti ca" [aṣṭādhyāyī, 1.1.5] iti atra luptanirdiṣṭaḥ gakāraḥ, kiti giti ṅiti iti, evam atra api | athavā dviyakāroccāraṇe api viśeṣaḥ na asti eva | evam yād iti asya ayam arthaḥ siddhaḥ | yadi ekottarāṇi avargashānasthitatvāt daśottarāṇi eva bhavanti tadā kim iti ācāryeṇa "ṅmau yaḥ" iti mahāprayāsaḥ kṛtaḥ | katham tarhi vaktavyaḥ? "gaḥ yaḥ" iti gakāraḥ trisaṅkhyaḥ, avargasthānasthitatvāt eva ayam triṃśatkaḥ
bhaviṣyati | na, ṅakāramakārasaṅkhyāvat eva śeṣāṇi api rephādīni catvāriṃśadādisaṅkhāni bhavanti iti avargasthānāśrayāt eva siddhe sati ṅmakāragrahaṇam kurvan ācāryaḥ jñāpayati iti uktam ã yāvanti vargasthānāni teṣu sarveṣu eva sā saṅkhyā yugapat prāptā, avargākṣarāṇām ca yā saṅkhyā yāvanti avargasthānāni teṣu sarveṣu eva |
body.translated_text: Others say: <s>ra</s> and the following increase by increments of ten — <s>ra</s> is forty, <s>la</s> is fifty. Similarly, [higher numbers] cannot be understood because of the absence of [further] unclassified letters. Just as, because the master has stated '<s>kāt</s>' (starting from <s>ka</s>), the numbers of the classified-group letters are understood as increasing by one from [<s>ka</s> onward], similarly, when '<s>yāt</s>' is stated for the unclassified letters, numbers increasing by ten can be understood. Otherwise, even when '<s>yāt</s>' is stated, how [would one know of] the increment by ten — would it not be by one? No, he says: since the classified-group letters are accumulated in the <s>varga</s> (odd) place starting from <s>ka</s>, their numbers increase by one; but the unclassified letters from <s>ya</s> onward, which accumulate by increments of one in the <s>avarga</s> (even) place — therefore the increment is by ten only, since the <s>avarga</s> place carries [multiples of] ten. If so, then '<s>yāt</s>' should be explicitly stated. It need not be stated. How? Even without stating it, this meaning is understood. If it is understood even without being stated, then even if stated, why is it not read [explicitly]? It is read — '<s>ṅmau yaḥ</s>.' Here, this <s>ya</s> without a vowel [means] '<s>ṅmau yaḥ</s>'; the other <s>ya</s>, also without a vowel, [is to be understood as] in the fifth case (ablative) — '<s>ṅmau yaḥ</s>.' Here, one <s>ya</s> must be understood as indicated by elision (<s>luptanirdiṣṭa</s>). Just as in [the rule] '<s>kṅiti ca</s>' [<s>Aṣṭādhyāyī</s> 1.1.5], the <s>ga</s> is indicated by elision — meaning 'in <s>ki</s>, <s>gi</s>, <s>ṅi</s>' — so too here. Alternatively, even with the utterance of two <s>ya</s>s, there is no [real] difference. Thus the meaning of '<s>yāt</s>' is established. If [it is asked:] when the [numbers] increasing by one become increasing by ten because of being in the <s>avarga</s> place, then why did the master go to the great effort of stating '<s>ṅmau yaḥ</s>'? How then should it be stated? '<s>gaḥ yaḥ</s>' — <s>ga</s> has the number three; because of being in the <s>avarga</s> place, it would become thirty. No — the remaining [letters] <s>ra</s> and the following would also have numbers of forty and above, just like the numbers of <s>ṅa</s> and <s>ma</s>. Since this is already established from the <s>avarga</s> place itself, the master, by including <s>ṅa</s> and <s>ma</s>, indicates — as has been said: whatever [number of] <s>varga</s> places there are, in all of them that number applies simultaneously; and whatever number belongs to the unclassified letters, [it applies] in all the <s>avarga</s> places.

body.text:
ataḥ tatsaṅkhyānirūpaṇārtham āha ã khadvinavake svarāḥ nava varge avarge | khāni śanyāni, khānam dvinavakam khadvinavakam, tasmin khadvinavake, aṣṭādaśasu śūnyopalakṣiteṣu [sthāneṣu] | svarāḥ nava varge avarge | varge vargasthāne nava svarāḥ | aṣṭādaśasu ca sthāneṣu nava vargasthānāni, tatra navasu vargasthāneṣu nava svarāḥ | ke punar te nava svarāḥ grāhyāḥ? yadi hrasvāḥ eva kevalam parigṛhyante tadā na pūryante | atha dīrghāḥ eva kevalam
parigṛhyante tadā api aṣṭau svarāḥ bhavanti, nanu lṛvarṇasya dīrghābhāvāt | atha hrasvāḥ dīrghaḥ ca parigṛhyante tadā atiricyante, aniṣṭam prāpnoti | "jhā gḍa glā rdha dḍa" [gītikāí, 10] iti atra ākārasya dvitīye ca pratipāditatvāt dvitīyavargasthāne jhakārasaṅkhyā sthāpyamānā navaśatāni syuḥ, na nava | abhīṣyate ca navasaṅkhyā, navasaṅkhyākaḥ jhakāraḥ | tatra hrasvaḥ eva jhakāraḥ paṭhyate iti cet "nṛṣi yojanam ñilā bhūvyāsaḥ" [gītikāí, 6] iti atra lakāre pañcasahasrāṇi
syuḥ, na pañcāśat | tatra ca avaśyam dīrghaḥ lakāraḥ paṭhitavyaḥ, anyathā gītiḥ eva bhidyeta | ataḥ na kevalam hrasvāḥ na kevalam dīrghāḥ, na api hrasvadīrghāḥ, na svarāḥ mātṛkāpaṭhitāt parigṛhyante | kasmāt tarhi svarāḥ parigṛhītavyāḥ? ucyate ã yatra nava eva kevalāḥ svarāḥ paṭhyante, tasmāt parigṛhītavyāḥ | kasmin nava eva kevalāḥ paṭhyante? āha ã pāṇinīye vyākaraṇe pratyāhāre a i u ṛ ḷ e o ai au iti ete nava svarāḥ | tatra prathame vargasthāne akāraḥ, dvitīye
ikāraḥ, tṛtīye ukāraḥ, iti ādi | evam svaropalakṣiteṣu vargasthāneṣu vargākṣarasaṅkhyā | avargākṣarasaṅkhyā ca svaropalakṣitavargasthānottare avargasthāne |
body.translated_text: Therefore, for the purpose of determining that number, he says: 'The nine vowels in the two nines of voids, in <s>varga</s> and <s>avarga</s>.' The voids (<s>kha</s>) are zeros (<s>śūnya</s>); the two nines of voids (<s>khadvinavaka</s>) [means] in those eighteen places of zeros...

body.text:
athavā varge avarge iti ayam vīpsā, varge avarge ca, vargasthāne avargasthāne ca te eva nava svarāḥ | tad yathā ã akāraḥ prathame vargasthāne tadanantarāvargasthāne ca | tad yadi vargākṣarasaṃyuktaḥ akāraḥ prathamavargasthāne "bhṛgubudha" iti ādiṣu, sa eva yadā avargākṣarasaṃyuktaḥ tadā tatprathamavargasthānānantarāvargasthāne "navarāṣaha" iti ādiṣu | evam ikārādiṣu api sveṣu vargāvargasthāneṣu yojyam | atha dīrgheṣu akārādiṣu katham karaṇīyam?
ucyate ã yathā te vyākaraṇe akārādayaḥ svarāḥ aṣṭādaśaprabhedāḥ, dvādaśa bhedāḥ ca lṛvarṇasandhisvarāḥ parigṛhyante, evam atra api | tena "ñilā bhūvyāsa" iti ādiṣu ākāraḥ prathamaḥ eva vargasthāneṣu | aṣṭādaśasthāneṣu yāni vargasthānāni avargasthānāni ca teṣu vargākṣarāvargākṣarasaṅkhyā nirūpitā |
body.translated_text: Alternatively, '<s>varga</s> and <s>avarga</s>' is a distributive expression (<s>vīpsā</s>) — in the <s>varga</s>-place and in the <s>avarga</s>-place, those same nine vowels [are used]. That is as follows: the letter 'a' in the first <s>varga</s>-place and in the <s>avarga</s>-place immediately following it...

body.text:
yadā punar aṣṭādaśavyatirikteṣu sthāneṣu saṅkhyā kasyacit vivakṣitā bhavati tadā katham karaṇīyam iti? atra āha ã navāntyavarge vā | navānām antaḥ navāntaḥ | navānte bhavam navāntyam | navāntyaḥ ca asau vargaḥ ca navāntyavargaḥ | tasmin navāntyavarge vā svarāḥ bhavanti, vikalpitāḥ svarāḥ bhavanti | vikalpaḥ ca kasmiṃśit katham upalakṣyate? yathā "putracchedyavikalpā apatyacchedyaprakārāḥ", evam atra api kenacit prakāreṇa vikalpitāḥ navātyavarge
daśame vargasthāne svarāḥ bhavanti | yadi prathame vargasthāne akāraḥ śuddhaḥ vikalpitaḥ sa eva tasmāt vargasthānāt daśame vargasthāne anusvārādinā vikalpyate, evam ikārādayaḥ svasmāt vargasthānāt daśame vargasthāne, punar api ca yāvat abhīṣṭam bhavati tāvat tena api anubandhena svarān vikalpya saṅkhyopadeṣṭavyā | etat paribhāṣābījam ācāryeṇa saṅkhyāvivakṣūṇām anugrahāya upadiṣṭam | svaśāstravyavahāraḥ tu lṛvarṇavargasthānāt na atiricyate |
body.translated_text: But when a number is intended by someone in places beyond the eighteen, then how should it be done? Here he says: '<s>navāntyavarge vā</s>' (or [the nine] at the end of a <s>varga</s>). The end of the nine is <s>navānta</s>...

body.text:
vargākṣarāṇām avargākṣarāṇām ca [yā] saṅkhyā sā akṣarābhihitatvāt yāvanti vakṣyamāṇāni gītikāsūtreṣu akṣarāṇi teṣām sarveṣām eva prāpnoti tat ca aniṣṭam prasajyeta, tena atra arthavanti yāni akṣarāṇi teṣām saṅkhyā na bhavet iti etat vaktavyam | yathā ã "yugaravibhagaṇāḥ khyughṛ" [gītikā í, 3] iti atra khyughṛ-śabdasya saṅkhyā iṣyate na yugaravibhagaṇaśabdasya | yadi pratiṣedhaḥ na ucate tadā khyughṛ-śabdasya yathā saṅkhyā evam yugaravibhagaṇaśabdasya
api prāpnoti | sa tarhi pratiṣedhaḥ avaśyam vaktavyaḥ | na vaktavyaḥ | yadi sarveṣām eva akṣarāṇām gītikāsūtrapratibaddhānām saṅkhyā syāt tadā sarvam eva etat śāstram anarthakam syāt |
body.translated_text: The number of the <s>varga</s>-letters and <s>avarga</s>-letters — since it is expressed by letters — extends to all the letters that will be mentioned in the <s>gītikā</s>-sūtras. And that undesired consequence would follow...

body.text: jyotiṣaśāstraprādurbhāve vyākhyākāramatam
body.translated_text: The commentator's view on the origin of the science of astronomy

body.text: atha katham asya atīndriyāṇām sphuṭagrahagatyarthānām prādurbhāvaḥ? brahmaṇaḥ prasādena iti | evam anuśrūyate ã anena ācāryeṇa mahadbhiḥ tapobhiḥ brahmā ārādhitaḥ | ataḥ asya tatprasādena sphuṭagrahagatyarthānām prādurbhāvaḥ iti | āha ca ã
body.translated_text: Now, how is the origin of [this science dealing with] supersensible [matters] such as the true positions and motions of planets? [Answer:] Through the grace of <s>Brahmā</s>. For thus it is traditionally heard: By this teacher (<s>ācārya</s>), <s>Brahmā</s> was propitiated through great austerities...

children.translated_text: He who, through austerities, attained the comprehension of supersensible objects, who had the vision of poetry capable of benefiting others,

children.text: yaḥ alaṅkṛteḥ avyayam anvayasya parāśarasya anukṛtim cakāra ||
children.translated_text: and who adorned [his work] with the imperishable lineage — he composed [this] in imitation of <s>Parāśara</s>.

body.text:
iti | brahmaṇaḥ kutaḥ? brahmā svayaṃbhūḥ jñānarāśiḥ | tataḥ sarvāsām vidyānām prādurbhāvaḥ | ataḥ anena lokānugrahāya sphuṭagrahagatyarthavācakāni daśa gītikāsūtrāṇi gaṇitakālakriyāgolārthavācakam āryāṣṭaśatam ca vinibaddham | sphuṭagrahagatyarthahetavaḥ arthāḥ, tasmāt sarvadā eva nityāḥ, teṣām śabdebhyaḥ avagatiḥ iti śabdabaddhāḥ, yathā suvarṇikāraḥ suvarṇam ādāya kaṭakakeyūrakuṇḍalādyalaṅkāram niṣpādya niṣpannam api alaṅkāram bhaṅktvā
anyatvam āpādayati | atha ca suvarṇasya tāpacchedanikaṣādiparīkṣaṇena anyatvam manāg api na bhavati iti arthānām api sādhuśabdālaṅkāranānāvṛttabandhaiḥ viracyamānānām ananyatvam iti | śrutau api śatapathe bṛhadāraṇyake paṭhyate; tad yathā ã "peśaskārī peśasaḥ mātrām apādayānyannavataram kalyāṇataram rūpam tanute" [bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣat, 4.4.4] iti | evam ayam āgamārthaḥ brahmaṇaḥ sakāśāt ācāryeṇa adhigataḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus. From <s>Brahmā</s> — how? <s>Brahmā</s> is self-born, a mass of knowledge. From him is the origin of all sciences. Therefore, for the benefit of the world, he [<s>Āryabhaṭa</s>] composed the ten <s>gītikā</s>-sūtras expressing the true positions and motions of planets...

body.text:
atha anye manyante ã "jyotiṣām udayamadhyāstamayaprāptīn dṛṣṭvā pratyakṣānumānābhyām paricchidya svadhīviracitam" iti | etat ca na | jyotīṃṣi kṣititalam bhitvā pūrvasyām diśi udgatāni krameṇa ambaramadhyam atītya parasyām diśi kṣititalam bhitvā eva praviśantaḥ lakṣyante | etāvati udayāstamayāntare viyatyupalakṣaṇābhāvāt jyotiṣām gatipramāṇaparicchedaḥ duḥsampādyaḥ, gateḥ ceyattāparijñānābhāvāt "etāvatā kālena iyatī gatiḥ etāvatā kālena
kiyatī" iti gaṇitakarma na pravartate | pramāṇaphalarāśyoḥ aparijñānāt apravatteḥ ca gaṇitakarmaṇaḥ grahāṇām yugabhagaṇāparijñānam, yugabhagaṇāparijñānāt grahagatiparijñānābhāvaḥ | yathā atra aśvādīnām gatiḥ pratyakṣeṇa deśakālābhyām saha upapadyate iti ataḥ gaṇitakarma pravartate, atīndriyatvāt grahagateḥ viyatyupalakṣaṇābhāvāt na pratyakṣeṇa paricchidyate, katham tarhi āgamāt upagatagrahayutigrahanakṣtrayogagrahaṇādayaḥ pratyakṣīkriyante?
body.translated_text: Now others think: 'Having observed the rising, meridian-transit, and setting of the luminaries, and having determined [them] through perception and inference, [this science] was composed by his own intellect.' But this is not [correct] — for the luminaries, piercing through the surface of the earth...

body.text:
anyat ca ã grahādīni jyotīṃṣi kṣititalam bhittvā eva pūrvasyām diśi udgatāni krameṇa ambaramadhyam atītya kṣititalam bhitvā eva astam gacchantaḥ lakṣyante | jyotiścakrasya pravahākṣepāt jyotiścakrapratibaddhāḥ grahāḥ prāṅmukhāḥ svagatyā bhramantaḥ api laghvyā jyotiścakragatyā aparām diśam āsādayantaḥ lakṣyante, kulālacakrārūḍhakīṭavat | tasmāt anyā jyotiścakragatiḥ, anyā grahagatiḥ prāṅmukhī | kutaḥ? yasmāt grahaḥ aśvinyām dṛṣṭaḥ bharaṇyādiṣu
parasparam prāgvyavasthiteṣu nakṣatreṣu upalakṣyate bhacakre, na revatyādiṣu parasparāparasthiteṣu | tasmāt jyotiścakragrahagatyoḥ bhinnatvāt udayāstamayadeśāntaraprāptyanumānam upapadyate | tasmāt ayam āgamaḥ brahmaṇaḥ prasādāt ācāryeṇa adhigataḥ iti | grahasya nakṣatrāṇām ca nityasambandhāt nakṣatrāṇām niscalatvāt grahagatyanumānam iti etat ca na | bahūni nakṣatrāṇi teṣu grahasya pāramparyeṇa bhukteḥ anekarūpatvāt vikṣepāpakramacakravaśāt
dakṣiṇottaramachyāsannadūracāritvāt grahasya ekasmin eva nakṣatre gatiparyayeṇa udayāstamayavakrānuvakrasambhavāt grahagativaicitryam, gaṇitena ca ekarūpā gatiḥ anumīyate | tasmāt ayam āgamaḥ brahmaṇaḥ prasādāt ācāryeṇa adhigataḥ iti |
body.translated_text: And another [point]: The luminaries such as planets, having risen in the eastern direction after piercing through the surface of the earth, gradually crossing the middle of the sky and piercing through the surface of the earth, are observed to set. The luminaries...

body.text:
anyat ca ã deśāntarākṣaviśeṣāt grahagativaicitryam | tat yathā ã laṅkāyām akṣābhāvāt sarvadā eva tulye rātryahanī laṅkāsamīpavartinām rohaṇasiṃhalānām ca; tataḥ uttarataḥ divasasya vṛddhiḥ niśāyāḥ hāniḥ, dakṣiṇataḥ niśāyāḥ vṛddhiḥ divasasya hāniḥ iti | sūryagrahaṇam api akṣadeśāntaravaśāt kvacit khaṇḍam, kvacit sakalam, kvacit na eva | candragrahaṇam ca iha ghaṭīvyatītāyām rātryām, ghaṭikādeśāntarāparadeśasthitā grahītāraḥ dinānte kathayanti,
pūrvataḥ ca yātā dūrodgatasya candramasaḥ grahaṇam kathayanti | tasmāt udayamadhyāstaprāptinakṣatrayogaparyayādibhiḥ vicitrā iyam grahagatiḥ deśāntarākṣaviśeṣaiḥ ca ativicitratvam āpadyamānā na śakyate anekarūpatvāt gaṇitanyāyena ānetum | na ca kaścit evam prakārāṇām deśakālaparyayeṇa upapadyamānānām pratijāgaritā | yaḥ ca sarvaḥ ciram jīvati sa varṣaśatam jīvati | tasya api yugapat anekadeśāntarākṣaviśeṣat nakṣatrayogaparyayādibhiḥ utpadyamānagrahagatayaḥ
yugapat na pratyakṣībhavanti | tasmāt ayam āgamaḥ brahmaṇaḥ prasādāt ācāryeṇa adhigataḥ iti | vakṣyati ca ã
body.translated_text: Moreover: the diversity of planetary motions [arises] from the particularity of the latitude (<s>akṣa</s>) [and] longitude (<s>deśāntara</s>) of different places. That is as follows: In <s>Laṅkā</s>, due to the absence of latitude, nights and days are always equal; and [the same holds] for those dwelling near <s>Laṅkā</s>, the <s>Rohaṇa</s> and <s>Siṃhala</s> [peoples]. From there northward, the day increases and the night decreases; southward, the night increases and the day decreases. A solar eclipse too, due to the effect of latitude and longitude, is partial in some places, total in some places, and does not [occur] at all in some places. And a lunar eclipse — here, when a <s>ghaṭī</s> (time unit) of the night has passed, those situated in a place at a [different] longitude of a <s>ghaṭikā</s> report it at the end of the day, and those who have gone eastward report the eclipse of the moon that has risen far [above the horizon]. Therefore, this planetary motion, being diverse due to rising, meridian transit, setting, conjunction with <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions), cycles, and the like, and becoming extremely diverse due to the particularities of longitude and latitude, cannot be brought under a single mathematical rule because of its manifold nature. And no one has been vigilant [enough to observe] such [phenomena] that are accounted for by the cycle of place and time. And whoever lives the longest lives a hundred years. Even for him, the planetary motions arising simultaneously from the particularities of multiple longitudes and latitudes, conjunctions with <s>nakṣatras</s>, cycles, and the like, do not become simultaneously perceptible. Therefore, this teaching (<s>āgama</s>) was obtained by the <s>Ācārya</s> (teacher) through the grace of <s>Brahmā</s>. And he will say:

children.translated_text: From the ocean of true and false knowledge, extracted by the grace of <s>Brahmā</s>,
the supreme jewel of true knowledge has been retrieved by me with the boat of my own intellect.

body.text: golapādaḥ, 49
body.translated_text: <s>Golapāda</s>, 49

body.text: iti |
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: vedāṅgeṣu jyotiṣaśāstraprādhānyam
body.translated_text: The preeminence of <s>Jyotiṣaśāstra</s> (astronomical science) among the <s>Vedāṅgas</s>

body.text: na kevalam jyotiṣām ayam āgamaḥ, vedāṅgam ca | "tasmāt brāhmaṇeṇa niṣkāraṇam ṣaḍaṅgaḥ vedaḥ adhyeyaḥ" [pātāñjalamahābhāṣyam, paspaśāhnikam] ṣaḍaṅgeṣu pradhānam jyotiṣām ayanam | kutaḥ asya prādhānyam? yasmāt anadhītaśikṣādayaḥ api prāg gurūpadeśāt vedān adhīyate, na ca teṣām duradhītam bhavati | na anadhigatajyotiṣām ayanā vedoktān yajñakālān jānate | atha śikṣayā varṇānām sthānakaraṇaprayatnāni nirūpyante ã
body.translated_text: This is not merely the teaching of the astronomers — it is also a <s>Vedāṅga</s> (limb of the Veda). "Therefore, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should study the <s>Veda</s> with its six limbs without any [ulterior] motive" [<s>Pātañjala-Mahābhāṣya</s>, <s>Paspaśāhnika</s>]. Among the six limbs, the study of astronomy (<s>jyotiṣām ayanam</s>) is preeminent. Why is it preeminent? Because even those who have not studied <s>śikṣā</s> (phonetics) and the like recite the <s>Vedas</s> prior to the teacher’s instruction, and their recitation does not become faulty. But those who have not studied the course of astronomy do not know the times of sacrifice prescribed by the <s>Veda</s>. Now, by <s>śikṣā</s>, the places of articulation, instruments of articulation, and efforts of phonemes are determined:

children.text: aṣṭau sthānāni varṇānām uraḥ kaṇṭhaḥ śiraḥ tathā |
children.translated_text: The eight places of articulation of phonemes are: the chest, the throat, the head,

children.text: jihvāmūlam ca dantāḥ ca nāsikoṣṭhau ca tālu ca ||
children.translated_text: the root of the tongue, the teeth, the nose, the lips, and the palate.

body.text: pāṇinīyaśikṣā, śloí 13
body.translated_text: <s>Pāṇinīyaśikṣā</s>, verse 13

body.text:
iti ādi | varṇāḥ uccāryamāṇāḥ svaiḥ svaiḥ sthānakaraṇaprayatnaiḥ svabhāvataḥ eva āsyāt niṣkrāmanti, na anyataḥ | "akuhavisarjanīyāḥ kaṇṭhyāḥ, ṛṭuraṣāḥ mūrdhanyāḥ |" akuhavisarjanīyāḥ uccāryamāṇā kaṇṭhapradeśāt eva āsyāt niṣkrāmanti na mūrdhnaḥ, ṛṭuraṣāḥ uccāryamāṇāḥ mūrdhnaḥ eva na anyasmāt pradeśāntarāt iti | yasmāt teṣām sthānakaraṇaprayatnāḥ svabhāvataḥ eva siddhāḥ tasmāt teṣām sthānakaraṇaprayatnaḥ nirarthakaḥ | tathā ca anadhītavyākaraṇāḥ
api brāhmaṇāḥ vedān adhīyate | na ca teṣām duradhītam bhavati | na ca anadhītajyotiṣām ayanā vedoktān yajñakālān jānate | vyākaraṇena kila vedānām rakṣā kriyate | rakṣā api prajānām pārthivaiḥ duṣṭanigraheṇa śiṣṭānugraheṇa ca kriyate | evam vedānām śabdarāśitvāt asādhūnām uddhāraḥ nigrahaḥ, sādhūnām śabdānām samyak kṛtaḥ anugrahaḥ iti | etat ca na | nityāḥ vedāḥ | teṣu śabdarāśiprakṣepāṇām [svataḥ siddhiḥ], dṛṣṭānuvidhitvāt chandasaḥ | yaḥ yaḥ
śabdaḥ vedeṣu paṭhyate tasya tasya aprasiddhalakṣaṇasya api svayam lakṣaṇam sādhyam pratyayaprakṛtilopāgamavarṇavikārādibhiḥ | na ca jyotiṣām ayanasya api | ye ye vede yajñakālāḥ dṛṣṭāḥ te sarve eva jyotiṣām ayane gaṇitalakṣaṇasiddhāḥ eva |
body.translated_text: And so on. Phonemes, when being pronounced, naturally emerge from the mouth through their respective places, instruments, and efforts of articulation — not from elsewhere. "<s>A</s>, <s>ku</s>, <s>ha</s>, <s>visarjanīya</s> are guttural; <s>Ṛ</s>, <s>ṭu</s>, <s>ra</s>, <s>ṣa</s> are cerebral." <s>A</s>, <s>ku</s>, <s>ha</s>, and <s>visarjanīya</s>, when being pronounced, emerge from the mouth from the throat region only, not from the palate; <s>Ṛ</s>, <s>ṭu</s>, <s>ra</s>, and <s>ṣa</s>, when being pronounced, [emerge] from the palate only, not from any other region. Since their places, instruments, and efforts of articulation are naturally established, their [study of] places, instruments, and efforts is purposeless. Similarly, even <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who have not studied grammar recite the <s>Vedas</s>, and their recitation does not become faulty. But those who have not studied the course of astronomy do not know the times of sacrifice prescribed by the <s>Veda</s>. By grammar, supposedly, the protection of the <s>Vedas</s> is accomplished. But the protection of subjects too is accomplished by kings through the punishment of the wicked and the favoring of the virtuous. Similarly, since the <s>Vedas</s> are a collection of words, the extraction and rejection of incorrect [words] is [their] punishment, and the proper maintenance of correct words is [their] favoring. But this is not so. The <s>Vedas</s> are eternal. The inclusion of [correct] words in them is self-established, because the <s>Chandas</s> (Vedic meter) follows what is observed. Whatever word is recited in the <s>Vedas</s>, even if its [grammatical] characteristics are not well-known, its own characteristics are to be derived through suffixes, stems, elisions, augments, phonemic modifications, and the like. But this is not [the case] for the study of astronomy either. Whatever sacrificial times are found in the <s>Veda</s> — they are all established through mathematical calculation in the study of astronomy.

body.text:
anyat ca ã "dṛṣṭānuvidhitvāt chandasaḥ" iti yadi vedeṣu dṛṣṭaḥ eva anuvidhīyate tadā nahi kiñcit prayojanam vyākaraṇena | atha ṛgyajuḥsāmnām sarveṣām eva pratipadānirukteḥ niruktasya āvyāpitā | atha chandovicitaiḥ ṛgyajuḥsāmnām nityaḥ eva chandaḥ nibaddhaḥ | na ca teṣām idānīm kāvyapadapūrvaḥ nibaddhaḥ kriyate | na ca anyūnādhikalakṣaṇānām ṛgyajuḥsāmnām idānīm anyathākaraṇam karaṇam | evam ca bāhvṛce śrutau śrūyate, na hi ekena akṣareṇa
dvābhyām vā ūnāni chandāṃsi kriyante iti | na hi evam vedoktānām yajñakālānām iti kramaḥ śrūyate | na hi ādhānādiṣu saṃskāreṣu kālaviśeṣāḥ jyotiṣām ayanāt vinā avagamyante | tat yathā saṃskāreṣu ã
body.translated_text: Moreover: "Because the <s>Chandas</s> follows what is observed" — if only what is observed in the <s>Vedas</s> is followed, then grammar serves no purpose at all. Furthermore, since not every word of the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s> has an etymological explanation (<s>nirukti</s>), the <s>Nirukta</s> (etymology) does not cover [them all]. And by those learned in <s>Chandas</s> (meter), the meter of the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s> is always already fixed. And their [meters] are not now composed anew from [individual] literary words. And there is no making of the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s>, whose characteristics are neither deficient nor excessive, into something different now. Thus it is heard in the <s>Bāhvṛca Śruti</s>: "<s>Chandas</s> (meters) are not made deficient by one or two syllables." But the sequence "the times of sacrifice prescribed by the <s>Veda</s>" is not heard [to be self-evident in the same way]. For the specific times in rituals such as the <s>Ādhāna</s> (fire-establishment) and other <s>saṃskāras</s> (ceremonies) are not understood without the study of astronomy. That is, in [the context of] <s>saṃskāras</s>:

children.text: evam gacchan striyam kṣāmām maghām mūlam ca varjayet |
children.translated_text: Thus proceeding, one should avoid [the <s>nakṣatras</s>] <s>Maghā</s> and <s>Mūla</s> when the woman is thin;

children.text: susthaḥ indau sulakṣaṇyām vidvāṃsam putram aśnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: when the moon is well-placed, on an auspicious [<s>nakṣatra</s>], a learned son would be obtained.

body.text: yājñavalkyasmṛtiḥ, ācārādhyāyaḥ, vivāhaprakaraṇam, śloí 80
body.translated_text: <s>Yājñavalkya-Smṛti</s>, <s>Ācārādhyāya</s>, section on marriage, verse 80

body.text:
iti | tatra maghāmūlayoḥ pratipatticchedau indoḥ ca susthaduḥsthatām ca nānadhītajyotiṣām ayanā jānate | "sā yadi garbham na dadhīta siṃhyā śvetapuṣpyā upoṣya puṣyeṇa mūlam utthāpya" iti [pāraskaragṛhyasūtram, kāí 1, kaṇḍikā 13, sūí 1] tatra puṣyasya pratipatticchedau nānadhītajyotiṣām ayanā jānate | tathā ca puṃsavane ã "yat ahaḥ puṃsā nakṣatreṇa candramāḥ [yujyeta] tat ahar upavāsya" iti [pāraskaragṛhyasūtram, 1. 14. 3] | tatra puṃnakṣatrāṇi punar
vasupuṣyahastasvātiśravaṇāḥ | eteṣām nirupahatānām anukūlahatānām ca pratipatticchedau nānadhītajyotiṣām ayanā jānate |
body.translated_text: Thus. There, the determination and exclusion of [the <s>nakṣatras</s>] <s>Maghā</s> and <s>Mūla</s>, and the favorable or unfavorable position of the Moon, are not known by one who has not studied the course of astronomy. "If she does not conceive, having fasted on [the day of] <s>Puṣya</s> with a white flower for a <s>Siṃhī</s>, one should uproot a root" [<s>Pāraskara-Gṛhyasūtra</s>, 1.13.1] — there, the determination and exclusion of <s>Puṣya</s> is not known by one who has not studied the course of astronomy. Likewise, in the <s>puṃsavana</s> (male-producing rite): "On whatever day the moon is conjoined with a masculine <s>nakṣatra</s>, on that day one should fast" [<s>Pāraskara-Gṛhyasūtra</s>, 1.14.3]. There, the masculine <s>nakṣatras</s> are <s>Punarvasu</s>, <s>Puṣya</s>, <s>Hasta</s>, <s>Svātī</s>, and <s>Śravaṇa</s>. The determination and exclusion of these, whether unafflicted or favorably aspected, is not known by one who has not studied the course of astronomy.

body.text: anyat ca ã
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: nāmadheyam daśamyām tat dvādaśyām vā asya kārayet |
children.translated_text: The naming ceremony should be performed for him on the tenth or twelfth [day],

children.text: puṇye ahani muhūrtte vā nakṣatre vā guṇānvite ||
children.translated_text: on an auspicious day, or at a [favorable] <s>muhūrta</s> (moment), or under a <s>nakṣatra</s> endowed with good qualities.

body.text: manusmṛtiḥ, 2.30
body.translated_text: <s>Manu-Smṛti</s>, 2.30

body.text: iti | atra puṇyasya ahnaḥ, nakṣatrasya guṇānvitasya, muhūrtasya vā pratipatticchedau nānadhītajyotiṣām ayanā jānate |
body.translated_text: Thus. Here, the determination and exclusion of an auspicious day, a <s>nakṣatra</s> endowed with good qualities, or a [favorable] <s>muhūrta</s> is not known by one who has not studied the course of astronomy.

body.text:
anyat ca ã "udagayane āpūryamāṇapakṣe puṇyāhe kumāryāḥ pāṇim gṛhṇīyāt", "triṣu triṣu uttarādiṣu", "svātau mṛgaśirasi rohiṇyām ca" [pāraskaragṛhyasūtram, 1.4.5-7] iti atra udagayanādīnām uttarādīnām nakṣtrāṇām vadhūvarayoḥ anukūlānām ca pratipatticchedau nānadhītajyotiṣām ayanā jānate, evamādi pratiśākham saṃskārāṇām puṇyāhanakṣatramuhūrtacodanā jyotiṣām ayanāṅgaviṣayāḥ tadvidbhyaḥ eva avagantavyāḥ, na gurūpadeśāt sampradāyāvicchedāt
vā avagantavyāḥ | iti adhyeyam jyotiṣām ayanam |
body.translated_text: Moreover: "During the northern course [of the sun], in the waxing fortnight, on an auspicious day, one should take the hand of the maiden," "in each of the three [<s>nakṣatras</s>] beginning with the <s>Uttara</s>s," "under <s>Svātī</s>, <s>Mṛgaśiras</s>, and <s>Rohiṇī</s>" [<s>Pāraskara-Gṛhyasūtra</s>, 1.4.5–7]. Here, the determination and exclusion of the northern course and other [conditions], the <s>nakṣatras</s> beginning with <s>Uttara</s>, and those favorable to the bride and groom, is not known by one who has not studied the course of astronomy. Similarly, the injunctions regarding auspicious days, <s>nakṣatras</s>, and <s>muhūrtas</s> for <s>saṃskāras</s> in each <s>śākhā</s> (Vedic branch) are subject-matters of the limbs of the study of astronomy, to be understood only from those who know it — not to be understood from the teacher’s instruction or the unbroken tradition alone. Therefore, the study of astronomy should be studied.

body.text:
anyat ca ã chandasaḥ upākarmaṇi "atha ataḥ adhyāyopākarma | oṣadhīnām prādurbhāve śravaṇena śrāvaṇyām paurṇamāsyām śrāvaṇasya pañcamī hastena vā" [pāraskaragṛhyasūtram, 2.10.1-2] iti atra śrāvaṇapaurṇamāsīm śravaṇena yuktām, śrāvaṇasya pañcamīm hastena yuktām nānadhītajyotiṣām ayanā jānate | anyat ca ã [chandasaḥ utsarge] "pauṣasya rohiṇyām madhyamāyām vāṣṭakāyām adhyāyān utsṛjeran" [pāraskaragṛhyasūtram, 2.12.1] iti etat ca
| atha nakṣatrādhāneṣu "yā asau vaiśākhasya āmāvāsyā tasyām ādadhīta sā rohiṇyā sampadyate" [āpastambaśrautasūtram, 4.3.20; baudhāyanavyākhyā] iti atra prāg eva rohiṇyā vaiśākhasya āmāvāsyāyāḥ parijñānayogyasya ādhānadravyasya arjanam ṛtvijām ca varaṇam iti etat ca jyotiṣām ayanāṅgaviṣayam, tadvidbhyaḥ eva avagantavyam, na gurūpadeśāt sampradāyāvicchedāt vā avagantavyam iti adhyeyam jyotiṣām ayanam | tathā ca "kṛttikāsu agnim ādadhīta" [taittirīyabrāhmaṇam,
1.1.2.1] evamādi nakṣatrādhānacodanāḥ ca "paśvijyā saṃvatsare [saṃvatsare], prāvṛṣi āvṛttimukhayoḥ vā" [kātyāyanaśrautasūtram, paśubaṃdhaí, 1-2] iti āvṛttimukhayoḥ pratipatticchedau vedinām anadhītajyotiṣām ayanā [na] jānate | anyat ca ã "darśapaurṇamāsābhyām yajeta" [śatapathabrāhmaṇam, 11.2.5.10] iti evamādi codanāḥ ca [śrauta]smārteṣu ca karmasu "aparapakṣe śrāddham kurvīta ūrdhvam vā caturyyām" [pāraskaragṛhyasūtrapariśiṣṭakārabhāṣyam, śrāddhasūtram
1] |
body.translated_text: Moreover: Regarding the <s>Upākarmaṇa</s> (commencement of Vedic study) of the <s>Chandas</s>: "Now then, the commencement of study. At the appearance of herbs, on the full-moon day of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> conjoined with [the <s>nakṣatra</s>] <s>Śravaṇa</s>, or the fifth of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> conjoined with <s>Hasta</s>" [<s>Pāraskara-Gṛhyasūtra</s>, 2.10.1–2]. Here, the full-moon of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> conjoined with <s>Śravaṇa</s>, or the fifth of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> conjoined with <s>Hasta</s>, is not known by one who has not studied the course of astronomy. Moreover: [Regarding the <s>Utsarga</s> (suspension of Vedic study)] "On the <s>Rohiṇī</s> of <s>Pauṣa</s>, or on the middle <s>Aṣṭakā</s>, one should suspend the lessons" [<s>Pāraskara-Gṛhyasūtra</s>, 2.12.1] — and this too. Now, in the <s>Nakṣatrādhāna</s> (fire-establishments based on <s>nakṣatras</s>): "That new-moon day of <s>Vaiśākha</s> — on that day one should establish [the fire]; that coincides with <s>Rohiṇī</s>" [<s>Āpastamba-Śrautasūtra</s>, 4.3.20; <s>Baudhāyana</s> commentary]. Here, the prior knowledge of <s>Rohiṇī</s> [coinciding with] the new-moon of <s>Vaiśākha</s>, the procurement of materials suitable for the fire-establishment, and the selection of <s>ṛtvijs</s> (priests) — this too is a subject-matter of the limbs of the study of astronomy, to be understood only from those who know it — not from the teacher’s instruction or the unbroken tradition alone. Therefore, the study of astronomy should be studied. Similarly, "One should establish the fire under <s>Kṛtikās</s>" [<s>Taittirīya-Brāhmaṇa</s>, 1.1.2.1] and similar injunctions regarding fire-establishment based on <s>nakṣatras</s>, and "The animal sacrifice [is performed] year after year, or at the beginning of the rainy seasons" [<s>Kātyāyana-Śrautasūtra</s>, <s>Paśubandha</s>, 1–2] — the determination and exclusion of the beginnings of the two [rainy] seasons is [also] not known by Vedic scholars who have not studied the course of astronomy. Moreover: "One should sacrifice with the <s>Darśa-Pūrṇamāsa</s> (new-moon and full-moon sacrifices)" [<s>Śatapatha-Brāhmaṇa</s>, 11.2.5.10] and similar injunctions; and in <s>Śrauta</s> and <s>Smārta</s> rites: "One should perform the <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rite) in the dark fortnight, or after the fourth [<s>tithi</s>]" [<s>Pāraskara-Gṛhyasūtra</s> supplement, <s>Śrāddha-Sūtra</s>, 1].

children.text: api naḥ sa kule jāyāt yaḥ naḥ dadyāt trayodaśīm |
children.translated_text: May he be born in our family who would give us [the offering of] the thirteenth [<s>tithi</s>],

children.text: pāyasam madhusaṃyuktam varṣāsu ca maghāsu ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice) mixed with honey, during the rainy season under [the <s>nakṣatra</s>] <s>Maghā</s>.

body.text: manusmṛtiḥ, 3.264
body.translated_text: <s>Manu-Smṛti</s>, 3.264

body.text: iti |
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: kim bahunā, śrautasmārtaviṣayāṇām tithinakṣatraviṣayāṇām karmaṇām nityānām kāmyānām ca na jyotiṣām ayanāt vinā samārambhaḥ, iti adhyeyam jyotiṣām ayanam |
body.translated_text: In short, the <s>Śrauta</s> and <s>Smārta</s> rites pertaining to <s>tithis</s> (lunar days) and <s>nakṣatras</s>, whether obligatory (<s>nitya</s>) or desire-motivated (<s>kāmya</s>), cannot be undertaken without the study of astronomy. Therefore, the study of astronomy should be studied.

body.text: lokavyavahāre jyotiṣaśāstropādeyatā
body.translated_text: The usefulness of <s>Jyotiṣaśāstra</s> (astronomical science) in worldly affairs

body.text:
lokaḥ ca tithinakṣatramuhūrtaviṣayāṇām [sambandhena eva] śubheṣu kāryeṣu pravartate | tathā ca puṣpaphalapāṇiḥ sarvaḥ eva daivajñam upetya pṛcchati ã "kadā me kim bhaviṣyati? kadā aham kṛṣyādikarmaṇi pravarte? kadā aham daivajñakena upatiṣṭhe? kadā aham adhvānam prapadye? kadā rājānam paśyāmi? ihasthasya śubham me bhaviṣyati āhosvid anyasthānagatasya? kena karmaṇā pravṛttasya me phalam bhaviṣyati?" iti etat daivajñāt avagatārthaḥ
sarvaḥ eva śubheṣu kāryeṣu pravartate | aśubheṣu api ã "kadā paradeśam didhakṣuḥ aham pravarte? kadā vairiṇaḥ vināśāya pratiṣṭhe? kadā gajāśvaharaṇam [vidadhe]? kadā puram grāmam vā ghātayāmi?" etat ca daivajñāt avagatya sarvaḥ pravartate | mlecchādayaḥ api ca śakunanimittasvapnabalāt eva kāryeṣu pravartante | yasya ca yatkiñcit śubham bhavati sa bravīti "śubhanakṣatramuhūrteṣu aham āgataḥ", yasya vā yatkiñcit skhalitam bhavati sa bravīti ã "mama nakṣatrapīḍā
vartate, na anukūlāḥ grahāḥ" iti | tathā ca hastiśikṣāvidaḥ svaśāstroktatithinakṣatreṣu eva pāribandhādihastikarmasu pravartante |
body.translated_text: And the world engages in auspicious activities in connection with <s>tithis</s>, <s>nakṣatras</s>, and <s>muhūrtas</s>. Thus, every person with offerings of flowers and fruits in hand approaches the astrologer (<s>daivajña</s>) and asks: "When will what happen to me? When should I engage in agriculture and other activities? When should I approach the astrologer? When should I set out on a journey? When should I see the king? Will good fortune come to me while staying here, or while gone to another place? From what activity will I obtain results?" Thus, having understood the matter from the astrologer, everyone engages in auspicious activities. Even in inauspicious [matters]: "When should I, desiring to burn enemy territory, set out? When should I proceed toward the destruction of enemies? When should I seize elephants and horses? When should I destroy a city or village?" Having understood this too from the astrologer, everyone proceeds. Even <s>Mlecchas</s> (foreigners) and others engage in activities solely on the strength of omens, portents, and dreams. And whoever has anything auspicious happen says: "I came at auspicious <s>nakṣatras</s> and <s>muhūrtas</s>"; and whoever has any misfortune says: "There is affliction of my <s>nakṣatra</s>, the planets are not favorable." Similarly, those learned in the science of elephants (<s>hastiśikṣā</s>) engage in elephant-training activities such as binding and the like only at the <s>tithis</s> and <s>nakṣatras</s> prescribed in their own <s>śāstra</s>.

body.text: pakṣacchidreṣu tithayaḥ ye yasya -ravaḥ matā|
body.translated_text: On the <s>tithis</s> that are the gaps of the fortnights, those which are considered [auspicious] for each respective [activity],

body.text: teṣu teṣu pāripraveśabandham ca parivarjayanti |
body.translated_text: on those [<s>tithis</s>], they avoid entry, binding, and the like.

children.text: nakṣatram hastinām prāha svayam eva prajāpatiḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s> himself declared the <s>nakṣatra</s> of elephants;
for the work of elephants is declared to be pure [when performed] under <s>Hasta</s>, [the <s>nakṣatra</s> of] the hand.

body.text: iti ādi | tathā ca aśvaśikṣāyām ã
body.translated_text: And so on. Similarly, in the science of horses (<s>aśvaśikṣā</s>):

children.text: aśvinyām revatau puṣye punar vasyoḥ ca kārayet |
children.translated_text: Under <s>Aśvinī</s>, <s>Revatī</s>, <s>Puṣya</s>, and the two <s>Punarvasus</s>, one should perform
all activities for horses, [and also] under <s>Svātī</s>, <s>Vāruṇa</s> (Śatabhiṣā), and <s>Hasta</s>.

body.text: iti | tathā ca viṣatantre ã
body.translated_text: Thus. Similarly, in the <s>Viṣatantra</s> (treatise on poisons):

children.translated_text: In <s>Kṛttikā</s>, <s>Viśākhā</s>, <s>Maghā</s>, and <s>Bharaṇī</s>,

children.text: sārpe mūle tathā ardrāyām sarpadaṣṭaḥ na jīvati ||
children.translated_text: in <s>Sārpa</s> [i.e. <s>Āśleṣā</s>], <s>Mūla</s>, and also <s>Ārdrā</s> — one bitten by a serpent does not survive.

body.text: āviddhamlecchādayaḥ api ca na śubhatithinakṣatramuhūrtān ullaṅghya pravartante | tathā kṣutaruditākruṣṭapratyaskhalitaśravaṇam pariharanti | tṛṇakāṣṭhabhāralavaṇāsthimattonmattaklībāhidarśanam pariharanti | sitakusumasvāduphalekṣuvaṃśā[mbara]sa[ma]laṅkṛtastrīpūrṇakumbhādidarśanam abhinandanti | iti adhyeyam jyotiṣām ayanam lokānugrahāya | iti evam idam prathamam gītikāsūtram || 2 ||
body.translated_text: Even the barbarians (<s>mleccha</s>) and others do not proceed without observing auspicious <s>tithis</s> (lunar days), <s>nakṣatras</s> (asterisms), and <s>muhūrtas</s> (auspicious moments). Similarly, they avoid sneezing, crying, shouting, stumbling, and overhearing. [They also avoid encountering] those carrying grass, wood, heavy loads, salt, bones, the intoxicated, the mad, the impotent...

body.text: grahāṇām yugabhagaṇāḥ
body.translated_text: Revolutions of the planets in a <s>yuga</s>

body.text: grahāṇām yugabhagaṇapradarśanāya āryām āha ã
body.translated_text: In order to show the number of revolutions of the planets in a <s>yuga</s>, he states the <s>āryā</s> verse:

children.translated_text: The revolutions of the Sun in a <s>yuga</s> are <s>khyughṛ</s>; [those of] the Moon
<s>cayagiyiṅuśuchlṛ</s>; [of] the Earth (<s>ku</s>) <s>ṅiśibuṇlṛṣkhṛ</s> — [these are] eastward.
<s>Śani</s> (Saturn) <s>ḍhuṅvighva</s>; <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter) <s>khri-</s>
<s>cyubha</s>; <s>Kuja</s> (Mars) <s>bhadlijhnukhṛ</s>; [those of] <s>Bhṛgu</s> (Venus) and <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) are solar. // 3 //

body.text: asyāḥ padāni ã yugaravibhagaṇāḥ, khyughṛ avibhaktikaḥ nirdeśaḥ, śaśi avibhaktikaḥ eva, cayagiyiṅuśuchlṛ avibhaktikaḥ, ku avibhaktikaḥ eva, ṅiśibuṇlṛṣkhṛ avibhaktikaḥ, prāk, śani, ḍhuṅvighva, guru, khricyubha, kuja, bhadlijhnukhṛ, etāni śanyādīni api ca padāni avibhaktikanirdiṣṭāni eva | avibhaktikanirdeśāḥ anyatra api dṛśyante "aiuṇ ṛḷk", "sarvaviśva" ityādiṣu ca | bhṛgubudhasaurāḥ |
body.translated_text: The words of this [verse are]: '<s>yugaravibhagaṇāḥ</s>' (revolutions of the Sun in a <s>yuga</s>); '<s>khyughṛ</s>' is an indeclinable notation; '<s>śaśi</s>' (Moon) is also indeclinable; '<s>cayagiyiṅuśuchlṛ</s>' is indeclinable; '<s>ku</s>' (Earth) is also indeclinable; '<s>ṅiśibuṇlṛṣkhṛ</s>' is indeclinable; '<s>prāk</s>' (eastward); '<s>śani</s>' (Saturn)...

body.text: yugaravibhagaṇāḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Yugaravibhagaṇāḥ</s>

body.text:
| yuge ravibhagaṇāḥ yugaravibhagaṇāḥ, yugasya vā ravibhagaṇāḥ yugaravibhagaṇāḥ | yugam kālakriyāpāde vakṣyate | atha atra dvandvanirdeśaḥ kasmāt na bhavati? ã yugam ca ravibhagaṇāḥ ca yugaravibhagaṇāḥ, yugam khyughṛ ravibhagaṇāḥ khyughṛ iti | evam ca sati dvandvanirdeśe yat tat kālakriyāpāde vakṣyate, tat eva na vaktavyam bhavati | satyam, kintu trairāśikam na siddhyati | saptamāsamāse ṣaṣṭhīsamāse vā kriyamāṇe trairāśikam
siddham | yadi divasasaṅkhye varṣasaṅkhye vā yuge yathānirdiṣṭāḥ grahabhagaṇāḥ labhyante tadā asmin nirdiṣṭe kiyantaḥ iti tatkālamadhyamagrahabhagaṇādayaḥ labhyante | ṣaṣṭhīsamāse ca yad yasya divasasaṅkhyasya varṣasaṅkhyasya yugasya yathānirdiṣṭāḥ grahabhagaṇāḥ labhyante, asya iṣṭasya kiyantaḥ iti madhyamagrahabhagaṇādisiddhiḥ | dvandve punar na etat siddhyati | asau ca atra yugabhagaṇaśabdaḥ sarvatra adhikārārthe prayujyate | adhikāre ca yathā yugaravibhagaṇāḥ
evam yuge śaśibhagaṇāḥ ityādi | anyathā kasmin kāle kasya vā kālasya ete grahabhagaṇāḥ iti etat ne nirdiṣṭam bhavati | tasmāt ṣaṣṭhīsaptamīsamāsābhyām anyatareṇa vyākhyeyam, arkeṇa eva grahāṇām yugaprasiddheḥ | uktam ca ã
body.translated_text: : The revolutions of the Sun in a <s>yuga</s> are <s>yugaravibhagaṇāḥ</s>, or the Sun's revolutions belonging to a <s>yuga</s> are <s>yugaravibhagaṇāḥ</s>. The <s>yuga</s> will be explained in the <s>Kālakriyāpāda</s> (chapter on the reckoning of time). Now, why is a <s>dvandva</s> (copulative) compound not used here?...

children.translated_text: Time arising from the conjunction of particular place, time, and the Sun's degree and similar [planetary positions]

children.text: kālaḥ grahāt ca sadasadvargaḥ syāt vyāvahārikam ||
children.translated_text: and from a planet — the good or bad division (<s>varga</s>) would be [only] conventional.

body.text:
iti | uttaratra api adhikārārtham raviyugabhagaṇaśabdaḥ sambandhanīyaḥ, raviyuge śaśibhagaṇāḥ raviyugasya vā iti | katham idam? [raviyugabhagaṇāḥ iti] pāṭhāntare api dvandvanirdeśāt ṣaṣṭhīsaptamyarthaḥ durlabhaḥ bhavet adhikāraḥ ca | evam tarhi ekaśeṣanirdeśaḥ atra pratipattavyaḥ, raviyugabhagaṇāḥ ca raviyugabhagaṇāḥ ca raviyugabhagaṇāḥ iti | ekena raviyugabhagaṇaśabdena raviyugabhagaṇāḥ ca raviyugabhagaṇapramāṇasaṃsiddhiḥ dvitīyena ṣaṣṭhīsaptamīsamāsābhyāṃ
trairāśikasiddhiḥ iti | yadi evam yugaravibhagaṇaśabdena api ayam arthaḥ śakyate jñātum, na kiñcit pāṭhāntare prayojanam |
body.translated_text: Thus. The word '<s>raviyugabhagaṇa</s>' (Sun's revolutions in a <s>yuga</s>) is to be connected [with what follows] for the purpose of governing [the subsequent passage] too: 'In a Sun-<s>yuga</s>, the Moon's revolutions' or 'of a Sun-<s>yuga</s>.' How is this? Even in the alternative reading '<s>raviyugabhagaṇāḥ</s>,' a <s>dvandva</s> compound...

body.text: yugaravibhagaṇāḥ kiyantaḥ? ucyante ã khyughṛ | ukāravargasthāne ayam khakāraḥ yakāraḥ ca, tena ukāravargasthāne dvātriṃśat | ghṛ ṛkāravargasthāne ghakāraḥ, tena tasmin sthāne catvāri | evam ekatra tricatvāriṃśat lakṣā viṃśatisahasrāṇi | aṅkaiḥ api 4320000 |
body.translated_text: How many are the revolutions of the Sun in a <s>yuga</s>? It is stated: <s>khyughṛ</s>. In the <s>u</s>-vowel <s>varga</s>-place, this [has] the letter <s>kha</s> and the letter <s>ya</s>; therefore, in the <s>u</s>-vowel <s>varga</s>-place, thirty-two. <s>Ghṛ</s> — in the <s>ṛ</s>-vowel <s>varga</s>-place, the letter <s>gha</s>; therefore, in that place, four...

body.text: śaśi cayagiyiṅuśuchlṛ | prakṛtādhikārayugabhagaṇasaṃyogena śaśiśabdaḥ vyākhyeyaḥ ã yugaśaśibhagaṇāḥ | atra api tau eva samāsau | yugaśaśibhagaṇāḥ cayagiyiṅuśuchlṛ | pūrvavat eva vargāvargasthāneṣu saṅkhyā sthāpanīyā | rasāgnirāmadahaneṣvadriśailaśilīmukhāḥ | aṅkaiḥ api 57753336|
body.translated_text: The Moon (<s>śaśi</s>) [has revolutions] <s>cayagiyiṅuśuchlṛ</s>. By connection with the governing [term] '<s>yuga</s>-revolutions' already stated, the word '<s>śaśi</s>' is to be interpreted as: 'The revolutions of the Moon in a <s>yuga</s>.' Here too the same two compounds [apply]. The Moon's revolutions in a <s>yuga</s> are <s>cayagiyiṅuśuchlṛ</s>. Just as before, [each letter-numeral is] placed in its proper position...

body.text: ku ṅiśibuṇlṛṣkhṛ | tathā eva yugakubhagaṇāḥ tathā eva svasthāne api viniveśitāḥ, khāmbareṣvadrirāmāśviyamāṣṭatithayaḥ, 1582237500 |
