body.translated_text: The Earth (<s>ku</s>) [has revolutions] <s>ṅiśibuṇlṛṣkhṛ</s>. Similarly, the revolutions of the Earth in a <s>yuga</s>, likewise placed in their proper positions, are: void-sky-mountain-<s>Rāma</s>-horse-<s>Yama</s>-eight-<s>tithi</s>s [= 1,582,237,500].

body.text: bhacakrapratibaddhāni nakṣatrāṇi tasya bhacakrasya pravahākṣepavaśāt aparām diśam āsādayanti | nakṣatrāṇi [bhuvam] grahavat svagatyā prāṅmukhīm bhramantīm iva paśyanti iti anayā yuktyā bhuvaḥ bhagaṇanirdeśaḥ |
body.translated_text: The <s>nakṣatras</s> (asterisms), being bound to the stellar sphere (<s>bhacakra</s>), reach the western direction due to the force of the <s>pravaha</s> wind carrying the stellar sphere. The <s>nakṣatras</s> observe [the Earth] as if revolving eastward by its own motion, like a planet — thus, by this <s>yuga</s>-[revolution number]...

body.text:
prāk | ye ete grahāḥ vivasvadādayaḥ prāṅmukhāḥ bhramanti | yadi api bhapañjarapravahākṣepāt apagacchanti diśam, tathā api ete svagatyā prāṅmukham eva gacchanti | alpatvāt gateḥ kālāntareṇa prācīm diśam āsādayantaḥ lakṣyante, kulālacakrasthakīṭavat | yadi ete prāggatayaḥ na syuḥ, tadā aśvinyām dṛṣṭaḥ [grahaḥ] bharaṇyām na upalakṣyeta | yadi ete aparābhimukhāḥ syuḥ, tadā aśvinyām dṛṣṭāḥ revatyām upalakṣyeran | tasmāt ete prāṅmukhāḥ eva
bhramanti iti ataḥ "prāk" iti |
body.translated_text: Eastward (<s>prāk</s>): These planets, beginning with the Sun, revolve eastward. Although they move westward due to the dragging force of the stellar cage's (<s>bhapañjara</s>) <s>pravaha</s> wind, nevertheless, by their own motion, they move precisely eastward. Because their [eastward] motion is small, for a time...

body.text:
kim punar bhūbhagaṇopadeśe prayojanam iti āha ã "ravibhūyogāḥ [bhūdivasāḥ]", [kālakriyāí, 5] iti bhūdivasānayanam | na etat asti, prakārāntaraniṣpannatvāt kudivasānām | yadi api ayam eva kudivasapratipatteḥ upāyaḥ syāt tathā api upadeśagauravāt na yujyate | kā upadeśagurutā? ucyate ã "ku ṅiśibuṇlṛṣkhṛ" iti kubhagaṇopadeśaḥ, "ravibhūyogāḥ bhūdivasāḥ" iti bhūdivasopadeśaḥ | katham tarhi abhidhīyate? ucyate ã bhūdivasapramāṇanirdeśaḥ | evam laghutaraprakāraḥ
| tasmāt na ekam prayojanam upadeśasya etāvataḥ kāraṇam bhavitum arhati | anyat api prayojanāntaram asti iti āha | tat yathā ã kaliyātabhūbhagaṇaiḥ sarve eva grahāḥ mīnameṣasandhyudayakālāvadhayaḥ ānīyante | kali[yāta]ravimaṇḍalāhargaṇasamāsaḥ [eva] kaliyātabhūbhagaṇāḥ | taiḥ trairāśikam ã yadi yugaprasiddhabhūbhagaṇaiḥ iṣṭagrahabhagaṇāḥ mīnameṣasandhiprārabdhāḥ prāpyante, tadā kaliyātabhūbhagaṇaiḥ kiyantaḥ iti iṣṭagrahabhagaṇādayaḥ | athavā
sūryodayakālāvadheḥ eva grahāḥ ānīyante | katham? ravibhagaṇāḥ yātāhargaṇe kṣiptvā taddivasasūryarāśyādīn ca adhaḥ vinyasya iṣṭagrahabhagaṇaiḥ krameṇa saṃguṇayya svacchedaiḥ ṣaṣṭyādibhiḥ bhaktvā upari upari āropya tathā eva bhūbhagaṇaiḥ vibhajeta, labdham iṣṭagrahamaṇḍalāni | śeṣam dvādaśādiguṇitam kṛtvā tad avaśiṣṭam [adhaḥ adhaḥ] prakṣipya tathā eva ca apahṛte rāśyādayaḥ | athavā, ravimaṇḍalāhargaṇayogam dvādaśabhiḥ saṃguṇayya raviyātarāśayaḥ

children.text: prakṣipyante, triṃśatā bhāgānityādi [arghāt triṃśatā saṃguṇayya raviyātabhāgān prakṣipet iti ādi] karma kṛtvā khakhaṣaḍghanacchedarāśim nidhāya trairāśikam ã yadi yugabhūbhagaṇaiḥ abhīṣṭagrahabhagaṇāḥ labhyante, tadā khakhaṣaḍghanabhāgahārabhūbhagaṇaiḥ kiyantaḥ? tena khakhaṣaḍghanaguṇitayugabhūbhagaṇaiḥ bhāge hṛte bhagaṇādilabdhiḥ | athavā, rāśyādiguṇakārasaṃvarga- [12 x 30 x 60]-khakhaṣaḍghana-[21600]yoḥ guṇakārabhāgahārayoḥ tulyatvāt naṣṭayoḥ
children.translated_text: are added; after performing the computation beginning with 'multiply by thirty degrees' [i.e., multiply the degrees traversed by the Sun by thirty, etc.], placing the divisor as the cube of void-void-six [= 21,600], [one performs] the rule of three: if by the Earth's revolutions in a <s>yuga</s>...

The divisor for the minutes (<s>liptā</s>) of the Earth's revolutions multiplied by the desired planet's revolutions is just the Earth's revolutions in a <s>yuga</s>; the result is the minutes of the desired planet.

body.translated_text: What then is the purpose of teaching the Earth's revolutions? He says: 'The conjunctions of the Sun and Earth [are the] terrestrial days' [<s>Kālakriyā</s>, 5] — for computing the terrestrial days. This is not so, because the terrestrial days are obtainable by another method. Even if this is so...

body.text: śani ḍhuṅivaghva | pūrvavat śaniyugabhagaṇāḥ ḍhuṅvighva, kṛtaraseṣu aṅgamanavaḥ, aṅkaiḥ api 146564 | guru khricyubha | pūrvavat eva, kṛtāśviyamābdhirasāgnayaḥ, aṅkaiḥ api 364224 | tathā eva kuja bhadlijhnukhṛ, vedāśvivasurasarandhrayamāsvinaḥ, aṅkaiḥ api 2296824 |
body.translated_text: <s>Śani</s> (Saturn) <s>ḍhuṅvighva</s>: As before, Saturn's revolutions in a <s>yuga</s> are <s>ḍhuṅvighva</s> — four-arrows-limbs-nine-[arranged as:] 146,564. <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter) <s>khricyubha</s>: As before — four-horses-<s>Yama</s>-seas-flavors-fires — in numerals: 364,224. <s>Kuja</s> (Mars) <s>bhadlijhnukhṛ</s>...

body.text: bhṛgubudhasaurāḥ | bhṛguḥ ca budhaḥ ca bhṛgubudhau, tayoḥ saurāḥ | sūryasya ime saurāḥ | ke? bhagaṇāḥ | bhṛgubudhayoḥ saurāḥ, bhṛgubudhasaurāḥ | sūryasya ye bhagaṇāḥ te eva śukrabudhayoḥ api khyughṛ-saṅkhyā iti | eteṣām yugabhagaṇānām utpattipratyākhyānam "kṣitiraviyogādinakṛd" [golapādaḥ, 48] iti asyām kārikāyām vyākhyāsyāmaḥ | evam dvitīyā gītiḥ || 3 ||
body.translated_text: <s>Bhṛgubudhasaurāḥ</s>: <s>Bhṛgu</s> (Venus) and <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) [form] '<s>Bhṛgubudhau</s>' (Venus and Mercury); their [revolutions are] solar (<s>saurāḥ</s>). 'Solar' means belonging to the Sun. Which ones? The revolutions. Of Venus and Mercury, [the revolutions are] solar — [hence] '<s>bhṛgubudhasaurāḥ</s>.' The revolutions of the Sun are the same as those of Venus and Mercury...

body.text: grahoccayugabhagaṇāḥ
body.translated_text: Revolutions of the planetary apogees in a <s>yuga</s>

body.text: grahoccayugabhagaṇapratipādanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: In order to teach the revolutions of the planetary apogees (<s>ucca</s>) in a <s>yuga</s>, he states:

body.text:
candrocca rjuṣkhidha budha
suguśithṛna bhṛgu jaṣabikhuchṛ śeṣārkāḥ |
body.translated_text: The lunar apogee (<s>candrocca</s>) <s>rjuṣkhidha</s>; Mercury (<s>budha</s>) <s>suguśithṛna</s>; Venus (<s>bhṛgu</s>) <s>jaṣabikhuchṛ</s>; the rest are solar.

body.text: candrocca, rjuṣkhidha, budha, suguśithṛna, bhṛgu, jaṣabikhuchṛ, eteṣām avibhaktikaḥ nirdeśaḥ, śeṣārkāḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Candrocca</s>, <s>rjuṣkhidha</s>, <s>budha</s>, <s>suguśithṛna</s>, <s>bhṛgu</s>, <s>jaṣabikhuchṛ</s> — these are given as indeclinable notations; '<s>śeṣārkāḥ</s>' (the rest are solar).

body.text: atra api adhikṛtayugabhagaṇasaṃyogena eva vyākhyeyam | candroccasya yugabhagaṇāḥ candroccayabhagaṇāḥ, rjuṣkhidha navenduyamāṣṭavasvabdhayaḥ, aṅkaiḥ api 488219 | budha evam budhoccayugabhagaṇāḥ suguśithṛna khāśvyambaramunirāmarandhrādriśaśinaḥ, aṅkaiḥ api 17937020 | bhṛgu tathā eva bhṛgūccayugabhagaṇāḥ jaṣabikhuchṛ vasvaṣṭāgniyamāśviśūnyādrayaḥ, aṅkaiḥ api 7022388 |
body.translated_text: Here too, it is to be interpreted by connection with the governing [term] '<s>yuga</s>-revolutions.' The revolutions of the lunar apogee in a <s>yuga</s> are <s>candroccayugabhagaṇāḥ</s>: <s>rjuṣkhidha</s> — nine-moon-<s>Yama</s>-eight-<s>Vasu</s>-seas — in numerals: 488,219. Mercury (<s>budha</s>) [means] the apogee of Mercury (<s>budhocca</s>)...

body.text:
atra ayam bhṛguśabdaḥ, āhosvit bhṛgujaśabdaḥ? bhṛguḥ nāma bhagavān maharṣiḥ tasya putraḥ śukraḥ tasya ye bhagaṇāḥ nirdiśyante; tena bhṛgujaḥ iti, athavā bhārgavaḥ iti nirdeśyaḥ | yadi ayam bhṛgujaśabdaḥ, tadā ṣabikhuchṛ iti ete bhagaṇāḥ prāpnuvanti, jaṣabikhuchṛ iti ete ca iṣyante | katham tarhi atra bhṛguśabdaḥ eva vijñeyaḥ, yat uta bhṛgujaśabdaḥ? bhṛguśabdaḥ eva vijñāyate | kutaḥ? anyatra bhṛgujaśabdasya āśravaṇāt | atra śāstre bhṛgujaśabdena na
kvacit śukraḥ ācāryeṇa nirdiṣṭaḥ | tena tarhi bhṛguśabdena bhṛgugurubudhaśani iti ādi yadi api ucyate, bhārgavaśabdena nirdeśaḥ kartavyaḥ, na bhṛguśabdena, bhṛgoḥ apatyam bhārgavaḥ iti | na eṣaḥ doṣaḥ, bhṛgoḥ apatyam bhṛguḥ iti api bhavati, "yathā babhruḥ, maṇḍuḥ, lamakaḥ" [aṣṭādhyāyī, 3.1.2. pātañjalabhāṣyam] iti | babhroḥ apatyam bābhravyaḥ iti ādi vaktavye babhruḥ iti ucyate, evam māṇḍavyaḥ maṇḍuḥ | tathā eva bhārgavaḥ bhṛguḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, is this the word '<s>Bhṛgu</s>' or the word '<s>Bhṛguja</s>' (son of <s>Bhṛgu</s>)? <s>Bhṛgu</s> is the name of the blessed great sage; his son is <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) — whose revolutions (<s>bhagaṇas</s>) are being stated. Therefore, it should be designated as '<s>Bhṛguja</s>' or alternatively '<s>Bhārgava</s>.' If this is the word '<s>Bhṛguja</s>,' then the revolutions obtained would be '<s>ṣabikhuchṛ</s>,' while the desired [number] is '<s>jaṣabikhuchṛ</s>.' How then is the word '<s>Bhṛgu</s>' alone to be understood here, rather than '<s>Bhṛguja</s>'? The word '<s>Bhṛgu</s>' alone is to be understood. Why? Because the word '<s>Bhṛguja</s>' is not heard elsewhere [in this treatise]. In this treatise, <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) has never been designated by the master with the word '<s>Bhṛguja</s>.' Then, even if '<s>Bhṛgu-Guru-Budha-Śani</s>' and so forth are stated with the word '<s>Bhṛgu</s>,' the designation should be made with the word '<s>Bhārgava</s>' (descendant of <s>Bhṛgu</s>), not with the word '<s>Bhṛgu</s>' — since the offspring of <s>Bhṛgu</s> is <s>Bhārgava</s>. This is not a fault, for the offspring of <s>Bhṛgu</s> can also [be called] '<s>Bhṛgu</s>' — 'just as <s>Babhru</s>, <s>Maṇḍu</s>, <s>Lamaka</s>' [<s>Aṣṭādhyāyī</s> 3.1.2, <s>Patañjala Bhāṣya</s>]. Where one should say '<s>Bābhravya</s>' (descendant of <s>Babhru</s>) and so forth, one says '<s>Babhru</s>'; similarly, '<s>Māṇḍavya</s>' [is called] '<s>Maṇḍu</s>.' In the same way, '<s>Bhārgava</s>' [is called] '<s>Bhṛgu</s>.'

body.text:
śeṣārkāḥ | nirdiṣṭebhyaḥ ye anye te śeṣāḥ, te ca śanigurubhaumāḥ | teṣām śeṣāṇām | arkasya ime ārkāḥ | ke? bhagaṇāḥ | śeṣāṇām ārkāḥ, śeṣārkāḥ | "khyughṛ"tulyāḥ eva uccabhagaṇāḥ śanigurubhaumānām | yataḥ sūryādayaḥ vigrahavantaḥ paribhramantaḥ rāśiṣu upalakṣyante, tena teṣām bhagaṇāḥ kīrtyante | ete punar śaśyuccādayaḥ na eva lakṣyante; teṣām katham bhagaṇāḥ bhavanti, alakṣyamāṇatvāt iti? atra ucyate ã atra candrādīnām eva [svoccasthitānām
bhagaṇāḥ] | athavā sphuṭagrahagatiḥ atra sādhyate | tasyāḥ sādhanopāyāḥ madhyamaḥ, śīghraḥ, mandaḥ, paridhayaḥ, jyā iti ādayaḥ | sā ca sphuṭā grahagatiḥ etaiḥ upāyaiḥ sādhayitum śakyate, na anyathā | yathā prakṛtipratyayalopāgamavarṇavikārādibhiḥ upāyaiḥ sādhuśabdaḥ sādhyate, evam atra api | tasmāt upāyāḥ upeyasādhakāḥ | teṣām na niyamaḥ | uktam ca ã
body.translated_text: 'The remaining [planets'] — [revolutions are those] of the Sun.' Those other than the ones [already] stated are the remaining [planets], and they are <s>Śani</s> (Saturn), <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter), and <s>Bhauma</s> (Mars). Of those remaining [planets]. Those pertaining to the Sun (<s>Arka</s>) are '<s>ārka</s>' — what are they? The revolutions (<s>bhagaṇas</s>). The revolutions of the remaining [planets] pertaining to the Sun — '<s>śeṣārkāḥ</s>.' The apogee-revolutions (<s>uccabhagaṇas</s>) of <s>Śani</s>, <s>Guru</s>, and <s>Bhauma</s> are equal to '<s>khyughṛ</s>' [i.e., equal to the Sun's revolutions]. Since the Sun and other [planets], having physical bodies, are observed revolving through the zodiacal signs (<s>rāśis</s>), their revolutions are stated. But these [entities] — the apogee of the Moon and the like — are never observed; how then can they have revolutions, since they are unobservable? To this it is said: here, [the revolutions are] of the Moon and the others themselves [when situated at their own apogees]. Alternatively, the true planetary motion (<s>sphuṭagrahagati</s>) is what is to be computed here. The means for computing it are: the mean [motion] (<s>madhyama</s>), the fast [correction] (<s>śīghra</s>), the slow [correction] (<s>manda</s>), the epicycles (<s>paridhis</s>), the sines (<s>jyā</s>), and the like. And the true planetary motion can be computed by these means and not otherwise. Just as a correct word (<s>sādhuśabda</s>) is derived through the means of base, suffix, elision, augment, phonetic modification, and the like — so too here. Therefore, the means accomplish the desired [result]. There is no fixed [restriction on] them. And it has been said:

children.text: upādāyāḥ api ye heyāḥ tān upāyān pracakṣate |
children.translated_text: Those which are to be taken up [only to be] abandoned — those are called means (<s>upāyas</s>);

children.text: upāyānām ca niyamaḥ na avaśyam avatiṣṭhate ||
children.translated_text: and the [specific form of the] means does not necessarily remain fixed.

body.text: vākyapadīyam, 2.38
body.translated_text: <s>Vākyapadīya</s>, 2.38

body.text: iti | tasmāt upāyamātratvāt na doṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therefore, since they are merely means, there is no fault.

body.text: pātayugabhagaṇāḥ
body.translated_text: Revolutions of the node in a <s>yuga</s>

body.text: atha pātabhagaṇapradarśanārtham āha ã
body.translated_text: Now, for the purpose of demonstrating the revolutions of the node (<s>pāta</s>), he says:

body.text: buphinaca pātavilomā
body.translated_text: '<s>buphinaca</s>' — the retrograde [revolutions] of the node.

body.text:
adhikṛtayugabhagaṇasaṃyogāt yugapātavilomabhagaṇāḥ | buphinaca rasāśviyamadasrāgniyamāḥ, aṅkaiḥ api 232226; ete bhagaṇāḥ | pātasya vilomā viparītagatiḥ prasiddhā, tena atra anulomagatijijñāsubhiḥ maṇḍalāt viśodhyate, tasya pātasya anulomagatiḥ bhavati | sā candrāt viśodhyate | tasmāt pātaviśuddhaśeṣāt candramasaḥ kṣepaḥ sādhyate | yadi etāvatā prayojanena pātaḥ maṇḍalāt śodhya anulomaḥ kriyate atra, tarhi mahāprayāsaḥ - pātaḥ maṇḍalāt śodhyaḥ,
sa candrāt iti | katham tarhi? yaḥ eva karaṇāgatapātaḥ candramasi kṣipyate, vilomatvāt apacayaḥ kṣepaḥ iti | tasmāt uttaraḥ dakṣiṇaḥ vā vikṣepaḥ sādhyate | kim ayam candramasaḥ pātaḥ ucyate, nanu ca sarveṣām eva ayam iti? nahi, pāriśeṣyāt candrasya eva ayam pātaḥ, grahāṇām pātāḥ vakṣyante, "navarāṣaha" [gītikāí, 8] iti | tasmāt pariśiṣṭaḥ candrasya eva ayam | nanu sūryaḥ api anyaḥ asti? tasya vikṣepābhāvāt pātābhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: From the connection with the revolutions of the <s>yuga</s> under consideration, the retrograde revolutions of the node in a <s>yuga</s> [are obtained]. '<s>Buphinaca</s>' [decoded as] <s>rasāśviyamadasrāgniyamāḥ</s>, in numerals: 232,226. These are the revolutions. The retrograde motion of the node is well established; therefore, here those who wish to know its direct motion subtract [it] from the [total] circle, [and thereby] the direct motion of the node is obtained. That is subtracted from the Moon. Therefore, from the remainder after subtracting the node, the latitude (<s>kṣepa</s>) of the Moon is computed. If the node is made direct for this purpose by subtracting it from the circle, it involves great effort — [first] subtracting the node from the circle, [then] that from the Moon. How then [should it be done]? The node obtained from the computational procedure (<s>karaṇa</s>) is simply added to the Moon; because of its retrograde nature, the subtraction [itself] is the latitude (<s>kṣepa</s>). From that, the northward or southward latitude (<s>vikṣepa</s>) is computed. Is this the node of the Moon alone, or is it [the node] of all [planets]? No — by elimination (<s>pāriśeṣya</s>), this is the node of the Moon alone; the nodes of the [other] planets will be stated [later]: '<s>navarāṣaha</s>' [<s>Gītikā</s> 8]. Therefore, this is the residual [node] of the Moon alone. But is not the Sun another [planet]? Because of the absence of latitude for the Sun, there is no node [for it].

body.text: bhagaṇārambhakālādinirdeśaḥ
body.translated_text: Statement of the epoch and location for the commencement of revolutions

body.text: ete grahoccapātabhagaṇāḥ kasmin kāle, kasmin deśe, kasmāt jyotiścakrapradeśāt pravṛttāḥ iti etat na jñāyate | ataḥ tatpradarśanārtham āha ã
body.translated_text: At what time, in what place, and from what point of the celestial circle did these revolutions of planets, apogees, and nodes commence? This is not known. Therefore, for the purpose of demonstrating that, he says:

body.text: budhāhni ajārkodayāt ca laṅkāyām || 4 ||
body.translated_text: 'On a Wednesday (<s>budhāhni</s>), from the sunrise at the beginning of <s>Aja</s> (Aries), and at <s>Laṅkā</s>.' (4)

body.text: budhāhni, ajārkodayāt, ca, laṅkāyām |
body.translated_text: '<s>Budhāhni</s>' (on a Wednesday), '<s>ajārkodayāt</s>' (from the sunrise of Aries), '<s>ca</s>' (and), '<s>laṅkāyām</s>' (at <s>Laṅkā</s>).

body.text:
budhasya ahaḥ budhāhaḥ, tasmin budhāhni | nanu ca "rājāhassakhibhyaṣṭac" [aṣṭādhyāyī, 5.4.19] iti samāsānte kṛte budhāhe iti bhavitavyam | na eṣaḥ doṣaḥ, samāsāntavidheḥ anityatvāt | anityaḥ samāsāntavidhiḥ, kasmin cit bhavati kasmin cit na bhavati iti | tena budhāhni iti api bhavati | budhadivase budhādivāraḥ anantarakṛtayugapravṛttau | tena budhādivārāt kṛtayugādi ahar gaṇaḥ gaṇyate | ajārkodayāt ajaḥ meṣaḥ | arkasya udayaḥ arkodayaḥ | ajaḥ ca arkodayaḥ
ca ajārkodayaḥ | "sarvaḥ dvandvaḥ vibhāṣāyām ekavat bhavati" [aṣṭādhyāyī 2.2.29, pātañjalabhāṣyam] iti ekavat bhāvaḥ | tasmāt ajārkodayāt, meṣādeḥ arkodayāt ca | meṣādeḥ bhagaṇapradeśāt sūryodayāt ca laṅkāyām ete grahāḥ svān svān bhagaṇān bhoktum ārabdhāḥ | meṣādeḥ yasmāt ete pravṛttāḥ tasmāt eṣu graheṣu na kṣepaḥ na apacayaḥ | yasmāt sūryodayāt tasmāt ardharātryādiṣu kālaviśeṣeṣu yathā iṣṭam svabhogaiḥ sañcālanam, yataḥ laṅkāyām tataḥ anyeṣu
deśeṣu deśāntararekhāyāḥ pūrvataḥ aparataḥ vyavasthiteṣu deśāntaraphalāpacayaḥ kṣepaḥ ca | cakāra etān eva arthān samuccinoti | budhāhni arkodayāt laṅkāyām iti | evam tṛtīyā gītiḥ || 4 ||
body.translated_text: The day of <s>Budha</s> (Mercury/Wednesday) is '<s>budhāha</s>'; on that — '<s>budhāhni</s>.' Now, [one might object:] by the rule '<s>rājāhassakhibhyaṣṭac</s>' [<s>Aṣṭādhyāyī</s> 5.4.19], with the compound-final suffix applied, it should be '<s>budhāhe</s>.' This is not a fault, because of the optionality of the compound-final suffix. The compound-final rule is optional — it applies in some cases and not in others. Therefore '<s>budhāhni</s>' is also valid. On a Wednesday — the day of Mercury at the immediately preceding commencement of the <s>Kṛta Yuga</s>. Therefore, from the Wednesday onward, the day-count from the beginning of the <s>Kṛta Yuga</s> is reckoned. '<s>Ajārkodayāt</s>' — '<s>Aja</s>' is Aries (<s>Meṣa</s>). The rising of the Sun is '<s>arkodaya</s>.' Both Aries and sunrise [combined form] '<s>ajārkodaya</s>.' [By the rule:] 'Every <s>dvandva</s> compound optionally behaves as a single [entity]' [<s>Aṣṭādhyāyī</s> 2.2.29, <s>Patañjala Bhāṣya</s>] — hence the singular behavior. Therefore, from '<s>ajārkodayāt</s>' — from the sunrise at the beginning of Aries. From the point of the zodiac at the beginning of Aries and from the sunrise at <s>Laṅkā</s>, these planets commenced traversing their respective revolutions. Since they commenced from the beginning of Aries, for these planets there is no additive or subtractive correction (<s>kṣepa</s>, <s>apacaya</s>). Since [the epoch is] from sunrise, at other desired time-points such as midnight and the like, adjustment is made by their own [daily] motions. Since [the location is] <s>Laṅkā</s>, for other places situated east or west of the meridian line (<s>deśāntararekhā</s>), the longitude-correction (<s>deśāntaraphala</s>) — subtractive or additive — [is applied]. The word '<s>ca</s>' (and) combines these very meanings: on a Wednesday, from sunrise, at <s>Laṅkā</s>. Thus the third <s>gītikā</s> [is explained]. (4)

body.text: alpamānam tadgatapramāṇam ca
body.translated_text: The smallest measure and the elapsed [time
thereof]

body.text: kalpayugamanvantarāṇām gatāgatapratipādanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of demonstrating the elapsed and remaining portions of <s>kalpas</s>, <s>yugas</s>, and <s>manvantaras</s>, he says:

children.translated_text: '<s>kāhaḥ</s>' (the day of <s>Ka</s>), '<s>manavaḥ</s>' (the <s>Manus</s>), '<s>ḍha</s>'—

children.text: gāḥ śkha gatāḥ te ca manuyugāḥ chnā ca |
children.translated_text: '<s>manu-yugāḥ</s>' (the <s>yugas</s> of a <s>Manu</s>), '<s>śkha</s>' — those that have elapsed; and those <s>manu-yugāḥ</s> [are] '<s>chnā</s>';
from the beginning of the <s>kalpa</s>, the <s>yuga</s>-quarters —

children.text: ga ca gurudivasāt ca bhāratāt pūrvam || 5 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>ga</s>' — and from the day of <s>Guru</s> (Thursday/Jupiter), and before the <s>Bhārata</s> [war]. (5)

body.text: kāhaḥ, manavaḥ, ḍha iti avibhaktikaḥ nirdeśaḥ, manuyugāḥ, śkha ayam api avibhaktikaḥ eva, gatāḥ, te, ca avibhaktikaḥ, manuyugāḥ, chnā [avibhaktikaḥ], ca, kalpādeḥ, yugapādāḥ, ga avibhaktikaḥ eva, ca, gurudivasāt, ca, bhāratāt, pūrvam |
body.translated_text: '<s>Kāhaḥ</s>,' '<s>manavaḥ</s>,' '<s>ḍha</s>' — this is a designation without case-endings; '<s>manuyugāḥ</s>,' '<s>śkha</s>' — this too is without case-endings; '<s>gatāḥ</s>' (elapsed), '<s>te</s>' (those), '<s>ca</s>' — without case-endings; '<s>manuyugāḥ</s>,' '<s>chnā</s>' [without case-endings], '<s>ca</s>,' '<s>kalpādeḥ</s>' (from the beginning of the <s>kalpa</s>), '<s>yugapādāḥ</s>' (<s>yuga</s>-quarters), '<s>ga</s>' — without case-endings, '<s>ca</s>,' '<s>gurudivasāt</s>' (from the day of Jupiter/Thursday), '<s>ca</s>,' '<s>bhāratāt</s>' (from [before] the <s>Bhārata</s> [war]), '<s>pūrvam</s>' (before).

body.text: kaḥ iti prajāpateḥ ākhyānam | kasya ahaḥ kāhaḥ, brahmadivasaḥ iti arthaḥ | tasya kāhasya kiyat pramāṇam iti āha ã manavaḥ ḍha | caturdaśa manavaḥ kāhasya pramāṇam | brahmaṇaḥ divase caturdaśa manavaḥ parivartante | ekaikasya manaḥ kiyat kiyat antaram iti āha ã manuyugāḥ śkha | dvāsaptatiyugāni manaḥ manoḥ antaram | atra katham ucyate tad dvāsaptatiyugāni manoḥ antaram iti | anye punar anyathā manyante ã
body.translated_text: '<s>Ka</s>' is the designation of <s>Prajāpati</s>. The day of <s>Ka</s> is '<s>kāha</s>' — meaning the day of <s>Brahmā</s>. Of that '<s>kāha</s>' (day of <s>Brahmā</s>), what is the measure? He says: '<s>manavaḥ ḍha</s>' — fourteen <s>Manus</s> is the measure of a '<s>kāha</s>.' In a day of <s>Brahmā</s>, fourteen <s>Manus</s> revolve. What is the interval of each <s>Manu</s>? He says: '<s>manuyugāḥ śkha</s>' — seventy-two <s>yugas</s> are the interval of a <s>Manu</s>. Here, how is it said that seventy-two <s>yugas</s> are the interval of a <s>Manu</s>? Others, however, think differently:

body.text: tad ekasaptatiguṇam manvantaram iha ucyate |
body.translated_text: That [interval] is said here to be seventy-one <s>yugas</s> multiplied — a <s>manvantara</s>.

body.text: iti | ekasaptatiḥ caturyugāni manoḥ antaram | atra katham? ucyate ã ye evam manyante teṣām pūrvāparavirodhaḥ | ekasaptatiḥ caturyugāni manoḥ antaram iti uktvā ta evam punar api āha ã
body.translated_text: [They say:] seventy-one <s>caturyugas</s> (sets of four <s>yugas</s>) are the interval of a <s>Manu</s>. How [do we respond] here? It is said: those who think thus have a self-contradiction between their earlier and later [statements]. Having said that seventy-one <s>caturyugas</s> are the interval of a <s>Manu</s>, those very [authorities] also say:

children.translated_text: They know a day of <s>Brahmā</s> to be a thousand <s>yugas</s> in extent;
and the night to end in a thousand <s>yugas</s> — those people know the day and night [of <s>Brahmā</s>].

body.text: śrīmadbhagavadgītā, 8.17; manusmṛtiḥ, 1.73
body.translated_text: <s>Śrīmadbhagavadgītā</s> 8.17; <s>Manusmṛti</s> 1.73

body.text: iti | tatra ekasaptatiḥ caturdaśabhiḥ guṇitāni na eva yugasahasram bhavati | tasmāt ucyate pūrvāparavirodhaḥ | yadi ekasaptatiḥ manoḥ antaram, katham caturdaśamanvantarāṇi yugasahasram bhavati? asmākam tu dvāsaptatiḥ caturyugāni manoḥ antaram | aṣṭottaram sahasram brāhmaḥ divasaḥ iti etat upapannam |
body.translated_text: In that case, seventy-one multiplied by fourteen does not equal a thousand <s>yugas</s>. Therefore, there is a self-contradiction between their earlier and later [statements]. If seventy-one is the interval of a <s>Manu</s>, how do fourteen <s>manvantaras</s> equal a thousand <s>yugas</s>? But for us, seventy-two <s>caturyugas</s> are the interval of a <s>Manu</s>. [And] that the day of <s>Brahmā</s> is one thousand and eight — this is consistent.

body.text:
teṣu manuṣu caturdaśasu kiyantaḥ manavaḥ vyatikrāntāḥ iti āha ã gatāḥ te ca | gatāḥ ca-saṅkhyā, ṣaṭ iti arthaḥ | saptamasya manoḥ kiyanti yugāni iti āha ã manuyugāḥ chnā | manoḥ saptamasya vyatītāni saptaviṃśatiḥ yugāni | aṣṭāviṃśatitamasya yugasya pādāḥ vyatītāḥ ga trisaṅkhyāḥ kṛtatretādvāparasaṃjñitāḥ | ca pādapūraṇe | gurudivasāt ca bhāratāt pūrvam | guroḥ divasaḥ gurudivasaḥ, tasmāt gurudivasāt, bhāratāt ca pūrvam | gurudivasena upalakṣitāt
bhāratāt pūrvam iti sāmānyena abhihitatvāt kaliyugādeḥ pūrvam iti vyākhyeyam | anyathā pūrvaśabdāt atiricyate | ete manavaḥ, etāni ca yugāni, ete ca yugapādāḥ vyatikrāntāḥ | cakāra etān eva arthān samuccinoti |
body.translated_text: Among those fourteen <s>Manus</s>, how many <s>Manus</s> have elapsed? He says: '<s>gatāḥ te ca</s>' — the elapsed [<s>Manus</s>] are '<s>ca</s>'-in-number, meaning six. How many <s>yugas</s> of the seventh <s>Manu</s> [have elapsed]? He says: '<s>manuyugāḥ chnā</s>' — twenty-seven <s>yugas</s> of the seventh <s>Manu</s> have elapsed. Of the twenty-eighth <s>yuga</s>, the elapsed quarters (<s>pādas</s>) are '<s>ga</s>' — three in number, designated as <s>Kṛta</s>, <s>Tretā</s>, and <s>Dvāpara</s>. '<s>Ca</s>' is a metrical filler. 'From the day of <s>Guru</s> (Thursday) and before the <s>Bhārata</s> [war].' The day of <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter) is '<s>gurudivasa</s>' (Thursday); from that Thursday. And before the <s>Bhārata</s> [war]. Since 'before the <s>Bhārata</s> [war] characterized by a Thursday' is stated in a general manner, it should be interpreted as 'before the beginning of the <s>Kali Yuga</s>.' Otherwise, the word 'before' (<s>pūrva</s>) would be redundant. These <s>Manus</s>, these <s>yugas</s>, and these <s>yuga</s>-quarters have elapsed. The word '<s>ca</s>' combines these very meanings.

body.text: atra etat praṣṭavyam ã kim etāni yugāni yugapādāḥ ca tulyapramāṇāḥ āhosvit bhinnapramāṇāḥ iti? kecit āhuḥ bhinnapramāṇāḥ iti | tad yathā ã
body.translated_text: Here, this is to be asked: are these <s>yugas</s> and <s>yuga</s>-quarters of equal measure, or of unequal measure? Some say they are of unequal measure. Namely:

children.text: catvāri āhuḥ sahasrāṇi [varṣāṇām yat kṛtam yugam] |
children.translated_text: They say four thousand [years constitutes] the <s>Kṛta Yuga</s>;

children.text: tasya tāvat śatī sandhyā sandhyāṃśaḥ ca tathāvidhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: its dawn-period (<s>sandhyā</s>) is as many hundreds, and its twilight-portion (<s>sandhyāṃśa</s>) is likewise.
In the other three [<s>yugas</s>], together with their dawn and twilight periods,
[the durations] decrease by one — in thousands and hundreds.

body.text: manusmṛtiḥ, 1.69-70
body.translated_text: <s>Manusmṛti</s> 1.69-70

body.text:
asmākam punaḥ tatra yugapādāḥ sarve eva tulyapramāṇāḥ | anyathā atītānāgatagrahagatiparijñānam eva na ghaṭate | ayam ca yugādigatanirdeśaḥ grahagatiparijñānāya eva | tad yathā ã ṣaṇmanavaḥ vyatikrāntāḥ iti | ṣaṇṇām ca manūnām vyatītāni yugāni dvyagnyabdhayaḥ, 432 | etāni ca saptamasya manoḥ saptaviṃśatiḥ yugāni, tatsahitāni naveṣu abdhayaḥ, 459 | etāni vyatītayugāni varṣāṇi kriyante | katham? khyughṛ-saṅkhyāni varṣāṇi yugapramāṇam | tena khyughṛ-guṇāni
varṣāṇi, vasvaṣṭāśvivasturandhrarūpāṇi ayutaguṇāni, 1982880000 | etāni ca aṣṭāviṃśatitamayugasya pādatrayasya varṣāṇi kṛtāśvyagnayaḥ ayutaguṇāḥ 3240000, etaiḥ sahitāni arkartuvasurandhrarūpāṇi ayutaguṇāni 1986120000 etāvān kālaḥ kaliyugādau brahmadivasya atītaḥ | yāvanti varṣāṇi atītāni kaliyugasya tāvanti atra prakṣpya ahargaṇaḥ kriyate | asmin ahargaṇe guroḥ prabhṛti dinavāraḥ, kṛtayugādyahargaṇe budhāt, kaliyugādeḥ śukrāt | "budhāhni ajārkodayāt ca
laṅkāyām" iti kṛtayugādau budhavāsaropadeśāt kalpādeḥ guruḥ abhyūhitaḥ, kaliyugādeḥ ca bhṛguḥ | evam kalpādyaharguṇe, kṛtayugādyahargaṇe vā kriyamāṇe na kasyadit kṣepaḥ |
body.translated_text: For us, however, all the <s>yuga</s>-quarters there are of equal measure. Otherwise, the knowledge of the past and future planetary motions simply cannot be achieved. And this statement of what has elapsed from the beginning of the <s>yuga</s> is precisely for the purpose of knowing planetary motions. Namely: six <s>Manus</s> have elapsed. And the <s>yugas</s> that have elapsed of the six <s>Manus</s> are '<s>dvyagnyabdhayaḥ</s>' — 432. And these, together with the twenty-seven <s>yugas</s> of the seventh <s>Manu</s>, total '<s>naveṣu abdhayaḥ</s>' — 459. These elapsed <s>yugas</s> are converted into years. How? The number of years in a <s>yuga</s> is '<s>khyughṛ</s>'-quantity [= 4,320,000]. Therefore, multiplied by '<s>khyughṛ</s>,' the years are '<s>vasvaṣṭāśvivasturandhrarūpāṇi</s>' in ten-thousands — 1,982,880,000. And the years of the three quarters of the twenty-eighth <s>yuga</s> are '<s>kṛtāśvyagnayaḥ</s>' in ten-thousands — 3,240,000. Together with these, [the total is] '<s>arkartuvasurandhrarūpāṇi</s>' in ten-thousands — 1,986,120,000. This much time of <s>Brahmā</s>'s day has elapsed at the beginning of the <s>Kali Yuga</s>. Whatever years of the <s>Kali Yuga</s> have elapsed — adding them here, the day-count (<s>ahargaṇa</s>) is computed. In this day-count, the weekday reckoning starts from Thursday (<s>Guru</s>); in the day-count from the beginning of the <s>Kṛta Yuga</s>, from Wednesday (<s>Budha</s>); from the beginning of the <s>Kali Yuga</s>, from Friday (<s>Śukra</s>). Since '<s>budhāhni ajārkodayāt ca laṅkāyām</s>' teaches that Wednesday was [the day] at the beginning of the <s>Kṛta Yuga</s>, Thursday is inferred for the beginning of the <s>kalpa</s>, and Friday for the beginning of the <s>Kali Yuga</s>. Thus, whether one computes the day-count from the beginning of the <s>kalpa</s> or from the beginning of the <s>Kṛta Yuga</s>, there is no additive correction (<s>kṣepa</s>) for any [planet].

body.text:
yadā punaḥ kaliyugavyatītāt eva ahargaṇaḥ kriyate, tadā śaśyuccasya rāśitrayam kṣepaḥ, pātasya ṣaḍrāśayaḥ | katham? [dvāpa]rāntāhargaṇam pātabhagaṇaiḥ śaśyuccasya bhagaṇaiḥ ca pṛthak pṛthak saṃguṇayya bhūdivasaiḥ bhāgalabdhāni maṇḍalāni, śeṣe dvādaśaguṇite bhūdivasaiḥ apahṛte ṣaḍrāśayaḥ pātasya, śaśyuccasya ca trayaḥ rāśayaḥ labhyante | athavā caturbhiḥ samaiḥ yugapādaiḥ pātabhagaṇāḥ śaśyuccabhagaṇāḥ ca labhyante, tat etaiḥ samaiḥ tribhiḥ
yugapādaiḥ kiyantaḥ iti bhagaṇāḥ labhyante | śeṣe dvādaśaguṇe [caturvibhakte rāśayaḥ] iti | evam idam caturtham gītikāsūtram || 5 ||
body.translated_text: But when the accumulated day-count (<s>ahargaṇa</s>) is reckoned from the elapsed <s>Kali Yuga</s> alone, then the additive constant (<s>kṣepa</s>) for the lunar apogee is three signs, and for the node, six signs. How? Having multiplied the accumulated day-count at the end of <s>Dvāpara</s> separately by the revolutions of the node and of the lunar apogee, [and] having divided by the civil days, the quotient gives the completed cycles; when the remainder is multiplied by twelve and divided by the civil days, six signs are obtained for the node, and three signs for the lunar apogee. Alternatively, by four equal quarter-<s>yugas</s>, the revolutions of the node and of the lunar apogee are obtained; from these, by three equal quarter-<s>yugas</s>, the corresponding number of revolutions is obtained. When the remainder is multiplied by twelve [and divided by four, signs are obtained]. Thus, this is the fourth <s>gītikā</s>-sūtra. // 5 //

body.text: grahāṇām kakṣyāpramāṇāni
body.translated_text: The Dimensions of Planetary Orbits

body.text: ete grahāḥ bhramantaḥ kiyatpramāṇāsu kakṣyāsu bhramanti iti etat na jñāyate, tatjñānārtham āha ã
body.translated_text: These planets revolve — but in orbits of what dimensions do they revolve? This is not known. For the purpose of knowing that, he says:

children.translated_text: The signs of the Moon [multiplied by] twelve [give] the circle;
those [converted to] degrees, minutes, and <s>yojanas</s> [by] the multipliers <s>ya</s>, <s>va</s>, <s>ña</s>.
In one breath (<s>prāṇa</s>), the asterism-sphere traverses one minute;
the velocity of a planet [is measured] by the share of the sky-<s>yuga</s>; the Sun by the share of the asterisms. // 6 //

body.text: śaśirāśayaḥ, ṭha avibhaktikaḥ, cakram, te, aṃśakalāyojanāni, ya-va-ña-guṇāḥ, prāṇena, eti, kalām, bham, khayugāṃśe, grahajavaḥ, bhavāṃśe, arkaḥ |
body.translated_text: Word-by-word analysis:

<s>śaśirāśayaḥ</s> (signs of the Moon), <s>ṭha</s> (twelve, uninflected), <s>cakram</s> (circle), <s>te</s> (those), <s>aṃśakalāyojanāni</s> (degrees, minutes, and <s>yojanas</s>), <s>ya-va-ña-guṇāḥ</s> (multiplied by <s>ya</s>, <s>va</s>, <s>ña</s>), <s>prāṇena</s> (in one breath), <s>eti</s> (traverses), <s>kalām</s> (one minute), <s>bham</s> (the asterism-sphere), <s>khayugāṃśe</s> (by the share of the sky-<s>yuga</s>), <s>grahajavaḥ</s> (the velocity of the planet), <s>bhavāṃśe</s> (by the share of the asterisms), <s>arkaḥ</s> (the Sun).

body.text:
śaśigrahaṇāt abhihitāḥ śaśibhagaṇāḥ parigṛhyante | te śaśibhagaṇāḥ rāśayaḥ kartavyāḥ | katham iti āha ã ṭha cakram, dvādaśarāśayaḥ cakram bhavati iti | śaśibhagaṇāḥ cakrasaṃjñitāḥ dvādaśabhiḥ guṇyante, tataḥ te rāśayaḥ bhavanti | te rāśayaḥ aṃśakalāyojanāni kartavyāḥ | katham iti āha ã te aṃśakalāyojanāni ya-va-ña-guṇāḥ | "ya"guṇāḥ rāśayaḥ aṃśāḥ, "va"guṇāḥ kalāḥ, "ña"guṇāḥ yojanāni | evam imāni ākāśakakṣyāyojanāni bhavanti |
vyomāmbarakharasādrīṣukhayamādrisāgarādivedaravayaḥ, aṅkaiḥ api 12474720576000, ākāśakakṣyā | yāvantam ākāśapradeśam raveḥ mayūkhāḥ samantāt dyotayanti tāvān pradeśaḥ khagolasya paridhiḥ, khakakṣyā | anyathā hi aparimitatvāt ākāśasya parimāṇākhyānam na upapadyate |
body.translated_text: By the word '<s>śaśi</s>' (Moon), the revolutions of the Moon that have been stated are taken up. Those revolutions of the Moon are to be converted into signs. How? He says: '<s>ṭha cakram</s>' — twelve signs make one circle. The revolutions of the Moon, designated as circles, are multiplied by twelve; then they become signs. Those signs are to be converted into degrees, minutes, and <s>yojanas</s>. How? He says: 'those [converted to] degrees, minutes, and <s>yojanas</s> [by] the multipliers <s>ya</s>, <s>va</s>, <s>ña</s>.' The signs multiplied by '<s>ya</s>' give degrees; multiplied by '<s>va</s>' give minutes; multiplied by '<s>ña</s>' give <s>yojanas</s>. Thus, these become the <s>yojanas</s> of the sky-orbit (<s>ākāśakakṣyā</s>): [in alphanumeric notation] <s>vyomāmbarakharasādrīṣukhayamādrisāgarādivedaravayaḥ</s>, and in numerals: 12,474,720,576,000 — the sky-orbit. The extent of space that the rays of the Sun illuminate on all sides — that extent is the circumference of the celestial sphere (<s>khagola</s>), [which is] the sky-orbit. For otherwise, since space is unlimited, an account of its measure would not be possible.

body.text:
candramasaḥ liptā daśayojanāni iti ataḥ aṇutvāt candrabhagaṇaiḥ eva upadiṣṭā khakakṣyā | anyeṣām bhagaṇaiḥ api eṣā śakyate eva | nanu tad yathā ã raveḥ yugabhagaṇāḥ liptīkṛtāḥ dvayekāgnirāmanavakāḥ daśalakṣābhyastāḥ, te ca aṅkaiḥ api 93312000000 | raveḥ liptāyojanāni rāmāgnīndavaḥ, yojanāṣṭādaśasahastrabhāgāḥ ca randhravasvagniravayaḥ, aṅkaiḥ api likhyante
  133
12389
18000 |
etaiḥ yojanaiḥ yojanabhāgaiḥ ca guṇitāḥ yugaraviliptāḥ khakakṣyāyojanāni bhavanti | śanaiḥ carasya api liptāyojanāni khavedarandhrāgnayaḥ, rūpābdhirasāṅgarāmāṃśāḥ khākāśāṣṭādrīndavaḥ, aṅkaiḥ api
  3940
17800
36641 |
etaiḥ yugaśanaiḥ caraliptāḥ guṇitāḥ tāni eva khakakṣyāyojanāni bhavanti | evam anyabhagaṇebhyaḥ api khakakṣyāyojanāni bhavanti |
body.translated_text: One minute (<s>liptā</s>) of the Moon equals ten <s>yojanas</s>; therefore, because of the smallness [of the unit], the sky-orbit has been specified using the revolutions of the Moon alone. It can indeed [be computed] from the revolutions of the other [planets] as well. For instance: The revolutions of the Sun in a <s>yuga</s>, converted to minutes, are [in notation] 'two-one-fire-Rāma-nine' [with] ten-<s>lakṣa</s> multiplication — in numerals: 93,312,000,000. The <s>yojanas</s> per minute of the Sun are '<s>Rāma-Agni-Indu</s>' (i.e., the integer part), and <s>yojana</s>-eighteen-thousandths are '<s>randhra-vasu-agni-rava</s>' — written in numerals as 133 and 12389/18000. When the minutes of the Sun in a <s>yuga</s> are multiplied by these <s>yojanas</s> and <s>yojana</s>-fractions, the sky-orbit <s>yojanas</s> are obtained. The <s>yojanas</s> per minute of Saturn too are '<s>kha-veda-randhra-agni</s>' [as the integer part], and '<s>rūpa-abdhi-rasa-aṅga-rāma</s>' over '<s>kha-ākāśa-aṣṭa-adri-indu</s>' — in numerals: 3940 and 17800/36641. When the minutes of Saturn in a <s>yuga</s> are multiplied by these, those very sky-orbit <s>yojanas</s> are obtained. Similarly, the sky-orbit <s>yojanas</s> can be obtained from the revolutions of the other [planets] as well.

body.text:
prāṇena eti kalām bham | nanu ca atra kakṣyāḥ prakrāntāḥ, tāsu prakrāntāsu "prāṇena eti kalām bham" iti etat aprākaraṇikam | na etat asti | etāni sūtrāṇi | sūtreṣu ca kecit arthāḥ prākaraṇikāḥ kecit aprākaraṇikāḥ, vicitratvāt sūtrāṇām | prāṇena ucchvāsena, eti gacchati, kalām liptām, bham jyotiścakram | pravaheṇa-ākṣipyamāṇam jyotiścakram kalām eti ucchvāsatulyena kālena | jyotiścakram liptānām khakhaṣaḍghanam, tat ahorātreṇa paryeti | ahorātrasya
prāṇāḥ khakhaṣaḍghanatulyāḥ | tena kalāḥ ca jyotiścakrasambandhāḥ prāṇāḥ ca tulyāḥ | tasmāt chāyākaraṇādiṣu prāṇeṣu eva jyādikam karma pravartate | jyotiścakrāhorātrayoḥ ādiḥ ravyudayāt iti kālakriyāpāde vistareṇa vyākhyāsyāmaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'In one breath, the asterism-sphere traverses one minute.' Now, orbits are the topic under discussion; while those are being discussed, 'in one breath the asterism-sphere traverses one minute' is not pertinent to the topic. This is not so. These are <s>sūtras</s> (aphorisms), and in <s>sūtras</s>, some matters are pertinent to the topic and some are not, because of the varied nature of <s>sūtras</s>. 'In one breath' (<s>prāṇena</s>) — in one exhalation; 'traverses' — goes; 'one minute' (<s>kalām</s>) — one <s>liptā</s>; 'the asterism-sphere' (<s>bham</s>) — the circle of stars. The circle of stars, being driven by the <s>pravaha</s> wind, traverses one minute in a time equal to one breath. The circle of stars [has] minutes equal to the cube of sixty (<s>khakhaṣaḍghana</s>); it completes one full revolution in a day-and-night. The <s>prāṇas</s> (breaths) of a day-and-night are equal to the cube of sixty. Therefore, the minutes belonging to the circle of stars and the <s>prāṇas</s> are equal [in number]. For this reason, in shadow calculations and the like, the arc-computation and similar operations are carried out in terms of <s>prāṇas</s> only. That the beginning of the circle of stars and of the day-and-night is from the rising of the Sun — this we shall explain in detail in the <s>Kālakriyāpāda</s> (chapter on time-reckoning).

body.text:
grahakakṣyāpradarśanārtham āha ã khayugāṃśe grahajavaḥ | kha iti anena pūrvanirdiṣṭā khakakṣyā parigṛhyate | yugagrahaṇena yugasambandhinaḥ grahāṇām bhagaṇāḥ parigṛhyante | yadi khayugāṃśe grahajavaḥ iti yugam parigṛhyate, ekatvāt yugasya ekā eva sarveṣām grahāṇām kakṣyā syāt | khasya yugāṃśaḥ khayugāṃśaḥ | khakakṣyāyāḥ svaiḥ svaiḥ yugabhagaṇaiḥ bhāge hṛte yat labdham tat yugāṃśaḥ | tasmin yugāṃśe | grahāṇām javaḥ grahajavaḥ | javaḥ
vegaḥ gatiḥ iti arthāntaram | tāvati paridhipradeśe grahāḥ paribhramanti, svaiḥ svaiḥ gativiśeṣaiḥ | khakakṣyāyām svaiḥ svaiḥ yugabhagaṇaiḥ bhāge hṛte yathāsvam grahakakṣyāḥ bhavanti | [katham?] ucyate ã trairāśikagaṇitaviśeṣeṇa | "ṣaṣṭyā sūryābdānām" [kālakriyāí, 12] iti atra khyughṛ-tulyaiḥ arkavarṣaiḥ khakakṣyātulyāni yojanāni sarve eva grahāḥ pūrayanti iti vakṣyati | tena yadi etāvadbhiḥ yugabhagaṇaiḥ iṣṭagrahasya [= iṣṭagrahasya yugabhagaṇaiḥ] khakakṣyā
[labhyate], tataḥ ekena bhagaṇena kā iti svakakṣyā labhyate |
body.translated_text: For the purpose of showing the planetary orbits, he says: 'The velocity of a planet [is measured] by the share of the sky-<s>yuga</s>.' By '<s>kha</s>' (sky), the sky-orbit previously specified is taken up. By '<s>yuga</s>,' the revolutions of the planets belonging to a <s>yuga</s> are taken up. If '[the velocity of a planet is measured] by the share of the sky-<s>yuga</s>,' [and] a <s>yuga</s> is taken up — since the <s>yuga</s> is one, there would be only one orbit for all planets. [But] '<s>khasya yugāṃśaḥ</s>' means the <s>yuga</s>-share of the sky[-orbit]. When the sky-orbit is divided by the respective <s>yuga</s>-revolutions of each [planet], the quotient is the <s>yuga</s>-share. In that <s>yuga</s>-share, the velocity (<s>java</s>) of the planets [is measured] — <s>java</s> means speed or motion, these being synonymous. In that much circumferential extent, the planets revolve, each with its own particular speed. When the sky-orbit is divided by the respective <s>yuga</s>-revolutions of each [planet], the corresponding planetary orbits are obtained. How? It is stated: By the specific rule of proportions (<s>trairāśika</s>). 'In sixty <s>sūrya</s> years' [<s>Kālakriyāpāda</s>, 12] — it will be stated there that in the number of solar years equal to the <s>yuga</s> [divided by sixty?], all planets complete <s>yojanas</s> equal to the sky-orbit. Therefore, if the sky-orbit is obtained by so many <s>yuga</s>-revolutions of a given planet [= by the <s>yuga</s>-revolutions of the desired planet], then from one revolution, what [is obtained]? — thus, one's own orbit is obtained.

body.text:
bhavāṃśe arkaḥ | bhasya vāṃśaḥ bhavāṃśaḥ, nakṣatraparidheḥ ṣaṣṭyaṃśaḥ sūryakakṣyā bhavati | katham ucyate nakṣatrakakṣyāyāḥ ṣaṣṭibhāgaḥ sūryakakṣyā iti, nakṣatrakakṣyāyāḥ asiddhatvāt? na atra sūryakakṣyā abhidhīyate | kim tarhi? nakṣatrakakṣyā | katham? yā atra sūryakakṣyā sā nakṣatrakakṣyāyāḥ ṣaṣṭibhāgaḥ | sūryakakṣyā ca "khayugāṃśe grahajavaḥ" iti anena siddhā yadi nakṣatrakakṣyāyāḥ ṣaṣṭibhāgaḥ tadā sarvā nakṣātrakakṣyā kiyatī bhavati
iti ṣaṣṭyā guṇyate, tadā tasyāḥ nakṣatrakakṣyāyāḥ pramāṇam bhavati | sā ca vasugaganāmbaraśūnyarasāśvirāmādriśaśinaḥ, aṅkaiḥ api 173260008 | vicitratvāt gaṇitanirdeśasya kvacit rāśiḥ sakalaḥ abhidhīyate, kvacit rāśeḥ ekadeśaḥ | atra punaḥ rāśeḥ ekadeśena ṣaṣṭyaṃśena sakalaḥ rāśiḥ abhyūhyate |
body.translated_text: 'The Sun by the share of the asterisms.' The sixtieth part of the asterism-circumference (<s>bha</s>) is '<s>bhavāṃśa</s>'; the sixtieth part of the <s>nakṣatra</s> circumference is the solar orbit. How can it be said that the sixtieth part of the <s>nakṣatra</s>-orbit is the solar orbit, when the <s>nakṣatra</s>-orbit is not yet established? Here, it is not the solar orbit that is stated — rather, it is the <s>nakṣatra</s>-orbit. How? The solar orbit as obtained here — that is a sixtieth part of the <s>nakṣatra</s>-orbit. And the solar orbit has been established by 'the velocity of a planet by the share of the sky-<s>yuga</s>' — if it is a sixtieth part of the <s>nakṣatra</s>-orbit, then the entire <s>nakṣatra</s>-orbit — how large is it? — is obtained by multiplying by sixty, and then the measure of that <s>nakṣatra</s>-orbit results. And it is [in notation] <s>vasugaganāmbaraśūnyarasāśvirāmādriśaśinaḥ</s> — in numerals: 173,260,008. Because of the varied nature of mathematical expression, sometimes a complete quantity is stated, sometimes only a fraction of the quantity. Here, however, from a fraction — the sixtieth part — the complete quantity is to be inferred.

body.text: iṣṭagrahakakṣyābhiḥ iṣṭagrahayojanakarṇāḥ ānīyante | yadi ã
body.translated_text: From the orbits of the desired planets, the <s>yojana</s>-radii of the desired planets are derived. If:

body.text:
caturadhikam śatam aṣṭaguṇam dvāṣaṣṭiḥ tathā sahasrāṇām |
[gaṇitapādaḥ, 10]
body.translated_text: One hundred and four, multiplied by eight, and sixty-two, and likewise thousands — [<s>Gaṇitapāda</s>, 10]

body.text: iti etāvatā paridhinā ayutapramāṇaviṣkambhārdham labhyate, tadā iṣṭakakṣyāparidhinā kim iti tatkakṣyāyojanaviṣkambhārdham labhyate | tad eva yojanakarṇaḥ svasphuṭajijñāṃsubhiḥ sphuṭīkriyate | yadi vyāsārdhaliptābhiḥ iyāniṣṭayojanakarṇaḥ labhyate, tadā tena aviśeṣakarṇena bhūtārāgrahavivareṇa kiyān yojanakarṇaḥ iti sphuṭayojanakarṇaḥ labhyate | evam idam pañcamam gītikāsūtram || 6 ||
body.translated_text: — by this much circumference, a semi-diameter of ten thousand is obtained — then from the circumference of the desired orbit, the semi-diameter in <s>yojanas</s> of that orbit is obtained. That very [semi-diameter in <s>yojanas</s>] is the <s>yojana</s>-radius, which those desiring the true [positions] render accurate (<s>sphuṭa</s>). If by the semi-diameter in minutes, a given <s>yojana</s>-radius is obtained, then by the corrected radius — the separation between the earth, star, and planet — what <s>yojana</s>-radius [is obtained]? — thus, the true <s>yojana</s>-radius is obtained. Thus, this is the fifth <s>gītikā</s>-sūtra. // 6 //

body.text: bhū-śaśi-grahāṇām vyāsāḥ
body.translated_text: The Diameters of the Earth, Moon, and Planets

body.text: yojanāni iti uktam | teṣām yojanānām pramāṇam na jñāyate | tatparijñānārtham bhūgrahāṇām vyāsapramāṇapratipādanārtham ca āha ã
body.translated_text: '<s>Yojanas</s>' has been mentioned. The measure of those <s>yojanas</s> is not known. For the purpose of knowing that, and for presenting the diameter-measures of the earth and planets, he says:

children.translated_text: '<s>Nṛṣi</s>' (eight thousand men) [equals one] <s>yojana</s>; '<s>ñilā</s>' [is] the earth's

children.text: vyāsaḥ arkendvoḥ ghriñā giṇa, ka meroḥ |
children.translated_text: diameter; of the Sun and Moon, '<s>ghriñā</s>' [and] '<s>giṇa</s>'; '<s>ka</s>' [is that] of <s>Meru</s>.
<s>Venus</s>, <s>Jupiter</s>, <s>Mercury</s>, <s>Saturn</s>, [and] <s>Mars</s>
are [respectively] fractions of the Moon[-diameter given by] '<s>ṅa</s>', '<s>ña</s>', '<s>ṇa</s>', '<s>na</s>', '<s>ma</s>'; [the star-diameter is] equal to the Sun. // 7 //

body.text: nṛṣi avibhaktikaḥ, yojanam, ñilā avibhaktikaḥ, bhūvyāsaḥ, arkendvoḥ, ghbiñā giṇa ka iti ete avibhaktikāḥ nirdeśāḥ, meroḥ, bhṛgu-guru-budha-śani-bhaumāḥ, śaśi-ṅa-ña-ṇa-na-māṃśakāḥ, samāḥ, arkasamāḥ |
body.translated_text: [Word analysis:] '<s>nṛṣi</s>' (uninflected), <s>yojanam</s> (<s>yojana</s>), '<s>ñilā</s>' (uninflected), <s>bhūvyāsaḥ</s> (earth-diameter), <s>arkendvoḥ</s> (of the Sun and Moon), '<s>ghbiñā</s>' '<s>giṇa</s>' '<s>ka</s>' — these are uninflected specifications, <s>meroḥ</s> (of <s>Meru</s>), <s>bhṛgu-guru-budha-śani-bhaumāḥ</s> (<s>Venus</s>, <s>Jupiter</s>, <s>Mercury</s>, <s>Saturn</s>, <s>Mars</s>), <s>śaśi-ṅa-ña-ṇa-na-māṃśakāḥ</s> (fractions of the Moon [designated by] '<s>ṅa</s>', '<s>ña</s>', '<s>ṇa</s>', '<s>na</s>', '<s>ma</s>'), <s>samāḥ</s> (equal), <s>arkasamāḥ</s> (equal to the Sun).

body.text: nṛṇām ṣi nṛṣi, aṣṭau puruṣasahasrāṇi | nṛṣiḥ eva yojanam nṛṣi yojanam | "puruṣaḥ dhanurdaṇḍaḥ naraḥ" iti paryāyāḥ | etat uktam bhavati ã aṣṭau dhanussahasrāṇi yojanam | anena yojanapramāṇena ñilā bhūvyāsaḥ | "ñilā" iti pañcāśaduttaram sahasram | ñilā eva bhūvyāsaḥ ñilā bhūvyāsaḥ, "vyāsaḥ viṣkambhaḥ vistaraḥ" iti paryāyāḥ |
body.translated_text: '<s>Nṛṣi</s>' — <s>ṣi</s> of <s>nṛ</s> (men): eight thousand men. '<s>Nṛṣi</s>' itself is a <s>yojana</s> — '<s>nṛṣi yojanam</s>.' '<s>Puruṣa</s>' (man), '<s>dhanurdaṇḍa</s>' (bow-staff), and '<s>nara</s>' (person) are synonyms. What this says is: eight thousand bow-lengths (<s>dhanus</s>) make one <s>yojana</s>. By this <s>yojana</s>-measure, '<s>ñilā</s>' is the earth-diameter. '<s>Ñilā</s>' means one thousand and fifty. '<s>Ñilā</s>' itself is the earth-diameter — '<s>ñilā bhūvyāsaḥ</s>.' '<s>Vyāsa</s>' (diameter), '<s>viṣkambha</s>' (breadth), and '<s>vistara</s>' (expanse) are synonyms.

body.text:
anye punar anyathā manyante ã jambūdvīpaviṣkambhaḥ, tataḥ dviguṇottarāḥ samudrāḥ dvīpāḥ ca iti anayā prakriyayā dviguṇaśreḍhyāḥ caturdaśagacchāyāḥ yat sarvadhanam tāvat pramāṇam tasya iti | etat api ca golapāde vistāreṇa vicārya pratyākhyāsyāmaḥ | anyat ca tatra eva akṣonnatyā bhūparidhiyojanānayanam upadekṣyāmaḥ | atha tu purāṇe gaṅgādvārakumāryantarālam yojanasahasram ucyate | tat ca [na] pratyakṣeṇa upalabhyate | tat yathā ã laṅkojjayinyoḥ
antarālam yojanānām śatadvayam | laṅkātaḥ dūrat uttareṇa kumārī | tathā ca kumāryujjayinyoḥ antarālam na yojanaśatadvayam api pūryate | ujjayinyāḥ gaṅgādvāram na yojanaśatamātram api | evam gaṅgādvārakumāryantarālam yojanaśatatrayam api na pūryate, kim ucyate yojanasahasram iti | atha anye manyante viṣayāntarabahutvāt bhuvaḥ mahattvam iti | yathā pāraśava-kulaparvata-[ku]ru- prabhṛtayaḥ deśāḥ yojanaśatasaṅkhyayā śrūyante, tena bhuvaḥ mahattvam
iti | tat ca na, golākāratvāt bhuvaḥ | tatpṛṣṭhaparidhyuparicakravyavasthitāḥ ete deśāḥ iti etat sarvam eva sambhavati | athavā tatra alpapramāṇāni yojanāni śrūyante, yena ekena divasena viṃśatimātrāṇi yojanāni gacchanti iti | tasmāt etāvān eva bhūvyāsaḥ |
body.translated_text: Others, however, think differently: the diameter of <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>, then oceans and continents each doubling in succession — by this method, the total of a geometric series of fourteen terms [is taken as] the measure of that [earth]. This too we shall examine in detail and reject in the <s>Golapāda</s> (chapter on the sphere). And there, we shall also teach the derivation of the earth's circumference in <s>yojanas</s> from the latitude-elevation. But in the <s>Purāṇas</s>, the distance from <s>Gaṅgādvāra</s> to <s>Kumārī</s> is said to be one thousand <s>yojanas</s>. And that is not confirmed by direct observation. For instance: the distance between <s>Laṅkā</s> and <s>Ujjayinī</s> is two hundred <s>yojanas</s>. <s>Kumārī</s> is far to the south of <s>Laṅkā</s>. And yet the distance between <s>Kumārī</s> and <s>Ujjayinī</s> does not even amount to two hundred <s>yojanas</s>. From <s>Ujjayinī</s> to <s>Gaṅgādvāra</s> is not even one hundred <s>yojanas</s>. Thus, the distance from <s>Gaṅgādvāra</s> to <s>Kumārī</s> does not even amount to three hundred <s>yojanas</s> — how then can it be said to be one thousand <s>yojanas</s>? Now, others think that the earth is large because of the multitude of different regions — such as the countries <s>Pāraśava</s>, <s>Kulaparvata</s>, <s>Kuru</s>, and so forth, which are heard [in scriptures] as being of hundreds of <s>yojanas</s>; therefore the earth is large. But this is not so, because of the spherical shape of the earth. All these regions are situated upon the circumferential circle on the surface of the earth — and all this is entirely possible. Or, smaller <s>yojanas</s> are referred to there, by which one travels approximately twenty <s>yojanas</s> in a single day. Therefore, the earth-diameter is exactly this much.

body.text:
bhūvyāsaḥ gaṇitena api ānetum śakyate | tat yathā ã sphuṭatithiḥ tāvat sūryagrahaṇe pūrvāparayoḥ kapālayoḥ pare [= parame tithau] vijñāyate eva | tatra parāyām [=amāyām] tithau udayāstamayayoḥ catasraḥ nāḍikāḥ apacīyante upacīyante vā | tatra kāle dṛgjyā vyasārdham, ādityasya [lambanam] madhyamagatyā tisraḥ liptāḥ ṣaṭpañcāśadviliptāḥ ca [3' 56''] | candramasaḥ api dvāpañcāśalliptikāḥ sārdhāḥ [52' 30''] | ubhayoḥ api sūryācandramasoḥ viparītakarmaṇā
svābhiḥ svābhiḥ lambanaliptābhiḥ svayojanakarṇāvabhyasya, dṛggatijyayā vyāsārdhatulyayā vibhajya, sūryācandramasoḥ bhūvyāsārdham pṛthak pṛthak labhyate | taddviguṇam bhūvyāsaḥ | ataḥ suṣṭhu uktam ācāryeṇa "ñilā bhūvyāsaḥ" iti |
body.translated_text: The earth-diameter can also be derived by computation. As follows: First, the true <s>tithi</s> (lunar day) during a solar eclipse is determined for both the eastern and western hemispheres at the extreme <s>tithi</s>. There, at the extreme <s>tithi</s> (new moon), four <s>nāḍikās</s> (time-units) are subtracted or added at the [moments of] rising and setting. At that time, the sight-sine (<s>dṛgjyā</s>) equals the semi-diameter. The parallax (<s>lambana</s>) of the Sun, by mean motion, is three minutes and fifty-six seconds [3' 56'']. That of the Moon is also fifty-two and a half minutes [52' 30'']. For both the Sun and the Moon, by the reverse operation, having multiplied the respective parallax-minutes by the respective <s>yojana</s>-radii, and dividing by the sight-motion-sine (which equals the semi-diameter), the semi-diameter of the earth in <s>yojanas</s> is obtained separately for the Sun and Moon. Doubling that gives the earth-diameter. Therefore, it is well stated by the master: '<s>ñilā bhūvyāsaḥ</s>' (the earth-diameter is 1,050 [<s>yojanas</s>]).

body.text:
arkaḥ ca induḥ ca arkendū, tayoḥ arkendvoḥ, vyāsaḥ iti anuvartamānāt, ghriñā catuścatvāriṃśacchatāni daśottarāṇi [4490] arkasya vyāṃsaḥ | indoḥ giṇa śatatrayam pañcadaśottaram [315] | sūryācandramasoḥ yojanavyāsau etau | liptābhiḥ vyavahāraḥ iti liptāvyāsaḥ kriyate ã yadi svayojanakraṇena vyāsārdhaliptāḥ labhyante tadā yojanavyāsaiḥ kiyantaḥ iti liptāvyāsalabdhiḥ, madhyamayojanakarṇena madhyamaḥ, sphuṭena sphuṭaḥ | ka meroḥ | meroḥ ekayojanam vyāsaḥ
| etat api ca "meruḥ yojanamātraḥ" [golapādaḥ, 11] iti asyām kārikāyām vakṣyāmaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Arka</s> (Sun) and <s>Indu</s> (Moon) — <s>arkendū</s>; of those two, <s>arkendvoḥ</s> (of the Sun and Moon). Since '<s>vyāsa</s>' (diameter) continues from [the previous verse], the diameter of the Sun is <s>ghriñā</s> — four thousand four hundred and ninety [4490 <s>yojanas</s>]. Of the Moon, <s>giṇa</s> — three hundred and fifteen [315]. These are the <s>yojana</s>-diameters of the Sun and Moon. Since the calculation is done in <s>liptās</s> (arc-minutes), the <s>liptā</s>-diameter is computed: if from one's own <s>yojana</s>-<s>karṇa</s> (hypotenuse/distance) the <s>liptās</s> of half the diameter are obtained, then from the <s>yojana</s>-diameter, how many [<s>liptās</s>]? — this gives the <s>liptā</s>-diameter. With the mean <s>yojana-karṇa</s>, [one gets] the mean [diameter]; with the true [distance], the true [diameter]. <s>Ka</s> [denotes] <s>Meru</s>. The diameter of <s>Meru</s> is one <s>yojana</s>. And this too we shall state in the verse '<s>Meruḥ yojanamātraḥ</s>' (Meru is one <s>yojana</s> in extent) [<s>Golapāda</s>, 11].

body.text:
bhṛgu-guru-budha-śani-bhaumāḥ | bhṛguḥ ca guruḥ ca budhaḥ ca śaniḥ ca bhaumaḥ ca bhṛgugurubudhaśanibhaumāḥ | atra api ṣaṣṭyā nirdeśaḥ yuktaḥ, bhṛgugurubudhaśanibhaumānām vyāsaḥ iti | na etat asti | yadā vyatirekaḥ vivakṣitaḥ tadā vyatirekalakṣaṇā ṣaṣṭhī bhavati | yadā punar vyatirekan eva na vivkṣitaḥ tadā ṣaṣṭhī na utpadyate | tat yathā kaścit kañcana bravīti "ādityasya bimbam paśa" iti | tadābimbavyatirekeṇa ādityaḥ, ādityavyatirekaṇa vā bimbam
nirdiṣṭam bhavati | yadā punar avyatirekavivakṣā tadā yat eva bimbam sa eva ādityaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Bhṛgu</s> (Venus), <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter), <s>Budha</s> (Mercury), <s>Śani</s> (Saturn), and <s>Bhauma</s> (Mars) — <s>bhṛgugurubudhaśanibhaumāḥ</s>. Here too, the genitive case is appropriate — 'the diameter of Venus, Jupiter, Mercury, Saturn, and Mars.' This is not so. When distinction is intended, the genitive marking distinction applies. But when distinction is not intended at all, the genitive does not arise. For example, when someone tells another: 'Look at the disc of the Sun' — then either the Sun is indicated as distinct from the disc, or the disc as distinct from the Sun. But when non-distinction is intended, whatever is the disc is indeed the Sun itself.

body.text:
na īkṣeta udyantam ādityam na astam yāntam kadācana
[manusṛtiḥ, 4.37]
body.translated_text: 'One should not look at the rising Sun, nor ever at the setting one.' [<s>Manusmṛti</s>, 4.37]

body.text: iti ādi | atra api ayam eva | bimbāvyatiriktāḥ grahāḥ nirdiśyante | śaśi-ṅa-ña-ṇa-na-ma-aṃśakāḥ | śaśivyāṃsasya anantaroktasya ṅa-ña-ṇa-na-māṃśakāḥ, ete bhṛgu-guru-budha-śani-bhaumāḥ | śaśivyāsasya ṅāṃśaḥ bhṛguḥ pañcabhāgaḥ, ñāṃśaḥ guruḥ daśabhāgaḥ, ṇāṃśaḥ budhaḥ pañcadaśabhāgaḥ, nāṃśaḥ śaniḥ viṃśatibhāgaḥ, māṃśaḥ bhaumaḥ pañcaviṃśatibhāgaḥ | etāni candrakakṣyāpramāṇaparimāṇāni grahāṇām vyāsayojanāni |
body.translated_text: And so forth. Here too it is the same. The planets that are non-different from their discs are being referred to. '<s>Śaśi-ṅa-ña-ṇa-na-ma-aṃśakāḥ</s>' — [the diameters of Venus, Jupiter, Mercury, Saturn, and Mars are] the <s>ṅa</s>, <s>ña</s>, <s>ṇa</s>, <s>na</s>, and <s>ma</s> fractions of the Moon's diameter stated just previously. The <s>ṅa</s>-fraction of the Moon's diameter is Venus — one-fifth; the <s>ña</s>-fraction is Jupiter — one-tenth; the <s>ṇa</s>-fraction is Mercury — one-fifteenth; the <s>na</s>-fraction is Saturn — one-twentieth; the <s>ma</s>-fraction is Mars — one-twenty-fifth. These are the <s>yojana</s>-diameters of the planets measured by the standard of the Moon's orbit.

body.text:
atha kim iti svakakṣyāpramāṇasambhavāni eva ca yojanāni na ucyante? ayam ācāryasya abhiprāyaḥ ã yadi grahāṇām svakakṣyāniṣpannāni vyāsayojanāni abhidhīyante tadā vyāsaliptānayane svakakṣyotpannāḥ sphuṭayojanakarṇāḥ bhāgahārāḥ syuḥ, lambanadṛkkṣepaliptānayane ca | tathā grahāṇām manāg api lambanadṛkkṣepaliptāḥ na syuḥ | dṛśyante ca teṣām lambananativiśeṣāḥ | tadartham atra bhāgahārāḥ pradarśyante | katham? śaśi-ṅa-ña-ṇa-na-ma-aṃśakāḥ
iti | śaśivyāsasya yojanapramāṇasya liptānayane śaśiyojanakarṇaḥ bhāgahāraḥ | tena sa bhāgahāraḥ pañcādibhiḥ guṇyate | sa tāvat chedaḥ śaśivyāsaḥ śukrādivyāsaḥ bhavati |
