uparimāṃśaḥ vyāsārdhena guṇitaḥ chedena vibhaktaḥ liptāgataḥ grahavyāsaḥ bhavati madhyamaḥ | sphuṭārtham punar yathā ã svabhūtārāgrahavivareṇa chedān saṃguṇayya vyāsārdhena vibhajet, sphuṭāḥ bhavanti | te eva grahayogeṣu bhūvyāsārdhaguṇitasya svadṛggateḥ svadṛkkṣepasya ca bhāgahārāḥ, phalam lambanāvanatiliptāḥ iti |
body.translated_text: Now, why are the <s>yojana</s> [diameters] not stated as measured in their own orbits? The intention of the master (<s>ācārya</s>) is this: If the <s>yojana</s>-diameters of the planets derived from their own orbits were stated, then in computing the <s>liptā</s>-diameters, the true <s>yojana-karṇas</s> (hypotenuse distances) derived from their own orbits would be the divisors, and likewise in computing the <s>liptās</s> of <s>lambana</s> (parallax in longitude) and <s>dṛkkṣepa</s> (parallax in latitude). In that case, the <s>lambana</s> and <s>dṛkkṣepa</s> <s>liptās</s> of the planets would be practically nil. But the differences in their <s>lambana</s> (parallax) and <s>nati</s> (deflection) are indeed observed. For that purpose, the divisors are shown here. How? '<s>Śaśi-ṅa-ña-ṇa-na-ma-aṃśakāḥ</s>' — for computing the <s>liptā</s>-diameter from the <s>yojana</s>-measure of the Moon's diameter, the Moon's <s>yojana-karṇa</s> is the divisor. That divisor is multiplied by five and so forth. That quotient — [originally] the Moon's diameter — becomes the diameter of Venus and the others. [The divisors are:] For Venus: 315/171885; for Jupiter: 315/343770; for Mercury: 315/515655; for Saturn: 315/687540; for Mars: 315/859425. The upper fraction, multiplied by half the diameter and divided by the divisor, gives the planet's diameter in <s>liptās</s> — the mean [value]. For the true [value], however: multiply the divisors by the difference between one's own <s>bhūtārā</s> (earth-star distance) planet-interval, and divide by half the diameter — [the results] become true. These very [divisors] are the divisors for the <s>lambana</s> (parallax) and <s>avanati</s> (deflection) <s>liptās</s> [obtained] from one's own <s>dṛggati</s> (sight-motion) and one's own <s>dṛkkṣepa</s> (sight-elevation) multiplied by half the earth's diameter, in planetary conjunctions.

body.text: catvāri mānāni vakṣyante saura-sāvana-nākṣatra-cāndrāṇi | tatra na jñāyate kena mānena śāstre asmin vyavahāraḥ kartavyaḥ iti ataḥ āha ã samārkasamāḥ | samāḥ varṣam, samāḥ asmin śāstre arkasamāḥ | arkeṇa varṣeṇa vyavahartavyam asmin | asya eva niścayāvagamanārtham vakṣyati "ṣaṣṭyā sūryābdānām" [kālakriyāpādaḥ, 12] iti ādi | evam idam ṣaṣṭham gītikāsūtram || 7 ||
body.translated_text: Four kinds of measure will be stated: <s>saura</s> (solar), <s>sāvana</s> (civil), <s>nākṣatra</s> (sidereal), and <s>cāndra</s> (lunar). Among these, since it is not known which measure is to be used for calculations in this treatise, therefore he says: '<s>samārkasamāḥ</s>' — '<s>samāḥ</s>' means a year; the years in this treatise are solar years (<s>arkasamāḥ</s>). One should calculate with solar years. For the purpose of ascertaining this very [point], he will state: '<s>ṣaṣṭyā sūryābdānām</s>' (of sixty solar years) [<s>Kālakriyāpāda</s>, 12] and so on. Thus this sixth <s>gītikā</s>-sūtra [is explained]. // 7 //

body.text: paramāpakramaḥ grahavikṣepāḥ ca
body.translated_text: Maximum declination and planetary latitudes

body.text: ete grahāḥ svakakṣyāsu bhramantaḥ viṣuvate uttareṇa dakṣiṇena ca vyāvartamānāḥ lakṣyante | tasmāt tatparijñānārtham āha ã
body.translated_text: These planets, revolving in their own orbits, are observed to turn north and south of the equator. Therefore, for the purpose of knowing that, he says:

children.translated_text: '<s>Bhāpakrama</s>' (the declination [in terms of] signs) and the degrees of the planets,
the latitude (<s>vikṣepa</s>) of the Moon from the ecliptic (<s>apamaṇḍala</s>) is half of <s>jha</s> [= 4½ degrees],
<s>Śani</s> (Saturn), <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter), <s>Kuja</s> (Mars) — half of <s>kha</s>, <s>ka</s>, <s>ga</s>,
<s>Bhṛgu</s> (Venus), <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) — <s>kha</s>; <s>scāṅgulaḥ</s> (96 <s>aṅgulas</s>), <s>ghahastaḥ</s> (4 <s>hastas</s>), <s>nā</s> (a man). // 8 //

body.text: bhāpakramaḥ, grahāṃśāḥ, śaśivikṣepaḥ, apamaṇḍalāt, jhārdham, śani-guru-kuja, kha-ka-ga-ardham, bhṛgu-budha, kha scāṅgulaḥ, ghatastaḥ, nā |
body.translated_text: The word-by-word analysis: <s>bhāpakramaḥ</s>, <s>grahāṃśāḥ</s>, <s>śaśivikṣepaḥ</s>, <s>apamaṇḍalāt</s>, <s>jhārdham</s>, <s>śani-guru-kuja</s>, <s>kha-ka-ga-ardham</s>, <s>bhṛgu-budha</s>, <s>kha</s>, <s>scāṅgulaḥ</s>, <s>ghahastaḥ</s>, <s>nā</s>.

body.text:
bha caturviṃśatiḥ | bha eva apakramaḥ bhāpakramaḥ | prāṅmukha[gamanena] yaddakṣiṇena uttareṇa vā samarekhātaḥ apagamanam apakramaḥ | keṣām ayam apakramaḥ kimātmakaḥ vā caturviṃśatiḥ iti āha ã grahāṃśāḥ | grahāṇām ādityādīnām ete aṃśakāḥ rāseḥ triṃsadbhāgāḥ | samarekhātaḥ uttareṇa caturviṃśatibhāgān grahaḥ apakrāmati meṣavṛṣamithuneṣu krameṇa, tān eva apakramabhāgān utkrameṇa karkaṭakasiṃhakanyāsu nivartate; dakṣiṇena
tulāvṛścikadhanuḥṣu [krameṇa] tān eva utkrameṇa makarakumbhamīneṣu iti |
body.translated_text: <s>Bha</s> is twenty-four. <s>Bha</s> itself being the declination (<s>apakrama</s>) is <s>bhāpakrama</s>. The eastward motion that goes south or north from the equator (<s>samarekhā</s>) is the declination (<s>apakrama</s>). Whose is this declination, and what is the nature of the twenty-four? He says: '<s>grahāṃśāḥ</s>' — of the planets, beginning with the Sun, these are the degrees (<s>aṃśaka</s>), i.e., the thirtieth parts of a sign (<s>rāśi</s>). From the equator, a planet declines northward through twenty-four degrees in [the signs of] <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries), <s>Vṛṣa</s> (Taurus), and <s>Mithuna</s> (Gemini) in order; those same declination-degrees it traverses in reverse order in <s>Karkaṭaka</s> (Cancer), <s>Siṃha</s> (Leo), and <s>Kanyā</s> (Virgo); southward in <s>Tulā</s> (Libra), <s>Vṛścika</s> (Scorpio), and <s>Dhanus</s> (Sagittarius) [in order]; those same [it traverses] in reverse in <s>Makara</s> (Capricorn), <s>Kumbha</s> (Aquarius), and <s>Mīna</s> (Pisces).

body.text:
atra grahagrahaṇam kim artham kriyate? grahāṇām sarveṣām eva ete apakramāṃśakāḥ yathā syuḥ iti, anyathā hi keṣām eva syuḥ | na etat asti | atra grahāḥ prakrāntāḥ teṣām prakṛtatvāt grahāṇām eva ete aṃśakāḥ na anyeṣām | avaśyam grahagrahaṇam kartavyam | apakramamaṇḍalāt vikṣepāṃśāḥ ucyante | apakramamaṇḍalāt jhārdham candraḥ vikṣipati tathā śanigurukujabhṛgubudhāḥ svān bhāgān vikṣipanti | yasmāt candrādīnām apakramamaṇḍalāt vikṣepabhāgāḥ
abhidhīyante ataḥ candrādīnām eva kevalānām apakramabhāgāḥ api syuḥ na ādityasya | grahagrahaṇe punaḥ kriyamāṇe sarveṣām eva apakramabhāgāḥ siddhyanti iti |
body.translated_text: Here, what is the purpose of the word '<s>graha</s>' (planet)? So that these declination-degrees may apply to all the planets. Otherwise, they would apply only to some. This is not so. Here, the planets are the topic under discussion; because they are the topic, these degrees belong to the planets alone, not to others. The word '<s>graha</s>' must necessarily be used. The latitude-degrees from the ecliptic are being stated. From the ecliptic, the Moon's [latitude is] half of <s>jha</s>; similarly <s>Śani</s> (Saturn), <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter), <s>Kuja</s> (Mars), <s>Bhṛgu</s> (Venus), and <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) have their respective latitudes. Since the latitude-degrees of the Moon and the others from the ecliptic are being stated, the declination-degrees too would apply only to the Moon and the others, not to the Sun. But when the word '<s>graha</s>' is used, the declination-degrees are established for all [planets, including the Sun].

body.text:
śaśivikṣepaḥ apamaṇḍalāt jhārdham | śaśinaḥ vikṣepaḥ śaśivikṣepaḥ | saḥ apamaṇḍalāt | apa-maṇḍalam apakramamaṇḍalam, tasmāt apakramamaṇḍalāt, uttareṇa dakṣiṇena vā candrasya vikṣepaḥ | viṣuvan maṇḍalāt apakramaḥ uttareṇa dakṣiṇena vā, apakramamaṇḍalam [ca], tasmāt vikṣepaḥ uttareṇa dakṣiṇena vā | jhārdham, jhakāreṇa nava, jhasya ardham jhārdham, ardhonapañcabhāgāḥ candramasaḥ vikṣepaḥ | tathā eva apakramamaṇḍalāt eva śeṣāṇām
api grahāṇām vikṣepāḥ |
body.translated_text: '<s>Śaśivikṣepaḥ apamaṇḍalāt jhārdham</s>' — the latitude of the Moon (<s>śaśi</s>) is the Moon's latitude (<s>śaśivikṣepa</s>). That is from the ecliptic (<s>apamaṇḍala</s>). '<s>Apa-maṇḍala</s>' is the ecliptic circle (<s>apakramamaṇḍala</s>); from that ecliptic, the Moon's latitude is either north or south. From the equator, the declination is either north or south; and from the ecliptic, the latitude is either north or south. '<s>Jhārdham</s>' — by the letter <s>jha</s>, [the value is] nine; half of <s>jha</s> is <s>jhārdham</s>, [meaning] four and a half degrees is the Moon's latitude. Similarly, the latitudes of the remaining planets too are from the ecliptic alone.

body.text:
śani-guru-kuja kha-ka-gārdham | śanigurukujānām yathāsaṅkhyena, śaneḥ kha, dvau [bhāgau] vikṣepaḥ; guroḥ ka, ekaḥ bhāgaḥ; kujasya gārdham, gakāreṇa trayaḥ bhāgāḥ, gasya ardham gārdham, sārdhaḥ aṃśaḥ | bhṛgu-budha kha | bhṛgubudhayoḥ kha-saṅkhyā vikṣepaḥ dvau bhāgau | atra "bhṛgubudhaśanīnām kha" iti ucyamāne khakāragrahaṇam ekam na kartavyam bhavati, tat kim iti ācāryeṇa pṛthak pāṭhena dviḥ khakāragrahaṇam kṛtam? ucyate ã pṛthak
pṛthak karmapradarśanārtham; śanigurukujānām ekam vikṣepakarma bhṛgubudhayoḥ anyat, tasmāt etat karmadvayam iti pṛthak pṛthak pāṭhāt eva siddhyati |
body.translated_text: '<s>Śani-guru-kuja kha-ka-gārdham</s>' — for Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars, in respective order: Saturn — <s>kha</s>, two degrees of latitude; Jupiter — <s>ka</s>, one degree; Mars — <s>gārdham</s>, by the letter <s>ga</s> [the value is] three degrees, half of <s>ga</s> is <s>gārdham</s> — one and a half degrees. '<s>Bhṛgu-budha kha</s>' — for Venus and Mercury, the latitude is the number <s>kha</s> — two degrees. Here, if one were to say '<s>bhṛgubudhaśanīnām kha</s>,' a single use of the letter <s>kha</s> would not need to be made. Then why did the master make two uses of the letter <s>kha</s> through a separate reading? The answer is: for the purpose of showing separate procedures — the latitude-procedure for Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars is one, and for Venus and Mercury it is another. Therefore, these two procedures are established precisely through the separate reading.

body.text:
"nṛṣi yojanam" iti atra puruṣaḥ eva kevalaḥ abhihitaḥ | saḥ puruṣaḥ katyaṅgulaḥ, katihastaḥ vā iti etat na upadiṣṭam | tadartham āha ã scāṅgulaḥ | sakāreṇa navatiḥ, cakāreṇa ṣaṭ, scāṅgulaḥ ṣaṇṇavatyaṅgulaḥ | aṅgulasya pramāṇam gaṇitaparibhāṣātaḥ pratipattavyam ã aṣṭau yavamadhyānyaṅgulapramāṇam iti ādi | ghahastaḥ caturhastaḥ | nā puruṣaḥ | nanu ca "nṛṣiyojanam" iti atra eva etat vaktum yuktam | evam manyante | yathā iṣṭagrahayogeṣu antaram
vikṣepaliptāḥ labhyante | aṅgulāni hastān ca kṛtvā grahayoḥ antaram avadhāryam iti | evam api vijñāyate eva kiyatībhiḥ liptābhiḥ aṅgulam bhavati iti | atra svadhiyā pratidinagrahacāragaṇitanipuṇatayā abhyūhyam | uddeśataḥ tu svadhiyā upalakṣitam ucyate ã
body.translated_text: In '<s>nṛṣi yojanam</s>' (a man is a <s>yojana</s>), only the person (<s>puruṣa</s>) was mentioned. How many <s>aṅgulas</s> (finger-breadths) or how many <s>hastas</s> (cubits) is that person — this was not taught. For that purpose he says: '<s>scāṅgulaḥ</s>' — by the letter <s>sa</s>, ninety; by the letter <s>ca</s>, six; <s>scāṅgulaḥ</s> means ninety-six <s>aṅgulas</s> (finger-breadths). The measure of an <s>aṅgula</s> is to be understood from the convention of mathematical science: 'eight medium-sized barley grains [equal] the measure of one <s>aṅgula</s>,' and so on. '<s>Ghahastaḥ</s>' means four <s>hastas</s> (cubits). '<s>Nā</s>' means a person (<s>puruṣa</s>). Objection: This should have been stated in '<s>nṛṣi yojanam</s>' itself. [Response:] They think thus: Just as in desired planetary conjunctions, the interval in latitude-<s>liptās</s> is obtained — having converted [them] into <s>aṅgulas</s> and <s>hastas</s>, the interval between the two planets is to be determined. Even thus, it is understood how many <s>liptās</s> make one <s>aṅgula</s>. Here, [the exact correspondence] is to be worked out by one's own intellect through skill in daily planetary-motion computation. But what is tentatively observed by one's own intellect is stated:

body.text:
yoge pādāṅgulam liptā yathā vā lakṣyate dṛśā |
[mahābhāskarīyam, 6.55]
body.translated_text: 'In a conjunction, the <s>liptā</s> [equals] a quarter of a finger-breadth, or as it is observed by sight.' [<s>Mahābhāskarīya</s>, 6.55]

body.text: iti | evam idam saptamam gītikāsūtram || 8 ||
body.translated_text: Thus this seventh <s>gītikā</s>-sūtra [is explained]. // 8 //

body.text: grahoccapātasthānāni
body.translated_text: Positions of the apogees and nodes of the planets

body.text: candrapātāt pravṛttasya candramasoḥ vikṣepaḥ sādhyate | anirdiṣṭatvāt pātasya, grahāṇām punaḥ kasmāt prabhṛti vikṣepāḥ sādhyante eva iti etat na jñāyate | ataḥ teśām pātabhāgānām mandoccabhāgānām ca pratipādanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: The latitude of the Moon is computed from the node of the Moon. Since the node is not specified [for the other planets], it is not known from what [point] the latitudes of the planets are to be computed. Therefore, for the purpose of teaching their nodal degrees and apogee degrees, he says:

children.translated_text: <s>Budha</s> (Mercury), <s>Bhṛgu</s> (Venus), <s>Kuja</s> (Mars), <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter), <s>Śani</s> (Saturn) — <s>na</s>, <s>va</s>,
<s>rā</s>, <s>ṣa</s>, <s>ha</s> — having gone [that many] degrees, [are] the first nodes.
Of the Sun and of these [planets] likewise,
<s>dvā</s>, <s>ñakhi</s>, <s>sā</s>, <s>hdā</s>, <s>hlya</s>, <s>khicya</s> — [are] the <s>mandocca</s> (apogee of the slow correction). // 9 //

body.text: budha-bhṛgu-kuja-guru-śani avibhaktikaḥ nirdeśaḥ, na-va-rā-ṣa-ha ayam api avibhaktikaḥ, gatvā, aṃśakān, prathamapātāḥ, savituḥ, amīṣām, ca, tathā, dvā ñakhi sā hdā hlya khicya etāni api dvādīni avibhaktikāni, mandoccam |
body.translated_text: The word-by-word analysis: '<s>budha-bhṛgu-kuja-guru-śani</s>' — without case-ending; '<s>na-va-rā-ṣa-ha</s>' — this too without case-ending; '<s>gatvā</s>' (having gone), '<s>aṃśakān</s>' (degrees), '<s>prathamapātāḥ</s>' (first nodes), '<s>savituḥ</s>' (of the Sun), '<s>amīṣām</s>' (of these), '<s>ca</s>' (and), '<s>tathā</s>' (likewise), '<s>dvā</s>, <s>ñakhi</s>, <s>sā</s>, <s>hdā</s>, <s>hlya</s>, <s>khicya</s>' — these too, from '<s>dvā</s>' onward, are without case-endings; '<s>mandoccam</s>' (apogee).

body.text:
budha-bhṛgu-kuja-guru[-śani] avibhaktikam etat grahaṇakavākyam | sūtrāṇām sopasaṃskāratvāt saṃskāram apekṣate | kaḥ asya saṃskāraḥ? prakrāntadyotikayā vibhaktyā saṃyogaḥ, budha-bhṛgu-kuja-guru-śanīnām iti | eteṣām budhādīnām "nā"dayaḥ aṃśāḥ | yathāsaṅkhyena budhasya na viṃśatiḥ, bhṛgoḥ va ṣaṣṭiḥ, kujasya rā catvāriṃśat, guroḥ ṣa aśītiḥ, śaneḥ ha śatam | etān aṃśakān gatvā, eteṣām budha-bhṛgu-kuja-guru-śanīnām prathamapātāḥ vyavasthitāḥ
iti | prathamapātagrahaṇam dvitīyapātanirākaraṇārtham | yadi prathamapātagrahaṇan na kriyate tadā sāmānyena dvayoḥ api pātayoḥ grahaṇam syāt | tathā ca vikṣepādigrahaṇe niścayaḥ na syāt, yasmāt prathamapātāt uttareṇa grahāṇām vikṣepaḥ bhavati, dvitīyāt pātāt dakṣiṇena | uktam ca ã
body.translated_text: '<s>Budha-bhṛgu-kuja-guru-śani</s>' — this is an expression without case-ending. Since <s>sūtras</s> require grammatical completion, it requires completion. What is its completion? The joining with the case-ending that illuminates the topic already introduced — [yielding] '<s>budhabhṛgukujaguruśanīnām</s>' (of Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn). Of these [planets] beginning with Mercury, the degrees are '<s>nā</s>' and the following. In respective order: of Mercury — <s>na</s>, twenty; of Venus — <s>va</s>, sixty; of Mars — <s>rā</s>, forty; of Jupiter — <s>ṣa</s>, eighty; of Saturn — <s>ha</s>, one hundred. Having gone these degrees, the first nodes of Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn are situated. The use of 'first node' is for the purpose of excluding the second node. If the word 'first node' were not used, then there would be a general reference to both nodes. And in that case, there would be no certainty in computing the latitude and so forth, since the latitude of the planets is northward from the first node and southward from the second node. As stated:

children.text: prathamāt pātāt śaśinaḥ apamaṇḍalasya uttareṇa vikṣepaḥ |
children.translated_text: From the first node, the latitude of the Moon is north of the ecliptic;

children.text: vikṣepaḥ dakṣiṇataḥ punar api pātāt dvitīyāt ca ||
children.translated_text: the latitude is southward again from the second node.

body.text:
iti | ete eva pātāḥ ṣaḍrāśiyutāḥ dvitīyapātāḥ bhavanti | atra "gatvā aṃśakān prathamapātāḥ" iti ucyate | yadi grahapātāḥ calanti tadā evam yuktam vaktum ã etān aṃśakān gatvā prathamapātāḥ vyavasthitāḥ iti | bāḍham calanti ete grahapātāḥ, anyathā hi ayam nirdeśaḥ eva na ghhaṭate "gatvā aṃśakān" iti | yadi eteṣām grahapātānām [gatiḥ tarhi] candrapātavat yugabhagaṇanirdeśaḥ kim iti ācāryeṇa na kriyate ? anyat ca, yadi eteṣām gatiḥ syāt grahavikṣepāḥ na sphuṭāḥ
bhaveyuḥ | atyantasūkṣmā eṣām gatiḥ, mahatā kālena kiyatī upacīyate, tataḥ stokatvāt antarasya vikṣepāḥ sphuṭāḥ eva lakṣyante | ācāryeṇa gatimatvam pātānāt nirdeśatā teṣām gatiḥ api nirdiṣṭā eva "yasmāt iṅgitena, ceṣṭitena, nimiṣitena, mahatā vā sūtraprabandhena ca, ācāryāṇām abhiprāyaḥ gamyate" | tasmāt anena eva sūtrabandhena grahapātānām gatimatvam upadiṣatā teṣām yugabhagaṇān muktakāt eva nirdiṣṭavān, anyathā hi teṣām gatimatvanirdeśaḥ anarthakaḥ
syāt | sampradāyāvicchedāt smaranti vṛddhāḥ tat yugabhagaṇam | tat yathā ã
body.translated_text: Thus. These same nodes (<s>pāta</s>), when added with six signs, become the second nodes. Here it is said: 'Having traversed [so many] degrees, [they become] the first nodes.' If the planetary nodes move, then it is proper to say thus: having traversed these degrees, the first [nodes]...

children.translated_text: <s>Vasu</s>-ocean-<s>Yama</s>-<s>Aśvin</s>-void-arrow-mountain-arrow-fire is the number of years in a <s>yuga</s>;
multiplied by a hundred, [this gives] the [revolutions] of the nodes — this was stated by <s>Ārya</s> [<s>Āryabhaṭa</s>] in a standalone [verse].
One, three, two, four, and five revolutions respectively — all of them traverse [these many]

children.text: kalpādeḥ gatakālāt gaṇanīyam ataḥ gatiḥ teṣām ||
children.translated_text: from the elapsed time since the beginning of the <s>kalpa</s>; therefore their motion is to be computed from that.

body.text:
tadānayanam idānīm ã kalpādeḥ abdanirodhāt ayam abdarāśiḥ iti īritaḥ khāgnyadrirāmārkarasavasurandhrendavaḥ | te ca aṅkaiḥ api 1986123730 | asmin budhādipātabhagaṇaguṇite svayugavibhakte bhagaṇādayaḥ pātabhogāḥ labhyante | pātayugapramāṇam sarveṣām eva "khākāśāṣṭakṛtadvidvivyomeṣvadrīṣuvahnayaḥ" aṅkaiḥ api 35750224800 | etaiḥ yugavarṣaiḥ budhasya pātaḥ bhagaṇam ekam bhuṅkte, śukrasya trīṇi, kujasya dvau, guroḥ catvāraḥ, śanipātaḥ
pañca | eteṣām yathāsvam labdhāḥ pātabhāgāḥ yathāpaṭhitāḥ, etat eva guruśanaiḥ carayoḥ ekā tatparā [ca] labhyate |
body.translated_text: Now, the computation of that: From the beginning of the <s>kalpa</s>, from the determination of years, this number of years has been stated as void-fire-mountain-<s>Rāma</s>-Sun-flavor-<s>Vasu</s>-<s>Rudra</s>-Moon, which in numerals is 1,986,123,730. When this is multiplied by the revolution numbers of the nodes of Mercury and the like, and divided by its own <s>yuga</s>...

body.text:
ayam aparaḥ prakāraḥ ã budha-bhṛgu-kuja-guru-śani | prathamābahuvacanasaṃskṛtam idam grahaṇakavākyam vyākhyāyate budha-bhṛgu-kuja-guru-śanayaḥ | na-va-rā-ṣa-ha iti etān aṃśakān meṣādiparamāṇoḥ prabhṛti gatvā prathamapāteṣu vyavasthitāḥ iti arthaḥ | atra "tātsthyāt tācchābdyam", yathā "mañcāḥ krośanti", mañcastheṣu krośatsu mañcāḥ krośanti iti ucyate | evam atra api prathamapātavyavasthitān eva grahān prathamapātaḥ iti uktavān | tadā tāvantaḥ
eva bhāgāḥ, na ete calanti | yadi api kaiścit eṣām gatiḥ ucyate tathā api asmākam nādaraḥ, yena atimahatā api kālena manāg api antaram na bhavati, yataḥ kaliyugānte śanaiḥ carapātasya tisraḥ liptāḥ, na kiñcit antaram | kaliyuge ca parisamāpte sarvam eva jagat pralīyate, pralīne ca jagati punar anyā sṛṣṭiḥ jāyate, tatra na jānīmaḥ kim bhaviṣyati iti | atha ca antare ne kiñcit antaram, na kaścit viśeṣaḥ | yat api uktam ācāryeṇa tat śāstrabhāvaprakriyāsampradāyāvicchedapradarśanārtham
| anyathā hi anantatvāt kālasya gatiḥ eṣām alpā api upacīyamānā mahatī sañjāyate | sā ca anyathā na pratipattum śakyate iti pātayugabhagaṇanirdeśaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here is another method: Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn. This grasp-sentence, formed as a first-person plural nominative, is explained as: Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn. <s>Na-va-rā-ṣa-ha</s> — these many degrees from <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries)...

body.text: savituḥ amīṣām ca | savituḥ ādityasya, amīṣām ca grahāṇām budhabhṛgukujaguruśanīnām mandoccabhāgāḥ, kena eva prakāreṇa savituḥ dvā aṣṭasaptatibhāgāḥ, budhasya ñakhi śatadvayam daśottaram, bhṛgoḥ sā navatiḥ, kujasya hdā śatam aṣṭādaśottaram, guroḥ hlya sāśītikam śatam, śaneḥ khicya śatadvayam ṣaṭtriṃśaduttaram mandoccam | ete bhāgāḥ eṣām grahāṇām pṛthak pṛthak mandoccam | mandoccānām bahutvāt mandoccāni iti bhavitavyam | na

children.text: etat asti | sāmānyopakramaḥ atra kṛtaḥ, yathā ã "rakṣohāgamalaghvasandehāḥ prayojanam" [aṣṭādhyāyī, 1.1.1., pātañjalabhāṣyam] iti, evam atra api "dvā ñakhi sā hdā hlya khicya mandoccam" |
children.translated_text: This is so. A general introduction has been made here, just as [in the statement]: 'Protection from demons, grammar, brevity, and absence of doubt are the purpose' [<s>Aṣṭādhyāyī</s> 1.1.1, <s>Patañjali</s>'s <s>Bhāṣya</s>]; similarly here too, 'seventy-eight, <s>ñakhi</s>, <s>sā</s>, <s>hdā</s>, <s>hlya</s>, <s>khicya</s> — the slow apogee'...

body.translated_text: 'Of the Sun and of these': Of the Sun, i.e., of <s>Āditya</s>, and of these planets — Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn — the degrees of the slow apogee (<s>mandocca</s>). In what manner: of the Sun, seventy-eight degrees; of Mercury, <s>ñakhi</s> [= two hundred and ten]...

body.text: atra śīghroccam mandoccam iti | yasya śīghrā gatiḥ tat śīghroccam, yasya punar gatiḥ eva na asti tat mandoccam iti | katham? ucyate | loke ã "śīghraḥ devadattaḥ" yaḥ hi kṣiprataram gacchati sa śīghraḥ, "mandaḥ yajñadattaḥ" iti yaḥ hi mandataram gacchati sa mandaḥ | evam atra api yasya atiśīghragatiḥ grahagateḥ tat śīghroccam | yasya punar grahagateḥ alpīyasī gatiḥ [tat mandoccam] | evam grahāṇām api yuktam eva etat |
body.translated_text: Here, [the terms] '<s>śīghrocca</s>' (fast apogee) and '<s>mandocca</s>' (slow apogee) [are explained]: that whose motion is fast is the <s>śīghrocca</s>; that which has no motion at all is the <s>mandocca</s>. How? It is said: In common usage, '<s>Devadatta</s> is fast' [means] one who goes more quickly...

body.text:
atha kim iti mandoccagatiḥ na abhihitā? ucyate ã sūkṣmatvāt ācāryasya na atra ādaraḥ, mahatā api kālena na kiñcit eva antaram bhavati | api ca muktakena eva ācāryeṇa abhihitam iti sampradāyāvicchedāt avadhāryate | athavā gatvā aṃśakān savitrādīnām mandoccāni vyavasthitāni iti vyākhyāyate | anyathā hi "tathā"-śabdaḥ sārthakaḥ na syāt | yathā budhādīnām prathamapātāḥ "nā"dīn aṃśakān gatvā vyavasthitāḥ, evam eteṣām savitrādīnām mandoccāni
"dvā"dīn aṃśakān gatvā vyavasthitāni iti | teṣām ca mandoccānām atyantasūkṣmatvāt varṣagaṇena eva ācāryeṇa yat ākhyātam tat eva avyavacchinnasampradāyapratipattyā abhidhīyate | tat yathā ã
body.translated_text: Now why is the motion of the slow apogee not stated? It is said: Because of its minuteness, the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) pays no attention to it here; even over a great period of time, there is hardly any difference. Moreover, the <s>ācārya</s> has stated it in a standalone [verse]...

children.translated_text: By eight-four-mountain-eight-nine-horses, the apogee-<s>yuga</s> of the Sun is stated;

children.text: daśaghanaguṇitaiḥ abdaiḥ viśvān bhuṅkte kramāt bhagaṇān ||
children.translated_text: multiplied by the cube of ten years, [the Sun] traverses all its revolutions in sequence.
Teeth-eight-ocean-fire-quality-eight-<s>Rāma</s>-twin constitute the <s>yuga</s>; [multiplied by] the oceans,

children.text: śataguṇitāḥ śaśijasya prāhuḥ bhagaṇān ca sapta eva ||
children.translated_text: multiplied by a hundred, they declare the revolutions of [the node] born from the Moon — and seven exactly.
Void-sky-<s>Veda</s>-four-hole-ocean-four-ocean-<s>Nanda</s>-mountain-ocean —

children.text: śukrasya ardham sūreḥ bhagaṇaḥ bhogaḥ tayoḥ ekaḥ ||
children.translated_text: half of [that of] Venus is the Sun's revolution; the enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>) of those two is one.
Void-sky-zero-four-<s>Aśvin</s>-<s>Rudra</s>-arrow-mountain-<s>Vasu</s>-sage-Moon-years —
the dark one's (<s>Kuja</s>/Mars) apogee-<s>yuga</s>, doubled, [gives] the revolutions — nine are the substances of those two.
The motions of the slow apogees, computed from the time elapsed since the beginning of the <s>kalpa</s>,
are explained here by <s>Bhāskara</s> from the word 'having traversed' (<s>gatvā</s>).

body.text:
tat yathā ã mandoccānayanam pratyeteṣām kalpādeḥ abdanirodhāt gatakālaḥ khāgnyadrirāmārkarasavasurandhrendavaḥ, te ca 1986123730 | eteṣu varṣeṣu yathāsvam mandoccabhagaṇaguṇiteṣu svayugābdavibhakteṣu ravyādīnām mandoccānām rāśibhāgādayaḥ labhyante | eteṣām api kaliyugānte api alpam antaram, yataḥ ca śanaiḥ carasya api saptamātrā liptā mandoccasya upacayaḥ, na kaścit phalaviśeṣaḥ | yathā api tu śāstrasampradāyāvicchittikathane grahapāteṣu uktam
tat atra api avadhāraṇīyam iti | evam idam aṣṭamam gītikāsūtram || 6 ||
body.translated_text: That is as follows: For computing the slow apogees of these [planets], the elapsed time from the beginning of the <s>kalpa</s> is void-fire-mountain-<s>Rāma</s>-Sun-flavor-<s>Vasu</s>-<s>Rudra</s>-Moon, which is 1,986,123,730. When these years are multiplied by the respective slow-apogee revolution numbers and divided by their own [<s>yuga</s>]...

body.text: ojapadayoḥ mandaśīghraparidhayaḥ
body.translated_text: The circumferences of the slow and fast epicycles in the odd quadrants

body.text: mandaśīghroccaparidhipramāṇapratipādanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: In order to teach the measure of the circumferences of the slow and fast apogee [epicycles], he states:

children.translated_text: Half of <s>jha</s> [= the slow epicycle circumference]
of the Moon is <s>cha</s>; <s>ga-cha-gha-ḍha-cha-jha</s> from those stated [planets];
<s>jhā-gḍa-glā-rdha-dḍa</s> likewise
from the fast apogees of Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Venus, and Mercury. // 10 //

body.text: jhārdhāni, mandavṛttam, śaśinaḥ, cha ga cha gha ḍha cha jha ete chādayaḥ avibhaktikanirdeśāḥ, yathā uktebhyaḥ, jhā-gḍa-glā-rdha-dḍa avibhaktikaḥ nirdeśaḥ, tathā śani-guru-kuja-bhṛgu-budhoccaśīghrebhyaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Jhārdhāni</s>, <s>mandavṛttam</s>, <s>śaśinaḥ</s>, <s>cha ga cha gha ḍha cha jha</s> — these beginning with <s>cha</s> are given as indeclinable notations; <s>yathā uktebhyaḥ</s> (from those stated); <s>jhā-gḍa-glā-rdha-dḍa</s> is an indeclinable notation; likewise, Saturn-Jupiter-Mars-Venus-Mercury...

body.text:
jhārdhāni | jhasya ardhāni jhārdhāni | vakṣyamāṇāni mandaśīghroccavṛttāni jhārdhapramāṇāni pratipattavyāni | mandavṛttam iti ekavacananirdeśaḥ | "pratyekam vākyaparisamāptiḥ" [aṣṭādhyāyī, 1.1.1, pātañjalabhāṣyam] iti anena nyāyena mandavṛttam śaśinaḥ cha, sapta jhārdhāni, sārdhaikatriṃśat bhāgāḥ; yathā uktebhyaḥ mandoccabhāgavidhānakrameṇa savitṛ-budha-bhṛgu-kuja-guru-śanayaḥ parigṛhyante | savituḥ ga, trīṇi jhārdhāni, sārdhatrayodaśabhāgāḥ
| budhasya cha, sapta jhārdhāni, sārdhaikatriṃśadbhāgāḥ | bhṛgoḥ gha, catvāri jhārdhāni, aṣṭādaśabhāgāḥ | kujasya ḍha, caturdaśa jhārdhāni, triṣaṣṭibhāgāḥ | guroḥ cha, sapta jhārdhāni, sārdhaikatriṃśadbhāgāḥ | śaneḥ jha, nava jhārdhāni, sārdhacatvāriṃśadbhāgāḥ | yathā uktebhyaḥ yathā uktam yathoktam, tebhyaḥ yathā uktebhyaḥ | savitrādīnām ca mandoccebhyaḥ | nanu ca atra sambandhalakṣaṇayā ṣaṣṭhyā bhavitavyam, yathā uktānām iti | na etat asti | yathā uktebhyaḥ
iti anayā pañcamyā mandoccaviśuddhebhyaḥ rāśibhyaḥ mandoccāt adhikebhyaḥ rāśibhyaḥ vā rāśyādibhyaḥ jyāvibhāgena ete paridhayaḥ guṇakārāḥ | yathā uktebhyaḥ iti anena eva vacanena mandoccam grahamadhyāt pātyate, pariśiṣṭasya jyāsaṅkalanāya trairāśikam kriyate | paridhisaṃskārakaraṇam ca trairāśikaprasiddhyartham | yady asya ṣaṣṭiśatatrayaparidheḥ iyam jyā tataḥ abhīṣṭagrahaparidheḥ kā jyā labhyate | sā eva jyā bhujāphalam koṭiphalam ca iti abhidhīyate
| tatra jhārdhena apavartya ṣaṣṭiśatatrayaparidhim yathā uktāḥ ca grahaparidhayaḥ jhārdhāpavartitāḥ | tena guṇakārabhāgahārayoḥ jhārdhāpavartitayoḥ karmaṇi kriyamāṇe iṣṭajyāyāḥ aśītiḥ bhāgahāraḥ yathoktākṣarasaṅkhyāparidhayaḥ guṇakārāḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Jhārdhāni</s>: The halves of <s>jha</s> are <s>jhārdhāni</s>. The slow and fast apogee epicycle circumferences that will be stated are to be understood as having the measure of half of <s>jha</s>. '<s>Mandavṛttam</s>' (slow epicycle circumference) — the singular usage. 'Sentence-completion for each [is implied individually]' [<s>Aṣṭādhyāyī</s>]...

body.text:
śīghroccaparidhayaḥ ã jhā, nava jhārdhāni, catvāriṃśat sārdhāḥ bhāgāḥ śaneḥ | gḍa, ṣoḍaśa jhārdhāni, dvāsaptatibhāgāḥ guroḥ | glā, tripañcāśat jhārdhāni, śatadvayam aṣṭatriṃśaduttaram sārdham bhāgānām kujasya | rdha, ekonaṣaṣṭiḥ jhārdhāni, pañcaṣaṣtyadhikaśatadvayam sārdham bhāgānām bhṛgoḥ | dḍa ekatriṃśat jhārdhāni, ekonacatvāriṃśaduttaram śatam sārdham bhāgānām budhasya | śani-guru-kuja-bhṛgu-budhoccaśīghrebhyaḥ |
śani-guru-kuja-bhṛgu-budhānām uccaśīghrāḥ tebhyaḥ śani-guru-kuja-bhṛgu-budhoccaśīghrebhyaḥ |
body.translated_text: The circumferences of the fast-apogee (<s>shīghrocca</s>): <s>jhā</s> — nine <s>jhārdhas</s> (half-segments), forty and a half degrees for <s>Śani</s> (Saturn). <s>gḍa</s> — sixteen <s>jhārdhas</s>, seventy-two degrees for <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter). <s>glā</s> — fifty-three <s>jhārdhas</s>, two hundred and thirty-eight and a half degrees for <s>Kuja</s> (Mars). <s>rdha</s> — fifty-nine <s>jhārdhas</s>, two hundred and sixty-five and a half degrees for <s>Bhṛgu</s> (Venus). <s>dḍa</s> — thirty-one <s>jhārdhas</s>, one hundred and thirty-nine and a half degrees for <s>Budha</s> (Mercury). [These are] from the fast-apogees of <s>Śani</s>, <s>Guru</s>, <s>Kuja</s>, <s>Bhṛgu</s>, and <s>Budha</s>. The fast-apogees of <s>Śani</s>, <s>Guru</s>, <s>Kuja</s>, <s>Bhṛgu</s>, and <s>Budha</s> — from those fast-apogees of <s>Śani</s>, <s>Guru</s>, <s>Kuja</s>, <s>Bhṛgu</s>, and <s>Budha</s>.

body.text:
śīghroccebhyaḥ iti vaktavye uccaśīghrebhyaḥ iti viparītanirdeśam kurvan ācāryaḥ jñāpayati ã śīghroccāt grahaḥ śodhyate iti | tasmāt śuddhaśeṣāt jyā utpādyante | tābhiḥ trairāśikam pūrvavat | pūrvam ācāryeṇa mandakrameṇa grahāḥ nirdiṣṭāḥ | śaśī sarvebhyaḥ śīghraḥ lakṣyate, tasmāt mandaḥ savitā, tataḥ mandaḥ budhaḥ, tathā uttaram bhṛgu-kuja-guru-śanayaḥ | ayam punar śīghrakramaḥ, śani-guru-kuja-bhṛgu-budhāḥ iti | ete śanyādayaḥ yathā uttaram
śīghrāḥ | evam idam navamam gītikāsūtram || 10 ||
body.translated_text: Though he should say 'from the fast-apogees,' the <s>Ācārya</s> (teacher), by making the reversed statement 'from the apogee-fast,' indicates that the planet is to be subtracted from the fast-apogee (<s>shīghrocca</s>). From the purified remainder, the sines (<s>jyā</s>) are produced. By means of those, the rule of three [is applied] as before. Previously, the <s>Ācārya</s> stated the planets in the slow (<s>manda</s>) order. The Moon is observed as the fastest of all; then the Sun is slower; then <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) is slower; then after that, <s>Bhṛgu</s> (Venus), <s>Kuja</s> (Mars), <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter), and <s>Śani</s> (Saturn) [are progressively slower]. But this fast (<s>shīghra</s>) order is: <s>Śani</s>, <s>Guru</s>, <s>Kuja</s>, <s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Budha</s>. These, beginning with <s>Śani</s>, are progressively faster. Thus, this is the ninth <s>Gītikā-Sūtra</s>. // 10 //

body.text: yugmapadayoḥ mandaśīghraparidhayaḥ
body.translated_text: The slow and fast circumferences for the even quadrants

body.text: etebhyaḥ eva mandaśīghrebhyaḥ dvitīyacaturthapadaparidhipramāṇaparijñānāya āha ã
body.translated_text: In order to ascertain the circumference-measures of the second and fourth quadrants from these very slow and fast [corrections], he states:

children.translated_text: From the slow [apogee], <s>ṅa</s>, <s>kha</s>, <s>da</s>, <s>ja</s>, <s>ḍā</s> —
of the retrograde [planets], in the second and the fourth quadrant.
<s>jā</s>, <s>ṇa</s>, <s>kla</s>, <s>chla</s>, <s>jhna</s> from the apogee,
from the fast [apogee]; <s>giyiṅśa</s> — the outermost orbit of the terrestrial wind. // 11 //

body.text: mandāt, ṅa kha da ja ḍā iti etāni avibhaktikāni, vakriṇām, dvitīye, pade, caturthe, ca, jā ṇa kla chla jhna etāni avibhaktikāni, uccāt, śīghrāt, giyiṅśa avibhaktikaḥ, kuvāyukakṣyā, antyā |
body.translated_text: 'From the slow [apogee]'; <s>ṅa</s>, <s>kha</s>, <s>da</s>, <s>ja</s>, <s>ḍā</s> — these are indeclinable [notations]; 'of the retrograde [planets]'; 'in the second'; 'quadrant'; 'the fourth'; 'and'; <s>jā</s>, <s>ṇa</s>, <s>kla</s>, <s>chla</s>, <s>jhna</s> — these are indeclinable; 'from the apogee'; 'from the fast'; <s>giyiṅśa</s> is indeclinable; 'the outermost orbit of the terrestrial wind.'

body.text: mandāt | tathā eva mandoccaviśuddhāt rāśyādikāt utpannāyāḥ jyāyāḥ ete paridhisaṃjñitāḥ guṇakārāḥ | tathā eva jhārdhapramāṇaparimitāḥ ã budhasya ṅa, pañca jhārdhāni, dvāviṃśatissārdhabhāgāḥ, bhṛgoḥ kha, dve jhārdhe, nava bhāgāḥ | kujasya da, aṣṭādaśa jhārdhāni, ekāśītibhāgāḥ | guroḥ ja, aṣṭau jhārdhāni, ṣaṭtriṃśadbhāgāḥ | śaneḥ ḍā, trayodaśa jhārdhāni, aṣṭapañcāśat sārdhabhāgāḥ |
body.translated_text: From the slow [apogee]: similarly, from the corrected slow-apogee [position] expressed in signs and so on, the sines produced [are used with] these multipliers called circumferences (<s>paridhi</s>). Similarly, they are measured in <s>jhārdha</s> units: for <s>Budha</s> (Mercury), <s>ṅa</s> — five <s>jhārdhas</s>, twenty-two and a half degrees. For <s>Bhṛgu</s> (Venus), <s>kha</s> — two <s>jhārdhas</s>, nine degrees. For <s>Kuja</s> (Mars), <s>da</s> — eighteen <s>jhārdhas</s>, eighty-one degrees. For <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter), <s>ja</s> — eight <s>jhārdhas</s>, thirty-six degrees. For <s>Śani</s> (Saturn), <s>ḍā</s> — thirteen <s>jhārdhas</s>, fifty-eight and a half degrees.

body.text:
vakriṇām dvitīye pade caturthe ca | vakram yeṣām te vakriṇaḥ | vakriṇaḥ iti anena śaśisavitroḥ agrahaṇam, yena tayoḥ vakrā gatiḥ na asti | vakriṇaḥ ca budha-bhṛgu-kuja-guru-śanayaḥ | teṣām ete paridhayaḥ | dvitīye pade caturthe ca | ye pūrvābhihitāḥ paridhayaḥ te utsargeṇa caturṣu padeṣu prāptāḥ | teṣām dvitīyacaturthayoḥ padayoḥ ete paridhayaḥ apavādena abhidhīyante | dvitīyacaturthapādavyatirekeṇa pūrvoktaparidhīnām viṣayaḥ | cakāraḥ dvitīyeṣu
ca caturtheṣu ca iti etat artham samuccinoti |
body.translated_text: Of the retrograde [planets] in the second and fourth quadrant: Those which have retrogression are the retrograde [planets]. By the word 'retrograde,' the Moon and the Sun are excluded, since they have no retrograde motion. The retrograde [planets] are <s>Budha</s> (Mercury), <s>Bhṛgu</s> (Venus), <s>Kuja</s> (Mars), <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter), and <s>Śani</s> (Saturn). These are their circumferences. In the second and fourth quadrant: the circumferences previously stated are, by default, applicable in all four quadrants. For those [planets], in the second and fourth quadrants, these circumferences are stated as exceptions. The domain of the previously stated circumferences is exclusive of the second and fourth quadrants. The word 'and' (<s>ca</s>) combines [the meaning] 'in the second and in the fourth.'

body.text:
athavā ã vakriṇām dvitīye pade | ete budhādayaḥ grahāḥ dvitīye pade vakriṇaḥ bhavanti | vakrām gatim caranti iti arthaḥ | nanu ca mandagrahaṇānantaram dvitīye pade vakriṇaḥ iti ucyante, tena mandoccasya dvitīyapade vakraparijñānam prāpnoti, tat ca na iṣyate | na etat asti | vakriṇaḥ dvitīye pade budhādayaḥ iti sāmānyena ucyate | "sāmānyacodanāḥ ca viśeṣe avatiṣṭhante " iti viśeṣe avasthāpyate | kaḥ ca viśeṣaḥ ? śīghroccadvitīyapade eteṣām budhādīnām
vakraparijñānam iti ayam viśeṣaḥ | uktam ca ã
body.translated_text: Alternatively: 'Of the retrograde in the second quadrant.' These planets beginning with <s>Budha</s> become retrograde in the second quadrant. The meaning is: they traverse a retrograde motion. Now, since 'in the second quadrant, retrograde' is stated immediately after the word 'slow' (<s>manda</s>), the knowledge of retrogression in the second quadrant of the slow-apogee would follow — but that is not intended. This is not so. 'The retrograde in the second quadrant are those beginning with <s>Budha</s>' is stated generally. [The rule] 'General injunctions are to be restricted to the specific' restricts it to the specific. And what is the specific? The knowledge of retrogression of these [planets] beginning with <s>Budha</s> in the second quadrant of the fast-apogee — this is the specific. And it has been said:

body.text:
mandoccāt anulomam pratilomam ca eva śīghroccāt |
[golaí, 17]
body.translated_text: Direct motion from the slow-apogee, and retrograde indeed from the fast-apogee. [<s>Gola</s>, 17]

body.text: iti | caturhe ca | ete paridhayaḥ dvitīye caturthe ca pade guṇakārāḥ | dvitīye eva pade vakraparijñānam anyatra api ã
body.translated_text: Thus. 'And in the fourth': these circumferences are the multipliers in the second and fourth quadrants. The knowledge of retrogression is in the second quadrant only; elsewhere too:

body.text:
prathame dṛśyavidhānam dvitīyapadagāḥ tu vakragāḥ sarve |
anuvakragāḥ tṛtīye pade caturthe astam upayānti || iti |
body.translated_text: 'In the first [quadrant] the rule of visibility [applies]; those in the second quadrant are all retrograde; those in the third [quadrant] have resumed direct motion; and in the fourth quadrant they approach setting.' Thus.

body.text: jā ṇa kla chla jhna | śīghroccāt dvitīyacaturthayoḥ padayoḥ paridhayaḥ | śaneḥ jā, aṣṭau jhārdhāni, ṣaṭtriṃśadbhāgāḥ | guroḥ ṇa, pañcadaśa jhārdhāni, saptaṣaṣṭiḥ sārdhabhāgāḥ | kujasya kla, ekapañcāśat jhārdhāni, ardhonakam triṃśaduttaram śatadvayam bhāgānām | bhṛgoḥ chla, saptapañcāśajjhārdhāni, sārdham ṣaṭpañcāśaduttaram śatadvayam bhāgānām | budhasya jhna, ekonaviṃśajjhārdhāni triṃśaduttaram śatam sārdham bhāgānām |
body.translated_text: <s>jā</s>, <s>ṇa</s>, <s>kla</s>, <s>chla</s>, <s>jhna</s>: The circumferences from the fast-apogee in the second and fourth quadrants. For <s>Śani</s> (Saturn), <s>jā</s> — eight <s>jhārdhas</s>, thirty-six degrees. For <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter), <s>ṇa</s> — fifteen <s>jhārdhas</s>, sixty-seven and a half degrees. For <s>Kuja</s> (Mars), <s>kla</s> — fifty-one <s>jhārdhas</s>, two hundred and twenty-nine and a half degrees. For <s>Bhṛgu</s> (Venus), <s>chla</s> — fifty-seven <s>jhārdhas</s>, two hundred and fifty-six and a half degrees. For <s>Budha</s> (Mercury), <s>jhna</s> — nineteen <s>jhārdhas</s>, one hundred and thirty and a half degrees.

body.text: uccāt śīghrāt | atra api śīghroccāt iti vaktavye uccāt śīghrāt iti viparītagrahaṇam kurvannāccāryaḥ jñāpayati ã śīghroccāt grahaḥ śodhyate iti | padacatuṣṭayagrahaṇāt ca karmacatuṣṭayam ã prathamam mandoccakarma, tadanantaram śīghrakarma, punar mandakarma, tadanantaram śīghrakarma | tataḥ grahasphuṭaḥ labhyate | ravicandrayoḥ ekaparidhinirdeśāt ekam eva karma |
body.translated_text: From the apogee, from the fast: Here too, though he should say 'from the fast-apogee,' the <s>Ācārya</s>, by making the reversed statement, indicates that the planet is subtracted from the fast-apogee. And from the four-fold mention of quadrants, a fourfold computation [follows]: first, the slow-apogee computation; then the fast computation; again the slow computation; then the fast computation. From that, the true (<s>sphuṭa</s>) planet is obtained. For the Sun and Moon, since only one circumference is stated, there is only one computation.

body.text:
atha kaścit jyārahitam karma kartum icchati, tadartham āha ã giyiṅśa kuvāyukakṣyāntyā | trayastriṃśacchatāni pañcasaptatyadhikāni [3375] kuvāyukakṣyāpramāṇam | kuḥ bhūḥ, kuvāyuḥ bhūsambandhī vāyuḥ, tasya iyam antyā kakṣyā | etāvataḥ vāyukakṣyāparicchinnākāśapradeśāt parataḥ niyataḥ vāyuḥ yena niyatagatinā pravaheṇa jyotiścakram idam bhrāmyate | kuvāyukakṣyāpramāṇaparicchinnāt ākāśapradeśāt ārādaniyatāḥ vāyavaḥ itaḥ tataḥ paribhramanti
|
body.translated_text: Now, if someone wishes to perform the computation without sines, for that purpose he states: <s>giyiṅśa</s> — the outermost orbit of the terrestrial wind. Three thousand three hundred and seventy-five [3375] is the measure of the orbit of the terrestrial wind. <s>Ku</s> is the Earth; <s>kuvāyu</s> is the wind connected with the Earth; this is its outermost orbit. Beyond the region of space delimited by this wind orbit, the fixed wind by whose steady course, the <s>pravaha</s> (trade-wind), causes this wheel of luminaries to revolve. The winds that are unbound, away from the region of space delimited by the orbit of the terrestrial wind, wander about here and there.

body.text: kuvāyukakṣyāyāḥ grahakarma ã ye abhīṣṭāḥ bhāgāḥ tān cakrārdhabhāgebhyaḥ viśodhya śeṣam taiḥ eva abhīṣṭabhāgaiḥ guṇitam pratirāśya ekam kuvāyukakṣyāyāḥ dvādaśaguṇitāyāḥ śodhyate, tataḥ śeṣasya yaḥ caturthoṃśaḥ sa bhāgahāraḥ | yat pratirāśitam tat antyaphalena guṇitam bhāgahāreṇa vibhajet | labdham abhīṣṭaphalam | uktam ca asmābhiḥ karmanibandhe ã
body.translated_text: The planetary computation of the orbit of the terrestrial wind: Take the desired degrees, subtract them from the half-circle degrees, multiply the remainder by those same desired degrees, and subtract one-twelfth from the orbit of the terrestrial wind multiplied by twelve. Then, one-fourth of the remainder is the divisor. The quotient multiplied by the last result, divided by the divisor — the result is the desired result. And we have stated in the <s>Karmanibandha</s>:

children.translated_text: The computation without <s>makhyādi</s> (sine differences) is stated here in brief:
The degrees of the arc (<s>bhuja</s>) should be subtracted from the half-circle degree-collection.
That remainder, multiplied [by the arc-degrees], placed in two positions, should be subtracted from void-void-arrow-void-ocean [= 40,500].
By one-fourth of the remainder, the two-placed [value] multiplied by the last result
gives the result of the arc and co-arc, or of the direct and reverse sine-multiplier.
<s>Mahābhāskarīya</s>, 7.17–19
Thus, the tenth <s>Gītikā-Sūtra</s>. // 11 //

body.text: caturviṃśatijyārdhāni
body.translated_text: The twenty-four half-chord sines

body.text: atra aśeṣagrahakarma, tat ca jyāpratibandham iti ataḥ jyādarśanārtham āha ã
body.translated_text: Here, the entire planetary computation is dependent on sines; therefore, for the purpose of showing the sines, he states:

children.text: makhi bhakhi phakhi dhakhi ṇakhi ñakhi
children.translated_text: <s>makhi</s>, <s>bhakhi</s>, <s>phakhi</s>, <s>dhakhi</s>, <s>ṇakhi</s>, <s>ñakhi</s>,

children.text: ṅakhi hasjha skaki kiṣga śghaki kighva |
children.translated_text: <s>ṅakhi</s>, <s>hasjha</s>, <s>skaki</s>, <s>kiṣga</s>, <s>śghaki</s>, <s>kighva</s>;
<s>ghlaki</s>, <s>kigra</s>, <s>hakya</s>, <s>dhaki</s>, <s>kica</s>,

children.text: sga jhaśa ṅva kla pta pha cha kalārdhajyāḥ || 12 ||
children.translated_text: <s>sga</s>, <s>jhaśa</s>, <s>ṅva</s>, <s>kla</s>, <s>pta</s>, <s>pha</s>, <s>cha</s> — the half-chord sines. // 12 //

body.text: "makhi"ādayaḥ nigadena eva vyākhyātāḥ | kalārdhajyāḥ | kalāḥ ca tāḥ ardhajyāḥ ca kalārdhajyāḥ | etāḥ jyāḥ liptāpramāṇaparimitāḥ | ardhajyābhiḥ yataḥ śāstravyavahāraḥ tena ardhajyā eva uktā || 12 ||
body.translated_text: '<s>Makhi</s>' and the rest are explained by mere recitation. 'The half-chord sines' (<s>kalārdhajyāḥ</s>): <s>kalās</s> (arc-minutes) that are also half-chords — [hence] 'half-chord sines of arc-minutes.' These sines are measured in minutes (<s>liptā</s>). Since the mathematical usage in the <s>śāstra</s> is with half-chords, only the half-chords have been stated. // 12 //

body.text: daśagītikāsūtraparijñānaphalam
body.translated_text: The fruit of understanding the ten <s>Gītikā-Sūtras</s>

body.text: daśagītikāsūtraparijñānaphalapradarśanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: In order to show the fruit of understanding the ten <s>Gītikā-Sūtras</s>, he states:

children.translated_text: This <s>Daśagītika-Sūtra</s>,
having understood the motion of the Earth and planets within the stellar cage (<s>bhapañjara</s>),
the revolutions of the planets and the stars —
he goes, having pierced through, to the supreme <s>Brahman</s>. // 13 //

body.text:
atra paribhāṣāgītikāḥ daśagītikāḥ gṛhyante | etat daśagītikasūtram bhūgrahacaritam | bhuvi loke | grahāṇām caritanibandhanatvāt etat eva daśagītikasūtram grahacaritam, grahacaritahetutvāt vā yathāsukham kṛtam iti | bhuvi grahacaritam bhūgrahacaritam | na anyaloke grahacaritanibandhanam asti yataḥ daśagītikasūtram tena ucyate bhūgrahacaritam | bhapañjare jñātvā | bhapañjaraḥ golaḥ, tasmin gole tat grahacaritam jñātvā, avagamya, grahāṇām sphuṭagateḥ pratipattihetuḥ
yataḥ golaḥ, etat grahāṇām bhānām ca paribhramaṇamārgam bhittvā param brahma yāti | yaḥ gole samagram daśagītikasūtrapratibaddham grahacaritam jānāti sa param brahma yāti iti || 13 ||
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>paribhāṣā-gītikās</s> (definitional verses) are taken as the ten <s>Gītikās</s>. This <s>Daśagītika-Sūtra</s> [describes] the motion of the Earth and planets. 'On Earth' means 'in the world.' Because this very <s>Daśagītika-Sūtra</s> is the basis for the motion of the planets, it is the planetary motion; or because it is the cause of [understanding] planetary motion, it is made for ease [of understanding] — thus. The planetary motion on Earth is '<s>bhūgrahacarita</s>.' There is no other-worldly basis for planetary motion from which the <s>Daśagītika-Sūtra</s> [derives]; therefore it is called '<s>bhūgrahacarita</s>' (terrestrial planetary motion). 'Having known within the stellar cage': <s>bhapañjara</s> is the celestial sphere (<s>gola</s>); having known, having understood, that planetary motion within that sphere — since the sphere is the cause for understanding the true motions of the planets — having pierced through the path of revolution of the planets and stars, one goes to the supreme <s>Brahman</s>. Whoever knows the complete planetary motion contained in the <s>Daśagītika-Sūtra</s> within the sphere — he goes to the supreme <s>Brahman</s>. // 13 //

children.translated_text: The meaning of the <s>Daśagītika-Sūtras</s> has been explained by <s>Bhāskara</s> for the understanding of those of dull intellect;

children.text: pratipattaye prakāmam sarvaḥ hi samānabhūtaye yatate ||
children.translated_text: for everyone indeed strives for the equal welfare [of all].

body.text: iti bhāskarasya kṛtau
body.translated_text: Thus, in the composition of <s>Bhāskara</s>,

body.text: daśagītikāsūtravyākhyā parisamāptā ||
body.translated_text: the commentary on the <s>Daśagītikā-Sūtras</s> is concluded.

body.text: Gaṇitapādaḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Gaṇitapāda</s> (Chapter on Mathematics)

body.text: maṅgalācaraṇam
body.translated_text: Invocatory verse

children.translated_text: He whose mere remembrance of the name [brings about] existence and non-existence,
blessings and inauspiciousness for gods, demons, and humans —
to Him, whose pair of lotus-feet are rubbed by the crowns of [<s>Brahmā</s>] born from the black lotus and [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] —
obeisance to <s>Śiva</s>. // 1 //
The <s>Ācārya</s> <s>Āryabhaṭa</s>, having propitiated the lotus-born [<s>Brahmā</s>] through pure austerities,

children.text: yat lebhe grahacārasāraviṣayam bījam mahārtham sphuṭam |
children.translated_text: obtained the seed — great in meaning, clear — concerning the essence of planetary motion.
Of that [work], which is skilled in matters beyond the senses, which is a clear and noble real entity,

children.text: vyākhyānam gurupādalabdham adhunā kiñcit mayā likhyate || 2 ||
children.translated_text: the commentary, obtained at the feet of the <s>Guru</s> (teacher), is now being written to some extent by me. // 2 //

body.text: pratipādyavastunirdeśaḥ
body.translated_text: Statement of the subject matter

body.text: atha ācāryāryabhaṭamukhāravindavinissṛtam padārthatrayam ã gaṇitam, kālakriyā, golaḥ iti yat etat gaṇitam tat dvividham caturṣu sanniviṣṭam | vṛddhiḥ hi apacayaḥ ca iti dvividham | vṛddhiḥ saṃyogaḥ, apacayaḥ hrāsaḥ | etābhyām bhedābhyām aśeṣagaṇitam vyāptam | āha ca ã
body.translated_text: Now, the threefold subject-matter that has issued from the lotus-mouth of <s>Ācārya</s> <s>Āryabhaṭa</s>: mathematics (<s>gaṇita</s>), time-reckoning (<s>kālakriyā</s>), and the sphere (<s>gola</s>). That mathematics is of two kinds, contained in four [categories]: increase (<s>vṛddhi</s>) and decrease (<s>apacaya</s>) are the two kinds. Increase is addition; decrease is subtraction. All mathematics without exception is pervaded by these two types. And it is said:

children.text: saṃyogabhedā guṇanāgatāni śuddheḥ ca bhāgaḥ gatamūlamuktam |
children.translated_text: Multiplication and cubing are varieties of addition; and division, the root, and extraction [are varieties] of subtraction.

children.text: vyāptam samīkṣya upacayakṣayābhyām vidyāt idam dvyātmakam eva śāstram ||
children.translated_text: Having observed [that mathematics is] pervaded by increase and decrease, one should know this <s>śāstra</s> to be of dual nature.

body.text:
saṃyogasya vṛddheḥ, bhedāḥ guṇanāgatāni | tāni ca ã asadṛṣayaḥ rāśyoḥ abhyāsaḥ guṇanā, yathā caturṇām pañcānām ca viṃśatiḥ | gatam sadṛśābhyāsaḥ vargaḥ ghanaḥ ca | dvigatam vargaḥ, yathā caturṇām caturṇām ca ṣoḍaśa | evam trigatam ghanaḥ, yathā caturṇām caturṇām caturṇāñ ca catuṣṣaṣṭiḥ | "śuddheḥ ca" iti atra yogārtham cakāraḥ paṭhyate | tena śreḍhīkuṭṭākārādiṣu loke ca aniyatasvarūpavṛddhiḥ sā ca parigṛhītā bhavati | śuddheḥ ca bhāgaḥ
gatamūlamuktam | śuddheḥ apacayasya bhedaḥ bhāgaḥ, gatānām mūlāni ca | atra api śreḍhīkuṭṭākārādi[ṣu] loke ca aniyatasvarūpaḥ apacayaḥ cakārāt eva parigṛhyate | evam śāstre, loke ca na saḥ asti gaṇitaprakāraḥ yaḥ ayam vṛddhyātmakaḥ apacayātmakaḥ vā na bhavati |
body.translated_text: Of addition, i.e. increase, the varieties are multiplication and cubing. And they are: the product of two unequal quantities is multiplication — for example, of four and five, twenty. Cubing is the product of equal quantities: squaring and cubing. Squaring is twofold [self-multiplication] — for example, of four and four, sixteen. Similarly, cubing is threefold [self-multiplication] — for example, of four, four, and four, sixty-four. 'Of subtraction, and' — here the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>) is read for the purpose of inclusion. By that, the increase of indeterminate form in series (<s>śreḍhī</s>), indeterminate analysis (<s>kuṭṭākāra</s>), and worldly [computation] is also included. 'And of subtraction, division, the root, and extraction': division is a variety of decrease; and [the extraction of] the roots of powers. Here too, the decrease of indeterminate form in series, indeterminate analysis, and worldly [computation] is included by the very word 'and.' Thus, in the <s>śāstra</s> and in the world, there is no type of computation that is not of the nature of increase or decrease.

body.text:
yadi evam atra katham prakriyā parikalpanīyā? yatra caturbhāgaḥ pañcabhāgena guṇitaḥ jātaḥ viṃśatibhāgaḥ | iyam ca guṇanā saṃyogasya bhedaḥ ucyate | sa ca ayam śuddheḥ bhedaḥ āpatitaḥ | yatra caturbhāgena viṃśatibhāgasya bhāgaḥ, tatra dṛṣṭaḥ pañcabhāgaḥ | evam ayam śuddheḥ bhedaḥ saṃyogabhedaḥ āpatitaḥ | ubhayatra parigāraḥ ucyate ã [ ekāyām avistāre caturaśrakṣetre viṃśatyāyātacaturaśrakṣetrāṇi | ] tatra ekasya āyāmaḥ pañcabhāgaḥ, vistāraḥ
caturbhāgaḥ | tayoḥ abhyāsaḥ phalam kṣetrasya viṃśatibhāgaḥ | viṃśatibhāgasya caturbhāgaḥ pañcabhāgaḥ iti na doṣaḥ | evam kṣetragaṇite parihāraḥ | rāśigaṇite parihārārtham yatnaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | aparaḥ āha ã "gaṇitam rāśikṣetram dvidhā" | evam karaṇīparikarma ã
body.translated_text: If so, how is the procedure to be conceived here? Where a one-fourth part multiplied by a one-fifth part yields a one-twentieth part — and this multiplication is called a type of addition (<s>saṃyoga</s>), and this has turned out to be a type of subtraction (<s>śuddhi</s>). Where one-fourth is the divisor of one-twentieth, there the result seen is one-fifth. Thus this type of subtraction has turned out to be a type of addition. In both cases the resolution is stated: [In a square field of unit breadth, there are twenty rectangular fields.] There, the length of one is one-fifth, the breadth is one-fourth. The product of these two is the area of the field, which is one-twentieth. That one-fourth of one-twentieth is one-fifth — there is no fault in this. Thus is the resolution in <s>kṣetragaṇita</s> (geometry). In <s>rāśigaṇita</s> (arithmetic), effort must be made for a resolution. Another says: "Mathematics is twofold: arithmetic and geometry." Thus the <s>karaṇī</s> (surd) operations:

body.text: karṇabhujayoḥ samatvam karoti yasmāt tataḥ karaṇī |
body.translated_text: Because it makes the hypotenuse and the side equal, therefore it is called <s>karaṇī</s> (surd).

body.text:
gaṇitam dviprakāram ã rāśigaṇitam kṣetragaṇitam | anupātakuṭṭākārādayaḥ gaṇitaviśeṣāḥ rāśigaṇite abhihitāḥ, śreḍhīcchāyādayaḥ kṣetragaṇite | tat evam rāśyāśritam kṣetrāśritam vā aśeṣam gaṇitam | yat etat karaṇīparikarma tat kṣetragaṇite eva | yadi api anyatre karaṇīparikarma, tathā api tasya na karṇabujākoṭipratipādakatvam iti na doṣaḥ | etat ca karaṇīparikarmatvam yatkarṇādipratipādakatvam | caturṣu sanniviṣṭam, catvāri bījāni, teṣu sanniviṣṭām
| uktam gaṇitam | kālakriyāgolau tatra tatra eva upadekṣyāmaḥ |
  atra ācāryāryabhaṭaḥ śāstram ārabhamāṇaḥ cetasi iṣṭadevatāpraṇāmaḥ hi bhaktyā prayuktaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Mathematics is of two kinds: <s>rāśigaṇita</s> (arithmetic) and <s>kṣetragaṇita</s> (geometry). Proportion, <s>kuṭṭākāra</s> (pulverizer), and other special mathematical topics are stated under arithmetic; series, shadows, and other topics under geometry. Thus all mathematics is either based on quantities or based on figures. That which is <s>karaṇī</s> (surd) operation belongs to geometry alone. Even though surd operations occur elsewhere, there is no fault since those do not serve to establish the hypotenuse, side, and upright. And this character of being a surd operation is precisely that which establishes the hypotenuse and so forth. It is contained in four [sections]; the four seeds (<s>bīja</s>), in those is contained the stated mathematics. The <s>kālakriyā</s> (reckoning of time) and <s>gola</s> (sphere) sections we shall teach in their respective places. Here, master <s>Āryabhaṭa</s>, commencing the treatise, being impelled by devotion, makes a salutation to his chosen deity in his mind:

children.translated_text: Having saluted <s>Brahma</s>, the Earth (<s>ku</s>), the Moon (<s>śaśin</s>), <s>Budha</s> (Mercury), <s>Bhṛgu</s> (Venus), <s>Ravi</s> (the Sun),
<s>Kuja</s> (Mars), <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter), <s>Koṇa</s> (Saturn), and the asterisms (<s>bhagaṇa</s>),
<s>Āryabhaṭa</s> here declares
the knowledge honored at <s>Kusumapura</s>. // 1 //

body.text:
brahmā asya iṣṭadevatā | iṣṭadevatāpraṇāmaḥ hi bhaktyā prayuktaḥ svābhiḥ lāṣateṣṭakāryavighātinaḥ vighnān vinihanti | athavā devāsuramukuṭamaṇimayūkhamālālaṅkṛtacaraṇatvāt sarvāsām devatānām pradhānatamaḥ brahmā, ataḥ tasya ādau namaskriyām kṛtavān ācāryaḥ | athavā ācāryeṇa svāyaṃbhuvasiddhāntasaṃkṣepavasturacanā prastutā, svāyaṃbhuvasiddhāntasya ca vidhātā bhagavān vedhāḥ, tataḥ asya yujyate prathamam praṇāmaḥ tam kartum
| akṣadeśāntarāyattā grahagatiḥ, tau ca akṣadeśāntaraviśeṣau bhūvaśāt iti tat anantaram namaskṛtavān bhuvam | śaśyādīn upari upari avasthitān tadgatinibandhanatvāt śāstrasya iti namaskṛtavān | brahmā ca kuḥ ca śaśī ca budhaḥ ca bhṛguḥ ca raviḥ ca kujaḥ ca guruḥ ca koṇaḥ ca bhagaṇāḥ ca brahma-ku-śaśi-budha-bhṛgu-ravi-kuja-guru-koṇa-bhagaṇāḥ | ataḥ tān brahma-ku-śaśi-budha-bhṛgu-ravi-kuja-guru-koṇa-bhagaṇān, namaskṛtya praṇamya iti arthaḥ | bhāni jyotīṃṣi
aśvinyādīni, teṣām gaṇaḥ bhagaṇaḥ | yat atra śaśyādīnām upari upari avasthāne vaktavyam tat kālakriyāpāde vakṣyāmaḥ | āryabhaṭaḥ iti svasaṃjñābhidhānena anyāḥ svāyaṃbhuvasiddhāntānusāriṇyaḥ kṛtayaḥ santi iti etat pradarśayati | tena bahutvāt svāyāṃbhuvasiddhāntānusāriṇīnām kṛtīnām kena iyam kṛtiḥ kṛtā iti na jñāyate | ataḥ svasaṃjñābhidhānam | yathā "kauṭilyena kṛtam śāstram" iti [arthaśāstram, 1.1.19] | "tu"-śabdaḥ pādapūraṇe | ["iha"-śabdaḥ] asya puram
pradarśayati | nigadati bravīti | kusumapure abhyarcitam jñānam | kusumapuram pāṭaliputram, tatra abhyarcitam jñānam nigadati | evam anuśrūyate ã ayam kila svāyaṃbhuvasiddhāntaḥ kusumapuranivāsibhiḥ kṛtibhiḥ pūjitaḥ, satsu api pauliśa-romaka-vāsiṣṭha-sauryeṣu | tena āha ã "kusumapure abhyarcitam jñānam" iti || 1 ||
body.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> is his chosen deity. Being impelled by devotion, the salutation to the chosen deity destroys the obstacles that impede the desired task with one's own [efforts]. Alternatively, because his feet are adorned with garlands of rays from the crest-jewels of gods and demons, <s>Brahmā</s> is the foremost of all deities; therefore the master (<s>ācārya</s>) made obeisance to him first. Alternatively, since the master has undertaken the composition of an abridgment of the <s>Svāyambhuvasiddhānta</s>, and the author of the <s>Svāyambhuvasiddhānta</s> is the blessed Creator (<s>Vedhāḥ</s>), therefore it is fitting to make salutation to him first. The motion of planets depends on latitude and terrestrial longitude; and these particular differences of latitude and longitude are due to the Earth — therefore he next saluted the Earth. He saluted the Moon and the others positioned successively higher, because the treatise is based on their motions. <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>ku</s> (Earth) and <s>śaśin</s> (Moon) and <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) and <s>Bhṛgu</s> (Venus) and <s>Ravi</s> (Sun) and <s>Kuja</s> (Mars) and <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter) and <s>Koṇa</s> (Saturn) and <s>bhagaṇa</s> (asterisms) — these are "<s>brahma-ku-śaśi-budha-bhṛgu-ravi-kuja-guru-koṇa-bhagaṇāḥ</s>." Therefore, having saluted those — <s>brahma-ku-śaśi-budha-bhṛgu-ravi-kuja-guru-koṇa-bhagaṇān</s> — "<s>namaskṛtya</s>" means "having bowed down." <s>Bha</s> means stars (<s>jyotīṃṣi</s>), beginning with <s>Aśvinī</s>; their group (<s>gaṇa</s>) is <s>bhagaṇa</s>. What is to be said here regarding the successive positions of the Moon and others above [each other], that we shall state in the <s>Kālakriyāpāda</s> (chapter on reckoning of time). By stating his own name "<s>Āryabhaṭa</s>," he indicates that there are other compositions following the <s>Svāyambhuvasiddhānta</s>. Since there are many compositions following the <s>Svāyambhuvasiddhānta</s>, it is not known by whom this composition was made; therefore the statement of his own name. As in "the treatise composed by <s>Kauṭilya</s>" [<s>Arthaśāstra</s>, 1.1.19]. The word "<s>tu</s>" is a metrical filler. [The word "<s>iha</s>"] indicates his city. "<s>Nigadati</s>" means "he declares." The knowledge honored at <s>Kusumapura</s> — <s>Kusumapura</s> is <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>; there the honored knowledge he declares. Thus it is traditionally heard: this <s>Svāyambhuvasiddhānta</s> was venerated by the learned residents of <s>Kusumapura</s>, even though the <s>Pauliśa</s>, <s>Romaka</s>, <s>Vāsiṣṭha</s>, and <s>Saurya</s> [siddhāntas] also exist. Therefore he says: "the knowledge honored at <s>Kusumapura</s>." // 1 //

body.text: saṅkhyāsthānanirūpaṇam
body.translated_text: Determination of number-places

body.text: saṅkhyāsthānanirūpaṇārtham āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of determining number-places, he states:

children.text: ekam ca daśa ca śatam ca
children.translated_text: One, ten, a hundred,
a thousand, then <s>ayuta</s> (ten-thousand) and <s>niyuta</s> (hundred-thousand), likewise <s>prayuta</s> (million),
<s>koṭi</s> (ten-million), <s>arbuda</s> (hundred-million), and <s>vṛnda</s> (billion) —
from place to place, each is tenfold. // 2 //

body.text: laghvartham saṅkhyāsthānāni prakramyante | anyathā hi saṅkhyāsthāna nirūpaṇābhāvāt guruḥ gaṇitavidhiḥ syāt | katham? rūpabahutvasthāpanāyām rūpāṇi bahūni sthāpayitavyāni bhavanti | satyām punaḥ sthānakalpanāyām yat rūpaiḥ bahubhiḥ nirvartyam karma tat ekena eva nirvartayitum śakyate |
body.translated_text: For the sake of brevity, number-places are introduced. Otherwise, without the determination of number-places, the mathematical procedure would be cumbersome. How so? In representing a large number of units, many units would have to be placed. But when place-value notation is available, the operation that would require many units can be accomplished with just one.

body.text:
ekam ca daśa ca śatam ca sahasram | eteṣām ekadaśaśatasahasrāṇām prathamadvitīyatṛtīyacaturthāni sthānāni | tu pādapūraṇe | ayutaniyute ayutam ca niyutam ca ayutaniyute | ayutasya pañcamam sthānam | daśasahasrāṇi ayutam | niyutasya ṣaṣṭham sthānam | niyutam lakṣaḥ | tathā tena eva prakāreṇa prayutasya saptamam sthānam | daśalakṣāḥ prayutam | koṭiḥ, koṭyāḥ aṣṭamam sthānam | lakṣāḥ śatam, koṭiḥ | arbudam, arbudasya navamam sthānam | daśakoṭyaḥ
arbudam | vṛndam, vṛndasya daśamam sthānam | koṭiśatam vṛndam |
body.translated_text: One, ten, a hundred, and a thousand — the places of these, namely one, ten, hundred, and thousand, are the first, second, third, and fourth places. "<s>Tu</s>" is a metrical filler. <s>Ayuta</s> and <s>niyuta</s> — <s>ayuta</s> is the fifth place; ten-thousands are an <s>ayuta</s>. <s>Niyuta</s> is the sixth place; <s>niyuta</s> means <s>lakṣa</s> (a hundred thousand). Likewise, by the same pattern, <s>prayuta</s> is the seventh place; ten <s>lakṣas</s> are a <s>prayuta</s>. <s>Koṭi</s> — the eighth place is that of <s>koṭi</s>; a hundred <s>lakṣas</s> is a <s>koṭi</s>. <s>Arbuda</s> — the ninth place is that of <s>arbuda</s>; ten <s>koṭis</s> are an <s>arbuda</s>. <s>Vṛnda</s> — the tenth place is that of <s>vṛnda</s>; a hundred <s>koṭis</s> are a <s>vṛnda</s>.

body.text:
sthānāt sthānam daśaguṇam syāt | sthānāt sthānam anyat daśaguṇam svaparikalpitasthānāt uttaram sthānam daśaguṇam bhavati iti yāvat | kim artham idam ucyate | nanu ca etāni sthānāni anantarāpekṣayā daśaguṇāni eva | yadi ebhyaḥ anyasthānaparigrahārtham vacanam tathā sati sthānābhidhānam anarthakam | kutaḥ? sthānāt sthānam daśaguṇam syāt iti anena eva abhihitā, abhihitasthānaparigrahasya siddhatvāt | na eṣaḥ doṣaḥ | sthānāt sthānam daśaguṇam
syāt iti etat lakṣaṇam | ekādīni sthānāni asya lakṣaṇasya udāhṛtāni | na etat asti | na hi sūtrakārāḥ saṃkṣepavivakṣavaḥ lakṣaṇam udāharaṇam brūyuḥ | na evam vijñāyate | yadā lakṣaṇam udāharaṇam ca nirarthakam tarhi ekādivṛndānatāyāḥ saṅkhyāyāḥ saṃjñāḥ nirūpyante | sthānāt sthānam daśaguṇam iti ekādisaṃkhyāyāḥ sthānanirūpaṇamātram eva upadiśyate, upayogābhāvāt na saṅkhyāsaṃjñā |
body.translated_text: "From place to place, each is tenfold" — from one place, the next place is tenfold; that is, the place succeeding the one established by convention is tenfold. Why is this stated? After all, these places are already tenfold with respect to the one immediately preceding. If the statement is for the purpose of including other places beyond these, then the naming of [specific] places would be purposeless. Why? Because it is already expressed by "from place to place, each is tenfold," since the inclusion of the stated places is already established [by that rule]. This is not a fault. "From place to place, each is tenfold" — this is the definition (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>). The places beginning with one are illustrations of this definition. This is not so; for authors of <s>sūtras</s> who desire brevity would not state both a definition and an illustration. It is not to be understood thus. When both definition and illustration are purposeless, then what is being determined are the names of numbers from one up to <s>vṛnda</s>. "From place to place, each is tenfold" — only the determination of places of numbers beginning with one is being taught; the names of numbers are not [taught], since there is no use [for them here].

body.text:
atra etat praṣṭavyam ã kā eṣām sthānānām śaktiḥ, yat ekam rūpam daśa śatam sahasram ca bhavati | satyām ca etasyām sthānaśaktau krāyakāḥ viśeṣeṣṭakrayyabhojanāḥ syuḥ | krayyam ca vivakṣātaḥ alpam bahu ca syāt | evam ca sati lokavyavahārān yathābhāvaprasaṅgaḥ | na eṣaḥ doṣaḥ | sthāne vyavasthitāni rtūpāṇi daśādīni kṛtāni | kim tarhi taiḥ? tāni pratipādyante lekhāgamanyāyena | athavā laghvartham sthānāni prakramyante iti uktam asmābhiḥ |
nyāsaḥ ca sthānānām ã
body.translated_text: Here this is to be asked: What is the power of these places, by which a single unit becomes ten, a hundred, and a thousand? And if this power of place-value exists, then buyers would purchase goods of specific desired prices. And the price could be small or large according to one's wish. In that case, worldly transactions would be as one arbitrarily desires. This is not a fault. Units placed in [their respective] positions are made into ten and so forth. What then [is done] with them? They are represented by the method of written notation. Alternatively, we have stated that places are introduced for the sake of brevity. And the notation of places [is as follows]:

body.text: vargaparikarma
body.translated_text: Square operations

body.text: vargaparikarmapradarśanāya āryāpūrvārdham āha ã
body.translated_text: To demonstrate the square operation, he states the first half of the <s>āryā</s> verse:

body.text: vargaḥ samacaturaśraḥ phalam ca sadṛśadvayasya saṃvargaḥ |
body.translated_text: A square is an equilateral quadrilateral, and its area is the product of two equal [sides].

body.text:
vargaḥ karaṇī kṛtiḥ vargaṇāḥ yāvakaraṇam iti paryāyāḥ | samāścatasraḥ aśrayaḥ yasya saḥ ayam [sama]caturaśraḥ kṣetraviśeṣaḥ, sa vargaḥ | samacaturaśrakṣetraviśeṣaḥ saṃjñī, vargaḥ saṃjñā | atra saṃjñisaṃjñayoḥ abhedena upacāreṇa ucyate "vargaḥ samacaturaśraḥ" iti | yathā "māṃsapiṇḍaḥ devadattaḥ" iti | anyathā atra yāvān samacaturaśrakṣetraviśeṣaḥ tasya sarvasya aniṣṭasya api vargasaṃjñāprasaṅgaḥ | kva anyatra aniṣṭasya samacaturaśrakṣetraviśeṣasya
vargasaṃjñāprasaṅgaḥ? ucyate ã asamakarṇasya
body.translated_text: <s>Varga</s> (square), <s>karaṇī</s> (surd), <s>kṛti</s> (square), <s>vargaṇā</s> (squaring), and <s>yāvakaraṇa</s> (square-making) are synonyms. That which has four equal sides — this specific quadrilateral figure is a square. The specific equilateral quadrilateral figure is the referent (<s>saṃjñin</s>); <s>varga</s> is the name (<s>saṃjñā</s>). Here, by a figurative identification of name and referent, it is said "a square is an equilateral quadrilateral." Just as [one says] "<s>Devadatta</s> is a lump of flesh." Otherwise, every equilateral quadrilateral figure, even an unintended one, would be subject to the designation <s>varga</s>. Where else would an unintended equilateral quadrilateral figure be subject to the designation <s>varga</s>? It is said: [in the case] of one with unequal diagonals —

body.text: parilekhau 1 & 2
body.translated_text: Diagrams 1 & 2

body.text: samacaturaśrakṣetraviśeṣasya asya (parilekhaḥ 1) | dvisamatryaśrakṣetrasya samunnatavadavasthitasya asya (parilekhaḥ 2) |
body.translated_text: This (Diagram 1) is of an equilateral quadrilateral figure [with unequal diagonals]. This (Diagram 2) is of an isosceles triangular figure standing upright.

body.text:
vargasaṃjñāprasaṅge kaḥ doṣaḥ? ucyate ã "phalam ca sadṛśadvayasya saṃvargaḥ" iti sadṛśadvayasya saṃvargaḥ phalam prāpnoti, na ca iṣyate evam | kva tarhi? karṇagrahaṇam kartavyam; vargaḥ samakarṇasamacaturaśrakṣetraviśeṣaḥ iti | athavā tulyasaṅkhyābhyām karṇābhyām upalakṣitasya eva samacaturaśrakṣetraviśeṣasya vargasaṃjñā jijñāsyate | kutaḥ? na aniṣṭārthatvāt śastrapravṛtteḥ | athavā na eva loke evam ākāraviśiṣṭasya samacaturaśrakṣetrasya samacaturaśrasaṃjñā
susiddhā | āyatacaturaśrakṣetrādiṣu vargakarmaṇaḥ astitvāt teṣām asamacaturaśrāṇām api vargasaṃjñāprasaṅgaḥ | na eṣaḥ doṣaḥ | teśu api yaḥ vargaḥ sa samacaturaśrakṣetraphalam | tat yathā ã samacaturaśrakṣetram ālikhya aṣṭadhā vibhajya trikacatuṣkavistārāyāmāni catvāri āyatacaturaśrakṣetrāṇi pañcakarṇāni parikalpayet | tatra evam parikalpitacaturaśrāyatacaturaśrakṣetrakarṇabāhukam samacaturaśram kṣetram madhye avatiṣṭhate | yaḥ tatra
āyatacaturaśrakṣetrakarṇāyatavargaḥ, sa ca antaḥsamacaturaśrakṣetre phalam | tribhuje api etat eva darśanam, ardhāyatacaturaśratvāt tribhujasya | durvidagdhapratyāyanāya ca kṣetram ālikhyate ã
body.translated_text: What is the fault if the designation <s>varga</s> [were applied to these]? It is said: "And its area is the product of two equal [sides]" — the product of two equal [sides] would yield the area, but this is not desired [for such figures]. Where then [is the qualification]? The mention of diagonals must be made: a <s>varga</s> is a specific equilateral quadrilateral figure with equal diagonals. Alternatively, the designation <s>varga</s> is intended only for that specific equilateral quadrilateral figure characterized by two equal diagonals. Why? Because the treatise does not proceed for unintended purposes. Alternatively, in common usage, the designation "equilateral quadrilateral" is not well-established for a figure of such a [non-square] shape. Since square operations exist in rectangular and other figures, those non-equilateral quadrilaterals would also be subject to the designation <s>varga</s>. This is not a fault. In those cases too, the square [result] is the area of an equilateral quadrilateral figure. That is as follows: having drawn an equilateral quadrilateral figure and divided it eightfold, one should construct four rectangles with breadth three and length four and diagonal five. In the figure so constructed, an equilateral quadrilateral figure with sides equal to the diagonals of the rectangles remains in the middle. The square of the diagonal-length of the rectangular figures there is the area of the inner equilateral quadrilateral figure. For a triangle too, the same demonstration [applies], since a triangle is half a rectangle. And a figure is drawn to convince the slow-witted:

body.text: parilekhaḥ 3
body.translated_text: Diagram 3

body.text:
asmād yaḥ yaḥ vargaḥ samacaturaśrakṣetraviśeṣaḥ | evam phalam ca sadṛśadvayasya saṃvargaḥ | saṃvargaḥ iti asya samacaturaśrasya kṣetraphalam nirucyate | sadṛśasya dvayam sadṛśadvayam | athavā sadṛśadvayam ca taddvayam ca samasadṛśadvayam | sadṛśadvayasya saṃvargaḥ | saṃvargaḥ ghātaḥ guṇanā hatiruddhartanā iti paryāyāḥ | sadṛśadvayasaṃvargaḥ phalam tasya samacaturaśrasya | sadṛśadvayasaṃvargaḥ iti atra iṣṭabāhuvacanam kartavyam | anyathā hi
yayoḥ kayościt sadṛśayoḥ saṃvargaḥ phalam prāpnoti | na etat asti | nahi phalārthī anyakṣetram uddiśya anyayoḥ abhyāsam karoti | na hi odanārthī pāṃsūn ādatte |
body.translated_text: From this, every square is a specific equilateral quadrilateral figure. Thus, "and its area is the product of two equal [sides]." <s>Saṃvarga</s> (product) — by this the area of this equilateral quadrilateral is etymologically explained. The pair of equals is <s>sadṛśadvaya</s> (two equal things). Alternatively, <s>sadṛśadvaya</s> is that pair which is mutually equal. The product of two equal [quantities] — <s>saṃvarga</s>, <s>ghāta</s> (product), <s>guṇanā</s> (multiplication), <s>hati</s> (product), and <s>uddhartanā</s> are synonyms. The product of two equal quantities is the area of that equilateral quadrilateral. In [the expression] "the product of two equal quantities," it should be specified "of the desired side." Otherwise, the product of any two equal quantities whatsoever would yield the area. This is not so; for one who desires the area does not perform the multiplication of two [quantities] belonging to a different figure while intending a particular figure. Just as one who desires cooked rice does not take up sand.

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Example problem:

children.text: ekādinavāntānām vargāḥ ye tān pṛthak pṛthak brūhi |
children.translated_text: State separately the squares of [the numbers] ending with one through nine.

children.text: śatapādasya ca vargam śatasya tena eva yuktasya || 1 ||
children.translated_text: and the square of the square-root of a hundred, and of a hundred combined with that [square-root]. (1)

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9; śatapādaḥ 25, śatam anena yuktam 125 |
body.translated_text: Setting down (<s>nyāsa</s>): 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9; the square-root of a hundred is 25; a hundred combined with that is 125.

body.text: yathāsaṅkhyena ekādinavāntānām phalam ca "sadṛśadvayasya saṃvargaḥ" iti labdhāḥ vargāḥ, nyāsaḥ ã 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 81 |
body.translated_text: The results for [the numbers] one through nine, in order, obtained by [the rule] 'the product of two equal [numbers] is the square' — the squares set down are: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 81.

body.text: evam eṣām lakṣaṇāni sūtrāṇi ã
body.translated_text: Thus, the defining rules (<s>sūtras</s>) for these [operations] are:

children.text: antyapadasya ca vargam kṛtvā dviguṇam tat eva ca antyapadam |
children.translated_text: Having squared the last digit, and [multiplying] that very last digit by two,
one should multiply by the remaining digits, shifting each time, in the squaring procedure.

body.text: iti, taiḥ ekādinavāntānām rūpāṇām vargasaṅkhyā vaktavyā | kutaḥ? ajñātāyām vargasaṅkhyāyām yataḥ antyapadasya vargasaṅkhyā na śakyate nyastum | asmākam punaḥ sarvam lakṣaṇena eva saṃgṛhītam |
body.translated_text: By those [rules], the square-numbers of the digits one through nine must be stated [first]. Why? Because when the square-number is not known, the square-number of the last digit cannot be set down. For us, however, everything is comprehended by the [single] defining rule alone.

body.text: śatapādasya vargaḥ 625; śatasya tena eva yuktasya 15625 |
body.translated_text: The square of the square-root of a hundred is 625; [the square] of a hundred combined with that is 15,625.

body.text: bhinnavargaḥ api evam eva | kintu sadṛśīkṛtayoḥ chedāṃśarāśyoḥ pṛthak pṛthak vargam kṛtvā chedarāśivargeṇa aṃśarāśivargasya bhāgalabdham bhinnavargaḥ |
body.translated_text: The squaring of fractions is done in the same way. However, having made the denominator and numerator quantities homogeneous, one squares each separately, and the quotient obtained by dividing the square of the numerator-quantity by the square of the denominator-quantity is the square of the fraction.

children.translated_text: Practice problem (<s>uddeśaka</s>):
Of six-and-a-quarter, and of one combined with one-fifth,

children.text: rūpadvitayasya ca me brūhi kṛtim navamahīnasya || 2 ||
children.translated_text: and of two diminished by one-ninth — tell me the square. (2)

body.text:
nyāsaḥ ã 6 1 2
  1 1 1
  4 5 9í
body.translated_text: Setting down: 6, 1, 2 [over] 1, 1, 1 [over] 4, 5, 9.

body.text:
karaṇam ã "chedaguṇam sāṃśam" iti
25
 4 |
etayoḥ chedāṃśayoḥ rāsyoḥ pṛthak pṛthak vargarāśī 16, 625. chedarāśivargeṇa aṃśarāśivargam hṛtvā labdham
39
  1
16 |
evam śeṣayoḥ api yathāsaṅkhyena
body.translated_text: Computation: By [the rule] 'multiply by the denominator and add the numerator' — [we get] 25/4. Of these denominator and numerator quantities, the separate squares are 16 and 625. Dividing the square of the numerator-quantity by the square of the denominator-quantity, the result is 39 1/16. Similarly for the remaining two, in order:

body.text: ghanaparikarma
body.translated_text: Cube operations

body.text: ghanaparikarmapradarśanāya āryāparārdham āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of demonstrating the cube operation, he states the latter half of the <s>āryā</s>:

body.text: sadṛśatrayasaṃvargaḥ ghanaḥ tathā dvādaśāśritaḥ syāt || 3 ||
body.translated_text: The product of three equal [numbers] is the cube; and it is twelve-edged. (3)

body.text: sadṛśatrayasya saṃvargaḥ
body.translated_text: The product of three equal [numbers]

body.text:
sadṛśatrayasaṃvargaḥ | sadṛśatrayasaṃvargaḥ ghanaḥ bhavati | ghanaḥ vṛndam sadṛśatrayābhyāsaḥ iti paryāyāḥ | sa ca dvādaśāśritaḥ | dvādaśa aśrayaḥ yasya sa ayam dvādaśāśritaḥ, syāt bhavet | "tathā"śabdena samacaturaśratām ghanasya pratipādayati | na etat asti | antareṇa api "tathā"śabdam asya ghanasya samacaturaśratā śakyate eva pratipattum | kutaḥ ? sadṛśatrayasaṃvargaḥ iti anena samacaturaśrakṣetraphalasya tatkṣetravāhusaḍṛśam
eva ucchrāyam ācaṣṭe, yasmāt kṣetraphalam ucchrāyaguṇitam ghanaphalam | athavā "vargaḥ samacaturaśraḥ" iti atra adhikṛtam samacaturaśragrahaṇam anuvartate, aśrayaḥ yasya mṛdā anyena vā pradarśayitavyāḥ |
body.translated_text: is the cube. The cube, the solid — the product of three equal [numbers] — these are synonyms. And it is twelve-edged (<s>dvādaśāśrita</s>): that which has twelve edges (<s>aśrayas</s>) is twelve-edged; 'it would be' (<s>syāt bhavet</s>). By the word 'likewise' (<s>tathā</s>), he teaches the equilateral nature of the cube. This is not [necessary]. Even without the word 'likewise,' the equilateral nature of this cube can indeed be understood. Why? Because by [the phrase] 'the product of three equal [numbers],' he describes the height as equal to the area of an equilateral quadrilateral field, since the area [of the base] multiplied by the height gives the solid volume. Alternatively, the phrase 'equilateral quadrilateral' (<s>samacaturaśra</s>) that was used in '[the] square is equilateral-quadrilateral' carries over [to this context], and the edges are to be demonstrated with clay or other [material].
