children.translated_text: when the square has been subtracted from the <s>varga</s> (odd) [place], the quotient placed in the next position is the root. (4)

body.text:
bhāgaḥ hṛtiḥ bhajanam apavartanam iti paryāyāḥ | tam bhāgam, haret gṛhṇīyāt | kasmāt sthānāt prabhṛti iti āha ã avargāt, na vargaḥ avargaḥ, tasmāt avargāt | atra gaṇite viṣamam sthānam vargaḥ | tasya eva nañā viṣamatve pratiṣiddhe avargaḥ iti samam sthānam, yataḥ hi viṣamam samam ca sthānam | kena bhāgam haret iti āha ã nityam dviguṇena vargamūlena | dvau guṇaḥ yasya tat dviguṇam | kim tat ? vargamūlam | tena dviguṇena vargamūlena | katham
punar tat vargamūlam labhyate iti āha ã vargāt varge śuddhe labdham sthānāntare mūlam | vargāt viṣamasthānāt, śuddhe varge vargagaṇite iti arthaḥ, yat atra labdham tat sthānāntare mūlasaṃjñam bhavati | sthānāt anyasthānam sthānāntaram, tasmin sthānāntare tasya labdhasya mūlasaṃjñā | yatra punaḥ sthānāntaram eva na vidyate, tatra tasya tatra eva mūlasaṃjñā | kutaḥ ? sthānāntarasya asambhavāt | etat eva sūtram punar punar āvartaye yāvat parisamāptam gaṇitakarma
iti |
body.translated_text: 'Division' (<s>bhāga</s>), 'taking' (<s>hṛti</s>), 'apportioning' (<s>bhajana</s>), 'reducing' (<s>apavartana</s>) — these are synonyms. That division — one should take, i.e., perform. From which place onward? He says: 'from the <s>avarga</s>' — what is not <s>varga</s> is <s>avarga</s>; from that <s>avarga</s> [place]. Here in mathematics, the odd place is <s>varga</s>. When its odd-ness is negated by the particle <s>nañ</s>, <s>avarga</s> means the even place — for there are odd and even places. By what should one divide? He says: 'always by twice the square root.' That whose multiplier is two is 'twice' (<s>dviguṇa</s>). What is that? The square root. By that doubled square root. But how is that square root obtained? He says: 'when the square has been subtracted from the <s>varga</s> [place], the quotient placed in the next position is the root.' From the <s>varga</s>, i.e., from the odd place; 'when the square has been subtracted' means when the square-number [has been subtracted] — this is the meaning; whatever is obtained here, that, in the next position, receives the designation 'root.' A position other than [the current] position is 'the next position' (<s>sthānāntara</s>); in that next position, the designation 'root' [applies] to what was obtained. But where there is no next position at all, there the designation 'root' applies to it right there. Why? Because of the impossibility of a next position. This same rule (<s>sūtra</s>) is to be applied repeatedly until the computational operation is complete.

body.translated_text: Cube root

body.text: ghanamūlānayanāya āha ã

the square [of the quotient], multiplied by three times the preceding [root],

body.text:
na ghanaḥ aghanaḥ, tasmāt aghanāt | [bhajet] bhāgam haret, bhāgam gṛhṇīyāt iti arthaḥ | aghanasthānasya anekatvāt āha ã dvitīyāt | atra gaṇite ghanaḥ ekaḥ, dvau aghanau | kutaḥ etat ghanaḥ ekaḥ dvau aghanau iti ucyate ã "vargaḥ tripūrvaguṇitaḥ śodhyaḥ prathamāt aghanāt" iti prathamāghanasiddhiḥ, "aghanāt bhajet dvitīyāt" iti dvitīyāghanasiddhiḥ | ghanaḥ punar ekaḥ eva, dvitīyasya aśravaṇāt | aghanāt dvitīyāt prabhṛti kena bhāgam haret iti āha ã triguṇena
ghanasya mūlavargeṇa | trayaḥ guṇāḥ asya triguṇaḥ | kaḥ ? ghanasya mūlavargaḥ | tena triguṇena ghanasya mūlavargeṇa | vargaḥ tripūrvaguṇitaḥ sodhyaḥ prathamāt | vargaḥ tribhiḥ pūrveṇa ca rāśinā guṇitaḥ tripūrvaguṇitaḥ | kasya vargaḥ ? labdhasya iti vākyaśeṣaḥ | śodhyaḥ | śodhayitavyaḥ | prathamāt aghanāt iti sambandhanīyam | ghanaḥ ca ghanāt | ghanaḥ ca śodhayitavyaḥ | kutaḥ ? ghanāt | ghanasthānāt | tataḥ ghanamūlam bhavati iti adhyāhāryam | atra idam eva
ghanarāśim dṛṣṭvā ghanaḥ ekaḥ dvau aghanau iti vigaṇayya yatra ghanaḥ tasmāt ghanamūlam pūrvam eva kuryāt, ghanaḥ ca ghanāt śodhyaḥ iti anena | tataḥ sarvam idam āryāsūtram upasthitam bhavati, "aghanāt bhajet dvitīyāt" ityādi |
body.translated_text: What is not <s>ghana</s> (cube) is <s>aghana</s> (non-cube); from that <s>aghana</s> [place]. '[One should] divide' — one should take the quotient, i.e., perform the division. Since there are multiple <s>aghana</s> places, he says: 'from the second.' Here in mathematics, there is one <s>ghana</s> (cube) [place] and two <s>aghana</s> (non-cube) [places]. Whence is it known that there is one cube [place] and two non-cube [places]? 'The square multiplied by three times the preceding is to be subtracted from the first <s>aghana</s>' — this establishes the first non-cube [place]; 'one should divide from the second <s>aghana</s>' — this establishes the second non-cube [place]. But the cube [place] is only one, since a second is not heard. From the second <s>aghana</s> [place] onward, by what should one divide? He says: 'by three times the square of the cube root.' Three multipliers — [that is] 'triple' (<s>triguṇa</s>). Of what? The square of the cube root. By that tripled square of the cube root. 'The square multiplied by three times the preceding is to be subtracted from the first [<s>aghana</s>].' The square — multiplied by three and by the preceding quantity — is 'multiplied by three times the preceding.' Whose square? — of the quotient, this being the completion of the sentence. 'Is to be subtracted' — is to be removed. 'From the first' — this should be connected with 'from the first <s>aghana</s> [place].' 'And the cube from the <s>ghana</s> [place]' — and the cube is to be subtracted. From where? From the <s>ghana</s> [place] — from the cube-place. Then the cube root results — this is to be supplied. Here, having looked at the cube-number and identified 'one cube [place], two non-cube [places],' one should first extract the cube root from the cube [place] — by [the rule] 'and the cube from the <s>ghana</s> [place].' Then this entire <s>āryā</s>-sūtra comes into play: 'one should divide from the second <s>aghana</s>' and so forth.

body.text:
tisraḥ bhujāḥ yasya kṣetrasya tat idam kṣetram tribhujam | bhujā bāhuḥ pārśvam iti paryāyāḥ | tatra trīṇi kṣetrāṇi sama-dvisama-viṣamāṇi | "tribhujasya" iti tribhujakṣetrajātimaṅgīkṛtya ekavacananirdeśaḥ | tasya tribhujasya | phalaśarīram | phalasya śarīram phalaśarīram, phalapramāṇam iti arthaḥ | samadalakoṭībhujārdhasaṃvargaḥ | samadalakoṭī, avalambakaḥ | atra kecit ã same dale yasyāḥ sā iyam samadalā, samadalā ca asau koṭī ca samadalakoṭī iti varṇayanti
| teśām sama-dvisamatryaśrakṣetrayoḥ eva phalasiddhiḥ, na viṣamatryaśrakṣetrasya | asmākam punar samadalakoṭī iti anena avalambakavyutpattyā bruvatām trayāṇām api phalānayanam siddham | athavā ye vyutpattim kurvanti teṣām api trayāṇām tryaśrakṣetrāṇām phalānayanam siddham eva | kutaḥ ? "rūḍheṣu kriyā vyutpattikarmārthā na arthakriyā" iti | bhujāyāḥ ardham bhujārdham | atha atra bhujāśabdena bhujā bāhuḥ pārśvam iti sāmānyena trayāṇām pārśvānām
pratipattau prasaktāyām viśiṣṭā eva bhujā parigṛhyate, bhujāsaṃjñitā | "sāmānyacodanāḥ ca viśeṣe avatiṣṭhante" iti | atra gaṇite bhujāśabdaḥ auṇādikaḥ pratipattavyaḥ, anyathā hi "bhujānyubjau pāṇyupatāpayoḥ" [aṣṭādhyāyī, 7.3.61 ] iti bhujāśabdasya pāṇāvarthe nipātitattvāt kṣetrapārśve na labhyate | tasyāḥ bhujāyāḥ ardham bhujārdham | samadalakoṭyā bhujārdhasya ca saṃvargaḥ samadalakoṭībhujārdhasaṃvargaḥ, tribhujasya phalaśarīram bhavati |
body.translated_text: A field (<s>kṣetra</s>) that has three sides (<s>bhujas</s>) — that field is a triangle (<s>tribhuja</s>). 'Side' (<s>bhujā</s>), 'arm' (<s>bāhu</s>), 'edge' (<s>pārśva</s>) — these are synonyms. Among these, there are three [types of] fields: equilateral (<s>sama</s>), isosceles (<s>dvisama</s>), and scalene (<s>viṣama</s>). 'Of a triangle' — by accepting the class 'triangular field,' the singular designation [is used]. Of that triangle. 'The body of the area' (<s>phalaśarīra</s>) — the body (measure) of the area is the area-measure — this is the meaning. 'The product of the perpendicular and half the base' (<s>samadalakoṭībhujārdhasaṃvarga</s>). <s>Samadalakoṭī</s> is the perpendicular (<s>avalambaka</s>). Here, some [commentators explain]: that whose halves are equal is <s>samadala</s>; and [being] both <s>samadala</s> and <s>koṭī</s>, it is <s>samadalakoṭī</s> — thus they describe it. For them, the area-computation works only for equilateral and isosceles triangular fields, not for scalene triangular fields. For us, however, by explaining <s>samadalakoṭī</s> as meaning 'perpendicular' (<s>avalambaka</s>) through its derivation, the area-computation for all three [types] is established. Alternatively, even for those who [explain through] the derivation [as 'equal-halving'], the area-computation for all three triangular fields is indeed established. Why? Because [the principle is:] 'for conventional terms, the operation based on derivation is not [a restriction on] the actual function.' Half of the base (<s>bhujā</s>) is '<s>bhujārdha</s>.' Now, here, when the word '<s>bhujā</s>' (side) generally denotes all three sides — [since] 'side,' 'arm,' and 'edge' [are all synonyms] — with the application [to all three] being possible, only the specific [side called] '<s>bhujā</s>' is to be taken, [the one] designated as '<s>bhujā</s>.' [For the principle is:] 'general injunctions settle in the specific.' Here in mathematics, the word '<s>bhujā</s>' should be understood as an <s>Auṇādika</s> [derivation]; otherwise, since by [the rule] '<s>bhujānyubjau pāṇyupatāpayoḥ</s>' [<s>Aṣṭādhyāyī</s> 7.3.61], the word '<s>bhujā</s>' is grammatically restricted to the meaning 'hand,' it cannot be obtained for the side of a field. Half of that <s>bhujā</s> is '<s>bhujārdha</s>.' The product of the perpendicular (<s>samadalakoṭī</s>) and half the base (<s>bhujārdha</s>) is the '<s>samadalakoṭībhujārdhasaṃvarga</s>' — [this] is the body of the area of a triangle.

body.translated_text: Computation: 'In an equilateral triangular field, the perpendicular-foot (<s>avalambakasthiti</s>) is exactly the middle [of the base]' — thus the half-base is the foot-segment (<s>ābādhā</s>): 3 and 1/2. 'The square of the lateral side and the square of the upright together equal the square of the hypotenuse' [<s>Gaṇitapāda</s>, 17] — thus the squares of the side and the upright equal the hypotenuse-square. Therefore, when the side-square is subtracted from the hypotenuse-square, the remainder is the perpendicular-square: 36 and 3/4; the perpendicular is the surd of 36 and 3/4. The half-side too is the surd of 12 and 1/4. Therefore, there is a product of surds — and the area obtained is 'the product of the perpendicular and the half-side,' which is the surd of 450 and 3/16. For the remaining two equilateral [triangles] also, the area is similarly obtained in corresponding order [surd of 768], surd of 1230 and 3/16.

body.text:
karaṇam ã bhujayoḥ vargaviśeṣaḥ tayoḥ vā samāsaviśeṣābhyāsaḥ tribhujakṣetre ābādhāntarasamāsaviśeṣābhyāsaḥ bhavati | bhūmyā ābādhāntarasamāsapramāṇayā vibhajya labdham bhūmau eva saṃkramaṇam | "antarayuktam hīnam dalitam" iti [gaṇitaí, 24 ] | anena krameṇa ābādhāntarapramāṇe labhyete | tābhyām ābādhāntarapramāṇābhyām viṣamatribhujasya samadalakoṭyānayanam | tat yathā ã bhujayoḥ vargarāśī 169, 225 | etayoḥ viśeṣaḥ 56 | bhujayoḥ
ekībhāvaḥ 28, tayoḥ viśeṣaḥ 2 | tayoḥ abhyāsaḥ iti [bhujayoḥ vargaviśeṣaḥ] ābādhāntarasamāsapramāṇayā bhūmyā 14, anayā hṛte labdham 4, anena bhuvā saha saṃkramaṇam "antarayuktam hīnam" iti 18, 10 | dalam iti yathākrameṇa ābādhāntare 1, 5 | etābhyām tribhujakṣetrasya avalambakānayanam ã pañcadaśakena karṇena navapramāṇena ca ābādhāntareṇa labdhā samadalakoṭī 12; trayodaśapramāṇena karṇena pañcapramāṇena ca ābādhāntareṇa labdhā sā eva samadalakoṭī
12 | phalam "samadalakoṭībhujārdhasaṃvargaḥ" iti bhujā bhūmiḥ, tasyāḥ ardham 7, samadalakoṭībhujārdhasaṃvargaḥ iti phalam āgatam 84 |
body.translated_text: Computation: The difference of the squares of the two sides — or equivalently, the product of the sum and difference of those two — in a triangular field is [equal to] the product of the sum and difference of the foot-segments (<s>ābādhāntara</s>). Dividing by the base, whose measure equals the sum of the foot-segments, the quotient is the difference of the foot-segments applied to the base itself. 'The half of [the result obtained by] adding and subtracting the interval' [<s>Gaṇitapāda</s>, 24]. By this procedure, the measures of the two foot-segments are obtained. From those two foot-segment measures, the perpendicular of the scalene triangle is derived. As follows: The squares of the two sides are 169, 225. Their difference is 56. The sum of the two sides is 28, their difference is 2. The product of those [= the difference of the squares of the sides] [is 56]. Dividing by the base of measure 14 (which equals the sum of the foot-segments), the quotient is 4. Applying this to the base: 'adding and subtracting the interval' gives 18, 10. Halving gives the foot-segments in order: 9, 5. From these, the perpendicular of the triangular field is derived: with the hypotenuse of fifteen and the foot-segment of nine, the perpendicular obtained is 12; with the hypotenuse of thirteen and the foot-segment of five, the same perpendicular 12 is obtained. The area is 'the product of the perpendicular and the half-side' — the side being the base, its half is 7; the product of the perpendicular and the half-side gives the area: 84.

body.text: śaḍaśrighanaphalam
body.translated_text: Volume of a Six-Edged Solid (Tetrahedron)

body.text: ghanaphalānayanārtham asya eva tribhujakṣetrasya āryāpaścārdham āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of deriving the volume, he states the latter half of this same <s>āryā</s> verse for the triangular field:

body.text: ūrdhvabhujātatsaṃvargārdham sa ghanaḥ ṣaḍaśriḥ iti || 6 ||
body.translated_text: The product of the vertical height and the [base-]area, halved — that is the volume of the six-edged [solid] (<s>ṣaḍaśri</s>). // 6 //

body.text:
ūrdhvabhujā kṣetramadhyaḥ ucchrāyaḥ, tat iti kṣetraphalam, ūrdhvabhujāyāḥ tasya ca saṃvargaḥ ūrdhvabhujātatsaṃvargaḥ, tasya ardham ūrdhvabhujātatsaṃvargārdham | sa ghanaḥ ghanaphalam iti yāvat, sa ca ṣaḍaśriḥ | ṣaḍaśrayaḥ yasya saḥ ṣaḍaśriḥ ghanaḥ | atha nirjñāte ūrdhvabhujāpramāṇe ghanaphalam ūrdhvabhujātatsaṃvargārdham iti śakyate vaktum, na ca anirjñāte | satyam eva etat | kintu atra nirjñātam eva ūrdhvabhujāpramāṇam | kutaḥ ? śāstre
tadānayanopāyapradarśanāt | tat yathā ã ūrdhvabhujā hi nāma kṣetramadhyaḥ ucchrāyaḥ iti pratyakṣam | sa ca tiryagavasthitasya śṛṅgāṭakakṣetrabāhoḥ karṇavadavasthitasya koṭiḥ, bhujākarṇamūlakṣetrakendrāntarālam | tadānayane trairāśikam ã yadi tribhujakṣetrāvalambakena tribhujakṣetrabāhuḥ labhyate tadā tasya eva tribhujakṣetrabāhudalasaṅkhyakasya avalambakasya kiyān bāhuḥ iti | etat karṇabhujākoṭitrairāśikavidhānam pradeśāntaraprasiddham eva iti na

children.text: atra abhihitam | sa ca pradeśaḥ "yaḥ ca eva bhujāvargaḥ kotīvargaḥ ca karṇavargaḥ saḥ" [gaṇitaí, 17] iti, "trairāśikaphalarāśim tam atha icchārāśinā hatam" [gaṇitaí, 26 ] iti ca |
children.translated_text: is not stated here. And that other context is: 'The square of the side and the square of the upright together equal the square of the hypotenuse' [<s>Gaṇitapāda</s>, 17], and 'the result-quantity of the rule of three, then multiplied by the desire-quantity' [<s>Gaṇitapāda</s>, 26].

body.translated_text: The 'vertical height' (<s>ūrdhvabhujā</s>) is the elevation at the center of the field; 'that' refers to the area of the field; the product of the vertical height and that [area] is 'the product of the vertical height and that'; half of that is 'half the product of the vertical height and that.' 'That is the volume' — meaning: the solid volume. And it is 'six-edged' (<s>ṣaḍaśri</s>) — that which has six edges. Now, when the measure of the vertical height is known, the solid volume can be stated as 'half the product of the vertical height and the area' — but not when it is unknown. True indeed. But here, the measure of the vertical height is in fact known. From where? Because the method of its derivation is shown in the science. As follows: The 'vertical height' is by definition the elevation at the center of the field — this is directly perceivable. And it is the upright of the hypotenuse-like side of the tilted (<s>śṛṅgāṭaka</s>) triangular field; [and the distance] between the base of the side and the center of the base-field is [the base]. For its derivation, the rule of three: If by the perpendicular of the triangular field, the side of the triangular field is obtained, then by the perpendicular equal to half that very side of the triangular field, what side [is obtained]? This is the rule of proportions involving hypotenuse, side, and upright, which is well-known in other contexts — and therefore

body.translated_text: The inner hypotenuse obtained is [the surd of] 48. This very hypotenuse is the side of the upper triangular field. The difference between the square of the hypotenuse and the square of the side is the square of the vertical height. And that is 16. There the vertical height is to be displayed with strings, rods, or the like. The area is [the surd of] 3888. The half of the product of these area-surds and vertical-height-surds is the volume. 'Half' here — because both are surds, division is by four [of the surds]. The volume obtained is the surd of 93312.

body.text: vṛttakṣetraphalam
body.translated_text: Area of a Circular Field

body.text: atha vṛttakṣetraphalānayanārtham āha ã
body.translated_text: Now, for the purpose of deriving the area of a circular field, he says:

body.text: samapariṇāhasya ardham viṣkambhārdhahatam eva vṛttaphalam |
body.translated_text: Half the circumference of uniform perimeter, multiplied by the semi-diameter — that alone is the area of a circle.

body.text:
pariṇāhaḥ paridhiḥ | samaḥ ca asau pariṇāhaḥ ca samapariṇāhaḥ, tasya ardham | anye punar anyathā vigraham kurvanti ã samaḥ pariṇāhaḥ yasya kṣetrasya tat samapariṇāham, tasya ardham iti | teṣām kṣetraphalārdhasya grahaṇam prāpnoti, anya-pādārthena samapariṇāhaśabdena kṣetrābhidhānāt | viṣkambhaḥ vyāsaḥ, tasya ardham viṣkambhārdham, tena hatam viṣkambhārdhahatam, viṣkambhārdhaguṇitam iti yāvat | evakārakaraṇam āryāpūraṇārtham pratipattavyam
| athavā evakārakaraṇena upāyaniyamaḥ kriyate | samapariṇāhasya ardham viṣkambhārdhahatam eva vṛttaphalam, na anyat upāyāntaram iti | na, etat asti, upāyāntaraśravaṇāt anyatra "vyāsārdhakṛtiḥ trisaṅguṇā gaṇitam" iti | na etat upāyāntaram sūkṣmam, kintu vyāvahārikam iti | tasmāt ekam eva upāyāntaram, sūkṣmagaṇitānayanasya na anyat iti |
body.translated_text: <s>Pariṇāha</s> means circumference (<s>paridhi</s>). 'Uniform circumference' (<s>samapariṇāha</s>) — [the circumference that is] equal and [is] the perimeter; its half. Others, however, analyze the compound differently: 'that field whose perimeter is uniform is <s>samapariṇāha</s>'; its half. For them, the taking of half of the area would follow, since the word <s>samapariṇāha</s> would denote the field by its secondary meaning. '<s>Viṣkambha</s>' means diameter; its half is the semi-diameter (<s>viṣkambhārdha</s>); multiplied by that is 'multiplied by the semi-diameter' — i.e., multiplied by the semi-diameter. The use of the word '<s>eva</s>' (alone/indeed) is to be understood as completing the <s>āryā</s> meter. Or alternatively, by the word '<s>eva</s>', a restriction on the method is made: half the circumference multiplied by the semi-diameter alone is the circle-area — there is no other alternative method. No — this is [not right], because another method is heard elsewhere: 'the square of the semi-diameter multiplied by three is the area.' But that other method is not precise; rather, it is practical (<s>vyāvahārika</s>). Therefore, there is only one [precise] method, for deriving the exact (<s>sūkṣma</s>) area — no other.

body.text: golaghanaphalam
body.translated_text: Volume of a Solid Sphere

body.text: ghanaphalapradarśanārtham āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of showing the volume, he says:

body.text: tat nijamūlena hatam ghanagolaphalam niravaśeṣam || 7 ||
body.translated_text: That [area], multiplied by its own square root, is the exact volume of the solid sphere. // 7 //

body.text:
tat iti anena pūrvārdhagaṇitaniṣpannam vṛttakṣetrasya tatphalam parigṛhyate | nijamūlam ātmanaḥ mūlam | yat kṣetraphalam tat svakīyena mūlena guṇitam iti yāvat | athavā tat kṣetraphalam, nijam avitatham āmnāyāviruddham iti arthaḥ, mūlena hatam, anyasya aśrutatvāt svena mūlena tatkṣetraphalam guṇitam | nijamūlena hatam nijamūlahatam iti vigrahaḥ | tat punar kṣetraphalam mūlakriyamāṇam karaṇitvam pratipadyate, yasmāt karaṇīnām mūla[m apekṣitam]
| tataḥ punar api karaṇīnām akaraṇībhiḥ saṃvargaḥ na asti iti kṣetraphalam karaṇyate | evam ayam arthaḥ arthāt avasīyate kṣetraphalavargaḥ kṣetraphalena guṇitaḥ iti | ghanaḥ ca asau golaḥ ca ghanagolaḥ, golaḥ vṛttam, ghanagolasya phalam ghanagolaphalam | niravaśeṣam | na kiñcit anena karmaṇā śiṣyate | yena anyena karmaṇā ghanagolaphalam ānayanti na tena ghanagolaphalam niravaśeṣam bhavati, vyāvahārikatvāt tasya karmaṇaḥ ã
vyāsārdhaghanam bhitvā navaguṇitam ayoguḍasya ghanagaṇitam |
iti |
body.translated_text: 'That' — by this, the circle-area derived in the preceding half-verse is taken up. 'Its own root' (<s>nijamūla</s>) is the root of itself. The area multiplied by its own root — this is the meaning. Or alternatively: 'that' is the area; '<s>nija</s>' means true, not contradicting the tradition — this is the meaning; 'multiplied by the root' — since [the root] of no other [quantity] is heard, multiplied by its own root. The compound analysis is: '<s>nijamūlena hatam</s>' = '<s>nijamūlahatam</s>.' Now, that area, when its root is taken, acquires the status of a surd (<s>karaṇī</s>), since the root of surds is required. Therefore again, since there is no product of surds with non-surds, the area is converted to a surd. Thus, this meaning is determined by implication: the square of the area multiplied by the area. 'Solid' and 'sphere' — <s>ghanagola</s>; <s>gola</s> means circle; the volume of a solid sphere is the solid-sphere-volume. 'Exact' (<s>niravaśeṣam</s>) — nothing is left over by this operation. The method by which others derive the solid-sphere-volume — by that [method], the solid-sphere-volume is not exact, because that method is practical (<s>vyāvahārika</s>): 'Splitting the cube of the semi-diameter and multiplying by nine gives the solid volume of an iron ball.'

body.text: samalambacaturbhujaphalam
body.translated_text: Area of an Isosceles Trapezium

body.text: dvi[sama-viṣama]caturaśrādīnām antaḥkarṇayoḥ ca atra sampātapramāṇaphalaparijñānāya āryām āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of knowing the intersection-measure, the area, and the diagonals of isosceles and scalene quadrilaterals and the like, he states the <s>āryā</s> verse:

children.translated_text: The two sides multiplied by the length, divided by their sum, [give] the respective perpendicular segments;
multiplied by half the sum of the widths — the area of the figure is to be known [when expressed] in terms of length. // 8 //

body.text:
āyāmaḥ vistāraḥ dairghyam iti paryāyāḥ | āyāmaḥ guṇaḥ yayoḥ te āyāmaguṇe | ke te ? pārśve | bhūḥ ekam pārśvam mukham itaram | āyāmaguṇe bhūvadane iti arthaḥ | tayoḥ yogaḥ tadyogaḥ | kayoḥ ? pārśvayoḥ | tadyogahṛte | ke ? āyāmaghne pārśve | svasya pātaḥ svapātaḥ, svapātayoḥ lekhe svapātalekhe | dve api pṛthak pṛthak labdhe iti vākyaśeṣaḥ | svapātalekhā nāma antaḥkarṇayoḥ saṃpātasya bhūmukhamadhyasya ca antarālam | vistaraḥ kṣetrasya pṛthutvam
| yadi evam vistāraḥ iti prāpnoti "prathane vākyaśabde" [aṣṭādhyāyī, 3.3.33] iti ghañi kṛte | ne eṣaḥ doṣaḥ | ayam avastre staraśabdaḥ, tena viśabdena samāsāntaḥ asau "vividhastaraḥ vistaraḥ" iti | vistarayoḥ yogaḥ vistarayogaḥ, bhūvadanayogaḥ iti arthaḥ | vistarayogasya ardham vistarayogārdham, vistarayogārdham guṇaḥ yasya sa vistarayogārdhaguṇaḥ | kaḥ ? āyāmaḥ | tasmin vistarayogārdhaguṇe āyāme kṣetraphalam jñeyam | vistarayogārdhaguṇaḥ āyāmaḥ kṣetraphalam
iti yāvat | samyak anādiṣṭena ālikhite kṣetre svapātalekhāpramāṇam trairāśikagaṇitena pratipādayitavyam | tathā trairāśikena eva ubhayapārśve karṇāvalambakasampātānayanam | pūrvasūtreṇa atra dvisamaviṣamatryaśrakṣetraphalam darśayitavyam | vakṣyamāṇasūtreṇa antarāyatacaturaśrakṣetraphalānayanam anena vā anyeṣu api kṣetreṣu yāni teṣām antarvartīni kṣetrāṇi teṣām karṇāvalambakādisādhanam tat upadiṣṭalakṣaṇena eva | na ca teṣām anyatra avasthānamātrāt
eva anyat karaṇam syāt |
body.translated_text: <s>Āyāma</s> (length), <s>vistāra</s> (breadth), and <s>dairghya</s> (extension) are synonyms. Those of which the length is a multiplier are 'multiplied by the length.' Which are those? The two sides (<s>pārśve</s>). The base (<s>bhū</s>) is one side, the face (<s>mukha</s>) is the other. 'Multiplied by the length' means [multiplied by] the base and the face — this is the meaning. The sum of those two is 'their sum'...

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: bhūmiḥ caturdaśa syāt vadanam catvāri ca eva rūpāṇi |
children.translated_text: The base is fourteen, and the face is four measures;

children.text: karṇau trayodaśāgrau saṃpātāgram phalam ca vada || 1 ||
children.translated_text: the two lateral sides (<s>karṇa</s>) are thirteen each — state the intersection point and the area. // 1 //

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Notation:

body.text: parilekhaḥ 14
body.translated_text: Diagram 14

body.text: karaṇam ã mukhabhūmiviśeṣārdham bhujā [5] | tayā bhujayā pṛthaguktagaṇitena eva avalambakasiddhiḥ, sa ca 12 | ayam eva avalambakaḥ āyāmaḥ | pṛthak pṛthak pārśve anena guṇite jāte 48, 168. pārśvayoḥ yogaḥ 18. anena bhāgalabdhe svapātalekha
body.translated_text: Computation: Half the difference of face and base is the arm (<s>bhuja</s>) [= 5]. By that arm, through the previously stated calculation, the altitude (<s>avalambaka</s>) is obtained, which is 12. This altitude itself is the length. Each side multiplied separately by this gives 4...

body.text:
29
21
33 vistarayogārdhaḥ 1. anena āyāmaḥ guṇitaḥ kṣetraphalam 108 |
body.translated_text: 29, 21, 33. Half the sum of widths [= 1]. The length multiplied by this gives the area = 108.

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: viṃśatiḥ ekābhyadhikā paṅktiḥ nava ca eva kīrtitā saṅkhyā |
children.translated_text: Twenty-one is the row, and nine is the stated number;
state the computation of the base, lateral sides, and face, along with the intersection segments. // 2 //

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Notation:

body.text: parilekhaḥ 15
body.translated_text: Diagram 15

body.text:
svapātalekhe pūrvakaraṇena
  2 5
  2 3
  5 5 |
kṣetraphalam 120 |
body.translated_text: The intersection segments obtained by the previous computation: 2 5, 2 3, 5 5. Area = 120.

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: triṃśat tryadhikā bhūmiḥ saptadaśa anyāni kīrtitāni atra |
children.translated_text: Thirty-three is the base, and seventeen is the other [i.e., the face] stated here;

children.text: gaṇitam tatra kiyat syāt svapātalekhe ca ke syātām || 3 ||
children.translated_text: what would be the area there, and what would be the perpendicular segments? // 3 //

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Notation:

body.text: parilekhaḥ 16
body.translated_text: Diagram 16

body.text:
asya trisamacaturaśrasya kṣetrasya labdhe svapātalekhe
  5 9
  1 9
  10 10 |
kṣetraphalam 375 |
body.translated_text: For this equilateral quadrilateral figure, the perpendicular segments obtained are: 5 9, 1 9, 10 10. Area = 375.

body.text: viṣamacaturaśrakṣetreṣu phalamātram eva uddiśyate, na sampātalekhe, durjñātatvāt avalambakasya | anyat api ca ã yat atra viṣamacaturaśram kṣetram na tat anyagaṇitakṣetraiḥ samānam | tat ca ã
body.translated_text: For scalene quadrilateral figures, only the area is stated, not the intersection segments, because the altitude is difficult to determine. Moreover: the scalene quadrilateral figure here is not the same as those in other mathematical treatises...

children.translated_text: With face five-squared [= 25], added [to give] sixty as the measure of the base stated;
the two lateral sides measured as thirteen, multiplied by four and three respectively in order. // 4 //

body.text: asya yau avalambakau tau na sadṛśau | atra ca yat upadiśyate tasya yau avalambakau tau tulyasaṅkhyau | tena gaṇitaśāstrāntaropadiṣṭaviṣamacaturaśrakṣetrasya asya ca asādṛśyam sati api ca viṣamatve |
body.translated_text: The two altitudes of this [figure] are not equal. But in what is taught here, the two altitudes are of equal number. Therefore, the dissimilarity between the scalene quadrilateral figure taught in other mathematical treatises and this one, being established...

body.text: atha yat gaṇitaśāstrāntaropadiṣṭaviṣamacaturaśrakṣetram yat ca iha upadiśyate tayoḥ dvayoḥ api phalanirdeśaḥ api anena upadeśena śakyate [kartum] | durjñātāvalambakasya kim ? ucyate ã viṣamakṣetreṣu phalamātram eva uddiśya[te], na sampātalekhe ca iti | atha cet parijñātaḥ avalambakaḥ bhavati tadā phalam ca sampātalekhe ca śakyate vijñātum | katham ? pūrvopadiṣṭagaṇitakarmaṇā eva |
body.translated_text: Now, for the scalene quadrilateral figure taught in other mathematical treatises and for what is taught here — the statement of the area of both can be accomplished by this very instruction. What about the altitude being difficult to determine? It is said...

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Example:

children.translated_text: The length is stated as twelve, the base is nineteen less one [= eighteen];

children.text: mukham pañca samākhyātam karṇau tasya atha kīrtitau ||
children.translated_text: the face is stated as five, and the two lateral sides are then declared

children.text: daśa pañca-tribhiḥ ca eva samyuktāni pṛthak pṛthak |
children.translated_text: as ten and five-plus-three [= eight], separately;

children.text: phalam sampātalekhe ca jñātum icchāmi tattvataḥ || 5 ||
children.translated_text: I wish to know the area and the intersection segments accurately. // 5 //

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Notation:

body.text: parilekhaḥ 17
body.translated_text: Diagram 17

body.text:
labdhe sampātalekhe
  2 9
  1 1
  2 2 |
kṣetraphalam 144 | evam anyeṣu api evaṃvidheṣu kṣetreṣu phalānayanam sampātalekhānayanam ca || 8 ||
body.translated_text: The intersection segments obtained: 2 9, 1 1, 2 2. Area = 144. Thus, for other figures of this type also, the computation of area and intersection segments [is performed]. // 8 //

body.text: kṣetraphalam pratyayakaraṇam ca
body.translated_text: Area of figures and verification computation

body.text: sarvakṣetrāṇām phalapratyayakaraṇārtham āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of verification of the area of all figures, he says:

body.text: sarveṣām kṣetrāṇām prasādhya pārśve phalam tadabhyāsaḥ |
body.translated_text: Having refined the two sides, the area [of all figures] is their product.

body.text:
sarveṣām kṣetrāṇām phalam nirdeṣṭavyam | katham ? prasādhya pārśve | "pra"-śabdaḥ prakṛṣṭavācī, prakarṣeṇa pārśve sādhayitvā iti | kaḥ ca tayoḥ prasādhyamānayoḥ pārśvayoḥ prakarṣaḥ ? ucyate ã pārśvatā | kaḥ punar arthaḥ pārśvatāśabdasya iti | ucyate ã yadi sarvakṣetram prasādhyamānam, [tadā "pārśvatā"-śabdāsya arthaḥ] pārśve eva bhavati, āyatacaturaśram eva iti yāvat | phalam tadabhyāsaḥ | teṣām sarvakṣetrāṇām pratyākalitapārśvāyatacaturaśrāṇām
phalam tayoḥ pārśvayoḥ abhyāsaḥ, vistārāyāmābhyāsaḥ iti yāvat | "abhyāsaḥ guṇanā saṃvargaḥ" iti paryāyāḥ |
body.translated_text: The area of all figures is to be stated. How? 'Having refined the sides.' The prefix 'pra' denotes 'excellently'; having refined the sides excellently — this is the meaning. And what is the refinement (<s>prakarṣa</s>) of those two sides being refined?...

body.text: atha sarvaśabdasya niravaśeṣavācitvāt niravaśeṣāṇi eva kṣetrāṇi ākṣipyante, tasmāt sarvakṣetrāṇām phalasya anena eva sūtreṇa siddhatvāt pūrvābhihitasūtrābhidhānam anarthakam | na anarthakam | pratyayakaraṇam phalam ca anena ucyate | abhihitānām kṣetrāṇām phalasya pratyayakaraṇam, yasmāt gaṇitavidaḥ maskari-pūraṇa-pūtanādayaḥ sarveṣām kṣetrāṇām phalam āyatacaturaśrakṣetre pratyāyayanti | uktam ca ã
body.translated_text: Now, since the word 'all' (<s>sarva</s>) denotes without remainder, figures without remainder are encompassed. Therefore, since the area of all figures is established by this very <s>sūtra</s> alone, the statement of the previously mentioned <s>sūtras</s> is purposeless. Not so...

children.text: karaṇaiḥ uktaiḥ nityam phalam anugamya āyate tu vijñeyam |
children.translated_text: By the stated computations, having always verified the area, [the result] is to be known as it comes;

children.text: pratyayakaraṇam kṣetre vyaktam phalam āyate yasmāt ||
children.translated_text: because the verification computation of a figure [yields] the manifest area as it comes.

body.text: anabhihitānām kṣetrāṇām phalān ayanam abhīṣṭakṣetrāyatacaturaśrīkaraṇena eva |
body.translated_text: The method for finding the area of figures not [previously] mentioned is precisely the conversion [of the figure] into a rectangle of the desired figure.

body.text: atha katham ekena eva yatnena phalānayanam pratyayakaraṇam ca prasādhyate ? atha idam pratyayakaraṇārtham prakṛtam, sa katham phalānayanāya bhavati ? atha phalānayanārtham, katham pratyayakaraṇāya ? nea eṣaḥ doṣaḥ | anyārtham prakṛtam anyārtham sādhakam dṛṣṭam | tat yathā ã "śālyartham kulyāḥ praṇīyante | tābhyaḥ ca pānīyam pīyate, upaspṛśyate ca |" [ aṣṭādhyāyī, 1.1.22, pātañjalabhāṣyam ] evam iha api | tat yathā ã
body.translated_text: Now, how is finding the area and verification computation accomplished by a single effort? If this [<s>sūtra</s>] is intended for verification, how does it serve for finding the area? If intended for finding the area, how [does it serve] for verification?...

body.text: āyatacaturaśrakṣetraphalānayana uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Example for finding the area of a rectangular figure:

children.text: aṣṭau pañca ca paṅktivistāraḥ dairghyam api amīṣām yat |
children.translated_text: Eight, five, and the row-breadth, and whatever is the length of these —

children.text: aṣṭiḥ dvādaśa manavaḥ gaṇitam kiyat āyatānām tu || 1 ||
children.translated_text: sixty, twelve, nine — how much is the area of these rectangles? // 1 //

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Notation:

body.text: parilekhaḥ 18
body.translated_text: Diagram 18

body.text: aṣṭau ekam pārśvam ; ṣoḍaśa anyat | tayoḥ pārśvayoḥ abhyāsaḥ, phalam āgatam 128 | śeṣayoḥ api evam eva 60, 140 |
body.translated_text: Eight is one side; sixteen is the other. The product of those two sides [gives] the area obtained = 128. For the remaining two also, similarly: 60, 140.

body.text: pūrvasūtraniṣpannakṣetraphalānām pratyayakaraṇam pradarśyate | tat yathā ã
body.translated_text: The verification computation for the areas of figures obtained by the previous <s>sūtras</s> is now demonstrated. Namely:

children.translated_text: The areas that have been found by computation for three-sided, four-sided, and circular [figures] —

children.text: teṣām pratyayakaraṇam kathaya katham bhavati sarveṣām || 2 ||
children.translated_text: tell how the verification computation of all of them is done. // 2 //

body.text: asya samatryaśrikṣetrasya pūrvadṛṣṭasya eva katham phalapratyayakaraṇam [iti] nyāsaḥ ã
body.translated_text: For this equilateral triangular figure, which was previously seen — how is the verification of its area [done]? Notation:

body.text: parilekhaḥ 19
body.translated_text: Diagram 19

body.text: etat eva nyastam āyatacaturaśrakṣetram jātam ã
body.translated_text: This very [figure], when set up, becomes a rectangular figure:

body.text: parilekhaḥ 20
body.translated_text: Diagram 20

body.text: tribhujasya avalambakaḥ āyāmaḥ
body.translated_text: The altitude of the triangle is the length.

body.text:
karaṇyaḥ
36
  3
  4
[bhūmyardham vistāraḥ karaṇyaḥ
12
  1
  4 ]
phalam pārśvayoḥ abhyāsaḥ iti karaṇyaḥ
450
  3
  16
pūrvalikhitā [eva ] |
body.translated_text: Surds: 36, 3, 4. [Half the base is the breadth: surds 12, 1, 4.] The area is the product of the sides — thus, surds: 450, 3, 16 — as previously written.

body.text: evam eva [dvi]sameṣu, viṣameṣu ca | viṣamākhyasya nyāsaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Similarly for isosceles and scalene [triangles]. Notation for the scalene [triangle]:

body.text: parilekhaḥ 21
body.translated_text: Diagram 21

body.text: asya api avalambakaḥ āyāmaḥ 12, bhūmyardham vistāraḥ 7 |
body.translated_text: For this also, the altitude = length = 12; half the base = breadth = 7.

body.text: parilekhaḥ 22
body.translated_text: Diagram 22

body.text: asya api pūrvavat eva vistārāyām ayoḥ saṃvargaḥ phalam 84 |
body.translated_text: For this also, just as before, the product of the breadth and length is the area = 84.

body.text: athavā āyatacaturaśrakṣetrayoḥ ardhakṣetraphalasaṃyogaḥ asya phalam | tayoḥ dvayoḥ pañcavistārasya dvādaśāyām asya ekasya, dvitīyasya api navavistārasya dvādaśāyām asya ardhakṣetraphalasaṃyogaḥ asya phalam | tayoḥ dvayoḥ pañcavistārasya dvādaśāyām asya ekasya dvitīyasya api navavistārasya dvādaśāyām asya nyāsaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Alternatively, the sum of the half-areas of two rectangular figures is the area of this [triangle]. Of those two, the area of one with breadth five and length twelve, and of the second with breadth nine and length twelve — the half-area...

body.text: parilekhaḥ 23
body.translated_text: Diagram 23

body.text: dvādaśapañcakasya phalam vistārāyāmābhyāsakrameṇa 60, asya ardham eva asmin viṣamatryaśrikṣetre iti 30, nava[vistāra]dvādaśāyām asya phalam 108, asya api ardham eva asmin anupraviṣṭam iti 54 ; etayoḥ ardhaphalayoḥ yogaḥ sā eva caturaśītiḥ 84 |
body.translated_text: For the twelve-by-five [rectangle], the area by the method of product of breadth and length is 60; its half in this scalene triangle is 30. The area of the nine-[breadth]-by-twelve-length [rectangle] is 108; its half too, entering into this...

body.text: evam dvisamatrisamaviṣamacaturaśreṣu api phalam pratyāyanīyam | vṛttakṣetre viṣkambhārdham vistāraḥ, paridhyardham āyāmaḥ, tat eva āyatacaturaśrakṣetram | anayā diśā prakīrṇakṣetre phalam svadhiyā abhyūhyam | tat yathā ã
body.translated_text: Similarly, the area should be verified for isosceles, equilateral, and scalene quadrilaterals. For a circular figure, the semi-diameter is the breadth and the semi-circumference is the length — that itself is the rectangular figure. In this manner, for miscellaneous figures...

children.text: mukham ekādaśa dṛṣṭam pratimukham api ucyate tathā ca nava |
children.translated_text: The face is seen as eleven, and the counter-face is likewise stated as nine;

children.text: āyāmaḥ viṃśatikaḥ phalam asya kiyat bhavet gaṇaka || 3 ||
children.translated_text: the length is twenty — what would be the area of this, O mathematician? // 3 //

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Notation:

body.text: parilekhaḥ 24
body.translated_text: Diagram 24

body.text: karaṇam ã "prasādhya pārśve phalam tadabhyāsaḥ" iti viṣamayoḥ pārśvayoḥ yogaḥ 20, asya ardham 10. [ āyāmaḥ 20 ]. ete daśakaviṃśatike pārśve | etayoḥ abhyāsaḥ kṣetraphalam [ 200 ] |
body.translated_text: Computation: 'Having refined the sides, the area is their product' — the sum of the two unequal sides is 20; its half is 10. [Length = 20.] These are the sides of ten and twenty. Their product is the area [= 200].

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: aṣṭāṣṭau paṇavamukhe vyāsaḥ dvau ṣoḍaśa ucyate dairghyam |
children.translated_text: Eight and eight are the two mouths of the drum-shape (<s>paṇava</s>); the diameter is two; the length is stated as sixteen;

children.text: kiyat asya phalam vācyam paṇavākṛtisaṃsthitasya asya || 4 ||
children.translated_text: the area of this drum-shaped figure is to be stated. // 4 //

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Notation:

body.text: parilekhaḥ 25
body.translated_text: Diagram 25

body.text: karaṇam ã mukhayoḥ samāsaḥ 16, ardham 8. etat vistāreṇa 2 yuktam 10. asya ardham 5. evam "prasādhya pārśve phalam tadabhyāsaḥ" iti āgatam phalam 80 |
body.translated_text: Computation: The sum of the two faces = 16; half = 8. This added to the breadth 2 = 10; its half = 5. Thus, 'having refined the sides, the area is their product' — the area obtained = 80.

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: vistāraḥ pañca uktaḥ navodaram pṛṣṭham asya pañcadaśa |
children.translated_text: The breadth is stated as five, the belly (<s>udara</s>) is nine, the back (<s>pṛṣṭha</s>) of this is fifteen;
the area of the tusk-shaped (<s>karidanta</s>) figure — of what measure is it to be stated? // 5 //

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Notation:

body.text: parilekhaḥ 26
body.translated_text: Diagram 26

body.text: karaṇam ã pṛṣṭhodarasamāsaḥ 24. ardham 12. etat vistārārdhaguṇam phalam triṃśat 30 |
body.translated_text: Computation: The sum of the back and belly = 24. Half = 12. This multiplied by half the breadth gives the area = thirty, 30.

body.text: evam sarvakṣetreṣu pārśvadvayaparikalpanayā phalam nirdeṣṭavyam |
body.translated_text: Thus, in all [plane] figures, the result is to be stated by imagining two sides.

body.text: vyāsārdhatulyajyā
body.translated_text: The chord equal to the semi-diameter

body.text: samavṛttaviṣkambhārdhatulyajyāpradarśanārtham āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of showing the chord equal to the semi-diameter of a circle, he says:

body.text: paridheḥ ṣaḍbhāgajyā viṣkambhārdhena sā tulyā || 9 ||
body.translated_text: The chord of one-sixth of the circumference is equal to the semi-diameter. // 9 //

body.text:
paridhiḥ pariṇāhaḥ vṛttam iti paryāyāḥ | tasya paridheḥ ṣaḍbhāgasya yā jyā sā viṣkambhārdhena tulyā | paridheḥ ṣaḍbhāgaḥ rāśidvayam | rāśidvayakṣetrāvagāhinī yā jyā sā paridheḥ ṣaḍbhāgasya jyā | tasyāḥ ardham rāśeḥ ekasya ardhajyā | etat ca sarvam chedyake pratipādanīyam iti | asmin ca viracitamukhadeśasitavartyaṅkurakarkaṭena ālikhite chedyake yat ṣaḍbhāgajyāyāḥ ardham tat rāśeḥ ardhajyā | tayā ardhajyayā nirjñātāyāḥ ardhajyakotpattim vakṣyati
| etām eva ṣaḍbhāgajyām pratipādayiṣatā vṛtakṣetre ṣaṭ samatryaśrikṣetrāṇi prasaṅgena pradarśitāni | atra viṣkambhārdhabāhūni | ṣaṭ vā dhanuḥkṣetrāṇi viṣkambhārdhajyākāni | evam ca ṣaḍaśrikṣetram | prayojanam ca asya ṣaḍbhāgajyāpradarśanasya "samavṛttaparidhipādam chindyāt" [ gaṇitaí, 11 ] iti asyām kārikāyām vakṣyati || 9 ||
body.translated_text: <s>Paridhi</s> (circumference), <s>pariṇāha</s> (perimeter), and <s>vṛtta</s> (circle) are synonyms. The chord of one-sixth of that circumference is equal to the semi-diameter. One-sixth of the circumference is two signs (<s>rāśi</s>). The chord that spans the region of two signs is the chord of one-sixth of the circumference. Half of that is the half-chord (<s>ardhajyā</s>) of one sign. And all this is to be demonstrated on a figure drawn [on a board]. And in a figure drawn on this [board], with a compass whose pointed wick-sprout is whitened at the tip, the half of the chord of one-sixth is the half-chord of one sign. The derivation of the half-chords from this known half-chord he will state [later]. By presenting this very chord-of-one-sixth, six equilateral triangles within a circular figure have been incidentally demonstrated. Here, their sides equal the semi-diameter. Or, six bow-shaped figures with semi-diameter-chords [are demonstrated]. And thus a hexagonal figure. And the purpose of this demonstration of the chord-of-one-sixth is what he will state in the verse '<s>samavṛttaparidhipādam chindyāt</s>' (one should cut a quarter of the circumference of a circle) [<s>Gaṇita</s>, 11]. // 9 //

body.text: vṛtte vyāsaparidhisambandhaḥ
body.translated_text: The relation of diameter and circumference in a circle

body.text: trairāśikena samavṛttānayanārtham āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of finding [the circumference of] a circle by the rule of three, he says:

children.text: caturadhikam śatam aṣṭaguṇam dvāṣaṣṭiḥ tathā sahasrāṇām |
children.translated_text: One hundred plus four, multiplied by eight, plus sixty-two thousand —
this is the approximate circumference of a circle whose diameter is twenty thousand. // 10 //

body.text:
caturbhiḥ adhikam caturadhikam | kim tat ? śatam | aṣṭābhiḥ guṇitam aṣṭaguṇam | etat uktam bhavati ã aṣṭau śatāni dvātriṃśaduttarāṇi iti | sahasrāṇi ca dvāṣaṣṭiḥ | etat ubhayam ekatra 62832 | ayutadvayam ca viṣkambhaḥ ca ayutadvayaviṣkambhaḥ | athavā ayutadvayasaṅkhyaḥ viṣkambhaḥ ayutadvayapramāṇaḥ vā ayutadvayaviṣkambhaḥ | tasya ayutadvayaviṣkambhasya | sa ca 20000 | āsannaḥ vikaṭaḥ | kasya āsannaḥ ? sūkṣmasya pariṇāhasya | katham vijñāyate
sūkṣmasya āsannaḥ iti, na punar vyāvahārikasya āsannaḥ ; yāvatā śrutaparikalpanā sūkṣmavyāvahārikayāyoḥ tulyā | na eṣaḥ doṣaḥ, sandehamātram idam | sarvasandeheṣu vedam avatiṣṭhate "vyākhyānataḥ viśeṣapratipattiḥ [ nahi sandehāt alakṣaṇam ]" [ aṣṭādhyāyī, śivasūtram 6, pātañjalabhāṣyam ] iti | tasmāt sūkṣmasya āsannaḥ iti vyākhyāsyāmaḥ | athavā āsannaśabdena tatsamīpavartinā abhidhīyate | tena ca tat eva āsannaśabdena ucyate | tarhi kiñcit bhinnam | yadi
vyāvahārikāsannaḥ vyāvahārikāt api pāpīyān paridhiḥ, na kaścit pāpataram prayāsam karoti, tena sūkṣmāsannaḥ iti nyāyasiddham | atha āsannaparidhiḥ kasmāt ucyate, na punar sphuṭaparidhiḥ eva ucyate ? evam manyante ã sa upāyaḥ eva na asti yena sūkṣmaparidhiḥ ānīyate | nanu ca ayam asti ã
body.translated_text: Increased by four means <s>caturadhika</s>. Of what? Of a hundred. Multiplied by eight means <s>aṣṭaguṇa</s>. What is being said is: eight hundred and thirty-two. And sixty-two thousand. Both of these together: 62,832. <s>Ayutadvaya</s> (two <s>ayutas</s>) and <s>viṣkambha</s> (diameter) — <s>ayutadvayaviṣkambha</s>. Or: whose diameter is of the measure of two <s>ayutas</s> — <s>ayutadvayaviṣkambha</s>. Of that circle whose diameter is two <s>ayutas</s>. And that is 20,000. <s>Āsanna</s> means approximate. Approximate to what? To the exact circumference. How is it known that it is approximate to the exact [value], and not approximate to the practical [value] — since the verbal construction is the same for [being approximate to] the exact and the practical? This is no fault — it is merely a doubt. In all doubts, this [principle] holds: 'From the commentary, the specific understanding [is obtained]; for surely a doubt does not [constitute] a lack of definition' [<s>Aṣṭādhyāyī</s>, <s>Śivasūtra</s> 6, <s>Patañjali</s>'s <s>Bhāṣya</s>]. Therefore we shall interpret it as 'approximate to the exact [value].' Or, the word '<s>āsanna</s>' denotes what is close to that [exact value]. And by it, that very [thing close to the exact] is denoted. Then it is slightly different [from the exact]. If it were approximate to the practical value — [meaning] a circumference even worse than the practical — no one makes an effort worse than worst. Therefore, it is established by logic that [it is] approximate to the exact [value]. Now, why is the approximate circumference stated, rather than the exact circumference itself? They think thus: The very method by which the exact circumference can be obtained does not exist. But is there not this [method]:

body.text: vikkhaṃbhavaggadasaguṇakaraṇī vaṭṭassa parirao hodi |
body.translated_text: The square root of ten times the square of the diameter is the circumference of the circle.

body.text: viṣkambhavargadaśaguṇakaraṇī vṛttasya pariṇāhaḥ bhavati |
body.translated_text: The square root of ten times the square of the diameter is the circumference of the circle.

body.text: iti | atra api kevalaḥ eva āgamaḥ na eva upapattiḥ | rūpaviṣkambhasya daśakaraṇyaḥ paridhiḥ iti | atha manyate pratyakṣeṇa eva pramīyamāṇaḥ rūpaviṣkambhakṣetrasya paridhiḥ daśakaraṇyaḥ iti | na etat, aparibhāṣitapramāṇatvāt karaṇīnām | ekatrivistārāyām āyatacaturaśrakṣetrakarṇena daśakaraṇikena eva tadviṣkambhaparidhiḥ veṣṭyamāṇaḥ sa tatpramāṇaḥ bhavati iti cet tat api sādhyam eva |
body.translated_text: Here too, it is merely a tradition (<s>āgama</s>), not a proof (<s>upapatti</s>) — [namely] that the circumference of a circle with unit diameter is √10. Now if one thinks that, measured by direct perception itself, the circumference of a circle with unit diameter is √10 — that is not so, because the measures of surds are undefined. If [one says] that the circumference, when wrapped around a diagonal of a rectangle with sides one and three — which is exactly √10 — becomes equal to that measure, even that is something that requires proof.

body.text: anyat ca ã vṛttakṣetre catvāri dhanuḥkṣetrāṇi, ekam āyatacaturaśrakṣetram | teṣām phalasamāsena vṛttakṣetraphalena bhavitavyam | tāni phalāni saṃyojyamānāni na vṛttakṣetraphalatulyāni bhavanti |

śarārdha [1] yutiḥ 6, svaguṇā 36, daśasaṅguṇāḥ 360, etā karaṇyaḥ pṛṣṭham | sakalajyāvargaḥ catvāri śatāni, pṛṣṭham karaṇīnām ṣaṣṭiśatatrayam iti, katham etat saṃghaṭate | jyāyasā jyātaḥ pṛṣṭhena bhavitavyam | tat etat vicāryamāṇam atyantasūkṣmavādinām jyātaḥ pṛṣṭham alpīyamānam āpatitam ataḥ asyai avicāritamanoharāyai namaḥ astu daśakaraṇyai |
body.translated_text: By '<s>ogāhūṇam vikkhambham</s>' (diameter minus the penetration), the chord obtained is twenty [20]. [With this chord,] the arc computation: a quarter of the chord is [20/4 =] 5, plus half the arrow [1] gives 6, self-multiplied gives 36, multiplied by ten gives 360 — these are the surds [forming] the arc. The square of the full chord is four hundred, and the arc is three hundred and sixty surds — how does this work out? The arc must be greater than the chord. But when this is examined, for those who assert extreme precision, the arc turns out to be smaller than the chord. Therefore, salutations to this alluring-without-examination √10!

atha etau mahāntau rāśī kasmāt ucyete, na punar apavartitau eva ucyete; ācāryaḥ ca lāghavikaḥ, na tasya lāghavikasya mahārāśyabhidhānam yujyate | idam ekam ācāryasya mṛśyatām | athavā ayutadvayaviṣkambham iti alpaiḥ akṣaraiḥ ucyate | na tathā apavartitaviṣkambhābhidhāne alpākṣaratā | athavā manyate ã mahāparidhiviṣkambhābhidhāne mahāviṣkambhāsu jyāsu alpaparigrahāpacayeṣu na phalaviśeṣaḥ alpāntaratvāt iti, tathā ca "makhi" ādiṣu kvacit
asataḥ upādānam kṛtam, kvacit ca sataḥ parityāgaḥ |
body.translated_text: Now, why are these large numbers stated rather than the reduced [simplified] numbers? The <s>ācārya</s> (master) favors brevity; it is not appropriate for the brevity-seeking [master] to state large numbers. Let this one [peculiarity] of the master be tolerated. Or, '<s>ayutadvayaviṣkambham</s>' (a diameter of twenty thousand) is expressed in few syllables. Not so is the brevity of syllables in stating a reduced diameter. Or, he thinks: In stating large circumference and diameter values, with large diameters, the chords — in [their] small fractional remainders — show no difference in the result because of the smallness of the remainder. And accordingly, in the '<s>makhi</s>' [table of sine-differences] and the like, somewhere a non-existent [value] has been adopted, and somewhere an existent [value] has been discarded.

body.text: pariṇāhaḥ paridhiḥ, vṛttam kṣetram, vṛttasya pariṇāhaḥ vṛttapariṇāhaḥ, vṛttaparidhiḥ iti arthaḥ | anena viṣkambhe nirjñāte paridhiḥ ānīyate, paridhau ca nirjñāte viṣkambhe iti | katham ? yadi asya viṣkambhasya ayam paridhiḥ icchāviṣkambhasya kiyān, yadi asya paridheḥ ayam viṣkambhaḥ icchāparidheḥ kiyān iti |
body.translated_text: <s>Pariṇāha</s> is the circumference (<s>paridhi</s>); <s>vṛtta</s> is the [circular] figure; the circumference of the circle is '<s>vṛttapariṇāha</s>' — meaning the circumference of the circular figure. By this, when the diameter is known, the circumference is obtained, and when the circumference is known, the diameter [is obtained]. How? 'If this diameter has this circumference, what is [the circumference of] a desired diameter?' 'If this circumference has this diameter, what is [the diameter of] a desired circumference?'

children.translated_text: Now, for the purpose of finding chords, he says:

children.text: samavṛttaparidhipādam chindyāt tribhujāt caturbhujāt ca eva |
children.translated_text: One should cut a quarter of the circumference of a circle — from a triangle and from a quadrilateral indeed;
the half-chords of equal arcs, as many as desired, within the semi-diameter. // 11 //

body.text:
samavṛttam paridhiḥ yasya kṣetrasya tatkṣetram samavṛttaparidhiḥ, tasya pādaḥ samavṛttaparidhipādaḥ | sati etasmin vyākhyāne kṣetraphalasya grahaṇam prāpnoti | ācāryaprabhākareṇa ayam eva vigrahaḥ pradarśitaḥ | sa guruḥ iti kṛtvā asmābhiḥ na upālabhyate | anyat ca ã kāṣṭhatulyajyābhidhānam yuktam iti aśāstrajñaḥ api jānāti iti tena eva kāṣṭhatulyajyā pratyākhyātā | vayam tu brūmaḥ ã asti kāṣṭhatulyajyā iti | yadi kāṣṭhatulyajyā na syāt tadā samāyāmavanau
vyavasthānam eva ayoguḍasya na syāt | tena anumīmahe kaścit pradeśaḥ saḥ asti iti yena asau ayoguḍaḥ samāyāmavanau avatiṣṭhate | sa ca pradeśaḥ paridheḥ ṣaṇṇavatyaṃśaḥ | kāṣṭhatulyajyā anyaiḥ api ācāryaiḥ abhyavagatā ã
body.translated_text: A circle (<s>samavṛtta</s>) whose circumference is [uniform] — that figure is the '<s>samavṛttaparidhi</s>'; its quarter is the '<s>samavṛttaparidhipāda</s>.' With this interpretation, the grasping of [only] the area of the figure follows. The teacher <s>Prabhākara</s> has shown this very analysis. Since he is the teacher, we do not fault him. Moreover, even a non-expert in <s>śāstra</s> knows that the statement of a chord equal to an arc-segment is appropriate — and by that very [reasoning], a chord equal to the arc-segment has been rejected. But we say: there is a chord equal to the arc-segment. For if there were no chord equal to the arc-segment, then an iron ball would not remain in equilibrium on a level surface at all. From that we infer that there is some point where that iron ball rests on a level surface. And that point is one ninety-sixth part of the circumference. The chord equal to the arc-segment has been recognized by other teachers too:

body.text: tatparidheḥ śatabhāgam spṛśati dharām golakaśarīrāt |
body.translated_text: It touches the earth from the body of the sphere [by] a hundredth part of that circumference.

body.text:
iti | samavṛttaḥ ayam paridhiḥ samavṛttaparidhiḥ, samavṛttaparidheḥ pādaḥ samavṛttaparidhipādaḥ, tam samavṛttaparidhipādam chindyāt | jyāvibhāgena iti vākyaśeṣaḥ | jyāvibhāgena samavṛttaparidhau khaṇḍyamāne tribhujāt caturbhujāt ca kṣetrāt samacāpajyārdhāni niṣpadyante, na viṣamacāpajyārdhāni | tāni viśiṣṭāni eva parigṛhyante, dvicaturaṣṭaṣoḍaśadvātriṃśat iti ādīni dviguṇottarāṇi | "tu"-śabdāt dvicatuṣṣaḍaṣṭadaśadvādaśacaturdaśādīni ca | viṣkambhārdhe
tribhujakṣetram utpadyate | tasmāt tribhujāt caturbhujāt ca kṣetrajyārdhāni niṣpadyante |
body.translated_text: Thus. This circle [itself] is the circumference: <s>samavṛttaparidhi</s>; the quarter of the circumference of a circle: <s>samavṛttaparidhipāda</s>. One should cut that quarter of the circumference of a circle — by the division of chords, this is the completion of the sentence. When the quarter of the circumference is being divided by chord-division, from a triangular and from a quadrilateral figure, half-chords of equal arcs are produced — not half-chords of unequal arcs. Those specifically chosen ones are taken: two, four, eight, sixteen, thirty-two, and so on — doubling successively. From the word '<s>tu</s>' (but/indeed), also two, four, six, eight, ten, twelve, fourteen, and so on. Within the semi-diameter, a triangular figure is produced. From that triangle and from a quadrilateral, the figure-half-chords are derived.

body.text:
katham punar viṣkambhārdhe tribhujam ca caturbhujakṣetram utpadyate iti ucyate ã yasya vyāsārdham bhujā karṇaḥ vā bhavati tadvyāsārdhe niṣpannam | athavā viṣkambhārdhe eva jyārdhāni niṣpadyante | viṣkambhārdhāvayavatvāt na viṣkambhārdham atiricya vartante iti arthaḥ | athavā viṣkambhārdhe sati jyārdhāni niṣpadyante | nirjñāte hi viṣkambhārdhe śakyate jyā kalpayitum, na anyathā | katham ? yasmāt uktam "paridheḥ ṣaḍbhāgajyā viṣkambhārdhena
sā tulyā" [ gaṇitaí, 9 ] iti | yathā iṣṭāni yathā īpsitāni, samacāpajyārdhāni |
body.translated_text: But how does a triangle and a quadrilateral figure arise within the radius (<s>viṣkambhārdha</s>)? It is said: that whose arm or hypotenuse is the radius — [such a figure] is produced within the radius. Alternatively, it is within the radius itself that the half-chords (<s>jyārdhāni</s>) are produced. Since they are parts of the radius, they do not exceed the radius — this is the meaning. Alternatively, when the radius exists, the half-chords are produced. For when the radius is known, it is possible to construct a sine (<s>jyā</s>), not otherwise. How? Because it has been said: "The sine of one-sixth of the circumference is equal to the radius" [<s>Gaṇita</s>, 9]. 'As desired' means 'as wished' — the half-chords of equal arcs.

body.text: asyām kārikāyām jyotpattivistumātram eva pratipāditam ācāryeṇa, [ karaṇam ] tu na pratipāditam; pradeśāntaraprasiddhatvāt karaṇasya | athavā jyotpattau yat karaṇam tat sarvam chedyakaviṣayam, chedyakam ca vyākhyānagamyam iti [ na ] pratipāditam |
body.translated_text: In this verse, only the bare [method of] sine-generation (<s>jyotpatti</s>) has been taught by the <s>Ācārya</s>; but the [detailed] procedure has not been taught, because the procedure is well-known elsewhere. Alternatively, the entire procedure for sine-generation is a matter of geometric construction (<s>chedyaka</s>), and geometric construction is to be understood from the commentary — therefore it has not been taught [explicitly].

body.text: atha kim artham samavṛttaparidhipādaḥ eva jyāvibhāgena chidyate, na punar samavṛttaparidhiḥ chedyate ? na eṣaḥ doṣaḥ | samavṛttaparidhipādapramāṇamātram trayaḥ rāśayaḥ | evam caturṣu caturbhāgeṣu | yasmāt paridhipādapramāṇasya tulyatvāt sarveṣām paridhipādānām jyārdhāni tulyāni bhavanti iti paridhipādajyārdhe iti eva pratipāditāni vyavahāraprasiddhyartham |
body.translated_text: Now, why is only one quarter of the circumference of a circle divided by sine-segments, rather than the entire circumference? This is no defect. The measure of one quarter of the circumference of a circle is three signs (<s>rāśi</s>). Thus, in the four quadrants. Since all the quadrant-arcs are of equal measure, the half-chords of all the quadrants are equal — therefore, only the half-chords of one quadrant have been presented, for the purpose of establishing practical usage.

body.translated_text: In a radius whose number is fire-fire-product-fire [= 3438], how many half-chords of half-sign arcs (<s>rāśyardha-kāṣṭhāni</s>) are produced?

karaṇam ã yāvat tāvat pramāṇaparicchinnaviṣkambhārdhatulyena karkaṭakena maṇḍalam ālikhya tat dvādaśadhā vibhajet | te ca dvādaśabhāgāḥ rāśayaḥ iti parikalpyāḥ | atha dvādaśadhā vibhakte maṇḍale pūrveṇa rāśidvayāgrāvagāhinīm dakṣiṇottarām jyākārām lekhām kuryāt | evam paścimabhāge api | evam eva dakṣiṇottarabhāgayoḥ api ca pūrvāparāyatām jyām kuryāt | punar api ca pūrvāparadakṣiṇottaradikṣu tathā eva ca rāśicatuṣṭayāgrāvagāhinyaḥ
lekhāḥ kuryāt | tathā tryaśrī[ṇi] kartavyāni |
body.translated_text: Procedure: Draw a circle with a compass of measure equal to whatever desired radius, and divide it into twelve [parts]. Those twelve parts are to be conceived as signs (<s>rāśi</s>). Then, in the circle divided into twelve, on the eastern side, draw a chord-like line running north-south that penetrates [the circle] at the end of two signs. Similarly on the western side. Similarly also on the northern and southern sides, draw a chord extending east-west. Furthermore, in the eastern, western, southern, and northern directions, draw lines penetrating [the circle] at the end of four signs in the same manner. Likewise, triangles should be constructed.

body.text: tathā ca paridhiniṣpannam kṣetram karkaṭakena viracitavartikāmukhena likhyate | evam ālikhite kṣetre sarvam pradarśayitavyam |
body.translated_text: Similarly, the figure produced on the circumference is drawn with a compass whose mouth is turned outward. When the figure is thus drawn, everything should be demonstrated.

body.text: parilekhaḥ 29
body.translated_text: Diagram 29

body.text:
atra ālekhye vyāsārdhatulyā caturṇām kāṣṭhānām [pūrṇa]jyā | tadardham dvikāṣṭhajyā | sā ca 1719 | eṣā bhujā, vyāsārdham karṇaḥ iti, bhujākarṇavargaviśeṣasya mūlam avalambakaḥ | sā eva caturṇām kāṣṭhānām jyā | sā ca 2978 | etām vyāsārdhāt viśodhya śeṣam dvikāṣṭhaśaraḥ, śaradvikāṣṭhajyāvargayogamūlam karṇaḥ | sā eva dvikāṣṭha[pūrṇa]jyā ca 1780 | ardham asyāḥ kāṣṭhasya ekasya jyā, 890 | eṣā bhujā, vyāsārdham karṇaḥ | bhujākarṇavargaviśeṣasya
mūlam avalambakaḥ | sa ca pañcānām kāṣṭhānām jyā | sā ca 3321, viṣamatvāt ataḥ jyā na utpadyante | evam tribhujāt pañca jyārdhāni vyākhyātāni |
body.translated_text: Here in this diagram, the full chord (<s>pūrṇajyā</s>) of four arcs (<s>kāṣṭhas</s>) is equal to the radius. Its half is the sine of two arcs, and that is 1719. This is the arm (<s>bhujā</s>), the radius is the hypotenuse (<s>karṇa</s>); the square root of the difference of the squares of the arm and hypotenuse is the perpendicular (<s>avalambaka</s>). That itself is the sine of four arcs, and that is 2978. Subtracting this from the radius, the remainder is the arrow (<s>śara</s>) of two arcs. The square root of the sum of the squares of the arrow and the two-arc sine is the hypotenuse. That itself is the full chord of two arcs, and it is 1780. Half of this is the sine of one arc, 890. This is the arm, the radius is the hypotenuse. The square root of the difference of the squares of the arm and hypotenuse is the perpendicular. It is the sine of five arcs, and that is 3321. Due to asymmetry, no further sines are produced from this. Thus, five half-chord sines have been derived from the triangle.

body.text: antaḥsamacaturaśrakṣetre vyāsārdhatulyā bāhavaḥ | tasya karṇaḥ vyāsārdhayoḥ vargayogamūlam | tat ca 4862 | asya ardham trayāṇām kāṣṭhānām jyā | sā ca 2431 | evam ekā jyā caturbhujāt niṣpannā, viṣamatvāt utpattiḥ na asti |
body.translated_text: In the inscribed square figure, the sides are equal to the radius. Its diagonal is the square root of the sum of the squares of the two radii. That is 4862. Half of it is the sine of three arcs, and that is 2431. Thus, one sine has been produced from the quadrilateral; due to asymmetry, no further production is possible.

body.text:
viṣkambhārdhe ṣaṭ rāśyardhakāṣṭhajyārdhāni pratipāditāni | tasmin eva viṣkambhārdhe rāśicaturbhāgakāṣṭhajyā vyākhyāsyāmaḥ | tat yathā ã pūrvavat ālikhite kṣetre vyāsārdham eva aṣṭānām kāṣṭhānām [pūrṇa]jyā | tadardham caturṇām kāṣṭhānām jyā, sā ca 1719 | iyam bhujā, vyāsārdham karṇaḥ, bhujākarṇavargaviśeṣamūlam koṭiḥ | sā aṣṭānām kāṣṭhānām jyā, sā ca 2978 | etām vyāsārdhāt viśodhya śeṣam catuḥkāṣṭhajyāśaraḥ |
śaracatuṣkāṣṭhajyāvargayogamūlam karṇaḥ | sā caturṇām kāṣṭhānām [pūrṇa]jyā, sā ca 1780 | taddalam dvikāṣṭhajyā, [sā] ca 890 | eṣā bhujā, vyāsārdham karṇaḥ, bhujākarṇavargaviśeṣamūlam koṭiḥ | sā daśānām kāṣṭhānām jyā, sā ca 3321 | etām vyāsārdhāt viśodhya śeṣam dvikāṣṭhaśaraḥ | śaradvikāṣṭhajyāvargayogamūlam karṇaḥ | sā eva dvikāṣṭha[pūrṇa]jyā, sā ca 898 | ardham asyāḥ kāṣṭhasya ekasya jyā, sā ca 449 | eṣā bhujā, vyāsāṛdham karṇaḥ, bhujākarṇavargaviśeṣasya
mūlam koṭiḥ | sā ekādaśānām kāṣṭhānām jyā, sā ca 3409 | viṣamatvāt ataḥ jyā na utpadyate |
body.translated_text: Six half-chord sines of half-sign arcs have been presented within the radius. Within that same radius, we shall explain the sines of quarter-sign arcs. That is as follows: In a figure drawn as before, the radius itself is the full chord of eight arcs. Its half is the sine of four arcs, and that is 1719. This is the arm, the radius is the hypotenuse; the square root of the difference of the squares of the arm and hypotenuse is the cosine (<s>koṭi</s>). It is the sine of eight arcs, and that is 2978. Subtracting this from the radius, the remainder is the arrow of four arcs. The square root of the sum of the squares of the arrow and the four-arc sine is the hypotenuse. It is the full chord of four arcs, and that is 1780. Half of it is the two-arc sine, and it is 890. This is the arm, the radius is the hypotenuse; the square root of the difference of the squares of the arm and hypotenuse is the cosine. It is the sine of ten arcs, and that is 3321. Subtracting this from the radius, the remainder is the two-arc arrow. The square root of the sum of the squares of the arrow and the two-arc sine is the hypotenuse. It is the full chord of two arcs, and that is 898. Half of this is the sine of one arc, and that is 449. This is the arm, the radius is the hypotenuse; the square root of the difference of the squares of the arm and hypotenuse is the cosine. It is the sine of eleven arcs, and that is 3409. Due to asymmetry, no further sine is produced from this.

body.text: atha dvikāṣṭhajyām vyāsārdhāt viśodhya śeṣam daśakāṣṭhaśaraḥ | śaradaśakāṣṭhajyāvargayogamūlam karṇaḥ | sa [eva] kāṣṭhānām daśānām [pūrṇa] jyā, sā ca 4186 | ardham asyāḥ pañcānām kāṣṭhānām jyā, sā ca 2093 | eṣā bhujā, vyāsārdham karṇaḥ, bhujākarṇavargaviśeṣasya mūlam koṭiḥ | sā saptānām kāṣṭhānām jyā, sā ca 2728 | viṣamatvāt ataḥ jyā na utpadyate | evam tribhujāt nava jyārdhāni |
body.translated_text: Now, subtract the two-arc sine from the radius. The remainder is the arrow of ten arcs. The square root of the sum of the squares of the arrow and the ten-arc sine is the hypotenuse. It is the full chord of ten arcs, and that is 4186. Half of this is the sine of five arcs, and that is 2093. This is the arm, the radius is the hypotenuse; the square root of the difference of the squares of the arm and hypotenuse is the cosine. It is the sine of seven arcs, and that is 2728. Due to asymmetry, no further sine is produced from this. Thus, nine half-chord sines [are derived] from the triangle.

body.text:
pūrvavaduktasamacaturaśrakṣetrasya vyāsārdhabāhukasya vyāsārdhayoḥ vargayogamūlam karṇaḥ | sa ca dvādaśānām kāṣṭhānām [pūrṇa]jyā, sā ca 4862 | ardham asyāḥ ṣaṇṇām kāṣṭhānām jyā, sā ca 2431 | etām vyāsārdhāt viśodhya śeṣam ṣaṭkāṣṭhaśaraḥ, śaraṣaṭkāṣṭhajyāvargayogamūlam karṇaḥ | sa eva ṣaṇṇām kāṣṭhānām [pūrṇa]jyā, sā ca 2630 | ardham asyāḥ trayāṇām kāṣṭhānām jyā, sā ca 1315 | eṣā bhujā, vyāsārdham karṇaḥ, bhujākarṇavargaviśeṣasya
mūlam koṭiḥ | sā navānām kāṣṭhānām jyā | sā ca 3177 | viṣamatvāt ataḥ jyā na utpadyate | evam caturbhujāt tisraḥ jyāḥ | viṣkambhārdhe dvādaśa |
body.translated_text: The diagonal of the inscribed square figure with sides equal to the radius, as stated before, is the square root of the sum of the squares of the two radii. That is the full chord of twelve arcs, and it is 4862. Half of this is the sine of six arcs, and that is 2431. Subtracting this from the radius, the remainder is the six-arc arrow. The square root of the sum of the squares of the arrow and the six-arc sine is the hypotenuse. It is the full chord of six arcs, and that is 2630. Half of this is the sine of three arcs, and that is 1315. This is the arm, the radius is the hypotenuse; the square root of the difference of the squares of the arm and hypotenuse is the cosine. It is the sine of nine arcs, and that is 3177. Due to asymmetry, no further sine is produced from this. Thus, three sines from the quadrilateral. Twelve [sines total] within the radius.

body.text:
dvādaśa rāśicaturbhāgakāṣṭhajyārdhāni vyākhyātāni | tasmin eva viṣkambhārdhe rāśyaṣṭabhāgajyā vakṣyāmaḥ | tat yathā ã pūrvavadālikhite kṣetre vyāsārdham eva ṣoḍaśānām kāṣṭhānām [pūrṇa]jyā | tadardham aṣṭānām kāṣṭhānām jyā, sā ca 1719 | eṣā bhujā, vyāsārdham karṇaḥ, bhujākarṇavargaviśeṣasya mūlam koṭiḥ | sā ṣoḍaśānām kāṣṭhānām jyā, sā ca 2978 | etām vyāsārdhāt viśodhayet | śeṣam aṣṭakāṣṭhaśaraḥ | śarāṣṭakāṣṭhajyāvargayogamūlam
karṇaḥ | sa eva aṣṭānām kāṣṭhānām [pūrṇa]jyā, sā ca 1780 | ardham asyāḥ caturṇām kāṣṭhānām jyā, sā ca 890 | eṣā bhujā, vyāsārdham karṇaḥ, bhujākarṇavargaviśeṣasya mūlam koṭiḥ | sā eva viṃśateḥ kāṣṭhānām jyā, sā ca 3321 | etām vyāsārdhāt viśodhya śeṣam catuḥkāṣṭhaśaraḥ | śaracatuṣkāṣṭhajyāvargayogamūlam karṇaḥ | sa eva caturṇām kāṣṭhānām [pūrṇa]jyā, sā ca 898 | ardham asyāḥ kāṣṭhayoḥ jyā, sā ca 449 | eṣā bhujā, vyāsārdham karṇaḥ, bhujākarṇavargaviśeṣasya

body.translated_text: Twelve quarter-sign arc sines have been explained. Within that same radius, we shall state the sines of eighth-of-a-sign arcs. That is as follows: In a figure drawn as before, the radius itself is the full chord of sixteen arcs. Its half is the sine of eight arcs, and that is 1719. This is the arm, the radius is the hypotenuse; the square root of the difference of the squares of the arm and hypotenuse is the cosine. It is the sine of sixteen arcs, and that is 2978. This should be subtracted from the radius. The remainder is the eight-arc arrow. The square root of the sum of the squares of the arrow and the eight-arc sine is the hypotenuse. It is the full chord of eight arcs, and that is 1780. Half of this is the sine of four arcs, and that is 890. This is the arm, the radius is the hypotenuse; the square root of the difference of the squares of the arm and hypotenuse is the cosine. It is the sine of twenty arcs, and that is 3321. Subtracting this from the radius, the remainder is the four-arc arrow. The square root of the sum of the squares of the arrow and the four-arc sine is the hypotenuse. It is the full chord of four arcs, and that is 898. Half of this is the two-arc sine, and it is 449. This is the arm, the radius is the hypotenuse; the square root of the difference of the squares of the arm and hypotenuse is the cosine. It is the sine of twenty-two arcs, and that is 3409. This should be subtracted from the radius. The remainder is the two-arc arrow. The square root of the sum of the squares of the arrow and the two-arc sine is the hypotenuse. It is the full chord of two arcs, and that is 450. Half of this is the sine of one arc, and that is 225. This is the arm, the radius is the hypotenuse; the square root of the difference of the squares of the arm and hypotenuse is the cosine. It is the sine of twenty-three arcs, and that is 3431. Due to asymmetry, no further sine is produced from this.

atha caturṇām kāṣṭhānām jyām vyāsārdhāt viśodhayet | śeṣam viṃśateḥ kāṣṭhānām śaraḥ | śaraviṃśatikāṣṭhajyāvargayogamūlam karṇaḥ | sa viṃśateḥ kāṣṭhānām [pūrṇa]jyā, sā ca 4186 | ardham asyāḥ daśānām kāṣṭhānām jyā, sā ca 2093 | eṣā bhujā, vyāsārdham karṇaḥ, bhujākarṇavargaviśeṣasya mūlam koṭiḥ, sā eva caturdaśānām kāṣṭhānām jyā, sā ca 2728 | etām vyāsārdhāt viśodhayet | śeṣam daśakāṣṭhānām śaraḥ | śaradaśakāṣṭhajyāvargayogamūlam
karṇaḥ | sa eva daśānām kāṣṭhānām [pūrṇa]jyā, sā ca 2210 | ardham asyāḥ pañcānām kāṣṭhānām jyā, sā ca 1105 | eṣā bhujā, vyāsārdham karṇaḥ, bhujākarṇavargaviśeṣamūlam koṭiḥ | sā eva ekonaviṃśateḥ kāṣṭhānām jyā, sā ca 3256 | viṣamatvāt ataḥ jyā na utpadyate |

The square root of the sum of the squares of the arrow and the twenty-arc sine is the hypotenuse. It is the full chord of twenty arcs, and that is 4186. Half of this is the sine of ten arcs, and that is 2093. This is the arm, the radius is the hypotenuse; the square root of the difference of the squares of the arm and hypotenuse is the cosine. The square root of the sum of the squares of the arrow and the ten-arc sine is the hypotenuse. It is the full chord of ten arcs, and that is 2210. Half of this is the sine of five arcs, and that is 1105. This is the arm, the radius is the hypotenuse; the square root of the difference of the squares of the arm and hypotenuse is the cosine.
