evam tribhujāt rāśyaṣṭabhāgakāṣṭhajyāḥ vyākhyātāḥ | atha caturbhujāt vyākhyāsyāmaḥ | antaḥsamacaturaśrakṣetrasya vyāsārdhatulyāḥ bāhavaḥ | tayoḥ vargayogamūlam karṇaḥ | sa eva caturviṃśateḥ kāṣṭhānām [pūrṇa]jyā, sā ca 4862 | ardham asyāḥ dvādaśānām kāṣṭhānām jyā, sā ca 2431 | etām vyāsārdhāt viśodhayet | śeṣam dvādaśānām kāṣṭhānām śaraḥ | śaradvādaśakāṣṭhajyāvargayogamūlam karṇaḥ | sa eva dvādaśānām kāṣṭhānām [pūrṇa]jyā,
sā ca 2630 | ardham asyāḥ ṣaṇṇām kāṣṭhānām jyā, sā ca 1315 | eṣā bhujā, vyāsārdham karṇaḥ, bhujākarṇavargaviśeṣasya mūlam koṭiḥ | sā aṣṭādaśānām kāṣṭhānām jyā, sā ca 3177 | etām vyāsārdhāt viśodhayet | śeṣam ṣaṇṇām kāṣṭhānām śaraḥ | śaraṣaṭkāṣṭhajyāvargayogamūlam karṇaḥ | sa eva ṣaṇṇām kāṣṭhānām [pūrṇa]jyā, sā ca 1342 | ardham asyāḥ trayāṇām kāṣṭhānām jyā, sā ca 671 | eṣā bhujā, vyāsārdham karṇaḥ, bhujākarṇavargaviśeṣasya mūlam koṭiḥ,
sā eva ekaviṃśateḥ kāṣṭhānām jyā, sā ca 3372 | viṣamatvāt ataḥ jyā na utpadyate |
body.translated_text: Thus, the <s>jyās</s> (sine values) for the sign-eighth-degree arcs have been explained from the triangle. Now we shall explain from the quadrilateral. The sides of the inner square inscribed [in the circle] are equal to the semi-diameter. The square root of the sum of their squares is the diagonal. That diagonal itself is the four...

body.text: atha ṣaṇṇām kāṣṭhānām jyām vyāsārdhāt viśodhayet | śeṣam aṣṭādaśakāṣṭhānām śaraḥ | śarāṣṭādaśakāṣṭhajyāvargayogamūlam karṇaḥ | sa eva aṣṭādaśānām kāṣṭhānām [pūrṇa]jyā, sā ca 3820 | ardham asyāḥ navānām kāṣṭhānām jyā, sā ca 1910 | eṣā bhujā, vyāsārdham karṇaḥ, bhujākarṇavargaviśeṣamūlam koṭiḥ | sā eva pañcadaśānām kāṣṭhānām jyā, sā ca 2859 | viṣamatvāt ataḥ jyā na utpadyate |
body.translated_text: Now, one should subtract the <s>jyā</s> of six arcs from the semi-diameter. The remainder is the versine (<s>śara</s>) of eighteen arcs. The square root of the sum of the squares of the versine and the <s>jyā</s> of eighteen arcs is the diagonal. That diagonal itself is the full <s>jyā</s> of eighteen arcs, which is 3820...

body.text: evam rāśyaṣṭabhāgakāṣṭhajyāḥ caturvimśatiḥ | anena eva vidhānena viṣkambhārdhe yatheṣṭāni jyārdhāni niṣpādayitavyāni iti || 11 ||
body.translated_text: Thus, the twenty-four <s>jyā</s> values for the sign-eighth-degree arcs [are obtained]. By this very procedure, any desired half-<s>jyā</s> values in the semi-diameter are to be derived. // 11 //

body.text: prakārāntareṇa khaṇḍajyā
body.translated_text: Sine differences by another method

body.text: jyāvibhāgapradarśanārtham āha ã
body.translated_text: In order to show the division of <s>jyās</s> (sines), he says:

children.text: prathamāt cāpajyārdhāt yaiḥ ūnam khaṇḍitam dvitīyārdham |
children.translated_text: From the first half-chord of the arc, that by which the second half is diminished as a segment,
by those respective portions of the first half-chord, the remaining [segments] are diminished. // 12 //

body.text:
prathamāt ādyāt cāpajyārdhāt | yaiḥ ūnam yāvadbhiḥ aṃśaiḥ ūnam aprāptasadṛśam | kim tat ? khaṇḍitam dvitīyārdham, khaṇḍitam pūrvāryābhihitacchedyakavidhinā chinnam dvitīyacāpajyārdham | tatprathamajyārdhāṃśaiḥ | tat iti yāvadbhiḥ prathamacāpajyārdhāt dvitīyacāpajyārdham ūnam tāvantaḥ taiḥ parigṛhyante, jyāyāḥ ardham jyārdham, prathamam ca tajjyārdham ca prathamajyārdham ; athavā prathamā ca asau jyā ca prathamajyā, prathamajyā
ca asau ardham ca prathamajyārdham ; prathamajyārdhasya aṃśaḥ prathamajyārdhāṃśaḥ ; prathamajyārdhāṃśaḥ ca prathamajyārdhena bhāgam hṛtvā labdhā yathā pañcāṃśaḥ ṣaḍaṃśaḥ, te ca prathamajyārdhāṃśāḥ ca tatprathamajyārdhāṃśāḥ taiḥ tatprathamajyārdhāṃśaiḥ | taiḥ taiḥ aṃśaiḥ iti vīpsāgrahaṇam ca arthavat bhavati | ūnāni śeṣāṇi | ūnāni rahitāni, śeṣāṇi tṛtīyādi jyārdhāni bhavanti |
body.translated_text: 'From the first' — from the initial half-chord of the arc. 'By which it is diminished' — by however many parts it falls short [of being] equal. What is that? 'The segmented second half' — the second half-chord of the arc, segmented, i.e., cut by the method of cutting stated in the previous <s>āryā</s>...

body.text:
tat yathā ã prathamam cāpajyārdham idam chedyakena niṣpannam 225 | dvitīyam cāpajyārdhacchedam 224 | etat prathamacāpajyārdhāt ekena ūnam | dvitīyacāpajyārdhāṃśam prathamacāpajyārdham ca ekatra 449 | asya prathamacāpajyārdhena bhāge [hṛte] labdham ardhādhikena dve rūpe | tābhyām pūrveṇa ca [ekena ūnam] prathamacāpajyārdham [tṛtīyajyārdham] bhavati | tat ca 222 | trayāṇām saṃyogaḥ 671 | asya prathamacāpajyārdhena bhāgalabdham ardhādhikena
trīṇi rūpāṇi | taiḥ pūrvalabdhaiḥ ca tribhiḥ ūnam prathamacāpajyārdham caturthajyārdham bhavati | tat ca 219 | caturṇām jyārdhānām saṃyogaḥ 890 | asya prathamajyārdhena bhāgalabdham catvāri rūpāṇi ardhādhikena | taiḥ pūrvaiḥ ca ṣaḍbhiḥ ūnam prathamam cāpajyārdham pañcamajyārdham bhavati | tat ca 215 | etaiḥ śeṣāṇi vyākhyātāni iti |
body.translated_text: That is as follows: The first half-chord of the arc, produced by the cutting method, is 225. The second half-chord segment is 224. This is less than the first half-chord by one. The portion of the second half-chord relative to the first half-chord...

body.text:
idam ca vyākhyānam ācāryaprabhākareṇa vyākhyātam | tat ca ayuktam anarthakam apratyākhyāya vyākhyānam kartum | katham anarthakam ? atra gaṇitaśāstre laghūpāyapradarśanārtham upāyāntarapradarśanārtham vā sūtrāntaram ārabhyate | atra anyataragandhaḥ api na asti | katham ? pūrvāryābhihitachedyakavidhinā nirjñātābhyām prathamadvitīyacāpajyārdhābhyām idam karma kriyate | tasmin dvisūtrāyatatvāt karmaṇaḥ lāghavam na asti | upāyāntaratā
ca [na] pūrvasūtrāśrayatvāta |
body.translated_text: And this commentary was explained by the teacher <s>Prabhākara</s>. But it is improper to compose a commentary without refuting [what is] purposeless. How is it purposeless? In this mathematical science, methods are shown for the purpose of demonstrating simpler procedures...

body.text: etasmāt na arthaḥ anena sūtreṇa | katham punar imāḥ jyāḥ pṛthak pṛthak vijñāyante ? atibāliśavākyam etat | tajjyotpatteḥ | kāṣṭhadvikāṣṭhatrikāṣṭhādijyārdhāni pratipāditāni | teṣām anyonyaviśeṣeṇa pṛthak pṛthak jyāḥ bhavanti iti agaṇitajñaḥ api ca jānāti, kim punar sāṃvatsaraḥ | tathā ca mandabuddhipratipattyartham prastīryate | tat yathā ã
body.translated_text: Therefore, there is no purpose served by this <s>sūtra</s>. How then are these <s>jyās</s> known individually? This is a most naive statement. [They are known] from the generation of those <s>jyās</s>. The half-chords of one arc, two arcs, three arcs, and so forth have been demonstrated. From those...

body.text: anantarānantararahitāḥ krameṇa pṛthak pṛthak jyāḥ ã
body.translated_text: Subtracted successively from each subsequent [value], the individual <s>jyās</s> in order:

body.text: etāḥ eva utkrameṇa antyāt ārabhya utkramajyāḥ || 12 ||
body.translated_text: These same, in reverse order starting from the last, are the versed sines (<s>utkramajyā</s>). // 12 //

body.text: vṛttādisiddhiḥ
body.translated_text: Construction of circles and other figures

body.text: vṛttādisiddhim diṅmātrapradarśanārtham āha ã
body.translated_text: He states [the following] to show the direction for the construction of circles and such:

children.text: vṛttam bhrameṇa sādhyam tribhujam ca caturbhujam ca karṇābhyām |
children.translated_text: A circle is to be constructed by rotation; and a triangle and a quadrilateral by [their] diagonals;

children.text: sādhyā jalena samabhūḥ adhaḥ ūrdhvam lambakena eva || 13 ||
children.translated_text: a level surface is to be established by water; and vertical and horizontal [lines] by a plumb-line alone. // 13 //

body.text: vṛttam kṣetram bhrameṇa sādhyate | bhramaśabdena karkaṭakaḥ parigṛhyate | tena karkaṭena samavṛttam kṣetram parilekhapramāṇena parimīyate | tribhujam ca caturbhujam ca karṇābhyām | tribhujam kṣetram caturbhujam ca kṣetram karṇābhyām prasādhyate | tribhuja tāvat samāyāmavanau sūtram prasārya rekhām kuryāt | sā ca ã
body.translated_text: A circular figure is constructed by rotation. By the word 'rotation' (<s>bhrama</s>), a compass (<s>karkaṭaka</s>) is meant. By that compass, a circular figure is measured according to the size of the diagram. 'A triangle and a quadrilateral by diagonals'...

body.text:
ãããããããããããããããã
parilekhaḥ 30
body.translated_text: Diagram 30

body.text: atra ubhayāgravyavasthitena karkaṭakena matsyam utpādayet | etadvaktrapucchaniṣkrāntāparasūtram avalambakaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, with a compass placed at both ends, one should produce a fish-figure (<s>matsya</s>). The line emerging through the mouth and tail of this [fish-figure] is the altitude (<s>avalambaka</s>).

body.text: parilekhaḥ 31
body.translated_text: Diagram 31

body.text: asya agre sūtrasya ekam agram nidhāya dvitīyāgram bhūmyagre niścalam nidhāya rekhām kuryāt | dvitīyāgre api tathā eva | evam te karṇasūtre | tābhyām karṇasūtrābhyām prasādhitam tribhujam ã
body.translated_text: Placing one end of this upper line and fixing the second end at the base-point immovably, one should draw a line. At the second end also, similarly. Thus, those are the diagonal-lines. The triangle constructed by those two diagonal-lines...

body.text: parilekhaḥ 32
body.translated_text: Diagram 32

body.text: caturbhuje iṣṭacaturbhuja[karṇa]tulyam sūtram tiryak prasārayet | tat ca sūtram ã
body.translated_text: In the case of a quadrilateral, one should extend a cord equal to the desired [diagonal of the] quadrilateral transversely. And that cord:

body.text: parilekhaḥ 33
body.translated_text: Diagram 33

body.text: dvitīyam ca etat madhyajanitasvastikam tiryak eva prasāryate | tathā ca karṇasūtre
body.translated_text: And this second [cord], generating a cross at the center, is extended transversely as well. And thus the diagonal-cords:

body.text: parikekhaḥ 34
body.translated_text: Diagram 34

body.text: etayoḥ pārśvāni pūritāni, caturaśrakṣetram niṣpannam |
body.translated_text: The sides of these [diagonals] being filled in, the quadrilateral figure is completed.

body.text: parilekhaḥ 35
body.translated_text: Diagram 35

body.text:
sādhyā jalena samabhūḥ | samabhūḥ jalena sādhyate | tat yathā ã cakṣuḥsūtrasamīkṛtāyāmavanau trikāṣṭhopari nirvāte jalakumbham nidhāya adhaḥ suṣiram kuryāt, yathā tat udakam ekarūpayā dhārayā sravati | tat prasrutam ambhaḥ samantāt parivartulam yatra prayāti sā bhūḥ samā, yatra tat ambhaḥ vṛttam bhaṅktvā pratiṣṭhate tat nimnam, yatra na avagāhate tat unnatam iti | adhaḥ ūrdhvam lambakena eva | adhaḥ upalakṣitasya yaḥ ūrdhvapradeśaḥ saḥ
avalambakena eva sādhyate | ūrdhvapradeśasya vā yaḥ adhaḥpradeśaḥ asau api avalambakena eva | avalambakaḥ ca gurudravyaikāgrāsaktam sūtram iti || 13 ||
body.translated_text: A level surface is to be established by water. The level surface is constructed using water. Namely: On ground that has been leveled by eye and cord, placing a water-pot on a tripod in a windless [place], one should make a hole below, so that the water [flows] uniformly...

body.text: svavṛttaviṣkambhārdham
body.translated_text: The semi-diameter of one's own circle

body.text: svavṛttaviṣkambhārdhānayanārtham āha ã
body.translated_text: In order to find the semi-diameter of one's own circle (<s>svavṛtta</s>), he says:

children.translated_text: Having computed the square of the measure of the gnomon (<s>śaṅku</s>), combined with the square of the shadow (<s>chāyā</s>),
the square root of that is the semi-diameter of its own circle. // 14 //

body.text: śaṅkoḥ ākāraprakāravivecanam
body.translated_text: Discussion of the shape and manner of the gnomon

body.text:
atra śaṅkoḥ ākārapramāṇayoḥ vipravadante sāṃvatsarāḥ | kecit tāvat āhuḥ ã dvādaśāṅgulaśaṅkuḥ mūlatribhāge caturaśraḥ, madhyatribhāge tryaśriḥ, uparitribhāge śūlākāraḥ iti | sūkṣmatvāt vigrahasya sūkṣmayā ekayā koṭyā chāyāgrasya sulakṣyatvāt śeṣaiḥ ca duḥsampādatvāt iti tat ca na | śūlāgrasya avalambakasya vinyāsābhāvāt ṛjutā eva duḥsampādyā | tadabhāvāt sarvaguṇābhāvaḥ | gopucchākṛtivṛttodaraḥ tu bhraṣṭāvalambakatvena eva pratyākhyātā
|
body.translated_text: Here, the astronomers (<s>sāṃvatsara</s>) disagree regarding the shape and measure of the gnomon. Some say: A twelve-<s>aṅgula</s> gnomon — square in the bottom third, triangular in the middle third, and spike-shaped in the upper third. From the point of precision...

body.text:
apare āhuḥ ã caturaśraḥ caturdiśam avalambakasādhanasambhavāt koṭidvayena chāyāgrahaṇāt abhīṣṭakoṭyām diggrahaṇasiddhiḥ iti | etat api yujyate, kintu tādṛśasya samprati śilpinaḥ samacaturaśrakṣetrasampādinaḥ durlabhatvāt yadi api svabhyastavidyaḥ kaścit kadācit sambhavet, tathā api pratikṣaṇam sūryasya abhimukhasthāpanāt punar punar śaṅkoḥ mukhacālanam kartavyam | tathā ca atisūkṣmadṛśaḥ tāvatā abhīṣṭacchāyātikrāntā syāt iti doṣaḥ, etasmāt
parityājyaḥ ayam api śaṅkuḥ | anena eva sarvatra śaṅkavaḥ prayuktāḥ |
body.translated_text: Others say: It should be square, [since] from the four directions, the construction of the altitude is possible, and because the shadow is measured using two edges, the determination of direction for the desired edge is accomplished. This too is valid, but a craftsman of that kind at present...

body.text:
āryabhaṭīyāḥ svamatam abhininiṣṭhāpayiṣavaḥ vyāvarṇayanti | tat yathā ã praśastadārumayaḥ hi asuṣiraḥ rājigranthavraṇavarjitaḥ bhramasiddhaḥ mūlamadhyāgrāntarālatulyavṛttaḥ na alpavyāsaḥ na alpāyāmaḥ ca praśastaḥ | tribhiḥ caturbhiḥ vā avalambakaiḥ asya ṛjusthitiḥ sādhayitavyā | śaṅkoḥ madhyasūtrasya asiddhatvāt avalambakasthitiḥ api duḥsampādya iti ataḥ śaṅkumadhyasūtrasādhanam pradarśyate | tat yathā ã śaṅkumucce pradeśe niścalam nidhāya
avalambakena śaṅkumūlamastakayoḥ madhye vijñāya tadagrasaktam sūtram prasārya ubhayapārśve ca lekhe kuryāt | etat ubhayapārśvamadhyalekhe, tataḥ punar api karkaṭakena lohena mūlāgramadhyasūtrābhyām matsyam utpādya śeṣamadhyalekhāsādhanam | nanu ca atra api doṣaḥ asti eva, sarvadikṣu tanmastakasya chāyāgrasya vipulavṛttatvāt chāyāmadhyam durlakṣyam | tena ca vinā ādigrahaṇābhāvaḥ iti | na eṣaḥ doṣaḥ | śaṅkoḥ upari kendre viṣkambhārdhādhikānyā
samavṛttā śalākā madhyaprasādhinī lohī dārvī vā kriyate | tadā ādigrahaṇamadhyaparijñānam ca bhaviṣyati iti | athavā prājñasya avalambakasūtreṇa pūrvavinyastena eva kiñcit utkṣiptena madhyaparijñānam | atha aṅgulavibhāgāt tīkṣṇena śastreṇa manāk śakalitam kṛtam | anyathā hi pramāṇagrahaṇam anarthakam syāt | tasmāt yatheṣṭapramāṇaḥ śaṅkuḥ dvādaśāṅgulaḥ iti suprasiddham aṅgīkṛtya ucyate | uddeśakeṣu etat pratipādayiṣyāmaḥ | yāvat yāvat ayam pṛthuḥ
guruḥ ca bhavati tāvat tāvat vāyunā na eva cālyate, yāvat yāvat ca dīrghaḥ bhavati tāvat tāvat ca aṅgulāvayavāḥ sūkṣmāḥ suparijñātāḥ bhavanti | tasmāt pṛthugurudīrgheṣu ādaraḥ kāryaḥ iti abhihitaḥ śaṅkoḥ ākāraḥ |
body.translated_text: those who follow the <s>Āryabhaṭīya</s>, wishing to establish their own doctrine, explain [it] thus: A gnomon (<s>śaṅku</s>) made of excellent wood, not hollow, free from lines, knots, and scars, verified by turning [on a lathe], having a uniform circular cross-section at the base, middle, and tip, not of small diameter and not of small length — [such a gnomon] is commendable. Its upright position is to be established by three or four plumb-lines (<s>avalambaka</s>). Since the center-line of the gnomon is not [easily] established, even the perpendicular position is difficult to achieve — therefore the method of establishing the gnomon's center-line is demonstrated. As follows: Having placed the gnomon firmly on an elevated spot, determining the midpoint between the base and the top of the gnomon by means of a plumb-line, and stretching a thread attached to its tip, one should make marks on both sides. At these marks on both sides [and] the middle-mark, then again, by producing a fish-figure (<s>matsya</s>) using a compass or metal [tool] from the base-tip-center-threads, the remaining center-line is established. Now, there is a defect here too: because the shadow-tip is a broad circle [rather than a point] in all directions due to the tip of the gnomon, the middle of the shadow is hard to discern; and without that, there is no initial observation. This is no defect. On top of the gnomon, at the center, a rod (<s>śalākā</s>) — made of metal or wood — circular, with a diameter slightly more than the semi-diameter, and flat at the center, is attached. Then the initial observation and the determination of the center will be possible. Alternatively, for an intelligent person, the determination of the center [can be done] with the plumb-line thread previously set up, slightly lifted. Now, from the division into digits (<s>aṅgula</s>), a slight incision is made with a sharp instrument. For otherwise, the measurement-taking would be pointless. Therefore, having accepted that the gnomon is of whatever desired measure — conventionally twelve digits (<s>dvādaśāṅgula</s>) — [the exposition] proceeds. We shall demonstrate this in the example problems. The broader and heavier [the gnomon] is, the less it is disturbed by the wind; and the longer it is, the finer and more clearly discerned are the digit-subdivisions. Therefore, care should be taken with regard to the broad, heavy, and long [gnomon] — thus the form of the gnomon has been described.

body.text: śaṅkupramāṇavivecanam
body.translated_text: Discussion of the Measure of the Gnomon

body.text: idānīm pramāṇam upadekṣyāmaḥ | kecit āhuḥ ã ardhahastaḥ dvādaśadhā vibhaktaśarīraḥ iti | na eṣaḥ niyamaḥ | kintu abhīṣṭasaṅkhyāpravibhaktaśarīraḥ abhīṣṭasaṅkhyāpravibhaktaḥ iti arthaḥ | yatra pramāṇagrahaṇam kṛtam, tatra api samāṅgulavibhāge kendravibhāge ca kauśalam abhyasanīyam |
body.translated_text: Now we shall teach the measure. Some say: 'Half a <s>hasta</s> (cubit), its body divided into twelve [parts].' This is not a fixed rule. Rather, [it is] 'a body divided into a desired number of parts' — meaning [it is] divided into a desired number. Where the measurement has been made, there too, skill in equal-digit division and center-division should be practiced.

body.text: śloka-vyakhyā
body.translated_text: Explanation of the Verse

body.text:
śaṅkoḥ pramāṇavargam, śaṅkoḥ ittham prapañcatapramāṇasya pramāṇagrahaṇam aniyatapramāṇapratipādanārtham iti uktam | yadi śaṅkoḥ niyatam eva pramāṇam syāt tadā śaṅkoḥ vargam iti iyatā api ucyamāne tanniyatapramāṇaḥ eva pratipattiḥ | pramāṇasya vargaḥ pramāṇavargaḥ, tam pramāṇavargam | chāyāvargeṇa, chāyāyāḥ vargaḥ chāyāvargaḥ, tena chāyāvargeṇa | saṃyutam kṛtvā, ekīkṛtya iti arthaḥ | yat tasya vargamūlam, tasya saṃyuktasya rāśeḥ
vargamūlam yat, tat svavṛttaviṣkambhārdham bhavati | kim tat vṛttam yasya idam viṣkambhārdham iti ucyate ? tat mūlatulyena karkaṭakena ālikhitasya vṛttasya tat viṣkambhārdham | yadi evam sarve eva saṃkhyāviśeṣaḥ svavṛttaviṣkambhārdham bhavati | na eṣaḥ doṣaḥ | yadi sarvasaṅkhyāviśeṣaḥ svavṛttaviṣkambhārdham bhavati eva, kim naḥ chinnam ? atra punar śaṅkupramāṇacchāyāvargayogamūlam svaviṣkambhārdham viśiṣṭam eva parigṛhyate, tena anyasya
svavṛttaviṣkambhārdhasya grahaṇam na eva atra prasajyate | prasakte ca doṣaparihāraḥ vā vidhīyate | atra ca svavṛttaviṣkambhārdhagrahaṇam trairāśikaprasiddhyartham ã yadi asya svavṛttaviṣkambhārdhasya ete śaṅkucchāye tadā golaviṣkambhārdhasya ke iti śaṅkucchāye labhyete | tau eva viṣuvati avalambakākṣajye iti ucyate |
body.translated_text: 'The square of the measure of the gnomon' — the gnomon's measure, thus elaborately explained, has been said to be of indeterminate measure for the purpose of teaching a non-fixed measure. If the gnomon had a fixed measure, then even by saying just 'the square of the gnomon,' one would understand that fixed measure only. The square of the measure is the 'measure-square' (<s>pramāṇavarga</s>); that measure-square. 'With the shadow-square' — the square of the shadow is the 'shadow-square'; with that shadow-square. 'Having combined' — having unified, meaning having made into one. 'The square root of that' — the square root of that combined quantity — that becomes the semi-diameter of its own circle (<s>svavṛttaviṣkambhārdha</s>). What is that circle of which this is the semi-diameter? — it is asked. It is the semi-diameter of the circle drawn with a compass equal to that root. If so, then every number-particular would be the semi-diameter of its own circle. This is no defect. If indeed every number-particular is the semi-diameter of its own circle, what loss is ours? Here, however, the square-root of the sum of the gnomon-measure-square and the shadow-square is taken up as a specific semi-diameter of its own circle; therefore, the taking of any other semi-diameter of its own circle does not arise here at all. And even if it did arise, the removal of the defect would be prescribed. And here, the taking of the semi-diameter of its own circle is for the purpose of establishing the rule of three: if for this semi-diameter of its own circle, these are the gnomon and shadow, then for the semi-diameter of the [celestial] sphere, what are they? — thus the gnomon and shadow are obtained. Those same [values], at the equinox, are called the latitude-sine (<s>akṣajyā</s>) and the co-latitude-sine (<s>avalambaka</s>).

body.text: parilekhaḥ 36
body.translated_text: Figure 36

body.text:
svavṛttaviṣkambhārdham nāma chāyāgrāt ārabhya śaṅkumastakaprāpi sūtram | tatsūtrānusāreṇa bhūmau dṛṣṭim nidhāya śaṅkumastakāsaktam vivasvantam paśyati | akṣajyā ānayane trairāśikasthāpanā ã 13 | 5 | 3438 | labdham akṣajyā 1322 | eṣā bhujā, vyāsārdham karṇaḥ, bhujākarṇavargaviśeṣamūlam avalambakaḥ 3174 | trairāśikena api 13 | 12 | 2328 | labdham avalambakaḥ 3174 | apare api atra kṣetraviśeṣāḥ | trairāśike vācaḥ yuktiḥ ã yadi asya
svavṛttaviṣkambhārdhasya chāyātulyā bhujā śaṅkutulyaḥ avalambakaḥ tadā asya golavyāsārdhasya kau bhujau alambau iti | chāyayā ghaṭikānayane, madhyāhne chāyayā ca sūryānayane svavṛttaviṣkambhārdhasya ayam eva vidhiḥ | kintu chāyayā ghaṭikānayane śaṅkunā kāryam iti śaṅkuḥ eva ānīyate | samamaṇḍalachāyayā sūryānayane sa eva | madhyāhnacchāyayā sūryānayane natajyayā prayojanam iti chāyā eva ānīyate |
body.translated_text: The 'semi-diameter of its own circle' means the thread extending from the shadow-tip to the top of the gnomon. Placing the sight along that thread on the ground and looking [upward], one sees the Sun attached to the top of the gnomon. The setting up of the rule of three for deriving the latitude-sine: 13 | 5 | 3438 | The result obtained is the latitude-sine: 1322. This is the arm (<s>bhujā</s>); the semi-diameter is the hypotenuse; the square root of the difference of the squares of the arm and hypotenuse is the co-latitude-sine (<s>avalambaka</s>): 3174. Also by the rule of three: 13 | 12 | 3438 | The result: co-latitude-sine = 3174. There are also other field-specifics here. The verbal justification for the rule of three: If for this semi-diameter of its own circle, the shadow-equal is the arm and the gnomon-equal is the co-latitude, then for this semi-diameter of the [celestial] sphere, what are the arm and co-latitude? For deriving the <s>ghaṭikā</s> (time-unit) from the shadow, and for determining the Sun from the midday shadow, the procedure for the semi-diameter of its own circle is exactly this. But for deriving <s>ghaṭikās</s> from the shadow, the gnomon is what is needed — so the gnomon itself is derived. For determining the Sun from the co-meridian shadow, it is the same. For determining the Sun from the midday shadow, the declination-sine (<s>natajyā</s>) is needed — so the shadow itself is derived.

children.translated_text: how far from the meridian has the Sun, with extended rays, gone? State [this]. // 3 //

body.text:
nyāsaḥ ã śaṅkuḥ 30, chāyā 16 | āgatam svavṛttaviṣkambhārdham 34 | labdham tadakṣajyā 1618
|| 14 ||
body.translated_text: Setting down: Gnomon = 30, shadow = 16. The semi-diameter of its own circle obtained: 34. The latitude-sine obtained from it: 1618. // 14 //

body.text: pradīpacchāyākarma
body.translated_text: Lamp-Shadow Computation

body.text: pradīpacchāyākarma āha ã
body.translated_text: He states the lamp-shadow computation:

children.translated_text: The distance between the gnomon and the upright [lamp-post], multiplied by the gnomon, divided by the difference of the gnomon and the upright [lamp-post] —

children.text: yat labdham tā chāyā jñeyā śaṅkoḥ svamūlāt hi || 15 ||
children.translated_text: what is obtained, that is known to be the shadow of the gnomon from its own base. // 15 //

body.text: śaṅkuḥ guṇaḥ yasya tat śaṅkuguṇam | kim tat iti āha ã śaṅkubhujāvivaram | bhujāśabdena pradīpocchrāyaḥ ucyate, pradīpocchrāyasya śaṅkoḥ ca yat antarālam tat śaṅkubhujāvivaram, tat śaṅkuguṇam | śaṅkubhujayoḥ viśeṣahṛtam śaṅkoḥ pradīpocchrāyasya yaḥ viśeṣaḥ sa śaṅkubhujayoḥ viśeṣaḥ, tena hṛtam bhaktam | yat labdham sā chāyā śaṅkoḥ tasya eva svamūlāt tasya eva śaṅkoḥ mūlāt sā chāyā labhyate |
body.translated_text: 'Multiplied by the gnomon' (<s>śaṅkuguṇam</s>) — that which has the gnomon as multiplier. What is that? 'The distance between the gnomon and the upright' (<s>śaṅkubhujāvivaram</s>). By the word 'upright' (<s>bhujā</s>), the height of the lamp is meant; the interval between the lamp-height and the gnomon is the 'distance between the gnomon and the upright' — that, multiplied by the gnomon. 'Divided by the difference of the gnomon and the upright' — the difference between the gnomon and the lamp-height is the 'difference of the gnomon and the upright'; divided by that. 'What is obtained, that is the shadow' — the shadow of the gnomon; from 'its own base' — from the base of that very gnomon, the shadow is obtained.

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Example problem:

children.translated_text: From the base of a lamp-post, elevated to seventy-two, at a distance of eighty,
of a gnomon standing at a distance of thirty and twenty — state the two shadows. // 1 //

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Setting down:

body.text: parilekhaḥ 37
body.translated_text: Figure 37

body.text: śaṅkubhujāvivaram 80, etat śaṅkuguṇam 960; bhujā 72, śaṅkuḥ 12, etayoḥ viśeṣaḥ 60, anena hṛtam śaṅkuguṇam śaṅkubhujāvivaram, labdhā chāyā 16 |
body.translated_text: The distance between the gnomon and the upright = 80; this multiplied by the gnomon = 960. The upright (lamp) = 72, the gnomon = 12; their difference = 60. By this, dividing the gnomon-times-distance, the shadow obtained = 16.

body.text: dvitīyoddeśakanyāsaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Setting down for the second example:

body.text: parilekhaḥ 38
body.translated_text: Figure 38

13

  3 |
etat karma trairāśikam | katham ? śaṅkutaḥ adhikāyāḥ uparibhujāyāḥ yadi śaṅkubhujāntarālapramāṇam chāyā labhyate tadā śaṅkunā kā iti chāyā labhyate |
body.translated_text: By the previous procedure, the shadow obtained: 13 and 5/3. This computation is [based on] the rule of three. How? If from the upright that is greater than the gnomon, the shadow obtained is equal to the gnomon-upright interval, then from the gnomon, what shadow is obtained?

body.text: viparītakarmaṇā uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Example problem by the reverse operation:

children.translated_text: A shadow of sixteen is observed of a lamp elevated to seventy-two.

children.text: mūlam kiyatā śaṅkoḥ dvādaśakasya tvayā vācyam || 2 ||
children.translated_text: At what distance from the base of the gnomon of twelve — you must state [this]. // 2 //

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Setting down:

body.text: parilekhaḥ 39
body.translated_text: Figure 39

body.text: karaṇam ã śaṅkubhujāntareṇa anena 60 chāyā labdhā, tena "bhāgaharāḥ te bhavanti guṇakārāḥ" [gaṇitaí, 28 ] iti chāyā 16, guṇitā jātā 960; etat eva "śaṅkuguṇam śaṅkubhujāvivaram" atra api śaṅkuḥ guṇakāraḥ āsīt iti "guṇakārā bhāgaharā" [ gaṇita í, 28 ] iti śaṅkunā 12 hṛtam śaṅkubhujāvivaram labdham | tat ca 80 |
body.translated_text: Computation: From this gnomon-upright difference of 60, the shadow was obtained; therefore 'divisors become multipliers' [<s>Gaṇitapāda</s>, 28] — the shadow 16, multiplied, gives 960; this is itself 'the distance between the gnomon and the upright, multiplied by the gnomon.' Here too the gnomon was the multiplier — so 'multipliers become divisors' [<s>Gaṇitapāda</s>, 28] — dividing by the gnomon 12, the distance between the gnomon and the upright is obtained. And that is 80.

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Example problem:

children.translated_text: A gnomon situated at a distance of fifty from the base of a lamp-post;

children.text: tasya cchāyā paṅktiḥ vācyaḥ tasmin kiyān dīpaḥ || 3 ||
children.translated_text: its shadow is ten — state how tall the lamp is at that [post]. // 3 //

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Setting down:

body.text: parilekhaḥ 40
body.translated_text: Figure 40

body.text: karaṇam ã "śaṅkuguṇā koṭī sā chāyābhaktā bhujā bhavati" [gaṇitaí, 16 ] iti vakṣyamāṇakaraṇena śaṅkubhujāvivarayuktacchāyā koṭiḥ bhavati iti | śaṅkubhujāvivaram 50, chāyā 10, ekatra 60, etat śaṅkuguṇam 720, chāyābhaktam bhujāpramāṇam 72 || 15 ||
body.translated_text: Computation: 'The upright multiplied by the gnomon, that divided by the shadow, is the hypotenuse' [<s>Gaṇitapāda</s>, 16] — by the procedure to be stated, the shadow plus the gnomon-upright-distance becomes the base (<s>koṭi</s>). The gnomon-upright-distance = 50, the shadow = 10; together = 60. This multiplied by the gnomon = 720; divided by the shadow, the upright-measure = 72. // 15 //

body.text: śaṅkucchāyādvayena dīpocchrāyāpasārajñānam
body.translated_text: Determining Lamp-Height and Distance from Two Gnomon-Shadows

body.text: anirjñātadīpocchrāyāvasānayoḥ śaṅkucchāyādvayena ānayanam āha ã
body.translated_text: He states the derivation from two gnomon-shadows when the lamp-height and distance are unknown:

children.translated_text: The shadow-tip distance, multiplied by the shadow, divided by the difference — [gives] the base (<s>koṭi</s>);
the base multiplied by the gnomon, divided by the shadow, becomes the upright (<s>bhujā</s>). // 16 //

body.text:
chāyāguṇitam chāyayā guṇitam | kim chāyāguṇitam ? chāyāgravivaram, chāyāgrayoḥ vivaram chāyāgravivaram, chāyāgrāntarālabhūmiḥ iti arthaḥ | tat yathā ã anirjñātocchrāyayaṣṭipradīpāt kiyat api apasṛtya śaṅkuḥ sthāpitaḥ | tasya chāyā jñāyate eva | tacchāyāgrāt parigaṇite antare dvitīyaśaṅkuḥ, tacchāyāgrāt pūrvaśaṅkucchāyāgram iti antaram chāyāgravivaram | tadiṣṭayā prathamacchāyayā dvitīyacchāyayā vā guṇitam | ūnena bhājitam, ūnam chāyayoḥ
viśeṣaḥ, tena ūnena bhājitam | koṭī avasānabhūmiḥ | tat yadi prathamacchāyayā guṇitam tadā prathamacchāyāgrayaṣṭipradīpāntarālam bhavati, dvitīyayā chāyayā yadi tadagrayaṣṭipradīpāntarālam | śaṅkuguṇā koṭī, śaṅkuḥ guṇaḥ yasyāḥ sā iyam śaṅkuguṇā koṭī | chāyābhaktā bhujā bhavati, bhujā yaṣṭipradīpocchrāyaḥ | chāyādvayam api tatkoṭibhyām prasādhyate |
body.translated_text: 'Multiplied by the shadow' (<s>chāyāguṇitam</s>) — multiplied by the shadow. What is multiplied by the shadow? The shadow-tip distance (<s>chāyāgravivaram</s>) — the interval between the shadow-tips, meaning the ground-distance between the shadow-tips. As follows: From a lamp-post of unknown height, at some distance, a gnomon is placed. Its shadow is known. At a measured interval from that shadow-tip, a second gnomon [is placed]; [its shadow-tip] to the first gnomon's shadow-tip — that interval is the shadow-tip distance. That, multiplied by either the first or the second shadow. 'Divided by the difference' (<s>ūnena bhājitam</s>) — the 'less' is the difference of the two shadows; divided by that difference. [The result is] the base (<s>koṭi</s>), the ground-distance. If multiplied by the first shadow, then it gives the distance from the first shadow-tip to the lamp-post; if by the second shadow, then the distance from that [second] tip to the lamp-post. 'The base multiplied by the gnomon' — that base multiplied by the gnomon. 'Divided by the shadow becomes the upright' — the upright is the lamp-post height. Both shadows too are derived from their respective bases.

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Example problem:

children.text: śaṅkoḥ samayoḥ dṛṣṭe kramaśaḥ daśaṣoḍaśāṅgule chāye |
children.translated_text: Of two equal gnomons, shadows of ten and sixteen digits have been observed in order;

children.text: agrāntaram ca dṛṣṭam triṃśat koṭībhuje vācye || 1 ||
children.translated_text: and the tip-interval observed is thirty — the base and upright are to be stated. // 1 //

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Setting down:

body.text: parilekhaḥ 41
body.translated_text: Figure 41

body.text: karaṇam ã chāyāgravivaram 30, etat prathamacchāyāguṇitam 300; chāyayoḥ viśeṣaḥ 6, anena labdham koṭī 50; iyam eva koṭī śaṅkuguṇā jātā 600, chāyābhaktā bhujā 60 | dvitīyacchāyātaḥ api koṭī 80, bhujā sā eva 60 |
body.translated_text: Computation: The distance between shadow-tips is 30; this multiplied by the first shadow gives 300; the difference of the shadows is 6; dividing by this, the perpendicular (<s>koṭī</s>) is 50. This same perpendicular multiplied by the gnomon gives 600; divided by the shadow, the arm (<s>bhujā</s>) is 60. From the second shadow also, the perpendicular is 80 and the arm is the same, 60.

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Practice problem:

children.text: pañca sapta kramāt chāye narayoḥ tulyayoḥ smṛte |
children.translated_text: Five and seven are the two shadows of two equal persons, in order;

children.text: aṣṭau agrāntaram dṛṣṭam bhujakoṭī tadā ucyatām || 2 ||
children.translated_text: the distance between shadow-tips is observed as eight — then state the arm and perpendicular. (2)

body.translated_text: Setting down:

body.text: parilekhaḥ 42
body.translated_text: Diagram 42.

body.text: pūrvavat labdhā koṭī 20, bhujā 48 | dvitīyacchāyātaḥ api koṭī 28, bhujā sā eva 48 |
body.translated_text: As before, the perpendicular obtained is 20, the arm is 48. From the second shadow also, the perpendicular is 28, the arm is the same, 48.

body.text:
viṣuvat ahani gaganatala[madhya]vartini savitari samadakṣiṇottaradeśacchāyāgrāntarālayojanaiḥ chāyāviśeṣeṇa śaṅkunā [ca] kecit vivasvadavanitalāntarālayojanāni ānayanti, tat ayuktam | atra pradīpacchāyādvayakarmālāpāvatāraḥ api na upapadyate | kutaḥ ? yasmāt āha "bhūravivivaram vibhajet" [golaí, 39 ] iti | bhūḥ śaṅkuḥ, raviyojanakarṇaḥ śaṅkubhujāvivaram, sakalajagadekapradīpaḥ bhagavān bhāskaraḥ svayam eva pradīpocchrāyaḥ iti ataḥ
vivasvadavanitalāntarālayojanānayanam na ghaṭate, "bhūravivivaram" iti siddhānām eva yojanānām upadeśāt | atha savitā eva pradīpocchrāyaḥ iti savitṛviṣkambhapramāṇam ānīyate iti cet, tat ca na | yasmāt svakakṣyākarṇabhūvivarayojanaḥ gaganatalamadhyāsīnaḥ lokān dyotayan lakṣyate, tasmāt pradīpocchrāyaḥ svayam savitā [na] bhavitum arhati | atha vivasvān pradīpocchrāyaḥ, savitṛdharitrīmadhyāntarālayojanāni aśeṣāvanitalamaṇḍalavyāsapramāṇasya śaṅkoḥ
vivaram, tathā ca dvitīyasya tāvat śaṅkoḥ avasthānābhāvāt ca na yujyate | tasmāt suṣṭhu uktam "pradīpacchāyā[dvaya]karmālāpāvatāraḥ api na upapadyate " iti |
body.translated_text: On the equinoctial day, when the Sun is at the zenith, some [scholars] attempt to derive the distance in <s>yojanas</s> between the Sun and the surface of the earth by using the difference of shadows, the gnomon, and the <s>yojana</s>-distance between the tips of the shadows of equal gnomons placed due north and due south. That is improper. Here, even the approach through the two-shadow-lamp computation does not work. Why? Because he [<s>Āryabhaṭa</s>] says: 'one should divide the distance between the earth and the Sun' [<s>Gola</s>, 39]. The earth is the gnomon; the <s>yojana</s>-hypotenuse to the Sun is the distance between gnomon and arm; the blessed Sun, the single lamp of the entire world, is himself the lamp-height. Therefore, the derivation of the <s>yojana</s>-distance between the Sun and the earth's surface does not work, because [the rule] 'the distance between earth and Sun' teaches <s>yojanas</s> that are already established. Now, if the Sun himself is the lamp-height and thereby the Sun's diameter-measure is derived — that too does not work. Because the Sun, situated at his own orbital radius in <s>yojanas</s>, illuminating the worlds from the middle of the sky, is observed [as such]; therefore the Sun himself cannot serve as the lamp-height. Now, [if one says] the Sun is the lamp-height, and the <s>yojana</s>-distance between the Sun and the center of the earth is the separation of the gnomon whose measure equals the diameter of the entire earth-circle — even so, this does not work because there is no place for a second gnomon. Therefore, it is well said: 'even the approach through the two-shadow-lamp computation does not work.'

body.text:
iyam ca dharitrī golākārā paṭhyate | tena tatpṛṣṭhavartinām asmākam vakratvāt paridheḥ śaṅkucchāyā bhujakoṭikarmaparikalpanā atra [na] pravartate, yataḥ salilasamīkṛte pradeśe śaṅkucchāyayā bhujākoṭikarṇakṣetrasaṃsthānam, na ca etāvatyā bhuvaḥ śakyate samīkaraṇam kartum | atha abhyupagamya idam udāhriyate ã viṣuvatī ujjayinyām dinārdhavartinī uṣṇadīdhitau chāyā pañcāṅgulā | tayā akṣaḥ labdhaḥ bhāgāḥ dvāviṃśatiḥ liptāḥ saptatriṃśat
| anena akṣeṇa laṅkojjayinyantarālayojanāni labdhāni saptāmbarayamasaṅkhyāni 207 | tataḥ ujjayinyā uttareṇa viṣuvatī eva madhyāhnacchāyā sthāneśvare saptāṅgulā | tayā ca akṣaḥ labhdaḥ bhāgāḥ triṃśat sapādāḥ | anena akṣeṇa laṅkāsthāneśvarāntarālayojanāni labdhāni śarādriyamasaṅkhyāni 275 | atra eteṣām yojanānām viśeṣaḥ aṣṭaṣaṣṭiḥ śaṅkudvayavivaram, chāyayoḥ antareṇa dvābhyām yuktā aṣṭaṣaṣṭiḥ, chāyāgravivaram saptatiḥ | atra gaṇitakarma "chāyāguṇitam
chāyāgravivaram" iti ādikarmaṇā koṭiyojanāni labhyante | taiḥ ca dvitīyacchāyayā nīyamānaiḥ laṅkāsthāneśvarāntarālayojanaiḥ eva bhavitavyam , yasmāt tasmin kāle vivasvadadhovasthitaḥ deśaḥ laṅkā | yadi vivasvān bhujā yadi vā vivasvataḥ yaḥ ucchrāyaḥ, tasmāt koṭeḥ laṅkāsthāneśavarāntarālayojanasaṅkhyānatvāt gaṇitakarma api atra na krāmati | atra ca yayā koṭyā bhujā sādhyate sā ca tāvat na siddhā, tayā asiddhayā siddhabhujā sādhyate iti etat ayuktam | anyat
ca yat chāyā dvādaśāṅgulasya śaṅkoḥ pratyakṣam asmābhiḥ upalabdhā tayā āṅgulapramāṇayā yojanaiḥ karma kriyate iti etat ca na upapadyate | atha dvādaśayojanapramāṇasya śaṅkoḥ pañcayojanā saptayojanā ca chāyā iti etat api tāvataḥ śaṅkoḥ lambakena ṛjusthitiḥ aśakyā jñātum, na ca utkṣepaṇasthāpane | chāyā ca samāyāmavanau sādhyate tāvatsu yojaneṣu nimnonnatasarit iti ādiviṣamatā tena tadavagatiḥ na śakyate | tasmāt yathā āgamasiddhau eva sahasramarīceḥ
ucchrāyaviṣkambhau | tataḥ na atra iyam gaṇitaprakriyāprakāravāgurā prasāraṇīyā iti || 16 ||
body.translated_text: And this earth is taught to be spherical in shape. Therefore, for us who are on its surface, because of the curvature of the circumference, the gnomon-shadow arm-perpendicular computation does not apply here, since the arm-perpendicular-hypotenuse field-configuration from the gnomon-shadow [requires] a surface leveled with water, and it is not possible to level the earth to such an extent. Now, assuming [a level surface], this is illustrated: On the equinoctial day, at <s>Ujjayinī</s>, when the Sun is at mid-day, the shadow is five digits. From this, the latitude obtained is twenty-two degrees and thirty-seven minutes. From this latitude, the <s>yojana</s>-distance between <s>Laṅkā</s> and <s>Ujjayinī</s> is obtained as sky-<s>Yama</s>-seven in number, 207. Then, north of <s>Ujjayinī</s>, on the equinoctial day itself, the mid-day shadow at <s>Sthāneśvara</s> is seven digits. From this, the latitude obtained is thirty degrees and a quarter. From this latitude, the <s>yojana</s>-distance between <s>Laṅkā</s> and <s>Sthāneśvara</s> is obtained as arrow-mountain-<s>Yama</s> in number, 275. Here, the difference of these <s>yojanas</s> is sixty-eight — the separation between the two gnomons; the difference of the shadows is two, added to sixty-eight [gives] the distance between shadow-tips as seventy. Here the computation: 'the shadow-tip distance multiplied by the shadow' etc. — by this operation the perpendicular in <s>yojanas</s> is obtained. And that [perpendicular], when derived with the second shadow, should equal the <s>yojana</s>-distance between <s>Laṅkā</s> and <s>Sthāneśvara</s>, because at that time the place directly below the Sun is <s>Laṅkā</s>. Whether the Sun is the arm or the height of the Sun [is taken] — from that, because the perpendicular does not equal the <s>yojana</s>-number of the <s>Laṅkā</s>-<s>Sthāneśvara</s> distance, the mathematical operation does not proceed here either. And here, the perpendicular by which the arm is to be derived is itself not yet established; deriving the established arm from that unestablished [perpendicular] is improper. Furthermore, the shadow that we directly observe of a twelve-digit gnomon — using that digit-measure shadow to perform the computation with <s>yojanas</s> does not work. Now, if the shadow of a gnomon measuring twelve <s>yojanas</s> is five <s>yojanas</s> and seven <s>yojanas</s> — even this [is problematic], because the upright standing of a gnomon of that size by means of a plumb-line cannot be ascertained, nor [is it possible] by lifting and placing [it]. And the shadow is established on level ground — over that many <s>yojanas</s>, the unevenness of depressions, elevations, rivers, etc. [makes] its ascertainment impossible. Therefore, the height and diameter of the thousand-rayed [Sun] are established by tradition alone. Hence, the snare of this mathematical procedure should not be spread here. (16)

body.text: bhujakoṭikarṇānām sambandhaḥ
body.translated_text: The relationship among arm, perpendicular, and hypotenuse

body.text: karṇānayanārtham āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of deriving the hypotenuse, he says:

body.text: yaḥ ca eva bhujāvargaḥ koṭīvargaḥ ca karṇavargaḥ saḥ |
body.translated_text: The sum of the square of the arm and the square of the perpendicular is the square of the hypotenuse. (17 [first half])

body.text: yaḥ ca bhujāvargaḥ yaḥ ca koṭivargaḥ etau vargau ekatra karṇavargaḥ bhavati |
body.translated_text: The square of the arm and the square of the perpendicular — these two squares together constitute the square of the hypotenuse.

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Practice problem:

children.translated_text: For the arm and perpendicular of three and four, of six and eight, and of those two also;
and of twelve and nine — the hypotenuses are to be stated in order. (1)

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Setting down:

body.text: parilekhaḥ 43
body.translated_text: Diagram 43.

body.text: karaṇam ã ete bhujākoṭī 3, 4; etayoḥ vargau 9, 16; ekatra karṇavargaḥ 25, asya mūlam karṇaḥ 5 | evam adhyardhāśrikṣetre āyatacaturaśrakṣetre vā karṇaḥ yojyaḥ | evam pariśiṣṭakṣetrayoḥ karṇau labdhau 10, 15 ||
body.translated_text: Computation: These are the arm and perpendicular: 3, 4; their squares: 9, 16; together the square of the hypotenuse is 25; its root, the hypotenuse, is 5. Thus, the hypotenuse should be applied in a right triangle or a rectangular figure. Similarly, for the remaining two figures the hypotenuses obtained are 10 and 15.

body.text: vṛtte ardhajyāśarayoḥ sambandhaḥ
body.translated_text: The relationship between half-chord and arrow in a circle

body.text: vṛttakṣetrāvagāhajyānayanaāya āryāpaścārdham āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of deriving the chord from the penetration of a circular field, he states the latter half of the <s>āryā</s>:

body.text: vṛtte śarasaṃvargaḥ ardhajyāvargaḥ sa khalu dhanuṣoḥ || 17 ||
body.translated_text: In a circle, the product of the two arrows is the square of the half-chord; that is indeed [the half-chord] of those two arcs. (17)

body.text: vṛtte kṣetre, śarayoḥ saṃvargaḥ śarasaṃvargaḥ, saḥ ardhajyāvargaḥ bhavati | sa khalu dhanuṣoḥ, tayoḥ eva dhanuṣoḥ ardhajyāvargaḥ bhavati |
body.translated_text: In a circular field, the product of the two arrows is the 'arrow-product' (<s>śarasaṃvarga</s>); that equals the square of the half-chord. 'That is indeed of those two arcs' — of those very two arcs, that is the square of the half-chord.

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Practice problem:

children.text: kṣetre daśāviṣkambhe dvikāṣṭasaṅkhyau śarau mayā dṛṣṭau |
children.translated_text: In a field of diameter ten, the two arrows of two and eight are seen by me;

children.text: tatra eva navaikamitau ardhajye tu kramāt vācye || 1 ||
children.translated_text: and in the same [circle], those of nine and one — the half-chords are to be stated in order. (1)

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Setting down:

body.text: parilekhaḥ 44
body.translated_text: Diagram 44.

body.text: karaṇam ã etau dvau śarau 2, 8 | etayoḥ saṃvargaḥ ardhajyāvargaḥ 16 | asya mūlam 4, iyam ardhajyā | dvitīyoddeśake api labdhā ardhajyā 3 |
body.translated_text: Computation: These two arrows are 2 and 8. Their product is the square of the half-chord: 16. Its root is 4 — this is the half-chord. In the second problem also, the half-chord obtained is 3.

body.text: atra eva śyenamūṣikoddeśān vyāvarṇayanti | tat yathā ã ardhajyā bhujā, ardhajyāmaṇḍalakendrāntarālam koṭiḥ, tadvargayogamūlam karṇaḥ maṇḍalavyāsārdham | tat tu pradarśyate ã
body.translated_text: In this very [context], they illustrate the hawk-and-mouse problems. Namely: the half-chord is the arm, the distance between the half-chord and the center of the circle is the perpendicular, and the square root of the sum of their squares is the hypotenuse — [which equals] the semi-diameter. This is demonstrated:

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Setting down:

body.text: parilekhaḥ 45
body.translated_text: Diagram 45.

body.text:
iyam ardhajyā śyenasthānocchrāyaḥ, ardhajyāparidhyantarālam mūṣikapracārabhūmiḥ, viṣkambhārdham karṇaḥ śyenamārgaḥ | maṇḍalakendram mūṣikavadhapradeśaḥ | tatra śyenasthānocchrāyaḥ ardhajyā iti tadvargaḥ, mūṣikapracārabhūmiḥ śaraḥ iti tena vibhajyate, labdham dvitīyaḥ śaraḥ | tena "antarayuktam hīnam" [śloí 24 ] iti etam kṛtvā labdham mūṣikāvāsaprāpyabhūmiḥ śyena[gati]karṇapramāṇam ca | yaḥ eva dvitīyaḥ mahāśaraḥ sa eva vaṃśabhaṅgapade
ardhatryaśrikṣetrākāreṇa vyavasthitaḥ | tat ca pradarśitam | evam gaṇitam bījamātram upadiṣṭam |
body.translated_text: This half-chord is the height of the hawk's position; the distance between the half-chord and the circumference is the ground traversed by the mouse; the semi-diameter is the hypotenuse — the hawk's path. The center of the circle is the place where the mouse is killed. There, the height of the hawk's position is the half-chord, so its square [is computed]; the ground traversed by the mouse is the arrow, so [the square of the half-chord] is divided by it; the quotient is the second arrow. Then, by [the rule] 'the mean of the sum and difference' [verse 24], one obtains the distance to the mouse's den and the measure of the hawk's flight-path. The second large arrow itself, in the bamboo-breaking problem, is arranged in the form of a half-triangular field. This too is demonstrated. Thus, the mathematical [method] has been taught in seed-form only.

body.text: uddeśakaḥ
body.translated_text: Practice problem:

body.text: ã

dvādaśahastocchritasya prākārasya upari śyenaḥ vyavasthitaḥ | tena prākāramūlāt caturviṃśatihastaniṣkrāntaḥ mūṣikaḥ [dṛṣṭaḥ, tena] mūṣikena ca śyenaḥ | tatra mūṣikaḥ tadbhayāt prākārāvasthitam ātmīyālayam drutataram prasthitaḥ antare śyenena karṇagatinā vyāpāditaḥ | tatra icchāmaḥ jñātum [ki]yat antaram ākhunā prāptam, kiyat vā śyenena āyātam iti || 2 ||
body.translated_text: A hawk is situated atop a wall twelve <s>hastas</s> (cubits) high. A mouse has emerged twenty-four <s>hastas</s> from the base of the wall, [and is seen] by the hawk. The mouse, out of fear, hastened directly toward its own den at the base of the wall. [But] it was killed by the hawk, who traveled along the hypotenuse path, in between. There we wish to know: how much distance did the mouse cover, and how much did the hawk travel? (2)

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Setting down:

body.text: parilekhaḥ 46
body.translated_text: Diagram 46.

body.text: karaṇam ã śyenocchrāyavargaḥ 144, etat anena mūṣikapracārabhūmipramāṇena 24 vibhajya labdham 6, anena antareṇa mūṣikapracārabhūmiḥ yuktā 30, apacitā 18 | etayoḥ ardham śyenagatiḥ mūṣikāvāsāntarālam ca yathākrameṇa 15, 9.
body.translated_text: Computation: The square of the hawk's height is 144; dividing this by the mouse's ground-distance of 24, the result is 6. Adding this difference to the mouse's ground-distance gives 30; subtracting gives 18. Half of each gives, in order: the hawk's flight-distance and the distance to the mouse's den — 15 and 9.

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Practice problem:

children.text: aṣṭādaśakocchrāye śyenaḥ stambhe sthitaḥ hi ākhuḥ |
children.translated_text: A hawk is perched on a pillar eighteen [<s>hastas</s>] high; a mouse

children.text: āvāsāt niṣkrāntaḥ tu ekāśītyā bhayāt śrayenāt ||
children.translated_text: has come out eighty-one [<s>hastas</s>] from the den, out of fear of the hawk.

children.text: gacchan ālayadṛṣṭiḥ krūreṇa nipātitaḥ tataḥ mārge |
children.translated_text: Going [toward the den] with eyes on the den, it was struck down by the cruel [hawk] on the way;

children.text: kiyatā prāpnoti bilam śyenagatiḥ vā tadā vācyam || 3 ||
children.translated_text: how far did it reach the hole — or what was the hawk's flight? That is to be stated. (3)

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Setting down:

body.text: parilekhaḥ 47
body.translated_text: Diagram 47.

body.text:
labdham ākhoḥ āgatabhūmiḥ
8
1
2 ,
śyenagatiḥ
body.translated_text: The result: the ground covered by the mouse is 8 1/2;
the hawk's flight is 42 1/2.

body.text: anena eva prakāreṇa vaṃśabhaṅgoddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: By this very method, the bamboo-breaking problem:

children.translated_text: A bamboo eighteen [<s>hastas</s>] high was toppled by wind from its base;

children.text: ṣaḍgatvā asau patitaḥ tribhujam kṛtvā kva bhagnaḥ syāt || 4 ||
children.translated_text: having traveled six [<s>hastas</s> from the base], it fell making a triangle — where was it broken? (4)

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Setting down:

body.text: vaṃśaḥ 15, mūlāt yaḥ apasāraḥ tatpramāṇam ardhajyā 6, tasya vargaḥ 36, vaṃśapramāṇena anena 18 bhaktaḥ labdham 2, pūrvavat "antarayuktam hīnam dalitam" [ gaṇitaí 24 ] iti vaṃśaśakale 10, 8.
body.translated_text: Bamboo = 15 [sic, 18]; the distance from the base is the half-chord = 6; its square is 36; divided by the bamboo-measure 18, the result is 2. As before, by 'the mean of the sum and difference, halved' [<s>Gaṇita</s> 24], the two pieces of bamboo are 10 and 8.

body.text: parilekhaḥ 48
body.translated_text: Diagram 48.

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Practice problem:

children.text: ṣoḍaśahastaḥ vaṃśaḥ pavanena nipātitaḥ svamūlāt tat |
children.translated_text: A bamboo of sixteen <s>hastas</s> was toppled by wind from its own base;

children.text: aṣṭau gatvā patitaḥ kasmin bhagnaḥ marutvataḥ vācyaḥ || 5 ||
children.translated_text: having traveled eight [<s>hastas</s>], it fell — at what [point] was it broken? The wind's [effect] is to be stated. (5)

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Setting down:

body.text: parilekhaḥ 49
body.translated_text: Diagram 49.

body.text: labdhe vaṃśaśakale 10, 6.
body.translated_text: The two pieces of bamboo obtained: 10 and 6.

body.text: kamaloddeśakeṣu dṛśyakamalapramāṇam ekaḥ śaraḥ | kamalanimajjanabhūmiḥ ardhajyā | atra pūrvavat ardhajyāvarge śarahṛte mahāśaraḥ labhyate tatra dṛśyakamalasaṃkramaṇena jalapramāṇam kamalapramāṇam ca |
body.translated_text: In the lotus problems, the visible [portion of the] lotus is one arrow; the depth to which the lotus is submerged is the half-chord. Here, as before, when the square of the half-chord is divided by the arrow, the large arrow is obtained; then, by the operation with the visible lotus, the water-depth and lotus-length [are found].

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Practice problem:

children.text: kamalam jalāt pradṛśyam vikasitam aṣṭāṅgulam nivātena |
children.translated_text: A lotus visible above the water, blooming, eight digits [tall], by a windless [force]

children.text: nītam majjati haste śīghram kamalāmbhasī vācye || 6 ||
children.translated_text: is carried [and] quickly submerges at one <s>hasta</s> (cubit) — state the lotus[-length] and water[-depth]. (6)

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Setting down:

body.text: parilekhaḥ 50
body.translated_text: Diagram 50.

body.text: dṛśyakamalasya [pramāṇam] 8, nimajjanabhūmiḥ 24 |
body.translated_text: The visible lotus [measure] is 8; the submersion distance is 24.

body.text: karaṇam ã ardhajyāyāḥ caturviṃśateḥ vargaḥ 576, tat dṛśyakamalena aṣṭābhiḥ bhāgalabdham 72 | etat dṛśyakamalayuktam 80, vihīnam ca 64 | ete dalite kamalapramāṇam jalapramāṇam ca 40, 32 |
body.translated_text: Computation: The square of the half-chord (24) is 576; dividing this by the visible lotus (8), the quotient is 72. Adding the visible lotus to this gives 80; subtracting gives 64. These halved give the lotus-length and water-depth: 40 and 32.

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Practice problem:

children.text: aṅgulaṣaṭkam kamalam majjati hastadvayam gatam mūlāt |
children.translated_text: A lotus of six digits submerges two <s>hastas</s> [when carried] from the base;

children.text: icchāmi tatra boddhum paṅkajam ambhaḥpramāṇam ca || 7 ||
children.translated_text: I wish to know the lotus and the water-depth in that [pond]. (7)

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Setting down:

body.text: parilekhaḥ 51
body.translated_text: Diagram 51.

body.text: dṛśyam 6, nimajjanabhūmiḥ 48 | labdham pūrvavat paṅkajapramāṇam 195, ambhaḥ pramāṇam 189.
body.translated_text: Visible [portion] = 6, submersion distance = 48. As before, the lotus-length obtained is 195, water-depth is 189.

body.text: matsyabakoddeśakeṣu api evam eva āyatacaturaśrakṣetrasya ekaḥ bāhuḥ ardhajyā, bāhudvayam mahāśaraḥ, śeṣam mūṣikoddeśakavat karma |
body.translated_text: In the fish-and-crane problems too, similarly: one side of the rectangular field is the half-chord, [another] two sides [form] the large arrow; the remaining [computation] is like the mouse problem.

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Practice problem:

children.text: ṣaḍdvādaśikā vāpī tasyām pūrvottare sthitaḥ matsyaḥ |
children.translated_text: A pond [is] six by twelve; in its northeast [corner] a fish is situated;

children.text: vāyavye koṇe syāt bakaḥ sthitaḥ tadbhayāt tūrṇam ||
children.translated_text: a crane is stationed in the northwest corner. Out of fear of it, quickly,

children.text: bhitvā vāpīm matsyaḥ karṇena gataḥ diśam tataḥ yāmyām |
children.translated_text: the fish, cutting across the pond diagonally, went southward;

children.text: pārśvena āgatya hataḥ bakena vācyam tayoḥ yātam || 8 ||
children.translated_text: coming along the side, it was killed by the crane — state the distance traveled by each. (8)

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Setting down:

body.text: parilekhaḥ 52
body.translated_text: Diagram 52.

body.text:
bakamatsyakaraṇam ã vāpīpārśvam ardhajyā iti tasya vargaḥ 36, pārśvadvayam mahāśaraḥ iti jātam 18 | anena bhāgalabdham 2 | etena aṣṭādaśabhiḥ saṃkramaṇena labdham matsyabakagatipramāṇam vāpīpārśvaśeṣaḥ ca 10, 8 | pārśvaśeṣe pārśvapatite śeṣaḥ dakṣiṇāparakoṇaprāptiḥ matsyasya |
  uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: The crane-and-fish calculation: the side of the tank is the <s>ardhajyā</s> (half-chord), so its square is 36; twice the side is the <s>mahāśara</s> (great arrow), giving 18. By this, the quotient obtained is 2. With these eighteen, by the <s>saṃkramaṇa</s> (transition) operation, the measures of the distances traversed by the fish and the crane and the remainder of the tank-side are obtained as 10 and 8. When the remainder of the side falls on the side, the remainder gives the fish's arrival at the southwest corner. Example problem:

children.text: dvādaśadaśikā vāpī hi āgneyasthaḥ bakaḥ atha matsyaḥ api |
children.translated_text: A tank is twelve by ten; a crane stands at the southeast [corner], and a fish also;

children.text: aiśānyām aparāśāgataḥ hataḥ asau kiyat vācyam || 9 ||
children.translated_text: having gone toward the northeast, it was killed coming from the west. State how much [each traveled]. // 9 //

body.translated_text: Setting down:

body.text: parilekhaḥ 53
body.translated_text: Diagram 53

body.text: pratyayakaraṇam ca sarveṣu eva kṣetreṣu "yaḥ ca eva bhujāvargaḥ koṭīvargaḥ ca karṇavargaḥ saḥ" [gaṇitaí, 17 ] iti anena eva iti || 17 ||
body.translated_text: And the verification in all figures [is done] by this very [rule]: "that which is the square of the <s>bhujā</s> (side) and the square of the <s>koṭi</s> (upright) — that is the square of the <s>karṇa</s> (hypotenuse)" [<s>Gaṇita</s>, 17]. // 17 //

body.text: vṛttāvagāhaśarajñānam
body.translated_text: Knowledge of the arrow of intersection of circles

body.text: vṛttāvagāhaśarānayanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: For computing the arrow of intersection of circles, he states:

children.text: grāsone dve vṛtte grāsaguṇe bhājayet pṛthaktvena |
children.translated_text: The two circles diminished by the <s>grāsa</s> (obscuration), [each] multiplied by the <s>grāsa</s>, should be divided separately;
the quotients from the sum of the [diameters] diminished by the <s>grāsa</s> are the <s>saṃpātaśara</s> (arrows of intersection), mutually [exchanged]. // 18 //

body.text:
grāsena ūne grāsone | ke ? dve vṛtte, grāhyagrāhakamaṇḍaladvayam | grāsaguṇe, grāsaḥ guṇaḥ yayoḥ te grāsaguṇe | bhājayet pṛthaktvena, ekaikam | kena ? grāsonayogalabdhau | grāsonayoḥ yogaḥ grāsonayogaḥ, tayoḥ eva vṛttayoḥ grāsavivarjitayoḥ samāsaḥ ; tena grāsonayogena labdhau grāsonayogalabdhau | sampāte śarau sampātaśarau, avagrāhaśarau iti yāvat | parasparataḥ, anyonyataḥ | yasmāt mahāviṣkambhasya alpaḥ śaraḥ mahatvāt maṇḍalasya, alpavyāsasya
mahān śaraḥ | yasmāt alpasya maṇḍalasya alpaḥ api avayavaḥ ativakraḥ upalabhyate, na tathā mahataḥ | tasmāt tau saṃpātaśarau parasparataḥ bhavataḥ |
body.translated_text: Diminished by the <s>grāsa</s> (obscuration) means "<s>grāsona</s>" (reduced by the obscuration). Which? The two circles — the pair of eclipsed and eclipsing circles. "Multiplied by the <s>grāsa</s>" — those for which the <s>grāsa</s> is the multiplier are "<s>grāsaguṇa</s>." "Should be divided separately" — each one. By what? By the quotients from the sum of the [diameters] diminished by the <s>grāsa</s>. The sum of the two [diameters] diminished by the <s>grāsa</s> is the <s>grāsonayoga</s> — that is, the sum of those two circles reduced by the obscuration; by that <s>grāsonayoga</s>, the quotients [obtained] are the "<s>grāsonayogalabdha</s>." The arrows at the intersection are the <s>saṃpātaśara</s> — that is, the <s>avagrāhaśara</s> (arrows of obscuration). "Mutually" means "reciprocally." Because the arrow of a large-diameter [circle] is small due to the greatness of the circle, while the arrow of a small-diameter [circle] is large. Because even a small part of a small circle is observed to be very curved, but not so for a large one. Therefore those two arrows of intersection are [assigned] mutually.

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Example problem:

children.text: aśītiviṣkambhatamomayena dvātriṃśat indoḥ sthagitā yadā aṣṭau |
children.translated_text: When eight [units] of the Moon, [which has a diameter of] thirty-two, are obscured by the darkness [<s>Rāhu</s>] of eighty in diameter,

children.text: jñātum tat icchāmi śarau kiyantau rāhoḥ atha indoḥ paripūrṇamūlaiḥ || 1 ||
children.translated_text: I wish to know: how great are the two arrows of <s>Rāhu</s> and of the Moon, by the complete roots? // 1 //

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Setting down:

body.text: parilekhaḥ 54
body.translated_text: Diagram 54

body.text: karaṇam ã grāsone dve vṛtte 72, 24 | grāsaguṇe 576, 192 | grāsonayogaḥ 96 | anena labdhau śarau candramasaḥ 6, rāhoḥ 2, parasparataḥ iti || 18 ||
body.translated_text: Calculation: the two circles diminished by the <s>grāsa</s>: 72, 24. Multiplied by the <s>grāsa</s>: 576, 192. The sum of the [diameters] diminished by the <s>grāsa</s> is 96. By this, the arrows obtained are: of the Moon, 6; of <s>Rāhu</s>, 2 — mutually [exchanged]. // 18 //

body.text: śreḍhīgaṇitam
body.translated_text: Arithmetic of series

body.text: atha idānīm śreḍhīgaṇitānayanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: Now, for the computation of arithmetic series, he states:

children.text: iṣṭam vyekam dalitam sapūrvam uttaraguṇam samukham madhyam |
children.translated_text: The desired [number of terms], decreased by one, halved, [added] to the preceding [terms], multiplied by the common difference, [and then] added to the first term, is the middle [value];

children.text: iṣṭaguṇitam iṣtadhanam tu athavā ādyantam padārdhahatam || 19 ||
children.translated_text: that multiplied by the desired [number of terms] is the desired sum; or alternatively, [the sum of] the first and last [terms] multiplied by half the number of terms. // 19 //

body.text: iṣṭam, īpsitam | vigatam ekena vyekam | dalitam, ardhitam | sapūrvam, iṣṭāt padāt yāni prāgavasthitāni [ padāni ] tāni pūrvaśabdena ucyante, saha pūrveṇa vartate iti sapūrvam | uttaraḥ guṇaḥ yasya taduttaraguṇam | samukham, mukhamādiḥ, saha mukhena vartate iti samukham | madhyadhanam bhavati | iṣṭaguṇitam, iṣṭena guṇitam iṣṭaguṇitam | iṣṭadhanam, iṣṭasya gacchasya dhanam bhavati |
body.translated_text: "Desired" (<s>iṣṭa</s>) means wished for. "Decreased by one" is <s>vyeka</s>. "Halved" means divided by two. "With the preceding" — the terms that are positioned before the desired term are denoted by the word "preceding" (<s>pūrva</s>); "<s>sapūrva</s>" means "together with the preceding." That of which the common difference (<s>uttara</s>) is the multiplier is "<s>uttaraguṇa</s>" (multiplied by the common difference). "<s>Samukha</s>" — the face (<s>mukha</s>) is the first term; "together with the first term" is <s>samukha</s>. This gives the middle value (<s>madhyadhana</s>). "Multiplied by the desired" — multiplied by the desired [number] is <s>iṣṭaguṇita</s>. "The desired sum" (<s>iṣṭadhana</s>) — this gives the sum for the desired number of terms.

body.text:
atra bahūni sūtrāṇi muktakavyavasthitāni, teṣām yathāsaṃyogam sambandhaḥ | "iṣṭam vyekam dalitam uttaraguṇam samukham" iti madhyadhanānayanārtham sūtram | "madhyam iṣṭaguṇitam iṣṭadhanam" iti gacchadhanānayanārtham | "iṣṭam vyekam sapūrvam uttaraguṇam samukham" iti antyopāntyādidhanānayanārtham | "iṣṭam vyekam dalitam sapūrvam uttaraguṇam samukham iṣṭaguṇitam iṣṭadhanam" iti avāntarayatheṣṭapadasaṅkhyānayanārtham | evam
etāni pādonayā āryayā pratibaddhāni | tāni yathākrameṇa uddeśakeṣu eva pratipādayiṣyāmaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here many rules are arranged independently; their connection is according to [their] combination. "The desired, decreased by one, halved, multiplied by the common difference, added to the first term" — this is the rule for finding the middle value. "The middle value multiplied by the desired [number of terms] is the desired sum" — this is for finding the total sum. "The desired, decreased by one, with the preceding, multiplied by the common difference, added to the first term" — this is for finding the last term, penultimate term, and so forth. "The desired, decreased by one, halved, with the preceding, multiplied by the common difference, added to the first term, multiplied by the desired, is the desired sum" — this is for finding the sum of any desired intermediate number of terms. Thus these [rules] are bound together in a three-quarter <s>āryā</s> verse. We shall explain them in order through example problems.

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Example problem:

children.text: ādiḥ dvitayam dṛṣṭam śreḍhyāḥ pravadanti ca uttaram trīṇi |
children.translated_text: The first term of a series is seen to be two, and they state the common difference to be three;

children.text: gacchaḥ pañca niruktaḥ madhyāśeṣe dhane brūhi || 1 ||
children.translated_text: the number of terms is declared to be five — state the middle value and the remaining sums. // 1 //

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã ādiḥ 2, uttaram 3, gacchaḥ 5 |
body.translated_text: Setting down: first term 2, common difference 3, number of terms 5.

body.text: karaṇam ã iṣṭam gacchaḥ 5, vyekam 4, dalitam 2, uttaraguṇam 6, samukham 8, etat madhyadhanam | etat eva iṣṭagacchena guṇitam sarvadhanam jātam 40 |
body.translated_text: Calculation: the desired [number] is the number of terms 5, decreased by one gives 4, halved gives 2, multiplied by the common difference gives 6, added to the first term gives 8 — this is the middle value. This same [value] multiplied by the desired number of terms gives the total sum: 40.

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Example problem:

children.text: aṣṭāvādiḥ yasyāḥ pañca pravadanti ca uttaram śreḍhyāḥ |

children.text: gacchaḥ aṣṭādaśa dṛṣṭaḥ madhyāśeṣe dhane vācye || 2 ||
children.translated_text: the number of terms is seen to be eighteen — state the middle value and the remaining sums. // 2 //

body.translated_text: Example problem for finding the last, penultimate, and other term-values:

children.translated_text: Of a [series] with first term seven and common difference eleven, the number of terms is twenty-five;

children.text: tatra antyopāntyadhane vada śīghram viṃśateḥ ca kiyat || 3 ||
children.translated_text: state quickly the last and penultimate term-values there, and also [the value] of the twentieth. // 3 //

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã ādiḥ 7, uttaram 11, gacchaḥ 25 |
body.translated_text: Setting down: first term 7, common difference 11, number of terms 25.

body.text: karaṇam ã iṣṭam pañcaviṃśatiḥ 25, pūraṇam padam ekam iti ekam rūpam 1, etat eva vyekam śūnyam 0, etat eva sapūrvam iti śūnyena kṣiptā caturviṃśatiḥ 24, uttaraguṇam 264, samukham 271, etat antyadhanam | upāntyadhanānayane atra pūrvāṇi padāni trayoviṃśatiḥ 23 | etaiḥ pūrvakaraṇena upāntyadhanam labdham 260 | viṃśateḥ tu pūrvapadāni ekonaviṃśatiḥ | etaiḥ pūrvavat viṃśatitamasya padasya dhanam 216 |
body.translated_text: Calculation: the desired is twenty-five, 25; the term to be filled is one, so [add] one unit, 1; this decreased by one is zero, 0; this "with the preceding" means zero added to twenty-four gives 24; multiplied by the common difference gives 264; added to the first term gives 271 — this is the last term-value. For finding the penultimate term-value, the preceding terms here are twenty-three, 23. By these, using the previous procedure, the penultimate term-value obtained is 260. For the twentieth, the preceding terms are nineteen. By these, as before, the value of the twentieth term is 216.

body.text: avāntare yatheṣṭapadasaṅkhyādhanānayane uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Example problem for finding the sum of any desired intermediate number of terms:

children.text: dvyāditryuttarasaṅkhyam dine dine kārtike kramāt māse |

a king gives [to a Brahmin]; after fifteen days, a Brahmin
of great learning arrives; to him is given the sum of ten days' [worth]; to another, the amount arising from five days —

children.translated_text: state what is the wealth of each of those two. // 4 //

body.translated_text: Example problem:

children.text: pañcadaśādiḥ yasmin uttaram aṣṭādaśa ucyate gacchaḥ |
children.translated_text: In that [series] where the first term is fifteen and the common difference is stated to be eighteen, the number of terms
is thirty — compute quickly the sum of the middle ten terms. // 5 //

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Setting down:

body.text: ādiḥ
body.translated_text: First term 15, common difference 18, number of terms 30; the terms situated in the middle among the remaining separated [terms]

body.text: 15, uttaram 18, gacchaḥ 30, daśasu vyatirikteṣu ca śeṣeṣu madhyasthitāni padāni 10 | labdham pūrvakaraṇena 2760 |
body.translated_text: are 10. The result obtained by the previous procedure is 2760.

body.text: sarvadhanānayane upāyāntaram punar api āryāpādena āha ã
body.translated_text: For another method of finding the total sum, he states again with a quarter of the <s>āryā</s> verse:

body.text: tu athavā ādyantam padārdhahatam |
body.translated_text: Or alternatively, [the sum of] the first and last [terms] multiplied by half the number of terms.

body.text: athavā ayam aparaḥ prakāraḥ | ādiḥ ca antaḥ ca ādyantam | ādiśabdena ādidhanam parigṛhyate, antaśabdena antyadhanam | tat ādyantam | padam gacchaḥ, tasya ardham padārdham, padārdhena hatam padārdhahatam | tat ādyantam padārdhaguṇitam iṣṭadhanam iti anuvartanāt iṣṭadhanam bhavati |
body.translated_text: "Alternatively" — this is another method. The first and the last together are <s>ādyanta</s> (first-and-last). By the word "first" (<s>ādi</s>), the first term-value is understood; by the word "last" (<s>anta</s>), the last term-value. That is the <s>ādyanta</s>. The number of terms is the <s>pada</s> (step); its half is <s>padārdha</s> (half the number of terms); multiplied by <s>padārdha</s> is <s>padārdhahatam</s>. That first-and-last multiplied by half the number of terms gives the desired sum — by continuation [from the previous rule], it becomes the desired sum.

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Example problem:

children.translated_text: If the first conch[-shell's price] is five, and the last would be ninety-five,

children.text: ekādaśaśaṅkhānām yat tat mūlyam tvam ācakṣva || 6 ||
children.translated_text: state the total price of eleven conch-shells. // 6 //

body.translated_text: Setting down:

body.text: ādiśaṅkhamūlyam 5, antyasya 95, śaṅkhāḥ 11 |
body.translated_text: Price of the first conch-shell: 5; of the last: 95; conch-shells: 11.

karaṇam ã ādyantadhane 100, padārdham
5

anena guṇitam sarvaśaṅkhamūlyam 550 |
body.translated_text: Calculation: the first and last term-values are 100; half the number of terms is 5 1/2; multiplied by this, the total price of all conch-shells is 550.

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Example problem:

children.text: ādidhanam ekam uktam hi antyadhanam procyate śatam sadbhiḥ |
children.translated_text: The first term-value is stated to be one, and the last term-value is declared by the wise to be a hundred;

children.text: padam api tāvat proktam sarvadhanam tat kiyat dṛṣṭam || 7 ||
children.translated_text: the number of terms is also stated to be that much — what is the total sum seen [to be]? // 7 //

body.text: gacchajñānam
body.translated_text: Knowledge of the number of terms

body.text: gacchānayanārtham āha ã
body.translated_text: For finding the number of terms, he states:

children.translated_text: The number of terms: from [the total sum] multiplied by eight times the common difference, to which is added the square of the difference of twice the first term and the common difference,
[take] the root, subtract twice the first term, divide by the common difference, [and take] half plus one. // 20 //

body.text:
gacchaḥ iti anena [pa]dadhanam parigṛhyate | aṣṭottaraguṇitāt aṣṭābhiḥ uttareṇa ca guṇitam aṣṭottaraguṇitam | tasmāt aṣṭottaraguṇitāt | dviguṇādyuttaraviśeṣavargayutāt, dviguṇaḥ ca asau ādiḥ ca dviguṇādiḥ, dviguṇādeḥ uttarasya ca viśeṣaḥ dviguṇādyuttaraviśeṣaḥ, dviguṇādyuttaraviśeṣasya vargaḥ dviguṇādyuttaraviśeṣavargaḥ, dviguṇādyuttaraviśeṣavargeṇa yutam dviguṇādyuttaraviśeṣavargayutam, tasmāt dviguṇādyuttaraviśeṣavargayutāt gacchadhanāt
[sarvadhanāt] aṣṭottaraguṇitāt mūlam, dviguṇādyūnam dviguṇaḥ ca asau ādiḥ ca dviguṇādiḥ, tena dviguṇādinā ūnam dviguṇādyūnam, svottareṇa bhajitam svottarabhajitam, saha rūpeṇa vartate iti sarūpam, ardham dalitam, gacchaḥ bhavati |
body.translated_text: By "number of terms" (<s>gaccha</s>), the term-sum is understood. "Multiplied by eight times the common difference" — multiplied by eight and by the common difference is <s>aṣṭottaraguṇita</s>; from that <s>aṣṭottaraguṇita</s>. "To which is added the square of the difference of twice the first term and the common difference" — twice [the first term], that being also the first term, is <s>dviguṇādi</s> (twice the first term); the difference of <s>dviguṇādi</s> and the common difference is <s>dviguṇādyuttaraviśeṣa</s>; the square of <s>dviguṇādyuttaraviśeṣa</s> is <s>dviguṇādyuttaraviśeṣavarga</s>; added to that square is <s>dviguṇādyuttaraviśeṣavargayuta</s>; from that [sum], which is the term-sum [i.e., total sum] multiplied by eight times the common difference, [take] the root; subtract twice the first term — twice [the first term], that being also the first term, is <s>dviguṇādi</s>; reduced by that <s>dviguṇādi</s> is <s>dviguṇādyūna</s>; divided by its own common difference is <s>svottarabhajita</s>; "together with unity" is <s>sarūpa</s>; half means halved — [this] gives the number of terms.

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Example problem:

children.text: ādiḥ pañca proktaḥ saptākhyam ca uttaram bhavet śreḍhyā |
children.translated_text: The first term is stated to be five, and the common difference of the series is called seven;

children.text: pañconaśatam dravyam gacchaḥ vācyaḥ kiyān tasya || 1 ||
children.translated_text: the sum is ninety-five — state what is the number of terms. // 1 //

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Setting down:

body.text: ādiḥ 5, uttaram 7, sarvadhanam 95 |
body.translated_text: First term 5, common difference 7, total sum 95.

body.text: karaṇam ã gacchadhanāt aṣṭottaraguṇitāt iti gacchadhanam aṣṭābhiḥ uttareṇa ca guṇitam jātam 5320 | dviguṇaḥ ādiḥ 10, etat uttaraviśeṣitam 3, etasya vargaḥ 9, anena yuktam jātam 5329, etasmāt mūlam 73, dviguṇādyūnam 63, svottareṇa anena 7 bhajitam 9, sarūpam 10, ardham gacchaḥ 5 |
body.translated_text: Calculation: "from the term-sum multiplied by eight times the common difference" — the term-sum multiplied by eight and by the common difference gives 5320. Twice the first term is 10; this differentiated from the common difference gives 3; its square is 9; added to that gives 5329; the root of this is 73; subtracting twice the first term gives 63; divided by the common difference, 7, gives 9; adding one gives 10; halved, the number of terms is 5.

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Example problem:

children.text: navakāṣṭau vṛddhimukhe yatra yat kīrtyate dhanam kramaśaḥ |
children.translated_text: Where the common difference is nine and the first term is eight, and what is declared as the sum successively,
is seen to be five hundred eighty-three — state the measure of the number of terms. // 2 //

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Setting down:

body.text: ādiḥ 8, uttaram 9, gacchadhanam 583 | pūrvavat labdham padapramāṇam 11 || 20 ||
body.translated_text: First term 8, common difference 9, total sum 583. As before, the measure of the number of terms obtained is 11. // 20 //

body.text: citighanajñānam
body.translated_text: Knowledge of the volume of a pile

children.translated_text: For computing the <s>saṅkalana</s> (summation) of <s>saṅkalana</s> (summation), he states:
Of a series beginning with one and increasing by one, the product of the number of terms, the number of terms plus one, and the number of terms plus two,

children.text: ṣaḍbhaktaḥ sa citighanaḥ saikapadaghanaḥ vimūlaḥ vā || 20 ||
children.translated_text: divided by six, is the <s>citighana</s> (volume of the pile); or alternatively, the cube of the number of terms plus one, minus [its] root. // 20 //

body.text:
uttaram ca ādiḥ ca uttarādī | ekam uttarādī yasyāḥ saikottarādiḥ | ekottarādiḥ ca asau upacitiḥ ca ekottarādyupacitiḥ | upacitiḥ śreḍhī ekottarāditvena viśeṣyate | sa eva ekottarādyupacitiḥ saṅkalanā iti ucyate | tasyāḥ ekottarādyupaciteḥ saṅkalanāsaṃjñitāyāḥ gacchāt prabhṛti ekottaratrisaṃvargaḥ ekottarāṇām trayāṇām gacchādeḥ samvargaḥ | tat yathā ã gacchaḥ, sa ekottaram, punar api ekottaram | trayāṇām gacchādeḥ saṃvargaḥ | tat yathā ã gacchaḥ, sa ekottaram,
punar api ekottaram | etat uktam bhavati ã gacchaḥ, sa eva ekottaraḥ, sa eva gacchaḥ dvyuttaraḥ, teṣām trayāṇām saṃvargaḥ, ṣaḍbhaktaḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ vibhājitaḥ, sa citighanaḥ citeḥ ghanaḥ citighanaḥ saṅkalanāsaṅkalanā iti arthaḥ | atha anyaḥ karaṇopāyaḥ ã saikapadaghanaḥ, saikam ca tatpadam ca saikapadam, saikapadasya ghanaḥ saikapadaghanaḥ, vigataḥ mūlena vimūlaḥ ṣaḍbhaktaḥ iti anuvartate | vā saikasya padasya ghanagaṇitam vā svamūlavirahitam ṣaḍbhiḥ bhaktam citighanaḥ
bhavati |
body.translated_text: 'Increasing' and 'beginning' [make] 'increasing-beginning' (<s>uttaradi</s>). That whose increasing-beginning is one is '<s>saikottaradi</s>' (having one as the increasing-beginning). 'Having one as the increasing-beginning' and 'series' — [make] 'series with one as the increasing-beginning' (<s>ekottaradyupaciti</s>). The series (<s>upaciti</s>) is qualified by the property of having one as the increasing-beginning. That very 'series with one as the increasing-beginning' is called <s>sankalana</s> (summation). Of that series with one as the increasing-beginning, called summation, starting from the number of terms (<s>gaccha</s>), the product of three [numbers each] increasing by one (<s>ekottara-trisamvarga</s>) — the product of three [numbers] starting from the number of terms, each increasing by one. That is as follows: the number of terms, that increased by one, again increased by one. The product of three starting from the number of terms. That is as follows: the number of terms, that increased by one, again increased by one. What is stated is this: the number of terms, that same [number] increased by one, that same number of terms increased by two — the product of those three, divided by six, is the <s>citighana</s> (cube of the series), meaning the cube of the summation, i.e., the summation of summations (<s>sankalana-sankalana</s>). Now, another method of computation: the cube of the term increased by one (<s>saikapada-ghana</s>) — '<s>saikam</s>' means 'together with one,' and that is the term (<s>padam</s>), so '<s>saikapadam</s>'; the cube of '<s>saikapadam</s>' is '<s>saikapadaghana</s>'; deprived of [its own] root is '<s>vimula</s>' — 'divided by six' continues [from the previous rule]. Alternatively, the cube-computation of the term increased by one, deprived of its own root, divided by six — that becomes the <s>citighana</s>.

children.text: pañcānām aṣṭānām caturdaśānām ca yāḥ kramāt citayaḥ |

children.text: gacchaḥ tarāḥ trikoṇā [ rūpavidhānam ca ] me vācyam || 1 ||
children.translated_text: the number of terms, the layers [being] triangular [and the rule of] unit-arrangement — tell me. // 1 //
