body.translated_text: Diagram 55

body.text: yathākrameṇa gacchāḥ 5, 8, 14 |
body.translated_text: The numbers of terms in order: 5, 8, 14.

body.text: karaṇam ã gacchaḥ pañca 5 | ayam ekottaraḥ 6 | punar ayam ekottaraḥ 7 | eteṣām trayāṇām saṃvargaḥ 210 | ayam ṣaḍbhaktaḥ saṅkalanāsaṅkalanā bhavati 35 |
body.translated_text: Computation: The number of terms is five, 5. This increased by one is 6. Again this increased by one is 7. The product of these three is 210. This divided by six — the summation of summations is 35.

body.text: dvitīyopāyakaraṇam ã saikapadam 6, asya ghanaḥ 216, ayam vimūlaḥ iti ṣaḍbhiḥ eva rahitaḥ 210, pūrvavat ṣaḍbhaktaḥ saṅkalanāsaṅkalanā bhavati 35 |
body.translated_text: Second method computation: The term increased by one is 6; its cube is 216; this 'deprived of root' means diminished by six itself, [giving] 210; divided by six as before, the summation of summations is 35.

body.text: śeṣayoḥ api labdham yathākrameṇa 120, 560 || 21 ||
body.translated_text: For the remaining two also, the results in order are 120, 560. // 21 //

body.text: vargacitighanaḥ ghanacitighanaḥ ca
body.translated_text: The cube of the square-series and the cube of the cube-series

body.text: vargaghanasaṅkalanānayanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of finding the summation of squares and cubes, he states:

children.translated_text: Of the terms — [each] with one added, together with the number of terms — the sixth part of the successive product of three

children.text: vargacitighanaḥ sa bhavet citavargaḥ ghanacitighanaḥ ca || 22 ||
children.translated_text: would be the cube of the square-series; and the square of the series is the cube of the cube-series. // 22 //

body.text:
saha ekena vartate iti saikaḥ | saha gacchena vartate iti sagacchaḥ | anantaraprakṛtaḥ saikasagacchaḥ | padam gacchaḥ tatra saikam ca [saika] sagaccham ca padam ca saikasagacchapadāni | teṣām saikasagacchapadānām kramāt ānupūrvyāt | trayāṇām saṃvargitam trisaṃvargitam | keṣām trayāṇām ? prakṛtānām saikasagacchapadānam | ṣaṣṭhaḥ aṃśaḥ | tasya trisaṃvargitasya ṣaṣṭhaḥ aṃśaḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ bhāgaḥ | vargacitighanaḥ sa bhavet | vargasya citiḥ vargacitiḥ vargaciteḥ
ghanaḥ vargacitighanaḥ | vargasaṅkalanā iti arthaḥ | citivargaḥ ghanacitighanaḥ ca | citeḥ vargaḥ saṅkalanāvargaḥ iti yāvat | sa eva citivargaḥ ghanacitighanaḥ bhavati |
body.translated_text: 'Together with one' (<s>saika</s>) means 'existing with one.' 'Together with the number of terms' (<s>sagaccha</s>) means 'existing with the number of terms.' The previously mentioned '<s>saikasagaccha</s>' — 'term' is the number of terms (<s>gaccha</s>); there, '<s>saikam</s>' and '<s>sagaccham</s>' and 'term' [together form] '<s>saikasagacchapadani</s>.' Of those '<s>saikasagacchapadani</s>' — in order, i.e. successively. The product of three (<s>trisamvargita</s>) — of which three? Of the aforementioned '<s>saikasagacchapadani</s>.' The sixth part — of that product of three, the sixth part, the sixth share. 'Would be the cube of the square-series' — the series of squares is '<s>vargaciti</s>'; the cube of the square-series is '<s>vargacitighana</s>.' The meaning is: the summation of squares. 'The square of the series is the cube of the cube-series' — the square of the series is the summation-squared, i.e., [the series] raised to the second [power]. That very square of the series is the cube of the cube-series.

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Example problem:

children.translated_text: Of seven, eight, and seventeen — the series are quadrilateral;

children.text: ekavidhānam vācyam padaḥ tarāḥ tāḥ hi vargākhyāḥ || 1 ||
children.translated_text: the unit-arrangement is to be stated; the terms and layers — those are indeed called 'square.' // 1 //

body.translated_text: Computation: The term is 7, increased by one is 8, this same together with the number of terms is 15. The product of these three is 840; divided by six, the measure of the cube of the square-series is 140. For the remaining two also, the results in order are 204, 1785.

assembled one upon another, those are equal-quadrilateral bricks, in order. // 2 //

body.translated_text: Diagram 58

body.text: karaṇam ã citisaṅkalanā | sā ca "athavā ādyantam padārdhahatam" [ gaṇita í, 29 ] iti anena ānīyate | atra ādiḥ ekaḥ 1, antyadhanam pañca 5, ekatra ṣaṭ 6, padārdhena pañcānām ardhena hatam saṅkalanācitiḥ pañcānām jātā 15, asya vargaḥ ghanacitighanaḥ bhavati | sa ca 225 | śeṣayoḥ api yathākrameṇa labdham 100, 2025 || 22 ||
body.translated_text: Computation: The summation of the series. That is obtained by 'or, the beginning and end [multiplied by] half the number of terms' [<s>Ganita</s>, 29]. Here, the first [term] is one, 1; the last term is five, 5; combined, six, 6; multiplied by half the number of terms, half of five — the summation for five is 15. The square of this is the cube of the cube-series, and it is 225. For the remaining two also, the results in order are 100, 2025. // 22 //

body.text: prakārāntareṇa rāśidvayasaṃvargajñānam
body.translated_text: Finding the product of two quantities by another method

body.text: dvayoḥ rāsyoḥ saṃvargānayana upāyāntaram āha ã
body.translated_text: He states another method for finding the product of two quantities:

children.text: samparkasya hi vargāt viśodhayet eva vargasamparkam |
children.translated_text: From the square of the sum, one should indeed subtract the sum of the squares;

children.text: yat tasya bhavati ardham vidyāt guṇakārasaṃvargam || 23 ||
children.translated_text: half of the [remainder] — one should know [that to be] the product of the multipliers. // 23 //

body.text:
samparkaḥ samāsaḥ | yena dvayoḥ rāśyoḥ samparkaḥ bhavati iti dvayoḥ eva samparkaḥ parigṛhyate | tasya samparkasya | hi pādapūraṇe | vargāt, kṛteḥ | viśodhayet eva, apanayet eva | kim iti āha ã vargasamparkam | vargīkṛtayoḥ samparkaḥ vargasamparkaḥ vargasamāsaḥ, tam vargasamparkam samparkasya vargāt viśodhayet | yat tasya bhavati ardham, tasya śuddhaśeṣasya ardham dalam yat bhavati | vidyāt, avabuddhyāt | guṇakārasaṃvargam, guṇakārayoḥ saṃvargaḥ
guṇakārasamvargaḥ, tam guṇakārasaṃvargam vidyāt |
body.translated_text: 'Sum' (<s>samparka</s>) means 'total.' Since the sum is of two quantities, 'sum of two' alone is understood. Of that sum — '<s>hi</s>' is a metrical filler. From the square, from the product [of the sum with itself] — one should indeed subtract, i.e. remove. What? He says: the sum of squares (<s>vargasamparka</s>). The sum of the squared [quantities] is the sum of squares, the total of squares — that sum of squares [should be subtracted] from the square of the sum. 'Half of the [remainder]' — what is the half, the part, of the purified remainder. 'One should know' — one should understand. 'The product of the multipliers' — the product of the two multipliers is the product of multipliers — that product of multipliers one should know.

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Example problem:

children.text: pañcānām ca caturṇām saptanavānām ca kaḥ bhavet ghātaḥ |
children.translated_text: Of five and four, of seven and nine — what would be the product?

children.text: aṣṭānām ca daśānām pṛthak pṛthak vācyatām śīghram || 1 ||
children.translated_text: Of eight and ten — separately, separately, state [the answer] quickly. // 1 //

body.text:
nyāsaḥ ã
  5 7 8
  4 9 10
  karaṇam ã pañcānām caturṇām ca samparkaḥ 9, asya vargaḥ 81; pañcānām vargaḥ 25, caturṇām vargaḥ 16, ekatra 41, samparkavargāt imam pañcavargacaturvargasamparkam viśodhayet | tatra śeṣaḥ 40 | asya ardham pañcānām caturṇām ca saṃvargaḥ labdhaḥ 20 | śeṣayoḥ api yathākrameṇa 63, 80 || 23 ||
body.translated_text:
Layout:
  5  7  8
  4  9  10
Computation: The sum of five and four is 9; its square is 81. The square of five is 25; the square of four is 16; combined, 41. From the square of the sum, subtract this sum of the square of five and the square of four. The remainder there is 40. Half of this — the product of five and four — is obtained as 20. For the remaining two also, in order: 63, 80. // 23 //

body.text: guṇya-guṇakayoḥ ānayanam
body.translated_text: Finding the two factors

body.text: guṇakārayoḥ ānayanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of finding the two multipliers, he states:

children.translated_text: From the product multiplied by twice the square [of two], combined with the square of the difference of the two —
the root, increased and decreased by the difference — that pair of multipliers, halved. // 24 //

body.text: dvayoḥ kṛtiḥ dvikṛtiḥ, dvikṛtiḥ guṇaḥ yasya sa dvikṛtiguṇaḥ, tasmāt dvikṛtiguṇāt | kasmāt iti āha ã saṃvargāt | dvyantaravargeṇa samyutāt | dvayoḥ api antaram dvyantaram, dvyantarasya vargaḥ dvyantaravargaḥ, tena dvyantaravargeṇa saṃyutāt | dvikṛtiguṇāt saṃvargāt dvayoḥ api antaravargeṇa miśritāt yat mūlam | tat antarayuktam antareṇa yuktam antarayuktam | hīnam virahitam | tadguṇakāradvayam tasya saṃvargasya guṇakāradvayam | dalitam ardhitam |
body.translated_text: The square of two is '<s>dvikrti</s>'; that by which [the product] is multiplied is '<s>dvikrtrguna</s>'; from that '<s>dvikrtrguna</s>.' Of what? He says: from the product (<s>samvarga</s>). Combined with the square of the difference of the two (<s>dvyantaravarga</s>) — the difference of the two is '<s>dvyantara</s>'; the square of '<s>dvyantara</s>' is '<s>dvyantaravarga</s>'; by that '<s>dvyantaravarga</s>', combined. From the product multiplied by twice the square [of two], combined with the square of the difference of the two — the root of that. That [root] increased by the difference is 'increased by the difference.' Decreased means deprived [of the difference]. That pair of multipliers — of that product, the pair of multipliers. Halved means divided by two.

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Example problem:

children.text: saṃvargaḥ aṣṭau dṛṣṭaḥ vyaktam tatra antaram bhavet dvitayam |
children.translated_text: A product of eight is observed; the difference there should be two.

children.text: aṣṭādaśake munayaḥ guṇakārau tau tayoḥ vācyau || 1 ||
children.translated_text: In [the case of] eighteen, [the difference is] seven — state those two multipliers. // 1 //

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã saṃvargaḥ 8, antaram 2 | saṃvargaḥ 18, antaram 7 |
body.translated_text: Layout: product 8, difference 2. Product 18, difference 7.

body.text: karaṇam ã saṃvargaḥ 8, etat dvikṛtiguṇam 32; dvyantaram 2, asya vargaḥ 4, anena saṃyuktaḥ 36 | asya mūlam 6, etat tena antareṇa yuktam 8, hīnam 4 | yathākrameṇa dalitau parasparaguṇakārau 4, 2 |
body.translated_text: Computation: The product is 8; this multiplied by twice the square [of two] is 32. The difference of the two is 2; its square is 4; combined with this, 36. The root of this is 6; this increased by that difference is 8, decreased is 4. Halved in order, the mutual multipliers are 4, 2.

body.text: dvitīyoddeśake api guṇakārau labdhau 9, 2 |
body.translated_text: In the second example also, the multipliers obtained are 9, 2.

body.text: atra guṇyaguṇakārayoḥ aviśeṣāt guṇakāradvayam iti ucyate || 24 ||
body.translated_text: Here, since there is no distinction between the multiplicand and the multiplier, 'pair of multipliers' is said. // 24 //

body.text: mūlaphalajñānam
body.translated_text: Finding the principal and interest

body.text: mūlaphalānayanārtham āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of finding the principal and interest (<s>mulaphala</s>), he states:

children.translated_text: The principal-interest, together with interest, [when] multiplied by time and principal, combined with the square of half the principal —
the root of that, diminished by half the principal, divided by time, is one's own principal-interest. // 25 //

body.text:
mūlam śatādi, phalam vṛddhiḥ, mūlasya phalam mūlaphalam | saha phalena vartate iti saphalam, ātmīyayā vṛddhyā yuktam mūlaphalam iti yāvat | kālamūlaguṇam, kālam ca mūlam ca kālamūle, kālamūle guṇau yasya mūlaphalasya tat kālamūlaguṇam mūlaphalam | ardhamūlakṛtiyuktam, [ ardham mūlasya ardhamūlam mūlārdham iti, ardhamūlasya kṛtiḥ ardhamūlakṛtiḥ, mūlakṛteḥ caturthaḥ bhāgaḥ iti ], [ardha]kṛtitvāt dvayoḥ vargeṇa iti caturvibhāgaḥ, tayā
ardhamūlakṛtyā yuktam ardhamūlakṛtiyuktam | tanmūlam, tasya eva niṣpāditasya mūlam tanmūlam | mūlārdhonam, mūlasya śatādeḥ ardhena ūnam mūlārdhonam | kālahṛtam, kālena hṛtam kālahṛtam | svamūlaphalam, svasya mūlasya phalam svamūlaphalam |
body.translated_text: The principal (<s>mula</s>) is a hundred and so on; the interest (<s>phala</s>) is the profit; the interest of the principal is '<s>mulaphala</s>.' 'Together with interest' (<s>saphala</s>) means 'existing with interest,' i.e. the principal-interest combined with its own profit. 'Multiplied by time and principal' (<s>kalamulagunam</s>) — time and principal are '<s>kalamule</s>'; time and principal are the multipliers of the principal-interest; that is '<s>kalamulagunam mulaphalam</s>.' 'Combined with the square of half the principal' (<s>ardhamulakrtiyuktam</s>) — [half the principal is '<s>ardhamula</s>' or '<s>mulardham</s>'; the square of half the principal is '<s>ardhamulakrti</s>,' i.e. one-fourth of the square of the principal]; because of squaring two, i.e. divided by four; combined with that square of half the principal. 'The root of that' (<s>tanmulam</s>) — the root of that very computed [quantity]. 'Diminished by half the principal' (<s>mulardhona</s>) — decreased by half of the principal (a hundred, etc.). 'Divided by time' (<s>kalahrtam</s>) — divided by time. 'One's own principal-interest' (<s>svamulaphalam</s>) — the interest of one's own principal.

children.text: jānāmi śatasya phalam na ca kintu śatasya yatphalam saphalam |

body.translated_text: Example problem:

body.text: pañcaviṃśateḥ māsikī vṛddhiḥ na jñāyate | yā pañcaviṃśateḥ māsikī vṛddhiḥ sā tena eva ardheṇa anyatra prayuktā, saha vṛddhyā pañcabhiḥ māsaiḥ dṛṣṭā rūpatrayam pañcabhāgonam | tatra icchāmaḥ jñātum kā pañcaviṃśateḥ māsikī vṛddhiḥ, kā vā pañcaviṃśativa[ṛ]ddheḥ pañcamāsaprayuktāyā vṛddhiḥ iti || 2 ||
body.translated_text: The monthly interest of twenty-five is not known. The monthly interest of twenty-five — that same [amount], invested elsewhere at that same half-[rate], together with interest, is observed as three minus one-fifth in five months. We wish to know: what is the monthly interest of twenty-five, and what is the profit of the twenty-five-plus-interest invested for five months? // 2 //

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Example problem:

body.text: trairāśikam
body.translated_text: The rule of three

body.text: trairāśikapratipādanārthamadhyardhāryām āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of teaching the rule of three (<s>trairasika</s>), he states a verse-and-a-half:

children.text: trairāśikaphalarāśim tam atha icchārāśinā hatam kṛtvā |
children.translated_text: The result-quantity of the rule of three — having multiplied it by the desire-quantity,

children.text: labdham pramāṇabhajitam tasmāt icchāphalam idam syāt || 26 ||
children.translated_text: the result divided by the measure-quantity — that would be the desired result. // 26 //

body.text: chedāḥ parasparahatāḥ bhavanti guṇakārabhāgahārāṇām |
body.translated_text: The divisors of the multipliers and the divisors, [when] multiplied reciprocally, become [the reduced quantities].

body.text:
trayaḥ rāśayaḥ samāhṛtāḥ trirāśiḥ | trirāśiḥ prayojanam asya gaṇitasya iti trairāśikaḥ | trairāśike phalarāśiḥ trairāśikaphalarāśiḥ | tam trairāśikaphalarāśim | athaśabdaḥ parijñānavastuparigrahe uttaragranthapratipādane vartate | atra evaṃprakāraḥ arthaḥ kaḥ atra pratipāditaḥ ? ucyate ã paribhāṣā | sā ca lokavyavahārāt prativiṣayam bhinnā iti lokaprayogāt eva pradarśitā | anyathā hi prativiṣayam bhinnāḥ paribhāṣāḥ viṣayāḥ ca saṃkhyātītāḥ | tena upadeṣṭum
aśeṣataḥ sā na śakyate | ataḥ athaśabdena lokaprasiddhām paribhāṣām pratipādayati | icchārāśinā hatam kṛtvā, yaḥ asau phalarāśiḥ sa icchārāśinā hataḥ kriyate, tam icchārāśinā hatam guṇitam kṛtvā | labdham, labdham āptam | katham iti āha ã pramāṇabhajitam, pramāṇarāśinā bhajitam pramāṇabhajitam | tasmāt evaṃvidhāt rāśeḥ pramāṇabhajitāt | icchāphalam, icchāyāḥ phalam, icchāphalam, icchārāśiphalam iti arthaḥ | idam iti labdham pratyakṣīkṛtya uktam |
body.translated_text: Three quantities collected together are <s>trirāśi</s> (three-quantity [set]). The computation whose purpose is [this] three-quantity [set] is <s>trairāśika</s> (Rule of Three). The result-quantity in the Rule of Three is the <s>trairāśikaphalarāśi</s> (Rule-of-Three result-quantity). [One should find] that Rule-of-Three result-quantity. The word 'atha' (now) is used in the sense of taking up the object of knowledge and teaching what follows. What kind of content has been taught here? It is answered: a convention (<s>paribhāṣā</s>). And since that convention differs for each subject matter in worldly practice, it is demonstrated from worldly usage itself. For otherwise, the conventions differing for each subject, and the subjects being innumerable, it cannot be taught exhaustively. Therefore, with the word 'atha,' he teaches the convention well-known in the world. 'Having multiplied by the desire-quantity' — the result-quantity is multiplied by the desire-quantity; having multiplied, i.e., having made it multiplied by the desire-quantity. 'The obtained' — what is obtained. How? He says: 'divided by the measure' — divided by the measure-quantity is 'divided by the measure.' From such a quantity — divided by the measure. 'The desire-result' — the result of the desire; the desire-result; meaning the result-quantity of the desire-quantity. 'This' — [the word] 'this' is said by pointing to the obtained [result].

body.text:
atra trairāśikam eva kevalam abhihitam ācāryāryabhaṭena, pañcarāśikādayaḥ anupātaviśeṣāḥ katham avagantavyāḥ ? ucyate ã anupātabījamātram eva ācāryeṇa upadiṣṭam ; tena anupātabījena sarvam eva pañcarāśyādikam siddhyati | kutaḥ ? pañcarāśikādīnām trairāśikasaṅghātatvāt | kasmāt pañcarāśyādayaḥ trairāśikasaṃhatāḥ ? pañcarāśike trairāśikadvayam saṃhatam, saptarāśike trairāśikatrayam, navarāśike trairāśikacatuṣṭayam iti ādi uddeśakeṣu
eva upadekṣyāmaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, only the Rule of Three alone has been stated by the teacher <s>Āryabhaṭa</s>. How are the Rule of Five and other specific proportions to be understood? It is answered: Only the seed of proportion has been taught by the teacher. By that seed of proportion, the Rule of Five and all else are accomplished. Why? Because the Rule of Five and the rest are aggregates of the Rule of Three. Why are the Rule of Five and the rest aggregates of the Rule of Three? In the Rule of Five, two Rules of Three are combined; in the Rule of Seven, three Rules of Three; in the Rule of Nine, four Rules of Three — and so on, we shall teach in the very problems.

body.text: yadā punaḥ rāśayaḥ sacchedāḥ syuḥ tadā katham kartavyam iti āha ã
body.translated_text: But when the quantities have fractions (denominators), what is to be done? He says:

body.text: chedāḥ parasparahatāḥ bhavanti guṇakārabhāgahārāṇām |
body.translated_text: The denominators of the multipliers and divisors are cross-multiplied.

body.text:
chedāḥ parasparasya hatāḥ anyonyahatāḥ | keṣām iti ataḥ āha ã guṇakārabhāgahārāṇām | guṇyaguṇakārayoḥ parasparāpekṣayā guṇakāratvam , yasmāt guṇyaḥ guṇakāreṇa guṇyate, guṇakāraḥ api guṇyena, na kaścit phalaviśeṣaḥ | tena uktam guṇyaguṇakārau guṇakāraśabdena | guṇakārau ca bhāgahāraḥ ca guṇakārabhāgahārāḥ | ataḥ teṣām guṇakārabhāgahārāṇām chekāḥ parasparahatāḥ ye guṇakāracchedāḥ bhāgahārahatāḥ te bhāgahārāḥ bhavanti, bhāgahāracchedāḥ
ca guṇakārahatāḥ guṇakārāḥ bhavanti iti etat anuktam api avagamyate eva, yasmāt taddharmāya chedāḥ parasparam nīyante | bhāgahārāṇām saṃvargaḥ bhāgahāraḥ | guṇakārāṇām saṃvargaḥ guṇakāraḥ iti arthāt avagamyate |
body.translated_text: The denominators are mutually multiplied — <s>parasparahatāḥ</s> (cross-multiplied). Of what? He says: of the multipliers and divisors. The multiplied (<s>guṇya</s>) and the multiplier (<s>guṇakāra</s>) have the status of multiplier relative to each other, since the multiplicand is multiplied by the multiplier, and the multiplier [can be multiplied] by the multiplicand — there is no difference in the result. Therefore, the multiplicand and multiplier are both denoted by the word 'multiplier.' Multipliers and divisors — <s>guṇakārabhāgahārāḥ</s>. Therefore, of those multipliers and divisors, the denominators are cross-multiplied: the denominators of the multipliers, having been multiplied by the divisor, become the divisors; and the denominators of the divisors, having been multiplied by the multiplier, become the multipliers — this is understood even without being stated, since the denominators are taken reciprocally for that purpose. The product of the divisors is the [combined] divisor. The product of the multipliers is the [combined] multiplier — this is understood from the meaning.

body.text:
labdham rūpakadvayam [ 2, viṃśopakāḥ ] 4, viṃśopakabhāgāḥ ca
26
41 |
body.translated_text: Result: two <s>rūpakas</s> [2], 4 <s>viṃśopakas</s>, and <s>viṃśopaka</s>-fractions 26/41.

body.text: saptarāśikam
body.translated_text: The Rule of Seven

body.text: saptarāśike uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: In the Rule of Seven, a problem:

children.text: saptocchritasya kariṇaḥ triṃśat paridheḥ navāyatasya yadā |
children.translated_text: Of an elephant seven [cubits] high, thirty in circumference, and nine in length, when
nine <s>kuḍuvas</s> (measures) of pure cleaned rice-flakes are always obtained —

children.text: pañcocchritasya vācyam saptāyām asya dantinaḥ kim syāt |
children.translated_text: tell, for an elephant five [cubits] high, of this one, what would there be?
When its circumference is twenty-eight — the rice-flakes to be obtained? // 12 //

body.text:
sthāpanā ã 7 5
  30 28
  9 7
  9 0

labdham pṛthukakuḍuvāḥ 4, setike 2, setikabhāgāḥ
2
3
body.translated_text: Result: rice-flake <s>kuḍuvas</s> 4, <s>setikas</s> 2, <s>setika</s>-fractions 2/3.

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Problem:

body.text: hastyuttamasya caturhastocchritasya ṣaḍāyatasya pañcapariṇāhasya ardhatṛtīyāḥ kuḍuvāḥ labhyante māṣānām yadā tadā tryucchritasya pañcāyatasya ardhapañcamapariṇāhasya kim labhyam || 13 ||
body.translated_text: Of the best elephant, four cubits high, six in length, five in circumference, two and a half <s>kuḍuvas</s> of beans are obtained. Then, for one three [cubits] high, five in length, four and a half in circumference, what is obtained? // 13 //

body.text:
nyāsaḥ ã 4 3
  6 5
  5 9
  2
  5 0
  2

labdham kuḍuvaḥ 1, setikā 1, mānakau 2, ardhamānakam
1
2 |
  evam navarāsyādiṣu yojyāḥ |
body.translated_text: Result: 1 <s>kuḍuva</s>, 1 <s>setikā</s>, 2 <s>mānakas</s>, and half a <s>mānaka</s> 1/2. Similarly, in the Rule of Nine and others, [the method] is to be applied.

body.text: vyastatrairāśikam
body.translated_text: The inverse Rule of Three

body.text: vyastatrairāśikam api etat eva | tatra guṇakārabhāgahāraviparyāse viśeṣaḥ | tat yathā ã
body.translated_text: The inverse Rule of Three is this very [procedure]. There, the distinction is in the inversion of multiplier and divisor. Namely:

body.text: uddeśakaḥ
body.translated_text: Problem:

body.text: pañcasauvarṇike pale dṛṣṭāni ṣoḍaśā palāni suvarṇasya yadā tadā catussauvarṇike kiyanti iti || 14 ||
body.translated_text: When in gold of five [parts purity per] <s>pala</s>, sixteen <s>palas</s> of gold are seen, then in gold of four [parts purity], how many? // 14 //

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã 5 16 4
body.translated_text: Layout: 5, 16, 4

body.text: atra pañcasauvarṇikena palena ṣoḍaśa palāni iti pañcabhiḥ ṣoḍaśa guṇitāḥ suvarṇāḥ bhavanti | ete suvarṇāḥ caturbhiḥ hrṭāḥ catussauvarṇikapalāni bhavanti | evam labdhāni palāni 20 |
body.translated_text: Here, in gold of five-[part] purity per <s>pala</s>, there are sixteen <s>palas</s> — so five times sixteen gives the [total] gold[-value]. This gold[-value] divided by four gives the <s>palas</s> of four-[part] purity. Thus the result is 20 <s>palas</s>.

body.text: svasiddhānte ca yadi vyāsārdhamaṇḍale bhujāphalam idam labhyate tadā tatkālotpannakarṇaviṣkambhārdhamaṇḍale kim iti tatra mahati karṇapramāṇe alpīyasyaḥ [ bhujāphalakalā ] bhavanti, alpakarṇe vahvyaḥ iti vyāsārdham guṇakāraḥ [ karṇaḥ bhāgahāraḥ ] |
body.translated_text: And in his own system (<s>svasiddhānta</s>), if this corrective result (<s>bhujāphala</s>) is obtained in the circle with the semi-diameter, then in the circle with the semi-diameter equal to the hypotenuse (<s>karṇa</s>) produced at that time, what [is the result]? — since in that larger hypotenuse measure, the corrective arc-minutes are smaller...

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Example:

children.translated_text: Eight baskets are observed with a measure of fourteen <s>prasṛtis</s> [per basket];

children.text: aṣṭaprasṛtikamāne piṭakāḥ ke syuḥ tadā vācyāḥ || 15 ||
children.translated_text: how many baskets would there be with a measure of eight <s>prasṛtis</s>? State that. // 15 //

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã 8 14 8
body.translated_text: Notation: 8, 14, 8.

body.text: labdham piṭakāḥ 14 || 26-27 ||
body.translated_text: The result: baskets = 14. // 26–27 //

body.text: kalāsavarṇanam
body.translated_text: Reduction of fractions to a common denominator

body.text: kalāsavarṇoddeśapradarśanārtham āryāpaścārdham āha ã
body.translated_text: In order to illustrate the operation of reducing fractions to a common denominator (<s>kalāsavarṇa</s>), he states the latter half of the <s>āryā</s>:

body.text: chedaguṇam sacchedam parasparam tat savarṇatvam || 27 ||
body.translated_text: Multiplied by the [other's] denominator, [each fraction] with its denominator — mutually — that is [called] reduction to a common form (<s>savarṇatva</s>). // 27 //

body.text: saha chedena vartate iti sacchedam | kim tat ? rāśirūpam | atra sacchedam rāśirūpam vinyasya etat ucyate ã "chedaguṇam sacchedam parasparam" iti | chedaḥ guṇaḥ yasya rāśirūpasya tadrāśirūpam chedaguṇam | parasparam anyonyam, ekena rāśicchedena itaraḥ rāśiḥ sacchedaḥ guṇyate, itareṇa api itaraḥ [ rāśiḥ tadvat vinyastaḥ ] | tat savarṇatvam, tat eva nirvartitam karma savarṇatvam | savarṇakayoḥ yathā iṣṭam saṃyogaḥ viśleṣaḥ ca |
body.translated_text: That which exists together with a denominator (<s>cheda</s>) is 'with its denominator' (<s>saccheda</s>). What is that? The quantity in question (<s>rāśirūpa</s>). Here, having set down the quantity with its denominator, this is stated: 'multiplied by the denominator, with its denominator, mutually.' That quantity whose multiplier is the [other's] denominator...

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Example:

children.translated_text: One-half, one-sixth, one-twelfth, combined with one-fourth —

children.text: ekatra kiyat dravyam nirdeśyam tatkrameṇa eva || 1 ||
children.translated_text: how much is the total sum? It is to be stated in that very order. // 1 //

body.text:
nyāsaḥ ã 1 1 1 1
  2 6 12 4

karaṇam ã dvayoḥ
1 1
2 6,
etau parasparacchedena guṇitau sacchedau rāśī
  6 2
12 12 |
ekatra
2
3 |
punar tṛtīyarāsinā sthāpanā
2 1
3 12,
prakṣiptena
[ 3 ]
[ 4 ] |
evam caturtharāśinā
3 1
4 4, labdham rūpakam 1 |
body.translated_text: Computation: Of the two [fractions] 1/2 and 1/6, multiplied mutually by each other's denominator, the quantities with denominators [become] 6/12 and 2/12. Together: 2/3. Again, setting down with the third quantity: 2/3 and 1/12, added [gives] 3/4. Similarly with the fourth quantity...

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: ardham ṣaṣṭham bhāgam tṛtīyakena sahitam kiyat dravyam |
children.translated_text: One-half, one-sixth, combined with one-third — how much is the total?

children.text: ardham ṣaṣṭhaḥ dvādaśakaḥ viṃśaḥ sapañcabhāgaḥ ca || 2 ||
children.translated_text: One-half, one-sixth, one-twelfth, one-twentieth, and one-fifth. // 2 //

body.text:
nyāsaḥ ã 1 1 1
  2 6 3

dvitīyoddeśake sthāpanā ã
  1 1 1 1 1
  2 6 12 20 5
body.translated_text: For the second example, the setting down: 1/2, 1/6, 1/12, 1/20, 1/5.

body.text: labdham pūrvakaraṇena ubhayatraikarāśikam rūpam 1, 1 |
body.translated_text: The result by the previous computation: in both cases, the total is unity [= 1, 1].

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: ardham ṣaḍbhāgonam pañcāṃśam ca api saptabhāgonam |
children.translated_text: One-half diminished by one-sixth, and one-fifth diminished by one-seventh,

children.text: tryaṃśam pādonam vā gaṇayate [ gaṇakāḥ ] kiyat dravyam || 3 ||
children.translated_text: or one-third diminished by one-fourth — how much do the mathematicians compute? // 3 //

body.text:
nyāsaḥ ã 1 1í 1 1í 11í
  2 6 5 734

labdham yathākrameṇa ã1 2 1
  3 3512
body.translated_text: The results in order: 1/3, 2/35, 1/12.

body.text: viparītakarma
body.translated_text: Inverse operations

body.text: pratilomakaraṇapradarśanārtham āha ã
body.translated_text: In order to demonstrate the reverse computation (<s>pratilomakaraṇa</s>), he says:

children.text: guṇakārāḥ bhāgaharāḥ bhāgaharāḥ te bhavanti guṇakārāḥ |
children.translated_text: Multipliers become divisors; divisors become multipliers;

children.text: yaḥ kṣepaḥ saḥ apacayaḥ apacayaḥ kṣepaḥ ca viparīte || 28 ||
children.translated_text: what was additive becomes subtractive; and what was subtractive becomes additive — in the inverse [operation]. // 28 //

body.text: guṇakārāḥ bhāgaharāḥ, ye guṇakārāḥ āsan te pratilomakramaṇi [bhāgahārāḥ bhavanti] | bhāgaharāḥ te bhavanti guṇakārāḥ, [ye] bhāgahārāḥ te guṇakārāḥ bhavanti | yaḥ kṣepaḥ saḥ apacayaḥ, pūrvam yaḥ kṣepaḥ āsīt sa vilomakarmaṇi apacayaḥ bhavati | apacayaḥ kṣepaḥ ca, yaḥ apacayaḥ sa kṣepaḥ viparītakarmaṇi bhavati |
body.translated_text: Multipliers become divisors — those which were multipliers, in the reverse procedure, become divisors. Divisors become multipliers — those which were divisors become multipliers. What was additive becomes subtractive...

body.text:
atra ye uddeśakāḥ te prāyaśaḥ pradarśitāḥ | svatantre api ca chāyānītaśaṅkoḥ ghaṭikānayanam prati vyāsārdham bhāgahāraḥ āsīt iti guṇakāraḥ, lambakaḥ guṇakāraḥ āsīt iti bhāgahāraḥ | tatra uttaragole [kṣitijyā kṣipe] dityapanīyate, dakṣiṇagole apanayet iti prakṣipyate | tataḥ viparītatvāt eva vyāsārdham guṇakāraḥ, svāhorātrārdham bhāgahāraḥ | labdhajyā viparītakarmaṇā eva kāṣṭhīkriyate | tasmin kāṣṭhe uttaragole caraprāṇāḥ prakṣpyante viśodhitatvāt,
dakṣiṇagole viśodhyante kṣiptatvāt iti ādi | evam sarvatra svatantre viparītakarma niyojyam |
body.translated_text: Here, the examples for this have been mostly shown [already]. And independently too: in [the computation of] the <s>ghaṭikās</s> (time units) from the gnomon derived from the shadow, the semi-diameter was a divisor, hence [in reverse] it becomes a multiplier; the co-latitude (<s>lambaka</s>) was a multiplier, hence it becomes a divisor...

body.text: anyatra api uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Another example elsewhere:

children.translated_text: Doubled, increased by one, divided by five, multiplied by three again,

children.text: dvyūnam saptavibhaktam labdham rūpam kiyat bhavet pūrvam || 1 ||
children.translated_text: diminished by two, divided by seven — the result is one. What was the original [number]? // 1 //

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã 2 gu, 1 kṣe, 5 hā, 3 gu, 2 ū, 7 hā, saptabhiḥ bhāgalabdham rūpakam 1 |
body.translated_text: Notation: ×2, +1, ÷5, ×3, −2, ÷7. The result from dividing by seven is one [1].

body.text: karaṇam etat ã labdham rūpam 1, saptabhiḥ guṇitam jātam 7, dvābhyām yuktam 9, tribhiḥ bhaktam 3, pañcaguṇam 15, ekonam 14, dalitam labdham 7 |
body.translated_text: The computation is this: the result is 1; multiplied by seven = 7; increased by two = 9; divided by three = 3; multiplied by five = 15; diminished by one = 14; halved, the result = 7.

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: triguṇam rūpavihīnam dalitam dvābhyām samanvitam bhūyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Tripled, diminished by one, halved, increased by two again,

children.text: bhaktam tribhiḥ tu tasmāt dvikahīnam kim bhavet rūpam || 2 ||
children.translated_text: divided by three — then diminished by two — what is the original number? // 2 //

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã 3 gu, 1 ū, 2 hā, 2 kṣe, 3 hā, 2 ū, labdham rūpam 1 |pūrvavat āgatam 5 || 25 ||
body.translated_text: Notation: ×3, −1, ÷2, +2, ÷3, −2. The result is 1. By the previous [method], the answer is 5. // 25 //

body.text: anekavarṇasamīkaraṇaviśeṣaḥ
body.translated_text: Special case of multi-variable equations

body.text: rāśyūnakramasaṅkalitānayanam āha ã
body.translated_text: He states the computation of series with successive subtraction:

children.translated_text: Diminished by a quantity, [again] diminished by a quantity — the wealth [sum] of the terms, aggregated separately,

children.text: vyekena padena hṛtam sarvadhanam tat bhavati evam || 29 ||
children.translated_text: divided by the number of terms less one — that becomes the total wealth. // 29 //

body.text:
rāśinā ūnam rāśyunam | [ rāśyūnam ] rāśyūnam iti anayā vīpsayā anantyam gaṇitakarma pradarśayati | gacchaḥ padam paryavasānam iti paryāyāḥ | gacchasya dhanam gacchadhanam, padadhanam | rāśyūnanyāyena yāvat padam tat gacchadhanam ucyate | piṇḍitam pṛthaktvena | piṇḍitam ekatra kṛtam | pṛthaktvena iti rāśyūnakramalabdhapadānām avinaṣṭasthāpanām pradarśayati | avinaṣṭasthāpanāprayojanam ca sarvadhanam ca sarvadhanāt avinaṣṭasthāpitapadadhane
apanīte pṛthak pṛthak padānām dhanāni bhavanti | yadi kevalam sarvadhanaparijñānamātram eva syāt tadā pṛ(tha)ktvena iti anarthakam syāt, yasmāt apṛthakkaraṇe api sarvadhanasya siddhatvāt | vigatam ekam vyekam, tena vyekena, tena padena ca | vyekaiḥ padaiḥ iti bahuvacanena atra bhavitavyam | na eṣaḥ doṣaḥ | padajātim aṅgīkṛtya "jātyākhyāyām ekasmin bahuvacanam anyatarasyāt" [aṣṭādhyāyī, 1.2.58 ] iti ekavacanam kṛtam | tena yaḥ arthaḥ vyekaiḥ padaiḥ iti
sa eva arthaḥ vyekena padena iti avagamyate | hṛtam bhaktam | sarvadhanam, sarveṣām padānām yathākrameṇa dhanam ekatra tat sarvadhanam ucyate | tat bhavati evam, yat evam kṛte karmaṇi tat sarvadhanam bhavati |
body.translated_text: Diminished by a quantity is '<s>rāśyūna</s>' (decreased by the amount). '<s>Rāśyūna</s>, <s>rāśyūna</s>' — by this repetition (<s>vīpsā</s>), he indicates an infinite computational procedure. The term (<s>gaccha</s>), the step (<s>pada</s>), and the conclusion (<s>paryavasāna</s>) are synonyms. The wealth of the terms is '<s>gacchadhana</s>' (term-wealth), [also called] <s>padadhana</s> (step-wealth)...

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Example:

children.translated_text: Herds of elephants in the forest, consisting of rutting, non-rutting, and female elephants with young —

children.text: ekāpāyacayena [ ye atra ] gaṇitāḥ triṃśat rasānām kṛtiḥ |
children.translated_text: counted with a decrease of one at each step, thirty [is] the square of the flavors [= 36],

children.text: saptānām api sā eva ca ekasahitā nāgāgram āgaṇyatām
children.translated_text: of seven also, that same [expression] plus one — let the number of lead-elephants be computed,

children.text: yūthānām ca pṛthak pṛthaktvagaṇitam nirvarṇyatām tattvataḥ || 1 ||
children.translated_text: and the count of each herd separately should be determined accurately. // 1 //

body.text: karaṇam ã etāni dhanāni avinaṣṭāni ekatra 165 | vyekam padam 3 | anena labdham sarvadhanam 55 | etasmāt prathamapadam apāsya mattāgram 25, dvitīyam apāsya amattasaṅkhyā 19, tṛtīyam apāsya kareṇusaṅkhyā 6, caturtham apāsya vikkasaṅkhyā 5 |
body.translated_text: Computation: These undiminshed sums combined together [= 165]. The number of terms less one = 3. Dividing by this gives the total = 55. From this, subtracting the first term gives the lead-elephant count = 25; subtracting the second gives the non-rutting count = 19; subtracting the third...

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Example:

children.translated_text: Elephants, horses, donkeys, camels, mules, and cattle — each diminished by one in order —
twenty-eight, counted with a decrease of one, the last diminished by one again;

children.text: teṣām sarvadhanam pṛthak ca niyamāt vācyam tvayā niścitam
children.translated_text: their total wealth and each separately must be stated by you with certainty,

children.text: kṛtsnam ca āryabhaṭapraṇītagaṇitam dṛṣṭam guroḥ antike || 2 ||
children.translated_text: [if] the entire mathematics composed by <s>Āryabhaṭa</s> has been studied in the presence of a teacher. // 2 //

body.text: nyāsaḥ ã 28, 27, 26, 25, 24, 23, 21 | labdham sarvadhanam 29 | pṛthak pṛthak 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8 || 29 ||
body.translated_text: Notation: 28, 27, 26, 25, 24, 23, 21. The total obtained = 29. Separately: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8. // 29 //

body.text: ekavarṇasamīkaraṇam
body.translated_text: Simple linear equations

body.text: samakaraṇoddeśakapradarśanārtham āha ã
body.translated_text: In order to demonstrate examples of simple equations (<s>samakaraṇa</s>), he says:

children.text: gulikāntareṇa vibhajet dvayoḥ puruṣayoḥ tu rūpakaviśeṣam |
children.translated_text: Divide the difference in coins (<s>rūpaka</s>) of two persons by the difference in the number of pellets (<s>gulikā</s>);

children.text: labdham gulikāmūlyam yadi arthakṛtam bhavati tulyam || 30 ||
children.translated_text: the result is the price of one pellet — when the [total] expenditure is made equal. // 30 //

body.text:
gulikāśabdena avijñātamūlyavastvabhidhīyate | gulikānām antaram gulikāntaram tena gulikāntareṇa, avijñātamūlyavastūnām antareṇa iti arthaḥ | vibhajet dvayoḥ puruṣayoḥ tu rūpakaviśeṣam | dvayoḥ iti anena dvayoḥ eva idam karma na tryādīnām iti etat pradarśayati | rūpakaviśeṣam iti anena ca nirjñātasaṅkhyam dhanam parigṛhyate | rūpakam dīnārādikam | labdham gulikāmūlyam, yat atra labdham tat gulikāmūlyam | yadi arthakṛtam bhavati tulyam, yena
arthena kṛtam tat tulyam sadṛśam bhavati |
body.translated_text: By the word '<s>gulikā</s>' (pellet), an object of unknown price is meant. The difference between pellets is '<s>gulikāntara</s>' — by that difference in the objects of unknown price — this is the meaning. Divide the difference in coins of the two persons...

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: aśvāḥ lakṣaṇayuktāḥ vaṇijaḥ nityam balānvitāḥ sapta |
children.translated_text: Horses endowed with [good] marks — a merchant, always accompanied by strength, [has] seven;

children.text: prathamasya mayā dṛṣṭam dravyaśatam ca eva hastagatam ||
children.translated_text: I have seen the first one's property — a hundred coins exactly in hand.

children.text: nava turagāḥ nirdṛṣṭāḥ dravyāśītiḥ dhanam dvitīyasya |
children.translated_text: Nine horses are seen, and eighty coins are the wealth of the second.
State the price of each horse — when with equal expenditure they have equal wealth. // 1 //

body.text:
nyāsaḥ ã 7 100
  9 80
body.translated_text: Notation: 7 [horses], 100 [coins]; 9 [horses], 80 [coins].

body.text: karaṇam ã gulikāntaram 2, rūpakaviśeṣam 20, etat gulikāntareṇa vibhaktam ghoṭakasya ekasya mūlyadravyam daśa 10 | anena ardheṇa prathamasya ghoṭakānām mūlyam 70, dvitīyasya 90, [sva]svahastagatena anena [ca] gatau tulyadhanau 170 ubhayoḥ api |
body.translated_text: Computation: Difference in pellets [horses] = 2. Difference in coins = 20. This divided by the difference in pellets gives the price of one horse = ten [10]. With this value, the first person's horse-cost = 70, the second's = 90...

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: kuṅkumapalāni ca aṣṭau ekasya dhanasya rūpakā navatiḥ |
children.translated_text: Eight <s>palas</s> of saffron for one person with ninety coins;

children.text: dvādaśa palāni vidyāt anyasya dhanasya rūpakāḥ triṃśat ||
children.translated_text: twelve <s>palas</s> for another person with thirty coins.

children.text: tulyārdheṇa ca krītam kuṅkumam dvābhyām kiyat palārdheṇa |
children.translated_text: Purchased with equal shares by both — how many <s>palas</s> at what price per half-<s>pala</s>?

children.text: icchāmi tatra boddhum mūlyam vittam ca tulyam eva tayoḥ || 2 ||
children.translated_text: I wish to know the price and the wealth, which is equal for both. // 2 //

body.text:
nyāsaḥ ã 8 90
  12 30
body.translated_text: Notation: 8 [palas], 90 [coins]; 12 [palas], 30 [coins].

body.text: labdham pūrvavat kuṅkumapalasya ekasya mūlyam 15 | tulyadhanam 210 ubhayoḥ |
body.translated_text: The result as before: the price of one <s>pala</s> of saffron = 15. Equal wealth = 210 for both.

body.translated_text: 'Divided' — meaning: when the quotient is taken. 'Retrograde-interval' (<s>vilomavivara</s>) — one goes [forward] while the other comes back in the opposite direction — that is the retrograde-interval, [i.e.,] the difference between the direct motion and the retrograde motion. Here the word 'direct' (<s>anuloma</s>) is to be understood as indicated by elision. Alternatively, the retrograde-interval is taken as being of precisely this nature: if both were retrograde, then it would simply be a direct-interval. That retrograde-interval is divided. By what? He says: 'By the sum of the velocities.' The sum of the [two] velocities is the 'velocity-sum'; by that velocity-sum. 'Direct-interval' (<s>anulomavivara</s>) — the interval between the two direct motions. 'Two' makes a subsequent portion for both the retrograde and direct conjunction-times. 'By the difference of the velocities' — the difference of the velocities is the 'velocity-difference,' [i.e.,] the excess of velocities; by that velocity-difference. 'The two conjunction-times obtained' — the conjunction of two is the 'bi-conjunction'; the times of the bi-conjunction are the 'bi-conjunction-times.' 'Past and future' — past means elapsed; future means forthcoming. As follows: When one planet, situated ahead, is retrograde, [and] the other, situated behind, moves with direct motion — the minutes of their interval constitute the retrograde-interval. There, since the conjunction of the one moving directly and the other coming back in retrograde will occur in a short time, the quotient is taken by the sum of their daily motions, since that is their daily consumption. With that, the rule of three is performed: If by this daily motion, one day is obtained, then by this retrograde-interval, how much? — thus days or <s>ghaṭikās</s> (time-units) are obtained. That much time — in a past conjunction it is 'past,' in a future conjunction it is 'future.' There, for the equal-minute procedure, [one applies] the rule of three with the daily motion: If by sixty <s>ghaṭikās</s>, the true daily motion of the planet is obtained, then by the <s>ghaṭikās</s> generated from the retrograde [computation], what motion [is obtained]? The result, for the direct-moving planet, is added [to its position]; for the retrograde-mover, subtracted. Thus the two planets, at equal minutes, come to exist at the desired time. Now, when the retrograde-mover is behind and the direct-mover is ahead, then the result is added to the retrograde-mover, since [the conjunction] has passed, and subtracted from the direct-mover, also since it has passed. But when both are moving directly, the quotient of the direct-interval is taken by the velocity-difference, since the daily velocity-difference is equal to the excess of velocities. Then, from this velocity-difference — the excess of daily motions — sixty <s>nāḍīs</s> are obtained; then by the direct-interval, how many <s>ghaṭikās</s>? — [these] are obtained. With those [<s>ghaṭikās</s>] and the true daily motion of the planet, the rule of three: If by sixty, the true daily motion is obtained, then by these <s>ghaṭikās</s>, what? The result — when the faster is behind — both [corrections] are added to their respective [positions]; when the faster is ahead, both are subtracted from their respective [positions]. Thus the two conjunction-times, past and future, are obtained. And when both are retrograde, the same procedure applies. This very procedure was stated by us in the <s>Karmanibandha</s>:

children.translated_text: The interval between the two planets — of the retrograde and the direct-mover —
is to be divided by the sum of the daily motions; or, for the others, by the difference of the daily motions.
The time in days and the like is obtained — the conjunction-maker of the conjoining [planets].

children.text: bhukteḥ anekarūpatvāt sthūlaḥ kālaḥ sa gamyate ||

body.text: kuṭṭākāraḥ
body.translated_text: The Pulverizer (<s>Kuṭṭākāra</s>)

body.text: idānīm kuṭṭākāragaṇitam abhidhīyate | tatra āryāsūtradvayam ã
body.translated_text: Now the <s>kuṭṭākāra</s> (pulverizer) computation is expounded. Therein, two <s>āryā</s> verses:

children.translated_text: Divide the divisor of the greater remainder by the divisor of the lesser remainder;
the mutual division of the remainders — [the last remainder] multiplied by a chosen [number] — is added to or subtracted from the difference of the remainders. // 32 //
Multiplied below-and-above, added to the last — divided by the divisor of the lesser-remainder, the residue,
multiplied by the divisor of the greater-remainder, [added to] the remainder from both divisors, added to the greater-remainder. // 33 //

body.text:
adhikāgrabhāgahāram chindyāt | agram śeṣaḥ | adhikāgram yasya saḥ ayam adhikāgraḥ | adhikāgraḥ ca asau bhāgahāraḥ ca adhikāgrabhāgahāraḥ | tam adhikāgrabhāgahāram, chindyāt vibhajet iti arthaḥ | kena iti āha ã ūnāgrabhāgahāreṇa | śeṣaparasparabhaktam | labdhena na asti prayojanam, śeṣeṇa saha karma kriyate | paraspareṇa bhaktam parasparabhaktam, itaretarabhaktam iti arthaḥ | śeṣeṇa saha parasparabhaktam śeṣaparasparabhaktam | matiguṇam,
svabuddhiguṇam iti arthaḥ | katham punar svabuddhiguṇaḥ kriyate ? ayam rāśiḥ kena guṇitam idam agrāntaram prakṣipya viśodhya vā asya rāśeḥ śuddham bhāgam dāsyati iti | agrāntare kṣiptam | sameṣu kṣiptam viṣameṣu śodhyam iti sampradāyāvicchedāt vyākhyāyate |
body.translated_text: 'Divide the divisor of the greater remainder' — '<s>agra</s>' means remainder. That whose remainder is greater — that is the 'greater-remainder [divisor].' The greater-remainder [divisor] is also a divisor — [hence] the 'divisor of the greater remainder.' That divisor of the greater remainder — divide [it], meaning: take the quotient. By what? He says: 'By the divisor of the lesser remainder.' 'The mutual division of the remainders' — the quotient is not needed; the operation is performed with the remainder. Divided by each other is 'mutually divided,' meaning divided by one another. The remainder mutually divided is 'the mutual division of the remainders.' 'Multiplied by a chosen [number]' (<s>matiguṇam</s>) — meaning: multiplied by one's own intellectual choice. But how is the intellectual multiplier chosen? [The criterion is:] 'When this quantity is multiplied by what [number], and the difference of remainders is added or subtracted, it will give a clean quotient when divided by this quantity.' 'Added to or subtracted from the difference of the remainders.' '[Added] in the even [positions], subtracted in the odd' — this is explained through the unbroken tradition.

body.text:
evam paraspareṇa labdhāni padāni avasthāpya, matiḥ ca adhaḥ, paścimalabdham ca matyā adhaḥ | adhupariguṇitam, adhaḥsthitena rāśinā uparirāsiḥ guṇitaḥ | antyayuk, antyena rāśinā paścimalabdhena sahitaḥ | evam bhūyaḥ bhūyaḥ karma yāvat karmaparisamāptim iti | ūnāgracchedabhājite śeṣam, ūnāgrasya yat chedam tena bhājite śeṣam, tena ūnāgracchedena pūrvagaṇitakarmaṇā niṣpannarāśeḥ vibhaktaśeṣam parigṛhyate | adhikāgracchedaguṇam, adhikāgracchedena
abhyastam | dvicchedāgram, dvayoḥ chedayoḥ agram, agram saṅkhyā | adhikāgrayutam, adhikāgreṇa yutam adhikāgrayutam | etat uktam bhavati ã ūnāgracchedabhājite śeṣam adhikāgracchedena abhyastam adhikāgrasahitam tat dvayoḥ api chedayoḥ bhājyarāśiḥ bhavati iti |
body.translated_text: Thus, having placed the quotients obtained by mutual [division] in a column, and the chosen multiplier (<s>mati</s>) below, and the last quotient below the <s>mati</s>: 'Multiplied below-and-above' — the quantity below multiplies the quantity above. 'Added to the last' — combined with the last quantity, the last quotient. Thus, the operation is repeated until the completion of the procedure. 'Divided by the divisor of the lesser-remainder, the residue' — the residue when divided by the divisor of the lesser remainder; that is, the residue obtained from dividing the quantity produced by the previous computational procedure by the divisor of the lesser-remainder is taken. 'Multiplied by the divisor of the greater-remainder' — multiplied by the divisor of the greater remainder. 'The remainder from both divisors' — the remainder from both divisors; the remainder being the number. 'Added to the greater-remainder' — combined with the greater-remainder. What this says is: The residue obtained by dividing by the divisor of the lesser-remainder, multiplied by the divisor of the greater-remainder, and combined with the greater-remainder — that becomes the dividend for both divisors.

body.text: evam sāgrakuṭṭākāraḥ vyākhyātaḥ | niragrakuṭṭākāraḥ api uttaratra vakṣyati |
body.translated_text: Thus the <s>kuṭṭākāra</s> (pulverizer) with remainders (<s>sāgra</s>) has been explained. The pulverizer without remainders (<s>niragra</s>) too will be stated further on.

body.translated_text: Computation: The divisor of the greater-remainder is seven, 7; dividing by the divisor of the lesser-remainder, five, 5 — the remainder: above, two, 2; below, five, 5. Since the quantity is small, the chosen multiplier is assigned here itself. This quantity above — multiplied by what, and adding the remainder-difference of one, will give a clean quotient when divided by five? — the chosen multiplier obtained: two coins. The quotient: one, 1; the remainder: 0. Its arrangement: 2 / 1. Since a third column-entry is not possible, this itself has been produced. 'Divided by the divisor of the lesser-remainder, the residue': 2; 'multiplied by the divisor of the greater-remainder' (seven): 14; 'added to the greater-remainder' [2]: 16. This is the remainder from both divisors. This very quantity, when divided by five, has remainder one; when divided by seven, has remainder two.

body.translated_text: Computation: 'Divide the divisor of the greater-remainder by the divisor of the lesser-remainder' — the remainder: above, seven; below, twelve. These mutually divided — quotient one, then again one; remainder: above, two; below, five. Here [is] the chosen multiplier. Since the column-entries are even: 'this quantity, multiplied by what, and adding the remainder-difference of two, will give a clean quotient when divided by five?' — the result: the chosen multiplier is four. That [is placed] below the previous quotient. And the quotient is two — this result is placed below. 'Multiplied below-and-above, added to the last' — by this rule, the result is 10. This very [quantity] — 'divided by the divisor of the lesser-remainder, the residue, multiplied by the divisor of the greater-remainder': 310; 'added to the greater-remainder — the remainder from both divisors' — and that is 317.

apavartitabhāgahāraśeṣam iti arthaḥ | kuṭṭākāraḥ bhavati iti vākyaśeṣaḥ | upari [rāsiḥ] bhāgahāreṇa bhaktaḥ [kāryaḥ] adhorāśiḥ bhājyarāśinā bhājyaḥ | gaṇite api uktam ã
body.translated_text: Now we shall explain the same <s>sūtra</s> for the purpose of the remainder-free <s>kuṭṭākāra</s>. 'One should divide the larger-remainder divisor' — meaning: one should reduce it. By what? He says: by the smaller-remainder divisor. '<s>Agra</s>' means 'number'; what is smaller is that number, and that smaller number is also the divisor — hence 'smaller-remainder divisor'; by that smaller-remainder divisor [one should] reduce — this is the meaning. For example, twenty-one is reduced by seven. By whatever [factor] the divisor is reduced, by that same [factor] the dividend too must be reduced. How is it understood that by the very [factor] by which the divisor is reduced, the dividend too must be reduced? From the unbroken tradition of teaching. Alternatively, this is a principle: the reduced divisor must have a correspondingly reduced dividend — just as twenty-one parts reduced by seven become three parts. Alternatively, by the master's saying 'reducing the divisor,' the reduction of the dividend too is indeed stated. Why? Because the divisor and dividend always go together. Just as when one says 'sweep the terraces,' the walkways too are swept. By the text beginning with 'the larger-remainder divisor,' this is taught: the <s>kuṭṭākāra</s> is [to be performed] on the reduced divisor and dividend. 'The remainders [are] mutually divided' — the divisor and dividend [are] mutually divided. 'Multiplied by an assumed [number]' — this is the same as before. 'Added to the difference of remainders' — '<s>agra</s>' means 'number'; the difference of the numbers is 'the difference of remainders,' meaning the difference of quantities. And that is determined at will — adding or subtracting this difference of quantities will give an exact quotient for this quantity. 'The lower multiplied by the upper plus the last term' — all this is the same as before. 'The remainder when divided by the smaller-remainder denominator' — meaning the remainder when divided by the reduced-divisor and dividend. The <s>kuṭṭākāra</s> and quotient result — this is the completion of the sentence. 'The upper [quantity] divided by the divisor, [and] the lower quantity divided by the dividend.' It has also been stated in the mathematical [text]:

body.text: upari ca bhāgahāreṇa bhakte hi rāśiḥ bhavet vā |
body.translated_text: When the upper [quantity] is divided by the divisor, the quantity results.

body.translated_text: Now, if someone, referring to the Sun on a Sunday, asks 'After how much time will the Sun be in this [same position] on a Sunday, on a Monday, or on another planet's weekday?' — that is as follows: The <s>kuṭṭākāra</s> is performed on the remainders left after dividing the unreduced terrestrial days by seven. The weekday that is specified — the planet-weekday that is later than that [specified weekday] — starting from that, one postulates a decrease by successive increments of one. The <s>kuṭṭākāra</s> thus obtained is the multiplier of the unreduced terrestrial days. Having multiplied the unreduced terrestrial days by that [multiplier], and adding the day-count obtained with the specified Sun [position], the time equal to the resulting number of days should be announced. That is as follows:

body.translated_text: Now, if someone asks thus: 'The Sun and Moon are such-and-such quantities on a Sunday or Monday. After how much time will these two be exactly those same quantities?' — here, the procedure of the <s>kuṭṭākāra</s> is: Some quantity, when divided by the unreduced terrestrial days of the Sun, has zero remainder; and for the Moon too, [that same quantity] has zero remainder. In this problem, the connection of the two is the <s>dviccheda-agra-samvarga</s> (product of the two divisor-remainders), which is the 'equalization' of the quantity. Here, the unreduced days of the Sun, reduced by 3449, give the result 61; and the [unreduced days] of the Moon, reduced by that same [factor], yield 625. Then, the reduced lunar days become the multiplier of the Sun's unreduced days — and those are written here. When multiplied, the result is 131,493,125; and for the Moon too, when multiplied by the Sun's reduced days, the result is 131,493,125. By this quantity, the planetary <s>kuṭṭākāra</s> should be applied as before. That is as follows:

children.translated_text: To <s>Śambhu</s> (Śiva) — whose body is the source of the Sun, whose brilliance equals ten thousand suns,
who is the cause of the creation and destruction of the world — obeisance! // 1 //

body.translated_text: These planetary <s>kuṭṭākāras</s> are also composed in verses. Namely:

children.text: kuṭṭākāraḥ ca lābhaḥ ca dvandvataḥ bhagaṇāt itaḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>kuṭṭākāra</s> (pulverizer) and the result (<s>lābha</s>), in pairs from the revolutions onward,

children.text: nirdiśyate kramāt atra tadvidām prītaye mayā || 2 ||
children.translated_text: are stated here in order by me, for the delight of the learned. // 2 //

the result produced from the revolutions is nine-arrow-twin [= 259].
From the signs: <s>Vasu</s>-mountain-void, qualities, <s>Śiva</s>-s [= 113078];
the result would be: arrow-moon, mountain-<s>Rāma</s>-number [= 3715]. // 3 //

<s>Veda</s>-horse-serpent-fire-mountain-fire-<s>Veda</s> [= 4,373,824];
five-moon-<s>Rāma</s>-horse-quality-limb-serpent-
eye-ocean-world [= 3,428,632,315] — indeed that is the quotient there. (76)
The multiplier-quantity for the seconds (<s>viliptikā</s>)
is equal to seven-fire-serpent-fire-moon [= 13,837];
<s>Nanda</s>-mountain-serpent-tone-zero-serpent-
zero-arrow-six [= 650,807,879] is the equal quotient here. (77)
The observed multiplier — the third-seconds quotient —
is of the measure zero-eight-serpent-fire-sun [= 123,880];
<s>Rudra</s>-sky-mountain-limb-square-fire-hole-
arrow-digit-<s>Veda</s>, with the multiplier, is the quotient [= 34,959,346,011]. (78)
Of the fourth-seconds (<s>pratatpara</s>), <s>Jina</s>-fire-<s>Aśvin</s>-
<s>Śakra</s> [= 142,324] is the multiplier; there the quotient-quantity is
form-arrow-<s>Aśvin</s>-digit-<s>Vasu</s>-tone-horse-
serpent-arrow-serpent-digit-sky-<s>Jina</s> [= 24,098,582,789,251]. (79)
The reduction factor should be known as twelve [12] for the revolutions and signs;

children.text: bhāgādīnām kramāt chedāḥ pañca [5] dṛṣṭāḥ kramāt budhaiḥ || 80 ||
children.translated_text: for the degrees and following, the reduction factors are seen as five [5] in order, by the learned. (80)

body.text: adhidivasasya
body.translated_text: Of the intercalary day (<s>adhidivasa</s>)

children.translated_text: The surplus multiplier is equal to hole-zero-arrow-<s>Aśvin</s>-mountain-six [= 672,509];
the quotient-quantity, in order, is sky-seven-limb-sky-<s>Aśvin</s> [= 20,670]. (81)

body.text: avamadivasasya
body.translated_text: Of the omitted day (<s>avamadivasa</s>)

children.translated_text: Moon-fire-sky-seven-ocean-<s>Yama</s>-six [= 6,247,031] — the omission multiplier;
the quotient too is declared as nine-<s>Veda</s>-mountain-mountain-hole [= 97,749]. (82)

body.text: sūryāpakramasya
body.translated_text: Of the Sun's declination (<s>sūryāpakrama</s>)

children.translated_text: Of the declination, the multiplier is, in order, seven-ocean-lotus [= 347];
the quotient-quantity seen, in order, is form-<s>Veda</s>-moon [= 141]. (83)

body.text: adhimāsasya
body.translated_text: Of the intercalary month (<s>adhimāsa</s>)

children.translated_text: By the <s>yuga</s>-intercalary months, sage-moon-world-
sky-sky-digit-<s>Dhṛti</s>s [= 18,900,317] — [these are] observed.
The multiplicand here — the quotient too — arrow-eight-zero-
nine-moon [= 19,085] — in these revolutions, always. (84)
Cold-rayed-hole-fire-sky-<s>Śiva</s>-horse-
sun [= 122,110,391] is the equal multiplier-quantity;
world-ocean-six-<s>Nanda</s>-sage-<s>Indra</s> [= 1,479,643] in number —
the quotient here, indeed, derived from the signs. (85)
Flavor-fire-<s>Vasu</s>-ocean-fire-seven-
<s>Veda</s>-horse [= 24,734,836] would be the multiplier-quantity;
form-arrow-element-one-nine-digit-serpent [= 8,991,551] —
the quotient, in order, established by the degree-operation. (86)
<s>Vasu</s>-mountain-<s>Veda</s>-<s>Indra</s>-elephant-fire [= 3,814,478] in number —
seen in the minutes as the multiplier-quantity;
<s>Nanda</s>-moon-serpent-mountain-nine-one-world-
serpent [= 83,197,819] in measure — they declare the quotient. (87)
<s>Nanda</s>-ocean-five-horse-<s>Manu</s> [= 142,549] in measure —
seen as the achievement of the second-multiplier;
<s>Rudra</s>-mountain-correction-arrow-limb-serpent-
cold-rayed [= 186,548,711] — they declare the gain. (88)
And the number of the multiplier for the thirds (<s>tatpara</s>)
is flavors-sky-limb-ocean-fire-moon [= 134,606];
world-eight-six-<s>Nanda</s>-fire-<s>Aśvin</s>-
hole-limb-arrow, with direction [= 10,569,239,683] — the quotient. (89)
From the fourths (<s>pratatpara</s>), the quantity declared as the multiplier
is sun-square-fire-<s>Nanda</s> [= 93,412];
one-fire-element-eight-king-serpent-
sky-cloud-<s>Veda</s>-ocean [= 440,081,638,531] is the equal gain here. (90)
For the revolutions and signs, twelve [12] alone is the reduction factor;

children.text: pañca [5] pañca eva [5] śeṣāṇām chedaḥ asmin apavartane || 91 ||
children.translated_text: five [5] and five [5] are the reduction factors for the remaining [units] in this reduction. (91)

body.text:
iti bhāskarasya kṛtau āryabhaṭatantrabhāṣye
gaṇitapādaḥ samāptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus, in the composition of <s>Bhāskara</s>, in the commentary on the treatise of <s>Āryabhaṭa</s>, the <s>Gaṇitapāda</s> (chapter on mathematics) is completed.

body.text: Kālakriyāpādaḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Kālakriyāpāda</s> (Chapter on the Reckoning of Time)

body.text: maṅgalācaraṇam
body.translated_text: Invocation of auspiciousness

children.translated_text: Sun-Moon-Space-Fire-Wind-Water-Earth-Consecrated — [thus] named,
the eight-formed [<s>Śiva</s>], whose nature is the welfare of all worlds,

children.text: yaḥ abhūt svayam hi karuṇātanuḥ aprameyaḥ
children.translated_text: who of his own accord became [all this], compassionate in body, immeasurable —
to him, <s>Śiva</s>, obeisance — for the sustenance of the three worlds.

body.text: kālavibhāgaḥ kṣetravibhāgaḥ ca
body.translated_text: Division of time and division of space

body.text:
atha gaṇitānantaram kālakriyā prastūyate | atha kaḥ kālaḥ, kā vā kriyā? atra kecit vadanti ã "kriyāvyatiriktaḥ kālaḥ" | apare ã "kriyā kālaḥ" iti | kriyāvyatiriktaḥ astu kālaḥ [kriyā vā], kim etena | asmākam tu sūryācandramasoḥ yaḥ paraḥ viprakarṣaḥ saḥ ardhamāsaḥ | yaḥ ca tayoḥ sannikarṣaḥ sa māsaḥ | evam dvādaśa māsāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ iti ādi kālaḥ | kriyā vyāpāraḥ | kālasya kriyā kālakriyā | kālaparijñānārthā kriyā iti yāvat | sā ca kriyā gatiḥ | tayā kriyayā
kālaḥ jñāyate iti etat pratipādayiṣyati | tat yathā ã
body.translated_text: Now, after mathematics, the reckoning of time (<s>kālakriyā</s>) is introduced. Now, what is time (<s>kāla</s>), and what is action (<s>kriyā</s>)? Here, some say: 'Time is distinct from action.' Others [say]: 'Action is time.' Let time be distinct from action or [identical with] action — what does it matter? For us, the maximum separation of the Sun and Moon is a half-month (<s>ardhamāsa</s>). And their [maximum] proximity is a month (<s>māsa</s>). Thus, twelve months constitute a year (<s>saṃvatsara</s>) — and so on [is] time. Action (<s>kriyā</s>) is operation. The action of time is <s>kālakriyā</s> — the action for the purpose of knowing time, that is to say. And that action is motion (<s>gati</s>). He will teach that time is known through that action. Namely:

children.text: varṣam dvādaśamāsāḥ triṃśaddivasaḥ bhavet sa māsaḥ tu |
children.translated_text: A year is twelve months; a month would be thirty days;

children.text: ṣaṣṭiḥ nāḍyaḥ divasaḥ ṣaṣṭiḥ ca vināḍikā nāḍī || 1 ||
children.translated_text: a day is sixty <s>nāḍīs</s> (time-units); and a <s>nāḍī</s> is sixty <s>vināḍikās</s> (sub-units). (1)

body.text:
varṣam abdaḥ samāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ iti paryāyāḥ | ayam varṣaśabdaḥ napuṃsakaliṅgaḥ samāyām vartate | tasya varṣasya pramāṇam dvādaśa māsāḥ | dvau ca daśa ca dvādaśa | māsāḥ saṃvatsarasya śākhāḥ | triṃśaddivasaḥ bhavet sa māsaḥ tu | triṃśat saṅkhyā | divasāḥ dināni ahāni iti paryāyāḥ | bhavet syāt | sa yaḥ asau māsaḥ abhihitaḥ saḥ trimśaddivasaḥ iti arthaḥ | ṣaṣṭiḥ nāḍyaḥ divasaḥ | tasya divasasya ekasya pramāṇam ṣaṣṭiḥ nāḍyaḥ | nāḍyaḥ ghaṭikāḥ | ṣaṣṭiḥ
ca vināḍikā nāḍī | tasyāḥ nāḍyāḥ pramāṇam vināḍyaḥ ṣaṣṭiḥ | vināḍyaḥ vighaṭikāḥ |
body.translated_text: '<s>Varṣa</s>' (year), '<s>abda</s>,' '<s>samā</s>,' '<s>saṃvatsara</s>' — these are synonyms. This word '<s>varṣa</s>' is in the neuter gender when referring to a year. The measure of that year is twelve months. Two and ten make twelve. Months are the branches of a year. 'A month would be thirty days' — thirty is the number. 'Days' (<s>divasāḥ</s>), 'days' (<s>dināni</s>), 'days' (<s>ahāni</s>) — these are synonyms. 'Would be' (<s>bhavet</s>) means 'is.' That very month which was mentioned — that is [made of] thirty days, this is the meaning. 'A day is sixty <s>nāḍīs</s>' — the measure of one day is sixty <s>nāḍīs</s>. <s>Nāḍīs</s> are <s>ghaṭikās</s> (water-clock units). 'And a <s>nāḍī</s> is sixty <s>vināḍikās</s>' — the measure of that <s>nāḍī</s> is sixty <s>vināḍīs</s>. <s>Vināḍīs</s> are <s>vighaṭikās</s>.

body.text:
atra ucyate ã "varṣam dvādaśa māsāḥ" iti ādi na ārabdhavyam, lokaprasiddhatvāt | sarveṣu eva ayam nyāyaḥ lokavedaprasiddhyā aṅgīkaraṇīyaḥ | "varṣam dvādaśamāsāḥ" iti ādi vinā api lakṣaṇena lokaḥ jānīte, tathā ca bhṛtakebhyaḥ bhuktavetanam dadāti | yadi lokaprasiddham api abhidhīyate tadā atra bahu vaktavyam jāyate | "nṛṣi yojanam", [gītikāí, 7] "scāṅgulaḥ ghahastaḥ nā" [gītikāí, 8] iti atra
yava-sarṣapa-yūka-likṣā-vālāgra-rathareṇu-trasareṇusthūlasūkṣmaparamāṇūnām pramāṇam vaktavyam | trairāśike ca anekajanapadavyavahārātmikā paribhāṣā vaktavyā | atha yadi api lokaprasiddhiḥ aṅgīkriyate tathā api tu "vargākṣarāṇi varge" [gītikāí, 2] iti atra vargāvargākṣarasvaranirūpaṇam vaktavyam eva | kutaḥ? lokāprasiddheḥ | [yadi evam tadā] vyākaraṇe vargāvargākṣara[svaranirūpaṇam anartha]kam | na eṣa doṣaḥ | lokaḥ pūrvācāryāḥ abāhyaśāstrāṇām
praṇetāraḥ iti uktam | "vargākṣarāṇi varge" [gītikāí, 2] iti atra vargāvargākṣarasvaranirūpaṇāyām vyākaraṇam abāhyam śāstram | "gurvakṣarāṇi ṣaṣṭiḥ vināḍikā" [kālakriyāí, 2] iti atra gurvakṣarāṇām lakṣaṇam vaktavyam | yadi "varṣam dvādaśa māsāḥ" iti ādi granthaḥ na ārabhyate tadā etat sarvam lokaprasiddhyā setsyati | tasmāt apratyāyanam eva astu | na eṣa doṣaḥ | anārabhyamāṇāyām asyām paribhāṣāyām sāvanasya eva mānasya ete bhedāḥ syuḥ na sauracāndranākṣatrāṇām,
yasmāt sāvanam eva ekam mānam lokaprasiddham, na sauracāndranākṣatrāṇi | tat sarveṣu eva māneṣu iyam eva paribhāṣā yathā syāt iti [sūtram ārabdhavyam] |
body.translated_text: Here it is said: 'A year is twelve months' and so forth need not be commenced, because of being well-known to the world. In all cases, this principle should be accepted on the authority of common knowledge and the <s>Vedas</s>. Even without the defining rule 'a year is twelve months' and so forth, the world knows [this], and accordingly pays wages to laborers for work performed. If even what is well-known to the world is stated, then much would have to be said here. In '<s>nṛṣi yojanam</s>' (eight thousand men [make] a <s>yojana</s>) [<s>Gītikā</s> 7], '<s>scāṅgulaḥ ghahastaḥ nā</s>' [<s>Gītikā</s> 8] — here the measures of barleycorn, mustard-seed, louse, nit, hair-tip, chariot-dust, mote, and gross, subtle, and ultimate atoms would have to be stated. And in the rule of three, the conventions of various regions would have to be stated. Now, even if common knowledge is accepted, still, in 'the classified letters in the <s>varga</s> [place]' [<s>Gītikā</s> 2], the specification of <s>varga</s> and <s>avarga</s> letters and vowels must indeed be stated. Why? Because it is not commonly known. [If so, then] in grammar too, the specification of <s>varga</s> and <s>avarga</s> letters and vowels would be pointless. This is not a fault. By 'world' (<s>loka</s>) is meant the earlier teachers — the composers of treatises that are not external [to the tradition]. In 'the classified letters in the <s>varga</s> [place]' [<s>Gītikā</s> 2], for the specification of <s>varga</s> and <s>avarga</s> letters and vowels, grammar is the relevant, non-external treatise. In 'sixty long syllables make a <s>vināḍikā</s>' [<s>Kālakriyā</s> 2], the definition of long syllables must be stated. If the text 'a year is twelve months' and so forth is not commenced, then all this would be established by common knowledge. Therefore, let there be non-redundancy alone. This is not a fault. If this definitional [verse] is not commenced, then these divisions would belong only to the civil (<s>sāvana</s>) system of measurement, not to the solar, lunar, and sidereal [systems], since only the civil system alone is commonly known to the world, not the solar, lunar, and sidereal [systems]. Therefore, [the <s>sūtra</s> must be commenced] so that this very definition applies to all systems of measurement.

body.text:
anyathā hi "ravimāsebhyaḥ adhikāḥ tu ye cāndrāḥ" [kālakriyāí, 6] iti atra ravibhagaṇānām dvādaśa guṇakāraḥ na labhyeta, "śaśidivasāḥ vijñeyāḥ bhūdivasonāḥ tithipralayāḥ" [kālakriyāí, 6] iti atra śaśidivasānām triṃśatkaḥ guṇakāraḥ na labhyeta, "ṣaṣṭiḥ nāḍyaḥ divasaḥ" iti atra api horāśāstrāvirodhena ṣaṣṭiḥ nāḍyaḥ parikalpitāḥ | anyathā hi icchayā vibhāgaḥ divasasya śakyate parikalpayitum | icchayā vibhāge parikalpyamāne kaḥ punar horāśāstravirodhaḥ?
ucyate ã
body.translated_text: For otherwise, in 'the [months] in excess of the solar months are the lunar [intercalary months]' [<s>Kālakriyā</s> 6], the multiplier of twelve for the Sun's revolutions would not be obtainable; in 'the Moon's days should be known as the civil days minus the <s>tithi</s>-omissions' [<s>Kālakriyā</s> 6], the multiplier of thirty for the Moon's days would not be obtainable; in 'sixty <s>nāḍīs</s> make a day,' the sixty <s>nāḍīs</s> have been conceived in conformity with the <s>horā</s> science (horoscopy). For otherwise, the division of the day could be conceived at will. When the division is conceived at will, what then is the contradiction with the <s>horā</s> science? It is said:

body.text: ādyantarāśyorudayapramāṇam dvau dvau muhūrtau niyatam pradiṣṭau |
body.translated_text: The rising-measure of the first and last signs is declared as exactly two <s>muhūrtas</s> each.

body.text: iti atra dvināḍikaḥ muhūrtaḥ vyākhyāyate | sā ca nāḍikā divasasya ṣaṣṭibhāgaḥ iti | anyathā parikalpyamāne ayam arthaḥ anyathā syāt |
body.translated_text: Here, a <s>muhūrta</s> consisting of two <s>nāḍikās</s> is explained. And that <s>nāḍikā</s> is a sixtieth part of the day. If conceived otherwise, this meaning would be different.

body.text: katham punar divasasya ṣaṣṭibhāgaḥ sādhyate iti atra abhidhīyate ã atra kecit bruvate ã "suvarṇarajatatāmrāṇām anyatamam pātram ardhavṛttākāram ṣaṣṭipalapānīyādhārakam pūrakam nisrāvakam vā ghaṭike" iti | na eṣa niyamaḥ | yāvat palāni ṣaṣṭiḥ pānīyam prasravati āpūryate vā, tāvatā nāḍikākālaḥ iti | prājñāḥ tu na evam iti manyante | katham tarhi? ahorātraprasrutasya pānīyasya ṣaṣṭibhāgaḥ ghaṭikāpramāṇaḥ iti sthūlaḥ kalpaḥ, sūkṣmaḥ tu samāyāmavanau

children.text: nirdiṣṭākārasya śaṅkoḥ ghaṭikācchāyām aṅkayitvā ghaṭikā sādhyate, ghaṭikāchidram ca chāyākālavaśāt uktyā yojayitavyam || 1 ||
children.translated_text: having marked the <s>ghaṭikā</s>-shadow of a gnomon of the prescribed shape, the <s>ghaṭikā</s> is established; and the <s>ghaṭikā</s>-orifice must be adjusted by verbal instruction according to the shadow-time. (1)

body.translated_text: How then is the sixtieth part of the day established? Here it is explained: Here some say: 'A vessel of gold, silver, or copper, semicircular in shape, holding sixty <s>palas</s> of water — whether filling or draining — these are the <s>ghaṭikā</s> (water-clock).' This is not a fixed [rule]. The time during which sixty <s>palas</s> of water drain out or fill up — that much is the <s>nāḍikā</s>-time. But the wise do not think so. How then? A sixtieth part of the water that has flowed in a day-and-night is the <s>ghaṭikā</s>-measure — this is the approximate method. The precise [method], however, is: on level ground,

children.text: gurvakṣarāṇi ṣaṣṭiḥ vināḍikā ārkṣī ṣaṭ eva vā prāṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: Sixty long syllables make a <s>vināḍikā</s>; the sidereal one [equals] six <s>prāṇas</s> (breaths).
Thus is the division of time; and the division of space, likewise, from the revolutions. (2)

body.text:
gurvakṣarāṇi ṣaṣṭiḥ vināḍikā ārkṣī | gurūṇi ca tāni akṣarāṇi ca gurvakṣarāṇi, ṣaṣṭiḥ vināḍikā ārkṣī | yāvatā kālena ṣaṣṭiḥ gurvakṣarāṇi paṭhitāni tāvān kālaḥ vināḍīsaṃjñitaḥ | "gurvakṣarāṇi ṣaṣṭiḥ vināḍikā" iti anena sarveṣām eva saurasāvananākṣatracāndrāṇām mānānām vināḍikākālatulyatāyām prasaktāyām tadviṣayanirūpaṇārtham āha ã ārkṣī | katamā vināḍikā gurvakṣarāṇi ṣaṣṭiḥ? ārkṣī, na śeṣāḥ | ṛkṣāṇi nakṣatrāṇi | nakṣatraśabdena nākṣatram
mānam parigṛhyate | ṛkṣāṇām ayam kālaḥ ārkṣaḥ | ayam ca kālaḥ vināḍikābhidhīyamānaḥ strītvam pratipadyate iti strīliṅganirdeśena vināḍikā iti uktam |
body.translated_text: 'Sixty long syllables make a <s>vināḍikā</s>' — the sidereal one. Heavy [syllables], and those are letters — [hence] 'long syllables' (<s>gurvakṣarāṇi</s>). Sixty [of them make] the sidereal <s>vināḍikā</s>. The time during which sixty long syllables are recited — that much time is designated as a <s>vināḍī</s>. By [the statement] 'sixty long syllables make a <s>vināḍikā</s>,' when the equality of the <s>vināḍikā</s>-time across all systems — solar, civil, sidereal, and lunar — is implied, he specifies for the purpose of determining which [system is meant]: 'the sidereal one' (<s>ārkṣī</s>). Which <s>vināḍikā</s> is [equal to] sixty long syllables? The sidereal one — not the others. '<s>Ṛkṣas</s>' are <s>nakṣatras</s> (asterisms). By the word '<s>nakṣatra</s>,' the sidereal (<s>nākṣatra</s>) system of measurement is understood. The time belonging to the asterisms is '<s>ārkṣa</s>' (sidereal). And this time, being designated as <s>vināḍikā</s>, takes the feminine gender — hence the feminine designation '<s>vināḍikā</s>.'

body.text:
ṣaṭ eva vā prāṇāḥ, prāṇāḥ ucchvāsāḥ, ārkṣyavināḍikāyāḥ pramāṇam | ārkṣyam ca mānam bhacakrabhramaṇakālam | yataḥ āha ã "prāṇena eti kalām bham" [gītikāí, 6] iti | ucchvāsakālena bhacakram kalām paryeti, ṛkṣacakram iti arthaḥ | atra ārkṣī vināḍikā ṣaṭ vā prāṇāḥ [tulyāḥ] | ārkṣībhiḥ vināḍikābhiḥ [daśabhiḥ] ekāṃśakaḥ | ataḥ jyotiścakrasambandhinaḥ prāṇāḥ liptāsaṅkhyāḥ iti prāṇaiḥ jyādikarma pravartate | anyathā hi "[pha cha] kalārdhajyāḥ"
[giītikāí, 12] iti uktatvāt prāṇaiḥ jyāgrahaṇam na prāpnoti | anyat ca ã sāmānyena eva "ṣaṭ vā prāṇāḥ vināḍikā" it ucyamāne sarvamānānām eva vināḍikākālasya tulyatāprasaṅgaḥ | avaśiṣṭānām mānānām vināḍikāyāḥ pramāṇam nāḍikāyāḥ ṣaṣṭibhāgaḥ eva | na tasyāḥ vināḍikāyāḥ avayavapramāṇābhidhānam kriyate, prayojanābhāvāt |
body.translated_text: Or, six <s>prāṇas</s> (breaths) are [the measure of] a <s>vināḍikā</s> of the sidereal [measure]. The sidereal measure is the time of one revolution of the stellar sphere. Because he says: "In one <s>prāṇa</s>, the stellar sphere (<s>bha</s>) traverses one <s>kalā</s> (minute)" [<s>Gītikā</s>, 6]. In the time of one breath, the stellar sphere completes one minute — meaning the circle of asterisms (<s>ṛkṣacakra</s>). Here, one sidereal <s>vināḍikā</s> equals six <s>prāṇas</s>. Ten sidereal <s>vināḍikās</s> make one degree (<s>aṃśaka</s>). Therefore, the <s>prāṇas</s> related to the stellar sphere are equal in number to the minutes (<s>liptā</s>) — hence, the sine and other computations proceed with <s>prāṇas</s>. For otherwise, since it has been stated "<s>pha cha</s> — the half-chord sines" [<s>Gītikā</s>, 12], the use of <s>prāṇas</s> for obtaining sines would not be possible. Moreover, when it is stated generally that "a <s>vināḍikā</s> is six <s>prāṇas</s>," the consequence would be that the <s>vināḍikā</s>-durations of all measures are equal. The measure of a <s>vināḍikā</s> of the remaining measures is just one-sixtieth of a <s>nāḍikā</s>. The sub-measure of that <s>vināḍikā</s> is not stated, because there is no purpose.

body.text:
gurvakṣareṣu madhyamavṛttigrahaṇam | "gurvakṣarāṇi ṣaṣṭiḥ" iti atra madhyamāyām vṛttau ṣaṣṭiḥ gurvakṣarāṇi vināḍikākālaḥ iti vaktavyam | anyathā hi tisṛṣu api vṛttiṣu aviśeṣeṇa grahaṇam prāpnoti | tat yathā ã drutāyām vṛttau ṣaṣṭiḥ gurvakṣarāṇi alpena kālena paṭhyante, bilambitāyām mahatā kālena iti, madhyamāyām punar na alpena, na mahatā kālena | tat tarhi madhyamavṛttigrahaṇam kartavyam | katham anucyamānam avagamyate? lokaprasiddheḥ
| tat yathā ã loke anirdiṣṭeṣu kāryeṣu madhyamaprāptiḥ | evam atra api ã "māsānte pakṣasya ante sa hi ākāśe deśe svam miśram vakram kāntam vṛttam pūrṇam candram sattvāt rātrau te kṣutkṣāma prādante śvetaḥ prājyaḥ krūraḥ tasmāt vā ante harmyasya antaḥ saṃsuptasya ekānte kartavyā" | etāni ṣaṣṭiḥ gurvakṣarāṇi vināḍikākālaḥ | ṣaṭ eva vā prāṇāḥ | prāṇāḥ ucchvāsāḥ | te vā ṣaṭ, tasyāḥ eva arkṣyavināḍikāyāḥ kālaḥ | atra api svasthasya aśrāntasya nīrujasya yoginaḥ
prāṇāḥ parigṛhyante | atra api svasthaḥ na mahatā kālena ucchvasiti | evam [a]śrāntaḥ api | yogī na punar vyānavaśān mahatā kālena ucchvasiti | atra truṭi-truṭyavayavādayaḥ kālāvayavāḥ kasmāt na ucyante? evam manyante ã taiḥ vyavahāraḥ na asti iti | vyavahārārtham ca kālāvayavagrahaṇam iti |
body.translated_text: Regarding heavy syllables — the medium pace is to be understood. In "sixty heavy syllables" — it should be stated that sixty heavy syllables recited at a medium pace constitute the time of one <s>vināḍikā</s>. Otherwise, it would indiscriminately apply to all three paces. That is: at a rapid pace, sixty heavy syllables are recited in a short time; at a slow pace, in a long time; but at a medium pace, neither in a short nor in a long time. Then the medium pace must be understood. How is it understood without being stated? From common knowledge. That is: in worldly [practice], where the matter is not specified, the middle [option] is obtained. Similarly here too: "<s>māsānte pakṣasya ante sa hi ākāśe deśe svam miśram vakram kāntam vṛttam pūrṇam candram sattvāt rātrau te kṣutkṣāma prādante śvetaḥ prājyaḥ krūraḥ tasmāt vā ante harmyasya antaḥ saṃsuptasya ekānte kartavyā</s>" — these are sixty heavy syllables [constituting] the time of one <s>vināḍikā</s>. Or, six <s>prāṇas</s> (breaths). <s>Prāṇas</s> are exhalations. Six of those [equal] the time of that very sidereal <s>vināḍikā</s>. Here too, the breaths of a healthy, unexerted, illness-free <s>yogī</s> are taken [as the standard]. Here too, a healthy person does not breathe at long intervals. Similarly, one who is unexerted. A <s>yogī</s>, however, does not breathe at long intervals due to the control of <s>vyāna</s>. Here, why are the sub-divisions of time such as <s>truṭi</s>, sub-<s>truṭi</s>, and so on not stated? They think thus: there is no practical use for them. And the enumeration of time-subdivisions is for the purpose of practical use.

body.text:
evam kālavibhāgaḥ | evam varṣamāsadivasaghaṭikāprāṇāḥ kālavibhāgaḥ | kim artham idam abhidhīyate ã "evam kālavibhāgaḥ" iti | nanu ca kālavibhāgaḥ nirdiṣṭaḥ | evam tasya nirdiṣṭasya grahaṇam "evam kālavibhāgaḥ" iti | asya anabhidhānāt śakyate jñātum yathā aprapañcitapramāṇaḥ kālavibhāgaḥ iti | na eṣa doṣaḥ | "evam kālavibhāgaḥ" evaṃprakāraḥ kālavibhāgaḥ iti arthaḥ | prakārārthe tu vyākhyāyamāne anye api kālavibhāgāḥ parigṛhītāḥ bhavanti
| tat yathā ã pañcasaṃvatsarāḥ yugam, dvādaśamāsāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ, dvau māsau ṛtuḥ te ca vasanta-grīṣma-varṣā-śarad-hemanta-śiśirākhyāḥ, ṛtutrayam ayanam, māsārdham pakṣaḥ śuklaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ ca, divasarātricaturbhāgaḥ yāmaḥ, dvināḍikaḥ muhūrtaḥ, iti evam ādi |
  kṣetravibhāgaḥ tathā bhagaṇāt | kṣetram bhagolaḥ | tasya kṣetrasya vibhāgaḥ | tathā tena eva prakāreṇa | yathā kālasya vibhāgaḥ, kṣetrasya api bhagaṇāt | kālasya varṣāt prabhṛti vibhāgaḥ uktaḥ, kṣetrasya tu bhagaṇāt prabhṛti pravṛtteḥ | tat yathā ã dvādaśarāśayaḥ bhagaṇaḥ, rāśiḥ triṃśat bhāgāḥ, ṣaṣṭiḥ liptā bhāgaḥ, ṣaṣṭiḥ viliptā liptā, ṣaṣṭiḥ tatparā viliptā iti īdṛśaḥ | uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text:
