Thus, the division of time. Thus, years, months, days, <s>ghaṭikās</s>, and <s>prāṇas</s> are the division of time. Why is this stated: "thus, the division of time"? Indeed, the division of time has been specified. Thus, the acceptance of what has been specified [is expressed by] "thus, the division of time." Without stating this, it could be thought that the division of time has not been elaborated upon. This is no defect. "Thus, the division of time" means "such is the manner of the division of time." And when it is explained in the sense of 'manner,' other divisions of time are also included. That is: five years are a <s>yuga</s>; twelve months are a year (<s>saṃvatsara</s>); two months are a season (<s>ṛtu</s>) — and they are named <s>Vasanta</s> (Spring), <s>Grīṣma</s> (Summer), <s>Varṣā</s> (Rains), <s>Śarat</s> (Autumn), <s>Hemanta</s> (Early Winter), and <s>Śiśira</s> (Late Winter); three seasons are an <s>ayana</s> (solstice-period); half a month is a <s>pakṣa</s> (fortnight) — bright (<s>śukla</s>) and dark (<s>kṛṣṇa</s>); a quarter of a day-and-night is a <s>yāma</s> (watch); two <s>nāḍikās</s> are a <s>muhūrta</s> — and so on.
  The division of space, likewise, from the revolution. Space is the stellar sphere (<s>bhagola</s>). The division of that space. Likewise — by that same manner. Just as time has its division, so does space, from the revolution. The division of time has been stated starting from the year; but the division of space starts from the revolution. That is: twelve signs (<s>rāśis</s>) are one revolution (<s>bhagaṇa</s>); one sign is thirty degrees (<s>bhāgas</s>); one degree is sixty minutes (<s>liptās</s>); one minute is sixty seconds (<s>viliptās</s>); one second is sixty thirds (<s>tatparās</s>) — such is this. Example:

children.text: bhagaṇaḥ rāśiḥ bhāgaḥ kalā ca vikalā ca tatparā ca eva |
children.translated_text: Revolution, sign, degree, minute, second, and third —

children.text: kṣetrasya etāḥ saṃjñāḥ kālavibhāgena tulyāḥ syuḥ ||
children.translated_text: these are the designations of space, which correspond to the divisions of time.

body.text: dviyogaparijñānam
body.translated_text: Knowledge of planetary conjunctions

body.text: dviyogaparijñānāya āryāpūrvārdham āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of knowing planetary conjunctions (<s>dviyoga</s>), he states the first half of the <s>āryā</s> verse:

body.text: bhagaṇāḥ dvayoḥ dvayoḥ ye viśeṣaśeṣāḥ yuge dviyogāḥ te |
body.translated_text: The revolutions of two [planets], taken in pairs — the remainders of their differences in a <s>yuga</s> are their conjunctions (<s>dviyoga</s>).

body.text: bhagaṇāḥ nirdiṣṭāḥ eva grahāṇām gītikāsu | dvayoḥ dvayoḥ iti vīpsāgrahaṇam tryādinivṛttyartham | ye viśeṣaśeṣāḥ, dvayoḥ dvayoḥ grahayoḥ bhagaṇānām ye viśeṣaśeṣāḥ bhagaṇāḥ tāvantaḥ tayoḥ yuge dviyogāḥ babhūvuḥ bhaviṣyanti vā |
body.translated_text: The revolutions of the planets have been specified in the <s>Gītikās</s>. 'Of two, of two' — the repetition (<s>vīpsā</s>) is for the purpose of excluding three and more. 'The remainders of the differences' — the differences between the revolutions of two planets at a time — whatever those remainder-revolutions are, that many are their conjunctions in a <s>yuga</s>, [which] have occurred and will occur.

body.text:
atra dvayoḥ dvayoḥ bhagaṇaviśeṣāḥ eva tayoḥ yogāḥ iti katham avasīyate, na punar tayoḥ abhyāsaḥ yogaḥ vā? ucyate | tat yathā ã dvau aśvau ca parimaṇḍalārohe parikalpitau | tatra ekasya kakṣyā ṣaṣṭiḥ dhanuṣām, aparasya triṃśat | tau pañcadaṇḍagatī | mahati maṇḍale yāvat maṇḍalacaturbhāgam gacchati tāvat alpe maṇḍale ardham gacchati | yāvat mahati maṇḍale ardham gacchati tāvat sakalam alpamaṇdalam gacchati | evam yāvat mahati maṇḍale ekaḥ parāvartaḥ
tāvat alpe maṇḍale parāvartadvayam, tāvati ca tayoḥ ekaḥ yogaḥ | evam graheṣu api yojyam | yujyate etat yadi grahāḥ samagatayaḥ | samagatayaḥ grahāḥ iti pratipādayiṣyati |
body.translated_text: Here, how is it established that the differences between the revolutions of two [planets] at a time are their conjunctions, and not their product or their sum? It is explained. That is: suppose two horses are placed on a circular racecourse. One's track is sixty cubits, the other's thirty. Both have a speed of five rods. In the time the one on the large circle traverses a quarter of the circle, the one on the small circle traverses half. In the time the one on the large circle traverses half, the one on the small circle traverses the entire small circle. Thus, in the time one revolution is completed on the large circle, two revolutions are completed on the small circle — and in that much [time], there is one conjunction of those two. Similarly, this should be applied to the planets. This is valid if the planets have equal speeds. That the planets have equal speeds — he will demonstrate.

body.text: uddeśakaḥ ã guroḥ aṅgārakasya ca yuge kiyantaḥ yogāḥ iti |
body.translated_text: Example problem: How many conjunctions of <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter) and <s>Aṅgāraka</s> (Mars) [are there] in a <s>yuga</s>?

body.text: labdham yogāḥ gagana[jala]darasayamāgnirandhraśaśāṅkāḥ [1932600] | evam sarveṣām api |
body.translated_text: Result: The conjunctions are sky-water-<s>Rasa</s>-<s>Yama</s>-fire-hole-moon [= 1,932,600]. Similarly for all [planet-pairs].

body.text:
kaḥ punar atra dviyogānām viniyogaḥ? ucyate | yadi caturyugāhargaṇena iṣṭagrahayoḥ dviyogāḥ labhyante, [tarhi] kaliyātāhargaṇena kiyantaḥ iti labdham samatikrāntāḥ dviyogāḥ | śeṣam gatagantavyam kṛtvā yugadviyogaiḥ vibhajet | labdham gatagantavyadivasā iti ekaḥ viniyogaḥ | [śeṣam ṣaṣṭyā saṅguṇya yugadviyogaiḥ vibhajet labdham ghaṭyādi |] yadi caturyugāhargaṇena iṣṭagrahayoḥ dviyogāḥ labhyante [tarhi] kaliyātāhargaṇena kiyantaḥ iti labdham samatikrāntāḥ
dviyogāḥ | śeṣe dvādaśādiguṇite rāsyādilabdhiḥ | taiḥ dviyogarāśyādibhiḥ mandagatigrahaḥ yuktaḥ śīghragatigrahaḥ bhavati | śīghragatiḥ ca dviyogarāśyādihīnaḥ mandagatiḥ bhavati iti aparaḥ viniyogaḥ | dviyogaiḥ ca rāśyādīn ānīya tayoḥ api bhagaṇasamāsena api bhagaṇasamāsagatabhagaṇarāśyādīn vidhāya "antarayuktam hīnam" [gaṇitaí, 24] iti anena ekatra kṣipet ekatra viśodhayet, kṣiptaviśodhitayoḥ ardham tayoḥ gatabhagaṇarāśibhāgaliptāḥ iti anyaḥ viniyogaḥ
| kuṭṭākāraviniyogaḥ tu pradarśitaḥ eva iti |
body.translated_text: What then is the application of these conjunctions? It is explained. If by the <s>caturyuga</s> day-count the conjunctions of the desired two planets are obtained, [then] by the <s>Kali</s>-elapsed day-count, how many? — the result is the elapsed conjunctions. Making the remainder into elapsed-and-remaining [portions], and dividing by the <s>yuga</s>-conjunctions, the result is the elapsed-and-remaining days — this is one application. [The remainder, multiplied by sixty, divided by the <s>yuga</s>-conjunctions, gives the result in <s>ghaṭīs</s> and so on.] If by the <s>caturyuga</s> day-count the conjunctions of the desired two planets are obtained, [then] by the <s>Kali</s>-elapsed day-count, how many? — the result is the elapsed conjunctions. When the remainder is multiplied by twelve and so on, signs and so on are obtained. The slow-moving planet, combined with those conjunction-signs and so on, becomes the fast-moving planet. And the fast-moving [planet], diminished by the conjunction-signs and so on, becomes the slow-moving one — this is another application. Having obtained the signs and so on from the conjunctions, and also having computed the elapsed revolutions, signs, and so on from the sum of both revolutions, 'increased and decreased by the difference' [<s>Gaṇita</s>, 24] — by this, add to one and subtract from the other; the halves of the added and subtracted [values] are the elapsed revolutions, signs, degrees, and minutes of those two — this is yet another application. The application in the <s>kuṭṭākāra</s> (pulverizer) has already been demonstrated.

body.text: yuge vyatīpātasaṃkhyā
body.translated_text: The number of <s>vyatīpātas</s> in a <s>yuga</s>

body.text: vyatīpātajñānāya āryāpaścārdham āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of knowing the <s>vyatīpāta</s> (astronomical malefic yoga), he states the latter half of the <s>āryā</s> verse:

body.text: raviśaśinakṣatragaṇāḥ sammiśrāḥ ca vyatīpātāḥ || 3 ||
body.translated_text: The numbers of the asterism[-revolutions] of the Sun and Moon, combined, are the <s>vyatīpātas</s>. // 3 //

body.text: nakṣatrāṇām gaṇāḥ nakṣatragaṇāḥ | nakṣatrāṇi aśvinyādīni | raviḥ ca śaśī ca raviśaśī | raviśaśinaḥ nakṣatragaṇāḥ candrādityabhagaṇāḥ iti yāvat | te ca rasadahanaśikhiguṇaśailākāśayamartavaḥ [62073336] | ete vyatīpātāḥ | sammiśrāḥ ca vyatīpātāḥ | sammiśrāḥ ekīkṛtāḥ | kena saṃmiśrāḥ? anyasya aśrutatvāt, raviśaśibhagaṇāḥ nakṣatragaṇaiḥ eva | te eva vyatīpātāḥ dviguṇitāḥ iti arthaḥ | te ca dviśailarasartumanukṛtaravayaḥ [124146672] |
body.translated_text: The numbers of the asterisms are the asterism-numbers (<s>nakṣatragaṇāḥ</s>). The asterisms are those beginning with <s>Aśvinī</s>. The Sun and Moon [together form] '<s>raviśaśi</s>.' The asterism-numbers of the Sun and Moon are the revolutions of the Moon and Sun — that is the meaning. And they are <s>rasa-dahana-śikhi-guṇa-śailākāśa-yama-ṛtavaḥ</s> [= 62,073,336]. These are the <s>vyatīpātas</s>. 'Combined, the <s>vyatīpātas</s>' — 'combined' means unified. Combined with what? Since nothing else has been mentioned, the revolutions of the Sun and Moon are [combined] with the asterism-numbers alone. [The asterism-numbers] are doubled — that is the meaning. And they are <s>dvi-śaila-rasa-ṛtu-manu-kṛta-rava-yaḥ</s> [= 124,146,672].

body.text:
atha etau vyatīpātau abhihitau dvādaśaṣaḍrāśyātmakau | atra idam praṣṭavyam ã [kim idam] vyatīpātayoḥ udāharaṇam āhosvit lakṣaṇam iti? yadi idam udāharaṇam tadā sarvam iṣṭam setsyati, tat astu udāharaṇam iti | tat yathā ã candrādityau sphuṭīkṛtau yadi ekatra dvādaśarāśayaḥ tadā vyatīpātaḥ | nanu ca loke dvādaśarāśikaḥ vaidhṛtaḥ iti prasiddham ? na eṣaḥ doṣaḥ | saṃjñākṛtaḥ bhedaḥ na phalam prati, yasmāt vyatīpātasya vaidhṛtasya ca tulyam phalam
bhagavadbhiḥ gargādibhiḥ upadiṣṭam | tau eva sūryācandramasau sphuṭau ekatra yadi ṣaḍrāśayaḥ tadā api vyatīpātaḥ |
body.translated_text: Now, these two <s>vyatīpātas</s> have been described as consisting of twelve and six signs [respectively]. Here, one should ask: Is this an illustration of the <s>vyatīpātas</s>, or a definition? If it is an illustration, then everything desired will be established — so let it be an illustration. That is: when the Sun and Moon, corrected to true [positions], together [amount to] twelve signs in one [direction], then [it is] a <s>vyatīpāta</s>. But is it not well-known in the world that [the configuration of] twelve signs is called <s>Vaidhṛta</s>? This is no defect. The difference made by names does not affect the result, since the blessed <s>Garga</s> and others have taught that the result of <s>vyatīpāta</s> and <s>Vaidhṛta</s> is the same. Those same true Sun and Moon, when together [they amount to] six signs in one [direction] — that too is a <s>vyatīpāta</s>.

body.text:
atha vyatīpātasya atītaiṣyaparijñānārtham trairāśikam ã yadi sūryācandramasoḥ sphuṭabhuktisamāsena ṣaṣṭighaṭikāḥ labhyante, [tadā] anena atītaiṣyeṇa kiyatya iti labhdam ghaṭikāḥ vighaṭikāḥ ca | athavā atītaiṣyavyatīpātakālikau sūryācandramasau jñātum icchati, tadā atītaiṣyeṇa saha trairāśikam ã yadi sūryācandramasoḥ sphuṭabhuktisamāsena sūryabhuktiḥ candrabhuktiḥ vā labhyate, [tadā] anena atītaiṣyasūryācandramasoḥ bhuktisamāsena kim iti bhuktiḥ
labhyate | tena rahitau sahitau sūryācandramasau vyatīpātakālikau | evam sthūlā vyatīpātabhuktiḥ | yathā sūkṣmā bhavati tathā pradarśyate | uktam ca ã
body.translated_text: Now, for the purpose of knowing the elapsed and remaining [portions] of the <s>vyatīpāta</s>, the rule of three: If by the sum of the true daily motions of the Sun and Moon, sixty <s>ghaṭikās</s> are obtained, [then] by this elapsed-and-remaining [portion], how many? — the result is <s>ghaṭikās</s> and <s>vighaṭikās</s>. Alternatively, if one wishes to know the Sun and Moon at the time of the <s>vyatīpāta</s>, then the rule of three with the elapsed-and-remaining [portion]: If by the sum of the true daily motions of the Sun and Moon, the Sun's daily motion or the Moon's daily motion is obtained, [then] by this elapsed-and-remaining sum of the daily motions of the Sun and Moon, what daily motion is obtained? With that [amount], diminished or combined, the Sun and Moon at the time of the <s>vyatīpāta</s> [are determined]. This is the rough <s>vyatīpāta</s> computation. How the precise [computation] is done will be demonstrated. And it has been stated:

children.translated_text: The <s>vyatīpāta</s> [occurs] when those two [Sun and Moon] are in different <s>ayanas</s> (solstice-periods) and have equal declinations.

children.text: uddeśaḥ tasya cakrārdham vikṣepam ca adhikonakam ||
children.translated_text: Its indicator is half a revolution, and the latitude (<s>vikṣepa</s>) is added or subtracted.

body.text: mahābhāskarīyam, 4.36
body.translated_text: <s>Mahābhāskarīya</s>, 4.36

body.text: iti | sūryācandramasau nānāyane tulyāpakramau yadā bhavataḥ tadā vyatīpātaḥ, candrasya vikṣepasahitaḥ rahitaḥ vā apakramaḥ | asmin kila vyatīpātayoge kṣīrataruśākhāvacchede vigatakṣīratā || 3 ||
body.translated_text: Thus. When the Sun and Moon are in different <s>ayanas</s> and have equal declinations, [it is] a <s>vyatīpāta</s> — the Moon's declination being with or without the latitude (<s>vikṣepa</s>). At this conjunction of <s>vyatīpāta</s>, supposedly, cutting a branch of a milk-tree [results in] the loss of milk. // 3 //

body.text: yuge grahoccanīcabhagaṇāḥ
body.translated_text: The revolutions of the planetary apogees and perigees in a <s>yuga</s>

body.text: uccanīcaparivartajñānārtham āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of knowing the revolutions of the apogee and perigee, he states:

body.text: svoccabhagaṇāḥ svabhagaṇaiḥ viśeṣitāḥ svoccanīcaparivartāḥ |
body.translated_text: The revolutions of one's own apogee, diminished by one's own revolutions, are the apogee-perigee revolutions.

body.text:
svoccabhagaṇāḥ svabhagaṇaiḥ viśeṣitāḥ | svakīyam uccam svoccam, tasya svoccasya bhagaṇāḥ svoccabhagaṇāḥ | atra grahāṇām uccadvayam, mandoccam śīghroccam ca | atra katarat uccam parigṛhyate? śīghroccam iti āha | mandoccasya yadi api gatiḥ abhyupagatā tathā api yugabhagaṇasya vyavahāraḥ na asti iti śīghroccabhagaṇāḥ eva parigṛhyante | svabhagaṇaiḥ viśeṣitāḥ svoccanīcaparivartāḥ | uccabhagaṇānām svabhagaṇānām ca yaḥ viśeṣaḥ sa uccanīcaparivartaḥ
| yasmāt nairaṃśyāt yāvat nairaṃśyam tāvat udayāstamayavakrānuvakrāḥ bhavanti iti uccaparivartaḥ parikalpitaḥ | ye niraṃśadvayāntare divasāḥ te parivartasya divasāḥ | parivartāḥ grahāḥ ca yugādau meṣāditaḥ pravṛttāḥ | mīnānte śīghrabhagaṇaparisamāptiḥ | grahabhogādhikaḥ śīghrabhogaḥ parikalpitaḥ | uccanīcaparivartāḥ | uccaparivartāḥ nīcaparivartāḥ ca tāvantaḥ eva, yasmāt ekasmin niraṃśadvayāntareṣu grahasya uccanīcaprāptī saṃbhavataḥ |
body.translated_text: The revolutions of the <s>svocca</s> (own apogee) are differentiated from one's own revolutions. One's own apogee is <s>svocca</s>; its revolutions are the <s>svoccabhagaṇas</s> (apogee-revolutions). Here, planets have two kinds of apogee: <s>mandocca</s> (slow apogee) and <s>śīghrocca</s> (fast apogee). Which apogee is taken here? He says: the <s>śīghrocca</s>. Although the motion of the <s>mandocca</s> is acknowledged, since its revolution-count per <s>yuga</s> is not used in practice, only the <s>śīghrocca</s> revolutions are taken. Differentiated from one's own revolutions, [these give] the <s>svoccanīcaparivartāḥ</s> (apogee-perigee cycles). The difference between the apogee-revolutions and one's own revolutions is the apogee-perigee cycle. Since from one zero-point to the next zero-point, the risings, settings, retrograde and direct motions occur — thus the apogee cycle is conceived. The days between two zero-points are the days of a cycle. The cycles and planets commence from the beginning of <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries) at the start of the <s>yuga</s>. The <s>śīghra</s> revolution is completed at the end of <s>Mīna</s> (Pisces). The <s>śīghra</s> traverse is conceived as exceeding the planet's traverse. The apogee-perigee cycles: the apogee cycles and perigee cycles are equal in number, since within one interval between two zero-points, the planet's attainment of apogee and perigee [both] occur.

body.text: atha kaḥ punar uccaḥ, kaḥ vā nīcaḥ iti? yatra grahāḥ sūkṣmāḥ lakṣyante karṇasya mahattvāt sa ākāśapradeśaḥ uccasaṃjñitaḥ | yatra asau eva grahaḥ mahābimbaḥ lakṣyate karṇasya alpatvāt sa ākāśapradeśaḥ nīcasaṃjñitaḥ iti |
body.translated_text: Now, what then is the apogee, and what is the perigee? Where a planet appears small due to the greatness of the <s>karṇa</s> (hypotenuse/radius vector), that region of space is designated as the apogee. Where that same planet appears as a large disc due to the smallness of the <s>karṇa</s>, that region of space is designated as the perigee.

body.text:
atha parivartaiḥ api uccam kendram vā ānīyate | katham? yadi caturyugāhargaṇena ete uccanīcaparivartāḥ labhyante, tadā kaliyātāhargaṇena kiyantaḥ iti labdham samatikrāntāḥ parivartāḥ, śeṣe dvādaśā[diguṇite] rāśyādikaḥ parivartabhogaḥ | parivartabhogarahitaḥ grahaḥ grahasahitaḥ vā parivartabhogaḥ uccabhogaḥ | uccabhogasahitaḥ parivartabhogaḥ [parivartabhogarahitaḥ vā uccabhogaḥ ] grahabhogaḥ | parivartabhogaḥ eva kendrabhogaḥ | anyat ca dviyogābhihitena
samānam |
body.translated_text: Now, by means of the cycles too, the apogee or the <s>kendra</s> (anomaly) can be derived. How? If by the <s>caturyuga</s> day-count these apogee-perigee cycles are obtained, then by the <s>Kali</s>-elapsed day-count, how many? — the result gives the elapsed cycles; from the remainder, multiplied by twelve and so on, the signs etc. of the cycle-traverse [are obtained]. The planet minus the cycle-traverse, or the cycle-traverse plus the planet, gives the apogee-traverse. The cycle-traverse plus the apogee-traverse [or the apogee-traverse minus the cycle-traverse] gives the planet's traverse. The cycle-traverse itself is the <s>kendra</s>-traverse (anomaly-traverse). The rest is the same as stated in the <s>dviyoga</s> (conjunction) [method].

body.text: atha "bhagaṇāḥ dvayoḥ dvayoḥ ye viśeṣaśeṣāḥ yuge dviyogāḥ te" [kālakriyāí, 3] iti asyām eva kārikāyām nanu gataḥ ayam arthaḥ kim atra abhidhīyate? uccanīcaparivartasaṃjñārtham ayam ārambhaḥ | tatra dviyogamātram eva pratipāditam | atha ca tat dvayoḥ dvayoḥ grahayoḥ bhagaṇaviśeṣaḥ iti abhihitaḥ | na uccagrahabhagaṇaviśeṣaḥ iti [ pṛthak uktiḥ ] |
body.translated_text: Now, 'The revolutions of any two [planets], the remainders of their differences in a <s>yuga</s>, are their <s>dviyogas</s> (conjunctions)' [<s>Kālakriyāpāda</s>, verse 3] — since this meaning has already been conveyed in that very verse, what is being stated here? This passage is begun for the purpose of establishing the technical term <s>uccanīcaparivarta</s> (apogee-perigee cycle). There, only the <s>dviyoga</s> was explained. And that was described as the difference in revolutions of any two planets — not specifically as the difference between apogee and planet revolutions [as a separate statement].

body.text: aśvayujādyāḥ gurvabdāḥ
body.translated_text: The <s>Jovian</s> years beginning with <s>Aśvayuj</s>

body.text: guruvarṣanirūpaṇāya āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of determining the <s>Jovian</s> year, he says:

body.text: gurubhagaṇāḥ rāśiguṇāḥ aśvayujādyāḥ guroḥ abdāḥ || 4 ||
body.translated_text: The revolutions of <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter) multiplied by the number of signs are the years of <s>Guru</s> beginning with <s>Aśvayuj</s>. // 4 //

body.text:
gurubhagaṇāḥ rāśiguṇāḥ | guroḥ bhagaṇāḥ gurubhagaṇāḥ, bṛhaspatibhagaṇāḥ iti yāvat | rāśiguṇāḥ dvādaśaguṇāḥ iti yāvat | aśvayujādyāḥ guroḥ abdāḥ | aśvayuk abdaḥ, ādau bhavati [iti] ādyaḥ, aśvayuk ādyaḥ yeṣām te aśvayujādyāḥ | guroḥ abdāḥ guroḥ saṃvatsarāḥ iti arthaḥ | te ca aśvayuk-kārtika-mārgaśīrṣa-pauṣa-māgha-phālguna-caitra-vaiśākha-jyeṣṭha-āṣāḍha-śrāvaṇa-prauṣṭhapadākhyāḥ | atra trairāśikam ã yadi caturyugāhargaṇena ete guroḥ abdāḥ
vasuvasurasākāśamunidahanakṛtāḥ [4370688] [labhyante, tadā] kaliyātāhargaṇena kiyantaḥ iti | labdhāḥ samatikrāntāḥ samāḥ | labdhāsu samāsu dvādaśabhakte, śeṣāḥ aśvayujādyāḥ samāḥ | katham idam vijñāyate aśvayujādyāḥ samāḥ iti ? ucyate ã "aśvayujādyāḥ guroḥ abdāḥ" iti vacanāt | nanu tat eva vacanam asmābhiḥ coditam parihāraḥ api asmābhiḥ ucyate | yasmāt yugādau aśvinyām amarapatigururudayaśikhariśikharamadhirūḍhaḥ tasmāt aśvayujādyāḥ guroḥ samāḥ
|
body.translated_text: The revolutions of <s>Guru</s> multiplied by the number of signs: the revolutions of <s>Guru</s> are the <s>gurubhagaṇas</s>, meaning the revolutions of <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter). Multiplied by the number of signs means multiplied by twelve. The years of <s>Guru</s> beginning with <s>Aśvayuj</s>: <s>Aśvayuj</s> is a year; that which occurs first is <s>ādya</s> (initial); those whose initial [year] is <s>Aśvayuj</s> are <s>aśvayujādya</s>. The years of <s>Guru</s> means the <s>saṃvatsaras</s> (years) of <s>Guru</s>. They are named: <s>Aśvayuj</s>, <s>Kārtika</s>, <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, <s>Pauṣa</s>, <s>Māgha</s>, <s>Phālguna</s>, <s>Caitra</s>, <s>Vaiśākha</s>, <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, and <s>Prauṣṭhapada</s>. Here the rule of three: if by the <s>caturyuga</s> day-count these years of <s>Guru</s>, numbering <s>Vasu</s>-<s>Vasu</s>-<s>Rasa</s>-sky-sage-fire-made [4370688], [are obtained, then] by the <s>Kali</s>-elapsed day-count, how many? The result gives the elapsed years. When the resulting years are divided by twelve, the remainders are the years beginning with <s>Aśvayuj</s>. How is it known that the years begin with <s>Aśvayuj</s>? It is said: from the statement 'the years of <s>Guru</s> begin with <s>Aśvayuj</s>.' But we have raised that very statement [as a question]; the answer too is given by us: since at the beginning of the <s>yuga</s>, in [the month of] <s>Aśvinī</s>, the lord of the gods, <s>Guru</s>, has risen to the peak of the eastern mountain — therefore the years of <s>Guru</s> begin with <s>Aśvayuj</s>.

body.text: uktam ca ã
body.translated_text: And it has been stated:

children.translated_text: In whichever <s>nakṣatra</s> (constellation) <s>Aṅgiras</s> (Jupiter) rises, having gone abroad,
the <s>Bārhaspatya</s> (Jovian) year is reckoned as beginning from that constellation.

body.text: iti |
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: atha vasuvasurasākāśamunidahanakṛtasaṅkhyaiḥ [4370688] trairāśikena bṛhaspatiḥ api ānīyate | katham? yadi caturyugāhargaṇena vasuvasvādayaḥ bṛhaspatirāśayaḥ labhyante, [tadā] kaliyātāhargaṇena kiyantaḥ iti labdhāḥ rāśayaḥ | śeṣe triṃśadādiguṇite bhāgaliptā[dayaḥ] | evam idam arthāt āpannam bhavati | ye samatikrāntāḥ guroḥ rāśayaḥ te samatikrāntāḥ guroḥ aśvayujādyāḥ saṃvatsarāḥ, śeṣe ca vartamānaḥ iti |
body.translated_text: Now, by means of the rule of three with the number <s>Vasu</s>-<s>Vasu</s>-<s>Rasa</s>-sky-sage-fire-made [4370688], <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter) too can be derived. How? If by the <s>caturyuga</s> day-count the <s>Vasu</s>-<s>Vasu</s> etc. signs of <s>Bṛhaspati</s> are obtained, [then] by the <s>Kali</s>-elapsed day-count, how many? — the result gives the signs. From the remainder, multiplied by thirty and so on, degrees, minutes, [and so on are obtained]. Thus this follows as a consequence: the signs of <s>Guru</s> that have elapsed are the elapsed <s>Aśvayuj</s>-initial years of <s>Guru</s>, and the remainder gives the current [year].

body.text: atha vasuvasvādayaḥ guroḥ saṃvatsarāḥ iti abhidhīyante | nanu ca taiḥ yugasaṃvatsaraiḥ tulyaiḥ bhavitavyam? na iti āha | ye yugasaṃvatsarāḥ te sauryeṇa mānena dṛṣṭāḥ, am ca ye guroḥ abdāḥ te gurumānena | ttat eva yugam sauryeṇa anumīyamānam gaganajaladabindume[gha]yamahutāśakṛta [4320000] saṅkhyam | tat eva bārhaspatyena vasuvasvādi [4370688] saṅkhyam | bārhaspatyābdam bṛhaspateḥ rāśibhogaḥ iti na sauryabārhaspatyau tulyau iti || 4 ||
body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Vasu</s>-<s>Vasu</s> etc. are stated to be the years of <s>Guru</s>. But should they not be equal to the <s>yuga</s>-years? No, he says. The <s>yuga</s>-years are reckoned by the solar measure, whereas the years of <s>Guru</s> are by the <s>Guru</s>-measure. That same <s>yuga</s>, measured by the solar [standard], numbers sky-water-tip-drop-cloud-<s>Yama</s>-great-fire-made [4320000]. That same [<s>yuga</s>], by the <s>Bārhaspatya</s> (Jovian) [standard], numbers <s>Vasu</s>-<s>Vasu</s> etc. [4370688]. A <s>Bārhaspatya</s> year is the sign-traverse of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>; hence the solar and <s>Bārhaspatya</s> [years] are not equal. // 4 //

body.text: sauracāndrasāvananākṣatramānāni
body.translated_text: The solar, lunar, civil, and sidereal measures

body.text: saura-cāndra-sāvana-nākṣatramānapradarśanārtham āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of demonstrating the solar, lunar, civil, and sidereal measures, he says:

children.translated_text: The revolutions of the Sun are the solar years; the conjunctions of the Sun and Moon are the lunar months;

children.text: ravibhūyogāḥ divasāḥ bhāvartāḥ ca api nākṣatrāḥ || 5 ||
children.translated_text: the conjunctions of the Sun and Earth are the [civil] days; and the rotations of the stellar sphere are the sidereal [days]. // 5 //

body.text:
ravibhagaṇāḥ ravyabdāḥ | raveḥ bhagaṇāḥ, ravibhagaṇāḥ, ravyabdāḥ, ravivarṣāṇi iti yāvat | ye eva ravibhagaṇāḥ te eva ravyabdāḥ | tathā idam anuktam api gamyate ravirāśi-bhāga-liptā ravimāsa-divasa-nāḍyaḥ iti | yasmāt dvādaśarāśayaḥ bhagaṇaḥ, triṃśadbhāgā rāśiḥ, bhāgaṣaṣṭyavayavaḥ liptā, ṣaḍrāśayaḥ ayanam uttaram dakṣiṇam ca makarakulīrāditaḥ iti | katham idam avasīyate makarakulīrāditaḥ iti na punar dhaniṣṭhādeḥ āśleṣārdhāt iti, yasmāt uktam
ã
body.translated_text: The revolutions of the Sun are the solar years: the revolutions of <s>Ravi</s> (the Sun) are the <s>ravibhagaṇas</s>, [which are] the solar years, meaning the solar annual periods. The very revolutions of the Sun are the solar years. Likewise, though unstated, it is understood that the Sun's signs, degrees, and minutes [correspond to] the solar months, days, and <s>nāḍīs</s>. Since twelve signs make a revolution, thirty degrees make a sign, sixty subdivisions of a degree make a minute, and six signs make a half-year — the northward and southward [courses] beginning from <s>Makara</s> (Capricorn) and <s>Kulīra</s> (Cancer) respectively. How is it determined that [the solstices begin] from <s>Makara</s> and <s>Kulīra</s>, and not from the beginning of <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s> or the middle of <s>Āśleṣā</s>? Because it has been stated:

body.text:
ardhāśleṣāt śraviṣṭhādeḥ pravṛtte dakṣiṇottare |
kṣemasasyasubhikṣākhye tu ayane gharmatejasaḥ || iti |
body.translated_text: From the middle of <s>Āśleṣā</s> and the beginning of <s>Śraviṣṭhā</s> (Dhaniṣṭhā), the southward and northward [courses] commenced; the two <s>ayanas</s> (half-years), named 'prosperity, harvest, and abundance,' belong to the radiant Sun. Thus.

body.text:
atra ucyate ã śrutyoḥ bhinnavākyatā | śakyate eva tat vaktum, adṛṣṭārthatvāt | "śrutyarthānuṣṭhānaphalasya sarvaśākhāpratyayam ekam karma" iti | śrutismṛtyoḥ punar bhede yā ca smṛtiḥ pratyakṣāviruddhā sā parigṛhyate | iyam asmākam smṛtiḥ pratyakṣāvyabhicāriṇī, yataḥ pratyakṣeṇa eva uttaradakṣiṇapravṛttiḥ makarakarkaṭāditaḥ eva upalakṣyate | katham? yasmāt dhanuṣaḥ ante makarādisthite vidhvastāśeṣadhvāntasaṃghāte bhagavati bhāskare dinamadhyaṃgate
sarvamadhyāhnacchāyābhyaḥ mahatī madhyāhnacchāyā lakṣyate | sā ca krameṇa apacīyamānā makarāditaḥ eva, na śraviṣṭhādeḥ | yat ca karkaṭādau sarvamadhyāhnacchāyābhyaḥ svalpīyasī madhyāhnacchāyā, sā ca krameṇa upacīyamānā karkaṭāditaḥ eva, na aśleṣārdhāt iti ataḥ pratyakṣasiddham ayanam |
body.translated_text: Here it is said: the two <s>śrutis</s> (Vedic statements) express different meanings. One can indeed say that, since the purpose is unseen [i.e., pertaining to ritual merit]. 'The performance of a <s>śruti</s>-prescribed act, whose fruit depends on all branches [of the Veda], constitutes a single rite.' But when there is a conflict between <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>, whichever <s>smṛti</s> does not contradict direct perception is accepted. Our <s>smṛti</s> [i.e., the astronomical tradition] does not deviate from direct perception, because by direct observation itself the northward and southward movement is seen to commence from <s>Makara</s> (Capricorn) and <s>Karkaṭa</s> (Cancer) only. How? Because when the blessed <s>Bhāskara</s> (Sun), having destroyed all darkness, stands at midday at the end of <s>Dhanus</s> (Sagittarius), i.e., at the beginning of <s>Makara</s>, the midday shadow is the longest of all midday shadows. And that [shadow] progressively diminishes from the beginning of <s>Makara</s> only, not from [the beginning of] <s>Śraviṣṭhā</s>. And at the beginning of <s>Karkaṭa</s> (Cancer), the midday shadow is the shortest of all midday shadows, and it progressively increases from the beginning of <s>Karkaṭa</s> only, not from the middle of <s>Āśleṣā</s>. Therefore the <s>ayana</s> (solstitial point) is established by direct perception.

body.text:
athavā ayam anyārthaparaḥ eva granthaḥ | karkaṭādeḥ dakṣiṇāyanam makarādeḥ ca uttarāyaṇam iti etasya abhyupagamāt eva ucyate ã yadā bhavagān bhāskaraḥ ardhāśleṣāt dakṣiṇam mārgam pravartate punar vasvoḥ caturthāṃśadim [arthāt karkaṭādim] parityajyate tadā kṣemasasyasubhikṣāḥ bhavanti | yadā ca makarādim parityajya śraviṣṭhādeḥ uttaram [mārgam] pratipadyate tadā ca tatphalārthatvam iti | atha ayam vivasvān katham evam pravartate iti?
ucyate ã grahāṇām dvayī gatiḥ, saṅkhyānugatā autpātikī ca | yadā autpātikī gatiḥ evam prakārā bhavati tadā kṣemasasyasubhikṣākhye ayane [bhavataḥ] | yadā punar karkaṭamakarādim aprāptvā eva dakṣiṇottarapravṛttinivṛttī bhavataḥ tadā akṣemā asasyā asubhikṣā iti etat pradarśayati |
body.translated_text: Alternatively, that text [about <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s> and <s>Āśleṣā</s>] has a different intended meaning. Since it is accepted that the southward course begins from <s>Karkaṭa</s> and the northward course from <s>Makara</s>, it is stated thus: when the blessed <s>Bhāskara</s> (Sun) turns southward from the middle of <s>Āśleṣā</s>, abandoning the fourth quarter of <s>Vasu</s> [i.e., the beginning of <s>Karkaṭa</s>], then there is prosperity, harvest, and abundance. And when, abandoning the beginning of <s>Makara</s>, he proceeds northward from [the beginning of] <s>Śraviṣṭhā</s>, then too that is the fruit [of the auspicious <s>ayana</s>]. Now, how does the Sun behave in this manner? It is said: planets have two kinds of motion — regular (governed by calculation) and anomalous (<s>autpātikī</s>). When the anomalous motion is of this kind, then the <s>ayanas</s> are called 'prosperity, harvest, and abundance.' But when the northward and southward turning occurs without [the Sun] reaching [the standard points of] <s>Karkaṭa</s> and <s>Makara</s>, then [the result is] 'no prosperity, no harvest, no abundance' — this is what [the text] indicates.

body.text: api atra aviditaparamārthāḥ romakāḥ paṭhanti ã
body.translated_text: Moreover, here the <s>Romakas</s>, who do not understand the true meaning, recite:

children.translated_text: From the half of <s>Sārpa</s> (Āśleṣā) and beginning of <s>Vasudeiva</s> (Dhaniṣṭhā), the sages declared the <s>ayana</s>;

children.text: mṛgakarkyāditaḥ dṛṣṭam katham tat hi gateḥ vinā ||
children.translated_text: [But it is] observed from the beginnings of <s>Mṛga</s> (Makara/Capricorn) and <s>Karkī</s> (Cancer) — how [can that be] without motion [of the solstitial point]?

body.text: iti ādigranthena | kṣudravidrāvaṇopanyāsakrameṇa yugabhagaṇān āhuḥ ã
body.translated_text: Thus, with such an introductory text. By the method of refuting inferior [opinions], they state the <s>yuga</s>-revolutions:

body.text:
tasmāt atra viyadrudrakṛtanandadhṛtīḥ (1894110) yugam |
bhagaṇān saptaviśvākhyānādityāntyotkramāt kramāt || iti |
body.translated_text: Therefore, the <s>yuga</s> here [contains] sky-<s>Rudra</s>-made-<s>Nanda</s>-<s>Dhṛti</s> (1894110) revolutions; with <s>Sapta</s>-<s>Viśva</s>-named-<s>Āditya</s>-last in reverse order and forward order. Thus.

body.text:
atra katham idam ghaṭate yadi utkrameṇa kramāt vā punar vasvoḥ meṣādeḥ api dakṣiṇāyanam pravartate na karkaṭādau eva? tathā ca varṣāṛtuḥ meṣādeḥ pravarteta [makarādeḥ] vasantaḥ | tathā ca kālaviparyāsaḥ prasajyeta | evam ca śrutyarthaḥ na anuṣṭhitaḥ bhavati | "vasante yajeta", caitravaiśākhau vasantaḥ, "madhuḥ ca mādhavaḥ ca vāsantikau ṛtū" [taittirīyasaṃhitā, 4.4.11] | tathā ca "śaradi vājapeyena yajet", aśvayukkārtikau śarat, "iṣaḥ ca ūrjaḥ ca śāradau
ṛtū" [taittirīyasaṃhitā, 4.4.11] iti | idam ca jyotiṣām ayanam aṅgam vedasya | tasmāt na ayanasya gatiḥ | makarakarkaṭāditaḥ ayanam iti | sarvasiddhāntaguruḥ ācāryalāṭadevaḥ āha ã
body.translated_text: Here, how does this work if, by reverse order or forward order, the southward course proceeds from the beginning of [the quarter of] <s>Vasu</s> [i.e.] <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries) and not from <s>Karkaṭa</s> (Cancer) itself? In that case, the rainy season would begin from <s>Meṣa</s>, and spring from [<s>Makara</s>]. And thus a reversal of seasons would follow. And thus the purpose of the <s>śruti</s> would not be fulfilled: 'One should sacrifice in spring' — <s>Caitra</s> and <s>Vaiśākha</s> are spring — '<s>Madhu</s> and <s>Mādhava</s> are the spring months' [<s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 4.4.11]. Likewise, 'One should perform the <s>Vājapeya</s> in autumn' — <s>Aśvayuj</s> and <s>Kārtika</s> are autumn — '<s>Iṣa</s> and <s>Ūrja</s> are the autumn months' [<s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 4.4.11]. And this astronomical [determination of] the <s>ayana</s> is an auxiliary of the <s>Veda</s>. Therefore, the <s>ayana</s> has no [progressive] motion. The <s>ayana</s> [begins] from <s>Makara</s> and <s>Karkaṭa</s>. The teacher of all <s>siddhāntas</s>, <s>Ācārya Lāṭadeva</s>, has said:

body.text: makarādau udagayanam dakṣiṇam ayanam ca candrabhavanādau |
body.translated_text: The northward course [begins] at the beginning of <s>Makara</s>, and the southward course at the beginning of <s>Candrabhavana</s> (Cancer, the abode of the Moon).

body.text: iti |
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: ṛtuniścayāya āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of determining the seasons, he says:

children.translated_text: The seasons are: <s>Śiśira</s> (late winter), <s>Vasanta</s> (spring), <s>Grīṣma</s> (summer), <s>Ghanāgama</s> (rains), <s>Śarad</s> (autumn), and <s>Himāgamana</s> (early winter);
they are equal in duration to the Sun's traverse of two signs beginning from <s>Makara</s> (Capricorn).

body.text: iti |
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: anyat ca ã apakramavṛddhiḥ dhanuḥ mithunānte eva iti | rātridivasayoḥ mahatī vṛddhiḥ makarakarkaṭādau eva, na anyataḥ eva iti | pratyakṣasiddham idam iti | ataḥ ayanayugabhagaṇaparikalpanā mudhā |
body.translated_text: And further: the increase of declination [ends] at the end of <s>Dhanus</s> (Sagittarius) and <s>Mithuna</s> (Gemini) only. The greatest increase in the length of night and day occurs at the beginning of <s>Makara</s> and <s>Karkaṭa</s> only, and not from any other [point]. This is established by direct perception. Therefore, the postulation of <s>ayana</s>-revolutions in a <s>yuga</s> is futile.

body.text: atha idam praṣṭavyam ã sphuṭagatyā parigahyante āhosvit madhyamagatyā iti | yadi madhyamagatyā, [tadā] yāni sauryamānābhihitāni prayojanāni tāni madhyamagatyā prāpnuvanti, sphuṭagatyā ceṣyante | kāni punar tāni prayojanāni iti? ucyate ã
body.translated_text: Now, this must be asked: are [solar years] reckoned by the true (<s>sphuṭa</s>) motion or by the mean (<s>madhyama</s>) motion? If by the mean motion, then the purposes stated for the solar measure are achieved by the mean motion, [but] they are desired by the true motion. What then are those purposes? It is said:

children.text: vāyoḥ mūrcchanam abhrāṇām utpattiḥ cakṣuṣoḥ balam |
children.translated_text: The swelling of the wind, the arising of clouds, the strength of the eyes,
the onset of cold, heat, and rain, and the clarity of water,

children.text: sattvānām madalābhāḥ syuḥ ārtavaḥ ca api yoṣitām |
children.translated_text: the states of excitement in living beings, and also the menstrual periods of women,
and indeed the sprouting of fruits and flowers, the growth of leaves and shoots,

children.text: ayanānā[m ṛtūnām] ca muhūrtānām ca darśanam |
children.translated_text: the observation of the <s>ayanas</s> (solstices), the <s>ṛtus</s> (seasons), and the <s>muhūrtas</s> (auspicious moments),
the appearance of halos and <s>parīdhas</s> (mock suns), and of atmospheric circles likewise,
and also of <s>Gandharva</s>-cities (mirages) and of rainbows —

children.text: ulkānām aśanīnām ca sandhyayoḥ vidyutām tathā ||
children.translated_text: of meteors (<s>ulkā</s>) and thunderbolts (<s>aśani</s>), of the twilights (<s>sandhyā</s>), and of lightning,
of earthquakes (<s>bhūratha</s>), thunder (<s>abhranināda</s>), of the falling of fireballs (<s>dhiṣṇya</s>),
of the color-changes of luminaries, and of the movements of planets,

children.text: agneḥ auṣṇyasya śaktyoḥ ca vilayasya udbhavasya ca |
children.translated_text: of fire, of heat, of the two powers, and of dissolution and origination —
one should know the solar measure as the activator and the deactivator.

body.text: iti ādi prayojanāni |
body.translated_text: These and such are the purposes [of solar reckoning].

body.text:
yadi sphuṭagatyā tat etāni prayojanāni parigṛhītāni bhavanti, idam tu na siddhyati adhikāvamānām grahaṇam | yasmāt adhikāvamānām grahaṇam madhyamena mānena | atha katham sphuṭārtham vacanam madhyamagatipratipattaye bhaviṣyati | atha madhyamagatipratipattaye sphuṭārtham katham iti | na eṣaḥ doṣaḥ | "śalyartham kulyāḥ praṇīyante, tābhyaḥ ca pānīyam pīyate, tāsu ca upaspṛśyate" [aṣṭādhyāyī, 1.1.22 pātañjalabhāṣyam] iti siddham | etat ubhayagrahaṇāt
ubhayam atra parigṛhyate iti madhyamagatyā sphuṭagatyā ca | madhyamagatyā adhikāvamānām grahaṇam siddham, sphuṭagatyā ca saṃhitākārābhihitāni prayojanāni |
body.translated_text: If by the true motion these purposes are fulfilled, then this does not work for the intercalary and omitted [day computations]. Since the intercalary and omitted [days] are computed by the mean measure. Now, how can a statement intended for true [motion] serve for understanding mean motion? And [conversely], if intended for understanding mean motion, how can it be for the true [purpose]? There is no fault here. [Just as] 'Canals are dug for the purpose of rice cultivation, and from them water is drunk, and in them ablutions are performed' [<s>Aṣṭādhyāyī</s> 1.1.22, <s>Patañjali</s>'s <s>Bhāṣya</s>] — this is established. Since both are grasped by this [statement], both are included here — by the mean motion and by the true motion. By the mean motion, the computation of intercalary and omitted [days] is established; and by the true motion, the purposes stated by the authors of <s>Saṃhitā</s> [texts].

body.text: raviśaśiyogāḥ bhavanti śaśimāsāḥ | raveḥ śaśinaḥ ca yogāḥ raviśaśiyogāḥ | bhavanti śaśimāsāḥ | ye yuge raviśaśiyogāḥ abhihitāḥ te śaśimāsāḥ | te ca prāg yathā siddhyanti tathā vyākhyātam | śaśimāsaiḥ śaśidivasaghaṭikāḥ vyākhyātāḥ | śaśimāsena kāni punar prayojanāni?
body.translated_text: The conjunctions of the Sun and Moon are the lunar months. The conjunctions of the Sun and Moon are '<s>raviśaśiyogāḥ</s>' (Sun-Moon conjunctions). They become lunar months. The Sun-Moon conjunctions stated for a <s>yuga</s> are the lunar months. And how they are established has been explained previously. From the lunar months, the lunar days and <s>ghaṭikās</s> are explained. What further are the purposes of the lunar month?

children.text: darśam ca paurṇamāsam ca tathejyādyāḥ kriyā bhuvi |
children.translated_text: The new-moon (<s>darśa</s>) and full-moon (<s>paurṇamāsa</s>) rites, as well as sacrifices (<s>ijyā</s>) and other rituals on earth,

children.text: parvāṇām ca parijñānam tithīnām pratyayaḥ tathā ||
children.translated_text: the knowledge of the <s>parvans</s> (junctures/eclipses), and similarly the verification of <s>tithis</s> (lunar days),

children.text: prābalyam auṣadhīnām ca rasānām vyaktiḥ eva ca |
children.translated_text: the potency of herbs, and the manifestation of [bodily] humors,

children.text: pūraṇam hīnatā ca indoḥ tathā eva lavaṇāmbhasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the waxing and waning of the Moon, and similarly of the salt-ocean,

children.text: garbhāṇām jīvanam ca api tathā api ayanam eva ca |
children.translated_text: the sustenance of embryos, and also the [solstitial] turning (<s>ayana</s>),
the arrival and approach of <s>Rāhu</s> [the eclipse-causer] — these are dependent on the lunar measure.

body.text: evam ādīni prayojanāni |
body.translated_text: Such and similar are the purposes [of lunar reckoning].

body.text: ravibhūyogāḥ divasāḥ | raveḥ bhuvaḥ ca yogāḥ ravibhūyogāḥ | ye yuge ravibhūyogāḥ te yuge bhūdivasāḥ | bhūdivasaḥ nāma raveḥ ardhodayāt prabhṛti punar ardhodayam iti | sāvanaḥ divasaḥ bhūdivasaḥ iti ucyate | romakaiḥ sa eva bhūdivasaḥ ravyudayaḥ iti saṃjñitaḥ | kāni punar sāvanamānasya prayojanāni?
body.translated_text: The conjunctions of the Sun and Earth are days. The conjunctions of the Sun and Earth are '<s>ravibhūyogāḥ</s>.' The Sun-Earth conjunctions in a <s>yuga</s> are the terrestrial days in a <s>yuga</s>. A terrestrial day (<s>bhūdivasa</s>) is [defined as] from one half-rising of the Sun to the next half-rising. A civil day (<s>sāvana divasa</s>) is called a terrestrial day. By the <s>Romakas</s> (Greco-Roman astronomers), that same terrestrial day is designated as 'Sun-rise' (<s>ravyudaya</s>). What then are the purposes of the civil measure?

children.translated_text: The knowledge of the time of sacrifice, and the <s>savanas</s> (pressings) in sacrifices,
vows, the time of consecration (<s>dīkṣā</s>), and the tonsure (<s>cūḍā</s>) and investiture (<s>upanayana</s>) [ceremonies],

children.text: āyuṣām ca api nirlekhā prayogāṇām ca vṛddhayaḥ |
children.translated_text: the calculation of lifespans, and the progressions of [ritual] performances,
the knowledge of planetary motions, and journeys of [astrological] predictions,

children.text: yāni ca api evam ādīni saṅkhyoddiṣṭāni tāni vai |
children.translated_text: and whatever other such things are specified by count —

children.text: sāvanena eva mānena gaṇyante iti niścayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: they are certainly reckoned by the civil measure alone.

body.text: etāni prayojanāni |
body.translated_text: These are the purposes [of civil reckoning].

body.text:
bhāvartāḥ ca api nākṣatrāḥ | bhānām āvartāḥ bhāvartāḥ, bhacakrabhramaṇāni | tat ca bhacakram kim ādiḥ iti etat vicāryam | yadi meṣādiḥ syāt [tadā] meṣādisthe savitari savitṛbhacakrādyoḥ yugapat udayaḥ, dvitīyaḥ punar anudite eva savitari bhacakrādyudayaḥ, na ca bhacakrādidvayodayāntare ṣaṣṭiḥ nāḍyaḥ | tathā ca "prāṇena iti kalām bham" [gītikāí, 6] iti cakraliptānām ahorātraghaṭikāpramāṇaliptānām ca tulyatā na upapadyate, yasmāt apūrṇe eva ahorātre
bhacakrādiḥ udeti | yadā punar ādityodayaḥ bhacakrādiḥ parigṛhyate tadā ahorātraprāṇāḥ svadeśarāśyudayaprāṇatulyāḥ | te ca khakhaṣaḍghanatulyāḥ | bhacakraliptāḥ ca tāvatyaḥ iti etat upapannam |
body.translated_text: And the sidereal revolutions (<s>bhāvarta</s>) are also sidereal (<s>nākṣatra</s>). The revolutions of the stars (<s>bha</s>) are '<s>bhāvartāḥ</s>' — the rotations of the stellar sphere. And what is the beginning of that stellar sphere? This must be investigated. If it begins from <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries), then when the Sun is at the beginning of <s>Meṣa</s>, the Sun and the beginning of the stellar sphere rise simultaneously; the second [rising of the stellar sphere] occurs when the Sun has not yet risen, and sixty <s>nāḍīs</s> do not [elapse] between two risings of the stellar-sphere beginning. And thus, [the statement] 'In one <s>prāṇa</s>, the stellar sphere moves one minute' [<s>Gītikā</s> 6] — the equality of the stellar-sphere minutes and the day-night <s>ghaṭikā</s>-measure minutes would not be established, since the stellar-sphere beginning rises before the day-night [period] is complete. But when the sunrise is taken as the beginning of the stellar sphere, then the day-night <s>prāṇas</s> equal the local sign-rising <s>prāṇas</s>. And those equal the cube of void-void-six [= 21,600]. And the stellar-sphere minutes are exactly that many — so this is established.

body.text:
anyat ca ã udayalagnavidhiḥ sūryāt eva pravartate, audayikāt ca raveḥ | sa ceṣṭakāle svābhīṣṭakālāditya[rāśeḥ vicārya]māṇaḥ yāvat punar udayaḥ iti tāvat na antaram vidadhāti | tasmāt ravyudayaḥ eva bhacakrādiḥ, vyavahāraprasiddhyartham | yadi evam grahabhuktarāśayaḥ ravyākrāntarāśipradeśāt eva prāpnuvanti? na eṣaḥ doṣaḥ, "budhāhnyajārkodayāt ca laṅkāyām" [gītikāí, 4] iti eṣām ajādinirūpaṇāt | kubhagaṇāḥ ca yugādyantayoḥ ajārkodayāt eva pratiparisamāptāḥ
iti teṣām ca ajāditā siddhā | te eva yugabhacakrāvartāḥ nākṣatradivasāḥ bhūdivasāḥ iti, divasagrahaṇānuvartanāt | ke punar te bhāvartāḥ? ye kubhagaṇāḥ, "ku ṅiśibuṇlṛṣkhṛ" [1582237500] iti gītikāsu [gītikāí, 3] uktāḥ | katham ete kubhagaṇāḥ bhāvartāḥ iti uktāḥ? bhacakraprativaddhāni nakṣatrāṇi | tasya pravahākṣepāt aparām diśam āsādayanti | nakṣatrāṇi bhuvam svagatyā prāṅmukham bhramantīm iva paśyanti iti anayā gatyā bhuvaḥ bhagaṇānirdeśāḥ | tena uktam
ã "bhāvartāḥ ca api nākṣatrāḥ" iti | anye punar "kva āvartāḥ ca api nākṣatrāḥ" iti paṭhanti | teṣā pāṭhāt eva hi sarvam upapannam |
body.translated_text: Moreover: the rising-<s>lagna</s> (ascendant) procedure commences from the Sun alone, and from the risen Sun. That [procedure], being examined from the desired-time Sun-sign until the next rising, does not create a difference. Therefore, the sunrise itself is the beginning of the stellar sphere — for the sake of practical convention. If so, would not the signs traversed by the planets be reckoned from the sign-position occupied by the Sun? There is no fault, because [the statement] 'Mercury, on a conjunction day, from sunrise at <s>Laṅkā</s>' [<s>Gītikā</s> 4] determines them from the beginning of <s>Aja</s> (Aries). And the Earth's revolutions are completed from the beginning of <s>Aja</s>-Sun-rise at the beginning and end of a <s>yuga</s> — so their beginning from <s>Aja</s> is established. Those very <s>yuga</s>-stellar-sphere revolutions are sidereal days [and] terrestrial days — since the term 'day' continues [to apply]. What then are those stellar revolutions? They are the Earth's revolutions — stated in the <s>Gītikās</s> as 'the Earth, <s>ṅiśibuṇlṛṣkhṛ</s>' [= 1,582,237,500] [<s>Gītikā</s> 3]. How are these Earth's revolutions called stellar revolutions? The <s>nakṣatras</s> (asterisms) are bound to the stellar sphere. Due to the <s>pravaha</s> wind's thrust, they reach the western direction. The <s>nakṣatras</s> observe the Earth as if it were revolving eastward by its own motion — by this motion, the Earth's revolutions are stated. Hence it is said: 'And the sidereal revolutions are also sidereal.' Others, however, read 'where are the revolutions, and also sidereal.' From their reading itself, everything is established.

body.text: atha anye punar anyathā varṇayanti ã
body.translated_text: Now, others describe it differently:

children.text: ddarśāt darśaḥ cāndraḥ triṃśat divasāḥ tu sāvanaḥ māsaḥ |
children.translated_text: From new-moon to new-moon is a lunar [month]; thirty days is a civil month;
a solar [month] is the traversal of one sign by the Sun; and a sidereal [month] is a revolution of the Moon.

body.text: lāṭadevasya kṛtitaḥ
body.translated_text: From the work of <s>Lāṭadeva</s>

body.text:
darśāt darśaḥ cāndraḥ iti sūryācandramasoḥ yaḥ paraḥ sannikarṣaḥ sa darśaśabdena ucyate, sa ca tayoḥ yogaḥ | "raviśaśiyogāḥ bhavanti śaśimāsāḥ" iti tulyam lakṣaṇam | triṃśat divasāḥ tu sāvanaḥ māsaḥ iti etat api "ravyudayāḥ triṃśat " iti tulyam | sauryaḥ arkarāśibhogaḥ iti "ravibhagaṇāḥ ravyabdāḥ", "raveḥ rāśayaḥ api ravimāsāḥ" iti etat api tulyam lakṣaṇam | "nākṣatram ca indumaṇḍalakam" iti indoḥ maṇḍalam nākṣatraḥ māsaḥ iti | tatra pratyaham yaḥ candrabhogaḥ
sa tanmāsāvayavaḥ iti |
body.translated_text: 'From new-moon to new-moon is lunar' — the closest proximity of the Sun and Moon is called by the word '<s>darśa</s>' (new-moon), and that is their conjunction. 'The conjunctions of the Sun and Moon are the lunar months' — the definition is the same. 'Thirty days is a civil month' — this too is the same as 'thirty sun-rises.' 'A solar [month] is the traversal of one sign by the Sun' — [this equals] 'the Sun's revolutions are solar years,' and 'the Sun's signs are also solar months' — this definition too is the same. 'And the sidereal [month] is a revolution of the Moon' — the Moon's revolution is a sidereal month. There, the daily traversal of the Moon is a component of that month.

body.text: nakṣatrāṇi api vibhajyante | tat yathā ã yaḥ candrabhagaṇasya triṃśadbhāgaḥ sa nākṣatraḥ divasaḥ | evam navanakṣatradaśabhāgaḥ nākṣatraḥ divasaḥ iti etat abhinnam lakṣaṇam |
body.translated_text: The <s>nakṣatras</s> too are divided [thus]: The thirtieth part of the Moon's revolution is a sidereal day. Thus, [one-thirtieth of] nine-nine-asterism-ten-parts is a sidereal day — this is the same definition.

body.text:
asmākam ācāryeṇa svatantrāntarāviruddhaprakriyāpratipādanārtham idam uktam "bhāvartāḥ ca api nākṣatrāḥ" iti | kā ca svatantrāntaraprakriyā? "prāṇena eti kalām bham" [gītikāí, 6] iti, prāṇena kalām bham gacchati iti jyotiścakraliptānām bhāvartaprāṇānām ca tulyatve jyādayaḥ vidhayaḥ siddhyante, na anyathā iti iyam prakriyā | yeṣām ca "nākṣatram ca indumaṇḍalakam" iti lakṣaṇam, taiḥ saṃhitākārābhihitaprayojanasiddhyartham uktam | atra ekena lakṣaṇena
prayojanasya aparigrahāt lakṣaṇadvayam idam iṣyate | katham? tatra āvṛttiḥ ekaśeṣaḥ iti, bhāvartaśabdasya ekaśeṣavyākhyānāt bhāvartāḥ ca bhāvartāḥ ca, bhāvartāḥ | bhāni jyotīṃṣi aśvinyādīni | teṣām āvartāḥ bhāvartāḥ, bhaparyayāḥ iti arthaḥ | paryayaḥ ca nakṣatrāṇām candraviṣayaḥ eva parigṛhyate, lokavyavahārāt | lokaḥ hi candrākrāntanakṣatraiḥ eva vyavaharati | athavā anyārtham prakṛtam anyārtham api bhavati, "śālyartham kulyāḥ praṇīyante, tāsu ca upaspṛśyate"
[aṣṭādhyāyī, 1.1.22, pātañjalamahābhāṣyam] iti | athavā "bhāvartaḥ ca nākṣatraḥ" iti ekavacanena siddhe "bhāvartāḥ ca nākṣatrāḥ" iti bahuvacananirdeśam kurvan ācāryaḥ jñāpayati nākṣatrasya anekalakṣaṇam iti | athavā cakāraḥ atra prayuktaḥ, na tena atra kaścit arthaḥ sādhyate, atha ca prayuktena manyāmahe nākṣatrasya anekam lakṣaṇam iti | tat ca anekam lakṣaṇam yathā vyavasthitam tathā vyākhyātam iti ataḥ lakṣaṇadvayam api svasiddhāntasiddham |
body.translated_text: Our <s>ācārya</s> has stated this — 'And the sidereal revolutions are also sidereal' — for the purpose of demonstrating a procedure not contradicted by [the procedures of] other treatises. And what is that procedure of other treatises? '[The stellar sphere] moves one minute in one <s>prāṇa</s>' [<s>Gītikā</s> 6] — when one <s>prāṇa</s> moves one minute of the stellar sphere, the procedures such as sine-computations are established only when the stellar-sphere minutes and stellar-revolution <s>prāṇas</s> are equal, not otherwise — this is the procedure. And for those whose definition is 'The sidereal [month] is a revolution of the Moon,' it is stated for the purpose of establishing the uses described by the <s>Saṃhitā</s> authors. Here, since a single definition does not encompass [all] purposes, this dual definition is accepted. How? There, the word '<s>bhāvarta</s>' is explained as an <s>ekaśeṣa</s> (single-remainder) compound: '<s>bhāvartāḥ</s> and <s>bhāvartāḥ</s>' [= two types of] '<s>bhāvartāḥ</s>.' '<s>Bha</s>' means the luminaries beginning with <s>Aśvinī</s>. Their revolutions are '<s>bhāvartāḥ</s>' — meaning stellar cycles. And the cycle of <s>nakṣatras</s> is understood as pertaining to the Moon alone, from common usage. For the world transacts only with the <s>nakṣatras</s> occupied by the Moon. Alternatively, what is intended for one purpose may also serve another — 'canals are dug for rice, and in them ablutions are performed.' Or, when the singular '<s>bhāvartaḥ</s> and <s>nākṣatraḥ</s>' would have sufficed, the <s>ācārya</s>, by using the plural '<s>bhāvartāḥ</s> and <s>nākṣatrāḥ</s>,' indicates that the sidereal [measure] has multiple definitions. Or, the particle 'ca' is used here — no purpose is served by it, but since it is used, we understand that the sidereal [measure] has multiple definitions. And that multiple definition, as it has been established, has been explained — hence the dual definition is established in his own system.

body.text: atha nākṣatrasya mānasya kāni prayojanāni?
body.translated_text: Now, what are the purposes of the sidereal measure?

children.translated_text: The completions and commencements of all years, months, seasons, and <s>parvans</s> (junctures),
and of all <s>ayanas</s> (solstitial periods),

body.text: śubhāśubham ca lokānām mānam unmānam eva vā |
body.translated_text: and the auspiciousness and inauspiciousness of the worlds, and the measurement or the non-measurement —

body.text: iti evamādīni prayojanāni |
body.translated_text: such and similar are the purposes.

body.text: atha iyam uktiḥ vāgvāgurā kṣudravidrāvaṇaparā nākṣatramānapradarśitaprayojanaiḥ lakṣyate "saṃvatsarāṇām māsānām ṛtūnām" iti | saṃvatsarāṇām tāvat pratipacchedanimittam nākṣatram [na] bhavati, yataḥ saṃvatsaraḥ śāstre caitraśuklādeḥ pravartate | sa ca caitraśuklādiḥ cāndreṇa upalakṣyate | saṃhitākārāṇām ca bṛhaspaticāre yaḥ saṃvatsaraḥ bṛhaspateḥ nakṣatrodayāt pravartate ã
body.translated_text: Now, this statement is a verbal trap aimed at driving away the small-minded, [as] is shown by the purposes demonstrated for the sidereal measure: 'of years, months, seasons.' First, for years, the sidereal [measure] is not the discriminating criterion, since the year in [our] treatise commences from the bright half of <s>Caitra</s>. And that beginning of the bright half of <s>Caitra</s> is identified by the lunar [measure]. And for the <s>Saṃhitā</s> authors, the year in [the cycle of] <s>Bṛhaspati</s>'s (Jupiter's) course commences from the rising of the <s>nakṣatra</s> occupied by <s>Bṛhaspati</s>:

body.text: yasmin udeti nakṣatre pravāsopagataḥ aṅgirāḥ |
body.translated_text: In whichever <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Aṅgiras</s> (Jupiter), who has gone abroad, rises —

body.text:
iti | māsānām api na bhavati | yasmin kṛttikābhiḥ yutaḥ candramāḥ, asmin māse ardhamāse ca iti kārtikaḥ māsaḥ | sa candranakṣatrayogaviśeṣaḥ cāndraḥ mānaviśeṣaḥ | ṛtūnām ayanānām [ca jñānam] sauryeṇa mānena iti pradarsitam eva asmābhiḥ | tasmāt etat na nākṣatramānam | yaiḥ "nākṣatram ca indumaṇḍalakam" iti asya anuvartanāt "bhāvartāḥ ca nākṣatrāḥ" iti asya śabdārthavyākhyāne naikaśeṣabahuvacananirdeśaḥ [kṛtaḥ] "ca"-śabdāt iti budhaiḥ eva viditaparamārthaiḥ
mukham āyāsitam | tasmāt asmākam ācāryeṇa atīndriyārthadarśinā abhihitam ācāryāryabhaṭena tat eva nākṣatramānam | tasmāt "iyam uktiḥ vagvāgurā kṣudravidrāvaṇaparā nākṣatramānapradarśitaprayojanaiḥ lakṣyate" iti suṣṭhu uktam |
  atha etāni saurya-sāvana-cāndra-nākṣatrāṇi mānāni madhyamagatyā pratipāditāni | tatprayojanārtham sphuṭagatyā pratipattavyāni iti pradiṣṭam | ācāryalāṭadevena tu sphuṭagatyā eva pratipāditāni ã
body.translated_text: And for months, it does not [serve as the criterion] either. In whichever [<s>nakṣatra</s>] the Moon is conjoined with <s>Kṛttikā</s>, in that month and half-month — that is the month of <s>Kārtika</s>. That particular conjunction of the Moon with a <s>nakṣatra</s> is a particular lunar measure. The knowledge of seasons and <s>ayanas</s> [is accomplished] by the solar measure — this has already been demonstrated by us. Therefore, this is not the sidereal measure. By those who, following the [reading] 'The sidereal [month] is a revolution of the Moon,' have explained the word-meaning of 'And the sidereal revolutions are also sidereal' by a non-<s>ekaśeṣa</s> plural usage [based on] the particle 'ca' — their mouths have been wearied [in vain]; only the wise who know the ultimate truth [understand this]. Therefore, what was stated by our <s>ācārya</s>, the seer of supersensible truths, <s>Āryabhaṭa</s> — that alone is the sidereal measure. Therefore, the statement 'This utterance is a verbal trap aimed at driving away the small-minded, as shown by the purposes demonstrated for the sidereal measure' — this is well said. Now, these solar, civil, lunar, and sidereal measures have been demonstrated by the mean motion. For the purpose of [applying] those, they are to be understood by the true motion — this has been indicated. But by the teacher <s>Lāṭadeva</s>, they have been demonstrated by the true motion alone:

body.text: darśāt darśaḥ cāndraḥ triṃśat divasāḥ tu sāvanaḥ māsaḥ |
body.translated_text: From new-moon to new-moon is a lunar [month]; thirty days is a civil month;

body.text: iti ādigranthena iti |
body.translated_text: thus [it is stated] in [his] earlier treatise.

body.text:
atra ca ayam praśnaḥ ã "avamādhimāsakaiḥ vinā dyugaṇam" iti | yātavarṣāṇi māsīkṛtya vartamānamāsaiḥ saṃyojya trairāśikam ã yadi yugaravimāsaiḥ yugacāndramāsāḥ labhyante, [tadā] etaiḥ [raviḥ] māsaiḥ kiyantaḥ cāndramāsāḥ iti, labdham cāndramāsāḥ | te triṃśadguṇāḥ vartamānatithiyuktāḥ kāryāḥ | tataḥ trairāśikam ã yadi yugacāndradivasaiḥ yugāhargaṇaḥ labhyate [tadā] etaiḥ cāndradivasaiḥ kim iti, ahargaṇaḥ labhyate | tatra ekaḥ prakṣepaḥ | atha kaḥ
ca asau ekaḥ prakṣepaḥ? ucyate ã yaḥ asau labhyate ahargaṇaḥ sa atītaḥ | śeṣaḥ vartamānaḥ | vartamānena ahargaṇaḥ bhavati iti ekaḥ prakṣepaḥ | "tena divākaroḍupau" iti etat uttaratra vakṣyate | tābhyām sphuṭaparvadarśanam iti |
body.translated_text: And here is this problem: '<s>ahargaṇa</s> (day-count) without intercalary months and omitted days.' Having converted the elapsed years into months and adding the current months, the Rule of Three [is applied]: if from the <s>yuga</s>-solar-months the <s>yuga</s>-lunar-months are obtained, then from these solar months, how many lunar months? — the result is the lunar months. Those, multiplied by thirty and joined with the current <s>tithis</s> (lunar days), are to be computed. Then the Rule of Three: if from the <s>yuga</s>-lunar-days the <s>yuga</s>-<s>ahargaṇa</s> is obtained, then from these lunar days, what? — the <s>ahargaṇa</s> is obtained. There, one is added. Now what is that addition of one? It is said: the <s>ahargaṇa</s> that is obtained — that is elapsed. The remainder is the current [day]. The <s>ahargaṇa</s> becomes [complete] with the current [day] — hence the addition of one. 'By that, the Sun and Moon [are found]' — this will be stated later. From those two, the observation of the true <s>parva</s> (conjunction/opposition) [is made].

body.text:
candrādityābhyām vinā sphuṭatithyānayanam | tat yathā ã "[yadi] yugāhargaṇena candravarṣāṇi vasumunigiriyamaviṣayakṛtaveda [4452778] tulyāni labhyante, tadā anena iṣṭāhargaṇena kiyanti iti varṣāṇi labhyante | śeṣe dvādaśā[di]guṇite māsa-divasa-ghaṭikā-vighaṭikāḥ ca labhyante | evam madhyamā tithiḥ bhavati | atha śaśyuccanīcaparivartaiḥ trairāśikam ã yadi yugāhargaṇena śaśyuccanīcaparivartāḥ labhyante, [tadā] anena iṣṭāhargaṇena kiyantaḥ iti, atītāḥ
parivartāḥ labhyante | śeṣe dvādaśādiguṇite rāśyādayaḥ labhyante | trirāśirahitam śaśikendram | tataḥ phalam śaśibhuktiḥ ca ānīyate | phalasya dvādaśabhiḥ bhāge nāḍyaḥ vināḍyaḥ ca labhyante | tāvat madhyamatithau yathānyāyena ṛṇam dhanam vā kartavyam | sūryānayanārtham trairāśikam ã yadi yugāhargaṇena vasumunigiriyamadahanendu[132778]tulyāni adhikavarṣāṇi labhyante, tadā kaliyātāhargaṇena kiyantaḥ iti, varṣa-māsa-divasa-ghaṭikāḥ labhyante |
pratirāśitamadhyamatithivarṣādibhyaḥ te śodhyāḥ śeṣam ravivarṣādayaḥ | tebhyaḥ māsadvayam [2] ca aṣṭādaśa [18] ca divasān apanīya ravikendram bhavati | tena phalānayanam bhaktyānayanam ca | phalasya dvādaśabhiḥ bhāge labdhāḥ nāḍyaḥ vināḍyaḥ ca | tithau eva ṛṇadhanavyatyāsam kuryāt | atha kim iti ṛṇadhanavyatyāsaḥ kriyate? ucyate ã sūryasya yat ṛṇam tat titheḥ upacayaḥ, dhanam yat tat apacayaḥ iti | evam tithiḥ niṣpannā bhavati | tataḥ idam kriyate ã yadi
madhyamabhuktyantareṇa ṣaṣṭiḥ nāḍyaḥ labhyante, [tadā] sphuṭagatyantareṇa kiyatya iti, gatyantaranāḍyaḥ upalabhyante | tābhiḥ trairāśikam ã yadi etābhiḥ gatyantaranāḍikābhiḥ ṣaṣṭiḥ nāḍyaḥ labhyante, [tadā] anena tithiśeṣeṇa kiyatya iti tithināḍyaḥ vināḍyaḥ ca labhyante | athavā trairāśikadvayam bhaṅktvā idam karma kriyate | madhyamabhuktyantareṇa tithiśeṣam guṇayitvā sphuṭabhuktyantareṇa bhāgasiddham ghaṭikāvighaṭikāḥ ca | katham punar trairāśikadvayam
bhinnam? ucyate ã yadi madhyamabhuktyantareṇa ṣaṣṭiḥ nāḍyaḥ labhyante [tadā] sphuṭabhuktyantareṇa kiyatya iti ekam trairāśikam | punar ã labdhena phalena yadi ṣaṣṭiḥ nāḍyaḥ, [tadā] anena tithiśeṣeṇa kiyatya iti | yaḥ pūrvatrairāśike guṇakāraḥ sa iha arthāt bhāgahāraḥ iti | atha deśāntaraviśeṣeṇa ca akṣaviśeṣeṇa ca yat phalam upajāyate tat api yuktyā yojayitavyam iti || 5 ||
body.translated_text: Finding the true <s>tithi</s> without [separately computing] the Moon and Sun. That is as follows: 'If from the <s>yuga-ahargaṇa</s>, lunar years equal to <s>Vasu</s>-sage-mountain-<s>Yama</s>-object-product-<s>Veda</s> [= 4,452,778] are obtained, then from this desired <s>ahargaṇa</s>, how many?' — years are obtained. When the remainder is multiplied by twelve and so on, months, days, <s>ghaṭikās</s> (time-units), and <s>vighaṭikās</s> (sub-time-units) are obtained. Thus the mean <s>tithi</s> is obtained. Now, the Rule of Three with the Moon's apogee-perigee revolutions: 'If from the <s>yuga-ahargaṇa</s>, the Moon's apogee-perigee revolutions are obtained, then from this desired <s>ahargaṇa</s>, how many?' — the elapsed revolutions are obtained. When the remainder is multiplied by twelve and so on, signs and so forth are obtained. Subtracting three signs gives the Moon's <s>kendra</s> (anomaly). From that, the equation (<s>phala</s>) and the Moon's daily motion (<s>bhukti</s>) are derived. When the equation is divided by twelve, <s>nāḍīs</s> (time-units) and <s>vināḍīs</s> (sub-time-units) are obtained. That much is to be applied as subtractive or additive to the mean <s>tithi</s> as appropriate. For finding the Sun, the Rule of Three: 'If from the <s>yuga-ahargaṇa</s>, excess years equal to <s>Vasu</s>-sage-mountain-<s>Yama</s>-fire-Moon [= 132,778] are obtained, then from the <s>Kali</s>-elapsed <s>ahargaṇa</s>, how many?' — years, months, days, <s>ghaṭikās</s> are obtained. These are to be subtracted from the previously computed mean-<s>tithi</s> years and so forth. The remainder gives the solar years and so on. From those, subtracting two months [2] and eighteen [18] days gives the Sun's <s>kendra</s> (anomaly). From that, the equation and daily motion are found. When the equation is divided by twelve, the obtained <s>nāḍīs</s> and <s>vināḍīs</s> [are found]. The subtractive-additive [correction] should be applied to the <s>tithi</s> itself in reverse. Now why is the subtractive-additive reversed? It is said: what is subtractive for the Sun is accumulative for the <s>tithi</s>; what is additive is diminutive. Thus the <s>tithi</s> is accomplished. Then this is done: 'If from the mean daily-motion difference, sixty <s>nāḍīs</s> are obtained, then from the true daily-motion difference, how many?' — the daily-motion-difference <s>nāḍīs</s> are found. With those, the Rule of Three: 'If from these daily-motion-difference <s>nāḍikās</s>, sixty <s>nāḍīs</s> are obtained, then from this <s>tithi</s>-remainder, how many?' — <s>tithi</s>-<s>nāḍīs</s> and <s>vināḍīs</s> are obtained. Or, breaking [this into] two Rules of Three, this computation is done: multiplying the <s>tithi</s>-remainder by the mean daily-motion difference and dividing by the true daily-motion difference gives the accomplished <s>ghaṭikās</s> and <s>vighaṭikās</s>. But how are the two Rules of Three broken? It is said: 'If from the mean daily-motion difference sixty <s>nāḍīs</s> are obtained, then from the true daily-motion difference how many?' — this is one Rule of Three. Again: 'If from the obtained result sixty <s>nāḍīs</s> [are obtained], then from this <s>tithi</s>-remainder how many?' In the first Rule of Three, the <s>yuga</s>-intercalary-months is the multiplier; in the second Rule of Three it is the divisor — hence, because the multiplier and divisor are equal, they cancel. Moreover, the result arising from the difference of longitude and the difference of latitude is also to be applied with proper reasoning. // 5 //

body.text: adhimāsāvamadināni
body.translated_text: Intercalary months and omitted days

body.text: adhimāsāvamaparijñānāya āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of knowing the intercalary months and omitted days, he says:

children.text: adhimāsakāḥ yuge te ravimāsebhyaḥ adhikāḥ tu ye cāndrāḥ |
children.translated_text: The intercalary months in a <s>yuga</s> are those lunar [months] that are in excess of the solar months;
the lunar days diminished by civil days are to be known as <s>tithipralaya</s> (destroyed <s>tithis</s>, i.e., omitted days). // 6 //

body.text:
ye ravimāsebhyaḥ adhikāḥ cāndramāsāḥ te yuge yuge adhimāsāḥ bhavanti, ye ca bhūdivasonāḥ śaśidivasāḥ te yuge tithipralayāḥ | pralayaḥ vināśaḥ | tithīnām pralayāḥ tithipralayāḥ | avamarātrāṇi iti arthaḥ | evam bruvatā etat pradarśitam bhavati ã sauryacāndrāntaram adhimāsabhogaḥ, sāvamam sāvanam cāndram mānam iti | adhikāvamayoḥ madhyamagatyā upacayaḥ iti uktam | yadi sphuṭagatyā syāt tadā dvitīyāyām pravṛttāyām pratipat tṛtīyā [ni]vṛttipravṛttī
na staḥ | adhimāsāvamaiḥ kim nirvartyate? ahargaṇaḥ iti āha | na etat asti, vinā api adhimāsāvamaiḥ ahargaṇasya nirvartitatvāt | na eṣaḥ doṣaḥ, upāyāntaratvāt | adhimāsāvamaiḥ vinā ahargaṇasya sādhanam pradarśitam | yena ca adhimāsāvamaiḥ ahargaṇaḥ labhyate sa upāyaḥ pradarśayitavyaḥ | na etat asti, ekopāyatvāt | sa ca ayam ca ekaḥ upāyaḥ | katham ekopāyatā? ye cāndramāsāḥ te sādhikāḥ teṣām sādhikatvāt sādhikaḥ eva māsarāśiḥ labhyate | punar api ca bhūdivasānām
rahitāvamatvāt trairāśikena rahitāvamaḥ ahargaṇaḥ labhyate | atha kaścit laghūkaraṇārthī guṇakārāt bhāgahāram apanayet tasya śeṣaguṇite labdham pratirāśitaguṇye [kṣipet] | yadi bhāgahārāt avaśiṣyate tatra śeṣaguṇite labdham guṇyāt pratirāśitāt apanīyam iti eṣaḥ gaṇitanyāyaḥ | atha atra guṇakārādhikatvāt māsāḥ kṣipyante bhāgahārādhikatvāt divasāḥ apacīyante iti ekopāyatā | tasmāt na arthaḥ anayā kārikayā, tathāpi lokavyavahārārtham adhimāsāvamānām
upadeśaḥ kartavyaḥ | lokaḥ ca adhimāsāvamaiḥ vyavaharati | uktam ca ã "karaṇādhiṣṭhitam adhimāsakam kuryāt", "triśatam sacatuṣpañcāśa[tam a]horātrāṇām karma sāṃvatsaraḥ" iti | adhimāsārtham trairāśikam ã yadi yugavarṣaiḥ māsaiḥ vā yugādhimāsakāḥ labhyante, tataḥ yātavarṣādibhiḥ kiyantaḥ iti adhimāsakalabdhiḥ | evam eva avamānām cāndradivasaiḥ iti |
body.translated_text: Those lunar months that are in excess of the solar months — they are the intercalary months in each <s>yuga</s>. And the lunar days diminished by the civil days — they are the <s>tithipralaya</s> (destroyed <s>tithis</s>) in the <s>yuga</s>. <s>Pralaya</s> means destruction. The destruction of <s>tithis</s> is <s>tithipralaya</s>. The meaning is <s>avamarātra</s> (omitted night/day). By saying this, the following is demonstrated: the difference between solar and lunar [months] is the intercalary-month accumulation; the <s>sāvana</s> (civil) [day-count] is the civil measure, and the <s>cāndra</s> (lunar) [day-count is the lunar] measure. It has been said that the accumulation of intercalary and omitted [days] is by the mean motion. If it were by the true motion, then when the second [tithi] has commenced, the first day [and] the third [tithi's] cessation and commencement would not exist. What is accomplished by intercalary months and omitted days? The <s>ahargaṇa</s> — he says. This is not so, since the <s>ahargaṇa</s> is accomplished even without intercalary months and omitted days. This is no fault, because it is an alternative method. The accomplishment of the <s>ahargaṇa</s> without intercalary months and omitted days has been demonstrated. But the method by which the <s>ahargaṇa</s> is obtained through intercalary months and omitted days — that method is to be shown. This is not so, because there is [only] one method. This and the other are one [and the same] method. How is there oneness of method? The lunar months have intercalary [months] included; because of their inclusion, the month-count obtained already contains the intercalary [months]. And again, because the civil days have the omitted [days] already removed, by the Rule of Three the <s>ahargaṇa</s> obtained already has the omitted [days] removed. Now, if someone seeking simplification were to subtract the divisor from the multiplier — the result [from the remainder] multiplied [by the quotient] would be added to the [previously] computed multiplicand. If a remainder is left from the divisor, then the result from the remainder-multiplication is to be subtracted from the previously computed multiplicand — this is the rule of arithmetic. Now here, because the multiplier is greater, months are added; because the divisor is greater, days are diminished — hence the oneness of method. Therefore, this verse has no [independent] purpose. Nevertheless, for the sake of worldly practice, the instruction of intercalary months and omitted days must be given. And the world does use intercalary months and omitted days. As it is said: 'One should make the intercalary month based on the astronomical manual' and 'Three hundred and fifty-four days-and-nights constitute one year's work.' For finding the intercalary [months], the Rule of Three: 'If from the <s>yuga</s>-years or [yuga]-months the <s>yuga</s>-intercalary months are obtained, then from the elapsed years and so on, how many?' — the intercalary-month result [is obtained]. Similarly for the omitted [days], with lunar days.

body.text:
atra ca ayam praśnaḥ ã "tena divākaroḍupau" iti ahargaṇena vinā candrādityānayanam | tat yathā ã yātavarṣeṣu dvādaśaguṇiteṣu gatamāsān kṣipet | tataḥ triṃśadguṇiteṣu divasān prakṣipya trairāśikam ã yadi pūrṇaviyadambarajaladharapayodharayamaśaraviṣayeṣucandraiḥ [1555200000] yugasauradivasaiḥ yugādhimāsakāḥ labhyante, tataḥ etaiḥ divasaiḥ kiyantaḥ iti, labhdam adhimāsakāḥ | śeṣe kṣepaḥ ucyate ã yadi bhūdivasatulyena avamaśeṣeṇa yugādhimāsatulyaḥ
upacayaḥ adhimāsakaśeṣasya labhyate, tadā anena avamaśeṣeṇa kiyān iti | yat labdham tat adhimāsakaśeṣe prakṣipya yugacāndramāsaiḥ rasarāmāgnigutāśanatrikṛtatriviṣayaiḥ [5343336] bhāgalabdham bhāgāḥ, ṣaṣṭiguṇite liptāḥ | triṃśaguṇādhikayutam divasarāśim kṛtvā trairāśikam ã yadi yugacāndradinaiḥ yugāvamadināni labhyante, tataḥ etaiḥ kim iti labhdam avamaḥ | śeṣam ṣaṣṭyā saṃguṇya bhūdivasaiḥ pūrṇāmbaraśaranagaśaśirandhramunigiriviṣayarūpaiḥ [1577917500]
vibhajet, labdham ghaṭikāḥ |
body.translated_text: And here is this problem: 'By that, the Sun and Moon [are found]' — finding the Sun and Moon without the <s>ahargaṇa</s>. That is as follows: Having multiplied the elapsed years by twelve and adding the elapsed months, then multiplying by thirty and adding the days, the Rule of Three [is applied]: 'If from the complete-sky-sky-ocean-cloud-<s>Yama</s>-arrow-object-arrow-Moon [= 1,555,200,000] <s>yuga</s>-solar days the <s>yuga</s>-intercalary months are obtained, then from these days how many?' — the result is the intercalary months. To the remainder, the following adjustment is stated: 'If from a remainder of omitted days equal to the civil days, an accumulation equal to the <s>yuga</s>-intercalary [months] is obtained for the intercalary-month remainder, then from this omitted-day remainder, how much?' The result is added to the intercalary-month remainder, and dividing by the <s>yuga</s>-lunar months <s>rasa</s>-<s>Rāma</s>-fire-<s>Guta</s>-fire-three-product-three-object [= 5,343,336] gives the quotient-parts; when multiplied by sixty, arc-minutes. Having made the day-count with the addition of thirty-times-the-surplus, the Rule of Three: 'If from the <s>yuga</s>-lunar days the <s>yuga</s>-omitted days are obtained, then from these, what?' — the result is the omitted [days]. The remainder, multiplied by sixty and divided by the civil days complete-sky-arrow-mountain-moon-hole-sage-mountain-object-unit [= 1,577,917,500], gives the quotient as <s>ghaṭikās</s>.

body.text:
atha kim artham adhikāvamaśeṣayoḥ śaśimāsabhūdivasaiḥ bhāgaḥ hriyate? ucyate ã yaḥ asau adhimāsaśeṣaḥ sa cāndramāsāvayavaḥ | ataḥ tena sacchedena trairāśikam ã yadi yugaśaśimāsaiḥ sūryabhagaṇāḥ labhyante, tataḥ anena śaśimāsāvayavena kiyantaḥ iti | tatra śaśimāsāvayavacchedena saha ravibhagaṇena apavartanam ã ravibhagaṇānām ravibhagaṇabhāgena ekaḥ guṇakāraḥ, chedasya tāvat bhāgena ṣaṣṭiśatatrayam | tatra bhagaṇeṣu bhāgam na prayacchati
iti dvādaśa triṃśat ca guṇakāraḥ | tatra ṣaṣṭiśatatrayabhāgena rūpam, tāvat bhāgena eva chedasya api rūpam eva | śaśimāsāḥ eva kevalāḥ bhāgahārāḥ iti | avamaśeṣaḥ api bhūdināvayavaḥ iti trairāśikam ã yadi bhūdinaiḥ cāndradivasāḥ labhyante, tataḥ anena bhūdivasāvayavena cāndradivasacchedena kim iti | tatra guṇakārabhāgahārayoḥ tulyatvāt nāśaḥ | śeṣe ṣaṣṭiguṇe bhūdivasabhakte ghaṭikāḥ iti | atha yātavarṣāṇi bhagaṇāḥ, māsāḥ rāśayaḥ, dināni bhāgāḥ iti parikalpya
avamaśeṣalabdhaghaṭikāḥ ca liptāḥ | ebhyaḥ adhikaśeṣalabdham viśodhayet | śeṣam madhyamasūryaḥ | tebhyaḥ eva trayodaśaguṇitebhyaḥ adhikaśeṣaphalam viśodhayet | śeṣam madhyamacandraḥ |
body.translated_text: Now, why are the remainders of the intercalary and omitted [days] divided by the lunar months and civil days? It is said: The intercalary-month remainder is a fraction of a lunar month. Therefore, with that fractional [quantity], the Rule of Three: 'If from the <s>yuga</s>-lunar months the Sun's revolutions are obtained, then from this lunar-month fraction, how many?' There, the reduction together with the lunar-month-fraction denominator and the Sun's revolutions: of the Sun's revolutions, one is the multiplier by the Sun's revolution-part; of the denominator, by the same part, three hundred and sixty. Since the revolutions do not yield a whole quotient, twelve and thirty become the multipliers. There, one is [obtained] by the three-hundred-sixty-part, and one is [obtained] for the denominator by that same part. The lunar months alone are the divisors. The omitted-day remainder too is a fraction of a civil day; hence the Rule of Three: 'If from the civil days the lunar days are obtained, then from this civil-day fraction, by the lunar-day denominator, what?' There, because the multiplier and divisor are equal, they cancel. When the remainder is multiplied by sixty and divided by the civil days, [the result is] <s>ghaṭikās</s>. Now, conceiving the elapsed years as revolutions, months as signs, days as degrees, and the <s>ghaṭikās</s> obtained from the omitted-day remainder as arc-minutes — from these, the result obtained from the intercalary remainder is to be subtracted. The remainder is the mean Sun. From those very [quantities], multiplied by thirteen, the intercalary-remainder result is subtracted. The remainder is the mean Moon.

body.text:
adhimāsakaiḥ api avamāḥ ānīyante | tat yathā ã abhīṣṭavarṣāṇi dinīkṛtya trairāśikam ã [yadi] yugasūryadivasaiḥ yugādhimāsakāḥ labhyante, tataḥ etaiḥ abhīṣṭasūryadivasaiḥ kiyantaḥ iti, adhimāsakāḥ samatikrāntāḥ labhyante, vartamānasya ca śeṣaḥ | tat etat trairāśikam ã yadi yugādhimāsaiḥ yugāvamarātrā[ṇi] labhyante tataḥ etaiḥ adhimāsakaiḥ abhīṣṭaiḥ kiyantaḥ iti gaṇitanyāyena savarṇīkṛtya yugāvamaiḥ guṇayet | athavā abhīṣṭādhimāsarāśim aṃśarāśim
ca pṛthak pṛthak yugāvamaiḥ saṃguṇayya aṃśarāśim yugasūryadivasaiḥ vibhajya labhdam upari kṣiptvā yugādhimāsakaiḥ bhāgalabdham abhīṣṭakālāvamāḥ | athavā trairāśikadvayam bhaṅktvā api ānīyante ã yadi yugasūryadivasaiḥ adhimāsakāḥ labhyante, tataḥ abhīṣṭadivasaiḥ kiyantaḥ iti ekam trairāśikam | tataḥ punar api ã yadi yugādhimāsakaiḥ yugāvamāḥ labhyante, tataḥ trairāsikanyāyaviracitarāśyutpannādhimāsakaiḥ kiyantaḥ iti | tatra pūrvatrairāśike yugādhimāsakaḥ
guṇakāraḥ dvitīyatrairāśike bhāgahāraḥ | ataḥ guṇakārabhāgahārayoḥ tulyatvāt naṣṭayoḥ abhīṣṭadivasānām yugāvamaḥ guṇakāraḥ, yugasauryadivasaḥ bhāgahāraḥ, labdham abhīṣṭāvamāḥ |
body.translated_text: The omitted days are also derived from the intercalary months. That is as follows: Having converted the desired years into days, the Rule of Three: 'If from the <s>yuga</s>-solar days the <s>yuga</s>-intercalary months are obtained, then from these desired solar days how many?' — the elapsed intercalary months are obtained, along with the remainder of the current [month]. Then this Rule of Three: 'If from the <s>yuga</s>-intercalary months the <s>yuga</s>-omitted days are obtained, then from these desired intercalary months how many?' — by the arithmetic rule, having reduced to common denominators, one multiplies by the <s>yuga</s>-omitted [days]. Alternatively, having separately multiplied both the integer intercalary-month quantity and the fractional quantity by the <s>yuga</s>-omitted [days], and dividing the fractional quantity by the <s>yuga</s>-solar days, adding the result above, and dividing by the <s>yuga</s>-intercalary months, the result is the omitted days for the desired period. Or, breaking [this into] two Rules of Three, they are also derived: 'If from the <s>yuga</s>-solar days the intercalary months are obtained, then from the desired days how many?' — this is one Rule of Three. Then again: 'If from the <s>yuga</s>-intercalary months the <s>yuga</s>-omitted [days] are obtained, then from the intercalary months produced by the Rule-of-Three procedure, how many?' In the first Rule of Three, the <s>yuga</s>-intercalary-months is the multiplier; in the second Rule of Three it is the divisor. Therefore, since the multiplier and divisor are equal, when they cancel, the <s>yuga</s>-omitted [days] is the multiplier of the desired days, and the <s>yuga</s>-solar day is the divisor; the result is the desired omitted days.

body.text:
abhīṣṭāvamaiḥ api adhimāsakāḥ ānīyante | abhīṣṭavarṣamāseṣu tat utpannādhimāsakān prakṣipya triṃśatā saṃguṇayya trairāśikadvayam kriyate ã yadi yugaśaśidivasaiḥ yugāvamāḥ labhyante tataḥ abhīṣṭaśaśidivasaiḥ kiyantaḥ iti avamāḥ | evam ekam trairāsikam | punar ã yadi yugāvamaiḥ yugādhimāsakāḥ labhyante tataḥ abhīṣṭāvamaiḥ pūrvatrairāśikaviracitaiḥ kiyantaḥ iti, adhimāsakāḥ labhyante | tatra pūrvatrairāśike yugāvamāḥ guṇakāraḥ, iha bhāgahāraḥ
| ataḥ guṇakārabhāgahārayoḥ tulyatvāt naṣṭayoḥ yugaśaśidivasaḥ bhāgahāraḥ, yugādhimāsakaḥ guṇakāraḥ, phalam abhīṣṭādhimāsakāḥ | pūrvavat vā pṛthak pṛthak trairāśikena api karaṇīyam |
body.translated_text: Intercalary months are also derived from the desired omitted days (<s>avamas</s>). Adding the intercalary months produced from the desired year-months, and multiplying by thirty, two rules of three are applied: if by the <s>yuga</s> lunar-days the <s>yuga</s> omitted-days are obtained, then by the desired lunar-days how many? — [these are] the omitted days. This is one rule of three. Again: if by the <s>yuga</s> omitted-days the <s>yuga</s> intercalary months are obtained, then by the desired omitted-days — constructed by the previous rule of three — how many? Thus, the intercalary months are obtained. In the first rule of three, the <s>yuga</s> omitted-days are the multiplier, and here [in the second], the divisor.
