Therefore, since the multiplier and divisor are equal, they cancel — [leaving] the <s>yuga</s> lunar-days as divisor, the <s>yuga</s> intercalary months as multiplier, and the result is the desired intercalary months. Or, as before, [it may be] done separately by individual rules of three.

body.text:
atha adhimāsakaiḥ abhīṣṭagrahāḥ api ānīyante | tat yathā ã yadi yugādhimāsakaiḥ abhīṣṭagrahabhagaṇāḥ labhyante, tadā iṣṭādhimāsakaiḥ kiyantaḥ iti | adhimāsapatanakālāvadheḥ abhīṣṭagrahabhagaṇādayaḥ labhyante | asau eva abhīṣṭakālikaḥ kriyate | katham? adhimāsaka[śeṣeṇa] abhīṣṭagrahabhagaṇān saṃguṇayya adhimāsakaiḥ guṇitaśaśidivasaiḥ vibhajet | tatra bhagaṇādayaḥ labhyante, [te] pūrvalabdhādhimāsakagrahabhagaṇeṣu yojyante tadā
avamarātrapatanakālāvadheḥ bhavati | tataḥ punar api avamarātraśeṣam ṣaṣṭyā saṃguṇayya śaśidivasaiḥ eva vibhajet | labdham ghaṭikāḥ | tataḥ ã yadi ṣaṣṭighaṭikābhiḥ abhīṣṭagrahabhuktiḥ labhyate, [tadā] ābhiḥ ghaṭikābhiḥ kim iti | labdham pūrvasthāpite grahe dadyāt, abhīṣṭadivasasya udayakālāvadheḥ [grahaḥ] bhavati |
body.translated_text: Now, the desired planets too are derived from intercalary months. Namely: if by the <s>yuga</s> intercalary months the revolutions of the desired planet are obtained, then by the desired intercalary months how many? The revolutions and so on of the desired planet are obtained up to the time-point of the intercalary-month occurrence. That itself is made into the desired time-point. How? Multiplying the desired planet's revolutions by the intercalary-month remainder, and dividing by the lunar-days multiplied by the intercalary months — the revolutions and so on are obtained, [which] are added to the previously obtained intercalary-month planetary revolutions; then [the result] corresponds to the time-point of the omitted-night occurrence. Then again, multiplying the omitted-night remainder by sixty and dividing by the lunar-days themselves — the result is <s>ghaṭikās</s>. Then: if by sixty <s>ghaṭikās</s> the daily motion of the desired planet is obtained, [then] by these [many] <s>ghaṭikās</s>, what? The result is added to the previously established planet — [giving] the planet at the time-point of sunrise on the desired day.

body.text: atha avamaiḥ api ã yadi yugā[vamaiḥ abhīṣṭagrahabhagaṇāḥ] labhyante tataḥ yātāvamaiḥ kiyantaḥ iti | avamarātraparisamāptikālāvadheḥ abhīṣṭagrahabhagaṇādayaḥ labhyante, tataḥ iṣṭadivasaudayikaḥ kriyate | katham? avamarātraśeṣeṇa abhīṣṭagrahabhagaṇān saṃguṇayya yugāvamabhūdivasasaṃvargeṇa vibhajet | labdham bhagaṇādayaḥ | tān pūrvalabdhabhagaṇādiṣu kṣipet | audayikaḥ grahaḥ bhavati |
body.translated_text: Now, by the omitted days too: if by the <s>yuga</s> omitted-days the revolutions of the desired planet are obtained, then by the elapsed omitted-days how many? The revolutions and so on of the desired planet are obtained up to the time-point of the completion of the omitted night; then [the planet] is made into the sunrise [value] for the desired day. How? Multiplying the desired planet's revolutions by the omitted-night remainder, and dividing by the product of the <s>yuga</s> omitted-days and civil-days — the result is revolutions and so on. Adding them to the previously obtained revolutions and so on — the sunrise planet results.

body.text: atra ayam praśnaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Here is this question:

body.translated_text: Thus. The derivation of the Sun and Moon from the intercalary-month and omitted-day remainders has been stated. Now, the derivation of all planets from the omitted-day remainder alone will be described. Namely: having reduced the <s>yuga</s> omitted-days by sixty, the setting down is: 418,043. Now, for deriving the Sun first — these reduced omitted-days, multiplied by what, with the reduced Sun's revolutions subtracted, would give an exact quotient when divided by the reduced civil-days — thus the <s>kuṭṭākāra</s> is performed. The result obtained as the <s>kuṭṭākāra</s> [multiplier] is seven-moon-flavor-mountain-<s>Vasu</s>-<s>Vasu</s>, and in numerals 87,617. Multiplying the omitted-day remainder by this and dividing by the reduced civil-days themselves — the remainder is the revolution-remainder of the Sun. By this, the derivation of the Sun has been explained.

body.translated_text: Practice problem:

By the stated omitted-day remainder, the derivation of the Moon [proceeds].

athavā madhyamāt sūryāt sahayātabhagaṇaiḥ liptīkṛtya trairāśikam ã yadi yugaraviliptābhiḥ yugaśaśibhagaṇāḥ labhyante, [tadā] etābhiḥ yātaraviliptābhiḥ kiyantaḥ iti | labdham bhagaṇāḥ, śeṣe dvādaśādiguṇite madhyamaḥ candraḥ labhyate | athavā khakhaṣaḍghanena yadā yugaraviliptāḥ apavartitāḥ bhavanti [tadā] ravibhagaṇāḥ bhāgahāraḥ, śaśibhagaṇāḥ yātaraviliptānām guṇakāraḥ, phalam madhyamacandraliptāḥ | evam anena nyāyana candrāt abhīṣṭagrahāt
vā iṣṭagrahaḥ ānīyate | katham? nirjñātagrahayātaliptānām abhīṣṭagrahabhagaṇāḥ guṇakāraḥ nirjñātagrahayugaliptāḥ bhagaṇāḥ vā bhāgahāraḥ, phalam [bhagaṇāḥ] liptāḥ [vā] | atra ayam praśnaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Alternatively, having converted the mean Sun together with its elapsed revolutions into minutes, the rule of three [is applied]: if by the <s>yuga</s> Sun-minutes the <s>yuga</s> Moon-revolutions are obtained, [then] by these elapsed Sun-minutes how many? The result is revolutions; when the remainder is multiplied by twelve and so on, the mean Moon is obtained. Alternatively, when the <s>yuga</s> Sun-minutes are reduced by <s>khakhaṣaḍghana</s> (= 21,600), the Sun's revolutions become the divisor, the Moon's revolutions become the multiplier of the elapsed minutes, and the result is the mean Moon's minutes. By this same method, the desired planet is derived from the Moon or from any desired planet. How? The revolutions of the desired planet are the multiplier of the elapsed minutes of the known planet; the <s>yuga</s>-minutes — or revolutions — of the known planet are the divisor; the result is [revolutions or] minutes. Here is this question:

children.text: savituḥ śaśinam karoti yaḥ śaśinaḥ sthititaḥ tārakagrahān |

[using a system] other than our <s>siddhānta</s> — he is called the foremost among time-knowers. (3)

body.translated_text: Thus. (6)

body.text: mānuṣapitṛdevavarṣapramāṇāni
body.translated_text: Measures of human, ancestral, and divine years

body.text: mānuṣapitṛdevānām varṣapramāṇanirūpaṇāya āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of specifying the year-measures of humans, ancestors, and gods, he says:

children.text: ravivarṣam mānuṣyam tat api triṃśadguṇam bhavati pitryam |
children.translated_text: A solar year is a human [year]; that, multiplied by thirty, becomes an ancestral [year];
an ancestral [year], multiplied by twelve, is specified as a divine year. (7)

body.text:
ravivarṣam, raveḥ varṣam ravivarṣam | ravivarṣasya ca pramāṇam abhihitam ã "ravibhagaṇāḥ ravyabdāḥ" [kālakriyāí, 5] iti | raveḥ bhagaṇabhogaḥ mānuṣāṇām varṣam | yat eva raveḥ varṣam tat eva mānuṣāṇām varṣam iti | tat api triṃśadguṇam bhavati pitryam | tat mānuṣyam varṣam triṃśadguṇitam pitryam varṣam bhavati, yasmāt māsaḥ teṣām ahorātram | uktam ca ã "śaśimāsārdham pitaraḥ" [kālakriyāí, 17] iti | pitryam dvādaśaguṇitam divyam varṣam
vinirdiṣṭam | piṭrṇām yat varṣam tat dvādaśaguṇitam ekam varṣam devānām, yasmāt pitryam varṣam māsaḥ devānām | yathākrameṇa ekatriṃśatṣaṣṭiśatatraya[guṇam] ca [ravivarṣam] manujapitṛdevānām [varṣāṇi] || 7 ||
body.translated_text: 'Solar year' — the year of the Sun is the solar year. And the measure of the solar year has been stated: 'the Sun's revolutions are the solar years' [<s>Kālakriyā</s> 5]. The traversal of one revolution by the Sun is a year for humans. That very year of the Sun is the year for humans. 'That, multiplied by thirty, becomes an ancestral [year]' — that human year, multiplied by thirty, becomes an ancestral year, since a month is a day-and-night for them. And it has been said: 'half a lunar month [is the day-and-night] of the ancestors' [<s>Kālakriyā</s> 17]. 'An ancestral [year], multiplied by twelve, is specified as a divine year' — the year of the ancestors, multiplied by twelve, becomes one year of the gods, since the ancestral year is a month of the gods. In order, [one solar year], multiplied by one, three-hundred-and-sixty, [gives] the human, ancestral, and divine years [respectively]. (7)

body.text: yugamānam brahmadinapramāṇam ca
body.translated_text: The measure of a <s>yuga</s> and the day of <s>Brahmā</s>

body.text: caturyugabrahmadinajñāpanārtham āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of specifying the <s>caturyuga</s> and the day of <s>Brahmā</s>, he says:

children.translated_text: A thousand divine years, common to all planets, is a <s>yuga</s>; [that] multiplied by twelve,
one thousand and eight is the day of <s>Brahmā</s>, in planetary <s>yugas</s>. (8)

body.text: yat etat divyam varṣam tat dvādaśabhiḥ sahasreṇa guṇitam grahasāmānyam yugam | grahāṇām sāmānyam grahasāmānyam | kim tat? yugam | yasmāt sarve grahāḥ sahaśīghroccaiḥ yugapat mīnameṣasandhau bhavanti, tasmāt yugam grahasāmānyam | tat ca viyadambarākāśaśūnyayamarāmavedāḥ [4320000] | etat eva kṛta-tretā-dvāpara-kalivarṣāṇām pramāṇam | asmākam tu yugapādāḥ sarve eva ca tulyakālāḥ | paurāṇikaiḥ tu bhinnakālāḥ vyākhyātāḥ ã
body.translated_text: That which is a divine year — that, multiplied by twelve thousand, is the <s>yuga</s> common to all planets. The commonality of the planets is '<s>grahasāmānya</s>.' What is that? A <s>yuga</s>. Since all planets together with their fast-apogees simultaneously come to the junction of <s>Mīna</s> (Pisces) and <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries), therefore the <s>yuga</s> is common to all planets. And it is sky-sky-space-zero-<s>Yama</s>-<s>Rāma</s>-<s>Veda</s> [= 4,320,000 years]. This itself is the measure of the <s>Kṛta</s>, <s>Tretā</s>, <s>Dvāpara</s>, and <s>Kali</s> years. For us, however, the <s>yuga</s>-quarters are all of equal duration. But the <s>Paurāṇikas</s> (Purāṇa-followers) have explained them as being of unequal duration:

children.text: catvāri āhuḥ sahasrāṇi varṣāṇām yat kṛtam yugam |
children.translated_text: They say four thousand years constitute the <s>Kṛta Yuga</s>;

children.text: tasya tāvat śatī sandhyā sandhyāṃśaḥ ca tathāvidhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: its twilight (<s>sandhyā</s>) is as many hundreds, and its twilight-portion (<s>sandhyāṃśa</s>) is likewise.
In the other three [<s>yugas</s>], together with their twilights and twilight-portions,
[the durations] decrease by one — in thousands and in hundreds.

body.text: manusmṛtiḥ, 1.69-70
body.translated_text: <s>Manusmṛti</s> 1.69-70

body.text:
iti | kṛtapramāṇam viyadambarākāśavasuyamamunicandrāḥ [1728000] | tretāpramāṇam viyadambarākāśarasanavārkāḥ [1296000] | dvāparapramāṇam viyadambarākāśavedarasavasavaḥ [864000] | kalipramāṇam viyadambarākāśayamarāmavedāḥ [432000] | samāsitāni viyadambarākāśaśūnyayamarāmavedāḥ [4320000]| kim punar atra yuktam ã purāṇakāraiḥ yathā bhinnapramāṇāni kṛtādīni vyākhyātāni tathā pratipattum, āhosvit yathā asmākam ācāryeṇa pratipāditāni samapramāṇāni
iti? yathā asmākam prasiddhāni tathā iti āha | yadi purāṇaprakriyāprasiddhāni yugapādapramāṇāni parigṛhyantām, tadā kaliyugādau grahāḥ mīnameṣasandhau yugapat madhyamagatyā na syuḥ | katham iti ucyate | yugapādānām trayāṇām ekatrapramāṇam viyadambarākāśāṣṭavasuvasurāmāḥ [3888000] iti etaiḥ ahargaṇam utpādya yathāvihitamadhyamagrahagaṇitaprakriyāyām yugapat mīnameṣasandhau madhyamagrahāḥ na labhyante | anayā eva prakriyayā idānīm
api grahagatyām sādhyamānāyām eva iṣṭagrahāṇām gatiḥ na labhyate | yadi punar samam eva kṛtādīnām pramāṇam tat idam trayāṇām api yugapādānām pramāṇam viyadambarākāśaśūnyakṛtayamāgnayaḥ [3240000], anena yātena sarvam iṣṭam upapadyate | tasmāt "yathā asmākam prasiddhāni " iti suṣṭhu uktam |
body.translated_text: The measure of <s>Kṛta</s> is sky-sky-space-<s>Vasu</s>-<s>Yama</s>-sage-moon [= 1,728,000]. The measure of <s>Tretā</s> is sky-sky-space-flavor-nine-sun [= 1,296,000]. The measure of <s>Dvāpara</s> is sky-sky-space-<s>Veda</s>-flavor-<s>Vasu</s>-<s>Vasu</s> [= 864,000]. The measure of <s>Kali</s> is sky-sky-space-<s>Yama</s>-<s>Rāma</s>-<s>Veda</s> [= 432,000]. Combined: sky-sky-space-zero-<s>Yama</s>-<s>Rāma</s>-<s>Veda</s> [= 4,320,000]. Now, what is proper here — to accept the unequal measures of <s>Kṛta</s> and the others as explained by the <s>Paurāṇikas</s>, or the equal measures as taught by our master? As established by us — he says so. If the <s>yuga</s>-quarter measures as established by the Purāṇic tradition are accepted, then at the beginning of the <s>Kali Yuga</s>, the planets would not simultaneously be at the junction of <s>Mīna</s> and <s>Meṣa</s> by mean motion. How so? It is said: the measure of the [first] three <s>yuga</s>-quarters combined is sky-sky-space-eight-<s>Vasu</s>-<s>Vasu</s>-<s>Rāma</s> [= 3,888,000]. By producing the day-count from this and applying the prescribed mean-planet computational procedure, the mean planets are not simultaneously obtained at the junction of <s>Mīna</s> and <s>Meṣa</s>. By this very procedure, even now when planetary motion is being computed, the motion of the desired planets is not obtained. But if the <s>Kṛta</s> and the other [<s>yuga</s>-quarters] have equal measure, then the measure of the three <s>yuga</s>-quarters too is sky-sky-space-zero-square-<s>Yama</s>-fire [= 3,240,000]. Using this as the elapsed [time], everything desired is achieved. Therefore, it is well said: 'as established by us.'

body.text: aṣṭottaram sahasram brāhmaḥ divasaḥ grahayugānām | grahayugam iti yat etat grahasāmānyam yugam tat parigṛhyate | tat aṣṭottareṇa sahasreṇa guṇitam prajāpateḥ ekadivasapramāṇam bhavati | nanu ca atra api paurāṇikaiḥ saha virudhyate | katham? paurāṇikaiḥ ã
body.translated_text: 'One thousand and eight is the day of <s>Brahmā</s>, in planetary <s>yugas</s>.' The planetary <s>yuga</s> — that which is the <s>yuga</s> common to all planets — that is taken up. That, multiplied by one thousand and eight, becomes the measure of one day of <s>Prajāpati</s>. Now, here too there is a contradiction with the <s>Paurāṇikas</s>. How? The <s>Paurāṇikas</s> [say]:

children.translated_text: They know a day of <s>Brahmā</s> to be a thousand <s>yugas</s> in extent;
and the night to end in a thousand <s>yugas</s> — those people know the day and night [of <s>Brahmā</s>].

body.text: bhagavadgītā, 8.17
body.translated_text: <s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 8.17

body.text:
iti sahasrayugaparyantam brahmaṇaḥ divasapramāṇam uktam | atra ca aṣṭottaram sahasram caturyugānām iti | atra tāvat vicāryate | paurāṇikaiḥ ã "sahasrayugaparyantam ahar yat brahmaṇaḥ viduḥ" iti abhidhāya taiḥ eva ekasaptatiḥ caturyugānām manvantaram caturdaśa manavaḥ brāhmaḥ divasaḥ iti [abhihitam] | atra ekasaptatiḥ caturdaśaguṇitā sahasrasaṅkhyām na prāpnoti | ucyate ca ã caturdaśa manvantarāṇi brahmaṇaḥ divasaḥ, sahasram caturyugānām iti svavacanavirodhaḥ
| asmākam tu dvāsaptatiḥ caturyugānām manvantaram, aṣṭottarasahasram brāhmaḥ divasaḥ iti yuktisiddham etam | katham punar idam jñāyate dvāsaptatiḥ caturyugānām manvantaram iti? gītikāsūktatvāt |
body.translated_text: Thus, the measure of the day of <s>Brahmā</s> is stated as one thousand <s>yugas</s> in extent. But here, [it is stated as] one thousand and eight <s>caturyugas</s>. Here now, this is examined: the <s>Paurāṇikas</s>, having stated 'they know a day of <s>Brahmā</s> to be a thousand <s>yugas</s> in extent,' those very same [authorities] also stated that seventy-one <s>caturyugas</s> make a <s>manvantara</s> and fourteen <s>Manus</s> make a day of <s>Brahmā</s>. Here, seventy-one multiplied by fourteen does not reach the number one thousand. And it is said: fourteen <s>manvantaras</s> are a day of <s>Brahmā</s>, [and also] a thousand <s>caturyugas</s> — [this is] a self-contradiction. For us, however, seventy-two <s>caturyugas</s> make a <s>manvantara</s>, and one thousand and eight is the day of <s>Brahmā</s> — this is logically established. How then is it known that seventy-two <s>caturyugas</s> make a <s>manvantara</s>? Because it is stated in the <s>Gītikā</s>:

body.text:
kāhaḥ manavaḥ ḍha manuyugāḥ śkha | iti |
[gītikāí, 5] || 8 ||
body.translated_text: '<s>Kāhaḥ manavaḥ ḍha manuyugāḥ śkha</s>.' [<s>Gītikā</s> 5] (8)

body.text: utsarpiṇyādiyugavibhāgaḥ
body.translated_text: The division of a <s>yuga</s> into <s>utsarpiṇī</s> and <s>apasarpiṇī</s>

body.text: utsarpiṇyapasarpiṇīsuṣamāduṣṣmāparijñānāya āha ãã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of knowing <s>utsarpiṇī</s> (ascending), <s>apasarpiṇī</s> (descending), <s>suṣamā</s> (happy), and <s>duḥṣamā</s> (unhappy), he says:

children.text: utsarpiṇī yugārdham paścāt apasarpiṇī yugārdham ca |
children.translated_text: The <s>utsarpiṇī</s> (ascending [half]) is half a <s>yuga</s>; afterwards, the <s>apasarpiṇī</s> (descending [half]) is [the other] half of a <s>yuga</s>;

children.text: madhye yugasya suṣamā ādau ante duṣṣamā indūccāt || 9 ||
children.translated_text: in the middle of the <s>yuga</s> is <s>suṣamā</s> (happiness); at the beginning and end, <s>duḥṣamā</s> (unhappiness) — [reckoned] from the Moon's apogee. (9)

body.text: utsarpiṇī nāma yasmin prāṇinām āyuryaśovīryasaukhyādīni upacīyante sa kālaḥ utasrpiṇīsaṃjñakaḥ | tasya ca pramāṇam yugārdham | yugasya ardham yugārdham | yugam tu abhihitam eva | tasya ardhasaṅkhyāpramāṇam utsarpiṇī viyadambarākāśaśūnyarasenduyamāḥ [2160000] | paścāt apasarpiṇī yugārdham ca | paścāt iti anena ustarpiṇīkālānantaram apasarpiṇīkālam darśayati | yasmāt pūrvapravṛttasya paścāt iti vyapadeśaḥ bhavati | yasmin prāṇinām

children.text: āyuryaśovīryasaukhyādīni apacīyante sa apasarpiṇīsaṃjñakaḥ kālaḥ | tasya ca pramāṇam yugasya paścārdham viyadambarākāśaśūnyarasenduyamāḥ [2160000] |
children.translated_text: happiness, and the like of living beings decrease — that time is designated <s>apasarpiṇī</s>. And its measure is the latter half of the <s>yuga</s>: sky-sky-sky-void-<s>Rasa</s>-moon-<s>Yama</s> [= 2,160,000].

body.translated_text: The <s>utsarpiṇī</s> (ascending era) is named thus: the time in which the lifespan, fame, vigor, happiness, and the like of living beings increase — that time is designated <s>utsarpiṇī</s>. And its measure is half a <s>yuga</s>. Half of a <s>yuga</s> is a <s>yugārdha</s> (half-<s>yuga</s>). The <s>yuga</s> has already been described. Its half-measure, the <s>utsarpiṇī</s>, is sky-sky-sky-void-<s>Rasa</s>-moon-<s>Yama</s> [= 2,160,000]. Afterwards, the <s>apasarpiṇī</s> (descending era) is also half a <s>yuga</s>. By 'afterwards,' he indicates the <s>apasarpiṇī</s> period as following the <s>utsarpiṇī</s> period — because the designation 'afterwards' applies to what has been preceded [by something]. In which [era] the lifespan, fame, vigor,

body.text:
evam ca ã madhye yugasya suṣamādau ante duṣṣamenūccāt | tasya pūrvārdhasya madhye suṣamā duṣṣamā ca | ādau ante ca | ādau suṣamā ante duṣṣamā | suṣamāduṣṣamāpramāṇam yugacaturbhāgaḥ | katham? madhye iti vacanāt | yugārdhasya ardham yugacaturbhāgaḥ iti | pratigraham yugabhedāt āha ã "indūccāt" | indūccāt niṣpannāt yugāt ete utsarpiṇyapasarpiṇīsuṣamāduṣṣamākālāḥ avagantavyāḥ iti | atha kim ucyate indūccāt iti ? nanu ca grahasāmānyam
yugam iti abhihitam | satyam | evam etat | pratigraham apavartanaviśeṣāt yugabhedaḥ | tat yathā ã raveḥ maṇḍalāni ṣaṇmuniśarāḥ [576], divasapramāṇena yugam api navavasurāmaśūnyenduyamāḥ [210389] | candrasya divasapramāṇena yugam śarayamāṅgaviṣayeṣurūpadasrāḥ [2155625] | evam anyeṣām api |
body.translated_text: And thus: in the middle of the <s>yuga</s>, <s>suṣamā</s> (well-being [period]); at the beginning and end, <s>duḥṣama</s> (ill-being [period]) — from the lunar apogee (<s>induccya</s>). In the first half, in the middle is <s>suṣamā</s> and <s>duḥṣamā</s>. At the beginning and end: <s>suṣamā</s> at the beginning, <s>duḥṣamā</s> at the end. The measure of <s>suṣamā</s> and <s>duḥṣamā</s> is one-quarter of a <s>yuga</s>. How? Because of the word 'in the middle.' Half of a <s>yugārdha</s> is a quarter of a <s>yuga</s>. Because of the variation of <s>yugas</s> for each planet, he says 'from the lunar apogee.' From the <s>yuga</s> produced from the lunar apogee, these <s>utsarpiṇī</s>, <s>apasarpiṇī</s>, <s>suṣamā</s>, and <s>duḥṣamā</s> periods are to be understood. But why is 'from the lunar apogee' stated? Has it not been said that the <s>yuga</s> is common to all planets? True. It is so. But for each planet, due to the particular reduction [factors], there are different <s>yugas</s>. That is: the Sun's revolutions are six-sage-arrows [= 576]; the <s>yuga</s> in terms of days is also nine-<s>Vasu</s>-<s>Rāma</s>-void-moon-<s>Yama</s> [= 210,389]. The Moon's <s>yuga</s> in terms of days is arrow-<s>Yama</s>-limb-sense-arrow-form-<s>Dasra</s> [= 2,155,625]. Similarly for others.

body.text: atha yugasya kim lakṣaṇam? ucyate ã caitraśuklapratipadi ardhodite savitari laṅkāyām mīnameṣasandhau pravṛttaḥ grahaḥ punar mīnameṣasandhau caitraśuklapratipadi savituḥ ardhodaye laṅkāyām yāvatā kālena prāpnoti tāvat kālaḥ yugam iti | uktam ca ã
body.translated_text: Now, what is the definition of a <s>yuga</s>? It is said: On the first day of the bright fortnight of <s>Caitra</s>, when the Sun is half-risen at <s>Laṅkā</s>, at the junction of <s>Mīna</s> (Pisces) and <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries) — a planet that has commenced [from there], the time in which it again reaches the junction of <s>Mīna</s> and <s>Meṣa</s> on the first day of the bright fortnight of <s>Caitra</s> at the half-rising of the Sun at <s>Laṅkā</s> — that time is a <s>yuga</s>. And it has been said:

children.translated_text: At the beginning of the bright [fortnight] of <s>Caitra</s>, when the Sun is at the equinox, half-risen, having commenced
from the beginning of <s>Meṣa</s> to the end of <s>Mīna</s> — the return of one exactly so [positioned].

body.text: iti |
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text:
bhinnāgreṣu yugeṣu ekāgrīkaraṇam kuṭṭākāreṇa abhihitam ã "kaścit dvābhyām ekāgraḥ tribhiḥ dvyagraḥ" iti ādi | athavā indūccāt nimittāt utsarpiṇyapasarpiṇīsuṣamāduṣṣamāṇām gatagantavyam vijñeyam iti | katham punar gatagantavyaparijñānasya indūccanimittatvam pratipadyate iti ? ucyate ã kuṭṭākāragaṇitena, yasmāt indūccayātāgrasya indūccabhagaṇāḥ yugavarṣāṇi yugadivasāḥ [vā] bhājyabhāgahāratām pratipadyante | tat yathā asmin vastubhiḥ
vā parikalpitaḥ uddeśakaḥ ã
body.translated_text: The equalization of [planets with] different remainder-offsets in [their respective] <s>yugas</s> has been described through the <s>kuṭṭākāra</s>: 'some [quantity] having remainder one when [divided] by two, remainder two when [divided] by three,' and so on. Alternatively, from the lunar apogee as the cause, the elapsed and remaining [portions] of the <s>utsarpiṇī</s>, <s>apasarpiṇī</s>, <s>suṣamā</s>, and <s>duḥṣamā</s> are to be known. But how is it understood that the lunar apogee is the cause for knowing the elapsed and remaining [portions]? It is explained: through the <s>kuṭṭākāra</s> computation, since the elapsed-remainder of the lunar apogee [and] the revolutions of the lunar apogee are the divisor-dividend of the <s>yuga</s>-years or <s>yuga</s>-days. That is, either with actual [values] or with postulated [values], the example problem:

children.text: niśīthinīnām adhipasya tuṅgajam gatam tu rāśitritayam yadā bhavet |
children.translated_text: When three signs of the apogee of the lord of the nights (Moon) have been traversed,

children.text: tadā kiyat yātam atha āśu gaṇyatām yugasya varṣāgradināgratām ca me || 1 ||
children.translated_text: then how much [time] has elapsed? Now, compute quickly the year-remainder and day-remainder of the <s>yuga</s> for me. // 1 //

body.text: labdham varṣāgram viyadambarākāśaśūnyakṛtayamāgnayaḥ [3240000], dināgram ca śararavivasuvahnivedarāmavasurudrāḥ [1183438125] |
body.translated_text: Result: The year-remainder is sky-sky-sky-void-square-<s>Yama</s>-fires [= 3,240,000]; and the day-remainder is arrow-sun-<s>Vasu</s>-fire-<s>Veda</s>-<s>Rāma</s>-<s>Vasu</s>-<s>Rudra</s> [= 1,183,438,125].

body.text:
athavā ayam aparaḥ prakāraḥ ã utsarpiṇī yugārdham | utsarpati iti utsarpiṇī, upacīyate iti arthaḥ | kā sā utsarpiṇī? grahabhuktiḥ iti adhyāhāryam | sā punar kiyantam kālam utsarpiṇī iti āha ã yugārdham | yujyante asmin grahāḥ iti yugam | tat ca nakṣatracakram eva parigṛhyate, yasmāt ekasmin maṇḍale grahasya grahaiḥ saha yogaḥ sambhavati | tasya yugasya ardham yugārdham, ṣaḍrāśayaḥ | paścāt apasarpiṇī yugārdham ca | paścāt punar api apasarpiṇī yugārdham
eva | rāśiṣaṭkam iti arthaḥ | madhye yugasya suṣamā, tasya yugasya madhye antare iti arthaḥ | suṣamā āditaḥ antataḥ ca gaṇyamāne suṣamā, ekasya padasya āditaḥ aparasya antataḥ iti arthaḥ | [ādau ante ca] duṣṣamā dṛṣṭā | anyaprakāreṇa iti vākyaśeṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: Alternatively, here is another interpretation: The <s>utsarpiṇī</s> is half a <s>yuga</s>. '<s>Utsarpati</s>' means 'ascends' — hence '<s>utsarpiṇī</s>,' meaning 'it increases.' What is this <s>utsarpiṇī</s>? 'The daily motion of a planet' is to be supplied. For how long is it <s>utsarpiṇī</s>? He says: half a <s>yuga</s>. '[That] in which planets are conjoined' is a <s>yuga</s>. And that is taken as the asterism-circle (<s>nakṣatracakra</s>) itself, since the conjunction of a planet with [other] planets occurs in a single revolution. Half of that <s>yuga</s> is a <s>yugārdha</s> — six signs. Afterwards, the <s>apasarpiṇī</s> is also half a <s>yuga</s>. Afterwards, again the <s>apasarpiṇī</s> is just half a <s>yuga</s> — meaning six signs. In the middle of the <s>yuga</s>, <s>suṣamā</s> — 'in the middle of that <s>yuga</s>' means 'in the interval.' <s>Suṣamā</s>, counted from the beginning and end — [meaning] from the beginning of one quadrant and from the end of another. [At the beginning and end,] <s>duḥṣamā</s> is observed. 'By another method' is the completion of the sentence.

body.text:
katham etāḥ punar utsarpiṇyapasarpiṇīsuṣamāduṣṣamāgrahabhuktayaḥ vijñāyante iti atra āha ã indūccāt, candrakendrāt iti arthaḥ | tat yathā ã indoḥ kendrasya yadā rāśitrayam dvau bhāgau aṣṭāviṃśatiḥ ca kalāḥ, tadā prabhṛti madhyamabhuktiḥ upacīyate, yāvat kendram rāśiṣaṭkam saṃjātam iti | tataḥ tasmāt rāśiṣaṭkāt kendrāt upacitānām bhuktīnām utkrameṇa apacayaḥ, yāvat kendrasya aṣṭau rāśayaḥ saptaviṃśatiḥ bhāgāḥ dvātriṃśat liptāḥ ca saṃjātāḥ
| etāḥ eva utkrameṇa dvitīyapadāntāt pravigaṇyamānāḥ tulyāḥ iti ādau ante ca suṣamā | athavā ādau ante ca, dvitīyapadanirdiṣṭakendrāt prabhṛti krameṇa yāḥ bhuktayaḥ yāḥ ca tṛtīyapadanirdiṣṭakendrāt utkrameṇa bhuktayaḥ tāḥ tulyāḥ, evam caturthaprathamapadayoḥ api, iti ādau ante ca suṣamā | anyathā duṣṣamā |
body.translated_text: How then are these <s>utsarpiṇī</s>, <s>apasarpiṇī</s>, <s>suṣamā</s>, and <s>duḥṣamā</s> [portions of] planetary daily motion known? To this he says: from the lunar apogee — meaning from the Moon's anomaly (<s>kendra</s>). That is: when the Moon's anomaly has [completed] three signs, two degrees, and twenty-eight minutes, from that point the mean daily motion increases, until the anomaly reaches six signs. Then, from that anomaly of six signs, the accumulated daily motions decrease in reverse order, until the anomaly reaches eight signs, twenty-seven degrees, and thirty-two minutes. These very [values], counted in reverse from the end of the second quadrant, are equal — hence <s>suṣamā</s> at the beginning and end. Alternatively, 'at the beginning and end' [means]: the daily motions from the anomaly specified for the second quadrant in direct order, and those from the anomaly specified for the third quadrant in reverse order, are equal; similarly for the fourth and first quadrants — hence <s>suṣamā</s> at the beginning and end. Otherwise, <s>duḥṣamā</s>.

body.text:
atra indukendram uddiśya ācāryeṇa utsarpiṇyapasarpiṇīsuṣamāduṣṣamāḥ pradarśitāḥ | etat vidhānam anyeṣām api grahāṇām pratipattavyam | tat yathā ã sūryasya yadā kendram rāśitrayam sacatuṣpañcāśalliptam, tadā sūryasya vyāsārdhatulyaḥ karṇaḥ, bhuktiḥ ca madhyamā | yadā ca aṣṭau rāśayaḥ ekonatriṃśadbhāgāḥ liptāḥ ca ṣaṭ gatāḥ [tadā api] vyāsārdhatulyaḥ [karṇaḥ] , madhyamā bhuktiḥ ca | kujā[dīnām api] vyāsārdhatulyam bhūtārāgrahavivaram
bhavati | tathā "[kakṣyāpratimaṇḍalagāḥ] [kālakriyāí, 17] iti asyām kārikāyām vakṣyate || 9 ||
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>Ācārya</s> has demonstrated the <s>utsarpiṇī</s>, <s>apasarpiṇī</s>, <s>suṣamā</s>, and <s>duḥṣamā</s> with reference to the Moon's anomaly. This procedure should be understood for other planets as well. That is: when the Sun's anomaly is three signs with fifty-four minutes, then the Sun's <s>karṇa</s> (hypotenuse) equals the radius, and the daily motion is mean. And when eight signs, twenty-nine degrees, and six minutes have elapsed, [then also] the <s>karṇa</s> equals the radius, and the daily motion is mean. For <s>Kuja</s> (Mars) and other [planets] also, the distance between the Earth and the planet equals the radius [at such points]. As will be stated in the verse '[those moving on] the orbits and eccentric circles' [<s>Kālakriyā</s>, 17]. // 9 //

body.text: āryabhaṭajanmakālaḥ
body.translated_text: The birth-date of <s>Āryabhaṭa</s>

body.text: ācāryāryabhaṭaḥ svajanmakālajñānārtham āha ã
body.translated_text: The <s>Ācārya</s> <s>Āryabhaṭa</s>, for the purpose of knowing his own birth-date, states:

children.text: ṣaṣṭyabdānām ṣaṣṭiḥ yadā vyatītāḥ trayaḥ ca yugapādāḥ |
children.translated_text: When sixty [times] sixty years had elapsed, and three quarter-<s>yugas</s>,

children.text: tryadhikā viṃśatiḥ abdāḥ tadā iha mama janmanaḥ atītāḥ || 10 ||
children.translated_text: twenty-three years had then passed since my birth. // 10 //

body.text: ṣaṣṭyabdānām ṣaṣṭiḥ | ṣaṣṭiḥ abdāḥ ṣaṣṭiguṇāḥ iti arthaḥ | yadā vyatītāḥ | yadā yasmin kāle, vyatītāḥ vyatikrāntāḥ | trayaḥ ca yugapādāḥ | yugasya pādāḥ yugapādāḥ, te ca yadā trisaṅkhyāḥ vyatītāḥ | tryadhikāḥ viṃśatiḥ abdāḥ | tribhiḥ adhikāḥ tryadhikāḥ viṃśatiḥ abdāḥ | tadā | tasmin kāle | mama janmanaḥ atītāḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Sixty [times] sixty years' — sixty years multiplied by sixty, that is the meaning. 'When they had elapsed' — 'when,' at which time; 'had elapsed,' had passed. 'And three quarter-<s>yugas</s>' — the quarters of a <s>yuga</s> are '<s>yugapādas</s>'; and those, when three in number, had elapsed. 'Twenty-three years' — twenty with three more, twenty-three years. 'Then' — at that time. 'Had passed since my birth.'

body.text:
etat eva ācāryāryabhaṭaḥ śāstravyākhyānasamaye vā pāṇḍuraṅgasvāmi-lāṭadeva-niśaṅku-prabhṛtibhyaḥ provāca | atha atra idam praṣṭavyam ã asya vyākhyānam kim upakaroti iti? ucyate ã anena atītena kālena parijñātena sukham ādityādīnām kālaḥ atītaḥ anāgataḥ vā paṭhyate | atha ca sampradāyāvicchedāt vyatītaḥ kālaḥ vijñāyate | na etat asti | anabhidhāne bahu atra smaraṇīyam | trayāṇām yugapādānām varṣasaṅkhyā śūnyāmbarākāśaviyadvedayamāgnayaḥ
[3240000] | gatam ca kaliyugasya | ekasya abhidhāne etāvataḥ tāvat sampradāyāvicchedāt araḥ na kartavyaḥ | kintu ācāryajanmakālāvadheḥ yaḥ uttaraḥ kālaḥ asya eva sampradāyāvicchedaḥ adhigantavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: This very [statement] was told by <s>Ācārya</s> <s>Āryabhaṭa</s> either at the time of expounding the treatise, or to <s>Pāṇḍuraṅgasvāmi</s>, <s>Lāṭadeva</s>, <s>Niśaṅku</s>, and others. Now, here one should ask: What purpose does this explanation serve? It is explained: By this elapsed time, once known, the time — elapsed or future — of the Sun and other [planets] is easily computed. Moreover, the elapsed time is known from the unbroken tradition. This is not so. Without stating [the elapsed time], much would need to be remembered here. The year-count of three quarter-<s>yugas</s> is void-sky-sky-sky-<s>Veda</s>-<s>Yama</s>-fires [= 3,240,000]. And the elapsed [portion] is of the <s>Kali-yuga</s>. By stating one [number], one need not resort to unbroken tradition for so much. Rather, the time subsequent to the boundary of the <s>Ācārya</s>'s birth-date — that alone should be ascertained from the unbroken tradition.

body.text:
anyat ca "ṣaṣṭyabdānām ṣaṣṭiḥ" iti asya abhidhāne prayojanam abhidhāsyate | ayam asya abhiprāyaḥ ã kṛtayugādeḥ ahargaṇaḥ sādhyaḥ | anyathā kṣepaḥ śaśyuccapātayoḥ jāyate iti | kṛtayugādeḥ punar ahargaṇe kriyamāṇe śaśyuccapātayoḥ na eva kṣepaḥ | "budhāhnyajārkodayāt ca laṅkāyām" [gītikāí, 4] iti budhādiḥ ahargaṇaḥ divasavāraḥ | idānīm tu laghugaṇitavyavahārārtham kaliyugāhargaṇaḥ kriyate | śukrādidivasavāraḥ | candroccasya rāśitrayam, rāśiṣaṭkam
ca rāhoḥ kṣepaḥ, tamasaḥ ca maṇḍalāt vilomatvāt viśodhyate | athavā karaṇāgatam eva tamaḥ yathā iṣṭasphuṭacandramasi prakṣipya dakṣiṇottaradigvidheḥ vikṣepānayanam iti |
body.translated_text: Moreover, the purpose of stating 'sixty [times] sixty years' will be described. His intention is this: the day-count should be computed from the beginning of <s>Kṛtayuga</s>. Otherwise, a displacement (<s>kṣepa</s>) occurs for the Moon's apogee and node. But when the day-count is computed from the beginning of <s>Kṛtayuga</s>, no displacement occurs for the Moon's apogee and node. 'From the rising of <s>Budha</s>-day (Wednesday) at <s>Laṅkā</s>' [<s>Gītikā</s>, 4] — the day-count beginning from Wednesday is the weekday. But now, for the purpose of convenient computation, the <s>Kali-yuga</s> day-count is used. The weekday begins from Friday. The displacement of the Moon's apogee is three signs, and of <s>Rāhu</s> (the node), six signs; and since the shadow (<s>tamas</s>) moves in the reverse direction from [its] orbit, [the displacement] is subtracted. Alternatively, the shadow as obtained from the manual (<s>karaṇa</s>) itself — having added it to the desired true Moon, the computation of the north-south latitude [follows].

body.text: atha ahargaṇe dṛṣṭe grahagatyānayanam ã yadi yugāhargaṇena grahāṇām gītikābhihitabhagaṇāḥ labhyante anena ahargaṇena kiyantaḥ iti, labdham samatikrāntāḥ bhagaṇāḥ | śeṣe dvādaśādiguṇite rāśyādimadhyamagrahasiddhiḥ |
body.translated_text: Now, when the day-count is known, the computation of planetary motions: If by the <s>yuga</s>-day-count the revolutions of the planets as stated in the <s>Gītikās</s> are obtained, by this day-count how many? — the result is the elapsed revolutions. When the remainder is multiplied by twelve and so on, the signs and other [units] of the mean planet are obtained.

body.text:
atha atra romakāḥ pratyabdaśodhanena ādityam ānayanti | tena ca ādityena sarvān eva grahān iti | etat atra api pradarśyam | tat yathā ã pratyabdaśodhanam hi nāma caitraśuklapratipadi ardhodayāt ārabhya yāvat ādityaudayikasya maṇḍalagantavyasya bhogakālaḥ | sa yugānte yugaravibhagaṇaiḥ pramāṇecchābhūtaiḥ divasasaṅkhyāḥ eva bhavanti | yathā iṣṭaravibhagaṇaiḥ trairāśikam kriyate, tat yathā ã "yadi yugaravibhagaṇaiḥ bhūdivasasaṅkhyaḥ ahargaṇaḥ
labhyate iṣṭaravibhagaṇaiḥ kiyān iti ahargaṇaḥ labhyate, śeṣe ṣaṣṭyādiguṇite ghaṭikādayaḥ iti ravibhagaṇasamāptikālāvadheḥ ahargaṇaḥ labhyate | tasmāt caitraśuklāvadhiniṣpannavarṣāntikaḥ ahargaṇaḥ śodhyate, caitraśuklādeḥ upariṣṭāt ravibhagaṇasamāptikālāvadhayaḥ bhaviṣyanti |
body.translated_text: Now here, the <s>Romakas</s> compute the Sun by annual correction (<s>pratyabdaśodhana</s>). And by that Sun, all planets [are computed]. This should be demonstrated here too. That is: annual correction means, starting from the half-rising [of the Sun] on the first day of the bright fortnight of <s>Caitra</s>, the duration of the Sun's traversal of its remaining revolution-portion. At the end of the <s>yuga</s>, [this duration], with the <s>yuga</s> Sun-revolutions as the measure-and-desired [quantities], equals the day-count itself. Just as the rule of three is performed with the desired Sun-revolutions: 'If by the <s>yuga</s> Sun-revolutions a day-count equal to the terrestrial-day count is obtained, by the desired Sun-revolutions how much?' — a day-count is obtained. When the remainder is multiplied by sixty and so on, <s>ghaṭikās</s> and so on [are obtained] — thus the day-count from the epoch of Sun-revolution-completion is obtained. From that, the year-end day-count starting from the bright [fortnight] of <s>Caitra</s> is subtracted — and those that are subsequent to the beginning of <s>Caitra</s>'s bright [fortnight] will be [the days] up to the Sun-revolution-completion epoch.

body.text:
athavā varṣāntikena ahargaṇena trairāśikam ã yadi caturyugāhargaṇena khughṛ-tulyāḥ sūryabhagaṇāḥ labhyante, anena kaliyātāhargaṇena kiyantaḥ iti labdham bhagaṇāḥ | śeṣāt gatagantavyam kṛtvā gatagantavyarāśeḥ yugasūryabhagaṇaiḥ bhāgalabdham divasāḥ | śeṣe ṣaṣṭyādiguṇite ghaṭikādayaḥ | caitraśuklādeḥ upariṣṭāt adhaḥ vā ravibhagaṇasamāptikālāvadhayaḥ divasādayaḥ bhavanti | etat eva pratyabdaśodhanam asmābhiḥ karmanibandhe laghutaram
pratipāditam | tat yathā ã
body.translated_text: Alternatively, the rule of three with the year-end day-count: If by the <s>caturyuga</s> day-count, <s>khughṛ</s>-equivalent Sun-revolutions are obtained, by this <s>Kali</s>-elapsed day-count how many? — the result is the revolutions. From the remainder, making [it into] elapsed-and-remaining, and from the elapsed-and-remaining quantity, dividing by the <s>yuga</s> Sun-revolutions, the quotient is the days. When the remainder is multiplied by sixty and so on, <s>ghaṭikās</s> and so on [are obtained]. [These] are the days and so on from the beginning of <s>Caitra</s>'s bright [fortnight] onwards or backwards up to the Sun-revolution-completion epoch. This very annual correction has been presented more concisely by us in the <s>Karmanibandha</s>. That is:

children.translated_text: Having multiplied the years by <s>Rudra</s>-[times]-thousand-hit-six-portions
[and combined] with hole-<s>Vasu</s>-fire-equal-numbers,
always counting, dividing by void-<s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: māsāḥ bhavanti divasāḥ ca hṛte avaśiṣṭāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the months are obtained; and the remaining [portion], when divided, gives the days.
Combining with hole-pair, with <s>Rasa</s>-<s>Rāma</s>-portion,
again, when multiplied by fire-<s>Veda</s>, one should divide the share.
By void-sky-void-two-sage, the destroyed [portions] of <s>tithis</s> (lunar days)
[are obtained]; combining, dividing by element-<s>Yama</s>-<s>Rudra</s>, [gives] the days.
When the years, multiplied by hole-square-moon,
are divided by six-seven-five, the day-and-so-on result [is obtained].
These, combined with the years multiplied by ten, attain the designation
of Sun-born [day-count] — this is my conviction.

body.text:
ravijadivasayojyāḥ ca avamāḥ ye atra labdhāḥ
satatam adhikamāsān śodhayet khāgninighnān |
bhavati yat avaśiṣṭam śodhanīyam samāyām
yadi tat adhikaśuddham kṣepyam eva upadiṣṭam || iti |
body.translated_text: The omitted days (<s>avama</s>) obtained here are to be added to the solar days; one should always subtract the intercalary months, multiplied by void-fire [= 30]; what remains is the subtractive [quantity] for the year — if that subtractive is exhausted, the addition itself is prescribed. Thus [is the verse from the <s>Mahābhāskarīya</s>, 1.22-23, 27-28].

body.text: mahābhāskarīyam, 1.22-23, 27-28
body.translated_text: <s>Mahābhāskarīya</s>, 1.22-23, 27-28

body.text: evam pratyabdaśodhanam ānīya tataḥ arkaḥ sādhyate | katham? etat api tatra uktam eva ã
body.translated_text: Having thus derived the year-by-year correction, from that the Sun is computed. How? This too has been stated there itself:

children.translated_text: The accumulated count of days beginning from the first day of <s>Madhu</s> (Caitra) and <s>Sita</s> (the bright half), diminished and again diminished,
the remainder after division by the planet-dividers [gives] the weekday-great-year-quarter;

children.text: tataḥ idam api śodhyam śodhanīyam samāyām
children.translated_text: then this too — the subtractive — is to be corrected for the year;
the one that has fallen equal or in excess is taken, not the other here.

body.text:
saptatyā divasādyāḥ śarabhāgāḥ dviguṇitāḥ vighaṭikāḥ ca |
tadrahitaḥ grahadehaḥ ravibudhabhṛgavaḥ ca nirdiṣṭāḥ || iti |
[mahābhāskarīyam, 1.30-31]
body.translated_text: The [accumulated] days and so forth, [multiplied] by seventy, [give] arrow-parts (<s>śarabhāga</s>) doubled [to give] sub-<s>ghaṭikās</s> (<s>vighaṭikā</s>). The planetary body diminished by that — the Sun, Mercury, and Venus are specified. Thus [is the verse from the <s>Mahābhāskarīya</s>, 1.30-31].

body.text: evam sūryaḥ siddhaḥ | [tasmāt bhagaṇeṣu] dvādaśaguṇiteṣu sūryabhuktarāśayaḥ prakṣipyante | tataḥ triṃśadguṇiteṣu bhāgāḥ iti | evam sūryāhargaṇaḥ siddhaḥ | sūryāhargaṇa[tulya]m aṃśam ādityaḥ bhuṅkte |
body.translated_text: Thus the Sun is established. From the revolution-numbers multiplied by twelve, the signs traversed by the Sun are added. Then, multiplied by thirty, [gives] the degrees. Thus the Sun-<s>ahargaṇa</s> (day-count) is established. The Sun traverses a degree-measure equal to the Sun-<s>ahargaṇa</s>.

body.text:
atha sarveṣām grahāṇām sūryadivasabhogānayanam | yugaravyabdāḥ ṣaṣṭiśatatrayaguṇitāḥ yugaravidivasāḥ | yadi etaiḥ abhīṣṭagrahabhagaṇāḥ labhyante, tadā ekena ravidivasena kiyantaḥ iti trairāśikanyāyena [labdham bhagaṇātmikā grahagatiḥ] | rāśibhāgaliptānayane dvādaśa-triṃśat-ṣaṣṭiḥ ca guṇakārāḥ | teṣām saṃvargaḥ khakhaṣaḍghanaḥ | ataḥ khakhaṣaḍghanasya khakhaṣaḍghanabhāge ekam, yugaravidivasānām khakhaṣaḍghanabhāgena dvāsaptatiḥ sahasrāṇi,
iti ataḥ dvāsaptatisahasraiḥ pratisvasvagrahabhagaṇānām bhāgaḥ, labhyante grahāṇām sūryadivasabhuktayaḥ ataḥ ca yathālabdhāḥ likhyante ã candramasaḥ liptāḥ dvāviṃśatiḥ liptātrisahasrabhāgāḥ navavasurāmāḥ, bhaumasya liptāḥ ekatriṃśat liptātrisahasrabhāgāḥ rūpakhamunipakṣāḥ, bṛhaspateḥ liptāḥ pañca liptāpañcasaptatyuttaratriṃśatabhāgāḥ dvāviṃśatiḥ, śanaiḥ carasya liptādvayam liptāṣṭādaśasahasrabhāgāḥ śaśikṛtarasāḥ, budhoccasya liptāḥ nava liptāṣaṭtriṃśacchatabhāgāḥ
śaśīṣuvedāḥ, bhṛgoḥ liptāḥ saptatriṃśat liptāṣāṭsahasrabhāgāḥ navanavendurāmāḥ | evam yathāvilikhitasūryadivasagrahabhuktibhiḥ sūryāhargaṇam guṇayet, sūryabhuktaliptābhiḥ ca trairāśikena yat avāptam phalam prakṣipya khakhaṣaḍghanena vibhajet, śeṣam grahabhuktaliptāḥ | iyān tatra viśeṣaḥ candramasi trayodaśaguṇaḥ sūryaḥ kṣepaḥ, budhocce caturguṇaḥ, śukrocce rūpaguṇitaḥ iti | etat api aśeṣagrahānayanam karma laghutaram eva karmanibandhe pradarśitam

children.translated_text: it is to be understood there itself. // 10 //

body.translated_text: Now, the derivation of the daily planetary motions in solar days for all planets. The <s>yuga</s> solar years multiplied by three-hundred-sixty [give] the <s>yuga</s> solar days. If by these [solar days] the desired planet's revolution-numbers are obtained, then by one solar day how much? — by the rule of three, [one obtains] the planetary motion in terms of revolution-numbers. For converting to signs, degrees, and minutes, twelve, thirty, and sixty are the multipliers. Their product is void-void-six-cube [= 21,600]. Therefore, the void-void-six-cube-th part of void-void-six-cube is one; and the void-void-six-cube-th part of the <s>yuga</s> solar days is seventy-two thousand — therefore, by seventy-two thousand, dividing the respective planet's revolution-numbers, the daily planetary motions in solar days are obtained. And as obtained, they are written: For the Moon — minutes: twenty-two; three-thousandths of a minute: nine-<s>vasu</s>-<s>Rāma</s> [= 938]; for Mars — minutes: thirty-one; three-thousandths of a minute: form-void-sage-wing [= 1,070]; for Jupiter — minutes: five; seventy-five-and-thirty-parts of a minute: twenty-two; for Saturn — minutes: two; eighteen-thousandths of a minute: moon-made-rasa [= 664]; for Mercury's fast apogee — minutes: nine; thirty-six-hundredths of a minute: moon-arrow-Veda [= 514]; for Venus — minutes: thirty-seven; six-thousandths of a minute: nine-nine-<s>Indra</s>-<s>Rāma</s> [= 9,933]. Thus, with the daily planetary motions in solar days as written, one should multiply the Sun-<s>ahargaṇa</s>, and by the rule of three with the solar-traversed minutes, add the obtained result and divide by void-void-six-cube [= 21,600]; the remainder is the planet's traversed minutes. The distinction therein is: for the Moon, the Sun multiplied by thirteen is the additive; for Mercury's apogee, multiplied by four; for Venus's apogee, multiplied by one [= the Sun itself]. This also — the complete planetary computation — has been demonstrated in the <s>Karmanibandha</s> as a lighter procedure;

body.text: yugādikālānantyanirdeśaḥ
body.translated_text: Indication of the Beginninglessness of the <s>Yuga</s>-Epoch

body.text: kālapravṛtyānantyapratipādanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of establishing the infinity of time's progression, he says:

children.translated_text: <s>Yuga</s> (age), year, month, and day have commenced simultaneously from the beginning of the bright half of <s>Caitra</s>;

children.text: kālaḥ ayam anādyantaḥ grahabhaiḥ anumīyate kṣetre || 11 ||
children.translated_text: this time is without beginning or end — it is inferred from the planets in the field. // 11 //

body.text:
yugam ca varṣam ca māsaḥ ca divasaḥ ca yugavarṣamāsadivasāḥ, ete samam pravṛttāḥ yugapat pravṛttāḥ iti arthaḥ | kasmāt iti āha ã caitraśuklādeḥ | caitraḥ māsaḥ, tasya [yaḥ] śuklaḥ pakṣaḥ, tasya śukla[pakṣa]sya yaḥ ādiḥ, [sa] ardhodayaḥ iti arthaḥ, tasmāt caitraśuklādeḥ yugādayaḥ ye te yugapat pravṛttāḥ | nanu ca yuge caitraśuklādeḥ pravṛtte sarve eva samam pravṛttāḥ syuḥ | tasmāt yugam caitraśuklādeḥ pravṛttam iti etat eva astu | na iti āha ã śāstrāntare
varṣādīnām anyasmāt pravṛttiḥ abhihitā ã
body.translated_text: <s>Yuga</s> and year and month and day — these are '<s>yugavarṣamāsadivasāḥ</s>' (age-year-month-day). These 'commenced simultaneously' — commenced at the same time, that is the meaning. From what [point]? He says: 'From the beginning of the bright half of <s>Caitra</s>.' The month <s>Caitra</s>, its bright (<s>śukla</s>) fortnight, the beginning of that bright fortnight — meaning the [moment of] half-rising; from that beginning of the bright half of <s>Caitra</s>, the <s>yuga</s>-commencements began simultaneously. Now, if in a <s>yuga</s>, when [things] commence from the beginning of the bright half of <s>Caitra</s>, all would indeed commence simultaneously. Therefore, let just this be [the statement]: 'The <s>yuga</s> commenced from the beginning of the bright half of <s>Caitra</s>.' No, he says — in other treatises, the commencement of years and so forth from different [starting points] has been stated:

children.text: prathame vāsavasya aṃśe dvitīyāṃśe tu ajasya tu |
children.translated_text: In the first quarter of [the <s>nakṣatra</s>] <s>Vāsava</s> (Dhaniṣṭhā), in the second quarter of <s>Aja</s> (Aja Ekapāda/Pūrvabhādrapadā),
in the third quarter of <s>Revatī</s>, in the fourth quarter of <s>Yama</s> (Bharaṇī),

children.text: saumyasya prathamāṃśe ca dvitīyāṃśe punar vasoḥ |
children.translated_text: in the first quarter of <s>Saumya</s> (Mṛgaśiras), and again in the second quarter of <s>Vasu</s> (Dhaniṣṭhā),

children.text: sārpasya aṃśe tṛtīye tu caturthāṃśe bhagasya ca ||
children.translated_text: in the third quarter of <s>Sārpa</s> (Āśleṣā), in the fourth quarter of <s>Bhaga</s> (Uttaraphalgunī),

children.text: tvāṣṭrasya ādyāṃśake ca eva dvitīyāṃśe viśākhayoḥ |
children.translated_text: in the first quarter of <s>Tvāṣṭra</s> (Citrā), and in the second quarter of <s>Viśākhā</s>,

children.text: aindrasya aṃśe tṛtīye ca āpyasya aṃśe caturthake ||
children.translated_text: in the third quarter of <s>Aindra</s> (Jyeṣṭhā), in the fourth quarter of <s>Āpya</s> (Pūrvāṣāḍhā) —

children.text: yadā samānām adhipaḥ bṛhaspatiḥ ataḥ utthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: when <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter), the lord of the years, having arisen from that [<s>nakṣatra</s>],

children.text: udayati aṃśakānte vā prathamaḥ paryayaḥ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: rises at the end of the quarter, the first cycle occurs.

body.text: iti|
body.translated_text: Thus [ends the citation].

body.text:
evam varṣāṇām pravṛttiḥ atidūrabhinnā | tasyām ca varṣapravṛttau bhinnāyām māsadivasapravṛttī api bhinne eva bhavataḥ | athavā evam syāt ã iyam varṣāṇām pravṛttiḥ nānāprakārā phalārthibhiḥ saṃhitākāraiḥ upadiṣṭā | na eṣā prasiddhā loke, na paratantreṣu | tasmāt yā paratantreṣu loke ca prasiddhā pravṛttiḥ tasyāḥ grahaṇam bhaviṣyati iti | etat api na | tat yathā ã surāṣṭrāsu kārtikaśuklapratipadaḥ pravṛttiḥ varṣamāsadivasānām, āśvayujaḥ [kṛṣṇa]pañcadaśyām
nivṛttiḥ | tathā ca magadhāsu āṣāḍhe kṛṣṇapratipadaḥ samāmāsadivasānām pravṛttiḥ, āṣāḍhasitapañcadaśyām nivṛttiḥ | tathā ca arthaśāstre api abhihitam ã "triśatam sacatuṣpañcāśatam ahorātrāṇām karma sāṃvatsaraḥ, tam āṣāḍhīparyavasānam ūnam pūrṇam vā dadyāt" iti | siṃharājena sahasrākṣare nibaddham ã
body.translated_text: Thus the commencements of years are widely different. And when the commencement of years is different, the commencements of months and days also become different. Alternatively, it may be [argued] thus: This variety of year-commencements has been prescribed by the <s>Saṃhitā</s> authors for the purpose of [predicting] results. This is not well-known in common usage, nor in other treatises. Therefore, the commencement that is well-known in other treatises and in common usage will be adopted. This too is not [correct]. As follows: In <s>Surāṣṭra</s>, the commencement of year, month, and day is from the first [day] of the bright half of <s>Kārtika</s>, and the termination is on the fifteenth of the dark half of <s>Āśvayuja</s>. Likewise, in <s>Magadha</s>, the commencement of year, month, and day is from the first [day] of the dark half of <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, and the termination is on the fifteenth of the bright half of <s>Āṣāḍha</s>. And in the <s>Arthaśāstra</s> too it is stated: 'Three hundred and fifty-four day-and-nights constitute the operative year; let one give that [year] ending with <s>Āṣāḍhī</s>, whether deficient or complete.' By <s>Siṃharāja</s>, in the <s>Sahasrākṣara</s>, it is recorded:

children.translated_text: At sunrise at <s>Laṅkā</s>, on the full-moon day of <s>Āṣāḍhī</s>, on a Monday,
with <s>kṛta</s>-<s>kṛta</s> years elapsed from the epoch of the <s>Śaka</s> lord, the beginning of the <s>yuga</s> [occurs].

body.text: iti |
body.translated_text: Thus [ends the citation].

body.text: yugādīnām caitraśuklādeḥ pravṛttyabhidhānam siddham eva etat |
body.translated_text: The statement that the <s>yuga</s>-commencements begin from the bright half of <s>Caitra</s> — this is indeed established.

body.text: idānām praṣṭavyam ã siṃharājena na śuklāntaḥ māsaḥ svatantre pratipāditaḥ, tathā ca loke śuklāntaḥ eva prasiddhaḥ, horāyām api ã
body.translated_text: Now, the following must be asked: <s>Siṃharāja</s> did not establish in his own treatise the month ending with the bright [fortnight]; and in common usage too, the month ending with the bright [fortnight] is well-known; in <s>Horā</s> (astrology) also:

body.text: candrayutāt navabhāgāt māsaḥ śuklāntanāmasamaḥ |
body.translated_text: From the ninth part [of the zodiac] conjoined with the Moon, the month has a name corresponding to the bright-ending [system].

body.text: iti |
body.translated_text: Thus [ends the citation].

body.text: atra ucyate ã yat tu siṃharājena abhihitam tat svābhiprāyeṇa adhikamāsakāvamānām yugapat pravṛttatvāt āṣāḍhapaurṇamāsī [taḥ ārabhya caturdaśī] paryantāvasānam saṃvatsaraḥ iti parikalpitaḥ | yadi api ucyate "śuklāntaḥ māsaḥ loke prasiddhaḥ" iti, tat na | nanu sarveṣu eva deśeṣu māsāḥ | santi ca deśāḥ kṛṣṇāntamāsavyavahārāḥ surāṣṭraprabhṛtayaḥ | yat api ucyate ã
body.translated_text: Here it is said: What <s>Siṃharāja</s> has stated is according to his own intent — since the intercalary months and omitted days commence simultaneously, the year is conceived as [ending on the] fourteenth up to the full-moon of <s>Āṣāḍha</s>. Even if it is said 'The month ending with the bright [fortnight] is well-known in common usage,' that is not so. Indeed, months exist in all regions. And there are regions — <s>Surāṣṭra</s> and others — where the convention is of months ending with the dark [fortnight]. As for what is also said:

body.text: candrayutāt navabhāgāt māsaḥ śuklāntanāmasamaḥ |
body.translated_text: From the ninth part [of the zodiac] conjoined with the Moon, the month has a name corresponding to the bright-ending [system] —

body.text: iti, asya api anyaḥ eva arthaḥ | candrayutāt navabhāgāt praṣṭuḥ māsaḥ vācyaḥ | [sa śuklāntena] nāmnā sadṛśaḥ | śuklānte [na] hi māsasya nāmaparijñānam | kṛttikāsu yuktaḥ candramā asmin sati kārtikaḥ māsaḥ iti ādi |
body.translated_text: this too has a different meaning. From the ninth part conjoined with the Moon, the month of the questioner is to be stated. It has a name similar to [that of] the bright-ending [month]. For the identification of a month's name [occurs] at the bright end — when the Moon is conjoined with <s>Kṛttikā</s>, that month is the month of <s>Kārtika</s>, and so forth.

body.text: anyat ca ã śuklāntena māsena na kadācit api mīnameṣasandhau māsasya varṣasya vā ante grahāḥ syuḥ |
body.translated_text: Moreover: with a month ending in the bright [fortnight], at the junction of <s>Mīna</s> (Pisces) and <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries) — at the end of the month or of the year — the planets would never [be at that point].

body.text: atra āha yavaneśvaraḥ ã
body.translated_text: Here <s>Yavaneśvara</s> says:

body.text: māse tu śuklapratipatpravṛtte pūrve śaśī mandabalaḥ daśāhe |
body.translated_text: In a month commencing from the bright-fortnight first day, the Moon is of feeble strength in the first ten days.

body.text: iti śuklādiḥ māsaḥ | yadā punar śuklādiḥ māsaḥ tadā punar śrutyarthaḥ anuṣṭhitaḥ bhavati | evam hi śrutau paṭhyate ã
body.translated_text: Thus the month begins from the bright [fortnight]. And when the month begins from the bright [fortnight], then the Vedic injunction is properly fulfilled. For in the <s>Śruti</s> it is read:

body.text: eṣā hi vai saṃvatsarasya prathamā rātriḥ yat phālgunī paurṇamāsī yā uttarā |
body.translated_text: This indeed is the first night of the year — namely the full-moon of <s>Phālgunī</s> that is the latter one (Uttarā).

body.text: iti | [yadi] kṛṣṇa[pratipad]ādiḥ māsaḥ syāt, tadā katham iyam uttarā paurṇamāsī phālgunī bhavati, yat uta tat caitramāsaḥ syāt ? kutaḥ? phālgunyām paurṇamāsyām phālgunaḥ māsaḥ pūrṇaḥ, tadā uttarā paurṇamāsī caitra[māsasya], pratipatkṛṣṇāditvāt māsasya | tataḥ manyāmahe na adya api phālgunaḥ māsaḥ samāpyate iti | yasmāt āha ã
body.translated_text: If the month were to begin from the dark-fortnight first day, then how could this full-moon of <s>Uttarā Phālgunī</s> be [the last night of the year], when it would [actually] be the [<s>Caitra</s>] month? Why? Because on the full-moon of <s>Phālgunī</s>, the month of <s>Phālguna</s> is complete; then the full-moon of <s>Uttarā</s> would be of the <s>Caitra</s> month, since the month begins from the dark-fortnight first day. Then we would think: 'Even now the month of <s>Phālguna</s> has not yet ended.' Because [the <s>Śruti</s>] says:

body.text: phālgunī paurṇamāsī yā uttarā |
body.translated_text: The full-moon of <s>Phālgunī</s> that is the latter one (Uttarā).

body.text: iti |
body.translated_text: Thus [ends the citation].

body.text: anyat ca ã
body.translated_text: Moreover:

body.text: yā asau
body.translated_text: One should establish the [sacred]

body.text:
vaiśākhasya amāvāsyā tasyām agnim ādadhīta, sā rohiṇyā sampadyate |
[śatapatha-brāhmaṇam, 11.1.1.7]
body.translated_text: fire on the new-moon of <s>Vaiśākha</s>; that [new-moon] coincides with <s>Rohiṇī</s>. [<s>Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa</s>, 11.1.1.7]

body.text: iti |
body.translated_text: Thus [ends the citation].

body.text:
yadi śuklāntaḥ māsaḥ parikalpyate tadā na vaiśākhasya amāvāsyāyām rohiṇyā candramasaḥ yogaḥ vidyate | yasmāt caitrapaurṇamāsyām citrāyām somaḥ yujyate, tasyām caitryām vyatītāyām vaiśākhapratipat | tataḥ ca svātyādiṣu nakṣatreṣu pratipat [prabhṛti] gaṇyamānā amāvāsyā bharaṇyā yujyate, na rohiṇyā | atha candragativiśeṣāt iti [cet, na] | nakṣatrārdhasya sakalasya vā hrāsavṛddhī bhavataḥ, na nakṣatradvayasya | śuklādau punar māse vaiśākhapaurṇamāsyām
vyatītāyām vaiśākhasya eva amāvāsyā bhaviṣyati | tataḥ kṛṣṇapakṣapratipatprabhṛtyanurādhādiṣu gaṇyamānāsu rohiṇyā amāvāsyāyāḥ ca yogaḥ saṃbhavati |
body.translated_text: If a month ending with the bright [fortnight] is assumed, then on the new-moon of <s>Vaiśākha</s> there is no conjunction of <s>Rohiṇī</s> with the Moon. Because on the full-moon of <s>Caitra</s>, the Moon is conjoined with <s>Citrā</s>; when that <s>Caitrī</s> [full-moon] has passed, it is the first day of <s>Vaiśākha</s>. Then, counting [successive <s>nakṣatras</s>] from <s>Svātī</s> and so forth starting from the first day, the new-moon is conjoined with <s>Bharaṇī</s>, not with <s>Rohiṇī</s>. Now, if [one objects] that it is due to a peculiarity of the Moon's motion — [the answer is] no; there is decrease or increase of half a <s>nakṣatra</s> or a whole [<s>nakṣatra</s>], not of two <s>nakṣatras</s>. But when the month begins from the bright [fortnight], the new-moon of <s>Vaiśākha</s> will fall after the full-moon of <s>Vaiśākha</s> has passed. Then, counting [<s>nakṣatras</s>] from the dark-fortnight first day onwards through <s>Anurādhā</s> and so forth, the conjunction of [the Moon with] <s>Rohiṇī</s> and the new-moon is possible.

body.text: anyat ca ã
body.translated_text: Moreover:

body.text: saḥ aparapakṣe apa oṣadhīḥ praviśati |
body.translated_text: In the latter fortnight, he enters the plants.

body.text: iti |
body.translated_text: Thus [ends the citation].

body.text: śatapatha [11.1.5.3] evam paṭhyate | tatra aparapakṣaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ, [na] śuklaḥ | anyat ca smārtavacanam ã
body.translated_text: In the <s>Śatapatha</s> [11.1.5.3] it is read thus. There, the 'latter fortnight' is the dark [fortnight], not the bright. Moreover, a <s>Smṛti</s> statement:

body.text: aparapakṣe śrāddham kurvīta ūrdhvam vā caturthyāḥ |
body.translated_text: One should perform the <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral offering) in the latter fortnight, or after the fourth [day].

body.text: iti atra kṛṣṇādi[māsatvāt] pūrvapakṣaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ, aparaḥ śuklaḥ | aparatvāt śuklapakṣasya śuklapakṣe eva śrāddhavidhiḥ prāpnoti na kṛṣṇe, iṣyate ca śukle [tare], tasmāt śuklādiḥ māsaḥ iti | tataḥ "yugavarṣamāsadivasāḥ samam pravṛttāḥ tu caitraśuklādeḥ" iti |
body.translated_text: Here, since the month begins from the dark [fortnight], the prior fortnight is the dark and the latter is the bright. Because the bright fortnight is the latter, the injunction of <s>śrāddha</s> in the bright fortnight would follow — not in the dark; yet it is desired [to be performed] in the bright [fortnight]. Therefore, the month begins from the bright [fortnight]. Hence: '<s>Yuga</s>, year, month, and day commenced simultaneously from the beginning of the bright half of <s>Caitra</s>.'

body.text: atra utprekṣitapūrvapakṣaḥ draṣṭavyaḥ | yugādīnām caitra[śuklāditaḥ pravṛtti]tvāt kālasya ādimattāprasaṅgaḥ iti āha ã kālaḥ ayam anādyantaḥ | ayam kālaḥ asmābhiḥ yugādiḥ abhihitaḥ, caitraśuklādeḥ pravṛttaḥ iti | na asya antaḥ na asya ādiḥ | vyavahārārtham ādiḥ antaḥ ca parikalpitaḥ | yadi kālasya ādiḥ syāt tataḥ kim syāt? āha ã saṃsārasya ādimattā prāpnoti, iṣyate ca anādiḥ saṃsāraḥ iti | tasmāt yuktam "kālaḥ ayam anādyantaḥ" iti |
body.translated_text: Here a hypothetical objection should be considered. Since the <s>yuga</s>-commencements begin from the bright half of <s>Caitra</s>, the implication would be that time has a beginning — [to address this] he says: 'This time is without beginning or end.' This time that has been described by us as having its <s>yuga</s>-commencement and as beginning from the bright half of <s>Caitra</s> — it has no end, and it has no beginning. The beginning and end are conceived merely for the sake of practical convention. If time had a beginning, then what would follow? He says: It would follow that <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence) has a beginning; but it is accepted that <s>saṃsāra</s> is beginningless. Therefore, the statement 'This time is without beginning or end' is well-founded.

body.text:
katham punar asya ādiḥ vyavahārārtham parikalpitaḥ iti āha ã grahabhaiḥ anumīyate kṣetre | grahāḥ ca bhāni ca grahabhāni | taiḥ grahabhaiḥ anumīyate ādiḥ antaḥ ca | "māṅ māne" [pāṇinīyadhātupāṭhaḥ 1143] iti ayam dhātuḥ dhūmāt agnyanumānam iti atra māne vartate | atra punar grahabhaiḥ anumīyate iti mānārthaḥ eva | vrīhyādirāśayaḥ prasthādibhiḥ anumīyante, kuṅkumādayaḥ vā palādibhiḥ, evam grahabhaiḥ iti | yadā sarve eva grahāḥ yugapat
mīnameṣasandhau kṣitisaṃyuktāḥ tadā yugasya ādiḥ iti | kaḥ bhuvaḥ grahasya ca yogaḥ, dvayoḥ atyantaviprakṛṣṭayoḥ? na eṣaḥ doṣaḥ | mukhyasya yogasya asaṃbhavāt gauṇaḥ yogaḥ parigṛhyate | yatra bhūlagnaḥ iva grahaḥ lakṣyate sa bhūgrahayoḥ yogaḥ | sa ca udayāstamayayoḥ saṃbhavati iti udayāstamayayoḥ vā parigṛhyate |
body.translated_text: Now, how is the beginning [of the <s>yuga</s>] conceived for practical purposes? He says: it is inferred by the planets and stars in the celestial sphere. Planets and stars together are '<s>grahabhāni</s>.' By those planets and stars, the beginning and end are inferred. The root '<s>māṅ</s>' [means] 'to measure' [<s>Pāṇinīya Dhātupāṭha</s> 1143] — as in 'fire is inferred from smoke,' this root is used in the sense of measurement. Here too, 'it is inferred by the planets and stars' is in the sense of measurement. Just as quantities of rice etc. are measured by <s>prasthas</s> and similar [units], or saffron etc. by <s>palas</s> and similar [units], so too by the planets and stars. When all the planets simultaneously are conjoined with the Earth at the junction of <s>Mīna</s> (Pisces) and <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries), that is the beginning of the <s>yuga</s>. What is the conjunction of the Earth and a planet, when the two are extremely far apart? This is not a fault. Since a primary conjunction is impossible, a secondary conjunction is accepted. Where a planet appears as if touching the horizon — that is the conjunction of Earth and planet. And that occurs at rising and setting; hence [the conjunction] is taken at rising or setting.

body.text: anye punar anyathā vyāvarṇayanti ã grahabhaiḥ anumīyate iti | grahaiḥ ca nakṣatraiḥ ca kālasya ādiḥ antaḥ ca parikalpyate | tat yathā ã
body.translated_text: Others, however, explain it differently: 'It is inferred by the planets and stars' — by the planets and by the <s>nakṣatras</s> (constellations), the beginning and end of time are conceived. That is as follows:

body.text:
udeti yasmin nakṣatre pravāsopagataḥ aṅgirāḥ |
tasmāt saṃvatsaraḥ māsāt bārhaspatyaḥ pragaṇyatām || iti |
body.translated_text: In whichever <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Aṅgiras</s> (Jupiter), who has gone abroad, rises — from that [<s>nakṣatra</s>], the <s>Bārhaspatya</s> (Jovian) year and month should be reckoned. Thus.

body.text: bṛhaspaticāravaśāt kālasya ādiḥ parikalpitaḥ | loke ca evam vaktāraḥ bhavanti ã "svātau udite prasthāsyāmahe udayaḥ " iti, "śukre astam gate prasthitaḥ" iti, "adya kṛttikāsu madhyasthitāsu dārukaḥ [gataḥ]" iti ādi | kṣetre | kṣetram bhagolaḥ, tasmin bhagole, nakṣatragrahacāravaśāt ādiḥ antaḥ ca parikalpitaḥ || 11 ||
body.translated_text: By the course of <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter), the beginning of time was conceived. And in common parlance, people speak thus: 'When <s>Svātī</s> has risen, we shall depart at dawn,' or 'He set out when <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) had set,' or 'Today, <s>Dāruka</s> [departed] when <s>Kṛttikā</s> was at the meridian,' and so on. In the celestial sphere: the <s>kṣetra</s> (field) is the <s>bhagola</s> (celestial sphere); in that celestial sphere, the beginning and end [of time] are conceived by the course of the <s>nakṣatras</s> and planets. // 11 //

body.text: grahāṇām samagatitvam
body.translated_text: The equal [linear
velocity of the planets]

body.text: grahāṇām samagatipratipādanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of demonstrating that the planets have equal [linear] velocity, he says:

children.translated_text: In sixty solar years, the planets complete the circumference of the stellar [sphere],
revolving uniformly in their own orbits, [they traverse] the circumference of the sky in a divine [<s>yuga</s>]. // 12 //

body.text:
ṣaṣṭyā sūryābdānām ādityavarṣāṇām ṣaṣṭyā grahāḥ nakṣatrakakṣyām prapūrayanti, nakṣatrakakṣyātulyāni yojanāni svāsu svāsu kakṣyāsu gacchanti iti arthaḥ | [kiyadyojanāni] punar nakṣatrakakṣyāyām grahāḥ sūryābdānām ṣaṣṭyā pūrayanti? ucyate ã vasuviyadambarākāśarasayamatriśailacandrāḥ [173260008] | na etat asmābhiḥ nakṣatrakakṣyāpramāṇam dṛṣṭam | kim tarhi? kā eṣā pratipāditā iti? ucyate ã "bhavāṃśe arkaḥ" [gītikāí, 6] iti | atra katham
punar etena eva nakṣatrakakṣyātulyāni yojanāni gacchanti iti ucyate? yadi khyughṛ-tulyaiḥ arkavarṣaiḥ svān-svān bhagaṇān grahāḥ bhuñjante [tadā] ṣaṣṭyā sūryābdaiḥ kiyantaḥ iti | ṣaṣṭibhāgena api ṣaṣṭyā ekaḥ, punar ṣaṣṭibhāgena ete[ṣām] khyughṛ-tulyānām arkavarṣāṇām dvāsaptatisahasrāṇi | evam yathābhāgena avinaṣṭarāśayaḥ sthāpyāḥ | tataḥ punar api ã yadi ekena bhagaṇena pratisvakakṣyā labhyate [tadā] ṣaṣṭyabdabhogena kā iti sarvagrahebhyaḥ nakṣatrakakṣyā
labhyate |
body.translated_text: In sixty solar years — in sixty years of the Sun, the planets complete the stellar orbit; meaning they traverse, in their respective orbits, a distance in <s>yojanas</s> equal to the stellar orbit. How many <s>yojanas</s> do the planets complete in the stellar orbit in sixty solar years? It is said: <s>Vasu</s>-sky-sky-sky-<s>Rasa</s>-<s>Yama</s>-mountain-three-mountain-Moon [173,260,008]. We have not directly seen the measure of the stellar orbit. What then? How is it established? It is said: 'In the <s>Bhava</s>-part, the Sun' [<s>Gītikā</s> 6]. How is it stated here that they traverse exactly as many <s>yojanas</s> as the stellar orbit? If in <s>khyughṛ</s>-many solar years the planets complete their own revolutions, then in sixty solar years, how many? One-sixtieth [of the total], and again one-sixtieth of those <s>khyughṛ</s>-many solar years gives seventy-two thousand. Thus the quantities are to be set down proportionally without losing remainders. Then again: if by one revolution one's own orbit is obtained, then by the sixty-year traverse, what? — from all planets, the stellar orbit is obtained.

body.text:
divyena nabhaḥparidhim | divi bhavam divyam, yugam iti arthaḥ | katham punar divyaśabdena yugam abhidhīyate? yasmāt divi sañcaratām grahāṇām ekatra yogaḥ bhavati, ataḥ [divyam yugam uktam tena] divyena nabhaḥparidhim | nabhasaḥ paridhiḥ nabhaḥparidhiḥ, ākāśakakṣyā iti arthaḥ | katham idam ucyate? nanu ca viyat aparimitayojanapramāṇam iti śrūyate | tasya parimitayojanapramāṇam katham kakṣyā bhavet? ucyate ã viyat asmākam yāvat
divasakaramarīcinidhānam avabhāsayati tāvat viyat iti | ataḥ param ākāśam aprameyam iti | atra khakakṣyābhidhānena etat pratipādayati, iyatpramāṇam viyadarkamarīcayaḥ prāpnuvanti iti |
body.translated_text: The circumference of the sky in a divine [period]: that which pertains to heaven (<s>diva</s>) is <s>divya</s>, meaning a <s>yuga</s>. How does the word <s>divya</s> denote a <s>yuga</s>? Because the conjunction of the planets, which move in heaven, occurs at one place — therefore [it is called] <s>divya</s> (celestial), [and] by that <s>divya</s> [period, they traverse] the circumference of the sky. The circumference of <s>nabhas</s> (the sky) is '<s>nabhaḥparidhi</s>' — meaning the orbit of space. How can this be said? Is it not heard that space is of immeasurable extent in <s>yojanas</s>? How can an orbit of finite <s>yojana</s>-measure exist for it? It is said: space, as far as it is illuminated by the rays of the day-maker (Sun) — that much is 'space.' Beyond that, the sky is immeasurable. Here, by the designation '<s>khakakṣyā</s>' (sky-orbit), he demonstrates this: the rays of the Sun in space extend to this measure.

body.text:
samam bhramantaḥ | tulyayā [gatyā] bhramantaḥ iti arthaḥ | yāvanti yojanāni svakakṣyāyām śaśī saṃcarati tāvanti eva yojanāni ārkiḥ api svakakṣyāyām sañcarati | tat yathā ã yadi ekena bhagaṇena svakakṣyā labhyate [tadā] yugabhagaṇaiḥ kim iti khakakṣyā labhyate | athavā ã ṣaṣṭyabdabhogena nakṣatrakakṣyā labhyate svaiḥ yugabhagaṇaiḥ kim iti khakakṣyā labhyate | evam yojanagatena grahāḥ tulyagatayaḥ | kakṣyātaḥ grahāṇām madhyamānayanam ã yadi
[yuga]bhūdinaiḥ sarve eva svāsu kakṣyāsu samagatyā bhramantaḥ [kha]kakṣyātulyāni yojanāni prayānti, ekena ahnā kiyanti iti sarvagrahāṇām yojanagatā dinabhuktiḥ labhyate iti, khakakṣyāyām bhūdinaiḥ bhāge hṛte yojanagatā grahāṇām dinabhuktiḥ labhyate | tayā trairāśikam bhaṅktvā madhyamagrahāḥ ānīyante ã yadi svakakṣyāyojanaiḥ bhagaṇaḥ labhyate tadā gatiyojanaiḥ kim iti āhnikī bhuktiḥ labhyate, tataḥ punar api ã yadi ekena ahnā bhuktiḥ labhyate ahargaṇena
kim iti | atra ekaḥ pūrvatrairāśike guṇakāraḥ, [apare bhāgahāraḥ |] ataḥ guṇakārabhāgahārayoḥ tulyatvāt naṣṭayoḥ ahargaṇasya dina[gati]yojanāni guṇakāraḥ sthitaḥ, [svakakṣyāyojanāni bhāgahāraḥ, labdhiḥ] bhagaṇādayaḥ | [uktam ca] ã
body.translated_text: Revolving uniformly: meaning revolving with equal velocity. As many <s>yojanas</s> as the Moon traverses in its own orbit, exactly that many <s>yojanas</s> does <s>Ārkī</s> (Saturn, son of the Sun) also traverse in its own orbit. That is: if by one revolution one's own orbit is obtained, then by the <s>yuga</s>-revolutions, what? — the sky-orbit is obtained. Alternatively: by the sixty-year traverse the stellar orbit is obtained; by one's own <s>yuga</s>-revolutions, what? — the sky-orbit is obtained. Thus, in terms of <s>yojana</s>-distance, the planets have equal velocity. Deriving the mean [positions of] planets from the orbits: if in [<s>yuga</s>]-terrestrial-days all [planets], revolving with equal velocity in their own orbits, traverse as many <s>yojanas</s> as the sky-orbit, then in one day how many? — from this, the daily motion in <s>yojanas</s> of all planets is obtained. Dividing the sky-orbit by the terrestrial days, the daily motion of the planets in <s>yojanas</s> is obtained. Breaking that into a rule of three, the mean planets are derived: if by the <s>yojanas</s> of one's own orbit a revolution is obtained, then by the <s>yojanas</s> of motion, what? — the daily traverse is obtained. Then again: if by one day the [daily] traverse is obtained, then by the <s>ahargaṇa</s> (day-count), what? Here, 'one' is the multiplier in the first rule of three [and the divisor in the second]. Therefore, since the multiplier and divisor are equal and cancel out, the <s>ahargaṇa</s> multiplied by the daily-motion <s>yojanas</s> remains as the multiplier, [one's own orbit <s>yojanas</s> as the divisor,] and the result is revolutions etc. [And it is stated:]

children.text: ambarakakṣyā bhūdinahṛtā phalam tatra yojanāni teṣu |
children.translated_text: The sky-orbit divided by the terrestrial days — the result there is <s>yojanas</s>; in those [<s>yojanas</s>],
multiplied by the elapsed days, divided by one's own planetary orbit — [gives] revolutions and so forth.

body.text: iti | a[thavā khakakṣyā]hargaṇasaṃvarge svakakṣyābhūdinasaṃvargahṛte bhagaṇādayaḥ bhavanti || 12 ||
body.translated_text: Thus. [Alternatively,] the product of the sky-orbit and the <s>ahargaṇa</s>, divided by the product of one's own orbit and the terrestrial days, gives revolutions and so forth. // 12 //

body.text: grahāṇām samagatitvena kakṣyāvyavasthā
body.translated_text: The arrangement of orbits due to the equal [linear
velocity of the planets]

body.text: samagatyā pravṛttagrahakakṣyāvyavasthāpradarśanārtham āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of demonstrating the arrangement of orbits of planets moving with equal velocity, he says:

children.text: maṇḍalam alpam adhastāt kālena alpena pūrayati candraḥ |
children.translated_text: The Moon completes a small orbit below in a short time;

children.text: upariṣṭāt sarveṣām mahat ca mahatā śanaiḥ cārī || 13 ||
children.translated_text: above all, [<s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn)], the slow-mover, [completes] a large [orbit] in a long time. // 13 //

body.text:
maṇḍalam alpam adhastāt | sarveṣām adhaḥ vyavasthitam maṇḍalam alpam alpe[na kālena pūraya]ti candramāḥ | adhastāt iti anena eva maṇḍalasya alpatvasiddhiḥ, alpam iti etat na vaktavyam | katham adhastāt iti etāvati ucyamāne maṇḍalasya alpatvam gamyate? ucyate ã upari upari kakṣyāḥ vyavasthitāḥ | tāsām upari upari vyavasthitānām adhaḥ yā vyavasthitā sā sarvatanīyasī | tasmāt adhastāt [induḥ] syāt | na etat asti | "bhānām adhaḥ śanaiḥ cara" [kālakriyāí,
15] iti atra kakṣyāṇām upari upari vyavasthitim vakṣyati | nanu ca anye bruvate ã sarveṣām upari candramasaḥ kakṣyā iti | [tat ayuktam |] sarveṣām grahāṇām adhaḥ candrakakṣyā iti āha | yadi upari syāt tadā candrasya grahanakṣatrabhede sphuṭakalaṅkahariṇe grahanakṣatra[tārāḥ dṛśyeran] | sūryavaśāt yadi upari candraḥ syāt tadā sūryeṇa ārāt vyavasthitena sadā candramasoḥ api svasya ārāt bhāgam akhaṇḍam dṛśyeta, uparisthitaḥ [na upalakṣyate] | tasmāt sarveṣām
adhaḥ candramāḥ |
body.translated_text: A small orbit below: the Moon completes the orbit situated below all, which is small, in a short time. By the word 'below' itself the smallness of the orbit is established — [so] the word 'small' need not be stated. How is the smallness of the orbit understood merely from saying 'below'? It is said: the orbits are arranged one above the other. Of those arranged successively higher, the one situated lowest is the most slender of all. Therefore, [the Moon] is below. But this is not so — [because] he will state the arrangement of orbits one above the other in 'Below the stars is the slow-mover [<s>Śani</s>]' [<s>Kālakriyāpāda</s>, verse 15]. Now, others say: the orbit of the Moon is above all [planets]. [That is incorrect.] The orbit of the Moon is below all planets, he says. If it were above, then when the Moon passes in front of a star, one would see the star through the Moon's clearly visible spots. If the Moon were above due to the Sun's [influence], then since the Sun is situated far away, the full disc of the Moon would always be visible — [but] one situated above is not [so] observed. Therefore, the Moon is below all.

body.text: anye punar sugata[matā]valambinaḥ sūryācandramasoḥ ekām kakṣyām ācakṣate ã
body.translated_text: Others, however, followers of the <s>Sugata</s> (Buddha), declare a single orbit for the Sun and Moon:

children.translated_text: <s>Meru</s>'s half[-height] — the Moon and Sun are fifty and fifty-one <s>yojanas</s> [respectively];

children.text: ardharātraḥ astagamanam madhyāhnaḥ udayaḥ sakṛt || iti ||
children.translated_text: midnight is [their] setting, midday [their] rising, at once. Thus.

body.text:
na evam yujyate | yadi pañcāśat yojanāni candraḥ, ekapañcāśat [yojanāni] sūryaḥ tadā kim iti sūryaḥ [na] mahān upalabhyate, tulyau etau [ardho]ditau ardhāstamitau paurṇamāsyām lakṣyete? atha vidūratvāt arkaḥ na mahān upalakṣyate iti cet na | tarhi mandarārdhe sūryācandramasoḥ dūrībhūtaḥ arkaḥ | anyat ca tulyakakṣyāvyavasthitatvāt sūryācandramasoḥ sūryagrahaṇam na eva syāt | na ca candramasam muktvā anyaḥ rāhuḥ asti yena savitā chādyate | yadi api adhaḥ candraḥ
syāt tathā api mahattvāt sūryabimbasya na eva arkaḥ sakalaḥ chādyate | na eva arkaḥ candreṇa chādyate iti cet tat api uttaratra vyākhyāsyate |
body.translated_text: This is not tenable. If the Moon is fifty <s>yojanas</s> and the Sun fifty-one <s>yojanas</s>, then why is the Sun not observed as larger? The two appear equal [in size] when half-risen or half-set on a full-moon day. If [one says] the Sun is not observed as larger because of its greater distance — no; then [at] half of <s>Mandara</s> (= <s>Meru</s>), the Sun would be farther from the Sun and Moon [observer]. Moreover, since the Sun and Moon would be in the same orbit, a solar eclipse could never occur. And there is no other <s>Rāhu</s> besides the Moon by which the Sun is obscured. Even if the Moon were below, due to the largeness of the Sun's disc, the Sun would never be completely obscured. [If one says] the Sun is not obscured by the Moon at all — that too will be explained later.

body.text:
kālena alpena pūrayati candraḥ | alpena stokena kālena pūrayati | kim? tat alpam maṇḍalam adhaḥ vyavasthitam | upariṣṭāt sarveṣām maṇḍalānām mahat maṇḍalam mahatā kālena śanaiḥ caraḥ pūrayati | etau alpamahatkakṣyāmaṇḍalaparimāṇau grahau uddiṣṭau, anyeṣām ca [maṇḍalāni svabuddhyā vijñeyāni] | tat yathā ã candramāḥ divasasaṅkhyayā saptaviṃśatyā sārdhaikayā maṇḍalam gacchati, budhaśukraravayaḥ kiñcit ūnena varṣeṇa, bhaumaḥ kiñcit ūnena
varṣadva[yena, guruḥ] tu varṣaiḥ dvādaśabhiḥ kiñcit ūnaiḥ, śanaiścaraḥ tu triṃśatā varṣaiḥ kiñcit ūnaiḥ iti | evam ete bhinnakakṣyāsthāḥ yojanagatena tulyagatayaḥ grahāḥ vyākhyātāḥ |
body.translated_text: The Moon completes [it] in a short time: it completes [it] in a small, brief time. What? That small orbit situated below. Above all orbits, [<s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn)] the slow-mover completes a large orbit in a long time. These two planets — [one with] a small and [one with] a large orbital circumference — have been specified; the orbits of the others are to be understood by one's own intelligence. That is: the Moon traverses its orbit in approximately twenty-seven and a half days; <s>Budha</s> (Mercury), <s>Śukra</s> (Venus), and <s>Ravi</s> (the Sun) in slightly less than a year; <s>Bhauma</s> (Mars) in slightly less than two years; <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter) in slightly less than twelve years; and <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn) in slightly less than thirty years. Thus, these planets situated in different orbits have been explained as having equal velocity in terms of <s>yojana</s>-distance.

body.text: atha yadi tulyakakṣyāsthāḥ yojanagatena tulyagatayaḥ eva syuḥ tadā eteṣām yugādeḥ saṃpravṛttānām na kadācit viyogaḥ syāt | atha [yadi] yojanagatena ete bhinnagatayaḥ syuḥ tadā eteṣām bhuktiliptānayane yojanaiḥ yathāsvam prasiddhabhuktiliptāḥ na āgaccheyuḥ | tasmāt bhinnakakṣyāsthāḥ api grahāḥ yojanagatena tulyagatayaḥ eva iti || 13 ||
body.translated_text: Now, if they were situated in the same orbit, they would have equal velocity in terms of <s>yojana</s>-distance, and then, having commenced together at the beginning of the <s>yuga</s>, they would never separate. On the other hand, if they had different velocities in terms of <s>yojana</s>-distance, then in computing their daily motion in minutes, the well-known daily minutes would not be obtained from the <s>yojanas</s> in each respective [orbit]. Therefore, even though the planets are in different orbits, they have equal velocity in terms of <s>yojana</s>-distance. // 13 //

body.text: bhinnakakṣyāsu rāśyādīnām alpamahattvam
body.translated_text: The smallness and largeness of signs etc. in different orbits

body.text: kakṣyāṇām alpamahattvāt rāśibhāgaliptāḥ bahvyaḥ alpāḥ iti sandehaḥ tannivṛttyartham āha ã
body.translated_text: Since the orbits are small or large, there arises a doubt whether the signs, degrees, and minutes are many or few — to remove that doubt, he says:

children.text: alpe hi maṇḍale alpāḥ mahati mahāntaḥ ca rāśayaḥ jñeyāḥ |
children.translated_text: In a small orbit, the signs should be known as small; in a large [orbit], large;

children.text: aṃśāḥ kalāḥ tathā evam vibhāgatulyāḥ svakakṣyāsu || 14 ||
children.translated_text: degrees and minutes likewise — [they are] equal in division within their own orbits. // 14 //

body.text: alpe maṇḍale alpāḥ rāśayaḥ mahati maṇḍale mahāntaḥ, evam aṃśāḥ kalāḥ ca, kevalam tu vibhāgena sadṛśāḥ | tat yathā ã alpe mahati ca maṇḍale maṇḍaladvādaśabhāgaḥ rāśiḥ, ṣaṣṭiśatatrayabhāgaḥ bhāgaḥ, khakhaṣaḍghanabhāgaḥ liptāḥ iti, svāsu svāsu kakṣyāsu jyotiścakrasya tulyatvāt || 14 ||
