body.translated_text: In a small orbit the signs are small; in a large orbit, large; likewise degrees and minutes — but they are equal in division. That is: in both a small and a large orbit, a sign is one-twelfth of the orbit, a degree is one-three-hundred-sixtieth, a minute is one-[twenty-one-thousand-six-hundredth] (= 1/void-void-six-cubed). In their respective orbits, the zodiacal circle is equal [in division]. // 14 //

body.text: grahakakṣyāvasthitikramaḥ
body.translated_text: The order of arrangement of planetary orbits

body.text: kakṣyāṇām upari adhaḥ ava[sthiti]kramaparijñānāya āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of knowing the order of arrangement of orbits above and below, he says:

children.translated_text: Below the stars are <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn), <s>Suraguru</s> (Jupiter), <s>Bhauma</s> (Mars), <s>Arka</s> (Sun), <s>Śukra</s> (Venus), <s>Budha</s> (Mercury), and <s>Candra</s> (Moon);

children.text: eṣām adhaḥ ca bhūmiḥ medhībhūtā khamadhyasthā || 15 ||
children.translated_text: and below these is the Earth, having become the center, situated in the middle of space. // 15 //

body.text:
bhāni jyotīṃṣi, aśvinyādīni | teṣām adhaḥ śanaiścaraḥ, tasya api adhaḥ bṛhaspatiḥ, tataḥ aṅgārakaḥ iti ādi | eṣām adhaḥ ca bhūmiḥ | eṣām nakṣatrādīnām bhūḥ adhaḥ | medhībhūtā | atra "bhūta"-śabdaḥ bahuṣu artheṣu vartamānaḥ iva arthe pratipattavyaḥ | medhī iva sthitā | khamadhyasthā | kham ākāśam tasya madhyam khamadhyam, tasmin sthitā khamadhyasthā | eṣām adhaḥ ca bhūmiḥ iti | atra ucyate ã yadā dṛśye
cakrārdhe grahanakṣatrāṇi, tadā teṣām adhaḥ bhūmiḥ | yadā ataḥ anyeṣu grahanakṣatrāṇi smararipusutahibukasahajadhaneṣu vartante tadā katham adhaḥ bhūḥ, yat uta upari syāt | na evam vijñāyate | yasmāt sarveṣām asmadādīnām bhūḥ adhaḥ, upari ca ākāśaḥ, [tasmāt] sarvadā grahāḥ upari, bhūḥ adhaḥ | vakṣyati ca ã
body.translated_text: The <s>bhāni</s> (luminaries) are the stars, beginning with <s>Aśvinī</s> and others. Below them is <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn), below that too is <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter), then <s>Aṅgāraka</s> (Mars), and so on. And below these is the Earth. Below these <s>nakṣatras</s> and others is the Earth. [It is] like a pillar (<s>medhī</s>). Here the word '<s>bhūta</s>' (become), though occurring in many senses, should be understood in the sense of 'like.' Situated like a pillar. Situated in the middle of space (<s>khamadhyasthā</s>). <s>Kha</s> means space (<s>ākāśa</s>); the middle of that is <s>khamadhya</s>; situated in that is <s>khamadhyasthā</s>. 'And below these is the Earth' — here it is said: when the planets and <s>nakṣatras</s> are in the visible half of the circle, then the Earth is below them. But when the planets and <s>nakṣatras</s> are in the other [houses] — the seventh, sixth, fifth, fourth, third, and second — then how is the Earth below, since it would be above? It should not be understood thus. Because for all of us and others, the Earth is below and the sky above, [therefore] the planets are always above and the Earth below. And he will state:

body.text:
yadvat kadambapuṣpagranthaḥ pracitaḥ samantataḥ kusumaiḥ |
 tadvat hi sarvasattvaiḥ jalajaiḥ sthalajaiḥ ca bhūgolaḥ || iti |
[golaí, 7]
body.translated_text: Just as a <s>Kadamba</s> flower-cluster is studded all around with blossoms, so indeed is the Earth-globe (<s>bhūgola</s>) [covered] with all creatures, aquatic and terrestrial. [<s>Gola</s>, 7]

body.text: anye tu imām kalpanām
body.translated_text: Others, however, consider this conception

body.text:
dūravipratipannām, bhagaṇaśanaiḥcarabṛhaspatikujaravisitabudhaniśākarān uparyuparivyavasthitān tulya[gatikān manyante | tat yathā ã yā]vat alpamaṇḍalam bhāni bhramanti, tāvat mahānti maṇḍalāni śanaiścarādayaḥ [na] śaknuvanti pūrayitum iti pṛṣṭhataḥ lakṣyante, yathākakṣyā[maṇḍalakrameṇa] iti | atra parihāraḥ prāk pradarśitaḥ ã yadi upari syāt tadā candrasya grahanakṣatrabhede sphuṭakalaṅkahariṇe grahanakṣatratārāḥ
kṛśyeran [pṛí 212] iti ādinā granthena |
body.translated_text: far-fetched, and hold that the stellar sphere, <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn), <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter), <s>Kuja</s> (Mars), <s>Ravi</s> (Sun), <s>Sita</s> (Venus), <s>Budha</s> (Mercury), and <s>Niśākara</s> (Moon) are situated one above the other with equal velocities. That is to say: as far as the stars revolve in small orbits, the larger orbits of <s>Śanaiścara</s> and the others [cannot] be completed, so they are observed to lag behind, in the order of their orbital circles. The refutation of this has been demonstrated previously: if [the Moon] were above, then when the Moon occults planets and <s>nakṣatras</s>, the planets and stars of <s>nakṣatras</s> would be obscured by [the Moon's] clear spots and deer-marks — by that passage and so forth.

body.text:
anye manyante ã tulyakakṣyāsthāḥ eva bhagaṇaśanaiścarabṛhaspatikujaravisitabudhaniśākarāḥ | kintu yathākrameṇa śīghragatayaḥ | ataḥ drutagatibhiḥ nakṣatraiḥ īṣamandagatiḥ īṣat jīyate, atimandagatiḥ tu dūrāt iti | īṣanmandagatitvāt śanaiścaraḥ iṣat jīyate, atimandagatitvāt candramāḥ [dū]ram iti | atra api yadi prāṅmukhāḥ grahādayaḥ tadā prāṅmukhaiḥ drutagatibhiḥ nakṣatraiḥ jīyamānaḥ aśvinyām dṛṣṭaḥ revatyām upalakṣyeta, na bharaṇyām | vakrakāle
api ca, pratilomagatitvāt aśvinyām dṛṣṭaḥ bharaṇyām eva upalakṣyeta | atha ete grahādayaḥ aparābhimukhāḥ kalpyante, tathā api vakrakāle aśvinyām dṛṣṭaḥ pratilomagatitvāt bharaṇyām upalakṣyeta | tulyakakṣyāvyavasthitānām ca lambanaviśeṣaḥ na syāt | anyat ca ã anyonyabimbacchādanam na syāt | grahoparāgaḥ api ca tulyakakṣyāvyavasthitatvāt na yujyate | tasmāt "bhānām adhaḥ śanaiścaraḥ" iti ādi suṣṭhu uktam || 15 ||
body.translated_text: Others hold: the stellar sphere, <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn), <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter), <s>Kuja</s> (Mars), <s>Ravi</s> (Sun), <s>Sita</s> (Venus), <s>Budha</s> (Mercury), and <s>Niśākara</s> (Moon) are situated in the same orbit. But they have progressively faster speeds in order. Therefore, by the fast-moving <s>nakṣatras</s>, a slightly slow one is slightly overtaken, and an extremely slow one [is overtaken] by far. Due to being slightly slow, <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn) is slightly overtaken; due to being extremely slow, the Moon [is overtaken] by far. Here too, if the planets and others move eastward, then being overtaken by the fast-moving eastward <s>nakṣatras</s>, [a planet] seen in <s>Aśvinī</s> would be observed in <s>Revatī</s>, not in <s>Bharaṇī</s>. And also during retrograde motion, due to moving in the opposite direction, [a planet] seen in <s>Aśvinī</s> would be observed in <s>Bharaṇī</s> itself. Now, if these planets and others are supposed to move westward, even then, during retrograde motion, [a planet] seen in <s>Aśvinī</s> would be observed in <s>Bharaṇī</s> due to backward motion. And for those situated in the same orbit, there would be no difference in parallax (<s>lambana</s>). Moreover, there would be no mutual occultation of discs. And eclipses of planets too would not be possible due to being situated in the same orbit. Therefore, 'Below the stars is <s>Śanaiścara</s>' and so forth is well stated. || 15 ||

body.text: kālahorādinādhipatijñānam
body.translated_text: Knowledge of the lords of the <s>kālahorā</s> (planetary hour) and the day

body.text: kālahorādinādhipatijñāpanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of explaining the lords of the <s>kālahorā</s> (planetary hour) and the day, he says:

children.text: sapta ete horeśāḥ śanaiścarādyāḥ yathākramam śīghrāḥ |
children.translated_text: These seven, beginning with <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn), are the lords of the <s>horā</s> (planetary hours), progressively faster in order;
The fourth from the fast sequence become the lords of the day (<s>dinapā</s>) from sunrise. || 16 ||

body.text:
ete grahāḥ śanaiścarādayaḥ tulyagatayaḥ api santaḥ yathākrameṇa śīghrāḥ lakṣyante, maṇḍalānām yathākrameṇa alpatvāt | te eva horeśāḥ yathākrameṇa | tat yathā ã śanaiścarasya kālahorāyām nivṛttāyām bṛhaspateḥ kālahorā, tataḥ aṅgārakasya, tataḥ raveḥ iti ādi | evam sūryodayāt prabhṛti yāvat sūryasya ardhāstamayaḥ iti dvādaśa kālahorāḥ | tataḥ ca ardhāstamayāt ardhodayaḥ iti punar dvādaśa | evam ahorātre caturviṃśatikālahorāḥ | kālahorā hi nāma lagnarāśeḥ
ardhodayasya kālaḥ | sā ca divase divase divasādhipātaḥ prabhṛti pratipattavyā | uktam ca sphujidhvajayavaneśvareṇa ã
body.translated_text: These planets, beginning with <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn), though of equal [orbital] speeds, are observed as progressively faster in order, due to the progressive smallness of their orbits. They themselves are the <s>horā</s>-lords (planetary hour lords) in order. That is: when the <s>kālahorā</s> of <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn) is completed, the <s>kālahorā</s> of <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter) [follows], then that of <s>Aṅgāraka</s> (Mars), then of <s>Ravi</s> (Sun), and so forth. Thus, from sunrise until the half-setting of the Sun, there are twelve <s>kālahorās</s>. Then from the half-setting to the half-rising, there are again twelve. Thus in a day-and-night there are twenty-four <s>kālahorās</s>. A <s>kālahorā</s> is indeed the time of the half-rising of the ascendant sign (<s>lagnarāśi</s>). And that is to be reckoned each day starting from the lord of the day. And it has been stated by <s>Sphujidhvaja</s>, the lord of the <s>Yavanas</s>:

children.translated_text: <s>Āditya</s> (Sun), <s>Śukra</s> (Venus), <s>Indu</s> (Moon), <s>Ja</s> (Mercury-born), <s>Candra</s> (Moon's son, i.e., <s>Budha</s>), <s>Saura</s> (Saturn), <s>Jīva</s> (Jupiter), and <s>Avaneya</s> (Mars) are [the lords] during day and night;

children.text: horeśvarāḥ taddivasādhipādikrameṇa tāḥ tatra caturguṇāḥ ṣaṭ ||
children.translated_text: They are the lords of the <s>horās</s>, in the order beginning with the lord of that day, [and] those [horās] are six multiplied by four.

body.text:
evam divasādhipāt sūryodayāt gaṇyamānāt uttaradivasasya adhipāt eva ardhodayāt śīghrakramāt caturthaḥ, yaḥ śīghrakramaḥ abhihitaḥ "bhānām adhaḥ śanaiścaraḥ" iti ādi tasmāt caturthaḥ divasādhipatiḥ | tat yathā ã śanaiścarāt caturthaḥ sūryaḥ divasādhipatiḥ, sūryāt somaḥ caturthaḥ, somāt aṅgārakaḥ iti ādi | evam anena krameṇa māsādhipāḥ abdādhipāḥ ca avagantavyāḥ | katham? [māsasya varṣasya ca yaḥ] prathamadivase adhipaḥ sa māsādhipaḥ varṣādhipaḥ ca
| sūryodayāt dinapāḥ | sūryasya udayaḥ sūryodayaḥ | yadi api śeṣeṇa uktaḥ sūryodayaśeṣeṇa ardhodayaḥ pratipattavyaḥ | kutaḥ? idam bimbāvayavābhidhāne api tadavayavapramāṇasya mānakālāvadhāraṇāśakyatvāt ardhodayasya ca vyaktalakṣaṇatvāt suparicchedanayā ardhodayaḥ āśriyate | athavā anirdiṣṭeṣu vastuṣu madhyamapratipatteḥ ardhodayāt ārabhya punar ardhodayaḥ iti |
body.translated_text: Thus, the lord of the next day from the day-lord counted from sunrise is the fourth in the fast sequence from the half-rising — from that fast sequence which has been stated as 'Below the stars is <s>Śanaiścara</s>' and so forth, the fourth is the day-lord. That is: the fourth from <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn) is <s>Sūrya</s> (Sun) as day-lord; from <s>Sūrya</s>, the fourth is <s>Soma</s> (Moon); from <s>Soma</s>, <s>Aṅgāraka</s> (Mars), and so forth. In this way, by this sequence, the month-lords and year-lords are also to be understood. How? Whoever is the lord on the first day [of a month or year], that one is the month-lord and year-lord. 'The day-lords from sunrise' — the rising of the Sun is sunrise. Even though stated by the remainder — by the remainder of sunrise, the half-rising is to be understood. Why? Because in the specification of parts of the [solar] disc, since the measure-time of that part-measure cannot be ascertained, and since the half-rising has a clear definition, the half-rising is adopted for ease of determination. Alternatively, in matters not [precisely] specified, [one takes] the middle interpretation — from the half-rising until the next half-rising.

body.text: atra kecit ardhāstamayāt vārapravṛttim manyante | tat ca ayuktam | yasmāt uktam ã
body.translated_text: Here, some hold that the weekday (<s>vāra</s>) commences from the half-setting. And that is incorrect. Because it is stated:

children.translated_text: This [universe] was enveloped in darkness, unknown, without characteristics,
beyond reasoning, unknowable, as if completely asleep.

body.text: manusmṛtiḥ, 1.5
body.translated_text: <s>Manusmṛti</s>, 1.5

body.text: atra janapadajyotiścakrābhāvāt na vārādivyavahāraḥ sañjātaḥ | yadā protpannaḥ sahasrakiraṇaḥ tadā prabhṛti vārādivyavahāraḥ sañjātaḥ iti | ataḥ suṣṭhu uktam sūryodayāt dinapāḥ iti || 16 ||
body.translated_text: Here, due to the absence of [organized] settlements and the stellar circle, the convention of weekdays and such did not arise. When the thousand-rayed one (the Sun) arose, from that time onward the convention of weekdays and such came into being. Therefore, 'the day-lords from sunrise' is well stated. || 16 ||

body.text: pratimaṇḍalavidhinā grahagatinirūpaṇam
body.translated_text: Determination of planetary motion by the method of the <s>pratimaṇḍala</s> (eccentric circle)

body.text: ete grahāḥ kasmin maṇḍale bhramanti iti [na jñāyate] ataḥ tannirūpaṇāya āha ã
body.translated_text: In which circle do these planets revolve — [this is not known,] therefore, for the purpose of determining that, he says:

children.translated_text: All planets revolve in [both] the orbital circle (<s>kakṣyā</s>) and the eccentric circle (<s>pratimaṇḍala</s>), by their own motion;

children.text: mandoccāt anulomam pratilomam ca eva śīghhroccāt || 17 ||
children.translated_text: In the direct direction from the <s>mandocca</s> (apogee of the slow epicycle), and in the reverse direction from the <s>śīghrocca</s> (apogee of the fast epicycle). || 17 ||

body.text:
kakṣyāyāḥ pratimaṇḍalam kakṣyāpratimaṇḍalam, tat gacchanti iti kakṣyāpratimaṇḍalagāḥ | athavā kakṣyā ca pratimaṇḍalam ca kakṣyāpratimaṇḍale, te gacchanti iti kakṣyāpratimaṇḍalagāḥ | atra kakṣyāgāḥ madhyamāḥ grahāḥ, sphuṭāḥ [prati]maṇḍalagāḥ | athavā kakṣyāpratimaṇḍalayoḥ yatra sampātaḥ sa kakṣyāpratimaṇḍalaśabdena ucyate | tam gacchanti iti kakṣyāpratimaṇḍalagāḥ | atra anekatvāt vigrahayogasya, katamaḥ vigrahaḥ parigṛhyate iti sandehe
ucyate ã kakṣyā ca pratimaṇḍalam ca kakṣyāpratimaṇḍale | te gacchanti iti kakṣyāpratimaṇḍalagāḥ, iti ayam parigṛhyate | katham? iṣṭatvāt śeṣavigrahārthavācakatvāt ca atra iṣyate | kakṣyāgāḥ madhyamāḥ grahāḥ yasmāt tulyabhuktayaḥ, pratimaṇḍalagāḥ sphuṭagrahāḥ yataḥ sasadṛśabhuktayaḥ |
body.translated_text: The eccentric circle of the orbital circle is <s>kakṣyāpratimaṇḍala</s>; those that move in it are <s>kakṣyāpratimaṇḍalagāḥ</s> (movers in the orbital-eccentric). Alternatively, the orbital circle and the eccentric circle together are <s>kakṣyāpratimaṇḍale</s>; those that move in them are <s>kakṣyāpratimaṇḍalagāḥ</s>. Here, the movers in the orbital circle are the mean (<s>madhyama</s>) planets, and the true (<s>sphuṭa</s>) [planets] move in the eccentric circle. Alternatively, the point where the orbital circle and the eccentric circle intersect is denoted by the word <s>kakṣyāpratimaṇḍala</s>; those that move to that [point] are <s>kakṣyāpratimaṇḍalagāḥ</s>. Here, since there are multiple possibilities for the compound analysis, when there is doubt as to which analysis is adopted, it is said: the orbital circle and the eccentric circle are <s>kakṣyāpratimaṇḍale</s>; those that move in them are <s>kakṣyāpratimaṇḍalagāḥ</s> — this [analysis] is adopted. How? Because it is desired and because it expresses the meanings of the remaining compound analyses as well. The mean (<s>madhyama</s>) planets move in the orbital circle since they have uniform motion; the true (<s>sphuṭa</s>) planets move in the eccentric circle since they have variable motion.

body.text:
atha ke te madhyamāḥ, ke vā sphuṭāḥ grahāḥ? nanu ca ekaḥ eva sūryaḥ, ekaḥ eva candramāḥ, ekaḥ eva aṅgārakaḥ iti ādi | madhyamasphuṭatāyām parigṛhyamāṇāyām grahadvayam prāpnoti | na evam vijñāyate madhyamaḥ grahaḥ sphuṭaḥ grahaḥ iti | katham tarhi? madhyamagrahaśabdena madhyamagrahasya grahagatiḥ abhidhīyate, sphuṭagrahaśabdena ca sphuṭagrahagatiḥ iti? tat yathā ã kaścit sāṃvatsaram pṛcchati ã "kaḥ savitā" iti, sa tasmā āha ã rāśiḥ
ekaḥ pañcadaśa bhāgāḥ triṃśat liptāḥ iti | tatra yaḥ paripṛcchati yaḥ ca ācaṣṭe tayoḥ ubhayoḥ abhi[prāya]dvayaprasaṅgaḥ | na eṣa doṣaḥ | yā madhyamā gatiḥ sā sphuṭagatisādhanasya upāyaḥ | anyathā aniyatatvāt sphuṭagatiḥ aśakyā syāt vijñātum | evam eva ca [madhyamagrahaḥ] pratimaṇḍalaparijñānārtham parikalpitaḥ | yat asya grahasya vyāsārdhatulyam bhūtārāgrahavivaram sa tasmāt pradeśāt prabhṛti kakṣyāmaṇḍalasya upari adhaḥ vā avatiṣṭhate |
body.translated_text: Now, which are those mean [planets] and which are the true planets? Is it not that there is only one <s>Sūrya</s> (Sun), only one <s>Candramā</s> (Moon), only one <s>Aṅgāraka</s> (Mars), and so forth? When the distinction of mean and true is adopted, a duality of planets would result. It should not be understood thus — [as if there were] a mean planet [and] a true planet [as separate entities]. How then? By the term 'mean planet,' the planetary motion of the mean planet is denoted; and by the term 'true planet,' the true planetary motion [is denoted]. Just as: someone asks an astronomer (<s>sāṃvatsara</s>), 'What is the Sun (<s>savitā</s>)?' — he replies: 'one sign, fifteen degrees, thirty minutes.' There, for both the questioner and the respondent, the implication of both [positions, not two suns,] is relevant. There is no fault here. The mean motion is the means for establishing the true motion. Otherwise, due to its irregularity, the true motion would be impossible to know. And in just this way, the [mean planet] is postulated for the purpose of understanding the eccentric circle. When the distance between the center of the Earth and the planet equals the semi-diameter (<s>vyāsārdha</s>), from that point onward [the planet] stands above or below the orbital circle.

body.text:
atha kaḥ asau ayam pradeśaḥ? ucyate ã yadā tṛtīye karmaṇi dvitīye pade mandoccakendram rāśitrayam dvau bhāgau pañcāśat liptāḥ, tadā bṛhaspateḥ mandoccakarṇaḥ vyāsārdhatulyaḥ | caturthe karmaṇi yadā śīghroccakendram rāśitrayam pañcabhāgāḥ viṃśatiḥ ca kalā, tadā vyāsārdhatulyaḥ śīghroccakarṇaḥ | atra vyāsārdhatulyam bhūtārāgrahavivaram | asmāt pradeśāt prabhṛti bhūtārāgrahavivaram pratidinam apacīyate | anayā yuktyā śeṣāṇām api grahāṇām
vyāsārdhatulyam bhūtārāgrahavivaram ūhyam |
body.translated_text: Now, what is that point? It is said: when, in the third operation, in the second quadrant, the <s>mandocca-kendra</s> (anomaly of the slow apogee) is three signs, two degrees, and fifty minutes, then the <s>manda-karṇa</s> (hypotenuse of the slow epicycle) of <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter) equals the semi-diameter (<s>vyāsārdha</s>). In the fourth operation, when the <s>śīghrocca-kendra</s> (anomaly of the fast apogee) is three signs, five degrees, and twenty minutes, then the <s>śīghrocca-karṇa</s> (hypotenuse of the fast epicycle) equals the semi-diameter. At this point, the distance between the center of the Earth and the planet equals the semi-diameter. From this point onward, the distance between the center of the Earth and the planet diminishes daily. By this reasoning, the distance equal to the semi-diameter between the center of the Earth and the planet for the remaining planets too should be inferred.

body.text:
bhramanti sarve grahāḥ svacāreṇa iti etat nigadavyākhyānam eva | mandoccāt anulomam | "mandoccāt" iti hetau pañcamī | tena mandoccāt hetoḥ anulomam iti vyākhyāyate, yasmāt na mandocce vakraparijñānam | pratilomam ca eva śīghroccāt | śīghroccāt hetoḥ pratilomam, yasmāt śīghrocce vakraparijñānam | katham punar śīghrocce vakraparijñānam? ucyate ã yadā śīghroccakendram dvitīyapade tadā sarve grahāḥ vakriṇaḥ bhavanti, yadā ca tṛtīyapade śīghroccakendram
tadā anuvakragatayaḥ | uktam ca ã
body.translated_text: That 'all planets revolve by their own motion' — this is a <s>nigada</s> (word-for-word) commentary itself. 'In the direct direction from the <s>mandocca</s> (slow apogee)' — '<s>mandoccāt</s>' is an ablative of cause. Thus it is explained: due to the <s>mandocca</s> as cause, [the motion is] direct, since retrograde motion is not determined at the <s>mandocca</s>. 'And in the reverse direction from the <s>śīghrocca</s> (fast apogee)' — due to the <s>śīghrocca</s> as cause, [the motion is] retrograde, since retrograde motion is determined at the <s>śīghrocca</s>. But how is retrograde motion determined at the <s>śīghrocca</s>? It is said: when the <s>śīghrocca-kendra</s> (fast anomaly) is in the second quadrant, then all planets become retrograde; and when the <s>śīghrocca-kendra</s> is in the third quadrant, then they have post-retrograde motion (<s>anuvakra</s>). And it has been stated:

children.translated_text: When the <s>śīghra</s> (fast) [anomaly] minus the planet [falls] in the six and eight [ranges], in order,

children.text: bhavet vakrātivakrā ca tathā anukuṭilā gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: there occurs retrograde, extreme retrograde, and likewise curved (<s>anukuliṭā</s>) motion.

body.text: iti | sūkṣmataraḥ [ca ayam] vidhiḥ iti | ucyate ã yadā adyatanāt grahāt śvastanaḥ grahaḥ tulyaḥ bhavati tadā vakraprārambhaḥ | athavā hyastanāt grahāt adyatanaḥ grahaḥ tulyaḥ tadā api vakraprārambhaḥ | yadā adyatanāt tṛtīyapade śvastanaḥ grahaḥ adhikaḥ tadā vakrasya nivṛttiḥ | athavā hyastanāt grahāt adyatanaḥ grahaḥ adhikaḥ tṛtīyapade tadā api vakrasya nivṛttiḥ | yadā grahaḥ bahvīḥ liptāḥ nivartate tadā ativakragatiḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus. And this is a more precise rule. It is said: when tomorrow's planet equals today's planet, then is the commencement of retrograde motion. Alternatively, when today's planet equals yesterday's planet, then too is the commencement of retrograde motion. When tomorrow's planet in the third quadrant exceeds today's planet, then is the cessation of retrograde motion. Alternatively, when today's planet exceeds yesterday's planet in the third quadrant, then too is the cessation of retrograde motion. When the planet retrogresses by many minutes, then that is extreme retrograde motion (<s>ativakragati</s>).

body.text:
katham punar idam vidhānam śīghroccāt eva gaṇakaḥ prajānate, na punar mandoccāt iti? ucyate ã yasmāt sūryavaśāt grahāṇām udayāstamayavakrānuvakrāḥ gatayaḥ | yadi evam atra katham budhaśukrayoḥ anyat śīghroccam, [madhyaḥ] sūryaḥ | atra api sūryavaśāt eva tayoḥ udayāstamayaparijñānam | vakragatiḥ tu ekatvāt upāyāntareṇa vijñāyate | athavā uccanīcamadhyamaparidhiḥ iti evamādisphuṭagatisādhanopāya[bhūtānām ca] upāyānām na [eva niyamo]ktiḥ
vā vidyate | kevalam tu upeyasādhakāḥ upāyāḥ | tasmāt iyam sarvā prakriyā asatyā, yayā grahāṇām sphuṭagatiḥ sādhyate | [evam ca paramārthajijñāsubhiḥ asatyopāye]na satyam pratipadyate | tathā hi bhiṣajaḥ hi utpalanālādiṣu vadhādīni abhyasyante | nāpitāḥ piṭharādiṣu muṇḍanādīni, yajñaśāstravidaḥ śu[ṣkeṣṭyā] yajñādīni, śābdikāḥ prakṛtipratyayavikārāgamavarṇalopavyatyayādibhiḥ śabdān pratijānate | evam atra api
madhyamamandoccaśīghroccatatparidhijyākāṣṭhabhujākoṭikarṇādi-vyavahāreṇa sāṃvatsarāḥ grahāṇām sphuṭagatim pratijānate | tasmāt upāyeṣu asatyeṣu satyapratipādanapareṣu na codyam asti |
body.translated_text: But how does the mathematician know this procedure from the fast apogee (<s>śīghrocca</s>) alone and not from the slow apogee (<s>mandocca</s>)? It is said: because the rising, setting, retrograde, and re-direct motions of the planets are subject to the Sun. If so, then why do Mercury and Venus have a different fast apogee [while their] mean [position] is the Sun? In their case too, the knowledge of rising and setting is from the Sun alone. But the retrograde motion, being singular, is known by another means. Or rather, of the procedures that are means for deriving the true motion — such as the apogee, the perigee, the mean-epicycle circumference, and so forth — there is no fixed authoritative statement. They are merely means that accomplish the goal. Therefore, this entire procedure is unreal (<s>asatya</s>), by which the true motion of the planets is derived. And thus, those who seek the ultimate truth reach the truth by means of an unreal procedure. For physicians practice cutting and the like on lotus-stalks and such; barbers [practice] shaving and the like on pots; those versed in sacrificial science [practice] sacrifices through mock-sacrifices (<s>śuṣkeṣṭi</s>); grammarians assert words through [the operations of] base, suffix, modification, augment, elision, transposition, and the like. Similarly here too, astronomers assert the true motion of planets through the operations of mean [position], slow apogee, fast apogee, their epicycle circumferences, sines, arcs, <s>bhujā</s> (base), <s>koṭi</s> (perpendicular), hypotenuse, and so forth. Therefore, there is no objection to [the use of] unreal means that serve to demonstrate the truth.

body.text: atha kim artham ime grahāḥ pratidinam bhrāmyanti | atha ca loke kaścit bhraman kāraṇena bhramati | anyat ca ã na evaṃvidhaḥ kaścit dṛśyate anavaratagatiḥ yathā ime tārāgrahāḥ bhramanti iti dṛṣṭāntatvena udāharaṇabhūtaḥ iti | ucyate ã sarvādau kila bhagavān prajāpatiḥ grahān uktavān yat "bhavantaḥ meṣādigaṇeṣu prajānām śubhāśubhaphalāya bhrāmyata" iti | uktam ca sphujidhvajayavaneśvareṇa ã

children.translated_text: Desiring to create beings, the creator of the universe,
<s>Prajāpati</s>, first undertook a vow.
Having created his own body, originating from the twelve limbs [= the twelve signs],
he first brought forth the stellar sphere (<s>bhagaṇa</s>).

body.translated_text: Now, for what purpose do these planets revolve every day? Moreover, in the world, whoever revolves, revolves for a reason. And another [point]: no one of this kind — one who has unceasing motion like these stellar planets — is seen that could serve as an example or illustration. It is said: In the very beginning, the blessed <s>Prajāpati</s> told the planets: 'You shall revolve in the groups beginning with <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries) for the auspicious and inauspicious results of beings.' And it was stated by <s>Sphujidhvaja</s>, the <s>Yavana</s> lord:

body.text:
tebhyaḥ sa meṣādigaṇān prajajñe
tebhyaḥ ca tadbhedavikalpataḥ anyān |
ataḥ bhavargasya vibhuḥ praṇetā
prajābhavābhāvavidhīśvaratvam || iti ādi |
body.translated_text: From those he generated the groups beginning with <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries), and from those, others through division and subdivision. Hence, the lord who is the creator of the stellar group [holds] sovereignty over the existence and non-existence of beings. — And so forth.

body.text:
athavā śabdena arthānumānam kriyate | śrūyante ca śabdāḥ ye ca apare atra gativācakāḥ | tat yathā ã "pathaḥ ṣkan" [aṣṭādhyāyī, 5.1.75] iti vartamāne "panthaḥ ṇa nityam" [aṣṭādhyāyī, 5.1.76] iti anena nityam panthānam gacchati iti asmin arthe pānthaḥ iti ayam śabdaḥ | atra loke na kaścit adhvānam anavaratam gacchan dṛśyate, tasmāt amī eva grahāḥ pānthāḥ | na ca ayam śabdaḥ asatsvārtheṣu śaśaviṣāṇakūrmaromavandhyāputraśabdavat pravṛttaḥ | tasmāt
suṣṭhu ucyate śabdena arthānumānam pānthāḥ grahāḥ iti |
body.translated_text: Alternatively, from a word one infers the meaning. And the words that express motion are heard here. Namely: From [<s>Pāṇini</s>'s rule] '<s>pathaḥ ṣkan</s>' [<s>Aṣṭādhyāyī</s> 5.1.75] in the present [tense], by [the rule] '<s>panthāḥ ṇa nityam</s>' [<s>Aṣṭādhyāyī</s> 5.1.76], the word '<s>pāntha</s>' (traveler) is formed in the meaning 'one who perpetually traverses a road.' Now, in the world, no one is seen who traverses a road without cessation; therefore, these very planets are the 'travelers' (<s>pāntha</s>). And this word is not employed for non-existent referents, like the words 'hare's horn,' 'tortoise-hair,' or 'barren woman's son.' Therefore, it is well said that by the word, the meaning is inferred: the planets are travelers.

body.text: athavā ayam aparaḥ prakāraḥ | mandoccāt anulomam pratilomam ca eva śīghroccāt | mandoccāt yataḥ mandoccakendrāt pratimaṇḍalavidhānena ānītam phalam pratyaham upacīyate | kva? anyasya aśrutatvāt mandocce eva | tasmāt mandoccāt anulomam | pratilomam ca eva śīghroccāt | yasmāt pratimaṇḍalavidhānena ānītam phalam sarvadā apacīyate | kutaḥ? anyasya aśṛutatvāt śīghroccāt eva | tasmāt "pratilomam ca eva śīghroccāt" iti || 17 ||
body.translated_text: Or, here is another mode [of explanation]. From the slow apogee (<s>mandocca</s>), [the motion is] direct; from the fast apogee (<s>śīghrocca</s>), [it is] precisely retrograde. From the slow apogee — since the result derived by the eccentric-circle (<s>pratimaṇḍala</s>) method from the slow-apogee anomaly increases daily. Where? Since nothing else is heard [as the reference], in the slow apogee itself. Therefore, from the slow apogee, [the motion is] direct. And precisely retrograde from the fast apogee — since the result derived by the eccentric-circle method always decreases. From where? Since nothing else is heard, from the fast apogee itself. Therefore, 'precisely retrograde from the fast apogee.' // 17 //

body.text: pratimaṇḍalavidhānam
body.translated_text: The eccentric-circle method

body.text: sphuṭāḥ pratimaṇḍale bhramanti iti uktam, ataḥ tajjñāpanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: It has been stated that [the planets] revolve with true motion on the eccentric circle (<s>pratimaṇḍala</s>); hence, to explain that, he says:

children.text: kakṣyāmaṇḍalatulyam svam svam pratimaṇḍalam bhavati eṣām |
children.translated_text: Each planet's own eccentric circle is equal to the orbit-circle (<s>kakṣyāmaṇḍala</s>);
the center of the eccentric circle is displaced from the center of the solid Earth. // 18 //

body.text:
kakṣyāmaṇḍalatulyam | kakṣyāmaṇḍalena tulyam kakṣyāmaṇḍalatulyam | kakṣyāmaṇḍalapramāṇam "śaśirāśayaṣṭha cakram" [gītikāí, 6] iti etasmin sūtre vyākhyātam | svam svam pratimaṇḍalam ātmīyam ātmīyam pratimaṇḍalam, bhavati | eṣām grahāṇām | pratimaṇḍalasya madhyam | yat madhyam kendram tat ghanabhūmadhyāt atikrāntam | ghanāḥ ca asau bhūḥ ca ghanabhūḥ, tasyāḥ ghanabhuvaḥ madhyam ghanabhūmadhyam, tasmāt ghanabhūmadhyāt,
atikrāntam nirgatam uparisthitam iti arthaḥ | tat yathā ã yāvat pramāṇaparikalpitam ṣaṣṭiśatatrayāṃśāvacchinnam kakṣyāmaṇḍalam pūrvāparam ūrdhvam vinyasya, tādṛś eva anyat maṇḍalam upari adhaḥ kakṣyāmaṇḍalāt vakṣyamāṇena antareṇa pūrvāparayoḥ diśoḥ yatra sampātaḥ tatra yat badhyate gole tatpratimaṇḍalam nāma | evam ete kakṣyāpratimaṇḍale vyākhyāte || 18 ||
body.translated_text: 'Equal to the orbit-circle' — equal in size to the orbit-circle. The measure of the orbit-circle was explained in the <s>sūtra</s> 'moon-sign-sixth is the circle' [<s>Gītikā</s> 6]. 'Each planet's own eccentric circle' — each planet's own eccentric circle exists. 'Of these' — of these planets. 'The center of the eccentric circle' — that center, [its] kernel, is displaced from the center of the solid Earth. 'Solid' and 'Earth' together make 'solid-Earth' (<s>ghanabhū</s>); the middle of that solid Earth is '<s>ghanabhūmadhya</s>'; from that center of the solid Earth, 'displaced' — meaning: gone beyond, situated above. Namely: Having set down the orbit-circle, delimited into three-hundred-sixty degrees of a specified measure, extending east-west and upward, another circle of the same kind, [displaced] above and below from the orbit-circle by the interval to be stated, where the two meet at the eastern and western directions — where it is bound on the sphere, that is called the eccentric circle (<s>pratimaṇḍala</s>). Thus these two — the orbit-circle and the eccentric circle — have been explained. // 18 //

body.text: nīcoccavṛttividhinā grahagatipratipādanam
body.translated_text: Demonstration of planetary motion by the apogee-perigee epicycle method

body.text: kakṣyāpratimaṇḍalāntarapratipādanārtham āha ã
body.translated_text: In order to teach the interval between the orbit-circle and the eccentric circle, he says:

children.translated_text: The distance between the eccentric circle and the Earth is the semi-diameter of the planet's own apogee-perigee epicycle (<s>uccanīcavṛtta</s>);

children.text: vṛttaparidhau grahāḥ te madhyamacārāt bhramanti evam || 19 ||
children.translated_text: on the circumference of the [orbit-]circle, those planets revolve — thus, by mean motion. // 19 //

body.text:
pratimaṇḍalasya bhūmaṇḍalasya ca vivaram pratimaṇḍalabhūvivaram | vyāsārdham svoccanīcavṛttasya | uccavṛttam nīcavṛttam ca uccanīcavṛttam, svasya uccanīcavṛttam svoccanīcavṛttam, tasya svoccanīcavṛttasya vyāsārdham pratimaṇḍalabhūvivaram | tat yathā ã "jhārdhāni mandavṛttam" iti adhikṛtya "śaśinaḥ cha" [gītikāí, 10] iti sapta śaśinaḥ jhārdhāni uccanīccavṛttam, sārdhaikatriṃśadbhāgapramāṇam iti arthaḥ | yasya yat vyāsārdham tat trairāśikagaṇitena
siddham | yadi "caturadhikam śatam aṣṭaguṇam" [gaṇitaí, 10] iti evamādeḥ paridheḥ ayutatulyam vyāsārdham labhyate tadā sārdhaikatriṃśadbhāgapramāṇasya paridheḥ kim iti labdham bhāgāḥ pañca, liptā ca ardhādhikena ekā | sūryasya api trīṇi jhārdhāni mandavṛttam, sārdhatrayodaśabhāgapramāṇam, tasya ca trairāśikena svavṛttaviṣkambhārdham labdham bhāgadvayam, ardhādhikena nava liptāḥ | athavā ã yadi ṣaṣṭiśatatraya[bhāgamita]paridheḥ [vasutrikṛtavahniliptāmitam]
vyāsārdham labhyate tadā uccanīcaparidheḥ kim iti labdham candrasya uccanīcavyāsārdham liptātriśatī sārdhādhikarūpā | evam sūryasya api śatam ekonatriṃśaduttaram [sārdham] | tatra bhāgapramāṇena liptāpramāṇena vā kakṣyāpratimaṇḍalamadhyāntaram parikalpyam | evam sūryācandramasoḥ | anyathā anyeṣām samaviṣamavṛttamandoccaśīghroccabhedena anekapratimaṇḍalaprasaṅgabhayāt uttaratra vakṣyati ã "bhūtārāgrahavivaram" [kālakriyāí, 25] iti | vṛttaparidhiḥ
kakṣyāmaṇḍalam, tasmin vṛttaparidhau madhyamacāram grahāḥ bhramanti | pratimaṇḍaleṣu sphuṭacāram bhramanti iti arthāt avasīyate || 19 ||
body.translated_text: The distance between the eccentric circle and the Earth-circle is '<s>pratimaṇḍalabhūvivara</s>.' [This equals] the semi-diameter of the planet's own apogee-perigee epicycle. The apogee-circle and perigee-circle [together constitute] the apogee-perigee epicycle; of one's own apogee-perigee epicycle, the semi-diameter equals the eccentric-Earth distance. Namely: Under the heading 'half of <s>jha</s> is the slow epicycle' [<s>Gītikā</s> 10], 'of the Moon, <s>cha</s>' — seven half-<s>jha</s>s of the Moon are the apogee-perigee epicycle, meaning a measure of thirty-one and a half degrees. Whatever is the semi-diameter of each, that is established by the rule of three. If from the circumference beginning with 'one hundred and four multiplied by eight' [<s>Gaṇita</s> 10] and such, the semi-diameter equal to ten thousand is obtained, then for the circumference of measure thirty-one and a half degrees, what [is the semi-diameter]? — the result is five degrees and one minute plus a half. For the Sun too, three half-<s>jha</s>s are the slow epicycle, of measure thirteen and a half degrees, and its semi-diameter by the rule of three is two degrees and nine minutes plus a half. Or: if the semi-diameter of the circumference measured at three-hundred-sixty degrees is [of a certain measure in] minutes, then what is the apogee-perigee semi-diameter of the Moon? — three hundred and one minutes plus one-and-a-half. Similarly for the Sun: one hundred and twenty-nine plus a half. The interval between the centers of the orbit-circle and eccentric circle should be conceived in degree-measure or minute-measure. Thus for the Sun and Moon. For the others, because of the danger of multiple eccentric circles due to the division into equal and unequal epicycles and slow-apogee and fast-apogee, he will state later: 'the distance between the Earth and the planet-star' [<s>Kālakriyā</s> 25]. The orbit-circumference is the orbit-circle; on that orbit-circumference, the planets revolve with mean motion. That they revolve with true motion on the eccentric circles is understood from the meaning. // 19 //

body.text: nīcoccavṛttaparidhau grahagatiḥ
body.translated_text: The motion of the planet on the apogee-perigee epicycle circumference

body.text: grahabhuktyānayanavakrānuvakraparijñānāya āha ã
body.translated_text: In order to determine the daily rate of the planet's motion and to know the retrograde and re-direct [phases], he says:

children.translated_text: That [planet] which has fast motion from its apogee has retrograde motion on its own epicycle-orbit;

children.text: anulomagatiḥ vṛtte mandagatiḥ yaḥ grahaḥ bhavati || 20 ||
children.translated_text: that planet which has direct motion on the [orbit-]circle has slow motion. // 20 //

body.text:
śīghrā gatiḥ yasya tat śīgrahgatiḥ, śīghragatiḥ ca tat svoccam ca śīghragatiḥ svoccam, śīghratatiḥsvoccāt yaḥ pratilomagatiḥ śīghragatiḥ | svoccaśabdena svaśīghroccabhuktiḥ parigṛhyate | sā yadi śīghroccabhuktiḥ svakendrāntajyā[sādhitasphuṭamadhya]mabhukteḥ [na patati] tadā sā eva sphuṭamadhyamā bhuktiḥ svakendrāntajyāsādhitā svaśīghroccabhukteḥ pratilome[na] pātyate | tadā śīghragatiḥ svoccagatiḥ iti ucyate | pratilomaśabdena ca viparītapātitaśeṣaliptāḥ
parigṛhyante | evam ayam vigrahārthaḥ niṣpannaḥ bhavati | pratilomā gatiḥ yasya saḥ pratilomagatiḥ iti |
body.translated_text: That whose motion is fast is 'fast-moving' (<s>śīghragati</s>). Both 'fast-moving' and 'its apogee' [combine as] 'fast-moving from its apogee' (<s>śīghragatiḥ svoccāt</s>) — [meaning] the fast motion from the apogee is retrograde. By the word 'its apogee' (<s>svocca</s>), the daily rate of the fast apogee is meant. If that fast-apogee rate does not fall below the true-mean rate derived from the sine of the anomaly at the end [of the arc], then that very true-mean rate derived from the sine of the anomaly is subtracted in the reverse direction from the fast-apogee rate. Then [the planet] is said to be 'fast-moving from its apogee.' And by the word 'retrograde' (<s>pratiloma</s>), the remaining minutes after the reverse subtraction are meant. Thus, this compound-analysis is derived: 'that whose motion is retrograde is <s>pratilomagati</s>'.

body.text:
āditaḥ eva etat bhuktyānayanam prati vakṣyate | tat yathā ã mandoccakendrāntajyām krameṇa utkrameṇa vā niṣpannām svamadhyamabhuktiliptābhiḥ guṇayet | punar ca tat kālapratidhinā guṇitasya aṣṭādaśabhiḥ sahasraiḥ bhāgalabdham kendrapadavaśāt ardhīkṛtya grahamadhyamabhuktiliptāsu prakṣipya viśodhya vā svaśīghroccabhuktiliptābhiḥ śodhayet | śeṣam svaśīghroccakendrāntajyākramotkramajyāguṇam tat kālaśīghroccaparidhinā guṇayet | bhāgaḥ aṣṭādaśabhiḥ
sahasraiḥ | labdham vyāsārdhagatam svakarṇena vibhajet | labhdasya ardham kendrapadavaśāt grahamadhyamabhuktiliptāsu kṣipet, viśodhayet vā | tataḥ tam kṣiptaviśodhitaśeṣam gṛhītvā tṛtīyakarma ã mandoccakendrāntajyākramotkramajyām tat kālaparidhiguṇam aṣṭādaśabhiḥ sahasraiḥ vibhajet | labdham samastam eva grahamadhyamabhuktiliptāsu mandakendrapadavaśāt kṣipet, viśodhayet vā | kṣiptam viśodhitaśiṣṭam vā sphuṭamadhyamabhuktiliptāḥ avinaṣṭāḥ
tāḥ svaśīghroccabhuktiliptābhyaḥ viśodhayet | śeṣam [gṛhītvā] caturthakarma ã śīghroccakendrānta[jyākramotkrama]jyām tat kālaparidhiguṇam aṣṭādaśabhiḥ sahasraiḥ vibhajet | labdham vyāsārdhaguṇam karṇena vibhajet | tatra yad avāptam tat yadi kṣepyam sphuṭamadhyamabhuktiliptāsu kṣipet, niṣpannā grahasya sphuṭabhuktiḥ | atha viśodhyam sad yadi sphuṭamadhyamabhuktitaḥ na patati tadā pratilomagatiḥ grahaḥ sphuṭamadhyamabhuktiliptāḥ eva viparītam
śodhyāḥ | śeṣam vakrabhogaḥ | asmin arthe iyam kārikā ã
body.translated_text: The computation of the daily rate will be stated from the beginning. Namely: Multiply the sine or versed-sine of the slow-apogee anomaly, derived in direct or reverse order, by the daily-rate minutes of one's mean motion. Then multiply by the epicycle circumference at that time, divide by eighteen thousand, halve the result according to the anomaly-quadrant, and add to or subtract from the planet's mean daily-rate minutes. Then subtract [this result] from the fast-apogee daily-rate minutes. The remainder, multiplied by the sine or versed-sine of the fast-apogee anomaly in direct or reverse order, multiply by the epicycle circumference at that time, and divide by eighteen thousand. The result, multiplied by the semi-diameter, divide by the hypotenuse. Halve the result and, according to the anomaly-quadrant, add to or subtract from the planet's mean daily-rate minutes. Then, taking the added or subtracted remainder, perform the third operation: multiply the sine or versed-sine of the slow-apogee anomaly by the epicycle circumference at that time and divide by eighteen thousand. Add or subtract the entire result to or from the planet's mean daily-rate minutes according to the slow-anomaly quadrant. The added or subtracted remainder gives the unperturbed true-mean daily-rate minutes. Subtract those from the fast-apogee daily-rate minutes. Taking the remainder, perform the fourth operation: multiply the sine or versed-sine of the fast-apogee anomaly by the epicycle circumference at that time and divide by eighteen thousand. Multiply the result by the semi-diameter and divide by the hypotenuse. If the obtained result is additive, add it to the true-mean daily-rate minutes — the result is the planet's true daily rate. But if it is subtractive and does not fall below the true-mean daily rate, then the planet has retrograde motion — the true-mean daily-rate minutes are subtracted in reverse. The remainder is the retrograde traversal. For this meaning, this verse [is stated]:

body.text: yaḥ śīghragatiḥ svoccāt pratilomagatiḥ svavṛttakakṣyāyām |
body.translated_text: That which has fast motion from its apogee has retrograde motion on its own epicycle-orbit;

body.text: pratilomagatiḥ vakragatiḥ iti arthaḥ |
body.translated_text: retrograde motion means backward motion — this is the meaning.

body.text: anulomagatiḥ vṛtte | asau anulomagatiḥ bhavati | yadā śīghroccāt śīghroccakendrāntajyāniṣpannā liptāḥ sphuṭamadhyamabhuktiliptābhyaḥ viśuddhāḥ, tadā asau grahaḥ anuvakrī | tatra ca viśeṣaliptāḥ anulomaśabdavācyāḥ | tataḥ arthāt ayam vigrahaḥ avasitaḥ ã anulomā gatiḥ yasya sa anulomagatiḥ iti | sa ca alpam gaccahati iti mandagatiḥ abhidhīyate || 20 ||
body.translated_text: Direct motion on the [orbit-]circle: That [planet] has direct motion. When, from the fast apogee, the minutes derived from the sine of the fast-apogee anomaly are subtracted from the true-mean daily-rate minutes, then that planet is re-direct (<s>anuvakrī</s>). And there, the difference-minutes are denoted by the word 'direct' (<s>anuloma</s>). Hence, from the meaning, this compound-analysis is concluded: 'that whose motion is direct is <s>anulomagati</s>.' And that [planet] traverses little, hence it is called 'slow-moving' (<s>mandagati</s>). // 20 //

body.text: nīcoccavṛttabhramaṇaprakārāntaram
body.translated_text: Another mode of the apogee-perigee epicycle revolution

body.text: grahāṇām sphuṭīkaraṇaprakārāntaram āha ã
body.translated_text: He states another method for the true-position computation of planets:

children.translated_text: The epicycles (<s>vṛttāni</s>) are direct (<s>anuloma</s>) from the <s>manda</s> (slow apogee), and retrograde (<s>pratiloma</s>) from the <s>śīghra</s> (fast apogee);
the mean planet is at the midpoint of its own epicycle, which is situated on the <s>kakṣyāmaṇḍala</s> (deferent circle). // 21 //

body.text:
anulomam gacchati iti anulomagatiḥ | tat uktam ã mandāt, uktamandoccāvadheḥ madhyamāt iti | tat atra api śīghroccāvadheḥ madhyamāt iti etat ekaprakrameṇa bhavitavyam | na iti āha ã śīghrā[t pratilomaga]tiḥ pratilomāvadheḥ | śīghroccasya pratilomagatīni viparītagatīni yāni vṛttāni paridhayaḥ | atra vṛttasya ekadeśe vṛttaśabdopa[cārāt paridhayaḥ ca] iti, yathā mandaśīghrakendrayoḥ tajjyākāṣṭhe dhanūṃṣi | ataḥ tāni dhanūṃṣi mandakendrāt jātāni krameṇa
upa[cīyante, śīghrakendrāt] jātāni utkrameṇa upacīyante | ataḥ "anulomagāni mandāt śīghrāt pratilomagāni vṛttāni" | katham punar vṛttāni mandaśīghrakendrayoḥ tajjyādhanūṃṣi kramotkrama[gatīni? gate]ḥ avasthāvācakatvāt | yathā ã
body.translated_text: That which moves in the direct direction is '<s>anulomagati</s>' (direct motion). That has been stated — 'from the <s>manda</s>,' meaning from the aforementioned <s>mandocca</s> (slow apogee), [reckoned] from the mean [planet]. Here too, 'from the <s>śīghrocca</s> (fast apogee), [reckoned] from the mean [planet]' — this should follow the same procedure. No — he says: 'from the <s>śīghra</s>, retrograde motion' — [reckoned] from the retrograde direction. The epicycles (<s>vṛttāni</s>), i.e., circumferences (<s>paridhayaḥ</s>), that are retrograde, i.e., moving in the reverse direction, of the <s>śīghrocca</s>. Here, by the figurative application of the word '<s>vṛtta</s>' (circle) to a part of a circle, [the meaning is] circumferences — just as in the <s>manda</s> and <s>śīghra</s> anomalies, the sine-arcs [correspond to] their respective sine-chord segments. Therefore, those arcs generated from the <s>manda-kendra</s> (manda anomaly) increase in direct order, while those generated from the <s>śīghra-kendra</s> (śīghra anomaly) increase in reverse order. Hence, 'the epicycles are direct from the <s>manda</s>, retrograde from the <s>śīghra</s>.' But how are the epicycles — the sine-arcs of the <s>manda</s> and <s>śīghra</s> anomalies — [said to have] direct and reverse motions? Because '<s>gati</s>' (motion) denotes a state. Just as —

children.text: gatiḥ asti iti bhūtānām sukumārāyate manaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'There is motion [i.e., departure]' — at this thought, the mind of beings becomes tender;
for one who has
not [departed], it bears the burden unceasingly, as does a cow.

body.text: tathā ã
body.translated_text: Similarly —

children.text: dānam bhogaḥ nāśaḥ tisraḥ gatayaḥ bhavanti vittasya |
children.translated_text: Giving, enjoyment, and destruction — these are the three courses (<s>gatayaḥ</s>) of wealth;

children.text: yaḥ na dadāti na bhuṅkte tasya tṛtīyā gatiḥ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: he who neither gives nor enjoys — for him there is the third course [i.e., destruction].

body.text: bhartṛhariḥ, nītiśatakam, 34
body.translated_text: <s>Bhartṛhari</s>, <s>Nītiśataka</s>, 34

body.text: tasmāt yāni eva jyādhanūṃṣi tāni eva pratilomānulomagatīni |
body.translated_text: Therefore, the sine-arcs themselves are the retrograde and direct motions.

body.text: atha atra idam praṣṭavyam ã mandoccajyādhanūṃṣi mandoccāt upacīyante, śīghroccajyādhanūṃṣi śīghroccāt apacīyante | kutaḥ etat? sampradāyāvicchedāt | atha "vyākhyānataḥ viśeṣapratipattiḥ, na hi sandehāt alakṣaṇam" [aṣṭādhyāyī, śivasūtram 6, pātañjalamahābhāṣyam] iti | athavā mandoccaśīghroccaśravaṇāt mandoccaśīghroccayoḥ eva pratipattiḥ, anyasya aśrutatvāt ca |
body.translated_text: Now here this is to be asked: the <s>mandocca</s>-sine-arcs increase from the <s>mandocca</s>; the <s>śīghrocca</s>-sine-arcs decrease from the <s>śīghrocca</s>. Whence is this? From the unbroken tradition (<s>sampradāyāviccheda</s>). Moreover, 'The specific understanding is from the commentary, for from doubt there is no non-rule' [<s>Aṣṭādhyāyī</s>, <s>Śivasūtra</s> 6, <s>Patañjala Mahābhāṣya</s>]. Or, since the words '<s>mandocca</s>' and '<s>śīghrocca</s>' are heard, the understanding pertains to the <s>mandocca</s> and <s>śīghrocca</s> alone, and because nothing else is mentioned.

body.text: pratimaṇḍalavidhinā grahasphuṭīkaraṇaprakriyā
body.translated_text: The procedure for computing true planetary positions by the eccentric-circle (<s>pratimaṇḍala</s>) method

body.text:
ayam āryāsūtrārthaḥ yathā ghaṭate tathā karmaṇā pratipādayiṣyāmaḥ | iṣṭāt grahāt tat mandoccam viśodhayet | śeṣam rāśyādikam mandoccāt pravṛttam tat kakṣyāmaṇḍalotpannam iti pratimaṇḍale kriyate, yasmāt pratimaṇḍale sphuṭagrahaḥ bhramati | tena tasmāt mandoccāt ārabhya yat kāṣṭham tat mahati maṇḍale alpam bhavati | "mahati mahāntaḥ ca rāśayaḥ jñeyāḥ | aṃśāḥ kalāḥ tathā evam [kālakriyāí, 14] iti | alpe pratimaṇḍale tat eva kāṣṭham bahutaram
bhavati, mānālpatvāt | vrīhyādayaḥ mahatā mānaviśeṣeṇa pramīyamānāḥ prasthādisaṅkhyayā alpāḥ bhavanti, [te] eva alpena mānaviśeṣeṇa mīyamānāḥ prasthādiśaṅkhyayā bahavaḥ bhavanti evam atra api | katham punar tat kāṣṭham kakṣyāmaṇḍalotpannam pratimaṇḍale pramīyate? ucyate ã tat kāṣṭhasya padāni vyatītāni pratyākalayya vartamānapadasya bhujākoṭijyayā karma idam kriyate ã "pratimaṇḍalasya madhyam ghanabhūmadhyāt atikrāntam" [kālakriyāí,
18] iti pratimaṇḍalabhūvivaram koṭyām prathamacaturthayoḥ padayoḥ prakṣipyate, dvitīyatṛtīyayoḥ apanīyate |
body.translated_text: We shall demonstrate the meaning of this <s>āryā</s>-verse through worked computation as it applies. From the desired planet, its <s>mandocca</s> should be subtracted. The remainder in signs and so forth, being generated from the <s>mandocca</s> and [thus] originating on the deferent circle (<s>kakṣyāmaṇḍala</s>), is transferred to the eccentric circle (<s>pratimaṇḍala</s>), since the true planet moves on the eccentric circle. Therefore, from that <s>mandocca</s> onwards, the arc that is small on the great circle — 'On the great [circle], the signs and so forth are great; degrees and minutes likewise' [<s>Kālakriyā</s>, 14] — that same arc becomes larger on the small eccentric circle, because the measure is smaller. Just as rice and such, when measured by a large unit-measure, are small in <s>prastha</s>-count, while the same, measured by a small unit-measure, are many in <s>prastha</s>-count — so here too. But how is that arc originating on the deferent circle measured on the eccentric circle? It is said: having ascertained the elapsed quadrants of that arc and with the sine (<s>bhujajyā</s>) and cosine (<s>koṭijyā</s>) of the current quadrant, this computation is performed: 'The center of the eccentric circle is displaced from the center of the solid Earth' [<s>Kālakriyā</s>, 18] — the eccentric-circle-to-Earth separation (<s>pratimaṇḍalabhūvivara</s>) is added to the cosine in the first and fourth quadrants, and subtracted in the second and third.

body.text:
etat pratipādanārtham samāyāmavanau vṛttakendram nidhāya yāvat tāvat pramāṇaparikalpitavyāsārdhapramāṇena karkaṭakena vṛttam ālikhet | tasya vṛttasya pūrvāpara[dakṣiṇottara]lekhe kṛtvā [tadvṛttakendrāt antya]phala[jyā]pramāṇam [sūtram mandoccābhimukham] dakṣiṇena nidhāya tatra kakṣyāmaṇḍalavyāsārdhatulyakarkaṭakena vṛttam ālikhet | tat pratimaṇḍalam iti ucyate | [tat prathamacaturthapadayoḥ] kakṣyāmaṇḍalāt upari avatiṣṭhate, dvitīyatṛtīyayoḥ
adhaḥ | tatra yā koṭijyā sā kakṣyāmaṇḍalotpannā kakṣyāmaṇḍalabhūmyantarālapramāṇā | tena pratimaṇḍalabhūvivarāntarālamātreṇa pratimaṇḍalam prathamacaturthayoḥ padayoḥ koṭiḥ na prāpnoti iti prakṣipyate, dvitīyatṛtīyapadayoḥ tāvatā atītāt pratimaṇḍalāt koṭiḥ iti apanīyate | evam pratimaṇḍalotpannā koṭiḥ bhavati | atha yadi koṭi[jyātaḥ] pratimaṇḍalabhūvivaram na śudhyati, tadā pratimaṇḍalabhūvivarāt koṭijyā śodhyate | tāvatī pratimaṇḍalakoṭiḥ bhavati
| tatra evam niṣpannāyāḥ koṭeḥ bhujajyāyāḥ ca vargasamāsamūlam karṇaḥ | tat sūkṣmārthibhiḥ aviśiṣyate, pratimaṇḍalakarṇasya vṛddhihrāsavaśāt dṛṣṭiḥ bhidyate iti | tat yadi vyāsārdhatulyena pratimaṇḍalakarṇena yathā uktam pratimaṇḍalabhūvivaram labhyate tadā tena pratimaṇḍalakarṇena kim iti | labdham pūrvakoṭijyāyām prakṣipyate apanīyate vā | tataḥ tadbhujajyāvarga[samāsa]mūlam karṇaḥ | tena punar pratimaṇḍalabhūvivarānayanam iti yāvat aviśeṣaḥ | tataḥ
aviśiṣṭakarṇena vyastatrairāśikam kriyate ã yadi vyāsārdhaviṣkambhasya kakṣyāmaṇḍalasya iyam bhujajyā labhyate, tadā tena karṇena pratimaṇḍalajena kā iti | vyastatrairāśikatvāt vyāsārdham guṇakāraḥ, karṇaḥ bhāgahāraḥ, labdham pratimaṇḍalabhujajyā | tat kāṣṭham mandocce prakṣipya sphuṭaḥ grahaḥ bhavati, yasya mandoccakendram prathamapade | dvitīyapade ṣaḍbhyaḥ rāśibhyaḥ viśodhya bhujā gṛhītā iti ṣaṅbhyaḥ apanīyate, śeṣam mandocce prakṣipyate |
tṛtīyapade cakrārdhādhikabhujā iti tat cāpam cakrārdhasahitam mandocce prakṣipyate | caturthapade dvādaśebhyaḥ viśuddhaśeṣam bhujā iti cakrāt tat kāṣṭham viśodhya śeṣam mandocce prakṣipyate | evam sphuṭagrahaḥ bhavati, yasya śīghroccam na vidyate |
body.translated_text: For demonstrating this: on a level sandy ground, fixing a center, one should draw a circle with a compass of radius equal to the assumed semi-diameter. Having drawn the east-west and north-south lines of that circle, from the circle's center, placing a thread of length equal to the <s>antyaphala</s> (maximum equation) toward the <s>mandocca</s> direction to the south, one should draw a circle there with a compass of radius equal to the deferent-circle semi-diameter. That is called the eccentric circle (<s>pratimaṇḍala</s>). It stands above the deferent circle in the first and fourth quadrants, and below in the second and third. There, the cosine is generated on the deferent circle and measures the distance between the deferent circle and the Earth. Therefore, by the amount of the eccentric-circle-to-Earth separation alone, the cosine does not reach the eccentric circle in the first and fourth quadrants — hence [the separation] is added; in the second and third quadrants, the cosine exceeds the eccentric circle by that amount — hence it is subtracted. Thus the cosine generated on the eccentric circle is obtained. Now, if the eccentric-circle-to-Earth separation is not subtractable from the cosine, then the cosine is subtracted from the eccentric-circle-to-Earth separation. That much becomes the eccentric-circle cosine. There, the square root of the sum of the squares of the thus-obtained cosine and sine is the hypotenuse (<s>karṇa</s>). This must be refined by those seeking precision, because the line of sight changes due to the increase and decrease of the eccentric-circle hypotenuse. If from the hypotenuse equal to the semi-diameter, the eccentric-circle-to-Earth separation as stated is obtained, then from that eccentric-circle hypotenuse, what? The obtained [quantity] is added to or subtracted from the previous cosine. Then the square root of the sum of the squares of that and the sine gives the hypotenuse. With that, again the eccentric-circle-to-Earth separation is computed — and so on until there is no difference (<s>aviśeṣa</s>). Then with the refined hypotenuse, the inverse Rule of Three is applied: if from the deferent circle of semi-diameter extent, this sine is obtained, then from that eccentric-circle hypotenuse, what? Because it is an inverse Rule of Three, the semi-diameter is the multiplier and the hypotenuse is the divisor; the result is the eccentric-circle sine. That arc, added to the <s>mandocca</s>, gives the true planet — for one whose <s>manda-kendra</s> is in the first quadrant. In the second quadrant, since the sine is taken by subtracting from six signs, it is subtracted from six, and the remainder is added to the <s>mandocca</s>. In the third quadrant, since the sine is the half-circle-plus sine, that arc together with the half-circle is added to the <s>mandocca</s>. In the fourth quadrant, since the sine is the remainder after subtracting from twelve, the arc is subtracted from the circle and the remainder is added to the <s>mandocca</s>. Thus the true planet is obtained — for one that has no <s>śīghrocca</s>.

body.text:
yeṣām punar śīghroccam vidyate teṣām karmaviśeṣaḥ ucyate | tat yathā ã paridhicālanāprayogeṇa sphuṭīkṛtaparidhinā vyāsārdham samguṇayya aśītyā bhāgalabdham pratimaṇḍalabhūvivaram mandaśīghroccayoḥ | tena anantarābhihitamandoccakarmaṇā mandocca[phalam] sādhayet | [tat] sakalasaṃskṛtaḥ grahaḥ bhavati | tat evam niṣpannasya, madhyamasya grahasya [ca] yat antarārdham tat madhyamāt mandoccasiddhe adhike madhyamagrahe dhanam, ūne ṛṇam
| evam mandoccasaṃ[skaraṇam] | etat eva karma "śanigurukujeṣu mande ardham ṛṇadhanam bhavati pūrvam" [kālakriyāí, 22] iti anena granthena abhidhīyate | katham? sanigurukujeṣu, mandāraguruṣu madhyameṣu madhyamakarmaṇā siddheṣu mandāraguruṣu iti arthaḥ | "ardham ṛṇadhanam bhavati pūrvam" [kālakriyāí, 22] iti kasya ardham ṛṇam dhanam vā bhavati iti atra sampradāyāvicchedāt mandasiddhamadhyamāntaram parigṛhyate | kim tasya ardham madhye grahe
dhanam ṛṇam vā pūrvasiddhe mandoccakarmaṇi bhavati? idam ca karma mandoccaśīghroccayoḥ sāmānyena prasiddham | kutaḥ? viśeṣānuvādanā[bhāvā]t | tat yathā ã evam ardhena phalena saṃskṛtam madhyamam graham śīghroccāt grahāt viśodhayet | tatra kendrapadavibhāgena bhujākoṭijye gṛhītvā sphuṭīkṛtasvaśīghroccaparidhinā vyāsārdham saṃguṇayya aśītyā bhāgalabdhapratimaṇḍalabhūvivareṇa pūrvakarmaṇā eva saṃskṛtāt karṇam ānayet | atra aviśeṣābhāvāt
aviśeṣakarma na pravartate | tataḥ bhujajyayā vyāsārdham saṃguṇayya karṇena bhāgalabdhasya kāṣṭham śīghroccakendre prathamapade śīghroccāt apanīyate, dvitīye pade ṣaḍbhyaḥ viśodhya śeṣam śīghroccāt apanīyate | tṛtīye pade cakrārdhayuktam, caturthe pade dvādaśabhyaḥ viśuddhaśeṣam, "śīghrāt pratilomagāni vṛttāni" iti vacanāt | evam sīghroccasakalaphalasaṃskṛtaḥ grahaḥ bhavati | tasya mandoccasiddhasya ca pūrvavat eva antarārdham mandoccasiddhe pūrvakalpanayā
eva dhanam ṛṇam vā kuryāt | tat mandaśīghra[siddha]m avinaṣṭam vidhāya tasmāt mandoccam viśodhya pūrvavat eva mandoccam sādhayet | tasya mandoccasiddhasya dvisaṃskṛtasya avinaṣṭasthāpitasya ca yaḥ viśeṣaḥ tam sakalam eva dvisaṃskṛtahīnamadhyamāt viśodhayet, adhikamadhyame prakṣipet | [arthāt dvisaṃskṛtamandasiddhe ūne sati viśodhayet anyathā prakṣipet] | tam evaṃkṛtam śīghroccāt viśodhya śīghroccaprasiddhakarmaṇā saṃsiddhaḥ sphuṭaḥ grahaḥ bhaviṣyati
iti | etat eva karma saṃkṣepeṇa asmābhiḥ karmanibandhe uktam ã
body.translated_text: For those that do have a <s>śīghrocca</s>, a special procedure is described. Namely: by the epicycle-displacement method, having multiplied the semi-diameter by the corrected epicycle and dividing by eighty, [one obtains] the eccentric-circle-to-Earth separation for both <s>mandocca</s> and <s>śīghrocca</s>. With that, by the <s>mandocca</s> procedure described above, one should derive the <s>mandocca</s> equation (<s>phala</s>). That becomes the fully corrected planet. Of that thus-obtained [planet] and the mean planet, half the difference — if the <s>manda</s>-corrected [planet] exceeds the mean planet, it is additive; if less, subtractive. Thus is the <s>manda</s> correction. This very procedure is expressed by the verse 'In Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars, for the <s>manda</s>, half is subtractive-additive first' [<s>Kālakriyā</s>, 22]. How? 'In Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars' — in the slow-moving planets, when corrected by the <s>manda</s> procedure, [they become] <s>manda</s>-corrected — this is the meaning. 'Half is subtractive-additive first' — half of what is subtractive or additive? Here, from unbroken tradition, the difference between the <s>manda</s>-corrected and the mean is taken. What — is that half additive or subtractive in the mean planet, [applied] before the <s>manda</s>-correction? And this procedure is common to both <s>mandocca</s> and <s>śīghrocca</s>. Why? Because of the absence of any statement specifying a difference. Namely: the mean planet corrected with [this] half-equation is subtracted from the <s>śīghrocca</s>. There, having taken the sine and cosine by quadrant-division, having multiplied the semi-diameter by its own corrected <s>śīghra</s> epicycle and dividing by eighty, with the obtained eccentric-circle-to-Earth separation, by the previous procedure itself, one derives the hypotenuse. Here, since there is no non-convergence, the iterative procedure does not apply. Then, having multiplied the sine by the semi-diameter and dividing by the hypotenuse, the arc [is found]: in the first quadrant of the <s>śīghra-kendra</s>, it is subtracted from the <s>śīghrocca</s>; in the second quadrant, the remainder after subtracting from six [signs] is subtracted from the <s>śīghrocca</s>. In the third quadrant, joined with the half-circle; in the fourth quadrant, the remainder after subtracting from twelve — 'from the <s>śīghra</s>, the epicycles are retrograde' — by this statement. Thus the planet corrected by the full <s>śīghra</s> equation is obtained. Of that and the <s>manda</s>-corrected [planet], as before, half the difference — by the previous convention — is made additive or subtractive in the <s>manda</s>-corrected [planet]. Having preserved that <s>manda-śīghra</s>-corrected [value], from it the <s>mandocca</s> is subtracted and the <s>manda</s>-correction is performed as before. Of that <s>manda</s>-corrected [planet], twice-corrected, and the preserved [value], the difference — the whole of it — is subtracted from or added to the twice-corrected-minus-mean [planet]. [That is, if the twice-corrected <s>manda</s>-corrected is less, subtract; otherwise add.] Having done thus, the <s>śīghrocca</s> is subtracted and, by the well-known <s>śīghra</s> procedure, the corrected true planet will be obtained. This very procedure has been stated by us in summary in the <s>Karmanibandha</s>:

children.translated_text: The eccentric-circle procedure too should be applied here by the discerning;

children.text: mandocce pūrvavat kuryāt śīghroccāt tat viśodhyate ||
children.translated_text: one should perform [the correction] at the <s>mandocca</s> as before; it is subtracted from the <s>śīghrocca</s>.

children.text: tat eva kevalam śodhyam [cakrārdhāt śodhya tat calāt] |
children.translated_text: That alone is to be subtracted [from the half-circle]; subtracting from the half-circle, that [is applied] to the <s>cala</s> (anomaly);

children.text: cakrārdhasaṃyutam cāpam cakrāt śuddham ca śeṣayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: the arc joined with the half-circle, and that subtracted from the circle, in the remaining [quadrants].
The semi-diameter multiplied by the corrected epicycle, divided by eighty, from its own cosine,

children.text: tyaktvā padeṣu yuktvā vā karṇaḥ prāgvat prasādhyate |
children.translated_text: subtracting or adding in the [respective] quadrants — the hypotenuse is derived as before.
Joined with half the difference of the <s>manda</s>-corrected and that mean,

children.text: mandasiddhe adhike hīne rahitaḥ madhyamaḥ grahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: when the <s>manda</s>-corrected exceeds, or diminished when less — [this gives] the mean planet.

children.text: sa śīghroccāt punar sādhyaḥ siddhayoḥ antarālajam |
children.translated_text: That is again to be derived from the <s>śīghrocca</s>; the difference between the two results,
having halved, should be applied to the once-corrected [value] as before.
Having done thus, one should again perform the <s>manda</s>-correction;

children.text: mandasiddhasya tasya ayam viśeṣaḥ yaḥ abhidhāsyate ||
children.translated_text: the difference of that <s>manda</s>-corrected [planet] — which will be stated — is this:
the difference between the twice-<s>manda</s>-corrected and the twice-corrected [value],

children.text: prāgvat tat madhyame kṛtvā śīghrasiddhaḥ sphuṭaḥ grahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: having applied that to the mean as before — the <s>śīghra</s>-corrected [planet] is the true planet.

body.text: mahābhāskarīyam, 4.45-51
body.translated_text: <s>Mahābhāskarīya</s>, 4.45-51

body.text: atra śanigurukujagrahaṇam śīghroccavat grahapratipādanārtham | tena budhaśukrayoḥ api idam karma kriyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the mention of Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars is for the purpose of teaching that the planets are [treated] like the <s>śīghrocca</s>. Therefore, this procedure is applied to Mercury and Venus as well.

body.text:
kakṣyāmaṇḍalalagnasvavṛttamadhye | kakṣyāmaṇḍale lagnam kakṣyāmaṇḍalalagnam | kim tat? svavṛttamadhyam, svavṛttamaṇḍalamadhyam | kakṣyāmaṇḍalalagnam ca tat svavṛttamadhyam ca kakṣyāmaṇḍalalagnasvavṛttamadhyam | tasmin kakṣyāmaṇḍalalagnasvavṛttamadhye | grahaḥ madhyaḥ | yaḥ asau madhyaḥ grahaḥ sa kakṣyāmaṇḍalalagnasvavṛttamadhye bhavati | etat uktam bhavati ã kakṣyāpratimaṇḍalayoḥ yatra sampātaḥ tatra yaḥ asau madhyamagrahaḥ,
sa eva sphuṭaḥ iti |
body.translated_text: 'At the midpoint of its own epicycle, which is situated on the deferent circle.' 'Situated on the deferent circle' means 'kakṣyāmaṇḍalalagnam' — bound to the deferent circle. What is that? 'The midpoint of its own epicycle' — the middle of its own epicyclic circle. 'Bound to the deferent circle and the midpoint of its own epicycle' — that is 'kakṣyāmaṇḍalalagnasvavṛttamadhya.' At that midpoint of its own epicycle bound to the deferent circle — the mean planet [is located]. That mean planet is at the midpoint of its own epicycle bound to the deferent circle. What is being said is: at the intersection of the deferent circle and the eccentric circle, the mean planet that exists there — that itself is the true [planet].

body.text: grahasphuṭīkaraṇe anyeṣām matapradarśanam
body.translated_text: Presentation of others' views on the computation of true planetary positions

body.text:
atha anye anyathā vyākhyānam kurvanti | anulomam gacchanti iti anulomagāni | kāni? vṛttāni, paridhayaḥ iti arthaḥ | mandāt | mandoccāt prabhṛti yāni mandoccavṛttāni mandoccāt ārabhya anulomam gacchanti, yasmāt mandoccakendram ahar ahar upacīyate | śīghrāt pratilomagāni | śīghrāt śīghroccāt ārabhya yāni śīghroccavṛttāni tāni pratilomam gacchanti, yasmāt śīghroccakendram ahar ahar apacīyate | atra idam praṣṭavyam ã katham vā mandoccakendram
ahar ahar upacīyate, katham vā śīghroccakendram ahar ahar apacīyate iti? ucyate ã grahāt patite mandocce [mandakendra]bhuktayaḥ upacīyante, grahāt patite śīghrocce śīghrakendrabhuktayaḥ apacīyante | yadi evam grahāt śīghroccam na patati mahattvāt tarhi maṇḍalam prakṣipya pātyate iti | tatra bhagaṇāḥ bhagaṇebhyaḥ viśodhyāḥ, rāśayaḥ rāśibhyaḥ, bhāgāḥ bhāgebhyaḥ, liptāḥ liptābhyaḥ iti eṣaḥ kramaḥ | tatra grahabhagaṇebhyaḥ śīghroccabhagaṇāḥ eva tāvat na
śuddhyanti | kutaḥ asau bhagaṇaḥ yam prakṣipya śīghroccam viśodhyate? tasmāt gaṇitayuktyā yāni api śīghravṛttāni tāni api anulomagāni eva | ācāryeṇa tu karaṇalāghavārtham "pratilomagāni vṛttāni" iti uktam | kim punar atra karaṇalāghavam? kāmacāraḥ | yadi grahaḥ śīghroccāt patati tadā grahaḥ śīghroccāt viśodhyate | yadā ca śīghroccam grahāt patati tadā grahāt śīghroccam viśodhyate iti | satyam eva etat, kintu jyāparidhikalpanā vyabhicarati | yadā grahāt śīghroccam
viśodhitam bhavati tadā anyathā jyā anyathā paridhiḥ, tadānīm eva śīghroccāt viśuddhe grahe anyathā jyā anyathā eva paridhiḥ | atha manyate śīghroccaviśuddhe grahe yat prathamapadam tat caturthapadam, yat dvitīyapadam tat tṛtīyapadam, yat tṛtīyapadam tat dvitīyapadam, yat caturthapadam tat prathamapadam iti | evam tarhi yat jyāyasī kalpanā, tasmāt mandoccam grahāt viśodhyam | grahaḥ ca śīghroccāt | mandaśīghravṛttāni kramotkrameṇa eva gacchanti |
  kakṣyāmaṇḍalalagnaḥ | kakṣyāyāḥ maṇḍalam kakṣyāmaṇḍalam | athavā kakṣyā ca sā maṇḍalam ca tat kakṣyāmaṇḍalam | tena kakṣyāmaṇḍalena lagnaḥ kakṣyāmaṇḍalalagnaḥ | kaḥ? grahaḥ madhyaḥ | svavṛttamadhye | svasya vṛttam svavṛttam | tat ca sāmānyena mandavṛttam śīghravṛttam ca parigṛhyate | tasya svamandavṛttasya [svaśīghra]vṛttasya ca madhyam svavṛttamadhyam | tatra grahasya madhyaḥ, sa ca kakṣyāmaṇḍalāsaktaḥ | svavṛttasya kakṣyāmaṇḍale
yathā madhyam bhavati tathā badhnīyāt | tasmin svavṛtte yathā kakṣyāmaṇḍale yathā madhyam bhavati tathā badhnīyāt | tasmin svavṛtte yathā kakṣyāmaṇḍale jyā avitiṣṭhate tathā eva avatiṣṭhamānā draṣṭavyā | katham? yathā kakṣyāmaṇḍalasya ṣaṇṇavatyaṃśakā kāṣṭhajyā | evam atra api ṣaṇṇavatyaṃśakā kāṣṭhajyā parikalpanīyā | tat yathā ã uccāt ārabhya bhujajyākoṭijyābhyām trairāśikam ã yadi ṣaṣṭiśatatrayaparidhau ime bhujajyākoṭijye, [tadā] uccanīcaparidhau
ke iti | athavā ã vyāsārdhena ime bhujajyākoṭijye, tataḥ antyaphalatulyena uccanīcavṛttavyāsārdhena ke iti | labdhe uccanīcavṛttasya bhujajyākoṭijye | tatra prathamacaturthayoḥ padayoḥ vyāsārdhāt upari koṭisādhanam sthitam iti vyāsārdhe prakṣipyate | dvitīyatṛtīyayoḥ padayoḥ vyāsārdhonam pravṛttam iti vyāsārdhāt apanīyate | evam koṭikā niṣpannā bhavati, bhujākoṭivargasamāsamūlam karṇaḥ | evam mandaśīghrayoḥ karṇotpattiḥ || 21 ||
body.translated_text: Now others offer a different explanation. 'That which moves in the direct direction' — [these are] 'anulomagāni' (direct-moving). What? 'Vṛttāni' — meaning epicycles (paridhayaḥ). 'From the manda': starting from the <s>mandocca</s> (slow apogee), the <s>mandocca</s>-epicycles move in the direct direction from the <s>mandocca</s>, because the <s>manda-kendra</s> (manda anomaly) increases day by day. 'From the <s>śīghra</s>, retrograde': starting from the <s>śīghrocca</s> (fast apogee), the <s>śīghrocca</s>-epicycles move in the retrograde direction, because the <s>śīghra-kendra</s> (śīghra anomaly) decreases day by day. Here this is to be asked: how does the <s>manda-kendra</s> increase day by day, and how does the <s>śīghra-kendra</s> decrease day by day? It is answered: when the <s>mandocca</s> falls behind the planet, the <s>manda-kendra</s> daily rates increase; when the <s>śīghrocca</s> falls behind the planet, the <s>śīghra-kendra</s> daily rates decrease. If so — if the <s>śīghrocca</s> does not fall behind the planet due to its greatness — then a full circle is added and [the subtraction] is carried out. There, revolutions are subtracted from revolutions, signs from signs, degrees from degrees, minutes from minutes — this is the procedure. There, the <s>śīghrocca</s> revolutions cannot be subtracted from the planet's revolutions in the first place. Whence is that [full] revolution which, when added, allows the <s>śīghrocca</s> to be subtracted? Therefore, by mathematical reasoning, the <s>śīghra</s> epicycles too move in the direct direction only. But the <s>ācārya</s> has said 'the epicycles are retrograde' for the sake of computational convenience. What, then, is this computational convenience? Freedom of choice. If the planet falls behind the <s>śīghrocca</s>, then the planet is subtracted from the <s>śīghrocca</s>. And when the <s>śīghrocca</s> falls behind the planet, then the <s>śīghrocca</s> is subtracted from the planet. This is true indeed, but the sine-and-epicycle assignment becomes inconsistent. When the <s>śīghrocca</s> has been subtracted from the planet, the sine is one thing and the epicycle is another; at the same time, when the planet is subtracted from the <s>śīghrocca</s>, the sine is different and the epicycle is different too. Now, if one thinks: when the planet is subtracted from the <s>śīghrocca</s>, what is the first quadrant [becomes] the fourth quadrant, what is the second [becomes] the third, what is the third [becomes] the second, and what is the fourth [becomes] the first — even so, the greater computation [applies]; therefore, the <s>mandocca</s> should be subtracted from the planet, and the planet from the <s>śīghrocca</s>. The <s>manda</s> and <s>śīghra</s> epicycles move in direct and reverse order respectively. 'Bound to the deferent circle': the circle of the orbit is the deferent circle (<s>kakṣyāmaṇḍala</s>). Or, the orbit which is also a circle is the deferent circle. Bound to that deferent circle — '<s>kakṣyāmaṇḍalalagnaḥ</s>.' Who? The mean planet. 'At the midpoint of its own epicycle': its own epicycle is '<s>svavṛtta</s>.' And that, in general, is taken to mean both the <s>manda</s>-epicycle and the <s>śīghra</s>-epicycle. The midpoint of one's own <s>manda</s>-epicycle and <s>śīghra</s>-epicycle is '<s>svavṛttamadhya</s>.' There the planet is mean, and that [mean planet] is attached to the deferent circle. One should bind [the model] so that its own epicycle has its midpoint on the deferent circle. On that epicycle, just as the sine stands on the deferent circle, so it should be seen as standing [on the epicycle]. How? Just as the deferent circle has a sine-chord of ninety-six degrees, so here too a sine-chord of ninety-six degrees should be conceived. Namely: starting from the apogee, with the sine and cosine, the rule of three [is applied]: if for a circumference of three-hundred-sixty degrees, these are the sine and cosine, then for the apogee-perigee epicycle circumference, what? Or: if with the semi-diameter, these are the sine and cosine, then with the apogee-perigee epicycle semi-diameter equal to the maximum equation (<s>antyaphala</s>), what? The obtained [values] are the sine and cosine of the apogee-perigee epicycle. There, in the first and fourth quadrants, the cosine-computation stands above the semi-diameter, hence it is added to the semi-diameter. In the second and third quadrants, it is less than the semi-diameter, hence it is subtracted from the semi-diameter. Thus the cosine is obtained; the square root of the sum of the squares of the sine and cosine is the hypotenuse (<s>karṇa</s>). Thus the generation of the hypotenuse for both <s>manda</s> and <s>śīghra</s> [corrections]. // 21 //

body.text: nīcoccavṛttavidhinā śanigurukujasphuṭīkaraṇam
body.translated_text: True-position computation of Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars by the apogee-perigee epicycle method

body.text: grahāṇām ṛṇadhanapratipādanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of teaching the additive and subtractive [corrections] for the planets, he says:

children.translated_text: Subtractive, additive, additive, subtractive — [these corrections] are [applied] from the <s>mandocca</s>, and in reverse from the <s>śīghrocca</s>;

children.text: śanigurukujeṣu mandāt ardham ṛṇam dhanam bhavati pūrve || 22 ||
children.translated_text: in Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars, from the <s>manda</s>, half is subtractive-additive first. // 22 //

body.text: kṣayadhanadhanakṣayāḥ | kṣayaḥ ca dhanaḥ ca dhanaḥ ca kṣayaḥ ca kṣayadhanadhanakṣayāḥ | ete kṣayadhanadhanakṣayāḥ yathāsaṅkhyena padeṣu pratyetavyāḥ | tat yathā ã prathame pade kṣayaḥ, dvitīye pade dhanam, tṛtīye pade dhanam eva, caturthe pade kṣayaḥ iti | ayam kṣayādikramaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Subtractive, additive, additive, subtractive' (<s>kṣayadhanadhanakṣayāḥ</s>): subtractive and additive and additive and subtractive — '<s>kṣayadhanadhanakṣayāḥ</s>.' These — subtractive, additive, additive, subtractive — are to be understood in correspondence with the [four] quadrants respectively. Namely: in the first quadrant, subtractive; in the second quadrant, additive; in the third quadrant, additive; in the fourth quadrant, subtractive. This is the order of subtractive and so forth.

body.text:
padakramaḥ ca kasmāt parigṛhyate iti āha ã mandoccāt pravṛttāt grahāt | kutaḥ? ucyate ã "mandoccāt" iyam pañcamī maryādābhidhāyinī | tataḥ mandoccāt iti anena mandoccāt pravṛttaḥ grahaḥ parigṛhyate | sa katham mandoccāt pravṛttaḥ grahaḥ jñeyaḥ? ucyate ã na atra kiñcit api jñeyam | yāvadbhiḥ mandoccāt adhikaḥ grahaḥ tavatā asau mandoccāt pravṛttaḥ grahaḥ jñeyaḥ | tena tatparijñānārtham mandoccam grahāt pātyate, tatra śeṣeṇa rāśyādinā mandoccāt
pravṛttaḥ asau grahaḥ bhavati | tasmāt prathamapade yā kramajyā tasyāḥ phalam trairāśikena ānīyate | yadi ṣaṣṭiśatatrayaparidheḥ iyam jyā, tadā iṣṭagrahaparidheḥ kā iti phalam labhyate | etat eva trairāśikam | jhārdhāpavartamānaṣaṣṭiśatatrayaparidheḥ aśītiḥ, svaparidhibhāgānām yathā uktākṣarasaṅkhyā | tena paridhinā guṇitajyāyāḥ aśītiḥ bhāgahāraḥ | svaparidhyakṣarasaṅkhyā guṇakāraḥ | labdham phalam ṛṇam eva | dvitīyapade utkrameṇa jyā vyavasthitā iti,
utkramajyāphalam dhanam | punar tṛtīyapade krameṇa jyā vyavasthitā iti kramajyāphalam dhanam | caturthe pade utkrameṇa jyā vyavasthitā iti utkramajyāphalam kṣayaḥ | tatra prathamapade eva mandakendram, tat utpannam eva phalam grahamadhye kṣayaḥ | yadā dvitīyapade kendram tadā prathamapadavyāsārdhajyotpannam aśeṣaphalam kṣayaḥ, dvitīyapadotkramajyāphalam dhanam | prathamadvitīyapadābhyām tṛtīyacaturthapade vyākhyāte |
body.translated_text: And why is the quadrant-order adopted? He says: 'from the <s>mandocca</s>' — from the planet that has proceeded from the <s>mandocca</s>. Whence [is this known]? It is answered: '<s>mandoccāt</s>' — this fifth-case (ablative) ending denotes a limit. Therefore, by '<s>mandoccāt</s>' (from the <s>mandocca</s>), the planet that has proceeded from the <s>mandocca</s> is taken. How is that planet that has proceeded from the <s>mandocca</s> to be known? It is answered: nothing special is to be known here. By however much the planet exceeds the <s>mandocca</s>, by that much the planet is known as having proceeded from the <s>mandocca</s>. Therefore, for ascertaining that, the <s>mandocca</s> is subtracted from the planet; by the remainder in signs and so forth, the planet has proceeded from the <s>mandocca</s>. Then, in the first quadrant, the equation of the direct-order sine is obtained by the rule of three: if for a circumference of three-hundred-sixty, this is the sine, then for the desired planet's epicycle, what? — the equation is obtained. This is the very same rule of three: [the three-hundred-sixty circumference] reduced by the half-<s>jha</s> gives eighty as the divisor; the letter-numeral value of one's own epicycle-degrees is the multiplier. The sine multiplied by the epicycle is divided by eighty. The result — the equation — is subtractive. In the second quadrant, the sine is arranged in reverse order, hence the reverse-sine equation is additive. Again in the third quadrant, the sine is in direct order, hence the direct-sine equation is additive. In the fourth quadrant, the sine is in reverse order, hence the reverse-sine equation is subtractive. There, in the first quadrant itself the <s>manda-kendra</s> [arises]; that very equation that arises is subtractive in the mean planet. When the anomaly is in the second quadrant, the complete equation from the first-quadrant's semi-diameter sine is subtractive, while the second-quadrant's reverse-sine equation is additive. The third and fourth quadrants are explained by the first and second.

body.text:
athavā karaṇalāghavārtham evam kriyate ã prathamapade yat utpannam krameṇa jyāphalam kṣayaḥ | dvitīyapade yat utpannam punar yat gatam rāśyādikam atītam prathamapadasaṃjñitarāśitrayāt kṣayātmakāt dhanātmakam tat dvitīyapadasya yat gatam tat viśodhya śeṣam tatra kṣayaḥ eva avatiṣṭhate, tena tat utpannam phalam madhyamagrahe kṣayaḥ | evam dvitīyapadānte kṣayadhanayoḥ tulyatvāt na kiñcit avatiṣṭhate | tasmāt sāmarthyataḥ ayam arthaḥ
saṃjātaḥ ã prathamapade gatajyāphalam kṣayaḥ, dvitīyapade api āgatajyāphalam kṣayaḥ | etena mandakendraphalam meṣādike kṣayaḥ | tat etat prathamapade gatam bhujāsaṃjñitam dvitīyapade anāgatam | koṭisaṃjñitam [prathamapade anāgatam] dvitīyapade gatam | tṛtīyacaturthayoḥ ca | tṛtīyapade kramajyāphalam dhanam | caturthapade tṛtīyapadarāśitrayāt dhanāt dhanasaṃjñitāt caturthapadarāśyādigatakṣayasaṃjñitam viśodhyate, śeṣam dhanam eva avatiṣṭhate | evam
caturthapadānte dhanakṣayayoḥ tulyatvāt na kiṃcit avaśiṣyate | tasmāt atra api sa eva arthaḥ tulādikendre bhujāphalam dhanam iti |
body.translated_text: Alternatively, for computational convenience, it is done thus: in the first quadrant, the direct-sine equation that arises is subtractive. In the second quadrant, what arises — again, whatever signs and so forth have elapsed of the current [quadrant] are from the second quadrant, [which is] additive in nature; that second-quadrant elapsed [portion] is subtracted from the three signs designated as the first quadrant, which are subtractive in nature; the remainder there is still subtractive — hence the equation that arises is subtractive in the mean planet. Thus at the end of the second quadrant, the subtractive and additive being equal, nothing remains. Therefore, by implication, this meaning arises: in the first quadrant, the elapsed-sine equation is subtractive; in the second quadrant also, the remaining-sine equation is subtractive. By this, the <s>manda-kendra</s> equation beginning from <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries) is subtractive. This [quantity], called the sine (<s>bhujā</s>) in the first quadrant when elapsed, is the remaining in the second quadrant. The cosine (<s>koṭi</s>) [is] the remaining in the first quadrant, the elapsed in the second. And in the third and fourth [quadrants likewise].
