In the third quadrant, the direct-sine equation is additive. In the fourth quadrant, from the three signs of the third quadrant — which are additive in nature — the current-quadrant elapsed [portion], which is subtractive in nature, is subtracted; the remainder is additive. Thus at the end of the fourth quadrant, the additive and subtractive being equal, nothing remains. Therefore here too the same meaning [holds]: beginning from the <s>Tulā</s> (Libra) anomaly, the sine equation is additive.

body.text:
suṣṭhu khalu etat avagamyate | yadi padeṣu sarveṣu tulyāḥ paridhayaḥ tadā evam syāt | na ca tulyāḥ paridhayaḥ paṭhyante | atulyeṣu ca paridhiṣu pratimaṇḍalasya ca api avasthā virudhyate | kutaḥ? prathamapade śukrasya catuṣkaḥ paridhiḥ | tatra dvitīyapadaprāptau eva dvikaḥ paridhiḥ | tatra ardhapahalam parihīyate | grahaḥ tu gacchan krameṇa gacchati, na hariṇaplutena | na eṣa doṣaḥ | tulyāḥ paridhayaḥ | nanu ca uktam ã na ca tulyāḥ paridhayaḥ paṭhyante
iti | na etat asti | evam vijñāyate ã ete paridhayaḥ upacayā[pacayā]tmakāḥ, yataḥ tena tulyopacayāpacayātmakatvāt kramotkramavyavasthāyāḥ, yataḥ te eva bhavanti iti | tena tulyāḥ ucyante | tat yathā ã prathamapade kramajyām paridhyantareṇa hatvā vyāsārdhena labdham ūne viṣamapadaparidhau prakṣipyate, adhike apanīyate | prathamadvitīyapadābhyām tṛtīyacaturthapade vyākhyāte |
body.translated_text: This is indeed well understood — if the epicycles are equal in all quadrants, it would be so. But unequal epicycles are taught. And with unequal epicycles, the configuration of the eccentric circle too is contradicted. Why? In the first quadrant, <s>Venus</s>'s epicycle is four. There, upon reaching the second quadrant, the epicycle is two. Then half the equation is lost. But the planet, as it moves, moves gradually — not by leaps like a deer. This is no fault — the epicycles are equal. But was it not said that unequal epicycles are taught? No, this is not so. It is understood thus: these epicycles involve increase and decrease; since they have equal increase and decrease, by the arrangement of direct and reverse order — since those very [epicycles] come about — they are said to be equal. Namely: in the first quadrant, the direct-sine is multiplied by the epicycle difference and divided by the semi-diameter; the result is added to the smaller odd-quadrant epicycle, or subtracted from the larger. The third and fourth quadrants are explained by the first and second.

body.text:
vyatyayena śīghroccāt | śīghroccakendrāt padavaśāt kramotkramajyāphalam viparītam | prathamacaturthayoḥ padayoḥ dhanam, dvitīyatṛtīyayoḥ kṣayaḥ iti viparyayaḥ | athavā bhujāphalam śīghrakrameṇa ānītam meṣādau dhanam, tulādāvṛṇam | paridhicālanādyaśeṣam pūrvavat eva | atra śīghraphalam vyāsārdhena saṃguṇayya tat utpannakrarṇena bhāgalabdham phalam dhanam ṛṇam vā | etat ca karma trairāśikam ã yadi vyāsārdhamaṇḍale idam phalam
labhyate, tadā śīghroccakarṇamaṇḍale kiyat iti vyastatrairāśikena vyāsārdham guṇakāraḥ, karṇaḥ bhāgahāraḥ | atra kim iti vyastatrairāśikam? ucyate ã "alpe hi maṇḍale alpāḥ mahati mahāntaḥ ca rāśayaḥ jñeyāḥ" [kālakriyāí, 14] iti anena | atha mandoccaphalam evam kasmāt na kriyate? ucyate ã kriyamāṇe api tāvat eva tat phalam bhavati iti na kriyate | kutaḥ? mandoccakarṇaḥ aviśiṣyate | tatra ca aviśeṣitena phalena vyāsārdham saṃguṇayya karṇena bhāge hṛte pūrvam
ānītam eva phalam bhavati iti | atha kim iti śīghroccakarṇaḥ na aviśiṣyate? abhāvāt aviśeṣakarmaṇaḥ |
body.translated_text: In reverse from the <s>śīghrocca</s> (fast apogee): From the <s>śīghrocca-kendra</s> (fast anomaly), the sine result in direct or reverse order, according to the quadrant, is reversed — in the first and fourth quadrants it is additive, in the second and third it is subtractive: this is the reversal. Alternatively, the <s>bhujāphala</s> (base-result), derived by the <s>śīghra</s> (fast) method, is additive from <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries) onward and subtractive from <s>Tulā</s> (Libra) onward. The remaining [procedure] — circumference adjustment and so forth — is exactly as before. Here, the <s>śīghra</s>-result is multiplied by the semi-diameter (<s>vyāsārdha</s>), and from the product thus obtained, the quotient obtained by division is the result — additive or subtractive. And this operation is a rule of three: if in the semi-diameter circle this result is obtained, then in the <s>śīghrocca-karṇa</s> (fast-apogee hypotenuse) circle, how much? — by the inverse rule of three, the semi-diameter is the multiplier and the hypotenuse is the divisor. Here, why is the inverse rule of three [used]? It is said: because 'in a small circle, the quantities are small, and in a large one, they are large' [<s>Kālakriyā</s> 14]. Now, why is the <s>mandocca</s> (slow apogee) result not treated in the same way? It is said: even when it is so treated, the result remains exactly the same, therefore it is not done. Why? Because the <s>mandocca-karṇa</s> (slow-apogee hypotenuse) is iterated [to convergence]. And there, multiplying the iterated result by the semi-diameter and dividing by the hypotenuse yields exactly the previously obtained result. Now why is the <s>śīghrocca-karṇa</s> (fast-apogee hypotenuse) not iterated? Because the iteration operation is inapplicable [to it].

body.text:
atha atra idam praṣṭavyam ã kakṣyāmaṇḍalasya yathā svayojanakarṇaḥ vyāsārdhaḥ, tat ca svaliptābhiḥ mīyamānaḥ vasvagnivedarāmāḥ [3438], pratimaṇḍalasya api etat eva vyāsārdham iti etat | kakṣyāmaṇḍalotpannajyāphalaliptābhiḥ trairāśikābhāvaḥ, kakṣyāpratimaṇḍalayoḥ tulyavyāsārdhatvāt | atha manyate ã tatkālotpannabhujākoṭiniṣpannakarṇaḥ vyāsārdham pratimaṇḍalasya | tena trairāśikopapattiḥ | evam tarhi na kakṣyāmaṇḍalatulyam pratimaṇḍalam
iti | atra ucyate ã caturthapadādau kakṣyāpratimaṇḍale tulye | tena kakṣyāpratimaṇḍalayoḥ tulyam vyāsārdham | tataḥ prabhṛti pratimaṇḍalavyāsārdham [krameṇa upacīyate] | evam krameṇa upacīyamānam uccatulyagrahe svoccavṛttaviṣkambhārdham upacitam bhavati | tat eva prathamapadādau prabhṛti utkrameṇa apacīyamānam prathamapadānte vyāsārdham eva bhavati | evam krameṇa apacīyamānam dvitīyapadānte uccavṛttaviṣkambhārdham apacitam bhavati | tṛtīye
[padānte] ca utkrameṇa upacīyamānam iti etat kakṣyāmaṇḍalavyāsārdham eva | grahasya uccanīcagatikramāt upacayāpacayātmakam bhavati iti ataḥ pratimaṇḍalasya upadeśaḥ | ghanabhūmadhyāt eva grahasya uccanīcaparijñānam iti ataḥ vyāsārdham eva koṭiphalena upacīyate apacīyate vā | atha yadi pratimaṇḍalamadhyāt vyāsārdhasya vṛddhihrāsau syātām | tadā tṛtīyam maṇḍalam parikalpayitavyam syāt | ghanabhūmadhyāt karṇasya upacayāpacayau, tena tatkarṇena
vyastatrairāśikopapattiḥ iti | etat gaṇitanyāyasiddham eva |
body.translated_text: Now, here this is to be asked: Just as the semi-diameter of the orbit-circle (<s>kakṣyāmaṇḍala</s>) is its own <s>yojana</s>-hypotenuse, and that, measured in its own arc-minutes, is <s>Vasu-Agni-Veda-Rāma</s> [= 3438], and the semi-diameter of the eccentric circle (<s>pratimaṇḍala</s>) is also the same — [how does this work?] Since the orbit-circle-derived sine-result arc-minutes [are used], there is no rule of three, because the orbit-circle and eccentric circle have equal semi-diameters. Now, one may think: the hypotenuse produced from the <s>bhujā</s> (base) and <s>koṭi</s> (perpendicular) generated at that time is the semi-diameter of the eccentric circle; hence the justification of the rule of three. If so, then the eccentric circle is not equal to the orbit-circle. To this it is said: at the beginning of the fourth quadrant, the orbit-circle and eccentric circle are equal. Therefore, the semi-diameters of the orbit-circle and eccentric circle are equal. From that point onward, the semi-diameter of the eccentric circle [progressively] increases. Thus progressively increasing, when the planet coincides with its apogee, it has increased by the semi-diameter of the apogee-perigee epicycle (<s>uccavṛtta</s>). That same [semi-diameter], from the beginning of the first quadrant onward, decreases in reverse order, and at the end of the first quadrant becomes equal to the semi-diameter itself. Thus progressively decreasing, at the end of the second quadrant it has decreased by the semi-diameter of the apogee-epicycle. And in the third [quadrant], increasing in reverse order — this is indeed the semi-diameter of the orbit-circle. Due to the planet's progression through apogee and perigee, [the semi-diameter] undergoes increase and decrease — hence the instruction about the eccentric circle. Since the knowledge of apogee and perigee of the planet is from the center of the solid Earth itself, it is the semi-diameter itself that is increased or decreased by the <s>koṭiphala</s> (perpendicular-result). Now, if the increase and decrease of the semi-diameter were from the center of the eccentric circle, then a third circle would have to be postulated. [But] the increase and decrease of the hypotenuse are from the center of the solid Earth; therefore, by that hypotenuse, the justification of the inverse rule of three [follows]. This is established by mathematical reasoning itself.

body.text:
śanigurukujeṣu | śaniḥ ca guruḥ ca kujaḥ ca śanigurukujāḥ | ataḥ teṣu śanigurukujeṣu mandāt mandoccāt prabhṛti ya[t phalam upapadyate] tat ardham ṛṇam dhanam vā bhavati | pūrve pūrvakarmaṇi, mandāt prabhṛti iti | śīghrāt api ca yat phalam tat teṣu ardham kriyate prathame śīghrakarmaṇi | anyatra dvitīyakarmaṇi mandaśīghrayoḥ sakalaphalam iti arthāt avasīyate | mandaśīghraphalāni kāṣṭhāni ṛṇam dhanam vā parikalpyate | yataḥ kāṣṭhena grahaḥ
bhramati | tat phalam kva ṛṇam kva vā dhanam iti ã śanigurukujeṣu | atra śanigurukujāḥ madhyamāḥ eva parigṛhyante | kutaḥ? madhyamasya sphuṭīkaraṇopāyatvāt | tadā hi ete sphuṭībhavanti |
body.translated_text: For <s>Śani</s> (Saturn), <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter), and <s>Kuja</s> (Mars): <s>Śani</s> and <s>Guru</s> and <s>Kuja</s> are '<s>Śanigurukujāḥ</s>.' Therefore, for these — <s>Śani</s>, <s>Guru</s>, and <s>Kuja</s> — from the <s>manda</s> (slow [apogee]), the result that is obtained from the slow apogee — half of that becomes subtractive or additive. 'Previously, in the prior operation' — from the slow [apogee] onward. From the <s>śīghra</s> (fast [apogee]) too, whatever result [is obtained], half of that is applied in the first <s>śīghra</s>-operation for them. In the other — the second — operation of both <s>manda</s> and <s>śīghra</s>, the full result [is used]: this is understood from the meaning. The <s>manda</s> and <s>śīghra</s> results as arcs are applied as subtractive or additive, since the planet traverses by the arc. Where is that result subtractive and where additive? For <s>Śani</s>, <s>Guru</s>, and <s>Kuja</s>: here, the mean [positions] of <s>Śani</s>, <s>Guru</s>, and <s>Kuja</s> are taken. Why? Because the mean [position] is the basis for the true-position computation. Then indeed do they become true.

body.text:
yadi etat karma śanigurukujeṣu madhyameṣu kriyate, mandoccaphalārdhena madhyame ṛṇadhane kṛte tasya ṛṇadhanīkṛtasya madhyamatvam hīyate | [ataḥ] śīghroccaphalacāpārdhasya avikṛtamadhyame dhanarṇe prāpnutaḥJ| na etat asti | mandoccaphalacāpārdhadhanarṇīkṛtaḥ eva bhaviṣyati | kutaḥ? "ekadeśavikṛtam ananyavat bhavati" iti [aṣṭādhyāyī, 4.1.83 pātañjalamahābhāṣyam] ekadeśavikṛtaḥ api madhyaḥ eva | yathā devakattaḥ svalaṅkṛtaḥ api svam ākhyānam
na jahāti, na ca karṇanāsāvacchedena api, evam atra api, dve karmaṇī tatra tatra eva madhyame kriyete | athavā prathamamadhyamāt mandoccāyātam phalārdham madhyamotpannatvāt madhyame kriyate | yat punar śīghroccāyātam sakṛtsaṃskṛtāt phalārdham tat sakṛtsaṃskṛtāyātam eva iti kṛtvā sakṛtsaṃskṛtaḥ eva kriyate | tasmāt dvikarmasaṃsiddhāt mandoccaphalam tat sakalam eva madhyame grahe kriyate | sa sphuṭamadhyamaḥ bhavati |
body.translated_text: If this operation is performed on the mean [positions] of <s>Śani</s>, <s>Guru</s>, and <s>Kuja</s>, when half the <s>mandocca</s>-result is applied as additive or subtractive to the mean, the mean-ness of that [modified value] is lost. [Therefore,] the half of the <s>śīghrocca</s>-result-arc should be applied as additive or subtractive to the unmodified mean. This is not so. It will be [applied to] the value already modified by the half <s>mandocca</s>-result-arc as additive or subtractive. Why? Because 'that which is modified in one part remains the same [in kind]' [<s>Aṣṭādhyāyī</s> 4.1.83, <s>Patañjala Mahābhāṣya</s>] — even when modified in one part, it is still a mean [planet]. Just as <s>Devadatta</s>, even when adorned, does not abandon his own name, nor even when his ears or nose are cut off — so here too, the two operations are performed on the mean [planet] in each case. Alternatively, the half-result derived from the <s>mandocca</s> in the first [operation] is applied to the mean since it arises from the mean. But the half-result derived from the <s>śīghrocca</s> in the once-corrected [value] — since it arises from the once-corrected [value] — is applied to the once-corrected [value] itself. Therefore, from the twice-corrected [value], the <s>mandocca</s>-result — that full result itself — is applied to the mean planet. That becomes the true mean (<s>sphuṭamadhyama</s>).

body.text:
atha idam praṣṭavyam ã yat etat dvikarmasiddhamandoccāyātam tat dvikarmasaṃsiddhe eva kasmāt na kriyate | ucyate ã " mandoccāt sphuṭamadhyāḥ" [kālakriyāí, 23] iti madhyame kriyate | nanu ca dvikarmasiddhaḥ api madhyamaḥ eva | kutaḥ? "ekadeśavikṛtam ananyavat bhavati" iti vacanāt | evam tarhi siddhe, punar sphuṭamadhyamagrahaṇam kurvan ācāryaḥ jñāpayati avikṛtamadhyaḥ iti | anyathā hi sphuṭamadhyamagrahaṇam atiricyate | tasmāt dvitīyaphalam
mandoccāyātam tat sakalam eva madhyame grahe kriyate |
body.translated_text: Now this is to be asked: that which is the <s>mandocca</s>-derived [result] from the twice-corrected [value] — why is it not applied to the twice-corrected [value] itself? It is said: because '[from the] <s>mandocca</s>, [the planets become] true means' [<s>Kālakriyā</s> 23] — it is applied to the mean. But is not the twice-corrected [value] also a mean? Why? Because 'that which is modified in one part remains the same [in kind]' — by this maxim. If so, then since it is established [that the twice-corrected is also mean], by making the additional specification 'true mean' (<s>sphuṭamadhyama</s>), the master indicates [that it should be applied to] the unmodified mean. Otherwise, the word 'true mean' (<s>sphuṭamadhyama</s>) would be redundant. Therefore, the second result derived from the <s>mandocca</s> — that full result itself — is applied to the mean planet.

body.text: śīghroccāt ca sphuṭāḥ jñeyāḥ iti | sa evaṃkṛte sphuṭamadhyamaḥ śīghroccakarmaṇā sphuṭaḥ bhavati iti sphuṭamadhyame śīghroccaphaladhanuḥ sakalam kriyate, sphuṭaḥ bhavati |
body.translated_text: 'And from the <s>śīghrocca</s>, [the planets] are to be known as true' — when this is done, the true mean (<s>sphuṭamadhyama</s>), [corrected] by the <s>śīghrocca</s> operation, becomes true (<s>sphuṭa</s>). Thus, the full <s>śīghrocca</s>-result arc is applied to the true mean, [and the planet] becomes true.

body.text:
ṛṇadhanayuktipradarśanārtham vyāsārdhatulyena karkaṭakena samāyāmavanau samavṛttamaṇḍalam ālikhya mātṛpitṛrekhām kuryāt | tat kakṣyāmaṇḍalam rāśijyārekhāviracitam | tanmaṇḍalakendrāt yāvatyaḥ abhīṣṭagrahāntyaphalaliptāḥ tāvati antare ca dakṣiṇena kendram kṛtvā vyāsārdhatulyena eva karkaṭakena tathā eva samavṛttamaṇḍalam ālikhet | tat pratimaṇḍalam | [kakṣyā]maṇḍalāt yāvadbhiḥ pratimaṇḍalam niṣkrāntam tāvatā vyāsārdhena
kakṣyāmaṇḍaladakṣiṇottararekhāsaṃpāte kendram kṛtvā ubhayatra vṛttadvayam ālikhya[te | te nīcocca]vṛtte | tayoḥ yathā kakṣyāmaṇḍale rāśijyāvikalpaḥ tathā karaṇīyam | prathamacaturthayoḥ padayoḥ kakṣyāmaṇḍalāt uparisthitatvāt pratimaṇḍalasya vyāsārdhe koṭisādhanam prakṣipya karṇaḥ kṛtaḥ, tāvat pramāṇam sūtram [pratimaṇḍalaparidhim] yatra spṛśati tatra sthāne sphuṭaḥ grahaḥ | kakṣyāmaṇḍalajyā ca tasmāt purataḥ iti arthaḥ | prathamacaturthayoḥ padayoḥ
tat utpannam phalam madhyamagrahāt apacīyate | dvitīyatṛtīyayoḥ padayoḥ kakṣyāmaṇḍalāt adhovyavasthitatvāt pratimaṇḍalasya, vyāsārdhāt koṭisādhanam apanīya kṛtaḥ karṇaḥ, tāvatpramāṇam sūtram kakṣyāmaṇḍalamadhyāt pratimaṇḍalaparidhim yatra spṛśati tatra sphuṭaḥ grahaḥ | sa ca kakṣyāmaṇḍalajyāpradeśāt purataḥ avatiṣṭhate | tena tat utpannam phalam dvitīyatṛtīyayoḥ padayoḥ madhyamagrahāt upacīyate |
body.translated_text: For the purpose of demonstrating the rationale of additive and subtractive [corrections]: Draw a uniform circle on a level surface using a compass of radius equal to the semi-diameter, and draw the north-south line (<s>mātṛpitṛrekhā</s>). This is the orbit-circle (<s>kakṣyāmaṇḍala</s>), marked with sign-sine lines. From the center of that circle, at a distance equal to however many arc-minutes constitute the desired planet's maximum epicyclic result (<s>antyaphala</s>), make a center to the south, and with a compass of the same semi-diameter, draw a uniform circle in the same manner. This is the eccentric circle (<s>pratimaṇḍala</s>). By as much as the eccentric circle extends beyond the orbit-circle, with that much as the semi-diameter, at the intersection of the orbit-circle's north-south line, make a center and draw two circles on both sides. These are the perigee-apogee epicycles (<s>nīcoccavṛtte</s>). Just as the sign-sine analysis [applies] on the orbit-circle, so should it be done on them. In the first and fourth quadrants, since the eccentric circle is situated above the orbit-circle, the <s>koṭi</s>-result (<s>koṭisādhana</s>) is added to the semi-diameter, the hypotenuse is computed, and a thread of that length [extended from the orbit-circle center] touches the eccentric circle at a certain point — that point is where the true planet is. And the orbit-circle sine is ahead of that point — this is the meaning. In the first and fourth quadrants, the result thus produced is subtracted from the mean planet. In the second and third quadrants, since the eccentric circle is situated below the orbit-circle, the <s>koṭi</s>-result is subtracted from the semi-diameter, the hypotenuse is computed, and a thread of that length from the orbit-circle center touches the eccentric circle at a certain point — there the true planet is. And it stands ahead of the orbit-circle sine position. Therefore, the result produced in the second and third quadrants is added to the mean planet.

body.text:
śīghrocce punar yeṣām kṣayadhanadhanakṣayāḥ syuḥ mandoccāt evam eva śīghroccāt iti ayam pāṭhaḥ teṣām iyam ṛṇadhanopapattiḥ | yeṣām punar vyatyayena śīghroccāt iti ayam pāṭhaḥ teṣām iyam eva upapattiḥ viparītā | katham? pratimaṇḍale sphuṭaḥ ca grahaḥ, madhyamaḥ ca śīghroccaparikalpanāya kakṣyāmaṇḍale | punar kendrajyā tena prathamacaturthayoḥ padayoḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ sthitatvāt madhyamasya kendrajyāgrahasya ānīyamānasya kendrajyotpannam
phalam dhanam bhavati puraḥsthitatvāt kendrajyāgrahasya, dvitīyatṛtīyayoḥ padayoḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ sthitatvāt kendrajyāgrahasya tat phalam apanīyate | ataḥ evam mandaśīghrayoḥ parasparaviruddhatvāt upapatteḥ, ācāryeṇa paramārthasphuṭagrahapradeśaḥ bhūtārāgrahavivarapramāṇapradeśaḥ darśitaḥ | tena yāvat bhūtārāgrahavivarapramāṇam sūtram kakṣyāmaṇḍalamadhyāt pratimaṇḍalaparidhim padavibhāgena prasāritam yatra spṛśati, tatra sphuṭaḥ grahaḥ |
body.translated_text: Regarding the <s>śīghrocca</s> (fast apogee) — for those [texts] whose reading has 'subtractive-additive-additive-subtractive' from the <s>mandocca</s> and 'likewise from the <s>śīghrocca</s>' — for them, this is the rationale of additive and subtractive. But for those whose reading is 'in reverse from the <s>śīghrocca</s>' — for them, this very same rationale is reversed. How? The true planet is on the eccentric circle, and the mean planet on the orbit-circle for the purpose of the <s>śīghra</s> postulation. Further, the anomaly-sine: in the first and fourth quadrants, since the mean stands behind, when the anomaly-sine planet is being derived, the result produced from the anomaly-sine becomes additive — because the anomaly-sine planet stands ahead; in the second and third quadrants, since the anomaly-sine planet stands behind, that result is subtracted. Therefore, since the rationale of the <s>manda</s> and <s>śīghra</s> [corrections] is mutually opposite, the master has shown the position of the absolutely true planet — the position corresponding to the distance-measure between the Earth-star and the planet. By that [distance-measure], a thread of the length equal to the Earth-star-planet distance, extended from the orbit-circle center to the eccentric-circle circumference according to the quadrant-division, touches [the eccentric circle] at the point where the true planet is.

body.text:
anye punar anyathā paṭhanti ã śanigurukujeṣu mande ardham ṛṇam dhanam bhavati pūrvam iti | mande mandocce ardham phalasya ṛṇam dhanam, yadi tat grahe ṛṇam dhanam tadā tat mandocce dhanam ṛṇam iti arthāt avasīyate | tatra kiyat tat phalam mandocce ṛṇam sat dhanam bhavati, dhanam sat ṛṇam bhavati iti ucyate ã śīghroccaphalam yasmāt mandoccaphalam ca phaladvayam etat | tayoḥ mandoccam ādhāraḥ | phaladvayam ādheyaḥ | ataḥ śīghroccaphalam
kriyate | karmacatuṣṭayagrahaṇāt tat utpannam ca phalam tatra eva | tat yathā ã prāg eva śīghraphalam ānīya tat ardham ṛṇam dhanam vā mandocce kṛtvā tat mandāyātam ca tena phaladvayasaṃskṛtena mandoccena saṃskṛtaḥ sa sphuṭamadhyaḥ grahaḥ bhavati | sa śīghrakarmaṇā sphuṭaḥ iti prakriyāntaram etat || 22 ||
body.translated_text: Others, however, read differently: 'For <s>Śani</s> (Saturn), <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter), and <s>Kuja</s> (Mars), in the <s>manda</s> [correction], half is subtractive [or] additive — previously.' In the <s>manda</s> (slow apogee), half of the result is subtractive or additive — if that [half-result] is subtractive from the planet, then it is additive to the <s>mandocca</s>, and vice versa: this is understood from the meaning. There, how much of that result, being subtractive to the <s>mandocca</s>, becomes additive, and being additive, becomes subtractive? It is said: The <s>śīghrocca</s>-result and the <s>mandocca</s>-result — these are the two results. Of these, the <s>mandocca</s> is the base (<s>ādhāra</s>) and the two results are the superimposed (<s>ādheya</s>). Therefore, the <s>śīghrocca</s>-result is applied. Due to the four-fold operation, the result produced [is applied] there itself. Namely: first deriving the <s>śīghra</s>-result, half of it is applied as subtractive or additive to the <s>mandocca</s>; that <s>manda</s>-derived [result] too, together with the two-result-corrected <s>mandocca</s> — the [mean planet] corrected by that is the true mean (<s>sphuṭamadhya</s>) planet. That, by the <s>śīghra</s>-operation, becomes true — this is an alternative procedure. // 22 //

body.text: prakārāntareṇa śanigurukujasphuṭīkaraṇam
body.translated_text: True-position computation of <s>Śani</s>, <s>Guru</s>, and <s>Kuja</s> by an alternative method

body.text: grahāṇām sphuṭīkaraṇaprakārāntaram āha ã
body.translated_text: He states an alternative method for the true-position computation of planets:

children.text: mandoccāt śīghroccāt ardham ṛṇam dhanam graheṣu mandeṣu |
children.translated_text: From the <s>mandocca</s> (slow apogee), from the <s>śīghrocca</s> (fast apogee), half is subtractive [or] additive to the planets, [which are] slow [apogee planets];

children.text: mandoccāt sphuṭamadhyāḥ śīghroccāt ca sphuṭāḥ jñeyāḥ || 23 ||
children.translated_text: from the <s>mandocca</s>, [the planets become] true means (<s>sphuṭamadhya</s>); and from the <s>śīghrocca</s>, [they] are to be known as true. // 23 //

body.text: mandoccāt yat phalam āyātam tasya cāpārdham ṛṇam dhanam vā graheṣu ṛṇam dhanam [mandeṣu vā kartavyam] | evam tarhi cakāraḥ kartavyaḥ | cakāreṇa vinā graheṣu mandeṣu ca iti cārthaḥ na labhyate | na cakāraḥ kartavyaḥ | antareṇa api cakāram cārthaḥ avagamyate | [katham?] evam ã
body.translated_text: The result derived from the <s>mandocca</s> — half its arc is subtractive or additive to the planets, or subtractive or additive [to the slow apogee planets]. If so, then a conjunction 'and' (<s>ca</s>) should be used. Without the conjunction, the meaning 'to the planets and to the slow ones' cannot be obtained. The conjunction is not needed. Even without the conjunction, the conjunctive meaning is understood. [How?] Thus:

body.text: bāle vṛddhe kṣate kṣīṇe kṣīram yuktyā prayojayet |
body.translated_text: For a child, an old person, an injured one, or a weakened one, milk should be administered judiciously.

body.text: iti atra cakāreṇa vinā cārthasya avagamanāt | evam ayam api | "sva"mandeṣu api vaktavyam, yena sveṣu madhyameṣu sveṣu ca mandeṣu kriyate | "sva"śabdaḥ api na kartavyaḥ | svasya grahasya yaḥ madhyamaḥ svasya ca yat mandam tatra eva karmasiddheḥ | yathā "mātari vaktavyam pitari śuśrūṣitavyam" iti | na ca tatra ucyate ã "svasyām mātari svasmin vā pitari" iti | evam atra api iti |
body.translated_text: Thus here, the meaning of 'and' (<s>ca</s>) is understood even without the particle <s>ca</s>. So too is this [case]. It should also be stated '[applied to] one's own <s>manda</s> (slow apogee),' by which [the operation] is performed on one's own mean [positions] and one's own slow [apogees]. The word '<s>sva</s>' (one's own) need not even be used, since the operation is accomplished with the mean of one's own planet and the slow [apogee] of one's own [planet]. Just as [in the expression] 'one should speak to [one's] mother, one should serve [one's] father' — and there one does not say 'to one's own mother or one's own father.' So too here.

body.text: atha yat etat mandoccāyātam phalārdham tat kṣayadhanakrameṇa madhye grahe dhanam ṛṇam vā kriyate | mande punar katham kriyate, mandasya ṛṇadhanakramasya anabhidhānāt? ucyate ã mandoccam sarvadā eva grahasya ṛṇabhūtam | tatra yat grahasya ṛṇam tat mandocce prakṣipyate, ṛṇabhūtatvāt | yat grahe dhanabhūtam tat mandoccāt apanīyate, mandoccasya ṛṇabhūtatvāt eva | ayam ca gaṇitanyāyaḥ ã
body.translated_text: Now, this half-result (<s>phalārdha</s>) derived from the <s>mandocca</s> (slow apogee) is applied as additive or subtractive to the mean planet in the order of subtraction and addition. But how is it applied to the <s>manda</s> (slow apogee), since the order of subtraction and addition for the <s>manda</s> has not been stated? It is said: the <s>mandocca</s> is always subtractive with respect to the planet. Therefore, what is subtractive for the planet is added to the <s>mandocca</s>, because it is of the nature of subtraction. What is additive to the planet is subtracted from the <s>mandocca</s>, precisely because the <s>mandocca</s> is of subtractive nature. And this is the mathematical principle:

body.text: ṛṇa[ṛṇayoḥ dhana]dhanayoḥ saṃkṣepaḥ ṛṇadhanayoḥ ca viśeṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: The sum [is taken] of two negatives or two positives, and the difference of a negative and a positive.

body.text: iti | tasmāt anena krameṇa mandocce phalārdhasya upacayāpacayau bhavataḥ | śīghroccāt ca yat phalārdham tat api evam eva grahavaiparītyena mande dhanam ṛṇam vā kriyate | graheṣu punar prayojanābhāvāt na kriyate |
body.translated_text: Thus. Therefore, by this procedure, the increase and decrease of the half-result occur at the <s>mandocca</s> (slow apogee). And the half-result derived from the <s>śīghrocca</s> (fast apogee) — that too, in exactly the same way, in reverse order with respect to the planet, is applied as additive or subtractive to the <s>manda</s>. But it is not applied to the planets, since there is no purpose [for doing so].

body.text:
mandoccāt | mandoccaśīghroccaphalārdhena saṃskṛtam mandoccam parigṛhyate | kutaḥ? karmadvayavṛttau mandanirdeśāt | tena tādṛgvidhena mandena madhyamāt viśodhitena yat phalam āyātam tat sakalam madhyeṣu ṛṇam dhanam vā kriyate | sphuṭamadhyāḥ | [madhyamasya] sphuṭasya antarvartitvāt [sphuṭāḥ ye na, na avikṛteṣu] madhyameṣu phalasya karaṇāt madhyamāḥJ| athavā sphuṭasya madhyamāḥ sphuṭamadhyamāḥ | ekena karmaṇā niṣpannā yena
dvitīyam karmāntaram apekṣante | śīghroccāt ca sphuṭāḥ jñeyāḥ | śīghroccāt āyātam phalam tena saṃskṛtāḥ sphuṭāḥ | cakāraḥ phalayoḥ samuccayam abhidhatte | jñeyāḥ avagantavyāḥ boddhavyāḥ iti yāvat || 23 ||
body.translated_text: 'From the <s>mandocca</s>.' The <s>mandocca</s> corrected by the half-results of the <s>mandocca</s> and <s>śīghrocca</s> is adopted. Why? Because in the procedure involving both operations, the <s>manda</s> is specified. With that such <s>manda</s>, subtracted from the mean [planet], the result obtained is applied in full as subtractive or additive to the mean [planets]. [These are] the corrected mean positions (<s>sphuṭamadhya</s>). Since [they are] intermediate between the mean and true [positions] — they are not true, [and since the result] is not applied to the unmodified mean positions — [they are called] mean. Alternatively, the mean of the true [planet] is <s>sphuṭamadhyama</s> (corrected mean). Having been produced by one operation, they require a second, different operation. 'And the true [positions] are to be known from the <s>śīghrocca</s>' — the result derived from the <s>śīghrocca</s>, those corrected by it are the true [positions]. The particle '<s>ca</s>' indicates the combination of both results. '<s>Jñeyāḥ</s>' means 'to be known, to be understood.' || 23 ||

body.text: bhṛgubudhayoḥ sphuṭīkaraṇam
body.translated_text: True position computation for <s>Bhṛgu</s> (Venus) and <s>Budha</s> (Mercury)

body.text: bhṛgubudhayoḥ karma āha ã
body.translated_text: He states the procedure for <s>Bhṛgu</s> (Venus) and <s>Budha</s> (Mercury):

children.text: śīghroccāt ardhonam kartavyam ṛṇam dhanam svamandocce |
children.translated_text: Half [the result] from the <s>śīghrocca</s> (fast apogee) is to be subtracted, [and applied as] subtractive or additive to one's own <s>mandocca</s> (slow apogee);

children.text: sphuṭamadhyau tu bhṛgubudhau siddhāt mandāt sphuṭau bhavataḥ || 24 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhṛgu</s> (Venus) and <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) become corrected-mean (<s>sphuṭamadhya</s>), and from the established <s>manda</s>, they become true (<s>sphuṭa</s>). || 24 ||

body.text:
śīghroccāt iti prāk śīghroccaniṣpannam phalam gṛhyate | tat eva śīghroccaphalam agre | tatra tat ardhonam ardham iti arthaḥ | ṛṇadhanam kartavyam | yadi grahe ṛṇam tadā dhanam kartavyam | dhanasya ṛṇam kartavyam iti arthāt avasīyate | kva iti āha ã svamandocce | svakīyam mandoccam svamandoccam, tasmin svamandocce | sphuṭamadhyau bhṛgubudhau bhavataḥ | katham? siddhāt mandāt | yat eva śīghroccaphalārdhena saṃskṛtam mandoccam tat siddham
iti abhidhīyate | tasmāt siddhāt mandāt sphuṭamadhyau bhavataḥ | etat uktam bhavati ã yat eta[t siddhamandam tat madhyama]grahāt viśodhya śeṣaphalasya ca ṛṇadhanena tayoḥ bhṛgubudhayoḥ madhyau sphuṭamadhyau bhavataḥ | "tu"-śabdāt "śīghroccāt ca sphuṭāḥ jñeyāḥ" [kālakriyāí, 23] iti etat kriyate || 24 ||
body.translated_text: 'From the <s>śīghrocca</s>' — the result previously produced from the <s>śīghrocca</s> operation is taken. That very <s>śīghrocca</s>-result [is used] further. There, '<s>ardhonam</s>' means 'half' is the meaning. It is to be applied as subtractive or additive. If it is subtractive for the planet, then it is to be made additive; the additive [for the planet] is to be made subtractive — this is understood from the meaning. Where? — he says: 'to one's own <s>mandocca</s>.' One's own <s>mandocca</s> is <s>svamandocca</s>; in that <s>svamandocca</s>. <s>Bhṛgu</s> (Venus) and <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) become corrected-mean (<s>sphuṭamadhya</s>). How? From the established <s>manda</s>. That very <s>mandocca</s> corrected by the half-result of the <s>śīghrocca</s> is called 'established' (<s>siddha</s>). From that established <s>manda</s>, they become corrected-mean. What is meant is this: that established <s>manda</s>, subtracted from the mean planet, and with the subtractive or additive [application] of the remaining result — for those two, <s>Bhṛgu</s> and <s>Budha</s>, [the positions] become the corrected-mean (<s>sphuṭamadhya</s>). By the word '<s>tu</s>' (but), the [procedure] 'and the true [positions] are to be known from the <s>śīghrocca</s>' [<s>Kālakriyā</s>, 23] is [then] performed. || 24 ||

body.text: bhūtārāgrahāntarālam
body.translated_text: The distance between the center of the Earth and the planet

body.text: bhūtārāgrahā
body.translated_text: For the purpose of deriving the measure of the distance between [the center of]

body.text: ntarālapramāṇānayanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: the Earth and the planet, he says:

children.translated_text: The distance between the center of the Earth and the planet (<s>bhūtārāgrahavivara</s>) is the product of one's own hypotenuses (<s>svakarṇa</s>) divided by the semi-diameter (<s>vyāsārdha</s>);

children.text: kakṣyāyām grahavegaḥ yaḥ bhavati sa mandanīcocce || 25 ||
children.translated_text: The velocity of the planet that obtains in the orbit (<s>kakṣyā</s>) is [the velocity] at the perigee and apogee of the slow epicycle (<s>mandanīcocca</s>). || 25 ||

body.text:
tārāgrahāṇām bhuvaḥ ca yat antaram tasya ānayanopāyaḥ ucyate | bhūtārāgrahavivaram bhuvaḥ tārāgrahasya ca yat antaram tat bhūtārāgrahavivaram bhavati iti vakṣyati | vyāsārdhahṛtaḥ svakarṇasaṃvargaḥ | vyāsārdham trijyā | trijyayā hṛtaḥ vyāsārdhahṛtaḥ | svakarṇayoḥ saṃvargaḥ svakarṇasaṃvargaḥ | etat uktam bhavati ã mandoccakarṇasya śīghroccakarṇasya ca yaḥ ghātaḥ saḥ svakarṇasaṃvargaḥ vyāsārdhahṛtaḥ | kakṣyāyām grahavegaḥ | tāvat ucchritāyām
[kakṣyāyām] grahasya yaḥ mandaśīghroccaphalajanitaḥ vegaḥ sa tasya bhūtārāgrahavivarasya agre bhavati iti | ataḥ eva bhūtārāgrahavivaram vikṣepānayane bhāgahāraḥ |
body.translated_text: The method for deriving the distance between the star-planets (<s>tārāgraha</s>) and the Earth is stated. The distance between the center of the Earth and the planet — the distance between the Earth and the star-planet is the <s>bhūtārāgrahavivara</s>, he will say. 'The product of one's own hypotenuses divided by the semi-diameter' — the semi-diameter is the <s>trijyā</s> (radius, R = 3438). Divided by the <s>trijyā</s> is '<s>vyāsārdhahṛta</s>.' The product of one's own hypotenuses is <s>svakarṇasaṃvarga</s>. What is meant is: the product of the <s>manda-karṇa</s> (slow hypotenuse) and the <s>śīghrocca-karṇa</s> (fast hypotenuse) is the '<s>svakarṇasaṃvarga</s>,' divided by the semi-diameter. 'The velocity of the planet in the orbit' — in the orbit of that extent, the velocity of the planet generated by the results of the <s>manda</s> and <s>śīghrocca</s> — that becomes [the velocity] for the <s>bhūtārāgrahavivara</s> (Earth-planet distance) further on. Therefore, the <s>bhūtārāgrahavivara</s> is the divisor in the computation of latitude (<s>vikṣepa</s>).

body.text:
apare āhuḥ ã na bhūtārāgrahavivaram bhāgahāraḥ | kaḥ tarhi? vyāsārdham | yasmāt etat atra trairāśikam ã yadi trijyayā svagrahābhihitavikṣepaḥ labhyate, anayā abhīṣṭagrahasvapātavivarāntarālāṃśajyayā bhujajyayā kim iti | na etat samyak avasīyate | yadi idam eva trairāśikam syāt, tadā nakṣatratārāgrahaśaśiyogāḥ sarvadā tasyām eva diśi tulyavikṣepavivarāḥ syuḥ, nakṣatratārāṇām uccanīcagatyasambhavāt | dṛśyante ca amī grahanakṣatrāṇām dūrāsanna[vaśāt]
bhedāṃśumardanasavyāpasavyayogagata[yaḥ | yadi vyāsārdha]m eva bhāgahāraḥ syāt tadā sarve eva tulyagatayaḥ syuḥ | bhūtārāgrahavivaram | bhūtārāgrahavivaravaśāt vikṣepaḥ alpaḥ mahān ca nakṣatratārāgrahayogeṣu labhyate | [alpe vā] mahadvikṣepe dakṣiṇottaradigvaśāt niyatavikṣepāntaradiśaḥ yogāḥ upapadyante | tasmāt bhūtārāgrahavivaram eva bhāgahāraḥ | etat api karma trairāśikadvayam | katham? yadi vyāsārdhatulyayā pātāntarabhujajyayā yathāsvam vikṣepaḥ
alpaḥ mahān ca labhyate, tadā ana[yā bhuja]jyayā pātāntarotpannayā kaḥ iti vikṣepaḥ labhyate | [ataḥ] punar api vyastatrairāśikam ã yadi ayam vikṣepaḥ kakṣyāmaṇḍale vyāsārdhaviṣkambhe labhyate, tadā paramārthapratimaṇḍale bhūtārāgrahavivaraviṣkambhārdhe kiyān iti | pūrvatrairāśike vyāsārdham bhāgahāraḥ āsīt, tat eva dvitīyatrairāśike vyastatvāt guṇakāraḥ | ataḥ guṇakārabhāgahārayoḥ naṣṭayoḥ, pātāntarabhujajyāyāḥ vikṣepaḥ guṇakāraḥ, bhūtārāgrahavivaram
bhāgahāraḥ, phalam iṣṭagrahasya vikṣepaḥ | evam iṣṭagrahayoḥ vikṣepāvabhinnadikkau viśiṣyate, yasmāt apakramamaṇḍalāt tau pravṛttau | tataḥ tadviśeṣatulyam tayoḥ antaram bhavati, tatra api tayoḥ ūnādhikavikṣepavaśāt parasparāpekṣayā [tayoḥ yāmyottaradiktvam] | bhinnadikkau vikṣepau yojyate | yasmāt ekaḥ apakramamaṇḍalāt dakṣiṇena aparaḥ uttareṇa, tasmāt tadantaram [vikṣepayoga]pramāṇam bhavati | vikṣepaliptāntaracaturbhāgaḥ aṅgulapramāṇam vācyam
| yadā punar antaraliptāḥ na syuḥ, alpāḥ vā [syuḥ] tadā tayoḥ anyonyāśeṣāt chādanam ekadeśāt chādanam vā [bhavati] | tatra grahaṇavat iṣṭagrahasaṃparkārdhatadvikṣepa[viśleṣeṇa yogena vā] sthityardhanāḍikānayanam |
body.translated_text: Others say: the <s>bhūtārāgrahavivara</s> (Earth-planet distance) is not the divisor. What then? The semi-diameter (<s>vyāsārdha</s>). Because the rule of three (<s>trairāśika</s>) here is: if by the <s>trijyā</s> (radius) the stated latitude of the planet is obtained, then by this sine of the arc-distance between the desired planet and its own node, what [is obtained]? This is not correctly understood. If this were the only rule of three, then in the conjunctions of <s>nakṣatra</s>-stars and planets with the Moon, the latitude-differences would always be equal in that same direction, since <s>nakṣatra</s>-stars cannot have apogee-perigee motion. But these are observed — separations, ray-occultations, direct and reverse conjunctions of planets and <s>nakṣatras</s> due to far and near [distances]. If the semi-diameter alone were the divisor, then all would have equal motions. [But using] the <s>bhūtārāgrahavivara</s> — due to the Earth-planet distance, the latitude obtained in the conjunctions of <s>nakṣatra</s>-stars and planets is small or large. With either small or large latitude, conjunctions with definite latitude-differences in the north-south direction are established due to direction. Therefore, the <s>bhūtārāgrahavivara</s> alone is the divisor. This procedure also involves two rules of three. How? If by the sine of the node-distance equal to the semi-diameter, the latitude — whether small or large — is obtained respectively, then by this sine produced from the node-distance, what latitude is obtained? [Then] again an inverse rule of three: if this latitude is obtained in the orbital circle with the semi-diameter as width, then in the true eccentric circle with the <s>bhūtārāgrahavivara</s> as semi-width, how much? In the first rule of three, the semi-diameter was the divisor; that very [semi-diameter] in the second rule of three, being inverse, becomes the multiplier. Therefore, with multiplier and divisor cancelled, the sine of the node-distance times the latitude is the multiplier, and the <s>bhūtārāgrahavivara</s> is the divisor; the result is the latitude of the desired planet. Thus, the latitudes of the two desired planets — if in the same direction — are differentiated, since both proceed from the ecliptic (<s>apakramamaṇḍala</s>). Then the difference of those equals the separation between them; and there too, due to their greater or lesser latitude, their relative north-south direction [is determined]. If the latitudes are in opposite directions, they are added, since one is south and the other north of the ecliptic; therefore their separation equals the sum of the latitudes. One-quarter of the latitude-difference in minutes is to be stated as the measure in <s>aṅgulas</s> (finger-widths). When, however, there are no minutes of separation, or [they are] few, then there is complete or partial occultation of one by the other. There, as in an eclipse, the half-duration in <s>nāḍikās</s> is derived from the half-sum of the discs of the desired planets and the difference or sum of their latitudes.

body.text: tārāgrahāṇām sphuṭayojanakarṇānayanam
body.translated_text: Computation of the true <s>yojana</s>-hypotenuse of the star-planets

body.text:
atha nakṣatratārāgrahayogeṣu natilambanaparijñānārtham idam karma kriyate | "śaśiṅañaṇanamāṃśakāḥ" [gītikāí, 7] iti atra śaśiyojanakarṇaḥ ṅādibhiḥ guṇitaḥ śukrādīnām bhāgahārāḥ bhavanti iti vyākhyātam | tena śaśiyojanakarṇaḥ pañcabhiḥ guṇitaḥ śukrasya yojanakarṇaḥ bhavati daśabhiḥ guroḥ, pañcadaśabhiḥ budhasya, viṃśatyā śaneḥ, pañcaviṃśatyā aṅgārakasya | yadi evam tarhi grahāṇām kakṣyābhidhānam virudhyate | na eṣaḥ doṣaḥ | tāvat kakṣyāsthāḥ
eva grahāḥ, atra punar ṅādiguṇakāraiḥ dṛṣṭiparikarma kriyate iti | ayam yojanakarṇaḥ bhūtārāgrahavivaraguṇitaḥ vyāsārdhahṛtaḥ sphuṭaḥ bhavati | etat api trairāśikam ã yadi vyāsārdhaliptābhiḥ etāvanti yojanāni labhyante bhūtārāgrahavivaraliptābhiḥ kiyanti iti, athavā trairāśikadvayaikīkaraṇena abhīṣṭagrahasphuṭayojanakarṇaḥ ānīyate | katham? bhūtārāgrahavivarānayane vyāsārdham bhāgahāraḥ āsīt, iha ca bhūtārāgrahavivarasvamadhyamayojanakarṇābhyāsasya
vyāsārdham eva bhāgahāraḥ | ataḥ bhāgahārayoḥ saṃvargaḥ mandoccaśīghroccakarṇasvamadhyamayojanakarṇābhyāsasya bhāgahāraḥ | phalam sphuṭayojanakarṇaḥ | tayoḥ ayam arthaḥ sañjātaḥ ã mandaśīghra[karṇa]guṇitaḥ madhyamayojanakarṇaḥ vyāsārdhakṛtivibhaktaḥ sphuṭayojanakarṇaḥ bhavati | mandanīcocce mandasya mandoccasya ucce nīce ca ānītaḥ mandakarṇaḥ eva anena vidhinā sphuṭīkṛtaḥ iti |
body.translated_text: Now, this procedure is performed for the purpose of ascertaining the parallax in latitude (<s>nati</s>) and parallax in longitude (<s>lambana</s>) in the conjunctions of <s>nakṣatra</s>-stars and planets. As explained for '<s>śaśiṅañaṇanamāṃśakāḥ</s>' [<s>Gītikā</s>, 7]: the <s>yojana</s>-hypotenuse of the Moon, multiplied by the [values beginning with] <s>ṅa</s>, becomes the divisors for <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) and the others. Thus, the Moon's <s>yojana</s>-hypotenuse multiplied by five is the <s>yojana</s>-hypotenuse of <s>Śukra</s>; by ten, that of <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter); by fifteen, that of <s>Budha</s> (Mercury); by twenty, that of <s>Śani</s> (Saturn); by twenty-five, that of <s>Aṅgāraka</s> (Mars). If so, then the stated orbital sizes (<s>kakṣyā</s>) of the planets would be contradicted. There is no fault here. The planets are situated in those very orbits; but here, by the multipliers beginning with <s>ṅa</s>, the correction for apparent size (<s>dṛṣṭiparikarma</s>) is performed. This <s>yojana</s>-hypotenuse, multiplied by the <s>bhūtārāgrahavivara</s> (Earth-planet distance) and divided by the semi-diameter (<s>vyāsārdha</s>), becomes the true [<s>yojana</s>-hypotenuse]. This too is a rule of three: if by the semi-diameter in minutes, this many <s>yojanas</s> are obtained, then by the <s>bhūtārāgrahavivara</s> in minutes, how many? Alternatively, by combining two rules of three, the true <s>yojana</s>-hypotenuse of the desired planet is derived. How? In deriving the <s>bhūtārāgrahavivara</s>, the semi-diameter was the divisor; and here too, the semi-diameter is the divisor of the product of the <s>bhūtārāgrahavivara</s> and one's own mean <s>yojana</s>-hypotenuse. Therefore, the product of the two divisors [becomes] the divisor of the product of the <s>manda</s>-<s>śīghrocca</s>-hypotenuses and one's own mean <s>yojana</s>-hypotenuse. The result is the true <s>yojana</s>-hypotenuse. The meaning thus obtained is: the mean <s>yojana</s>-hypotenuse multiplied by the <s>manda</s>-<s>śīghra</s>-hypotenuses and divided by the square of the semi-diameter becomes the true <s>yojana</s>-hypotenuse. 'At the perigee and apogee of the slow epicycle (<s>mandanīcocca</s>)' — the <s>manda-karṇa</s> (slow hypotenuse) derived at the apogee and perigee of the <s>manda</s> [epicycle] is made true by this very method.

body.text: grahasphuṭīkaraṇe viśeṣaḥ
body.translated_text: Special considerations in the computation of true planetary positions

body.text:
atha vivasvaddhanarṇodayāstamayavaśāt sāmānyasarvagrahāṇām sphuṭagaṇitavidhiviśeṣaḥ abhidhāsyate | tat yathā ã savituḥ bhujāphalena ravyādibhuktayaḥ guṇitāḥ khakhaṣaḍghanena vibhajya āptakalā graheṣu bhujāphaladhanarṇavaśāt kriyate | tat vicāryate ã idam karma anupadiṣṭam katham avagamyate? na eṣaḥ doṣaḥ | upadiṣṭam eva etat ã "budhāhnyajārkodayāt ca laṅkāyām" [gītikāí, 4] iti | arkodayāvadheḥ gateḥ eteṣām pratipacchedau iti upadeśāt
arkaḥ hi sphuṭagaṇitāvagatagateḥ eva udayaśikharamadhyāste iti sphuṭasya arkasya udayaḥ parigṛhyate | sphuṭagatiḥ ca madhyamā eva svabhujāphalādiliptābhiḥ upacitāpacitā vā iti ataḥ bhujāphalaliptābhiḥ prāṇatulyābhiḥ trairāśikam kriyate ã yadi ahorātraprāṇaiḥ khakhaṣaḍghanatulyaiḥ vivasvadādisphuṭabhuktayaḥ labhyante, bhujāphalaliptābhiḥ prāṇatulyābhiḥ kim iti | āsām bhujāphalaliptānām prāṇatulyatvam iti | atra ucyate ã ravyudayāt eva jyotiścakrādeḥ api
udayādiḥ iti vyākhyātam | tena pravahākṣepāt madhyamaḥ sarvadā svabhujāphalena adhikaḥ ūnaḥ vā bhavati | yadā adhikaḥ tadā jyotiścakram bhujāphalaliptātulyam ravigatyā jīyate, [ūnaḥ cet bhujāphalaliptātulyam ravigatyā apacīyate] iti | anayā parikalpanayā jyotiścakrasambandhinyaḥ tadā bhujāphalaliptāḥ bhavanti, jyotiścakraliptāḥ prāṇāḥ ca tulyāḥ iti | ataḥ tāsām prā[ṇatulyabhujāphalaliptānām abhāvaḥ, ahargaṇāt āga]taḥ [sakalaḥ sūryaḥ] yadā svoccatulyaḥ tadā
eva udaye bhavati iti | anyathā tatra api bhujāntaraphalam kriyate eva | arkaḥ hi sphuṭagaṇi[tāvagateḥ eva udaya]śikharamadhyāste iti |
body.translated_text: Now, by reason of the Sun’s positive and negative [equation] and its rising and setting, the specific procedure for the true computation (<s>sphuṭagaṇita</s>) common to all planets will be explained. That is as follows: The daily motions of the Sun and other [planets] are multiplied by the Sun’s <s>bhujāphala</s> (equation of the anomaly), divided by <s>khakhaṣaḍghana</s> (21600), and the resulting minutes are applied positively or negatively to the planets according to the <s>bhujāphala</s>. This is examined: How is this unstated operation understood? There is no fault here. It has indeed been stated: ‘<s>Budha</s> and the half-night-born [planets] from the sunrise at <s>Laṅkā</s>’ [<s>Gītikā</s> 4]. Because it is taught that the motions of these are measured from the boundary of sunrise. For the Sun, established through true computation, rises at the horizon-peak — thus the rising of the true Sun is adopted. And the true motion is simply the mean [motion] increased or decreased by the minutes of its own <s>bhujāphala</s> and so forth; therefore, a rule of three (<s>trairāśika</s>) is performed with the <s>bhujāphala</s> minutes, which equal <s>prāṇas</s> (time-units): if by the day-and-night <s>prāṇas</s> equal to <s>khakhaṣaḍghana</s> (21600), the true daily motions of the Sun and other [planets] are obtained, then by these <s>bhujāphala</s> minutes equal to <s>prāṇas</s>, what [is obtained]? Regarding the equivalence of these <s>bhujāphala</s> minutes to <s>prāṇas</s>, it is stated: it has been explained that the beginning of the stellar circle (<s>jyotiścakra</s>) is also from the rising of the Sun. Therefore, due to the propulsion of the <s>pravaha</s> wind, the mean [planet] is always greater or less than [the true planet] by its own <s>bhujāphala</s>. When greater, the stellar circle is diminished by an amount equal to the <s>bhujāphala</s> minutes by the Sun’s motion; [when less, the stellar circle is decreased by an amount equal to the <s>bhujāphala</s> minutes by the Sun’s motion]. By this reasoning, the <s>bhujāphala</s> minutes then pertain to the stellar circle, and the minutes of the stellar circle and <s>prāṇas</s> are equal. Therefore, the absence of those <s>bhujāphala</s> minutes equal to <s>prāṇas</s> [occurs when] the complete Sun derived from the day-count, when equal to its own apogee, rises at exactly [the expected time]. Otherwise, the equation-of-center correction is applied there as well. For the Sun, established through true computation, rises at the horizon-peak.

body.text:
evam eteṣām vivasvadādīnām grahāṇām sphuṭagatayaḥ sūryodayāvadheḥ bhavanti iti ataḥ ravi[vaśāt eva upacayāpaca]yātmakam phalam kriyate | deśāntaracaradalakarmaṇī ca anayā eva upapattyā | ardharātrāstamayadinamadhyasaṃsthitasūryā[t trairāśikam] ã yadi ṣaṣṭyā nāḍībhiḥ yathāsvam madhyamā bhuktiḥ labhyate tadā pañcadaśabhiḥ ghaṭikābhiḥ triṃśatā pañcacatvāriṃśadbhiḥ ca kim iti [phalali]ptāḥ audayikebhyaḥ grahebhyaḥ viśodhyante, tataḥ tena
ravyādayaḥ tātkālikāḥ bhavanti | teṣām ca sphuṭaprakriyā pūrvābhihitā eva | [dinamadhyārdharātrayoḥ cara]dalakarma na pravartate | kṣitijamaṇḍalaprāptyatikrāntī ravyudayāstamayayoḥ eva iti | evam ādityagatyavadhayaḥ grahāḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus, the true daily motions of these planets beginning with the Sun (<s>Vivasvat</s>) are measured from the boundary of sunrise; therefore, the positive or negative correction is applied on account of the Sun alone. The <s>deśāntara</s> (longitude-correction) and <s>caradala</s> (half-ascensional-difference) operations follow by this same reasoning. From the Sun situated at midnight, setting, or midday, the rule of three [is applied]: if by sixty <s>nāḍīs</s> (time-units) the respective mean daily motion is obtained, then by fifteen, thirty, or forty-five <s>ghaṭikās</s>, what [is obtained]? The resulting minutes are subtracted from the sunrise-based planets; then by that [correction], the Sun and other [planets] become contemporaneous. Their true-position procedure has been stated earlier. For [the positions at] midday and midnight, the <s>caradala</s> (half-ascensional-difference) correction does not apply, since the intersection with the horizon circle pertains only to the rising and setting of the Sun. Thus, the planets are referenced to the Sun’s motion.

body.text: yadā punar para[sya grahasya raveḥ iva] kalpyante tadā candroda[yajñā]nena udayakālam eva avagatya tadudayakālāvadhayaḥ kriyante |
body.translated_text: When, however, the [rising] of another planet is postulated like that of the Sun, then by knowledge of the Moon’s rising, having ascertained the time of rising itself, [the planetary positions] are made referenced to the time of that rising.

body.text: tithipratipacchedaparijñānam
body.translated_text: Determination of the <s>tithi</s> (lunar day) intercept

body.text:
evam yathopadiṣṭagaṇitaprakriya[yā tithi]pratipacchedaparijñānāya ucyate | tat yathā ã sphuṭaśaśinaḥ sphuṭaḥ raviḥ apanīyate, yasmāt tithiḥ śaśimāsavaśāt bhavati tena "raviśaśiyogāḥ bhavanti [śaśimāsāḥ" [kālakriyāí, 5] iti sphuṭavidho]rinaḥ apanīyate | yathāsambhavam atra bhagaṇaḥ na sambhavati iti rāśyādayaḥ eva rāśyādibhyaḥ apanīyante | athavā ka[lpāditaḥ ye ravighagaṇāḥ] bhuktāḥ te śaśibhagaṇebhyaḥ viśodhyante, rāśyādibhyaḥ rāśyādayaḥ iti | tatra
avaśiṣṭāḥ śaśimāsādayaḥ bhavanti | [māsānām prayojanābhāvaḥ i]ti māsāḥ tyajyante |
body.translated_text: Thus, for the purpose of knowing the <s>tithi</s> (lunar day) intercept through the computational procedure as taught, it is stated as follows: The true Sun is subtracted from the true Moon, because the <s>tithi</s> depends on the lunar month; hence ‘the conjunctions of the Sun and Moon are the lunar months’ [<s>Kālakriyā</s> 5] — the true Sun is subtracted from the true Moon. Here, since a full revolution is not possible, only signs and so forth are subtracted from signs and so forth. Alternatively, the Sun’s revolutions elapsed from the beginning of the <s>kalpa</s> are subtracted from the Moon’s revolutions — signs and so forth from signs and so forth. The remainder gives the lunar months and so forth. Since there is no purpose for the months, the months are discarded.

body.text:
tatra ye avaśiṣṭāḥ rāśyādayaḥ vartamānaśaśimāsasya avayavabhūtāḥ taiḥ liptīkṛtaiḥ trairāśi[kam ã yadi khakhaṣaḍghana]tulyena sūryācandramasoḥ viśeṣeṇa śaśimāsaḥ labhyate tadā ābhiḥ candrādityaviśeṣaliptābhiḥ kiyacchaśimās[āḥ iti sampūrṇa]māsam na prayacchati iti divasāḥ kriyante | "triṃśaddivasaḥ bhavet sa māsaḥ" [kālakriyāí, 1] iti triṃśatkaḥ guṇakāraḥ | tatra guṇakārabhāgahārayoḥ apavartane [triṃśataḥ triṃśadbhāgena ekam] khakhaṣaḍghanasya
tāvadbhāgena saptaśatāni viṃśatyadhikāni | saptaśatyā viṃśatyuttarayā ravicandravivaraliptāḥ vibhajyante | [phalam gatatithayaḥ va]rtamānaśaśimāsasya śuklapratipatpravṛttāḥ, tatra śeṣaliptāḥ vartamānatitheḥ bhuktāḥ, tadviśuddhāḥ bhāgahāraliptāḥ bhojyāḥ iti | ataḥ tābhiḥ bhuktabhojyaliptābhiḥ trairāśikam ã yadi tat ahaḥ sūryācandramasoḥ sphuṭabhuktyantaraliptābhiḥ ekaḥ śaśidivasaḥ labhyate tataḥ ābhiḥ bhuktabhojyaliptābhiḥ kiyān śaśidivasasya labhyate iti, tatra

children.text: divaseṣu bhāgam na prayacchanti iti nāḍyaḥ kriyante | "ṣaṣṭiḥ nāḍyaḥ divasaḥ" [kālakriyāí, 1] iti ṣaṣṭyā saṅguṇayya sphuṭabhuktyantaraliptābhiḥ bhāgalabdhāḥ bhuktabhojyāḥ titheḥ nāḍyaḥ sūryodayāvadheḥ gatāḥ gantavyāḥ vā bhavanti iti |
children.translated_text: since it does not yield [complete] days as quotient, <s>nāḍīs</s> (time-units) are computed. ‘Sixty <s>nāḍīs</s> make one day’ [<s>Kālakriyā</s> 1] — multiplying by sixty and dividing by the true daily-motion difference in minutes, the elapsed and remaining <s>nāḍīs</s> of the <s>tithi</s> from sunrise are the past and future [portions].

body.translated_text: There, the remaining signs and so forth, which are fractional parts of the current lunar month, are converted to minutes and the rule of three is applied: if by the difference between the Sun and Moon equal to <s>khakhaṣaḍghana</s> (21600), one lunar month is obtained, then by these difference-minutes of the Moon and Sun, how many lunar months [are obtained]? Since it does not yield a complete month, days are computed. ‘Thirty days constitute one month’ [<s>Kālakriyā</s> 1] — thirty is the multiplier. In the reduction of the multiplier and divisor, one-thirtieth of thirty is one, and the same fraction of <s>khakhaṣaḍghana</s> gives seven hundred and twenty. The Sun-Moon difference in minutes is divided by seven hundred and twenty. The quotient gives the elapsed <s>tithis</s> (lunar days) of the current lunar month starting from the bright-fortnight first day (<s>śuklapratipat</s>); the remainder-minutes are the elapsed [portion] of the current <s>tithi</s>; and the divisor-minutes minus that remainder are the remaining [portion]. Therefore, with these elapsed and remaining minutes, the rule of three [is applied]: if by the true daily-motion difference in minutes of the Sun and Moon on that day, one lunar day is obtained, then by these elapsed and remaining minutes, how much of the lunar day is obtained? There,

body.text: sūryācandramasoḥ samaliptīkaraṇam
body.translated_text: Making the Sun and Moon have equal minutes (<s>samaliptīkaraṇa</s>)

body.text:
iṣṭakālāvadheḥ vā parvaṇi samaliptāvidhānam | gatagantavyatām parvaṇaḥ vidhāya gatagantavyaliptābhiḥ trairāśikam | tat yathā ã yadi sūryācandramasoḥ taddinasphuṭabhuktyantaraliptābhiḥ sūryācandramasoḥ sphuṭabhuktiḥ yathāsvam labhyate tataḥ ābhiḥ gatagantavyatithiliptābhiḥ kiyatyaḥ sphuṭabhuktiliptāḥ iti labdhāḥ liptāḥ ravau gantavyaparvaṇi prakṣipyante, śaśini ca | atha gataparvaṇi tayoḥ eva yathāsvam trairāśikāyātaliptāḥ viśodhyante | evam
gantavyagataparvaṇaḥ paryavasānakālikau samaliptau bhavataḥ iti gaṇitapāde api asmābhiḥ "bhukteḥ vilomavivare" [gaṇitaí, 31] iti asyām āryāyām saṃkṣepataḥ abhihitam iti kṛtvā iha tu vistareṇa pradarśitam |
body.translated_text: Alternatively, the procedure for making [the Sun and Moon] have equal minutes at a <s>parvan</s> (syzygy) from a desired time-boundary. Having determined the elapsed and remaining [portions] of the <s>parvan</s>, the rule of three is applied with the elapsed and remaining minutes. That is: if by the true daily-motion difference in minutes of the Sun and Moon on that day, the true daily motion of the Sun and Moon respectively is obtained, then by these elapsed and remaining <s>tithi</s> minutes, how many true-motion minutes [are obtained]? The obtained minutes are added to the Sun and Moon respectively for the future <s>parvan</s>; and for the past <s>parvan</s>, the minutes obtained from the rule of three are subtracted from those same [Sun and Moon]. Thus, at the conclusion of the future and past <s>parvan</s>, [the Sun and Moon] become equal in minutes. This was also briefly stated by us in the <s>Gaṇitapāda</s> under the verse ‘by the inverse difference of daily motions’ [<s>Gaṇita</s> 31]; here, however, it is demonstrated in detail.

body.text: candranakṣatrapratipacchedaparijñānam
body.translated_text: Determination of the lunar <s>nakṣatra</s> (asterism) intercept

body.text:
candrayuktena nakṣatreṇa vyavahāraḥ iti pratyaham candrayuktanakṣatrapratipaccheda [parijñānam] kriyate | tat yathā ã śaśiliptābhiḥ trairāśikam ã yadi maṇḍalaliptābhiḥ khakhaṣaḍghanatulyābhiḥ saptaviṃśatiḥ nakṣatrāṇi labhyante tataḥ [ābhiḥ candragataliptābhiḥ kim iti | atra guṇakārabhāgahārayoḥ apa]vartanam kriyate | saptaviṃśateḥ saptaviṃśatibhāgena ekam khakhaṣaḍghanasya api tāvatbhāgena aṣṭau [śatāni, ataḥ śaśiliptā]nām aṣṭābhiḥ śataiḥ bhāge
nakṣatrāṇām aśvinyādīnām [yāni gatāni teṣām saṃkhyā] labhyate | śeṣe gatagantavyam kṛtvā vartamānasya nakṣatrasya gatagantavyāḥ nāḍyaḥ sādhyante | katham? yadi sphuṭabhuktyā ṣaṣṭiḥ nāḍyaḥ labhyante, ābhiḥ gatagantavyaliptābhiḥ kiyatyaḥ iti gatagantavyanāḍyaḥ labhyante | śaśibhukteḥ ahorātrakālāvadhiniṣpannatvāt, ahorātrasya ca pramāṇam ṣaṣṭiḥ nāḍyaḥ iti ṣaṣṭyā trairāśikam kriyate || 25 ||
body.translated_text: Since the practice [of astrology] is based on the <s>nakṣatra</s> (asterism) conjoined with the Moon, the daily determination of the Moon’s conjoined <s>nakṣatra</s> intercept is performed. That is: the rule of three is applied with the Moon’s minutes: if by the minutes of one full circle equal to <s>khakhaṣaḍghana</s> (21600), twenty-seven <s>nakṣatras</s> are obtained, then by these minutes of the Moon’s [longitude], what [is obtained]? Here, the multiplier and divisor are reduced: one twenty-seventh of twenty-seven is one, and the same fraction of <s>khakhaṣaḍghana</s> is eight hundred; therefore, dividing the Moon’s minutes by eight hundred, the count of the elapsed <s>nakṣatras</s> beginning with <s>Aśvinī</s> is obtained. Making the remainder into elapsed and remaining [portions] of the current <s>nakṣatra</s>, the elapsed and remaining <s>nāḍīs</s> are computed. How? If by the true daily motion, sixty <s>nāḍīs</s> are obtained, then by these elapsed and remaining minutes, how many [<s>nāḍīs</s> are obtained]? — the elapsed and remaining <s>nāḍīs</s> are obtained. Since the Moon’s daily motion is accomplished within a day-and-night, and since the measure of a day-and-night is sixty <s>nāḍīs</s>, the rule of three is performed with sixty. || 25 ||

body.text: iti bhāskarasya kṛtau āryabhaṭatantrabhāṣye kālakriyāpādaḥ samāptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Kālakriyāpāda</s> (Chapter on Time-Reckoning) in the commentary on the treatise of <s>Āryabhaṭa</s> composed by <s>Bhāskara</s>.

body.text: Golapādaḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Golapāda</s> (Chapter on the Sphere)

children.translated_text: Auspicious invocation
Obeisance to Him who shines as the auspicious pot (<s>kumbha</s>) full of true and auspicious knowledge,
whose footstool is rubbed by the heads of gods and demons — to <s>Vedhas</s> (Brahmā, the Creator).

body.text: golabandhaḥ
body.translated_text: Construction of the armillary sphere (<s>gola</s>)

body.text:
kālakriyānantaram golam, "trīṇi gadati gaṇitam kālakriyām golam" iti uktatvāt | gamyate jñāyate asmāt iti golam | kim punar asmāt gamyate? grahabhramaṇadharitrīsaṃsthānādīni sarvam | evam paramārthajijñāsavaḥ hi asatyapūrvakam satyam pratipadyante | tat yathā bhiṣajaḥ hi utpalanālādiṣu sirāvedhanādīni pratipadyante, yajñaśastravidaḥ śuṣkeṣṭyā yajñādīni [pratipadyante], vaiyākaraṇāḥ prakṛtipratyayalopāgamavarṇavikārādibhiḥ sādhuśabdam pratipadyante,
evam atra api sāṃvatsarāḥ vṛttaśalākāsūtrāvalambakādibhiḥ kṣetragaṇitaviśeṣaiḥ pāramārthikam golam pratipadyante | tasmāt diṅmātrapradarśanam eva etat ārabhyate, aśakyatvāt aśeṣapradarśanasya | kaḥ hi citrayan nimeṣonmeṣādi api citrayati | tasmāt śrīparṇivañculakāṣṭhayoḥ anyatamam ardhavṛttacakrasvarūpam krākacikaiḥ vṛttam ekam niṣpādayet | tataḥ sughaṭitārdhavṛttadvayena tribhiḥ vā sughaṭitavṛttaśakalaiḥ vṛttam ekam nirmāpayet | tatra vṛttaśakalasandhicchedāḥ
trayaḥ śurapuṅkhapārśvacchedāvayavārdhacchedaḥ iti | tatra eteṣām anyatamena vṛttaśakalāni anyonyam ghaṭayet | tāmrakīlakaiḥ tatra evam niṣpannam ekam vṛttam pūrvāparam nidhāya dvitīyam dakṣiṇottaram upari adhaḥ ca janitasvastikam svastikasampāte ca maṇḍaladvayam ardhaccedena chitvā tathā saṃyojyam yathā ekam eva vṛttam lakṣyate | tau vihitārdhacchedena svastikacatuṣṭayam praveśya niścalam nidadhya tāmrakīlakaiḥ niścalīkriyate |
body.translated_text: After the chapter on time-reckoning (<s>Kālakriyā</s>) comes the sphere (<s>gola</s>), because it was stated: ‘[<s>Āryabhaṭa</s>] teaches three [subjects]: computation (<s>gaṇita</s>), time-reckoning (<s>kālakriyā</s>), and the sphere (<s>gola</s>).’ <s>Gola</s> means: ‘from this (<s>gola</s>) [things] are known’ — that is, [the sphere] from which [things] are understood. What then is understood from it? Everything: the revolution of planets, the configuration of the Earth, and so forth. Thus, those who seek ultimate truth apprehend the truth by means of an unreal [model]. Just as: physicians practice vein-cutting and the like on lotus-stalks and such; those versed in sacrificial science [practice] sacrificial rites through mock-sacrifices (<s>śuṣkeṣṭī</s>); grammarians apprehend correct speech through [the operations of] base, suffix, elision, augment, phonetic modification, and the like — similarly here too, astronomers (<s>sāṃvatsaras</s>) apprehend the true sphere through the special geometric operations of circles, rods, strings, plumb-lines, and the like. Therefore, this is undertaken merely as an indication of direction, since a complete demonstration is impossible. For who, when painting, would also paint the blinking [of eyes] and such? Therefore, one should produce a circle from either <s>śrīparṇī</s> (Gmelina arborea) or <s>vañculā</s> (Calamus rotang) wood, in the form of a semicircular disc, [made round] by sawyers. Then, from two well-fitted semicircles, or from three well-fitted arc-segments, one should construct a single circle. The cuts at the joints of the arc-segments are of three types: the side-cut of the arrow-feather type, and the half-cut type. By one of these, the arc-segments should be joined to each other using copper rivets. Having thus produced one circle, it is placed in the east-west direction; a second circle is placed in the north-south direction, intersecting above and below. At the intersection-points (<s>svastika</s>), the two circles are cut with a half-cut so that they may be joined such that they appear as a single circle. Having inserted [the joints] at the four intersection-points with the prepared half-cuts, it is fixed immovably and secured with copper rivets.

body.text:
tataḥ tayoḥ maṇḍalayoḥ bahiḥ parikaravat dikcatuṣṭayajanitasvastikam anyam tathā eva ardhacchedena svastikacatuṣṭayam praveśya niścalam nidadhyāt | pūrvāparamaṇḍalam ṣaṣṭyaṅkāṅkitam kārayet, yathā ekaikasmin caturbhāge pañcadaśa pañcadaśāṅkāḥ syuḥ | te ca ahorātraghaṭikāḥ | evam pariśeṣam maṇḍaladvayam api, ekaikam ṣaṣṭiśatatrayāṅkitam [kārayet] | tāni viṣuvat [yāmya uttarakṣitija]maṇḍalāni | tat tulyam eva aparam maṇḍalam ṣaṣṭiśatatrayāṅkitam
pūrvasvastike aparasvastike ca tiryak tribhāgacchedam kṛtvā dvau tribhāgau maṇḍalapradeśasya svastikam ghaṭayet | yathā vā maṇḍalatrayasampātam ekam eva lakṣyate tathā avachedaḥ kalpanīyaḥ | pūrvāparadakṣiṇottaramaṇḍalayoḥ yaḥ adhaḥ svastikaḥ tasmāt uttareṇa uttaraśalākāyām caturviṃśatibhāge tathā eva ardhacchedena svastikam kārayet | upari api tathā eva uparisvastikāt dakṣiṇena [dakṣiṇa]śalākāyām caturviṃśatitame bhāge svastikam kārayet | sarvatra niścalīkaraṇam
tāmrakīlakaiḥ | evam tiryak rāśipadaḥ vyavasthitaḥ | sa eva apamaṇḍalam iti ucyate | tāvatpramāṇam eva anyat maṇḍalam sañcāri yatra candramasaḥ sampātaḥ vartate tasmin badhvā tataḥ uttareṇa parataḥ nivatitame bhāge yathā ca ardhapañcamabhāgāḥ tasya ca apakramamaṇḍalasya ca antare bhavanti tathā vidhāya pātabhāge cakrārdhāntare badhīyāt | evam tataḥ dakṣiṇena navatitame bhāge ardhapañcamā bhāgāḥ tasya apakramamaṇḍalasya ca yathā antare bhavanti tathā
nidadhyāt | evam tat vimaṇḍalam, tat eva vikṣepamaṇḍalam iti ucyate |
body.translated_text: Then, outside those two circles, like a girdle, another [ring] with cross-junctions generated in the four directions, similarly inserting four cross-junctions by half-cuts, should be placed immovably. The east-west circle should be made marked with sixty [divisions], so that in each quarter there are fifteen markings. These are the day-and-night <s>ghaṭikās</s> (time-units). Likewise the remaining two circles also, each marked with three-hundred-sixty [divisions]. These are the equatorial (<s>viṣuvat</s>), [southern] and northern horizon circles. Another circle equal to these, marked with three-hundred-sixty [divisions], at the eastern and western cross-junctions, making a transverse one-third cut and fitting the cross-junction at two-thirds of the circle's section — or the cut should be arranged so that the triple-circle intersection appears as one — at the lower cross-junction of the east-west and north-south circles, to the north on the northern rod, at the twenty-fourth division, similarly a cross-junction should be made by a half-cut. Likewise above, from the upper cross-junction to the south on the southern rod, at the twenty-fourth division, a cross-junction should be made. Everywhere the fastening is with copper pegs. Thus the obliquely-placed sign-quadrant is established. That itself is called the ecliptic circle (<s>apamaṇḍala</s>). Another circle of the same size, movable, bound where the Moon's node (<s>sampāta</s>) is located, thence to the north at the ninetieth division, arranged so that four-and-a-half degrees fall between it and the ecliptic circle, and at the node-point [plus] half a circle, it should be bound. Likewise, thence to the south at the ninetieth division, four-and-a-half degrees should be placed between it and the ecliptic circle. Thus that is the deflection-circle (<s>vimaṇḍala</s>); that itself is called the <s>vikṣepamaṇḍala</s> (latitude-circle).

body.text:
evam anyeṣām api svebhyaḥ svebhyaḥ pātabhāgebhyaḥ api maṇḍalāni | budhaśukrayoḥ śīghroccābhyām | svāhorātramaṇḍalāni api sañcārīṇi ã viṣuvataḥ uttareṇa meṣāpakramakāṣṭhatulyāntare pūrvāparāyatam maṇḍalam meṣasya ahorātramaṇḍalam, vṛṣāntāpakramatulyakāṣṭhāntare vṛṣasya, mithunāntāpakramatulyakāṣṭhāntare mithunasya, tāni eva utkrameṇa karkaṭakasiṃhakanyānām; evam [viṣuvataḥ] dakṣiṇena tulāvṛścikadhanuṣām svāhorātramaṇḍalāni,
tāni eva utkrameṇa makarakumbhamīnānām | svāhorātramaṇḍaleṣu dakṣiṇottarāyatāni sūtrāṇi badhnīyāt | teṣām ardhāni apakramajyāḥ | meṣasya ahorātramaṇḍalena unmaṇḍalasya yatra sampātaḥ tatra sūtrasya ekam agram badhvā mīnasya ahorātronmaṇḍalasampāte dvitīyam agram badhnīyāt | bhūmadhyāvabhedisūtram viṣuvatā saha badhnīyāt, tasya prathamasūtrasya ca yatra sampātaḥ tatra prathamasūtrārdham bhavati | evam anyeṣām sūtrāṇām ardhāni | tāni
sarvāṇi ahorātrāpakramajyāḥ santi | aśakyatvāt kvacit tu pradarśyante | yāni vikṣepāpakramasvāhorātramaṇḍalāni vyākhyātāni [tāni na] pradarśyante | anyathā kālasamaḥ golaḥ bhramayitum na śakyate, maṇḍalabahutvāt |
body.translated_text: Likewise, for the other [planets] also, circles [are made] from their respective node-positions. For Mercury and Venus, from their <s>śīghroccas</s> (fast apogees). The day-circles (<s>svāhorātramaṇḍalāni</s>) are also movable: north of the equator, at an interval equal to the declination-arc of <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries), an east-west-extending circle is the day-circle of Aries; at an interval equal to the declination-arc of the end of <s>Vṛṣa</s> (Taurus), that of Taurus; at an interval equal to the declination-arc of the end of <s>Mithuna</s> (Gemini), that of Gemini; these same in reverse order are for <s>Karkaṭaka</s> (Cancer), <s>Siṃha</s> (Leo), and <s>Kanyā</s> (Virgo). Similarly, south of the equator are the day-circles of <s>Tulā</s> (Libra), <s>Vṛścika</s> (Scorpio), and <s>Dhanus</s> (Sagittarius); these same in reverse order are for <s>Makara</s> (Capricorn), <s>Kumbha</s> (Aquarius), and <s>Mīna</s> (Pisces). On the day-circles, north-south-extending threads should be tied. Their halves are the declination-sines. Where the day-circle of Aries intersects with the prime vertical (<s>unmaṇḍala</s>), there one end of the thread is tied, and where the day-circle of Pisces intersects with the prime vertical, the other end is tied. A thread passing through the center of the Earth should be tied with the equator; at the intersection of that and the first thread, the half of the first thread is obtained. Similarly the halves of the other threads. All these are the day-circle declination-sines. Due to impracticality, some are shown [only] partially. The latitude, declination, and day-circles that have been described are not displayed [completely]. Otherwise, the sphere equal to time cannot be made to rotate, because of the multiplicity of circles.

body.text:
atha suślakṣṇām ṛjvīm ayaḥśalākām gopucchāyatavṛttām dakṣiṇottarasvastikāvabhedinīm nirgatobhayāgrām pañjarabhārasahām nidadhyāt | tanmadhye bhuvam samavṛttām mṛdā anyena vā racayet | evam ayam ekaḥ eva pañjaraḥ sarveṣām grahāṇām | yasmāt bhinnakakṣyāsthāḥ api grahāḥ ekakakṣyāgatāḥ eva upalakṣyante, tasmāt ayam eva ekaḥ pañjaraḥ | athavā sarveṣām eva pṛthak pṛthak pañjarāḥ yāvat tāvat paricchinnasvakakṣyāpramāṇāḥ eva pradarśayitavyāḥ
|
body.translated_text: Now, a smooth, straight iron rod, with an oblong circular [cross-section] like a cow's tail, passing through the north-south cross-junctions, with both ends protruding, capable of bearing the weight of the cage-frame, should be placed. In the middle of that, the Earth, evenly round, should be fashioned with clay or other [material]. Thus this single cage-frame serves for all the planets. Since planets situated in different orbits are nevertheless perceived as if located on a single orbit, therefore this single cage-frame [suffices]. Alternatively, separate cage-frames for each and every [planet], with their own orbit-sizes properly delimited, should be displayed.

body.text:
athavā pañjarasya bahiḥ [dakṣiṇottara]svastikayoḥ ayaḥśalākāyām tryaṅgulām caturaṅgulām vā ślakṣṇām śaradaṇḍikām niścalām nidadhyāt | tataḥ yāvattāvatpramāṇaparicchinnakhakakṣyāparikalpitam ubhayataḥ cakrārdhāntarakṛtavedham [maṇḍalam] dakṣiṇottarāvagāhi nidhāya tasya madhye pañjaram praveśya tām ayaḥśalākām ubhayatra pārśvavedhau praveśayet, yathā sā śaradaṇḍikā pañjaradvayasīmāvagāhinī bhavati | tāvatpramāṇam eva anyadvṛttam
pūrvāparāvagāhi upari adhaḥ ca janitasvastikam pūrvavat nidadhyāt | tat samamaṇḍalam | punar api tāvat eva anyat maṇḍalam parikaravat dikcatuṣṭayajanitasvastikam dakṣiṇottarasvastikasampātakṛtavedham ubhayatra lohaśalākām praveśya niścalam nidadhyāt | tat kṣitijamaṇḍalam | evam ayam golaḥ viṣuvati samaḥ eva avatiṣṭhate | viṣuvataḥ uttareṇa yāvān akṣaḥ tāvatsu bhāgeṣu khagolottarasvastikāt upari vedham kārayet, dakṣiṇataḥ ca tāvati eva antare [adhaḥ] vedhaḥ
| pūrvavedhābhyām ayaḥśalākām niṣkāsya svadeśākṣabhāgapramāṇaparikalpitavedhayoḥ praveśayet | evam svaviṣayākṣapramāṇena avasthitaḥ golaḥ, tatra sarvam eva pradarśayet | atha khagolapramāṇam eva anyadvṛttam ubhayataḥ cakrārdhāntarakṛtavedham uttaraḥ nirgatāyaḥśalākāgram praveśayet | dvitīyavedham dakṣiṇataḥ nirgatāyaḥśalākāgram praveśayet | tatra tat niścalam nidhāya, tasya pūrvāparasvastikasampāte pūrvavat tiryagbhedena pūrvāparasvastikayoḥ
niścalam tat maṇḍalam nidadhyāt | tat unmaṇḍalam iti ācakṣate | sarvāṇi eva vṛttāni ṣaṣṭiśatatrayabhāgāṅkitāni kārayet |
body.translated_text: Alternatively, outside the cage-frame, on the iron rod at the north-south cross-junctions, a smooth bamboo rod of three or four <s>aṅgulas</s> (finger-breadths) should be placed immovably. Then, a circle of the determined size of the assumed sky-orbit, with holes made at half-circle intervals on both sides, plunging through the north-south [axis], having placed it and inserted the cage-frame in its middle, that iron rod should be passed through the side-holes on both sides, so that the bamboo rod becomes the boundary between the two [spheres — inner cage and outer ring]. Another circle of the same size, plunging east-west, with cross-junctions generated above and below, should be placed as before. That is the prime vertical (<s>samamaṇḍala</s>). Again, another [circle] of the same size, like a girdle, with cross-junctions generated in the four directions, with holes made at the north-south cross-junction intersection, inserting the iron rod on both sides, should be placed immovably. That is the horizon circle (<s>kṣitijamaṇḍala</s>). Thus this sphere stands level at the equator. North of the equator, at [a distance equal to] the latitude (<s>akṣa</s>), a hole should be made above the northern cross-junction of the celestial sphere at that many divisions, and likewise to the south at that same interval, a hole below. Removing the iron rod from the previous holes and inserting it into the holes determined by the local latitude, the sphere is established at one's local latitude — therein everything is to be demonstrated. Then, another circle of the same size as the celestial sphere, with holes made at half-circle intervals on both sides, should be inserted through the protruding end of the iron rod at the north; the second hole [is placed] through the protruding end of the iron rod at the south. Having placed it immovably there, at the east-west cross-junction intersection of that [circle], by a transverse cut as before, that circle should be placed immovably at the east-west cross-junctions. That is called the prime vertical (<s>unmaṇḍala</s>). All circles should be made marked with three-hundred-sixty divisions.

body.text: anye punar samāyāmavanau khagolārdhapramāṇam avaṭam khātvā tatra yathā kṣitijamaṇḍalam upari bhavati tathā ardhanimagnam khagolam nidhāya darśayanti | evam ayam kāṣṭhamayaḥ golaḥ kriyate | kāṣṭhāsambhave paripakvālpasuṣiraślakṣṇavaṃśaśalākāvṛttaiḥ vā golaḥ kriyate | evam golam badhvā sarvam eva avaśeṣam śāstre vyākhyāyate |
body.translated_text: Others, however, on level ground, having dug a pit of the size of half the celestial sphere, place the celestial sphere half-immersed therein so that the horizon circle is at the top, and demonstrate [it] thus. In this way, the armillary sphere is made of wood. When wood is unavailable, the sphere is made with rings of smooth, well-baked, slightly-hollow bamboo rods. Having thus constructed the sphere, everything else is explained in the treatise.

body.text: bhagole apakramamaṇḍalam
body.translated_text: The ecliptic circle on the celestial sphere

body.text: atra āditaḥ eva tāvat apakramamaṇḍalam āha ã
body.translated_text: Here, from the very beginning, he first states the ecliptic circle:

children.text: meṣādeḥ kanyāntam samam udak apamaṇḍalārdham apayātam |
children.translated_text: From the beginning of <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries) to the end of <s>Kanyā</s> (Virgo), an equal half of the ecliptic circle (<s>apamaṇḍala</s>) has gone northward;
from the beginning of <s>Tulā</s> (Libra) to the end of <s>Mīna</s> (Pisces), the remaining half is to the south only. // 1 //

body.text:
meṣādeḥ meṣasya ādiḥ meṣādiḥ, tasmāt meṣādeḥ, kanyāntam antam paryavasānam, kanyāyāḥ antam kanyāntam; meṣādeḥ ārabhya yāvat kanyāntam | samam tulyam | udak uttareṇa | apamaṇḍalārdham | apamaṇḍalasya apakramamaṇḍalasya ardham, apakramamaṇḍalārdham | apayātam tiryak vyavasthitam | taulyādeḥ taulinaḥ ādiḥ taulyādiḥ, tasmāt taulyādeḥ, mīnasya antam mīnāntam; taulyādeḥ ārabhya yāvat mīnāntam | śeṣārdham śeṣam ca tadardham
ca śeṣārdham, athavā śeṣasya jyotiścakrasya apamaṇḍalasaṃjñitasya ardham śeṣārdham | tat dakṣiṇena, dakṣiṇadigbhāgena tadardham | "eva"śabdaḥ āryāpūraṇārtahm pratipāditaḥ | athavā evam ardhamātram api paścārdhe pradarśayati, yathā uttareṇa samam apakramamaṇḍalam tiryak vyavasthitam, evam atra api dakṣiṇena tasya eva apakramamaṇḍalasya ardham tiryak eva avatiṣṭhate iti |
  atra vinā api "sama"śabdena ṣaḍrāśipramāṇābhidhānāt udagdakṣiṇāpakramamaṇḍalārdhasamatvam gamyate, samagrahaṇam atiricyate | na atiricyate ã pratideśam akṣaviśeṣāt rāśīnām udayakālāḥ viṣamāḥ upalakṣyante, tena samaśabdāt ṛte viṣamapramāṇānām rāśīnām grahaṇam syāt, tataḥ ca akṣaviśeṣāt meṣādīnām apakramajyāḥ pratideśam bhinnapramāṇāḥ syuḥ | "sama"śabde punar kriyamāṇe tulyapramāṇarāśigrahaṇam siddham, yasmāt sarvaḥ eva
rāśiḥ jyotiścakradvādaśabhāgaḥ, sa ca triṃśattriṃśadbhāgapramāṇaḥ iti |evam apakramamaṇḍalam viṣuvataḥ uttareṇa meṣādeḥ kanyāntam tiryak avatiṣṭhate | tat eva tulyādeḥ mīnāntam dakṣiṇena viṣuvataḥ tathā eva avatiṣṭhate | katham idam anuktam gamyate viṣuvataḥ iti | na eṣaḥ doṣaḥ | udagdakṣiṇena iti b(r)uvan ācāryaḥ siddham eva viṣuvanmaṇḍalam pradarśayati | anyathā hi udagdakṣiṇena iti, etat anarthakam syāt | udagdakṣiṇaśabdau ca digvācinau, dik vyavasthā
apekṣayā bhavati | ataḥ pūrvam viṣuvanmaṇḍalam badhvā tataḥ apakramamaṇḍalam badhyate | sarvāṇi eva maṇḍalāni ṣaṣṭiśatatrayāṅkitāni kriyante, yasmāt ṣaṣṭiśatatrayāṃśam jyotiścakram || 1 ||
body.translated_text: 'From the beginning of <s>Meṣa</s>' — the beginning of <s>Meṣa</s> is '<s>meṣādi</s>'; from that '<s>meṣādi</s>.' 'To the end of <s>Kanyā</s>' — the end, the termination, of <s>Kanyā</s> is '<s>kanyānta</s>'; from the beginning of <s>Meṣa</s> up to the end of <s>Kanyā</s>. 'Equal' (<s>sama</s>) — even, uniform. 'Northward' (<s>udak</s>) — to the north. 'Half of the ecliptic circle' — the half of the <s>apamaṇḍala</s>, the ecliptic circle, is the half of the ecliptic. 'Gone obliquely' (<s>apayāta</s>) — situated transversely. 'From the beginning of <s>Tulā</s>' — the beginning of <s>Tulā</s> (Libra) is '<s>taulyādi</s>'; from that '<s>taulyādi</s>.' 'To the end of <s>Mīna</s>' — the end of <s>Mīna</s> is '<s>mīnānta</s>'; from the beginning of <s>Tulā</s> up to the end of <s>Mīna</s>. 'The remaining half' — the remaining and its half are '<s>śeṣārdha</s>'; or, the half of the remaining zodiacal circle called the ecliptic is '<s>śeṣārdha</s>.' That [is] to the south, in the southern direction — that half. The word '<s>eva</s>' (only) is explained as serving to complete the <s>āryā</s> meter. Or, by [the word] '<s>eva</s>' he shows that even a mere half in the latter part [is the same], just as the ecliptic circle is situated transversely evenly to the north, so here too the half of that same ecliptic circle stands transversely to the south. Here, even without the word '<s>sama</s>' (equal), since the extent of six signs is stated, the equality of the northern and southern halves of the ecliptic is understood — [so] the word '<s>sama</s>' is superfluous. No, it is not superfluous: at each locality, due to differences in latitude, the rising-times of the signs are observed to be unequal; therefore, without the word '<s>sama</s>,' signs of unequal measure would be taken, and from that, the declination-sines from the beginning of <s>Meṣa</s> onward would have different measures at each locality. But when the word '<s>sama</s>' is used, the taking of signs of equal measure is established — since every sign is one-twelfth of the zodiacal circle, and that is of the measure of thirty degrees each. Thus the ecliptic circle stands obliquely to the north of the equator from the beginning of <s>Meṣa</s> to the end of <s>Kanyā</s>. That same [circle], from the beginning of <s>Tulā</s> to the end of <s>Mīna</s>, similarly stands to the south of the equator. How is this understood when 'from the equator' is not stated?
