Even birds, flying up into the sky, would not be able to reach their nests. Therefore, there is no evidence for the rotation of the Earth. Therefore, the <s>sūtra</s> (verse) should be explained otherwise. Just as a person moving in the same direction on a boat sees moving objects as going in the opposite direction, so the stars, which are moving — being impelled by the <s>pravaha</s> (prevailing cosmic wind) — are seen at <s>Laṅkā</s> as moving in the opposite direction with respect to the objects [on the ground]; and they see the Earth situated below as motionless, [though it appears] as if rotating. And by direct observation too, the stars that have risen in the east reach the western direction. || 9 ||

body.text: bhūbhramaṇakāraṇam
body.translated_text: The cause of the rotation of the stellar sphere

body.text: bhramaṇakāraṇam āha ã
body.translated_text: He states the cause of the rotation:

children.translated_text: Constantly impelled by the <s>pravaha</s> (prevailing) wind, which is the cause of rising and setting,
the stellar cage, together with the planets, rotates uniformly westward from <s>Laṅkā</s>. || 10 ||

body.text: udayaḥ ca astamayaḥ ca [udayāstamayau | tayoḥ ] udayāstamayayoḥ nimittam nityam pravaheṇa pravahasaṃjñitena vāyunā kṣiptaḥ bhapañjaraḥ, bhapañjaraḥ api nityagatiḥ eva, laṅkāyām samapaścimaḥ yaḥ dikpradeśaḥ sa laṅkāsamapaścimaḥ, tam gacchati iti laṅkāsamapaścimagaḥ, saha grahaiḥ vartate iti sagrahaḥ, bhramati kṣaṇam api na avatiṣṭhate |
body.translated_text: Rising and setting — for the purpose of rising and setting, the stellar cage (<s>bhapañjara</s>), always propelled by the wind called <s>pravaha</s>, which also has perpetual motion, [moves] westward at [the longitude of] <s>Laṅkā</s> — the direction-point that is due west of <s>Laṅkā</s> is '<s>laṅkāsamapaścima</s>' (due west of <s>Laṅkā</s>); it moves toward that, hence '<s>laṅkāsamapaścimagaḥ</s>' (moving due west of <s>Laṅkā</s>); it exists together with the planets, hence '<s>sagrahaḥ</s>' (with the planets).

body.text: yadi api grahāḥ prāṅmukham vrajanti tathā api bhapañjarāpekṣayā aparadiksaṅkramaṇam kurvanti, mahatā bhapañjaragatyā nīyamānāḥ lakṣyante, kulālacakrasthāḥ kīṭāḥ iva || 10 ||
body.translated_text: Although the planets move eastward, nevertheless, relative to the stellar cage, they appear to move westward — being carried by the great motion of the stellar cage, they are observed [thus], like insects on a potter's wheel. // 10 //

body.text: meruvarṇanam
body.translated_text: Description of <s>Meru</s>

children.translated_text: He states the measure of <s>Meru</s>:
<s>Meru</s>, one <s>yojana</s> in measure, luminous, is encircled by the <s>Himavat</s> [mountains];
in the middle of the <s>Nandana</s> garden, made of jewels, circular on all sides. // 11 //

body.text: yojanam mātrā yasya sa yojanamātraḥ, pramāṇe mātranpratyayaḥ | prabhākaraḥ, prabhām karoti iti prabhākaraḥ | [himavatā parikṣiptaḥ], himavatā parvatena samantāt veṣṭitaḥ | [nandanavanasya madhye], nandanam vanam [devānām apsarogaṇaparivṛtānām] krīḍāsthānam, tasya madhye | ratnamayaḥ | ratnāni [suvarṇarajata]muktāpravālapadmarāgamarakataprabhṛtīni, taiḥ nirmitaḥ ratnamayaḥ | [sarvataḥ] samantāt | vṛttaḥ golakākāraḥ iti arthaḥ |
body.translated_text: That whose measure (<s>mātrā</s>) is one <s>yojana</s> is '<s>yojanamātra</s>'; the suffix '<s>matran</s>' [is used] in the sense of measure. '<s>Prabhākara</s>' — it makes radiance, hence '<s>prabhākara</s>' (luminous). 'Encircled by <s>Himavat</s>' — surrounded on all sides by the <s>Himavat</s> mountain. 'In the middle of the <s>Nandana</s> garden' — <s>Nandana</s> is a garden, the pleasure-ground [of the gods] surrounded by hosts of <s>apsaras</s> (celestial nymphs); in the middle of that. 'Made of jewels' — the jewels [include gold...]

body.text: atha paurāṇikaiḥ lakṣayojanapramāṇaḥ meruḥ paṭhyate tat yuktirahitam | [laṅkātaḥ yāvat merumadhyam tāvat yojanasahasram api na asti, kutaḥ tat ekadeśe bhaviṣyati | atha bhūḥ eva mahāpramāṇā parikalpyate, tat ayuktam |] yat sapañcāśatsahasram yojanānām bhūvyāsāmanam akṣonnatiprasādhitam tat sopapattikam | grahodayāstamayamadhyāhnicchāyāvanatilambanādibhiḥ siddham utsṛjya kim anyat upalabhyate |
body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Purāṇic</s> authors read <s>Meru</s> as one hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s> in measure — that is devoid of reasoning. [From <s>Laṅkā</s> to the center of <s>Meru</s>, there are not even a thousand <s>yojanas</s>; how could it exist in a part of that? And if the Earth itself is conceived as of great measure, that is untenable.] That which was established with proof as fifty-three thousand <s>yojanas</s> as the measure of the Earth's diameter by means of the elevation of the [polar] axis...

body.text:
kim ca purāṇeṣu puṣkaradvīpasya uparigataḥ vivasvān madhyāhnam karoti iti paṭhyate | lakṣayojanānām kila jambūdvīpaḥ, [tataḥ dviguṇottarāḥ] samudrāḥ [dvīpāḥ ca] sapta, saptamaḥ ca puṣkaradvīpaḥ | tat anekaiḥ yojanasahasraiḥ antaraiḥ vyavasthitam | tatra yadi madhyāhnaḥ vivasvataḥ syāt asmākam uttaragolabhūtatvāt śaṅkoḥ chāyānāśaḥ [na] syāt | dṛśyate tacchāyānāśaḥ | tasmāt viṣuvati laṅkāmadhye savitā gacchati iti siddham | [viṣuvati laṅkāmadhye
na savitā gacchati iti taiḥ eva uktam | tat ca atidūratvāt na ghaṭate | yadi pataṅgavat utplutya gacchati tataḥ yujyate | tat ca aśakyam parikalpayitum, pratyakṣaviruddhatvāt |] tasmāt dhruvonnatyā [ānītam eva] bhuvaḥ pramāṇam siddham | tatra mahāpramāṇasya meroḥ avasthānam eva na asti |
body.translated_text: Moreover, in the <s>Purāṇas</s> it is read that the Sun makes midday above <s>Puṣkara</s> island. <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> is reportedly a hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s>, [and beyond that,] the oceans and islands, each successively double, are seven; and the seventh is <s>Puṣkara</s> island. That is situated at a distance of many thousands of <s>yojanas</s>. If the Sun's midday were there, then for us to the north...

body.text: yadi kathañcit mahāpramāṇaḥ eva meruḥ avatiṣṭhate tadā sa kim asmābhiḥ na dṛśyate |
body.translated_text: If somehow <s>Meru</s> of great measure exists, then why is it not seen by us?

body.text: dūratvāt meruḥ asmābhiḥ na dṛśyate, athavā niṣprabhatvāt tat na dṛśyate, na tarhi ratnamayaḥ | kim ca yadi mahāpramāṇaḥ meruḥ syāt meruśikharāntaritatvāt bhāvāt uttareṇa tārakāḥ na dṛśyeran | tasmāt tasya kanakagireḥ upariśikharapradeśe eva sarvaratnamayaḥ meruśabdena ucyate || 11 ||
body.translated_text: <s>Meru</s> is not seen by us because of its distance; or because it is without radiance, it is not seen — then it is not made of jewels. Moreover, if <s>Meru</s> were of great measure, then the stars to the north would not be seen because they would be hidden behind the peak of <s>Meru</s>. Therefore, its golden mountain...

body.text: merubaḍavāmukhayoḥ sthitī
body.translated_text: The positions of <s>Meru</s> and <s>Baḍavāmukha</s>

body.text: kva bhūpradeśe meruḥ, kva vā baḍavāmukham iti āha ã
body.translated_text: Where on the Earth is <s>Meru</s>, and where is <s>Baḍavāmukha</s> (the submarine fire)? He says:

children.text: svaḥ merū sthalamadhye narakaḥ baḍavāmukham ca jalamadhye |
children.translated_text: Heaven and <s>Meru</s> [are] in the middle of land; hell and <s>Baḍavāmukha</s> in the middle of water;
the gods and the dead (<s>mara</s>) consider each other to be situated below, certainly. // 12 //

body.text: svaḥ svargopalakṣitaḥ, meruḥ ca, sthalamadhye | narakaḥ baḍavāmukham ca jalamadhye | amaramarāḥ amarāḥ devāḥ, marāḥ narakasthāḥ, te parasparam adhaḥsthāḥ manyante | yataḥ sarveṣām bhūḥ adhaḥ, ataḥ anyonyam adhaḥsthitāḥ manyante | yatra uttareṇa ayaḥśalākā bhuvam bhitvā nirgatā tatra pradeśe svargaḥ meruḥ, yatra dakṣiṇena nirgatā tatra narakaḥ baḍavāmukham ca || 12 ||
body.translated_text: '<s>Svaḥ</s>' — indicated by heaven (<s>svarga</s>); and <s>Meru</s> — in the middle of land. 'Hell and <s>Baḍavāmukha</s> in the middle of water.' '<s>Amaramarāḥ</s>' — the <s>amaras</s> are the gods, the <s>maras</s> are those in hell; they consider each other to be situated below. Since for everyone the Earth is below, they consider each other to be situated below. Where to the north an iron needle piercing the Earth emerges — at that place is heaven...

body.text: udayādivyavasthā
body.translated_text: The arrangement of rising and the like

body.text: prakṛṣṭadeśāntaravyavasthitān deśān āha ã
body.translated_text: He states the places situated at great longitudinal distances:

children.text: udayaḥ yaḥ laṅkāyām saḥ astamayaḥ savituḥ eva siddhapure |
children.translated_text: What is sunrise at <s>Laṅkā</s> is sunset of the Sun at <s>Siddhapura</s>;
[it is] midday at <s>Yamakoṭi</s> and midnight in the land of the <s>Romakas</s>. // 13 //

body.text: laṅkānivāsinām yaḥ udayaḥ sa eva siddhapuranivāsinām astamayaḥ, [yataḥ laṅkāpradeśāt adhaḥ vyavasthitam siddhapuram] | madhyāhnaḥ yamakoṭyām, yaḥ eva laṅkāpuranivāsinām udayaḥ sa eva yamakoṭinivāsinām madhyāhnaḥ, yataḥ laṅkāpradeśāt pūrvasyām bhūparidhicaturbhāge yamakoṭiḥ | yaḥ laṅkānivāsinām udayaḥ sa romakanivāsinām ardharātraḥ, yataḥ laṅkātaḥ aparabhāge bhūparidhicaturbhāge romakam | evam ete bhūcaturthabhāg[āntarāla]vyavasthitāḥ

children.translated_text: The places situated at the junction of land and water are to be shown as having the interval of one-quarter of the day-and-night in time and longitudinal distance from each other. // 13 //

body.translated_text: What is sunrise for the inhabitants of <s>Laṅkā</s> is sunset for the inhabitants of <s>Siddhapura</s>, [since <s>Siddhapura</s> is situated diametrically below the place of <s>Laṅkā</s>]. Midday at <s>Yamakoṭi</s> — what is sunrise for the inhabitants of <s>Laṅkā</s> city is midday for the inhabitants of <s>Yamakoṭi</s>, since <s>Yamakoṭi</s> is at one-quarter of the Earth's circumference eastward from the place of <s>Laṅkā</s>. What is sunrise for the inhabitants of <s>Laṅkā</s>...

body.text: samarekhāsthanagaryau
body.translated_text: The cities on the prime meridian

body.text: deśāntarapradarśanārtham āha ã
body.translated_text: In order to show the longitudinal difference, he says:

children.translated_text: <s>Laṅkā</s> is at one-quarter of the Earth's orbit from the middle of land and the middle of water;
<s>Ujjayinī</s> is due north of <s>Laṅkā</s>, at one-quarter of that. // 14 //

body.text:
sthalamadhyāt meroḥ ārabhya jalamadhyāt ca baḍavāmukhāt laṅkā bhūkakṣyāyāḥ caturthabhāge vyavasthitā | bhūparidhiḥ

100 | etāvati antare vyavasthitā | ujjayinī sthalajalasandhivartilaṅkāyāḥ samottare digbhāge vyavasthitā | taccaturaṃśe, tasya bhūcaturthabhāgasya caturthabhāge | bhūparidheḥ ṣoḍaśabhāgaḥ

400 | etāvati antare laṅkātaḥ ujjayinī |
body.translated_text: From the middle of land, i.e., from <s>Meru</s>, and from the middle of water, i.e., <s>Baḍavāmukha</s>, <s>Laṅkā</s> is situated at one-quarter of the Earth's orbit. The Earth's circumference is 3298 17/25; one-quarter is 824 67/100. At such an interval it is situated. <s>Ujjayinī</s> is situated in the direction due north of <s>Laṅkā</s>, which is at the junction of land and water. 'At one-quarter of that' — of that one-quarter of the Earth...

body.text: laṅkojjayinīsamadakṣiṇottararekhāyām vātsyagulmacakorapuraprabhṛtīni sthānāni vyavasthitāni | ujjayinyāḥ uttareṇa daśapuramālavanagaracaṭṭaśivasthāneśvaraprabhṛtīni yāvat meruḥ iti |
body.translated_text: On the north-south line equidistant from <s>Laṅkā</s> and <s>Ujjayinī</s>, the places <s>Vātsyagulma</s>, <s>Cakorapura</s>, and others are situated. North of <s>Ujjayinī</s> [are] <s>Daśapura</s>, <s>Mālavanagara</s>, <s>Caṭṭa</s>, <s>Śivasthāneśvara</s>, and others, up to <s>Meru</s>.

body.text:
sarve grahāḥ karaṇāgatāḥ bhūmadhyasamadakṣiṇottararekhāyām bhavanti | pūrvabhāgavyavasthitāḥ prathamataram eva ravim paśyanti, ataḥ deśāntaraphalam apanīyate | paścimabhāge [vyavasthitāḥ] cireṇa paśyanti, ataḥ tatra deśāntaraphalam kṣipyate | svadeśākṣasamarekhākṣavivarabhāgaiḥ trairāśikam ã yadi cakrāṃśakaiḥ bhūparidhiyojanāni labhyante

  25,
 tadā akṣāṃśāvivarabhāgaiḥ kim iti, samadakṣiṇottararekhāntarālayojanāni bhavanti koṭyātmakāni | svadeśasthānataḥ tiryagvyavasthitojjayinyādisthānam | tasya antarālayojanāni lokāt avagatāni karṇaḥ | karṇakoṭivargaviśeṣamūlam bhujayojanāni | tataḥ yadi vyāsārdhatulyāvalaṃbake[na bhūparidhiḥ tadā iṣṭāvalaṃbakena kā iti, spaṣṭabhūparidhiḥ | punar yadi] spaṣṭabhūparidhinā grahabhuktiḥ labhyate deśāntarayojanaiḥ kā bhuktiḥ iti deśāntarphalam labhyate | pūrvavat

children.translated_text: positive or negative. // 14 //

body.translated_text: All planets computed by calculation are [given for positions] on the north-south line through the center of the Earth. Those situated in the eastern part see the Sun earlier, hence the longitudinal correction is subtracted. Those situated in the western part see it later, hence there the longitudinal correction is added. By the rule of three with the degrees of the difference between one's own latitude-line and the prime-meridian latitude: if...

body.text: bhagolasya dṛśyādṛśyabhāgau
body.translated_text: The visible and invisible halves of the stellar sphere

body.text: bhagoladṛśyādṛśyajñāpanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: In order to demonstrate the visible and invisible [halves] of the stellar sphere, he says:

children.text: bhūvyāsārdhena ūnam dṛśyam deśāt samāt bhagolārdham |
children.translated_text: Less than [full] by the Earth's semi-diameter — that much of the half of the stellar sphere is visible from a level place;
the [other] half, concealed by the Earth, is more than [half] by the Earth's semi-diameter. // 15 //

body.text: bhuvaḥ vyāsaḥ bhūvyāsaḥ tasya ardham bhūvyāsārdham, 525 | tena ūnam bhagolārdham dṛśyam upalabhyate | kasmāt? samāt deśāt | anantaritaḥ samaḥ, mahādridrumādyunnatapadārtharahitaḥ deśaḥ samaḥ iti | ardham bhūmicchannam na dṛśyate bhūvyāsārdhena adhikam adṛśyam |
body.translated_text: The diameter of the Earth is '<s>bhūvyāsa</s>'; its half is the Earth's semi-diameter = 525 [<s>yojanas</s>]. Less by that amount — that much of the stellar half-sphere is seen. From where? From a level place. 'Level' (<s>sama</s>) means unobstructed — a place devoid of tall mountains, trees, and other elevated objects. The [other] half, concealed by the Earth, is not seen — it is more than [half] by the Earth's semi-diameter, hence invisible.

body.text:
etat jijñāsuḥ bhūgolapṛṣṭhāvagāhi sūtram prasārya pūrvakṣitije aparakṣitije [ca] badhnīyāt | bhūpṛṣṭhasthitasya draṣṭuḥ prasāritasūtrānusāriṇī dṛṣṭiḥ yāti | tatra [pūrva]pradeśe jyotīṃṣi ardhoditāni paśyati, paścāt ardhāstamitāni [paścati] | evam bhūvyāsārdhena ūnam [golārdham] golasūtrāntarālasthitam dṛśyam | yat etat adṛśyam golārdham golasūtrāntarālam tat bhūvyāsārdhādhikam | etat samāyām bhuvi | yaḥ punar draṣṭā tuṃgaśailamastake bhavati tat
śailapramāṇādhikam tasya adṛśyam bhavati | vidyādharādayaḥ viyati dūre sthitāḥ prabhūtam jyotiścakram paśyanti, [yasmāt] upari dūrasthitasya nirvirodhaprasāraṇā dṛṣṭiḥ bhavati | atidūre sthitaḥ brahmā sarvadā vivasvantam paśyati |
body.translated_text: One who wishes to know this should extend a cord on the surface of the Earth-sphere, binding it at the eastern horizon and the western horizon. The sight of an observer standing on the Earth's surface follows along the extended cord. There, in the eastern region, he sees the luminaries half-risen; afterward, [in the west, he sees them] half-set. Thus, the [visible] half-sphere, less by the Earth's semi-diameter, situated within the horizon-cord interval...

body.text: bhūpṛṣṭhavyavasthitānām bhūvyāsārdhonabhapañjarārdhadarśinām svāt pramāṇāt satatam divasaḥ hīyate, niśā vardhate | tadartham
body.translated_text: For those standing on the Earth's surface who see a half-stellar-cage less by the Earth's semi-diameter, the day constantly decreases from its [standard

body.text: trairāśikam ã yadi ravikakṣyāyām ṣaṣṭiḥ nāḍyaḥ labhyante tadā bhūvyāsārdhayojanaiḥ 525 kiyatyaḥ | labdhena dviguṇena sarvadā hīnaḥ divasaḥ adhikā rātriḥ || 15 ||
body.translated_text: measure and the night increases. For that purpose,] the rule of three: if in the Sun's orbit sixty <s>nāḍīs</s> are obtained, then with 525 <s>yojanas</s> of Earth's semi-diameter, how many? By twice the result, the day is always diminished and the night increased. // 15 //

body.text: meruvaḍavāmukhasthānām bhagolabhramaṇadarśanam
body.translated_text: The observation of the stellar sphere's revolution by those at <s>Meru</s> and <s>Baḍavāmukha</s>

body.text: merubaḍavāmukhanivāsinām darśanārtham āha ã
body.translated_text: In order to show [what is observed by] the inhabitants of <s>Meru</s> and <s>Baḍavāmukha</s>, he says:

children.text: devāḥ paśyanti bhagolārdham udaṅ merusaṃsthitāḥ savyam |
children.translated_text: The gods, situated at <s>Meru</s> in the north, see the northern half of the stellar sphere [moving] clockwise;
the deceased (<s>preta</s>), at <s>Baḍavāmukha</s> in the south, [see] the [southern] half moving counter-clockwise. // 16 //

body.text: udaṅ merusthitāḥ devāḥ bhagolasya uttaram
body.translated_text: The gods situated at <s>Meru</s> in the north

body.text:
ardham savyam pradakṣiṇagatim paśyanti | dvitīyam ardham dakṣiṇam jyotiścakrasya apasavyam apradakṣiṇagatim baḍavāmukha[sthitāḥ] pretāḥ paśyanti | [sthalajalasandhau sthitvā etat ācāryaḥ pratipādayati | tat apekṣayā hi merubaḍavāmukhayoḥ uttaradakṣiṇatvam | na merubaḍavāmukhasthānām diṅniyamaḥ asti |] sūryagatyapekṣayā prācyādivyavahāraḥ | yatra vivasvān udeti sā prācī, [yatra astameti sā pratīcī]
| [na tathā merubaḍavāmukhasthānām api, paritaḥ sarvatra raveḥ udayāstamayasambhavāt |]
body.translated_text: see the northern half of the stellar sphere [moving] clockwise, i.e., with a rightward motion. The second half, the southern [half] of the stellar wheel, [moving] counter-clockwise, i.e., with a leftward motion — the deceased (<s>preta</s>) situated at <s>Baḍavāmukha</s> see [that]. [The <s>ācārya</s> demonstrates this while standing at the junction of land and water. For with reference to that, the northward and southward positions of <s>Meru</s> and <s>Baḍavāmukha</s>...

body.text:
deśāntaravyavadhānāt anyathā bhacakrārdhadarśanam bhavati | kaścit puruṣaḥ uttareṇa gataḥ deśāntaram eti tathātve dhruvam upari ārohitam paśyati, krameṇa merum prāptasya upari dhruvaḥ bhavati | meroḥ uttareṇa dakṣiṇena dhruvaḥ avalambate | etat uttarāyaḥśalākāgrasvastikam upari nidhāya dakṣiṇāyaḥśalākāgrasvastikam ca adhomukham nidhāya darśayet | tathā laṅkāsthasya yaḥ viṣuvat mārgapradeśaḥ pūrvāparaḥ pratibhāsate sa merusthānām kṣitijāsaktaḥ
| evam baḍavāmukhasthānām api cakravat bhāskaraḥ pratibhāsate || 16 ||
body.translated_text: Due to the intervening longitudinal distance, the observation of half the stellar sphere occurs differently. A certain person, having gone northward, goes to another longitude; in that situation, he sees the pole star (<s>dhruva</s>) ascended overhead. Progressively, for one who has reached <s>Meru</s>, the pole star is overhead. North of <s>Meru</s>, on the southern side, the pole star hangs down. This should be demonstrated by placing the northern iron-rod-tip intersection above and the southern iron-rod-tip intersection facing downward. Likewise, for one situated at <s>Laṅkā</s>, the region of the equatorial path that appears [extending] east-west — that, for those situated at <s>Meru</s>, is attached to the horizon. Similarly, for those situated at <s>Baḍavāmukha</s> (the south pole) too, the Sun appears [revolving] like a wheel. // 16 //

body.text: devāsurapitṛnarāṇām dinapramāṇam
body.translated_text: The day-measure of gods, demons, ancestors, and humans

body.text: merubaḍavāmukhasthāḥ kiyantam kālam ravim paśyanti iti āha ã
body.translated_text: He states for how long those situated at <s>Meru</s> and <s>Baḍavāmukha</s> see the Sun:

children.text: ravivarṣārdham devāḥ paśyanti uditam ravim tathā pretāḥ |
children.translated_text: The gods see the Sun risen for half a solar year; likewise the departed spirits (<s>pretas</s>);

children.text: śaśimāsārdham pitaraḥ śaśigāḥ, kudinārdham iha manujāḥ || 17 ||
children.translated_text: the ancestors (<s>pitaras</s>) [who are] Moon-dwellers, for half a lunar month; and the humans here [see it] for half a terrestrial day. // 17 //

body.text: devāḥ merunivāsinaḥ meṣādiṣu ṣaṭsu rāśiṣu samudgatam sūryam ravivarṣārdham paśyanti ṣaṇmāsān yāvat iti arthaḥ, pradakṣiṇam cakravat bhramantam kṣitijāsaktam krameṇa caturviṃśatikrāntibhāgān yāvat parityaktakṣitijam paśyanti | evam pretāḥ api ravivarṣārdham eva sakṛt udgatam sūryam paśyanti dakṣiṇagole ṣaṭsu rāśiṣu |
body.translated_text: The gods, who are residents of <s>Meru</s>, see the Sun risen in the six signs beginning with <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries) for half a solar year — meaning for six months — revolving clockwise like a wheel, touching the horizon, progressively [rising] up to twenty-four degrees of declination beyond the horizon. Likewise, the departed spirits (<s>pretas</s>) too see the Sun risen once for exactly half a solar year, in the six signs of the southern hemisphere.

body.text:
śaśimāsārdham pitaraḥ śaśigāḥ, śaśinam gacchanti iti śaśigāḥ, candralokanivāsinaḥ pitaraḥ śaśinaḥ māsārdham pañcadaśatithayaḥ etāvantam kālam paśyanti | pitṝṇām amāvāsyāyām upari savitā bhavati | [tat] teṣām aharmadhyam | tataḥ yathā yathā savitā pratipadādiṣu parataḥ avalambate tathā tathā pitṝṇām madhyāhnottarabhāgaḥ, rāśitrayāntaritaḥ astam eti, astamitaḥ pakṣeṇa rāśiṣaḍantaritaḥ prācyām udeti | ataḥ teṣām pakṣaḥ ahaḥ, pakṣaḥ rātriḥ iti
| kudinārdham iha manujāḥ | kudinam bhūdinam ravyudayāt ravyudayam yāvat, tadardham iha manujāḥ paśyanti | sarvam yathāvat sthitam gole pradarśayet iti || 17 ||
body.translated_text: 'The ancestors, Moon-dwellers, for half a lunar month': Those who go to the Moon are 'Moon-dwellers' (<s>śaśigāḥ</s>) — the ancestors (<s>pitaras</s>) who dwell in the lunar world see [the Sun] for half a lunar month, [that is,] fifteen <s>tithis</s> — for that much time. For the ancestors, at the new moon (<s>amāvāsyā</s>), the Sun is above them. [That] is their midday. Thereafter, as the Sun progressively descends on the first day of the bright fortnight and onward, that becomes the afternoon portion for the ancestors; [the Sun], separated by three signs, sets; having set, after a fortnight, separated by six signs, it rises in the east. Therefore, for them, a fortnight is the day and a fortnight is the night. 'Humans here for half a terrestrial day': A terrestrial day (<s>kudina</s>) is an Earth-day, from sunrise to sunrise. Half of that is [the duration for which] humans here see [the Sun]. Everything should be demonstrated as it is on the [armillary] sphere. // 17 //

body.text: khagole kṣitijamaṇḍalam
body.translated_text: The horizon circle on the celestial sphere

body.text: khagole kṣitijamaṇḍalapradarśanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of demonstrating the horizon circle on the celestial sphere, he says:

children.text: pūrvāparam adhaūrdhvam maṇḍalam atha dakṣiṇottaram ca eva |
children.translated_text: The east-west [circle extends] below and above; and then likewise the north-south [circle];
the horizon, situated at the sides as a girdle, is where the rising and setting of the stars [occurs]. // 18 //

body.text:
pūrvāparamaṇḍalam tat iha khagolapramāṇam | sa eva ūrdhvam uparyadhovagāhi sarvabhapañjarāṇām | tathā dakṣiṇottaram anyat maṇḍalam tāvatpramāṇam, dakṣiṇottarāvagāhi yāmya uttaramaṇḍalam upari adhaḥ ca janitasvastikam | kṣitijam samapārśvastham tathā anyat maṇḍalam tāvat eva | samapārśvāvagāhi parikaravat dikcatuṣṭayajanitasvastikam kṣitija iti ucyate | bhānām yatra udayāstamayau | yatra maṇḍale bhānām udayāstamayau lakṣyete | harijam
iti kaiścit ucyate | ayam khagolaḥ sarvabhapañjarāṇām bahiḥ avatiṣṭhate || 18 ||
body.translated_text: The east-west circle — that here has the measure of the celestial sphere. That same [circle extends] upward, passing through the upper and lower [points], for all the planetary cage-frames. Likewise the north-south [circle] — another circle of the same measure, passing through the south and north, the north-south circle, generating intersections above and below. 'The horizon situated at the sides as a girdle' — likewise another circle of the same measure, passing through the sides like a girdle, generating intersections in the four cardinal directions — this is called the horizon (<s>kṣitija</s>). 'Where the rising and setting of the stars [occurs]': the circle on which the rising and setting of the stars is observed. It is called '<s>harija</s>' (horizon) by some. This celestial sphere stands outside all the planetary cage-frames. // 18 //

body.text: unmaṇḍalam
body.translated_text: The prime vertical (<s>unmaṇḍala</s>)

body.text: unmaṇḍalapradarśanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of demonstrating the prime vertical, he says:

children.text: pūrvāparadiglagnam kṣitijāt akṣāgrayoḥ ca lagnam yat |
children.translated_text: That which is attached to the east-west direction, and attached to the horizon at the [points of] latitude and <s>agrā</s> (amplitude) —

children.text: unmaṇḍalam bhavet tat kṣayavṛddhī yatra divasaniśoḥ || 19 ||
children.translated_text: that is the prime vertical (<s>unmaṇḍala</s>), where the increase and decrease of day and night [occur]. // 19 //

body.text: dakṣiṇottarakṣitijasvastikāt yāmya uttaramaṇḍale svadeśākṣabhāgatulye antare vedhe kṛtvā lohaśalākāgre praveśya golam nidadhyāt | tataḥ unmaṇḍalam darśayet | pūrvāparadiglagnam pūrvāparayoḥ diśoḥ lagnam | kṣitijāt akṣāgrayoḥ ca lagnam yat | dakṣiṇottarakṣitijasvastikayoḥ upari adhaḥ svadeśākṣabhāgatulye antare lagnam kārayet | tat unmaṇḍalam | udayamaṇḍalam unmaṇḍalam | yatra maṇḍale divasasya rātreḥ ca kṣayavṛddhī lakṣyete |
body.translated_text: From the north-south horizon intersection, on the north-south circle, at an interval equal to the latitude-degrees of one's own locality, having made a bore-hole and inserting the iron rod-tip, one should place the sphere. Then, one should demonstrate the prime vertical. 'Attached to the east-west direction' — attached in the eastern and western directions. 'And attached to the horizon at the [points of] latitude and <s>agrā</s>': At an interval equal to the latitude-degrees of one's own locality, above and below the north-south horizon intersections, one should make the attachment. That is the prime vertical (<s>unmaṇḍala</s>). The rising-circle is the prime vertical — the circle on which the increase and decrease of day and night are observed.

body.text:
viṣuvati unmaṇḍalakṣitijayoḥ ekatvāt divasaniśoḥ kṣayavṛddhī na staḥ | viṣuvataḥ uttareṇa unmaṇḍalam upari kṣitijam adhaḥ avatiṣṭhate | tasmāt uttaragole aprāpte eva unmaṇḍalam [savitā] caradalaghaṭikāpramāṇena udeti | paścāt unmaṇḍalam atikrāntaḥ astam eti | ataḥ divasaḥ uttaragole vardhate | dakṣiṇagole unmaṇḍalam atikrāntaḥ kṣitijāt udeti | aprāptaḥ eva astameti | ataḥ dakṣiṇagole rātriḥ upacīyate | ataḥ tattulyā divasaniśoḥ kṣayavṛddhī | tadartham
trairāśikam ã yadi ṣaṣṭyā grahabhuktiḥ labhyate, tadā caradalaghaṭikābhiḥ kiyatī iti | labdham uttaragole ravau udaye viśodhayet | yāmye viparītam | evam uttaradiśi vyavasthitānām krameṇa divasaniśoḥ mahatyau kṣayavṛddhī bhavataḥ | yatra deśe raviḥ mithunāntasthaḥ na astam eti, ṣaṣṭiḥ nāḍyaḥ divasaḥ, tatra triṃśadghaṭikāḥ caram, pañcadaśaghaṭikāḥ carārdham | tasya kāṣṭhasya jyā carajyā | tayā viparītakarmaṇā kṣitijyā ānīyate ã yadi vyāsārdhasya iyam [vyāsārdhatulyā]
carajyā tadā mithunāntasvāhorātrārdhasya kā iti mithunāntasvāhorātrārdhatulyā kṣitijyā labhyate | tasyāḥ kṣitijyāyāḥ mithunāntāpakramajyāyāḥ ca vargayuteḥ mūlam arkāgrā trijyātulyā | tena tatra deśe yāmya uttare kṣitijāt upari krameṇa [sama]maṇḍalam avagāhya khamadhyāt dakṣiṇena dvicatvāriṃśadbhāge [yāmya uttaram atikramya] tataḥ prathamodaye punar kṣitijam āpnoti ca eva | tatra ṣaṣtiḥ nāḍyaḥ divasaḥ upalakṣyate | svārkāgrataḥ [kṣitijyā | tadartham trairāśikam]
ã arkāgrayā iṣṭatulyayā kṣitijyā labhyate vyāsārdhena kim iti | guṇakabhājakayoḥ tulyatvāt naṣṭayoḥ kṣitijyāpramāṇā akṣajyā bhavati | tat katham? akṣaḥ ṣaṭṣaṣṭibhāgāḥ | tatra deśe vyabhicārāt grahagatiḥ | uttareṇa tasmāt iyam vyavasthā na asti iti || 19 ||
body.translated_text: At the equinox, when the prime vertical and the horizon are one, there is no increase or decrease of day and night. North of the equator, the prime vertical is above and the horizon below. Therefore, in the northern hemisphere, even before reaching the prime vertical, [the Sun] rises by the measure of the <s>caradala</s> (half-equation of daylight) <s>ghaṭikās</s>. Afterward, having crossed the prime vertical, it sets. Therefore, the day increases in the northern hemisphere. In the southern hemisphere, having crossed the prime vertical, [the Sun] rises from the horizon; not having reached [the prime vertical], it sets. Therefore, in the southern hemisphere, the night increases. Hence, the corresponding increase and decrease of day and night. For this purpose, the rule of three [is applied]: if by sixty [<s>ghaṭikās</s>] the planet's daily motion is obtained, then by the <s>caradala</s> <s>ghaṭikās</s>, how much? The result, in the northern hemisphere, is subtracted from the Sun at sunrise; in the southern [hemisphere], the reverse. Thus, for those situated to the north, progressively the increase and decrease of day and night become great. At the locality where the Sun situated at the end of <s>Mithuna</s> (Gemini) does not set, sixty <s>nāḍīs</s> constitute the day; there, thirty <s>ghaṭikās</s> is the <s>cara</s> (equation of daylight), fifteen <s>ghaṭikās</s> is the <s>carārdha</s> (half-equation). The sine of that arc is the <s>carajyā</s> (equation-of-daylight sine). By the inverse operation from that, the horizon-sine (<s>kṣitijyā</s>) is derived: if the semi-diameter [has] this <s>carajyā</s> equal to the semi-diameter, then for the half-day-circle of the end of <s>Mithuna</s>, what? — the <s>kṣitijyā</s> equal to the half-day-circle of the end of <s>Mithuna</s> is obtained. The square-root of the sum of the squares of that <s>kṣitijyā</s> and the declination-sine of the end of <s>Mithuna</s> is the Sun's amplitude (<s>arkāgrā</s>), equal to the radius (<s>trijyā</s>). Therefore, at that locality, from the horizon to the south and north, [the Sun] ascends progressively, passing through the prime vertical, and at forty-two degrees south of the zenith, [having crossed to the north-south, and] from the first rising, reaches the horizon again. There, sixty <s>nāḍīs</s> are observed as the day. From one's Sun-amplitude, [one derives] the <s>kṣitijyā</s>. For this purpose, the rule of three [is applied]: if by the <s>arkāgrā</s> of the desired [amount], the <s>kṣitijyā</s> is obtained, then by the semi-diameter, what? Since the multiplier and divisor are equal, having cancelled them, the <s>kṣitijyā</s>-measure becomes the latitude-sine (<s>akṣajyā</s>). How then? The latitude is sixty-six degrees. At that locality, the planetary motion deviates. North of that, this arrangement does not hold. // 19 //

body.text: khagolāpekṣayā draṣṭuḥ sthitiḥ
body.translated_text: The position of the observer relative to the celestial sphere

body.text: prācyādivyavasthāpratipādanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of establishing the cardinal directions, he says:

children.text: pūrvāparadigrekhā adhaḥ ca ūrdhvā dakṣiṇottarasthā ca |
children.translated_text: The east-west line, and the line [extending] below and above, and the north-south [line] —

children.text: etāsām sampātaḥ draṣṭā yasmin bhavet deśe || 20 ||
children.translated_text: the intersection of these [is the point where] the observer is situated, at whatever locality. // 20 //

body.text: pūrvāpararekhā, adhaḥ ca ūrdhvā ca yā rekhā, dakṣiṇottarasthā ca | ca[kāraḥ] samuccaye | etāsām rekhāṇām sampātaḥ ekatra yogaḥ, yasmin deśe draṣṭā tatra tatra tāsām sampātaḥ |
body.translated_text: The east-west line, and the line below and above, and the north-south [line]. The conjunction 'and' (<s>ca</s>) serves as aggregation. The intersection of these lines — the conjunction at one point — at whatever locality the observer is, there is their intersection.

body.text:
tasmāt draṣṭṛvaśāt digvyavasthā | yatra draṣṭā ravim udgacchan paśyati sā prācī, yatra [raviḥ] madhyāhnam karoti sā dakṣiṇā, yatra astam eti sā parā, yatra ardharātram karoti sā uttarā | sarveṣām uttaraḥ meruḥ | laṅkānivāsinām yadā madhyāhne raviḥ bhavati romakanivāsinām udeti | tatra laṅkāpradeśe teṣām prācī | tadapekṣayā svasthānāt uttaraḥ meruḥ pratibhāsate | yadā romake madhyāhnaḥ tadā siddhapuranivāsinām udayaḥ [tatra romakapradeśe
teṣām prācī] | tadapekṣayā teṣām svasthānāt uttaraḥ meruḥ | evam yamakoṭyām api |
body.translated_text: Therefore, the establishment of the cardinal directions depends on the observer. Where the observer sees the Sun rising, that is the east; where [the Sun] reaches midday, that is the south; where it sets, that is the west; where it reaches midnight, that is the north. <s>Meru</s> is to the north of all. For the residents of <s>Laṅkā</s>, when the Sun is at midday, for the residents of <s>Romaka</s> it rises. There, the <s>Laṅkā</s> region is their east. Relative to that, <s>Meru</s> appears to the north from their own location. When it is midday at <s>Romaka</s>, it is sunrise for the residents of <s>Siddhapura</s> — there, the <s>Romaka</s> region is their east. Relative to that, <s>Meru</s> is to the north from their own location. Likewise at <s>Yamakoṭi</s> also.

body.text: bhūmau yāvattāvatpramāṇam vṛttam ālikhya pūrvāhṇe [aparāhṇe ca] chāyām lakṣayet | yatra pradeśe śaṅkucchāyā vṛttam praviśati sā paścimā | yatra niryāti sā prācī | tadagrayoḥ matsyam utpādya tanmukhapucchaspṛksūtram prasārayet | sā dakṣiṇottarā dig bhavati | athavā tricchāyāgramatsyadvayamukhapucchaspṛksūtradvayasampātaḥ uttarā dakṣiṇā ca | [athavā dik] prasādhanīyā citrāsvātyoḥ || 20 ||
body.translated_text: On the ground, having drawn a circle of a desired size, one should observe the shadow in the forenoon [and afternoon]. The point where the gnomon-shadow enters the circle — that is the west. Where it exits — that is the east. From the tips of those [two points], having generated a fish-figure, one should extend a thread touching the mouth and tail [of the fish]. That is the north-south direction. Alternatively, the intersection of two threads touching the mouth and tail of the two fish-figures [generated] from three shadow-tips — that is the north and south. [Alternatively,] the direction may be determined from [the stars] <s>Citrā</s> (Spica) and <s>Svāti</s> (Arcturus). // 20 //

body.text: dṛṅmaṇḍalam dṛkkṣepamaṇḍalam ca
body.translated_text: The sight-circle and the <s>dṛkkṣepa</s> (sight-deflection) circle

body.text: dṛṅmaṇḍaladṛkkṣepamaṇḍalasvarūpam āha ã
body.translated_text: He states the nature of the sight-circle and the sight-deflection circle:

children.text: ūrdhvam adhastāt draṣṭuḥ jñeyam dṛṅmaṇḍalam grahābhimukham |
children.translated_text: The sight-circle (<s>dṛṅmaṇḍala</s>), above and below the observer, is to be known as [directed] toward the planet;
the sight-deflection circle (<s>dṛkkṣepamaṇḍala</s>) too, attached to the east, is [the ascendant] minus three signs. // 21 //

body.text:
dṛṅmaṇḍalam [draṣṭuḥ ūrdhvam adhastāt] grahābhimukham [bhavati] | yatra draṣṭā bhavati tatra asya madhyam, yatra grahaḥ tatra asya paridhiḥ, yāvān dṛggrahayoḥ antaram tāvatā viṣkambhārdhena dṛṅmaṇḍalam pradṛśyam | tat eva madhyāhnasthite grahe dṛkkṣepamaṇḍalam bhavati | dṛkkṣepamaṇḍalam api | samamaṇḍalamadhyāt dakṣiṇena uttareṇa vā yatra grahābhimukham dṛṣṭeḥ kṣepaḥ tatra yaḥ mahāpramāṇakakṣyaḥ grahaḥ sa stokataram kṣipyate,
alpapramāṇakakṣyaḥ bahutaram kṣipyate iti | etat madhyāhne dṛgjyāpramāṇavyāsārdhena samamaṇḍalamadhyāt badhnīyāt | asya ānayanopāyaḥ ã prāglagnam syāt trirāśyūnam | parvakālaghaṭikāḥ pūrvāhṇe dinārdhāt śodhayet | śeṣaprāṇān trairāśikānītaravibhuktalaṅkodayaprāṇaiḥ ūnīkuryāt | śeṣebhyaḥ yāvat laṅkodayaprāṇāḥ śudhyanti tāvat śodhyāḥ | tānvantaḥ eva rāśayaḥ viśodhyante | śeṣaprāṇān triṃśatā guṇayet, aśuddhalaṅkodayena vibhajet, labdham bhāgādi
pūrvaviśodhitaiḥ eva śodhayet | pūrvāhṇe madhyalagnam bhavati | aparāhṇe adhikatvāt raveḥ yāvantaḥ laṅkodayāḥ viśudhyanti tāvantaḥ prakṣipya lagnam kriyate | ācāryeṇa sthūlaprakṛtyā iṣṭaghaṭikābhiḥ pūrvalagnam lagnavidhinā kṛtvā trirāśyūnam kriyate, madhyalagnam bhavati iti | rāśayaḥ laṅkodayaiḥ madhyam avagāhante iti laṅkodayaiḥ yat madhyalagnam tat sūkṣmam iti | tasya apakramakāṣṭham svadeśākṣabhāgayutam samadiśoḥ bhinnadiśoḥ viśuddham
khamadhyaravikakṣyāntarālam bhavati | tasya jīvā madhyajyā iti ucyate | candrasya apakramakāṣṭham vikṣepayutam viyutam kriyate | yataḥ vimaṇḍale candraḥ tataḥ akṣabhāgayutaviyutasya jyā candramadhyajyā bhavati | anayā atra madhyajyā vyākhyātā || 21 ||
body.translated_text: The sight-circle [extends] from the observer upward and downward, directed toward the planet. Where the observer is, there is its center; where the planet is, there is its circumference; the semi-diameter of the sight-circle is equal to the distance between the observer and the planet — [this is] to be displayed. That same [circle], when the planet is situated at the meridian, becomes the sight-deflection circle (<s>dṛkkṣepamaṇḍala</s>). 'The sight-deflection circle too': From the center of the prime vertical (<s>samamaṇḍala</s>), to the south or north, wherever the sight is deflected toward the planet — there, a planet in a large orbit is deflected slightly, and a planet in a small orbit is deflected more. This, at midday, should be bound with a semi-diameter of the measure of the sight-sine (<s>dṛgjyā</s>) from the center of the prime vertical. The method for deriving it: 'Attached to the east, [the ascendant] minus three signs.' The <s>parva</s>-time (syzygy) <s>ghaṭikās</s> are subtracted from the half-day in the forenoon. The remaining <s>prāṇas</s> are reduced by the <s>Laṅkā</s>-rising <s>prāṇas</s> derived by rule of three from the Sun's traversed [degrees]. From the remainder, as many <s>Laṅkā</s>-rising <s>prāṇas</s> as are subtracted — that many signs are subtracted. The remaining <s>prāṇas</s> are multiplied by thirty, divided by the unexhausted <s>Laṅkā</s>-rising [<s>prāṇas</s>]; the quotient as degrees and so forth is subtracted from the previously subtracted [signs] — [this gives] the meridian ascendant (<s>madhyalagna</s>) in the forenoon. In the afternoon, since the Sun has advanced, as many <s>Laṅkā</s>-rising [<s>prāṇas</s>] as are exhausted — that many are added and the ascendant is computed. The <s>ācārya</s> (<s>Āryabhaṭa</s>), in approximate fashion, having computed the eastern ascendant by the ascendant-method with the desired <s>ghaṭikās</s>, subtracts three signs — [that] becomes the meridian ascendant. Since the signs enter the meridian by the <s>Laṅkā</s>-rising [times], the meridian ascendant [computed] by the <s>Laṅkā</s>-rising [times] is precise. The declination-arc of that [meridian ascendant], added to the latitude-degrees when in the same direction, or subtracted when in different directions, becomes the interval between the zenith and the Sun's orbit. The sine of that is called the meridian-sine (<s>madhyajyā</s>). For the Moon, the declination-arc is combined with or separated from the deflection (<s>vikṣepa</s>). Since the Moon is on the deflection-circle, therefore the sine of that [combined or separated value] with the latitude-degrees becomes the Moon's meridian-sine. By this, the meridian-sine is explained here. // 21 //

body.text: svayaṃvahagolayantram
body.translated_text: The self-rotating sphere instrument (<s>svayaṃvahagolayantram</s>)

body.text: svayaṃvahagolayantrapratipādanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of teaching the self-rotating sphere instrument, he says:

children.text: kāṣṭhamayam samavṛttam samantataḥ samagurum laghum golam |
children.translated_text: A sphere made of wood, uniformly round, of equal weight all around, and light —

children.text: pāratatailajalaiḥ tam bhramayet svadhiyā ca kālasamam || 22 ||
children.translated_text: that [sphere] should be made to rotate, by one's own ingenuity, in mercury, oil, and water, keeping pace with time. // 22 //

body.text:
kāṣṭhaiḥ nirmitam kāṣṭhamayam śrīparṇyādibhiḥ pūrvavat | samavṛttam | sarveṣu pradeśeṣu [samam], na hīnādhikam iti | samagurum | samantataḥ samā gurutā kāryā | yadi atimātraguruḥ bhavati pāṣāṇavat niścalaḥ syāt, [mahatā kālena bhramati iti ataḥ] samavṛttam samagurum | laghum atra api samaśabdaḥ prayoktavyaḥ | etat guṇaviśiṣṭam golam katham bhramayet? pāratatailajalaiḥ iti | svadhiyā ca svakīyaprajñayā ca tam bhramayet | kālasamam kālena
samam kālasamam | kālasamam ahorātrasamam yathā bhramati tathā bhramayet | tat yathā ã ṣaṣṭighaṭikāṅkitasvāhorātramaṇḍale kanyātulāsandhipradeśe kīlakam īṣat unnatam ekam kārayet | siddhapūrvāparadakṣiṇottarasthāne jalapātram ekam sthāpayet | pātram ca samam vattam dīrgham [tala]madhyanihitasūkṣmacchidram ghaṭikāṣaṣṭyā jalapūrṇam yathā riktam bhavati tathā svadhiyā prasādhya tataḥ karma kriyate | yāvat pātrāt udakam sravati tāvat gurutvāt
alābuḥ jalavaśāt adhogacchan golam ākarṣati | evam sakṛt yuktaḥ golaḥ paramārthabhagolavat ahorātre bhramati | prathamam tāmrakīlake pāśakasūtrasya ekam agram badhvā golayantram adhastāt prabhṛti pariveṣṭya tatra eva pradeśe sūtram prāpayet iti kramaḥ || 22 ||
body.translated_text: Made of wood — wooden, from <s>śrīparṇī</s> (Gmelina arborea) and the like, as before. 'Evenly round' — uniform in all parts, neither deficient nor excessive. 'Of uniform weight' (<s>samaguru</s>) — the heaviness should be made uniform in all directions. If it is excessively heavy, it would be immovable like a stone; [if too heavy,] it would rotate only after a long time — therefore, evenly round and of uniform weight. The word '<s>sama</s>' (even) should be applied to '<s>laghu</s>' (light) here as well. How should one rotate this sphere endowed with [such] qualities? By means of mercury, oil, and water. And by one’s own intelligence — by one’s own sagacity, one should make it rotate. 'In time-correspondence' (<s>kālasamam</s>) — corresponding to time, meaning equal to a day-and-night — one should make it rotate such that it revolves [once in a day]. That is: on the day-circle marked with sixty <s>ghaṭikās</s>, at the junction of <s>Kanyā</s> (Virgo) and <s>Tulā</s> (Libra), one should make a peg slightly raised. At the established east-west-south-north location, one should place a water-vessel. The vessel should be even, round, elongated, with a fine hole set in the middle of the bottom, prepared by one’s own skill such that when filled with water it becomes empty in sixty <s>ghaṭikās</s>; then the operation is performed. As water flows from the vessel, the gourd (<s>alābu</s>), descending due to gravity through the force of the water, pulls the sphere. Thus, once set in motion, the sphere rotates in one day-and-night like the true stellar sphere. The procedure: first, having tied one end of a dice-string to the copper peg and wound the sphere-instrument from the bottom upward, one should bring the string to that very [starting] point. || 22 ||

body.text: akṣakṣetram
body.translated_text: The latitude-triangle (<s>akṣakṣetra</s>)

body.text: viṣuvat jyāpradeśapratipādanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: To explain the position of the equatorial sine (<s>viṣuvatjyā</s>), he says:

children.translated_text: In the hemisphere-bowl of the observer’s sphere (<s>dṛggola</s>), one should determine the stellar sphere’s hemisphere with the half-sine (<s>jyārdha</s>);
the equatorial sine (<s>viṣujjīvā</s>) is the latitude-base (<s>akṣabhujā</s>); and its perpendicular (<s>koṭi</s>) is the plumb-line (<s>avalambaka</s>). || 23 ||

body.text:
dṛggolārdham ghaṭakapālavat avasthitatvāt dṛggolārdhakapālam | bhagolārdham eva kevalam dṛśyate | yena vyavahāraḥ dṛśyaḥ | bhagolārdham jātau ekavacanam | jyārdhena vikalpayet | bhūmau vṛttam ālikhya pūrvāparadakṣiṇottaradikcihnitam kṛtvā ekaikasmin caturthabhāge rāśitrayam aṅkayet | punar ekaikaḥ rāśiḥ aṣṭadhā vibhajet | tatra sūtrāṇi prasārayitavyāni | tāni jyāsūtrāṇi | tadardhāni jyārdhāni | athavā anyaḥ vikalpakramaḥ | viṣuvajjīvākṣabhujā
| samamaṇḍalasya viṣuvataḥ uttareṇa akṣatulyāntare avasthitatvāt akṣaḥ iti ucyate | tasya akṣakāṣṭhasya bhujā, akṣajyā viṣuvajjyā iti paryāyāḥ | vyāsārdham karṇaḥ | bhujākarṇakṛtiviśeṣamūlam avalambakaḥ | sā koṭiḥ iti | etat gole pradarśayet | samamaṇḍalamadhyāt dakṣiṇena ākṣajyātulye antare sūtrasya ekam agram badhvā graham prāpayet | saḥ avalambakaḥ | bhujākoṭivargayogasya mūlam karṇaḥ vyāsārdham iti | evam anyatra api dṛggolārdhe kalpitajyārdheṣu

children.translated_text: the arrangement of base, perpendicular, and hypotenuse should be conceived. || 23 ||

body.translated_text: The hemisphere of the observer’s sphere (<s>dṛggola</s>), being situated like a pot-bowl, is the '<s>dṛggolārdhakapala</s>' (hemisphere-bowl of the observer’s sphere). Only the hemisphere of the stellar sphere (<s>bhagola</s>) is visible — [only] that with which practical affairs are observed. '<s>Bhagolārdham</s>' — the singular is used in the generic sense. 'One should determine with the half-sine': Having drawn a circle on the ground, marked with the east, west, south, and north directions, one should mark three signs in each quadrant. Then each sign should be divided into eight parts. Strings should be extended there — those are the sine-strings; their halves are the half-sines (<s>jyārdhas</s>). Or alternatively, [here is] another method of determination. 'The equatorial sine is the latitude-base' (<s>viṣuvajjīvākṣabhujā</s>): Since it is situated at an interval equal to the latitude north of the equatorial prime-vertical circle (<s>samamandaṇla</s>), it is called the latitude (<s>akṣa</s>). The base (<s>bhujā</s>) of that latitude-rod (<s>akṣakāṣṭha</s>) — latitude-sine and equatorial sine are synonyms. The semi-diameter (<s>vyāsārdha</s>) is the hypotenuse. The square-root of the difference of the squares of the base and hypotenuse is the plumb-line (<s>avalambaka</s>). That is the perpendicular (<s>koṭi</s>). This should be demonstrated on the sphere. From the center of the prime-vertical circle (<s>samamanḍala</s>), to the south, at an interval equal to the latitude-sine, having tied one end of a string and extending it to the planet — that is the plumb-line. The square-root of the sum of the squares of the base and perpendicular is the hypotenuse, [which equals] the semi-diameter. Thus, in other [positions] too, in the hemisphere of the observer’s sphere, with the posited half-sines,

body.text: svāhorātrārdhaviṣkambhaḥ
body.translated_text: The semi-diameter of the day-circle (<s>svāhorātrārdhaviṣkambhaḥ</s>)

body.text: apakramādibhiḥ bhujādikalpanām āha ã
body.translated_text: He states the determination of base and so forth by means of the declination and the like:

children.translated_text: Subtracting the square of the desired declination from the square of the semi-diameter, the square-root of the result
is the semi-diameter of the day-circle, to the north or south of the equator. || 24 ||

body.text: sūryasya iṣṭāpakramajyāyāḥ candrasya iṣṭāpakramajyāyāḥ ca yaḥ vargaḥ sa iṣṭāpakramavargaḥ | tam vyāsārdhakṛteḥ viśodhya [śeṣasya] yat mūlam tat viṣuvataḥ uttareṇa dakṣiṇena vā ahorātrasya viṣkambhaḥ bhavati | krāntijyā bhujā | vyāsārdham karṇaḥ | tayoḥ yat vargaviśeṣamūlam tat svāhorātrārdhaviṣkambhaḥ | pūrvavidhinā tat uttaragole uttareṇa, dakṣiṇagole dakṣiṇena pradarśayet || 24 ||
body.translated_text: Whatever is the square of the desired declination-sine of the Sun [or] the square of the desired declination-sine of the Moon, that is the square of the desired declination. Subtracting that from the square of the semi-diameter, the square-root of [the remainder] is the semi-diameter of the day-circle (<s>ahorātra</s>), to the north or south of the equator. The declination-sine is the base; the semi-diameter is the hypotenuse. The square-root of the difference of their squares is the semi-diameter of the day-circle (<s>svāhorātrārdhaviṣkambha</s>). By the previous method, in the northern hemisphere it should be demonstrated to the north, and in the southern hemisphere to the south. || 24 ||

body.text: meṣādīnām laṅkodayāḥ
body.translated_text: The <s>Laṅkā</s>-rising times of <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries) and the rest

body.text: laṅkodayaprāṇānayanam āha ã
body.translated_text: He states the derivation of the <s>Laṅkā</s>-rising <s>prāṇas</s> (breaths):

children.translated_text: The desired sine multiplied by the day-circle semi-diameter — precisely the [value at] the end of the quadrant (<s>kāṣṭhāntya</s>) —
divided by the semi-diameter of the day-circle, the result, from <s>Aja</s> (<s>Meṣa</s>, Aries), gives the <s>Laṅkā</s>-rising right-ascensional sines (<s>prāgjyās</s>). || 25 ||

body.text:
iṣṭajyā iti meṣavṛṣamithunāntajyāḥ gṛhyante | etābhiḥ guṇitam ahorātravyāsārdham svāhorātrārdhaviṣkambhaḥ iti arthaḥ | kāṣṭhasya antaḥ kāṣṭhāntaḥ, tatra bhavam kāṣṭhāntyam | navatiḥ bhāgāḥ yasmin [kāṣṭhe tasya ante bhavam] yat svahorātrārdham tat eva [iṣṭa]jyābhiḥ guṇitam svahorātrārdhahṛtam svakīyasvakīyāhorātrārdhahṛtam phalam iṣṭalaṅkodayaprāgjyāḥ | ajāt meṣāt prabhṛti kāṣṭham bhavati iti kāṣṭhīkriyate | [mithunānta]prāgjyākāṣṭhāt
vṛṣāntaprāgjyākāṣṭham viśodhayet | śeṣam mithunasya laṅkodayaprāṇāḥ | [evam] vṛṣāntaprāgjyākāṣṭhāt [meṣāntaprāgjyākāṣṭham viśodhayet | śeṣam vṛṣabhasya laṅkodayaprāṇāḥ] | svarūpataḥ eva meṣa[laṅko]dayaprāṇāḥ bhavanti || 25 ||
body.translated_text: 'Desired sines' means the sines at the ends of <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries), <s>Vṛṣa</s> (Taurus), and <s>Mithuna</s> (Gemini) are taken. Multiplied by these, 'the day-circle semi-diameter' means the semi-diameter of the day-circle (<s>svāhorātrārdhaviṣkambha</s>). '<s>Kāṣṭhāntya</s>' (end of the quadrant): the end (<s>anta</s>) of the quadrant (<s>kāṣṭha</s>), [what is] located there is '<s>kāṣṭhāntya</s>' — ninety degrees. The day-circle semi-diameter at [the point where] that quadrant ends — that very [value], multiplied by the desired sines and divided by the semi-diameter of one’s own day-circle gives the desired <s>Laṅkā</s>-rising right-ascensional sines (<s>prāgjyās</s>). From '<s>Aja</s>' — from <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries) onward, it becomes a quadrant; [the quadrant] is reduced to an arc (<s>kāṣṭhīkriyate</s>). Subtracting the right-ascensional arc at the end of <s>Mithuna</s> (Gemini) from the right-ascensional arc at the end of <s>Vṛṣa</s> (Taurus), the remainder is the <s>Laṅkā</s>-rising <s>prāṇas</s> of <s>Mithuna</s>. Similarly, subtracting the right-ascensional arc at the end of <s>Vṛṣa</s> from the right-ascensional arc at the end of <s>Meṣa</s>, the remainder is the <s>Laṅkā</s>-rising <s>prāṇas</s> of <s>Vṛṣabha</s> (Taurus). By its own nature, the <s>Meṣa</s> <s>Laṅkā</s>-rising <s>prāṇas</s> are [obtained directly]. || 25 ||

body.text: kṣitijyā
body.translated_text: The earth-sine (<s>kṣitijyā</s>)

body.text: dinaniśoḥ kṣayavṛddhipratipādanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: To explain the shortening and lengthening of day and night, he says:

children.translated_text: Multiplying the latitude-sine (<s>akṣajyā</s>) by the desired declination and dividing by the plumb-line (<s>lambaka</s>),
on the day-circle, that is the earth-sine (<s>kṣitijā</s>) — the sine of shortening and lengthening of day and night. || 26 ||

body.text: iṣṭāpakrameṇa guṇitām iṣṭāpakramaguṇitām | [iṣṭāpakramaguṇitām] akṣajyām lambakena hṛtvā phalam svāhorātramaṇḍale kṣitijyā bhavati | tatra iṣṭāpakramajyā koṭiḥ, kṣitijyā bhujā, tadvargayutimūlam karṇaḥ arkāgrā bhavati iti | pūrvāparasvastikayoḥ arkāgrayoḥ sūtram badhvā bhujakoṭivāsanā pradarśyā | kṣitijonmaṇḍalayoḥ antaram kṣitijā iti | tayā dinaniśoḥ kṣayavṛddhī | pūrvakṣitijāt uparyadhovyavasthitonmaṇḍala[kṣitijayoḥ madhye jyā]vat sā

children.translated_text: is to be demonstrated. || 26 ||

body.translated_text: Multiplied by the desired declination — 'multiplied by the desired declination' (<s>iṣṭāpakramaguṇitām</s>). The latitude-sine, multiplied by the desired declination and divided by the plumb-line — the result is the earth-sine (<s>kṣitijyā</s>) on the day-circle. There, the desired declination-sine is the perpendicular (<s>koṭi</s>), the earth-sine is the base (<s>bhujā</s>), and the square-root of the sum of their squares is the hypotenuse, which equals the <s>arkāgrā</s> (Sun’s amplitude). Tying a string between the <s>arkāgrās</s> (amplitudes) at the east and west <s>svastika</s>-points (cardinal intersections), the base-perpendicular derivation should be demonstrated. The earth-sine is [the interval] between the horizon (<s>kṣitija</s>) and the prime-vertical circle (<s>unmaṇḍala</s>). By that [earth-sine], the shortening and lengthening of day and night [are determined]. The [earth-sine], situated above or below the former horizon between the horizon and the prime-vertical, is the sine-like [quantity] that

body.text: svadeśodayāḥ
body.translated_text: Local rising-times (<s>svadeśodyāḥ</s>)

body.text: rāśyudayakālapratipādanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: To explain the sign-rising times, he says:

children.translated_text: A quarter of the circle (<s>cakrapāda</s>) rises in a quarter of the day (<s>divasapāda</s>) diminished by the <s>caradala</s> (half ascensional difference);

children.text: prathamaḥ antyaḥ ca atha anyau tatsahitena kramotkramaśaḥ || 27 ||
children.translated_text: the first and last [quarters rise thus], and the other two [rise] with that [<s>caradala</s>] added, in direct and reverse order. || 27 ||

body.text:
udayati darśanam yāti, ardham upari cakrapādaḥ, trayaḥ rāśayaḥ | caradalahīnena divasapādena iti anena laṅkodayāḥ trayaḥ parigṛhyante | yataḥ tribhiḥ meṣādilaṅkodayaiḥ pañcadaśaghaṭikāḥ tāḥ svāhorātracaturthaḥ aṃśaḥ, tataḥ krameṇa vyavasthitalaṅkodayaprāṇebhyaḥ meṣādicaradalaprāṇān svadeśākṣotpannān svakīyān viśodhayet | meṣādīnām svadeśodayāḥ bhavanti | antyaḥ cakrapādaḥ mīnakumbhamakarāḥ | ete api caradalahīnena cakrapādena udayanti
| caradalasahitena divasapādena | atra api divasapādagrahaṇena karkaṭasiṃhakanyāyāḥ utkrameṇa laṅkodayāḥ gṛhyante | tena karkaṭasiṃhakanyāyāḥ caraprāṇaiḥ utkrameṇa sahitāḥ udayanti | kramotkramaśaḥ iti | kramotkramagatyā krameṇa caradalahīnāḥ meṣavṛṣamithunāḥ, utkrameṇa sahitāḥ karkaṭasiṃhakanyāḥ | ete eva utkrameṇa tulāvṛścikadhanūṃṣi | tataḥ makarakumbhamīnāḥ utkrameṇa caradalahīnāḥ | meṣavṛṣamithunāḥ krameṇa apamaṇḍale tiryagvyavasthitāḥ,
tena meṣaḥ śīghram udeti ataḥ caradalāsubhiḥ apacīyate | evam vṛṣaḥ mithunaḥ ca | etaiḥ makarādayaḥ vyākhyātāḥ | karkaṭasiṃhakanyāḥ [tadbhinna]saṃsthānatvāt cireṇa udgacchanti | ataḥ caradalaprāṇaiḥ upacīyante | etaiḥ tulādayaḥ vyākhyātāḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Rises' means becomes visible. 'Half above' — the quarter-circle (<s>cakrapāda</s>) is three signs. 'Diminished by the <s>caradala</s> (half ascensional difference) in a quarter of the day' — by this, the <s>Laṅkā</s>-rising times of three [signs] are adopted. Because by the three <s>Laṅkā</s>-rising times of <s>Meṣa</s> and the rest, fifteen <s>ghaṭikās</s> [are obtained], and that is one-fourth of the day-circle; from those, in order, from the established <s>Laṅkā</s>-rising <s>prāṇas</s> of <s>Meṣa</s> and the rest, one should subtract the <s>caradala</s>-<s>prāṇas</s> produced at one’s own latitude. [The result is] the local rising-times of <s>Meṣa</s> and the rest. 'The last quarter-circle' is <s>Mīna</s> (Pisces), <s>Kumbha</s> (Aquarius), and <s>Makara</s> (Capricorn). These too rise in the quarter-day diminished by the <s>caradala</s>. 'With that [<s>caradala</s>] added, in a quarter of the day': Here too, by the term 'quarter of the day,' the <s>Laṅkā</s>-rising times of <s>Karkaṭaka</s> (Cancer), <s>Siṃha</s> (Leo), and <s>Kanyā</s> (Virgo) are taken in reverse order. Therefore, <s>Karkaṭaka</s>, <s>Siṃha</s>, and <s>Kanyā</s> rise with the <s>cara</s>-<s>prāṇas</s> added in reverse order. 'In direct and reverse order' (<s>kramotkramaśaḥ</s>): In direct-and-reverse progression — in direct order, with the <s>caradala</s> subtracted: <s>Meṣa</s>, <s>Vṛṣa</s>, <s>Mithuna</s>; in reverse order, with [<s>caradala</s>] added: <s>Karkaṭaka</s>, <s>Siṃha</s>, <s>Kanyā</s>. These very same, in reverse order, are <s>Tulā</s> (Libra), <s>Vṛścika</s> (Scorpio), and <s>Dhanus</s> (Sagittarius). Then <s>Makara</s>, <s>Kumbha</s>, and <s>Mīna</s>, with the <s>caradala</s> subtracted in reverse order. <s>Meṣa</s>, <s>Vṛṣa</s>, and <s>Mithuna</s> are situated obliquely on the ecliptic; therefore, <s>Meṣa</s> rises quickly, hence it is diminished by the <s>caradala</s> breaths. Similarly <s>Vṛṣa</s> and <s>Mithuna</s>. By these, <s>Makara</s> and the rest are explained. <s>Karkaṭaka</s>, <s>Siṃha</s>, and <s>Kanyā</s>, having a different orientation, rise slowly; therefore, they are augmented by the <s>caradala</s> <s>prāṇas</s>. By these, <s>Tulā</s> and the rest are explained.

body.text:
kṣitijyā vyāsārdhaguṇā svāhorātrārdhahṛtā carajyā, tatkāṣṭham caradalaprāṇāḥ | pṛthak meṣādīnām laṅkodayavat utpādyāḥ | svadeśarāśyudayaiḥ iṣṭakālalagnārtham sūryodayāt prabhṛti ghaṭikāḥ prāṇīkṛtya sūryabhogyarāśyudayaprāṇāḥ tebhyaḥ viśodhayet | sūrye bhogyāṃśam kṣepyam | punar yāvantaḥ rāśyudayāḥ śuddhyanti tāvantaḥ viśodhya sūrye rāśayaḥ kṣipyante | śeṣam triṃśatā guṇitam asuddhodayabhaktam bhāgādi vardhitaravau kṣipet | lagnam
bhavati | evam rātrau api rātrigataghaṭikāḥ dinamānaghaṭikāsu prakṣipya lagnam anena vidhinā kartavyam | rātriśeṣaghaṭikābhiḥ viparītakarmaṇā raveḥ gatabhāgādinā tadutkrameṇa yāvantaḥ udayaprāṇāḥ viśuddheyuḥ tāvantaḥ śodhanīyāḥ ] śeṣam triṃśatā guṇitam vartamānodayabhaktam bhāgādi śodhitam udayalagnam |
body.translated_text: The earth-sine multiplied by the semi-diameter and divided by the day-circle semi-diameter gives the <s>carajyā</s> (ascensional-difference sine); its arc gives the <s>caradala</s> <s>prāṇas</s> (half-ascensional-difference breaths). These should be derived separately for <s>Meṣa</s> and the rest, like the <s>Laṅkā</s>-rising times. With the local sign-rising-times, for determining the rising-ascendant (<s>lagna</s>) at a desired time: converting the <s>ghaṭikās</s> elapsed since sunrise into <s>prāṇas</s>, one should subtract the Sun’s remaining-sign rising <s>prāṇas</s> from them and add the remaining degrees to the Sun. Then, as many sign-rising-times as can be subtracted, that many signs are added to the Sun. The remainder, multiplied by thirty and divided by the unexhausted rising-time, gives degrees and so forth to be added to the augmented Sun — [that gives] the rising ascendant (<s>lagna</s>). Similarly at night too, adding the night-elapsed <s>ghaṭikās</s> to the day-measure <s>ghaṭikās</s>, the <s>lagna</s> should be computed by this method. With the night-remaining <s>ghaṭikās</s>, by the reverse operation, with the Sun’s elapsed degrees and so forth, as many rising <s>prāṇas</s> as can be subtracted in reverse order should be subtracted. The remainder, multiplied by thirty and divided by the current rising-time, gives degrees and so forth; subtracted from the [Sun augmented by] the subtracted rising-times gives the rising-ascendant.

body.text: atha raveḥ lagnasya ca antarakālasādhanam | raveḥ abhuktabhāgaiḥ abhyudayam saṃguṇya triṃśatā bhajet | labdham raveḥ abhuktaprāṇāḥ | evam lagnabhuktabhāgaiḥ tadudayam saṃguṇya triṃśatā vibhajet | labdham lagnabhuktaprāṇāḥ | antaraprāṇayuktāḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ bhaktāḥ vighaṭikāḥ, ṣaṣṭyā ghaṭikāḥ, sūryodayāt ārabhya bhavanti || 27 ||
body.translated_text: Now, the derivation of the time-interval between the Sun and the <s>lagna</s> (ascendant). Multiplying the Sun’s unconsumed degrees by its rising-time and dividing by thirty — the result is the Sun’s unconsumed <s>prāṇas</s>. Similarly, multiplying the ascendant’s consumed degrees by its rising-time and dividing by thirty — the result is the ascendant’s consumed <s>prāṇas</s>. The intermediate <s>prāṇas</s>, added [to both], divided by six give <s>vighaṭikās</s>; divided by sixty give <s>ghaṭikās</s> — [these are measured] from sunrise onward. || 27 ||

body.text: iṣṭakālaśaṅkuḥ
body.translated_text: The gnomon at a desired time (<s>iṣṭakālaśaṅkuḥ</s>)

body.text: iṣṭakālaśaṅkvānayanārtham āha ã
body.translated_text: To explain the derivation of the gnomon at a desired time, he says:

children.translated_text: The desired sine on the day-circle (<s>svāhorātreṣṭajyā</s>), multiplied by the plumb-line (<s>avalambaka</s>) from the horizon (<s>kṣitija</s>),
divided by the semi-diameter, is the gnomon (<s>śaṅku</s>) of the elapsed and remaining [portions] of the day. || 28 ||

body.text: svāhorātre
body.translated_text: The derivation of the desired sine on the day-circle (<s>svāhorātreṣṭajyā</s>) is from the elapsed and remaining <s>ghaṭikās</s> of the day. In the northern hemisphere, the horizon is situated below the prime-vertical (<s>unmaṇḍala</s>); therefore, subtracting the <s>caradala</s> <s>ghaṭikās</s> (half-ascensional-difference time-units) from the elapsed and remaining <s>ghaṭikās</s> of the day, the result is [measured]

body.text:
ṣṭajyānayanam dinagataśeṣaghaṭikābhyaḥ | uttaragole kṣitija[m unmaṇḍalā]t adhaḥ vyavasthitam ataḥ caradalaghaṭikāḥ [dinagataśeṣaghaṭikābhyaḥ ] viśodhya niṣpannāḥ unmaṇḍalāvadheḥ bhavanti | tāḥ prāṇīkṛtya jīvā grāhyā | caradalajyayā saumyetaragolayoḥ yutaviyutā kṣitijāvadheḥ bhavati | [ataḥ trairāśikam] ã yadi vyāsārdhamaṇḍale iyam jyā bhavati svāhorātrārdhamaṇḍale kiyatī iti kṣitijamaṇḍalāvadheḥ svāhorātreṣṭajyā abhidhīyate |
tām iṣṭajyām avalambakāhṛtām kṛtvā viṣkambhārdhena vyāsārdhena vibhajet | divasasya pūrvāhṇe gatasya, aparāhṇe śeṣasya śaṅkuḥ bhavati |
body.translated_text: from the boundary of the prime-vertical. Converting those to <s>prāṇas</s>, the sine is taken. The <s>caradala</s>-sine, added to or subtracted from [the result] in the northern or southern hemisphere respectively, gives [the sine] from the boundary of the horizon. Then the rule of three: if on the semi-diameter circle this is the sine, then on the day-circle semi-diameter how much? — [this result] is called the desired sine on the day-circle from the boundary of the horizon circle. That desired sine, having been multiplied by the plumb-line, is divided by the semi-diameter. It becomes the gnomon of the elapsed [portion] in the forenoon and the remaining [portion] in the afternoon.

body.text:
candraśaṅkvānayanam | rātrau candracchāyā upalakṣayet | tatra pūrvakapāle candramasaḥ iṣṭakālaghaṭikāḥ, aparakapāle tu candrāstalagnāntarālaghaṭikāḥ candramasaḥ śeṣaghaṭikāḥ ānīya iṣṭakarma | candrasvāhorātrārdham kṣitijyām caradalajyām ca ānīya caradalaviparyayaniṣpannaprāṇaiḥ sūryavat karma kartavyam | atha svāhorātreṣṭajyā dvādaśaguṇā viṣuvatkarṇena bhaktā iṣṭaśaṅkuḥ bhavati | athavā caradalena adhikonaghaṭikājyām
caradalajyāviparyayaniṣpannām, lambakaguṇitām svāhorātreṇa saṃguṇya trijyāvargeṇa [vibhajya] śaṅkulabdhiḥ | athavā tām dvādaśaguṇasvāhorātreṇa saṃguṇya viṣuvatkarṇaguṇavyāsārdhena bhajet | phalam śaṅkuḥ |
body.translated_text: Derivation of the Moon’s gnomon: At night, one should observe the Moon’s shadow. There, in the first half [of the night], the desired-time <s>ghaṭikās</s> of the Moon [are taken]; in the latter half, the <s>ghaṭikās</s> of the interval between the Moon and the setting ascendant are the Moon’s remaining <s>ghaṭikās</s> — having derived these, the desired operation [is performed]. Having derived the Moon’s day-circle semi-diameter, the earth-sine, and the <s>caradala</s>-sine, the operation should be performed as for the Sun, using the <s>prāṇas</s> produced by the reversed <s>caradala</s>. Then, the desired sine on the day-circle, multiplied by twelve and divided by the equinoctial hypotenuse (<s>viṣuvatkarṇa</s>), gives the desired gnomon. Alternatively, the sine of the <s>ghaṭikās</s> increased or decreased by the <s>caradala</s>, produced with the reversed <s>caradala</s>-sine, multiplied by the plumb-line and the day-circle, dividing by the square of the semi-diameter (<s>trijyā</s>) — [gives] the gnomon-result. Or, that [sine] multiplied by twelve times the day-circle, divided by the product of the equinoctial hypotenuse and the semi-diameter — the result is the gnomon.

body.text: divasagataghaṭikānayane ca śaṅkunā guṇitam vyāsārdham śaṅkucchāyāvargayutimūlena bhaktam bṛhacchaṅkuḥ bhavati | trijyāguṇitaḥ lambakabhaktaḥ svāhorātreṣṭajyā labhyate | tena uttaragole kṣitijyā śodhyate, dakṣiṇe kṣipyate | tataḥ vyāsārdhena hatvā svāhorātrārdhena bhajet | labdhasya kāṣṭham uttaragole caradalayutam dakṣiṇe hīnam dinagataśeṣaprāṇāḥ [ bhavanti | taiḥ ] prāgvat ghaṭikāḥ || 28 ||
body.translated_text: And for finding the <s>ghaṭikās</s> (time units) elapsed in the day: the <s>vyāsārdha</s> (semi-diameter) multiplied by the <s>śaṅku</s> (gnomon), divided by the square root of the sum of the squares of the <s>śaṅku</s> and its shadow, gives the great gnomon (<s>bṛhacchaṅku</s>). That, multiplied by the <s>trijyā</s> (radius) and divided by the <s>lambaka</s> (co-latitude sine), gives the desired <s>jyā</s> (sine) of the day-circle. From that, in the northern hemisphere the <s>kṣitijyā</s> (horizon sine) is subtracted, and in the southern hemisphere it is added. Then, multiplying by the <s>vyāsārdha</s> and dividing by the semi-day-circle, the arc of the result — increased by the <s>caradala</s> (half-ascensional difference) in the northern hemisphere, decreased in the southern — gives the <s>prāṇas</s> (time units) of the elapsed or remaining day. From those, the <s>ghaṭikās</s> are [obtained] as before. || 28 ||

body.text: śaṅkvagram
body.translated_text: The gnomon-tip distance

body.text: śaṅkvagrapradarśanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: In order to demonstrate the <s>śaṅkvagra</s> (gnomon-tip distance), he says:

children.translated_text: The desired gnomon, multiplied by the equinoctial sine and divided by one's own co-latitude sine,
gives the solar <s>śaṅkvagra</s> (gnomon-tip distance) to the south of the rising-setting line. || 29 ||

body.text: sveṣṭaśaṅkuḥ iṣṭakālotpannaśaṅkuḥ, viṣuvajjyayā akṣajīvayā guṇitaḥ lambakena bhaktaḥ astodayasūtrāt dakṣiṇataḥ sūryaśaṅkvagram bhavati | śaṅkoḥ agram antarālam śaṅkumūlāt samottarāvagāhisūtram yāvat astamayodaya[sūtra]m iti |
body.translated_text: The desired gnomon is the gnomon produced at the desired time. Multiplied by the equinoctial sine — that is, by the <s>akṣajīvā</s> (latitude sine) — and divided by the <s>lambaka</s> (co-latitude sine), it becomes the solar <s>śaṅkvagra</s> to the south of the rising-setting line. The <s>agra</s> (tip distance) of the <s>śaṅku</s> is the interval from the base of the gnomon to the line entering equally northward — that is, the rising-setting line.

body.text: kṣitijamaṇḍale prāksvastikāt dakṣiṇam uttaram vā arkāgrākāṣṭhatulyāntare sūtrasya ekam agram badhvā, dvitīyam agram tāvat [arkāgrākāṣṭhatulyāntare] eva aparabhāge badhnīyāt | tat pūrvāparāyatam udayāstasūtram | tasya sūtrasya śaṅkutalasya antare śaṅkvagram | śaṅkumūlāt bhūmadhyam yāvat sūtram dṛgjyā | bhūmadhyāt upari śaṅkumastakaprāpi yat sūtram karṇaḥ vyāsārdham iti || 29 ||
body.translated_text: On the horizon circle, having fastened one end of a cord at an interval equal to the arc of the <s>arkāgrā</s> (solar amplitude) to the south or north of the eastern cardinal point, one should fasten the other end at the same interval equal to the arc of the <s>arkāgrā</s> on the western side. That east-west extended cord is the rising-setting line. The interval between that cord and the base of the gnomon is the <s>śaṅkvagra</s> (gnomon-tip distance). The cord from the base of the gnomon to the center of the Earth is the <s>dṛgjyā</s> (sight-sine). The cord from the center of the Earth upward reaching the top of the gnomon is the hypotenuse, equal to the <s>vyāsārdha</s> (semi-diameter). || 29 ||

body.text: arkāgrā
body.translated_text: The solar amplitude

body.text: arkāgrānayanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: In order to derive the <s>arkāgrā</s> (solar amplitude), he says:

children.translated_text: The sine of the maximum declination, multiplied by the desired half-sine, should then be divided
by the sine of the co-latitude; the result is the <s>arkāgrā</s> (solar amplitude) on the eastern and western horizon. || 30 ||

body.text: paramāpakramajyā caturviṃśatibhāgajyā 1397 | tām iṣṭasya raveḥ bhujajyayā guṇitām [kṛtvā] lambakena vibhajet , [labdhā jyā] arkāgrā bhavati | iyati adhvani viṣuvataḥ uttareṇa dakṣiṇena vā raviḥ udeti, pūrvāpare ca kṣitijamaṇḍalapradeśe || 30 ||
body.translated_text: The sine of the maximum declination is the sine of twenty-four degrees = 1397. That, multiplied by the <s>bhujajyā</s> (base-sine) of the desired [position of the] Sun and divided by the <s>lambaka</s> (co-latitude sine), the result is the <s>arkāgrā</s> (solar amplitude). This is the distance at which the Sun rises to the north or south of the equinox, on the eastern and western regions of the horizon circle. || 30 ||

body.text: samaśaṅkuḥ
body.translated_text: The prime-vertical gnomon

body.text: samamaṇḍalaśaṅkvānayanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: In order to derive the gnomon [when the Sun is] on the prime vertical, he says:

children.translated_text: If that [declination sine] is less than the equinoctial sine, then it is multiplied by the equinoctial co-latitude sine
and divided by the equinoctial sine; the result is the gnomon on the east-west [prime vertical]. || 31 ||

body.text:
sā iti anena apakramajyā gṛhyate | uttaragole viṣuvajjyātulyā krāntijyā [yadā] bhavati, tadā madhyāhne eva savitā samamaṇḍalam viśati | viṣuvajjyā [yadā] krāntikāṣṭhajyayā ūnā [tadā] samamaṇḍalāt uttareṇa yāti | [krāntikāṣṭhajyā yadā] viṣuvajjyayā ūnā tadā samamaṇḍalam viśati | [krāntikāṣṭhajyā] yadā ūnā viṣuvajjyayā, tadā [pūrvānītā arkāgrā] lambakena guṇitā viṣuvajjyayā bhaktā samamaṇḍalaśaṅkuḥ bhavati |
  pūrvasamamaṇḍalena aparasamamaṇḍalena [ca] kṣitije arkāgrāntare astamayodayasūtram badhvā arkākrāntarāśibhāgapradeśaḥ samapūrvāparamaṇḍale yatra lagnam prāgbindutaḥ tat samamaṇḍalacāpam tathā gole bhramayet yathā kṣitijādhobhāge samamaṇḍale tāvati antare lagnam bhavet | tayoḥ samamaṇḍalabindvoḥ antare sūtram badhvā tadardham śaṅkuḥ pūrvavat eva pūrvāpararekhāspṛk bhavati | śaṅkoḥ uttareṇa astamayodayasūtram yāvat antaram śaṅkvagram
arkāgrātulyam | samamaṇḍalaśaṅkuḥ akṣajyayā guṇitaḥ paramakrāntijyābhaktaḥ sūryabhujajyā bhavati | [sūrye meṣādige] tatkāṣṭham ādityaḥ, karkaṭakādige ṣaḍrāśiviśuddham, tulādige ṣaḍrāśiyutam, makarādige cakraviśuddham raviḥ bhavati |
body.translated_text: By 'that' (<s>sā</s>), the declination sine is taken. In the northern hemisphere, when the declination sine equals the equinoctial sine, then the Sun enters the prime vertical only at midday. When the equinoctial sine is less than the declination arc-sine, [the Sun] goes to the north of the prime vertical. When the declination arc-sine is less than the equinoctial sine, it enters the prime vertical. When [the declination arc-sine] is less than the equinoctial sine, then the previously derived <s>arkāgrā</s> (solar amplitude), multiplied by the <s>lambaka</s> (co-latitude sine) and divided by the equinoctial sine, becomes the prime-vertical gnomon. Having fastened the rising-setting line at the interval of the <s>arkāgrā</s> on the horizon at the eastern and western prime vertical, the point where the arc-degree-position of the Sun's declination-sign meets the prime vertical from the eastern point — that is the prime-vertical arc. One should rotate the globe such that it meets at the same interval on the prime vertical below the horizon. Having fastened a cord between those two prime-vertical points, its half is the gnomon, which touches the north-south line as before. The interval from the gnomon northward to the rising-setting line is the <s>śaṅkvagra</s> (gnomon-tip distance), equal to the <s>arkāgrā</s>. The prime-vertical gnomon, multiplied by the <s>akṣajyā</s> (latitude sine) and divided by the sine of maximum declination, gives the solar <s>bhujajyā</s> (base-sine). [When the Sun is] at the beginning of <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries), that arc gives the Sun; at the beginning of <s>Karkaṭaka</s> (Cancer), subtract six signs; at the beginning of <s>Tulā</s> (Libra), add six signs; at the beginning of <s>Makara</s> (Capricorn), subtract the full circle — that gives the Sun.

body.text:
chedyake api ã samāyām bhūmau vṛttam ālikhya dikcihnitam kṛtvā sūryabimbodaye aste ca pūrvāparayoḥ bindū kṛtvā pūrvāpararekhāyāḥ dakṣiṇe [madhyāhnanatajyātulye antare] tṛtīyam bindum prakalpya bindutrayāvagāhi matsyadvayena vṛttam ālikhet | tat arkabhramavṛttam | arkāgrāgre savitā uditaḥ tadvṛttānusāreṇa samamaṇḍalam avagāhya dakṣiṇena natajyātulye antare madhyāhnam kṛtvā krameṇa aparabhāge samamaṇḍalāt niṣkrāntaḥ aparāgrāgre
astam eti | arkabhramavṛttasya prāgapararekhāyāḥ yatra sampātaḥ tatra samamaṇḍale praveśaḥ | samamaṇḍale tu madhyam yāvat antaram samamaṇḍalaśaṅkucchāyā bhavati | dakṣiṇagole samamaṇḍalāt dakṣiṇena yāti | [tadā] samamaṇḍalasya praveśābhāvaḥ || 31 ||
body.translated_text: Also in the graphical method: on level ground, having drawn a circle and marked the cardinal directions, having placed points at the east and west where the Sun's disc rises and sets, and having established a third point to the south of the north-south line at an interval equal to the midday deflection sine, one should draw a circle passing through all three points using two fish-figures. That is the Sun's diurnal circle. The Sun, having risen at the tip of the solar amplitude, following that circle, enters the prime vertical, makes midday at an interval equal to the deflection sine to the south, and then in the western portion, having exited from the prime vertical, sets at the tip of the western amplitude. Where the Sun's diurnal circle intersects the north-south line, there is the entry into the prime vertical. The interval on the prime vertical up to its middle is the prime-vertical gnomon shadow. In the southern hemisphere, [the Sun] goes to the south of the prime vertical; then there is no entry into the prime vertical. || 31 ||

body.text: madhyāhnaśaṅkuḥ
body.translated_text: The midday gnomon

body.text: madhyāhnaśaṅkucchāyayoḥ ānayanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: In order to derive the midday gnomon and shadow, he says:

children.text: kṣitijāt unnatabhāgānām yā jyā sā paraḥ bhavet śaṅkuḥ |
children.translated_text: The sine of the degrees elevated from the horizon — that is the greatest gnomon;

children.text: madhyāt natabhāgajyā chāyā śaṅkoḥ tu tasya eva || 32 ||
children.translated_text: the sine of the degrees depressed from the zenith is the shadow of that very gnomon. || 32 ||

body.text:
kṣitijāt iti samadakṣiṇottarasvastikapradeśāt ye unnatabhāgāḥ golamadhyasthite ravau lakṣitāḥ teṣām yā jyā sā paramaḥ śaṅkuḥ bhavati | yā madhyāt natabhāgajyā sā paramaśaṅkoḥ chāyā syāt | iṣṭamadhyāhne raveḥ apakramabhāgāḥ akṣabhāgeṣu dakṣiṇagole prayojayet | uttare gole viyojayet | te natabhāgāḥ bhavanti | candrasya vikṣepayutaviyutāḥ natabhāgāḥ bhavanti, yataḥ vimaṇḍale candraḥ | ete navateḥ viśodhyante | śeṣam unnatabhāgāḥ | teṣām [jyā]
unnatabhāgajyā | athavā taddinasvāhorātrārdham kṣitijyayā svayā udagyāmye viyutayutaṃ[vyāsārdhaguṇam svāhorātrārdhabhaktam] dvādaśaguṇam viṣuvatkarṇahṛtam mahāśaṅkuḥ tadunnatajyā bhavati || 32 ||
body.translated_text: From the horizon — that is, from the point of the southern or northern cardinal point — the degrees that are elevated, observed when the Sun is situated at the center of the sphere, the sine of those is the greatest gnomon. The sine of the degrees depressed from the zenith is the shadow of the greatest gnomon. At the desired midday, the degrees of the Sun's declination are to be applied to the latitude degrees — added in the southern hemisphere, subtracted in the northern hemisphere. Those become the degrees of depression. The Moon's degrees of depression are increased or decreased by the latitude (<s>vikṣepa</s>), since the Moon is on its own inclined orbit. These are subtracted from ninety; the remainder gives the degrees of elevation. The sine of those is the sine of elevation. Alternatively, the semi-day-circle of that day, with its own <s>kṣitijyā</s> (horizon sine) subtracted or added for northern or southern direction respectively, multiplied by the <s>vyāsārdha</s> and divided by the semi-day-circle, multiplied by twelve and divided by the equinoctial hypotenuse, gives the great gnomon — that is the sine of elevation. || 32 ||

body.text: dṛkkṣepajyā
body.translated_text: The <s>dṛkkṣepa</s> sine (sine of ecliptic zenith distance)

body.text: dṛkkṣepapratipādanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: In order to explain the <s>dṛkkṣepa</s> (ecliptic zenith distance), he says:

children.translated_text: The product of the meridian sine and the rising sine, divided by the semi-diameter —
the square root of the difference between the squares of that and the meridian sine is one's own <s>dṛkkṣepa</s> (ecliptic zenith distance). || 33 ||

body.text: madhyajyā ca udayajīvā ca madhyodayajīve | tayoḥ saṃvargaḥ parasparaguṇanam vyāsadalahṛtam yat bhavati tasya madhyajyāyāḥ ca kṛtyoḥ viśeṣamūlam svakīyaḥ dṛkkṣepaḥ | svagrahaṇena tu ravicandrakakṣyayoḥ bhinnaḥ dṛkkṣepaḥ || 33 ||
body.translated_text: The meridian sine and the rising sine — these are the <s>madhyodayajīve</s> (meridian and rising sines). Their product — the mutual multiplication — divided by the semi-diameter: the square root of the difference of the squares of that result and the meridian sine is one's own <s>dṛkkṣepa</s> (ecliptic zenith distance). By the word 'one's own' (<s>sva</s>), the <s>dṛkkṣepa</s> is different for the orbits of the Sun and the Moon. || 33 ||

body.text: dṛggatijyā
body.translated_text: The <s>dṛggati</s> sine (sine of ecliptic altitude)

body.text: dṛggatijyānayanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: In order to derive the <s>dṛggatijyā</s> (sine of ecliptic altitude), he says:

children.translated_text: The square root of the difference of the squares of the sight-sine and the <s>dṛkkṣepa</s> sine is one's own <s>dṛggati</s> (ecliptic altitude), due to the Earth;
on the horizon, one's own sight-shadow; the Earth's semi-diameter [is measured] from the center of the sky. || 34 ||

body.text:
dṛgjyādṛkkṣepakṛtyoḥ vivarasya mūlam svakīyā dṛggatiḥ bhavati | kuvaśāt bhūvaśāt iyam bhavati | madhyajyodayajīvayoḥ saṃvarge vyāsadalahṛte yat tat madhyajyākṛtyoḥ viśeṣāt mūlam dṛkkṣepaḥ hi bhavati | evam bhūvaśāt utpannatrijyāśaṅkuvargaviśeṣāt mūlam dṛgjyā bhavati | ataḥ bhūvaśāt utpanna[dṛgjyā]dṛkkṣepaniṣpannatvāt kuvaśāt iti ucyate | "kṣitije svā dṛkchāyā" iti atra tu "svā" iti anena svakīyadṛkkṣepadṛggatī abhidhīyete | bhūvyāsārdham 525
| kṣitijamaṇḍale svā dṛkchāyā kasmāt utpannā? nabhomadhyāt | vyāsārdha[tulya]m etat bhavati | tat yataḥ kudṛṣṭivaśāt samamaṇḍalamadhyāt pūrvāparayoḥ diśoḥ dṛggatiḥ [lambanam] ṛṇam dhanam vā iti, tathā eva bhagolamadhyāt dakṣiṇottaradiśoḥ dṛkkṣepasya grahaṇena natiḥ vā syāt |
body.translated_text: The square root of the difference of the squares of the <s>dṛgjyā</s> (sight-sine) and the <s>dṛkkṣepa</s> is one's own <s>dṛggati</s> (ecliptic altitude). 'Due to the Earth' (<s>kuvaśāt</s>) — this arises due to the Earth. In the product of the meridian sine and the rising sine, divided by the semi-diameter, the square root of the difference from the squares of the meridian sine is indeed the <s>dṛkkṣepa</s>. Similarly, due to the Earth, the square root of the difference of the squares of the <s>trijyā</s> (radius) and the gnomon is the <s>dṛgjyā</s> (sight-sine). Therefore, because it is produced from the <s>dṛgjyā</s> and <s>dṛkkṣepa</s> which arise due to the Earth, it is called 'due to the Earth.'
