'On the horizon, one's own sight-shadow' — here, by 'one's own' (<s>svā</s>), one's own <s>dṛkkṣepa</s> and <s>dṛggati</s> are denoted. The Earth's semi-diameter is 525. On the horizon circle, from where does one's own sight-shadow arise? From the center of the sky. This equals the <s>vyāsārdha</s> (semi-diameter). Since, due to the terrestrial perspective, the <s>dṛggati</s> [= parallax in longitude] from the middle of the prime vertical in the eastern and western directions is negative or positive, similarly, by taking the <s>dṛkkṣepa</s> in the southern and northern directions from the center of the ecliptic sphere, the <s>nati</s> (parallax in latitude) would result.

body.text:
jyānām viśeṣotpattim darśayati | [bhūmeḥ golākāratvāt] bhūvyāsārdha[tulya]m antaram kṣitije sūryakakṣyāyām candrakakṣāyām ca [bhavati] | sūryakakṣyotpannamadhyajyām sūryakakṣyodayajyayā saṃguṇya trijyayā bhāgalabdhasya vargam madhyajyāvargāt viśodhya mūlam ravikakṣyāyām dṛkkṣepaḥ, tathā candrakakṣyotpannamadhyajyām svodayajyayā saṃguṇya trijyayā bhāgalabdhasya vargam svamadhyajyāvargāt viśodhya mūlam candrakakṣyāyām dṛkkṣepaḥ
| sūryasvāhorātrādibhiḥ sādhitadṛgjyāvargāt sūryadṛkkṣepavargam viśodhya mūlam sūryakakṣyāyām dṛggatijyā | candrasvāhorātrādibhiḥ sādhitadṛgjyāvargāt candradṛkkṣepavargam viśodhya mūlam candrakakṣyāyām dṛggatijyā bhavati | evam anyeṣām api grahāṇām samamaṇḍalamadhyāt dṛggateḥ bhāvaḥ | udaye [sūrya]grahaṇe candrasya tāvadadhaḥsthitatvāt candrakakṣyāyām sūryabimbakendrasūtrāt pūrveṇa candrabimbam natam lakṣyate | astamaye tu tathā eva
aparataḥ | samabhūpradeśe sthitasya draṣṭuḥ vyāsārdhatulyayā dṛggatijyayā bhūvyāsārdhatulyam dṛggatyantaram [= lambanam] | evam eva dakṣiṇottarakapālayoḥ dṛkkṣepāntaram [= natiḥ] | [tatra idam trairāśikam] ã yadi vyāsārdhatulyayā dṛggatijyayā bhūvyāsārdhayojanatulyam dṛggatyantaram [=lambanam] tadā iṣṭakālotpannadṛggatijyayā kiyat iti | [punar ca trairāśikam ã yadi] sphuṭayojanakarṇena trijyātulyāḥ kalāḥ labhyante, tadā dṛggati[= lambana]yojanaiḥ kiyatyaḥ
iti | atra prathame trairāśike trijyā bhāgahāraḥ dvitīye guṇakāraḥ tulyatvāt [nāśe kṛte] ravicandrayoḥ dṛggateḥ bhūvyāsārdham guṇakāraḥ sphuṭayojanakarṇaḥ bhāgahāraḥ, phalam liptāḥ | sūryaliptāḥ candraliptābhyaḥ viśodhya trairāśikam ã yadi [dinasphuṭa]bhuktyantareṇa ṣaṣṭiḥ nāḍyaḥ [labhyante, tadā] ābhiḥ liptābhiḥ kiyatyaḥ iti | labdham nāḍyaḥ bhavanti, tāḥ dṛggati[=lambana]ghaṭikāḥ | pūrvakapāle pūrvataḥ grahaḥ kakṣyāyām nataḥ | tasmāt prāgyogaḥ ataḥ
grahe apanīyante | aparakapāle parataḥ natatvāt lambanaghaṭikātulyakālena yogaḥ bhaviṣyati iti ataḥ prakṣipyante | evam etat karma tāvat kriyate yāvat aviśeṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: He shows the derivation of the differences of the sines. Because the Earth is spherical, an interval equal to the Earth's semi-diameter exists on the horizon in the Sun's orbit and the Moon's orbit. Multiplying the meridian sine produced in the Sun's orbit by the rising sine of the Sun's orbit and dividing by the <s>trijyā</s> (radius), subtracting the square of that from the square of the meridian sine, the square root is the <s>dṛkkṣepa</s> in the Sun's orbit. Similarly, multiplying the meridian sine produced in the Moon's orbit by its own rising sine and dividing by the <s>trijyā</s>, subtracting the square of that from the square of its own meridian sine, the square root is the <s>dṛkkṣepa</s> in the Moon's orbit. Subtracting the square of the Sun's <s>dṛkkṣepa</s> from the square of the <s>dṛgjyā</s> computed from the Sun's day-circle and so forth, the square root is the <s>dṛggatijyā</s> (parallax-in-longitude sine) in the Sun's orbit. Subtracting the square of the Moon's <s>dṛkkṣepa</s> from the square of the <s>dṛgjyā</s> computed from the Moon's day-circle and so forth, the square root is the <s>dṛggatijyā</s> in the Moon's orbit. Thus for other planets also, the <s>dṛggati</s> originates from the middle of the prime vertical. At the time of a solar eclipse at rising, since the Moon is situated that much below [the Sun], the Moon's disc is observed to be deflected eastward from the line through the center of the Sun's disc in the Moon's orbit. At setting, similarly, it is [deflected] westward. For an observer situated on a level place on the Earth, with the <s>dṛggatijyā</s> equal to the <s>vyāsārdha</s>, the <s>dṛggati</s>-interval [= parallax in longitude] equals the Earth's semi-diameter. Similarly in the southern and northern hemispheres, the <s>dṛkkṣepa</s>-interval [= parallax in latitude]. The rule of three [is thus]: if with a <s>dṛggatijyā</s> equal to the <s>vyāsārdha</s>, the <s>dṛggati</s>-interval [= parallax in longitude] in <s>yojanas</s> equals the Earth's semi-diameter, then with the <s>dṛggatijyā</s> produced at the desired time, how much? And again the rule of three: if with the true <s>yojana</s>-hypotenuse, minutes equal to the <s>trijyā</s> are obtained, then with the <s>dṛggati</s> [= parallax] in <s>yojanas</s>, how many? Here, in the first rule of three the <s>trijyā</s> is the divisor and in the second it is the multiplier; since they are equal, they cancel out. [The result is:] for the Sun and Moon, the <s>dṛggati</s> multiplied by the Earth's semi-diameter and divided by the true <s>yojana</s>-hypotenuse gives the result in minutes. Subtracting the Sun's minutes from the Moon's minutes, the rule of three [is]: if with the difference of the true daily motions, sixty <s>nāḍīs</s> are obtained, then with these minutes, how many? The result is <s>nāḍīs</s>; those are the <s>dṛggati</s> [= parallax in longitude] <s>ghaṭikās</s>. In the eastern hemisphere, the planet is deflected eastward in its orbit; therefore the conjunction is earlier, hence [the parallax] is subtracted from the planet. In the western hemisphere, since it is deflected westward, the conjunction will occur later by the time equal to the parallax <s>ghaṭikās</s>, hence [the parallax] is added. This procedure is repeated until there is no further change.

body.text:
evam [ravicandrayoḥ] dṛkkṣepaliptāḥ prāgvat trairāśikena jñātāḥ | yadi ravicandrayoḥ madhya[jye] samadiksthe bhavataḥ tadā [ravicandrayoḥ] natiliptānām viśeṣaḥ anyathā yogaḥ | tataḥ avanatiḥ bhavati | tataḥ madhyagrahaṇacandrāt pātam viśodhya śeṣasya dakṣiṇottarabhujajyā ardhapañcamena guṇitā trijyābhaktā vikṣepaḥ | avanativikṣepayoḥ samadiśi yogaḥ, bhinnadiśi viyogaḥ [sphuṭavikṣepaḥ] | sphuṭavikṣepaḥ avanatiḥ iti paryāyaḥ | tayā ca avanatyā sthityardham
ānīya madhyatitheḥ viśodhya śeṣaḥ sparśakālaḥ | tena prāgvat lambanavidhiḥ | sparśamadhyalambanaghaṭikāntareṇa sthityardham upacīyate | tat punar madhyakālāt viśodhya asakṛt sthityardham utpādayet yāvat sthiram bhavati | mokṣe punar prathamānītasthityardham madhyatithau prakṣipet | pūrvavat mokṣalambanamadhyalambanaghaṭikāntareṇa sthityardham upacīyate | tat punar madhyatithau prakṣipya pūrvavat lambanaghaṭikāḥ utpādya tanmadhyalambanāntareṇa
sthityardham upacitam kṛtvā tat eva karma punar kriyate yāvat sthiram bhavati | evam sthirīkṛtasthityardhasambandhinam sūryendugatikalābhogam madhyagrahaṇasūryendoḥ sparśe viśodhayet mokṣe kṣipet | sparśamokṣakālikau bhavataḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus the parallax-in-latitude minutes (<s>dṛkkṣepaliptāḥ</s>) of the Sun and Moon are known as before by the rule of three. If the mid-sines (<s>madhyajye</s>) of the Sun and Moon are in the same direction, then the difference of the deflection-in-latitude minutes of the Sun and Moon [is taken]; otherwise, their sum. From that, the deflection-in-latitude (<s>avanati</s>) is obtained. Then, subtracting the node (<s>pāta</s>) from the mid-eclipse Moon, the north-south sine of the remainder, multiplied by four and a half and divided by the semi-diameter (<s>trijyā</s>), gives the deflection (<s>vikṣepa</s>). When the deflection-in-latitude and deflection are in the same direction, their sum [is taken]; when in different directions, their difference [gives] the true deflection (<s>sphuṭavikṣepa</s>). The true deflection is synonymous with '<s>avanati</s>' (deflection-in-latitude). With that deflection-in-latitude, having derived the half-duration (<s>sthityardha</s>) and subtracting from the mid-<s>tithi</s>, the remainder is the contact-time (<s>sparśakāla</s>). With that, the parallax procedure is [applied] as before. By the difference between the parallax <s>ghaṭikās</s> at contact and at mid-eclipse, the half-duration is augmented. That [augmented half-duration], again subtracted from the mid-time, should produce the half-duration iteratively until it becomes stable. For release (<s>mokṣa</s>), the initially derived half-duration should be added to the mid-<s>tithi</s>. As before, by the difference between the release-parallax and mid-parallax <s>ghaṭikās</s>, the half-duration is augmented. That, again added to the mid-<s>tithi</s>, and producing the parallax <s>ghaṭikās</s> as before, and augmenting the half-duration by the difference from the mid-parallax — that very procedure is repeated until it becomes stable. Thus, the daily-rate minutes of the Sun and Moon corresponding to the stabilized half-duration should be subtracted from the mid-eclipse Sun and Moon at contact, and added at release. [These] become the [Sun and Moon] at the times of contact and release.

body.text: atha prāgaparakapāladvaye api lambanayoḥ tayoḥ yogena yutam sthityardham sphuṭam bhavati |
body.translated_text: Now, when the parallaxes in both the eastern and western hemispheres are [of the same sign], their sum is added to the half-duration, and it becomes the true [half-duration].

body.text:
samāyāmavanau [vyāsārdhapramāṇena sūtreṇa] vṛttam ālikhya dikcihnitam kṛtvā maṇḍalapūrvabhāge prāgapararekhāyāḥ uttareṇa dakṣiṇena vā udayajyākāṣṭhatulye antare bindū kṛtvā bindudvayaśiraspṛksūtram prasārya rekhā kuryāt udayajyā bhavati | [punar] madhyam maṇḍalakendram kṛtvā madhyajyātulyasūtreṇa vṛttam bhrāmayet | tat madhyajyāmaṇḍalam | trijyāmaṇḍalaparidhibindudvayāt sūtradvayam madhyakendram ānīya rekhādvayam kuryāt
| tat antarajyārdham madhyajyāmaṇḍale tathā eva pūrvāparataḥ uttareṇa dakṣiṇena vā vyavasthāpyate | tat madhyajyāvargaviśeṣamūlam dṛkkṣepajyākoṭiḥ madhyajyāmaṇḍale bhavati |
body.translated_text: On a level ground, having drawn a circle [with a cord] of semi-diameter measure and marking the directions, in the eastern part of the circle, to the north or south of the east-west line, at an interval equal to the rising-sine arc (<s>udayajyākāṣṭha</s>), having placed two points and extending a cord touching the tops of both points, one should draw a line — that is the rising-sine. Again, making the center of the circle the center, one should rotate [a compass with] a cord equal to the mid-sine (<s>madhyajyā</s>) to draw a circle. That is the mid-sine circle. From the two points on the semi-diameter circle, extending two cords to the mid-center, one should make two lines. Half the distance between them is placed on the mid-sine circle likewise to the east and west, to the north or south. That, [being] the square root of the difference of the squares of the mid-sine, is the cosine of the parallax-in-latitude (<s>dṛkkṣepajyākoṭi</s>) on the mid-sine circle.

body.text: trijyāmaṇḍale pūrvāparayoḥ udayajyākāṣṭhatulye antare
body.translated_text: On the semi-diameter circle, at the east and west points,

body.text:
bindū kṛtvā [vṛttakendrāt madhyāhna]natajyātulye antare dṛkkṣepabinduḥ dakṣiṇena [prakalpya] bindutrayeṇa matsyam utpādya tanmukhapucchaspṛksūtrasampātāt bindutrayaspṛgvṛttam bhramayet | tat arkabhramavṛttam | tatra kṣitijāt ūrdhvam yatra pradeśe raviḥ tanmadhyakendrāntarālasūtram dṛgjyā karṇaḥ, sthānīyā dṛkkṣepajyā koṭiḥ, tadagrāt ārabhya dṛgjyāgram yāvat ravicihnopalakṣitam tadantarālam
dṛggatijyā sā pūrvāparā | evam viśiṣṭam tryaśram kṣetram niṣpādyate || 34 ||
body.translated_text: having placed points at an interval equal to the rising-sine arc, [and from the circle's center,] having conceived the parallax-in-latitude point (<s>dṛkkṣepabindu</s>) to the south at an interval equal to the midday deflection-sine (<s>madhyāhnanatajyā</s>), producing a fish-figure (<s>matsya</s>) with the three points and rotating a circle touching the three points from the intersection of the cord touching the mouth and tail [of the fish] — that is the Sun's revolution-circle (<s>arkabhramavṛtta</s>). There, above the horizon, at whatever position the Sun is, the cord between its center and the [position] is the sight-sine (<s>dṛgjyā</s>) hypotenuse; the parallax-in-latitude sine is the cosine (<s>koṭi</s>), standing [as the perpendicular]; and from its tip to the Sun-mark, that interval is the sight-motion sine (<s>dṛggatijyā</s>) — that [extends] east-west. Thus a specific right-triangle is produced. // 34 //

body.text: akṣadṛkkarma
body.translated_text: Latitude sight-correction (<s>akṣadṛkkarma</s>)

body.text: udayāstamayayoḥ vikṣepavaśāt ṛṇadhanatvapratipādanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of teaching the subtractive-additive [correction] due to deflection at rising and setting, he says:

children.text: vikṣepaguṇā akṣajyā lambakabhaktā bhavet ṛṇam udaksthe |
children.translated_text: The latitude-sine multiplied by the deflection and divided by the co-latitude (<s>lambaka</s>) — [the result] is subtractive when the [Moon is] to the north

children.text: udaye dhanam astamaye dakṣiṇage dhanam ṛṇam candre || 35 ||
children.translated_text: at rising, additive at setting; when the Moon is to the south, additive [at rising] and subtractive [at setting]. // 35 //

body.text: akṣajyā vikṣepaguṇā lambakabhaktā phalam liptāḥ | uttaravikṣepe udayasthitacandre ṛṇam, astamaye dhanam | yāmye vikṣepe udayasthe candre dhanam, astamaye ṛṇam iti | ṛṇadhanayuktī ravicaradalaphalopapattitulyā || 35 ||
body.translated_text: The latitude-sine (<s>akṣajyā</s>) multiplied by the deflection and divided by the co-latitude — the result is in minutes. When the deflection is northward and the Moon is at the horizon at rising, it is subtractive; at setting, additive. When the deflection is southward and the Moon is at the horizon at rising, it is additive; at setting, subtractive. The rationale for the subtractive-additive [rule] is the same as the rationale for the Sun's half-day-arc equation. // 35 //

body.text: ayanadṛkkarma
body.translated_text: Solstitial sight-correction (<s>ayanadṛkkarma</s>)

body.text: ayanavaśāt ṛṇadhanatvapratipādanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of teaching the subtractive-additive [correction] due to the solstice (<s>ayana</s>), he says:

children.translated_text: The versed-sine (<s>utkramaṇa</s>) multiplied by deflection and declination, divided by the square of the semi-diameter —

children.text: udagṛṇadhanam udagayane dakṣiṇage dhanam ṛṇam yāmye || 36 ||
children.translated_text: when northward, it is subtractive-additive in the northern solstice; when southward, additive-subtractive in the southern. // 36 //

body.text:
vikṣepaḥ ca apakramaḥ ca vikṣepāpakramau | [vikṣepāpakramau guṇau yasya tat vikṣepāpakramaguṇam | vikṣepaḥ tātkālikaḥ gṛhyate, apakramaḥ ca paramāpakramaḥ | utkramaṇam utkramajyām |] vikṣepeṇa paramāpakrameṇa guṇitām rāśitrayayutacandrasya utkramajīvām iti arthaḥ | katham rāśitrayayutacandrasya tat utkramaṇam? utkramaṇagrahaṇāt rāśitrayakṣepaḥ avagamyate | [rāśitrayayutacandrasya] utkramajyām guṇayet | vyāsārdhakṛtyā bhajet | phalam
liptāḥ udagvikṣipte uttarāyaṇe ṛṇam dakṣiṇe dhanam | tat eva phalam dakṣiṇe ayane uttaravikṣipte dhanam, ṛṇam yāmye, vikṣepe dakṣiṇe ṛṇam bhavet iti | ṛṇe dhane yuktiḥ api | yasmāt tulyadigvikṣepāyanayoḥ grahaḥ tāvat adhikaḥ prāpyate, udayāstamayakṣitijayoḥ viśodhyate; bhinnāyanavikṣepayoḥ tāvat hīnaḥ iti kṣipyate | sarvagrahāṇām svodayāstamayayoḥ idam karma pravartate | na madhyāhnārdharātrayoḥ || 36 ||
body.translated_text: Deflection and declination [together are] '<s>vikṣepāpakramau</s>.' That whose multipliers are deflection and declination is '<s>vikṣepāpakramaguṇam</s>.' The deflection is taken as the current [value]; the declination is the maximum declination. '<s>Utkramaṇam</s>' — the versed-sine. The meaning is: the versed-sine of the Moon plus three signs, multiplied by the deflection and the maximum declination. How is [it] the versed-sine of the Moon plus three signs? From the word '<s>utkramaṇa</s>' (versed-sine), the addition of three signs is understood. One should multiply the versed-sine [of the Moon plus three signs]. Divide by the square of the semi-diameter. The result is in minutes. When the deflection is northward and it is the northern solstice (<s>uttarāyaṇa</s>), [the result is] subtractive; when southward, additive. That same result, in the southern solstice, when the deflection is northward, is additive; when the deflection is southward, it is subtractive. The rationale for the subtractive and additive is also [this]: since, when the deflection and solstice are in the same direction, the planet is reached in greater measure, it is subtracted from the rising-and-setting horizons; when the solstice and deflection are in different directions, [the planet] is deficient by that much, hence it is added. This procedure applies for all planets at their own risings and settings — not at midday and midnight. // 36 //

body.text: candrādisvarūpam grahaṇakāraṇam ca
body.translated_text: The nature of the Moon and others, and the cause of eclipses

body.text: candrādisvarūpavyāvarṇanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: For the purpose of describing the nature of the Moon and others, he says:

children.text: candraḥ jalam arkaḥ agniḥ mṛdbhūccāyā api yā tamaḥ tat hi |
children.translated_text: The Moon is water, the Sun is fire; the Earth is clay, and the Earth's shadow, which is darkness, indeed —

children.text: chādayati śaśī sūryam, śaśinam mahatī ca bhūcchāyā || 37 ||
children.translated_text: the Moon covers the Sun, and the great Earth's shadow [covers] the Moon. // 37 //

body.text: yat etat candramaṇḍalam tat pratyakṣeṇa jalam, vivasvān uṣṇasvabhāvāt agniḥ, bhūḥ pṛthivī mṛṇmayī, bhūcchāyā tamaḥ svabhāvāt iti | śaśī candraḥ sūryam chādayati | uparisthitaḥ sūryaḥ adhaḥsthitena candramasā chādyate | mahatī ca bhūcchāyā śaśinam chādayati | grāhakabhedaḥ ca anayoḥ asti, yataḥ kucchāyā viśālā nyūnaḥ śaśī, śaśī nyūnaḥ viśālaḥ dinakṛt || 37 ||
body.translated_text: This disc of the Moon is visibly water; the Sun, being of hot nature, is fire; the Earth is made of clay; and the Earth's shadow is darkness by nature. The Moon covers the Sun — the Sun situated above is covered by the Moon situated below. And the great Earth's shadow covers the Moon. There is also a distinction in the eclipsing [agent] of these two: since the Earth's shadow is large and the Moon is small, [and since] the Moon is small and the Sun is large. // 37 //

body.text: grahaṇamadhyakālaḥ
body.translated_text: The mid-eclipse time

body.text: kadā grahaṇe bhavataḥ, tatpratipādanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: When do eclipses occur? For teaching that, he says:

children.text: sphuṭaśaśimāsānte arkam pātāsannaḥ yadā praviśati induḥ |
children.translated_text: At the end of a true lunar month, when the Moon, being near the node, enters [conjunction with] the Sun,
and at the end of a fortnight, [when the Moon enters] the Earth's shadow — then the eclipse-middle is greater or less [than the true tithi-end]. // 38 //

body.text:
sphuṭaḥ śaśimāsaḥ sphuṭaśaśimāsaḥ, tasya ante parisamāptau amāvāsyāyām arkam ādityam, pātāsannaḥ vikṣepamārgagatyā pātāsannaḥ, yadā praviśati induḥ yadā arkagrahaṇam bhavati | [pakṣānte paurṇamāsyante pātāsannaḥ induḥ yadā] bhūcchāyām praviśati | tadā adhikam ūnam vā grahaṇamadhyam bhavati | yataḥ pūrvakapāle grahaṇamadhyam adhikam bhavati sphuṭatithicchedajanitam tena tatra lambanaghaṭikāḥ viśodhyāḥ tāvatā kālena atītatvāt
grahaṇamadhyasya | aparakapāle grahaṇamadhyam ūnam bhavati sphuṭatithicchedajanitam tena tatra lambanaghaṭikāḥ kṣipyante, bhāvitvāt grahaṇamadhyasya || 38 ||
body.translated_text: A true lunar month is '<s>sphuṭaśaśimāsa</s>'; at its end, at the completion [of the month], on the new-moon day (<s>amāvāsyā</s>), [the Moon enters conjunction with] the Sun (<s>ārka</s>). Being near the node — approaching the node by the path of deflection — when the Moon enters [conjunction with the Sun], then a solar eclipse occurs. [At the end of a fortnight, at the full-moon (<s>paurṇamāsī</s>), when the Moon,] being near the node, enters the Earth's shadow — then the eclipse-middle is greater or less [than the true tithi-end]. Since in the eastern hemisphere the eclipse-middle is greater [i.e., later] than what the true tithi-intercept produces, the parallax <s>ghaṭikās</s> are subtracted there, because the eclipse-middle has already passed by that much time. In the western hemisphere, the eclipse-middle is less [i.e., earlier] than what the true tithi-intercept produces, hence the parallax <s>ghaṭikās</s> are added there, because the eclipse-middle is yet to come. // 38 //

body.text: bhūcchāyādairghyam
body.translated_text: The length of the Earth's shadow

body.text: bhūcchāyāpramāṇam āha ã
body.translated_text: He states the measure of the Earth's shadow:

children.translated_text: The Earth-Sun distance, multiplied by the Earth [diameter] and divided by the difference of the Sun and Earth [diameters] —
the result obtained is the length of the Earth's shadow, [measured] from the Earth's globe. // 39 //

body.text: bhuvaḥ raveḥ ca antaram bhūravivivaram, raviyojanakarṇaḥ 459585, bhūguṇitam bhūvyāsena 1050 guṇitam, ravibhuvoḥ viśeṣeṇa ravibhuvoḥ vyāsayoḥ 4410, 1050, antareṇa 3360 vibhajet | tat bhūgolacchāyādīrghatvam bhavati 143620 bhūgolaviṣkambhāt prabhṛti |
body.translated_text: The distance between the Earth and the Sun is the '<s>bhūravivivara</s>' (Earth-Sun separation) — the Sun's <s>yojana</s>-distance hypotenuse is 459,585. Multiplied by the Earth — multiplied by the Earth's diameter 1,050; divided by the difference of the Sun and Earth — the difference of the diameters of the Sun and Earth, 4,410 and 1,050, is 3,360. The result is the length of the Earth-globe's shadow: 143,620 [<s>yojanas</s>] from the Earth's globe onward.

body.text: atra idam pradīpacchāyākarma | ravivyāsaḥ pradīpaḥ bhujā, bhūvyāsaḥ śaṅkuḥ, ravibhūvyāsayoḥ antaram ravibhūvyāsaviśeṣaḥ, raviyojanakarṇaḥ śaṅkupradīpacchāyayoḥ antaram iti pradīpacchāyākarmasūtranibandhanam |
body.translated_text: Here, this is the lamp-shadow computation. The Sun's diameter is the lamp [height] (<s>bhujā</s>), the Earth's diameter is the gnomon (<s>śaṅku</s>), the difference between the Sun's and Earth's diameters is the Sun-Earth diameter-difference, and the Sun's <s>yojana</s>-distance is the distance between the gnomon and lamp-shadow — this is the formulation of the lamp-shadow computation rule.

body.text: upapattiḥ pradīpacchāyākarmaṇā eva | ravibhūgolavṛttapārśvayoḥ sūtradvayam tathā sūryabhūvyāsasūtradvayam ekatra badhnīyāt | bhūcchāyā krameṇa apacīyamānā bhūviṣkambhāt lakṣyate || 39 ||
body.translated_text: The proof is by the lamp-shadow computation itself. Two cords from the sides of the Sun and Earth globes, and likewise two cords [connecting] the Sun's and Earth's diameter-endpoints, should be bound to meet at one point. The Earth's shadow, gradually diminishing, is observed from the Earth's diameter onward. // 39 //

body.text: tamasaḥ viṣkambham
body.translated_text: The diameter of the shadow

body.text: candrakakṣyāyām bhūcchāyānayanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: For computing the Earth's shadow at the Moon's orbit, he says:

children.translated_text: The distance from the shadow-tip to the Moon, multiplied by the Earth's diameter,
divided by the [length of the] Earth's shadow — one should know [the result] as the diameter of the shadow (<s>tamas</s>). // 40 //

body.text: bhūchāyāgrāt ārabhya candram yāvat antaram chāyāgracandravivaram | bhūcchāyādairghyam 143620 candrakarṇena 34377 anena hīnam 109243 chāyāgracandravivaram jātam, bhūviṣkambheṇa 1050 guṇitam bhūcchāyādairghyeṇa 143620 vibhaktam labdham tamasaḥ viṣkambhaḥ 689 svagrahaṇe candrakakṣyāyām bhūcchāyāviṣkambhaḥ bhavati |
body.translated_text: From the Earth's shadow-tip to the Moon — that interval is the shadow-tip-to-Moon distance. The Earth's shadow length 143,620, diminished by the Moon's distance-hypotenuse 34,377, gives the shadow-tip-to-Moon distance 109,243. Multiplied by the Earth's diameter 1,050 and divided by the Earth's shadow length 143,620, the result is the shadow's diameter: 799 [<s>yojanas</s>] — this is the diameter of the Earth's shadow at the Moon's orbit in its own eclipse.

body.text: yadi candrayojanakarṇena vyāsārdham 3439 labhyate tadā tamoviṣkambhārdhena kiyat iti labdham [tamoviṣkambhārdha]liptāpramāṇam 800 | 19 || evam svakīyasphuṭayojanakarṇābhyām ravicandrayoḥ vyāsaliptānayanam | ravivyāsaḥ 4410 vyāsārdha 3438 guṇitaḥ raviyojanakarṇa 457585 bhaktaḥ ravibimbakalāḥ 33 | 00 || candravyāsaḥ 315 vyāsārdha 3438 guṇitaḥ candrayojanakarṇa 34377 hṛtaḥ candrabimbakalāḥ 31 | 10 || 40 ||
body.translated_text: If by the Moon's <s>yojana</s>-distance the semi-diameter 3,439 is obtained, then by the shadow's semi-diameter, how much? The result is the shadow semi-diameter in minutes: 800;19. Thus, the diameters in minutes of the Sun and Moon are computed from their respective true <s>yojana</s>-distances. The Sun's diameter 4,410, multiplied by the semi-diameter 3,438 and divided by the Sun's <s>yojana</s>-distance 457,585, gives the Sun's disc in minutes: 33;00. The Moon's diameter 315, multiplied by the semi-diameter 3,438 and divided by the Moon's <s>yojana</s>-distance 34,377, gives the Moon's disc in minutes: 31;10. // 40 //

body.text: sthityardhānayanam
body.translated_text: Computation of the half-duration

body.text: sthityardhapratipādanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: For teaching the half-duration, he says:

children.translated_text: From the square of the half-sum of that [shadow/Sun] and the Moon, the square of the Moon's deflection should be subtracted;
the square root of this is to be known as the half-duration — [converted] by the daily motion of the Moon and Sun. // 41 //

body.text: chādyachādakayoḥ samparkārdham mānaikyārdham iti arthaḥ | tasya kṛtiḥ tacchaśisamparkārdhakṛtiḥ | tasyāḥ śaśinaḥ vikṣepavargitam śodhyam | grahaṇadvaye api candrāt vikṣepaḥ iti | ravigrahaṇe avanatiyutaviyutaḥ sphuṭavikṣepaḥ gṛhyate | tasya mūlam sthityardham bhavati | katham? candrārkadinabhogāt | candrārkadinabhogaśabdena candrārkadinabhuktiḥ gṛhyate | tayoḥ anulomagatikayoḥ dinagatyantareṇa trairāśikam karma ã yadi raviśaśigativiśeṣeṇa

children.text: ṣaṣṭiḥ nāḍyaḥ labhyante, [tadā] sthityardhaliptābhiḥ kiyatyaḥ iti sthityardhaghaṭikāḥ labhyante || 41 ||
children.translated_text: sixty <s>nāḍīs</s> are obtained, then by the half-duration minutes, how many? — the half-duration <s>ghaṭikās</s> are obtained. // 41 //

body.translated_text: The half-sum (<s>samparkārdha</s>) of the eclipsed and eclipsing [bodies] means half the sum of their measures — this is the meaning. Its square is 'the square of the half-sum of that and the Moon.' From that, the square of the Moon's deflection should be subtracted. In both types of eclipses, the deflection is from the Moon. In a solar eclipse, the true deflection combined with or separated from the deflection-in-latitude (<s>avanati</s>) is taken. Its [i.e., the difference's] square root is the half-duration. How? 'By the daily motion of the Moon and Sun': by the word '<s>candrārkadinabhoga</s>' (daily motion of Moon and Sun), the daily rates of the Moon and Sun are taken. For those two moving in the direct direction, the rule of three with the difference of daily rates [is applied]: if by the difference of the daily rates of the Sun and Moon,

body.text: vimardārdhānayanam
body.translated_text: Computation of the half-totality (<s>vimardārdha</s>)

body.text: evam vimardārdham āneyam | katham?
body.translated_text: Similarly, the half-totality is to be derived. How?

children.translated_text: The square of the half of the shadow diminished by the Moon's semi-diameter —
diminished by the square of the deflection — the square root of that is the half-totality (<s>vimardārdha</s>). // 42 //

body.text: iti etasmāt | [sthityardham] titheḥ sparśe śodhyam mokṣe deyam, ravicandrapātāḥ api sparśamokṣakālikāḥ sthityardhaghaṭikābhiḥ kṛtvā punar sparśamokṣayoḥ vikṣepau, tābhyām sthityardhe ubhe yāvat aviśeṣam |
body.translated_text: From this [computation]: the half-duration should be subtracted from the <s>tithi</s> at contact and added at release. The Sun, Moon, and nodes at the times of contact and release should also be computed with the half-duration <s>ghaṭikās</s>, and again the deflections at contact and release [should be found]; with those, the two half-durations [should be recomputed] until there is no difference (<s>aviśeṣa</s>).

body.text:
gaṇitakarmaṇā upapattiḥ dṛśyate | grāhyabimbamānārdhena vṛttam ālikhet | tat grāhyabimbam | tataḥ mānaikyārdhatulyena karkaṭakena tena eva kendreṇa aparam vṛttam ālikhet | tat grāhyagrāhakasamparkārdhamaṇḍalam | tataḥ dakṣiṇottararekhāyām yathādiśam kendrāt uttareṇa dakṣiṇena vā vikṣepatulyam sūtram prasārya bindum kuryāt | tanmatsyavidhinā pūrvā[parām rekhām kuryāt | tatsamparkārdhamaṇḍalasampātāt kendraprāpiṇīm rekhām nayet
| evam ardhāyatacaturasram kṣetram utpadyate | tatra samparkārdham karṇaḥ, vikṣepaḥ ca bhujā | tadvargaviśleṣamūlam koṭiḥ sthityardham iti | yadā grāhyabimbārdhonagrāhakabimbārdhatulyam grāhyagrāhakayoḥ kendrāntarālam, tadā grāhyagrāhakabimbārdhaviśleṣaḥ karṇaḥ, vikṣepaḥ eva bhujā | tadvargaviśeṣamūlam koṭiḥ vimardārdham iti || 42 ||
body.translated_text:
The proof is seen through mathematical computation. Draw a circle with the semi-diameter of the eclipsed body (<s>grāhyabimba</s>). That is the eclipsed body. Then, with a compass equal to half the sum of the diameters, draw another circle with the same center. That is the half-circle of contact between the eclipsed and eclipser (<s>grāhyagrāhakasamparkārdhamaṇḍala</s>). Then, on the north-south line, extend a thread equal to the latitude (<s>vikṣepa</s>) northward or southward from the center as appropriate, and mark a point. By the fish-figure method, draw an east-west line. From the intersection with the half-contact circle, draw a line reaching the center.
Thus a half-rectangular figure (<s>ardhāyatacaturasra</s>) is produced. There, the half-contact is the hypotenuse (<s>karṇa</s>), and the latitude is the base (<s>bhujā</s>). The square root of the difference of their squares is the perpendicular (<s>koṭi</s>), which is the half-duration (<s>sthityardha</s>). When the distance between the centers of the eclipsed and eclipser equals the semi-diameter of the eclipser minus the semi-diameter of the eclipsed, then the difference of the semi-diameters of the eclipsed and eclipser is the hypotenuse, and the latitude itself is the base. The square root of the difference of their squares is the perpendicular, which is the half-duration of totality (<s>vimardārdha</s>). || 42 ||

body.text: candrasya agrastamānam
body.translated_text: The obscured remainder of the Moon

body.text: grastaśeṣapramāṇānayanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: In order to present the determination of the measure of the uneclipsed remainder, he says:

children.translated_text: Having subtracted the semi-diameter of the shadow diminished by the semi-diameter of the Moon

children.text: vikṣepāt yat śeṣam na gṛhyate tat śaśāṅkasya || 43 ||
children.translated_text: from the latitude, what remains is the portion of the Moon that is not eclipsed. || 43 ||

body.text:
śaśiviṣkambhārdhavarjitam tamasaḥ viṣkambhārdham candravikṣepāt apohya | yat śeṣam tat candrasya na chādyate | grahaṇamadhye uttareṇa dakṣiṇena vā yāvat eva vikṣepaḥ, tadā tāvat eva tayoḥ kendrāntarālam bhavati | yadā punar vikṣepaḥ, tasmāt śaśitamasaḥ viṣkambhārdhaviśeṣāt adhikaḥ bhavati, tadā tāvatpramāṇam eva bimbakendrāntarālasya dvitīya pārśvataḥ candrabimbam tamomadhyāt niṣkrāntam lakṣyate | yāvān bhāgaḥ candrasya na gṛhyate
tam candrabimbāt viśodhya śeṣam grāsapramāṇam syāt | candravat arke api || 43 ||
body.translated_text:
Having subtracted the semi-diameter of the shadow diminished by the semi-diameter of the Moon from the Moon's latitude — what remains is not obscured of the Moon. At the middle of the eclipse, the distance between the centers of the two equals the latitude, whether north or south. But when the latitude exceeds the difference of the semi-diameters of the Moon and the shadow, then to that extent the Moon's disc is seen emerging from the middle of the shadow on the other side, equal to that measure of the distance between the disc-centers. Whatever portion of the Moon is not eclipsed,
subtracting that from the Moon's disc, the remainder is the measure of obscuration (<s>grāsa</s>). The same applies to the Sun as to the Moon. || 43 ||

body.text: iṣṭakālikagrāsaḥ
body.translated_text: The obscuration at a desired time

body.text: iṣṭakālagrāsapratipādanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: In order to present the obscuration at a desired time, he says:

children.translated_text: From the half-duration minus the desired [time], combined with the square of the latitude, [take] the square root;
that should be subtracted from the half-contact; the remainder is the obscuration at that time. || 44 ||

body.text: vikṣepavargaḥ tena sahitāt, sthitiḥ sparśāt ārabhya yāvanmokṣaḥ, tasya madhyam sthityardham, iṣṭakālavarjitam iṣṭavarjitam, tasmāt | yat mūlam [tat] samparkārdhāt śodhyam mānaikyārdhāt viśodhyam | śeṣaḥ tātkālikaḥ grāsaḥ bhavati |
body.translated_text: The square of the latitude — combined with that; the duration (<s>sthiti</s>) is from the first contact (<s>sparśa</s>) up to the release (<s>mokṣa</s>); its middle is the half-duration (<s>sthityardha</s>); diminished by the desired time is 'desired-subtracted'; from that. The square root [of that] should be subtracted from the half-contact, that is, subtracted from the half of the sum of diameters. The remainder is the obscuration at that time.

body.text: sthityardham iṣṭakālahīnam bhuktyantaraguṇam ṣaṣṭihṛtam liptāḥ | vargaḥ tāvataḥ vikṣepasya liptātmakasya varge yuktvā mūlīkriyate, mūlam karṇaḥ | [tāvatkarṇam mānaikyārdhāt viśodhya śeṣaḥ tātkālikaḥ grāsaḥ bhavati |] tāvatā karṇena praviṣṭaḥ grāhakaḥ || 44 ||
body.translated_text: The half-duration minus the desired time, multiplied by the difference of daily motions and divided by sixty, gives the minutes (<s>liptā</s>). The square of that amount, added to the square of the latitude in minutes, is then square-rooted; the root is the hypotenuse (<s>karṇa</s>). [Subtracting that hypotenuse from the half of the sum of diameters, the remainder is the obscuration at that time.] With that hypotenuse, the eclipser has entered [the eclipsed body]. || 44 ||

body.text: akṣavalanam ayanavalanam ca
body.translated_text: The <s>akṣavalana</s> (axial deflection) and <s>ayanavalana</s> (solstitial deflection)

body.text: valanajyāpratipādanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: In order to present the deflection sine (<s>valanajyā</s>), he says:

children.translated_text: The latitude (<s>akṣa</s>), multiplied by the versed sine from midday, divided by the semi-diameter, [gives] the direction (<s>dik</s>) from the south;
and from the half-duration of the Sun and Moon, [one obtains the deflection] at the moment of contact from the <s>ayana</s> (solstitial longitude) increased by three signs. || 45 ||

body.text:
madhyāhnāt prabhṛti utkramaḥ madhyāhnotkramaḥ | madhyāhnatithyantarālaghaṭikā madhyāhnaśabdena ucyate | tatra prākkapāle tithighaṭikā dinārdhāt viśodhyā, aparakapāle tebhyaḥ dinārdham | madhyāhne iti upalakṣaṇam | tathā ca indugrahaṇe madhyarātritihyantarālaghaṭikāḥ gṛhyante | tāḥ ṣaḍguṇāḥ bhāgāḥ teṣām utkramajyā, tayā akṣajyā dakṣiṇataḥ vyavasthitā guṇanīyā, ardhavistareṇa vyāsārdhena bhaktā dik bhavati | dakṣiṇataḥ iti aparakapālam
adhikṛtya utktam ācāryeṇa, yataḥ aparakapāle pūrvabhāgaḥ dakṣiṇena valati, aparabhāgaḥ uttareṇa; prākkapāle punar pūrvabhāgaḥ uttareṇa, aparabhāgaḥ dakṣiṇena valati | evam bimbasya pūrvāparabhāgaḥ uttareṇa dakṣiṇena valati, yataḥ dikśabdena valanam ucyate | yatra candraḥ bhūcchāyāyām praviśati tatra candrabimbe khaṇḍyamāne tadvalanam prākkapāle candrabimbapūrvabhāge uttareṇa avatiṣṭhate, aparabhāge dakṣiṇena | aparakapāle viparītam |
body.translated_text:
The versine reckoned from midday is the 'midday versine' (<s>madhyāhnotkrama</s>). The <s>ghaṭikās</s> (time-units) of the interval between midday and the <s>tithi</s> (lunar day) are denoted by the word 'midday.' There, in the forenoon half, the <s>tithi</s>-<s>ghaṭikās</s> are subtracted from the half-day; in the afternoon half, the half-day [is subtracted] from them. 'Midday' is used by way of indication (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>). And thus, in a lunar eclipse, the <s>ghaṭikās</s> of the interval between midnight and the <s>tithi</s> are taken. Those, multiplied by six, become degrees; of those [degrees], the versed sine — by that, the latitude-sine (<s>akṣajyā</s>), situated to the south, is to be multiplied, and divided by the semi-diameter (<s>vyāsārdha</s>), yielding the direction (<s>dik</s>). 'From the south' is stated by the <s>ācārya</s> with reference to the afternoon half,
because in the afternoon half the eastern part deflects southward and the western part northward; in the forenoon half, however, the eastern part deflects northward and the western part southward. Thus the eastern and western parts of the disc deflect northward and southward; hence, by the word 'direction' (<s>dik</s>), deflection (<s>valana</s>) is meant. Where the Moon enters the Earth's shadow, there, when the Moon's disc is being cut, that deflection in the forenoon half remains on the eastern part of the Moon's disc to the north, and on the western part to the south. In the afternoon half it is reversed.

body.text: vikṣepaḥ ravigrahaṇe yathādiśam eva bhavati | yadā punar bhūcchāyā grāhakatvena kalpitā tadā vikṣepasya digviparyayaḥ |
body.translated_text: The latitude (<s>vikṣepa</s>) in a solar eclipse is in its own direction. But when the Earth's shadow is conceived as the eclipser, then the direction of the latitude is reversed.

body.text:
sthiteḥ ardham sthityardham, vikṣepaḥ | yataḥ sthiteḥ ardham vikṣepavaśāt bhavati, tena sthityardhaśabdena vikṣepaḥ ucyate | tasmāt vikṣepavaśāt dvitīyavalanānayanam ã arkendvoḥ iti | arkaḥ ca induḥ ca arkendū, tayoḥ arkendvoḥ trirāśisahitayoḥ yat ayanam | ayanaśabdena krāntiḥ, trirāśiśabdena jyā utkrameṇa grāhyā | trirāśisahitau yadā ravicandrau cakrārdhāt ūnau bhavataḥ tadā [pūrvakapāle] uttaram digvalanam | cankrārdhāt adhikau tadā [pūrvakapāle]
dakṣiṇam digvalanam | utkramajyā parakrāntiguṇā trijyāhṛtā krāntivalanajyā | tadbimbapūrvabhāge uttareṇa uttaram, dakṣiṇena dakṣiṇam | aparakapāle tu [vyatyayena] diksādhanam kartavyam |
body.translated_text:
Half of the duration is the half-duration; [this refers to] the latitude. Since half the duration arises due to the latitude, by the word 'half-duration' the latitude is meant. Therefore, the computation of the second deflection due to the latitude [is as follows]: 'of the Sun and Moon' — <s>arka</s> (Sun) and <s>indu</s> (Moon), of those two; increased by three signs — what is the <s>ayana</s> (solstitial longitude). By the word '<s>ayana</s>', the declination (<s>krānti</s>) [is meant]; by the word 'three signs,' the sine is to be taken as the versed sine. When the Sun and Moon, increased by three signs, are less than half the circle, then [in the forenoon half] the directional deflection is northward. When greater than half the circle, then [in the forenoon half]
the directional deflection is southward. The versed sine multiplied by the maximum declination and divided by the radius (<s>trijyā</s>) gives the declination-deflection sine (<s>krāntivalanajyā</s>). That, on the eastern part of the disc, is northward if north, southward if south. In the afternoon half, however, the directional assignment is to be done in reverse.

body.text:
samamaṇḍalamadhyāt dakṣiṇena akṣatulye antare pūrvāparāyatamaṇḍalasya [nāḍīmaṇḍalasya] yat antaram tat akṣavalanam | tat madhyāt utkrameṇa upacīyate | etat ānayanam ã samamaṇḍalamadhyāt natasya utkramajyayā kartavyam | pūrvakapāle karṇagatyā bimbapūrvabhāgaḥ uttareṇa pratibhāsate, aparabhāgaḥ dakṣiṇena | parakapāle bimbapūrvabhāgaḥ dakṣiṇena aparabhāgaḥ uttareṇa | iti gole pradarśayet | ayanavalanam tu uttaradakṣiṇāyanādau bhinnatvena
pratibhāsate, meṣādau uttaram, tulādau dakṣiṇam | evam akṣavalanatrayeṇa parilekhaḥ kriyate |
body.translated_text:
The interval between the prime vertical circle (<s>samamaṇḍala</s>) center and the equatorial circle (<s>nāḍīmaṇḍala</s>) to the south, equal to the latitude (<s>akṣa</s>), is the axial deflection (<s>akṣavalana</s>). That increases from the meridian by the versed sine. The computation of this is to be done with the versed sine of the hour angle from the prime vertical. In the forenoon half, by the motion of the hypotenuse, the eastern part of the disc appears to the north and the western part to the south. In the afternoon half, the eastern part of the disc [appears] to the south and the western part to the north. This should be demonstrated on the sphere (<s>gola</s>). The solstitial deflection (<s>ayanavalana</s>), however,
appears differently at the beginning of the northern and southern solstices — northward at the beginning of <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries), southward at the beginning of <s>Tulā</s> (Libra). Thus, with the three [types of] deflection including the axial deflection, the diagram (<s>parilekha</s>) is drawn.

body.text:
prathamam samabhūmau grāhyamaṇḍalam likhet | tat kendrāt eva samparkārdhamaṇḍalam [vyāsārdhamaṇḍalam ca likhet] | vyāsārdham iṣṭacchedena chinnam kartavyam | [vyāsārdhamaṇḍalam] pūrvāparadakṣiṇottaradigaṅkitam [kāryam] | akṣāyanavalane kāṣṭīkṛtya tulyadigyogaḥ bhinnadigviśleṣaḥ [ca kāryaḥ] | vyāsārdhamaṇḍale dakṣiṇena uttareṇa vā apamaṇḍalagatyā [paścimabhāge] valanam vidhāya bindum kuryāt | tataḥ kendraprāpi sūtram nayet | tasya
sūtrasya mānaikyārdhaparidheḥ yatra sampātaḥ tasmāt uttareṇa dakṣiṇena vikṣepam ca apagatyā paridhyanusāreṇa nītvā agre bindum kuryāt | tasmāt bindoḥ kendraprāpi sūtram nayet | yatra grāhyabimbam spṛśati tatra raveḥ aparabhāge sparśaḥ, candrasya bimbe pūrvabhāge sparśaḥ | [grāhakabimbakendraḥ tu] samparkārdhamaṇḍale bhavati | ravigrahaṇe sparśavalanam digvaśena mānaikyārdhaparidhau pūrvavat | tadagrāt vikṣepam yathādiśam, candragrahaṇe viparītam
prasārayet | tadagrāt kendraprāpi sūtram nayet | yatra grāhyaparidhim spṛśati tatra sparśaḥ | mokṣavalanam ravigrahaṇe pūrvabhāge, candragrahaṇe aparabhāge vyastam prasāryate | tataḥ mokṣavikṣepam yathādiśam savituḥ, candrasya viparītam prasārya bindum kuryāt | tadagrāt kendraprāpisūtram nayet | yatra grāhyaparidhim spṛśati tatra mokṣaḥ |
body.translated_text:
First, draw the eclipsed circle on level ground. From that same center, draw the half-contact circle [and the semi-diameter circle]. The semi-diameter should be divided by a chosen scale factor. [The semi-diameter circle] should be marked with the east, west, south, and north directions. Having determined the axial and solstitial deflections as line-segments, combine them if in the same direction, take the difference if in opposite directions. On the semi-diameter circle, to the south or north, mark the deflection along the ecliptic path [on the western side] and make a point. Then draw a thread reaching the center. Where that
thread meets the circumference of the half-sum-of-diameters, from there extend the latitude northward or southward along the circumference of the ecliptic path, and make a point at the end. From that point, draw a thread reaching the center. Where it touches the eclipsed disc — there, on the western part of the Sun, is the contact (<s>sparśa</s>); on the eastern part of the Moon's disc is the contact. [The center of the eclipser disc] lies on the half-contact circle. In a solar eclipse, the contact deflection along the direction on the half-sum circumference is as before. From its end, extend the latitude in the appropriate direction; in a lunar eclipse, the opposite direction
is to be extended. From its end, draw a thread reaching the center. Where it touches the eclipsed circumference, there is the contact. The release deflection (<s>mokṣavalana</s>) in a solar eclipse is on the eastern part, in a lunar eclipse on the western part, extended in reverse. Then extend the release latitude in the appropriate direction for the Sun, and opposite for the Moon, and make a point. From its end, draw a thread reaching the center. Where it touches the eclipsed circumference, there is the release (<s>mokṣa</s>).

body.text:
madhyagrahaṇe madhyagrahaṇavalanam vikṣepavaśāt | samparkārdhamaṇḍale dakṣiṇavikṣepe uttaram valanam pūrveṇa, dakṣiṇam pareṇa; uttare vikṣepe, uttaram valanam pareṇa, dakṣiṇam pūrveṇa praśārayet | [ravigrahaṇe viparītam kāryam |] tadagrāt yāmya uttararekhā kāryā | tanmānaikyārdhavṛttasampātāt kendraprāpi sūtram nītvā rekhām kuryāt | rekhānusāreṇa kendramadhyāt savituḥ yathādiśam, candrasya viparītam, vikṣepam prasārya tadagre
bindum kuryāt | tasmāt grāhakabimbavyāsārdhena [grāhyabimbam] khaṇḍayet | grāhyabimbam tāvat grastam dṛśyate |
body.translated_text:
At mid-eclipse, the mid-eclipse deflection is due to the latitude. On the half-contact circle, when the latitude is southward, extend the northward deflection to the east and the southward to the west; when the latitude is northward, extend the northward deflection to the west and the southward to the east. [In a solar eclipse, the reverse is to be done.] From its end, draw a north-south line. From the intersection of that with the half-sum-of-diameters circle, having drawn a thread reaching the center, draw a line. Along that line, from the center of the center, extend the latitude in the appropriate direction for the Sun, and opposite for the Moon,
and make a point at its end. From that, cut [the eclipsed disc] with the semi-diameter of the eclipser. The eclipsed disc is seen eclipsed to that extent.

body.text: iṣṭaparilekhe, pragrahaṇamadhyamokṣavikṣepabindutrayeṇa matsyadvayam utpādya tanmukhapucchanirgatasūtrasampātāt bindutrayaspṛksūtreṇa vṛttam bhrāmayet | [sa] grāhyabimbakendramārgaḥ | tatra iṣṭagrāsakarṇapramāṇam [sūtram] kendrāt yathādiśam grāhakamārgābhimukham prasārya yatra grāhakamārgam spṛśati tasmāt grāhakārdhena parilekhāt tatkālakhaṇḍagrahaṇam dṛśyate |
body.translated_text: For a diagram at a desired time, produce two fish-figures with the three latitude-points of the beginning, middle, and release of the eclipse, and from the thread emerging from the mouth and tail [of the fish-figures], rotate a circle touching the three points with a thread from the intersection. [That] is the path of the eclipsed body's center. There, extend a thread equal to the desired obscuration hypotenuse (<s>grāsakarṇa</s>) from the center in the appropriate direction toward the eclipser's path; where it touches the eclipser's path, from that point, with the eclipser's semi-diameter, the partial eclipse at that time is seen from the diagram.

body.text: nimīlanonmīlanayoḥ vimardārdhaliptābhiḥ iṣṭagrāsavat karṇam ānīya iṣṭagrāsavidhinā nimīlanonmīlane darśayitavye || 45 ||
body.translated_text: For immersion (<s>nimīlana</s>) and emersion (<s>unmīlana</s>), having derived the hypotenuse using the minutes of the half-duration of totality (<s>vimardārdha</s>) in the same manner as for the desired obscuration, the immersion and emersion are to be shown by the method of desired obscuration. || 45 ||

body.text: grāhyabimbasya varṇaḥ
body.translated_text: The color of the eclipsed disc

body.text: grāhyabimba
body.translated_text: In order to present the color of the [eclipsed]

body.text: varṇapratipādanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: disc, he says:

children.text: pragrahaṇānte dhūmraḥ khaṇḍagrahaṇe śaśī bhavati kṛṣṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: At the end of first contact, [the Moon is] smoky; during partial eclipse, the Moon becomes black;
during total eclipse, [it is] tawny (<s>kapila</s>); dark-coppery in the middle of the shadow. || 46 ||

body.text: pragrahaṇe sparśe, ante mokṣe, śaśī dhūmraḥ bhavati | khaṇḍagrahaṇe kṛṣṇaḥ bhavati | khaṇḍagrahaṇam pragrahaṇāt ardhāsannam sarvaiḥ gṛhyate | sarvagrāse kapilaḥ sakṛṣṇatāmraḥ tamomadhye | yadā sakalam bimbam channam bhavati tadā sarvagrāsaḥ, tatra kapilavarṇaḥ | tasmāt parataḥ vimardakālāt madhyam yāvat sakṛṣṇatāmraḥ bhavati | sūryagrahaṇe punar sarvadā kṛṣṇavarṇaḥ || 46 ||
body.translated_text: At first contact (<s>pragrahaṇa</s>), at the beginning, and at the end, at release (<s>mokṣa</s>), the Moon is smoky (<s>dhūmra</s>). During partial eclipse (<s>khaṇḍagrahaṇa</s>), it becomes black. Partial eclipse, being close to half of the first contact, is perceived by all. During total eclipse (<s>sarvagrāsa</s>), it is tawny (<s>kapila</s>); dark-coppery (<s>sakṛṣṇatāmra</s>) in the middle of the shadow. When the entire disc is covered, that is total eclipse; there, the color is tawny. Beyond that, from the time of totality up to the middle, it becomes dark-coppery. In a solar eclipse, however, the color is always black. || 46 ||

body.text: anādeśyam ravigrahaṇam
body.translated_text: The unpredictable solar eclipse

body.text: grahaṇopalabdhipradarśanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: In order to demonstrate the observation of eclipses, he says:

children.translated_text: When the circumferences of the Sun and Moon conjoin, one-eighth of the Sun's [disc] is unpredictable (<s>anādeśya</s>);
because of the radiant nature of the Sun, and because of the transparent thinness of the Moon's circumference. || 47 ||

body.text:
sūryenduparidhiyogaḥ sūryagrahaṇam | atra arkabimbasya aṣṭamabhāgaḥ channaḥ api anādeśyaḥ | bhānoḥ bhāsvarabhāvāt | tīkṣṇāṃśoḥ bhāsvarasvarūpatvāt iti | candrasya api svacchatanutvāt aṣṭamabhāgaḥ bimbasya channaḥ api anādeśyaḥ iti | grāhyabimbasya aṣṭamabhāgaḥ mānaikyārdhāt viśodhya śeṣaḥ iṣṭagrāsakarṇaḥ | tadvargāt sphuṭavikṣepavargonāt mūlam iṣṭonasthitidalaliptāḥ bhvanti | tāḥ ṣaṣṭiguṇāḥ gatyantarahṛtāḥ ghaṭikāḥ | tāḥ sparśe tithyante
viśodhayet | mokṣe api tithyante yojayet | tau sparśamokṣakālau bhavataḥ || 47 ||
body.translated_text:
The conjunction of the circumferences of the Sun and Moon is a solar eclipse. Here, one-eighth of the Sun's disc, even though covered, is unpredictable (<s>anādeśya</s>) — because of the radiant nature of the Sun. Because of the brilliant nature of the sharp-rayed one, so it is. Also, because of the transparent thinness of the Moon, one-eighth of the disc, even though covered, is unpredictable. Subtracting one-eighth of the eclipsed disc from the half of the sum of diameters, the remainder is the desired obscuration hypotenuse (<s>iṣṭagrāsakarṇa</s>). The square root of the difference of the square of that and the square of the true latitude gives the minutes of the desired-subtracted half-duration. Those, multiplied by sixty and divided by the difference of daily motions, give the <s>ghaṭikās</s>. Those should be subtracted
from the <s>tithi</s>-end at the moment of contact; and at the release, added to the <s>tithi</s>-end. Those become the times of contact and release. || 47 ||

body.text: grahasādhanopāyaḥ
body.translated_text: The method of computing planets

body.text: grahasādhanopāyapradarśanārtham āha ã
body.translated_text: In order to demonstrate the method of computing planets (<s>grahasādhana</s>), he says:

children.text: kṣitiḥ aviyogāt dinakṛt ravīnduyogāt prasādhayet ca indum |
children.translated_text: The Sun [is determined] from [its] inseparable [conjunction with] the Earth; and the Moon should be established from the conjunction of the Sun and Moon;
from the conjunction of the Moon with the star-planets, all the star-planets likewise. // 48 //

body.text: kṣitiḥ ca raviḥ ca, tayoḥ yogaḥ kṣitiraviyogaḥ | tasmāt ravim sādhayet | ravīnduyogāt indum sādhayet | śaśitārāgrahayogāt ca sarve tārāgrahāḥ ca sādhanīyāḥ |
body.translated_text: The Earth and the Sun — their conjunction is the Earth-Sun conjunction. From that, the Sun should be determined. From the Sun-Moon conjunction, the Moon should be determined. And from the Moon-star-planet conjunction, all the star-planets are to be determined.

body.text:
dṛgucchritam salilasamīkṛtabhūpradeśamaṇḍalakam cakrabhāgāṅkitavṛttaparidhim dikcatuṣṭayacihnitam kārayet | tasya aparabhāge sthitaḥ sāṃvatsaraḥ prākparidhau āsaktam udgacchantam sūryam lakṣayet | tataḥ tatpradeśe cihnam kṛtvā tiṣṭhet yāvat anyodayam | tatra api yatra paridhipradeśe sūryaḥ uditaḥ lakṣyate tatra cihnam nidadhyāt | evam udayatrayeṇa catuṣkeṇa vā antaraghaṭikāḥ yantrādinā lakṣayitavyāḥ | tāḥ ravibhuktayaḥ ravyudayāntarāle bhavanti
| tāḥ eva sphuṭaravibhuktiliptāḥ | madhyadinacchāyayoḥ vedhena tajjyādividhinā [ravidvayam ānayet |] tayoḥ antaram [vā] sphuṭaravibhuktiḥ |
body.translated_text: One should construct a circle at eye-level on a ground leveled with water, with its circumference marked in degrees of the circle and indicated with the four cardinal directions. The astronomer, standing at the western part of it, should observe the Sun rising on the eastern circumference. Then, placing a mark at that spot, he should wait until the next rising. There too, wherever on the circumference the Sun is observed to rise, he should place a mark. Thus, by three or four risings, the intervening <s>ghaṭikās</s> should be noted by an instrument and the like.

body.text:
atha meṣādau pravṛtte savitari sūryodayāḥ gaṇyante yāvat meṣādim praviśati, te ravibhūyogāḥ jāyante | evam samyak upalakṣyamāṇāḥ ravibhagaṇabhoge śatatrayam pañcaṣaṣṭyā adhikam dinam bhavati 365 | ghaṭikāḥ pañcadaśa 15 | vighaṭikāḥ ekatriṃśat 31 | prāṇāḥ sārdhaikāḥ
3
2|
tāḥ krameṇa savarṇitāḥ upari bhāgāḥ 210389, chedaḥ 576 | evam etaiḥ aṃśaiḥ ṣaṣṭasaptapañcacchedaiḥ ekaḥ arkabhagaṇaḥ | etaiḥ yagādimānam kriyate |
body.translated_text: Now, when the Sun has entered the beginning of <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries), sunrises are counted until it enters [the beginning of] <s>Meṣa</s> again — those become the Sun-Earth conjunctions. Thus, when properly observed, in the Sun's traversal of one revolution, there are three hundred and sixty-five days [365], fifteen <s>ghaṭikās</s> [15], thirty-one <s>vighaṭikās</s> [31], and one-and-a-half <s>prāṇas</s> [3/2]. These, when progressively reduced to a common denominator, [give] numerator 210389, denominator 576. Thus, with these fractional parts with denominator five-seven-six-sixty, [one gets] one solar revolution. By these, the <s>yuga</s>...

body.text: ravīnduyogaprasādhanāya sūryādhikrāntacandram upalakṣayet | punar dvitīyam evam varṣam prati jāgareṇa dvādaśa ravīnduyogāḥ 12, catvāraḥ rāśayaḥ 4, dvādaśa bhāgāḥ 12, ṣaṭcatvāriṃśat liptāḥ 46, catvāriṃśat viliptāḥ 40, aṣṭacatvāriṃśat tatparāḥ 48 | ekena ravibhagaṇena yutāḥ ete savarṇitāḥ
body.translated_text: For determining the Sun-Moon conjunctions, one should observe the Moon overtaken by the Sun. Again, for the second year, by vigilant observation, the Sun-Moon conjunctions [in one year are:] revolutions 12, signs 4, degrees 12, minutes 46, seconds 40, thirds 48. Added to one solar revolution, these when reduced to a common denominator become:

body.text:
yugagatacandrabhagaṇāḥ trairāśikena ã yadi ekena ravibhagaṇabhogena etāvantaḥ
1039560048
  77760000
candrabhagaṇāḥ labhyante, tadā yuga[ravibhagaṇa]bhogena anena 4320000 kiyantaḥ iti, labdham yuge candrabhagaṇāḥ 57753336 |
body.translated_text: The Moon's revolutions in a <s>yuga</s> [are found] by the rule of three: if in one solar revolution this many [= 1039560048 / 77760000] lunar revolutions are obtained, then in the <s>yuga</s>-solar-revolutions [= 4,320,000], how many? The result: lunar revolutions in a <s>yuga</s> = 57,753,336.

body.text: athavā candrasya iṣṭaśuklapratipat ārabhya pratidinam candrodayam upalakṣya binduḥ kāryaḥ yāvat ravibhagaṇam | evam ravibhagaṇabhoge candrodayasaṃkhyāḥ jātāḥ
body.translated_text: Alternatively, from the desired bright first day (<s>śukla pratipat</s>) of the Moon, observing the moonrise daily and marking a point until [the completion of] one solar revolution — thus, in one solar revolution, the count of moonrises obtained [is:]
Reduced to a common denominator: 352 11532492/216000.

body.text: etaiḥ trairāśikam ã yadi ekasmin [ravi]bhagaṇabhoge etāvantaḥ [candrodayāḥ] bhavanti, [tadā yuga]ravibhagaṇabhoge kiyantaḥ | prāgvat yuge candrodayāḥ jātāḥ 1524484164 | kṣitibhagaṇebhyaḥ 1582237500 śuddhāḥ yugacandrabhagaṇāḥ 57753336 |
body.translated_text: By the rule of three with these: if in one solar revolution this many moonrises occur, then in the <s>yuga</s>-solar-revolutions, how many? As before, the moonrises in a <s>yuga</s> obtained = 1,524,484,164. Subtracting from the Earth's revolutions [1,582,237,500], the Moon's revolutions in a <s>yuga</s> = 57,753,336.

body.text: śaśitārāgrahayogān śaśibhagaṇebhyaḥ viśodhya śeṣam iṣṭagrahasya bhagaṇāḥ | varṣam prati jāgareṇa candrabṛhaspatiyogāḥ bhagaṇāḥ 13, rāśayaḥ 3, bhāgāḥ 12, liptāḥ 25, viliptāḥ 33, tatparāḥ 36 | ete krameṇa savarṇitāḥ jātāḥ
body.translated_text: The Moon-star-planet conjunctions — subtracting from the Moon's revolutions, the remainder gives the desired planet's revolutions. By vigilant observation for one year, the Moon-Jupiter conjunctions [are:] revolutions 13, signs 3, degrees 12, minutes 25, seconds 33, thirds 36. These, progressively reduced to a common denominator, become:

body.text:
yadi ekasmin ravibhagaṇe etāvantaḥ
1033004016
  77760000
guruśaśiyogāḥ labhyante, tadā yugaravibhagaṇe 4320000 kiyantaḥJiti, labdhāḥ yugābde guruśaśiyogāḥ 57389112 candrabhagaṇebhyaḥ 57753336 viśodhya śeṣam gurubhagaṇāḥ yuge jātāḥ 364224 | evam bhaumādīnām api ravibhagaṇabhogam yāvat candreṇa saha yogān prasādhya grahabhagaṇasādhanam kartavyam | mārgadarśanam eva etat asmadādīnām aviṣayaḥ |
body.translated_text: If in one solar revolution this many [= 1033004016 / 77760000] Jupiter-Moon conjunctions are obtained, then in the <s>yuga</s>-solar-revolutions [4,320,000], how many? The Jupiter-Moon conjunctions obtained in a <s>yuga</s> = 57,389,112. Subtracting from the Moon's revolutions [57,753,336], the remainder gives Jupiter's revolutions in a <s>yuga</s> = 364,224. Similarly, for Mars and the others too, by determining the conjunctions with the Moon over one solar revolution, the determination of planetary revolutions should be done. This is merely a guide — it is beyond the scope of people like us.

body.text:
budhaśukrayoḥ śīghrasādhanam | prācyām astamitaḥ paścāt yāvadbhiḥ dinaiḥ uditaḥ tāvatām dinānām ardham udayadinebhyaḥ pātayet astamitadineṣu kṣipet | punar prācyām yadā astamayaḥ pratīcyām udayaḥ tadā anena eva vidhinā niraṃśadinasiddhiḥ kāryā | tayoḥ ādyantaniraṃśayoḥ madhye śīghrakendrabhagaṇaḥ bhavati | budhasya śīghrakendrabhagaṇadināni āsannāni 116, śukrasya 584 | etaiḥ bhūdinebhyaḥ 1577917500 bhāgam datvā labdham
budhaśukraśīghrakendrabhagaṇāḥ bhavanti |
body.translated_text: Determination of the fast [apogee] of Mercury and Venus: From the east, after setting, by however many days it rises [again] — half that many days should be subtracted from the rising-days and added to the setting-days. Again, when the setting is in the east and the rising in the west, by this same procedure the zero-remainder-day determination should be done. Between those two zero-remainder [days] at the beginning and end, there is one fast-anomaly revolution. Mercury's fast-anomaly revolution days are approximately 116; Venus's are 584. By these, from the terrestrial days [1,577,917,500]...

body.text:
ravyucca[paridhi]sādhanam | madhyāhnacchāyayā ravim prasādhya taddinamadhyamaraviṇā viśeṣya madhyame adhike ṛṇam, dhanamūle | evam pratidinam upalabhya yāvat vardhamānam raviphalam sthirībhavati, tatphalam paramaphalam | tataḥ param hrāsam eṣyati | paramaphaladine madhyame arke ṛṇaphalopalakṣite rāśitrayam śodhayet, śeṣam ravimandoccam | dhanaphalopalakṣite rāśitrayam kṣipet, mandoccam bhavati | paramaphalajyā cakrāṃśahatā trijyāhṛtā
raveḥ paridhiḥ bhavati |
body.translated_text: Determination of the Sun's apogee [epicycle]: Having determined the Sun from the midday shadow, comparing with the mean Sun of that day — when the mean is greater, it is negative; [otherwise] positive. Thus, observing daily until the increasing solar correction becomes stationary — that correction is the maximum correction. Thereafter it will decrease. On the day of maximum correction, when the mean Sun shows a negative correction, subtract three signs — the remainder is the Sun's slow apogee (<s>mandocca</s>). When showing a positive correction, add three signs — that becomes the slow apogee...

body.text:
candroccaparidhisādhanam | sūryāstamayāt kṛṣṇe pakṣe yāvatībhiḥ ghaṭikābhiḥ candrodayaḥ bhavati ghaṭikāyantrasādhitābhiḥ tābhiḥ ṣaḍrāśiyutāt arkāt lagnam svodayaiḥ tripraśnoktavidhinā kartavyam | sa sphuṭacandraḥ | tat tātkālikamadhyamacandraviśleṣaśeṣam māndaphalam dhanum ṛṇam vā | evam pratyaham upalakṣayet pūrvavat yāvat vardhamānaphalam sthirībhavati | tataḥ ravivat uccaparidhisādhanam | evam pratidinam kuryāt yāvat madhyamasphuṭayoḥ
na kiñcit antaram syāt | sa eva candraḥ taduccam bhavati | taddinaparamaphalapātadinoccayoḥ antaram kṛtvā taddinaparamaphalārkayoḥ antaram kāryam | tata[ḥ trairāśikam] ã yadi anena gatyantareṇa etat uccāntaram, tadā sūryabhagaṇaiḥ kim iti androccabhagaṇasiddhiḥ |
body.translated_text: Determination of the Moon's apogee epicycle: In the dark fortnight, by however many <s>ghaṭikās</s> after sunset the moonrise occurs — as measured by a water-clock instrument — from the Sun plus six signs, the ascendant (<s>lagna</s>) should be computed by one's own rising-times using the method stated in the three-question [chapter]. That is the true Moon. The difference of that from the mean Moon of that time is the slow-correction — positive or negative. Thus, one should observe daily as before until the increasing correction becomes stationary. Thereafter, the apogee-epicycle determination [is done] as for the Sun. Thus...

body.text:
candrasya pātabhagaṇasādhanam | candragrahaṇe [sparśakālāt] madhyagrahaṇam yāvat sthityardhaghaṭikāḥ candragrahaṇakālotpannāḥ tāḥ sphuṭasūryaśaśibhuktyantareṇa guṇayet, ṣaṣṭyā vibhajet, sthityardhaliptāḥ syuḥ | tadvargam samparkārdhavargāt viśodhya śeṣasya mūlam candravikṣepaḥ | sa trijyāhataḥ khāgākṣibhaktaḥ [270] kāṣṭhitaḥ bhujacāpam | evam mokṣam api [sthityardham] madhyagrahaṇāt jānīyāt | yadi prathamasthityardham mahat ojapade
grahaḥ bhavati, anyathā yugmapade syāt | yadi uttaravikṣepaḥ viṣamapade bhujacāpam sphuṭam, yugmapade cakrārdhāt viśodhya bhavati | dakṣiṇavikṣepe viṣamapade cakrārdham kṣipet, yugmapade cakrāt viśodhayet | sa bāhuḥ syāt | evam svadhiyā śeṣam ca | evam anyat grahaṇakālikam bāhum utpādayet | ubhayoḥ antaram sādhayet | grahaṇadvayakālāntarajā tatpātabhuktiḥ | tataḥ candrapātabhagaṇasiddhiḥ |
body.translated_text: Determination of the Moon's node-revolutions: In a lunar eclipse, from the contact time to mid-eclipse, the half-duration <s>ghaṭikās</s> produced at the time of the lunar eclipse — multiply those by the difference of the true rates of the Sun and Moon, divide by sixty — [the result] will be the half-duration in minutes. Subtract the square of that from the square of half the sum [of the diameters]; the square root of the remainder is the Moon's latitude (<s>vikṣepa</s>). That, multiplied by the radius (<s>trijyā</s>) and divided by 270 [= the maximum latitude], converted to an arc — [gives] the <s>bhuja</s> arc. Similarly, the release [time] should also be known from the half-duration after mid-eclipse. If...

body.text: athavā candrasya dinārdhacchāyayā krāntim uktavat prasādhayet | tasyāḥ taddinacandrakrāntyantaram vikṣepaḥ | śeṣam prāgvat iti |
body.translated_text: Alternatively, one should determine the Moon's declination by the half-day shadow as stated. The difference between that and the Moon's declination of that day is the latitude. The rest is as before.

body.text:
budhasitayoḥ yāvatā rātrigatakālena astamayaḥ jāyate tāvatā lagnam ṣaḍrāśiyutam sphuṭaḥ budhaḥ śukraḥ ca | śeṣāṇām candravat ānayanam rātrigate kāle | madhyasphuṭayoḥ antaram mandaphalayutaviyutam śīghraphalam | punar pañcabhiḥ ahobhiḥ phalasādhanam kartavyam | prākphalena saha viśleṣayet | evam tāvat parīkṣayet yāvat vardhamānam śīghraphalam sthirībhavati | evam svadhiyā abhyūhya śīghrocca[paridhi]sādhanam | tārāgrahayogāntarāt
grahavikṣepasādhanam kartavyam | udayāstamayavakrānuvakraiḥ śīghrabhagaṇasādhanam vidheyam | athavā graham yaṣṭyādiyantreṇa viditvā dvitīye api dine tāvati eva kāle viddhyāt, tadantaram sphuṭabhuktiḥ | sā madhyamabhukteḥ yadā ūnā syāt tadā kakṣyāmaṇḍalāt upari grahaḥ, adhikā cet tadā adhaḥ vartate | tadbhūmadhyāntaram karṇaḥ | tadvaśāt paramālpatām paramādhikatām ca bhukteḥ lakṣayet iti bhagaṇabhogam yāvat | bhagaṇabhogaḥ madhyamagatyā
eva bhavati | evam mandaphalasya paramādhikatām lakṣayitvā paramamandakarṇavyāsārdhāntaram paramaphalam māndam bhavati || 48 ||
body.translated_text: For Mercury and Venus, by however much elapsed night-time the setting occurs, with that [time], the ascendant plus six signs is the true Mercury or Venus. For the others, the computation is like the Moon at the elapsed night-time. The difference of mean and true, combined with or separated from the slow correction, is the fast correction. Again, the correction-determination should be done for five days. Compare with the previous correction. Thus, one should test until the increasing fast correction becomes stationary. Thus, by one's own intelligence, having inferred the fast apogee [epicycle]...

body.text: sampradāyasaṃsmaraṇam
body.translated_text: Remembrance of the tradition

body.text: bhagaṇādīnām pramāṇāni katham jñātāni ācāryeṇa tatpratipādanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: How were the measures of the revolutions and the like known by the <s>ācārya</s>? To demonstrate that, he says:

children.translated_text: From the ocean of true and false knowledge, raised up by the grace of <s>Brahmā</s>,
the supreme jewel of true knowledge — submerged — [was retrieved] by me with the boat of my own intellect. // 49 //

body.text: sadasat sat asat | sat śubham, asat aśubham | jñānam jñāyate anena iti | sajjñānottamaratnam sat jñānam tat eva uttamaratnam, utkṛṣṭam ratnam, jyotiḥśāstram | nimagnam nilīnam | svamatināvā svakīyā matiḥ (svamatiḥ), svamatiḥ eva nauḥ tayā svamatināvā sadasajjñānasamudrāt samuddhṛtam iti || 49 ||
body.translated_text: '<s>Sadasat</s>' — true and false. '<s>Sat</s>' is auspicious; '<s>asat</s>' is inauspicious. 'Knowledge' — that by which one knows. 'The supreme jewel of true knowledge' — true knowledge itself is the supreme jewel, the excellent gem — [meaning] the science of astronomy. 'Submerged' — hidden. 'With the boat of my own intellect' — one's own intellect is '<s>svamati</s>'; that intellect itself is the boat; by that boat of one's own intellect, [it was] raised up from the ocean of true and false knowledge. // 49 //

body.text: pratikañcukakāriṇe daṇḍavidhānam
body.translated_text: Punishment prescribed for one who counterfeits

body.text: śapathapratipādanāya āha ã
body.translated_text: In order to declare an imprecation, he says:

children.text: āryabhaṭīyam nāmnā pūrvam svāyambhuvam sadā nityam |
children.translated_text: The <s>Āryabhaṭīya</s> by name, formerly the <s>Svāyambhuva</s> (of <s>Svayambhū</s>), always eternal —

children.text: sukṛtāyuṣoḥ praṇāśam kurute pratikañcukam yaḥ asya || 50 ||
children.translated_text: whoever counterfeits this brings about the destruction of [his own] merit and lifespan. // 50 //

body.text: āryabhaṭasya idam āryabhaṭīyam | kim tat? yadā eva atyantavipralīnasampradāyam brahmaṇaḥ prasādena vā svanāmadheyam | yaḥ pūrvam svāyambhuvam āsīt idānīm āryabhaṭena prakāśitatvāt āryabhaṭīyam | svāyambhuvam tat sarvadā nityam | svayaṃbhuvā praṇītam artham gṛhītvā ācāryāḥ śāstrāṇi racayanti | sampradāyāvicchedāt tu saḥ arthaḥ jñātaḥ eva | anyathā atīndriyārthānām katham mānuṣamātraiḥ iyam yuktiḥ kartum śakyate | asya pratikañcukam

children.text: pratibimbam yaḥ karoti tasya sukṛtasya āyuṣaḥ ca praṇāśam bhavati || 50 ||
children.translated_text: Whoever makes a counterfeit (<s>pratibimba</s>) — the destruction of his merit and lifespan occurs. // 50 //

body.translated_text: This [work] of <s>Āryabhaṭa</s> is the <s>Āryabhaṭīya</s>. What is it? That which was formerly the <s>Svāyambhuva</s>, when the tradition had been completely lost — [it was recovered] by the grace of <s>Brahmā</s>, or [it bears] his own name. What was formerly the <s>Svāyambhuva</s> is now, having been brought to light by <s>Āryabhaṭa</s>, the <s>Āryabhaṭīya</s>. The <s>Svāyambhuva</s> is always eternal. Having grasped the content composed by the Self-born (<s>Svayambhū</s>), the teachers compose treatises. Through the unbroken continuity of tradition, that content is known. Otherwise, how could this method be [devised] by mere humans for supersensible objects?

body.text: someśvarabhāṣyasya upasaṃhāraślokaḥ
body.translated_text: Concluding verse of <s>Someśvara</s>'s commentary

children.translated_text: Clear in explaining the meaning, well-spoken and illuminating for those of tender intellect,
by <s>Someśvara</s>, whose mind is purified by logic, grammar, and the like —
the elucidation of the <s>sūtras</s> spoken by the teacher <s>Āryabhaṭa</s>, which was produced by <s>Bhāskara</s>,

children.text: tasyāḥ sārataram vikṛṣya racitam bhāṣyam prakṛṣṭam laghu ||
children.translated_text: from that, extracting the essence, this excellent and concise commentary has been composed.

body.text: iti someśvaraviracitam āryabhaṭīyam bhāṣyam samāptam |
body.translated_text: Thus, the commentary on the <s>Āryabhaṭīya</s> composed by <s>Someśvara</s> is completed.

body.text: bhāskarabhāṣyasya upasaṃhāraślokaḥ
body.translated_text: Concluding verse of <s>Bhāskara</s>'s commentary

children.translated_text: These <s>sūtras</s> (aphorisms), uttered by <s>Āryabhaṭa</s>,
which expound matters beyond the reach of the senses —
even a hundredth part of their meaning
cannot be expressed in full by ones such as ourselves — how much less the whole!

body.text: iti bhāskarasya kṛtau āryabhaṭatantrabhāṣye
body.translated_text: Thus, in the commentary (<s>bhāṣya</s>) on the treatise of <s>Āryabhaṭa</s>, composed by <s>Bhāskara</s>,

body.text: golapādaḥ samāptaḥ |
body.translated_text: the <s>Golapāda</s> (Chapter on the Sphere) is concluded.
